text: In recent years, as interest in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has increased, the development of UAV-based services in traffic monitoring, military defense, disaster prevention, logistics, and agricultural area has begun to be of interest. The main characteristic of these services is that it is effective to provide based on a plurality of UAVs rather than a single UAV. In addition, in order to expand the service provision, different types of UAVs, not the UAVs of a particular kind, should be able to operate in the same service together. In order for different types of UAVs to receive the same services efficiently, a standardized platform is needed and services need to be provided on that platform. In this paper, to address this issue, the platform based on the oneM2M global standard, which provides the Internet of Things (IoT) service layer for globally interoperable IoT solutions, is considered. Based on the global standard-based platform, we present UAV management and control system. Furthermore, we implemented an automated UAV-based surveillance system as an example of a service using the platform.

Cooperative human–agent–robot teamwork (HART) provides enormous opportunities for present-day human users to orchestrate their real-time tasks in a coordinated fashion. However, given human users’ different preferences for real-time HART task execution, e.g., lower delay and monetary cost, the selection of proper task coordination services has emerged as an important research problem by taking dynamically changing cloud agent/robot resources, network bandwidth utilization, as well as delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant HART task properties into account. To cope with these challenges, in this paper, we explore the synergy between caching, computation, and communications for achieving cost-effective HART task execution. To exploit the locality of different HART-centric tasks and local/non-local cloud agent/robot resources for different HART-centric task execution, we consider integrated fiber-wireless (FiWi) enhanced networks with computation task offloading as well as fiber backhaul sharing and WiFi offloading capabilities. More precisely, to minimize task execution delay and monetary cost, we propose a user preference aware HART task coordination framework that selects the appropriate dedicated or non-dedicated robot and cloud agent for given caching and computing HART task execution requirements. Further, to cope with varying bandwidth resources, we propose a proactive bandwidth allocation policy for the execution of both delay-sensitive and delay-tolerant HART tasks execution across FiWi enhanced network infrastructures. We evaluate the performance of our proposed preference aware task offloading scheme and compare it to various baseline schemes in terms of different key performance indicators, including the task execution time and monetary cost saving ratio, communication to computation ratio, and offloading gain overhead ratio. Our findings indicate that the proposed delay cost saving policy exhibits a 27% higher task execution time saving ratio and a 48% lower monetary cost saving ratio than the proposed monetary cost saving policy in a typical scenario.

Rolling bearings are essential components of rotating machinery and their fault diagnosis is crucial for ensuring safe and reliable operation. This paper proposes a novel method for fault diagnosis of rolling bearings based on wavelet packet (WP) reconstructed energy entropy and particle swarm optimization-least squares support vector machines (PSO-LSSVM). The proposed method employs WP decomposition for feature extraction and energy entropy calculation for fault identification. PSO-LSSVM is used for fault classification and diagnosis. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using experimental data of rolling bearings under varying fault conditions. Results show that the proposed method is effective in diagnosing rolling bearing faults and outperforms traditional methods. The proposed method provides a promising approach for rolling bearing fault diagnosis and can be applied to other rotating machinery for condition monitoring and fault prognosis.

Automatic headline generation is a sub-task of oneline summarization with many reported applications. Evaluation of systems generating headlines is a very challenging and undeveloped area. In this paper, we introduce a system that performs automatic evaluation of systems in terms of a quality of the generated headlines. The evaluation is performed using multiple metrics for comparing evaluated headlines with the gold standard ones or measuring their coverage of main document topics. Both types of metrics evaluate headline's content and informativeness, but not grammatical structure. The only input required by our system is a set of documents with gold standard and automatically generated headlines. The Headline Evaluation System (HEvaS) provides a user with a choice from multiple (10) metrics, then calculates the chosen metrics, performs statistical analysis of the evaluated systems and visualizes the results. Multiple headline generation systems can be evaluated at the same run. This paper describes all evaluation metrics and architecture, utilized by our system. As an evaluation of the HEvaS, we perform a case study with a couple of baseline systems and report the results. Although we tested the system on English content only, the multilingual content can also be supported.

This paper introduces a novel approach to rating prediction in review-based recommendations using an Adversarial Auto-Encoder. The proposed method leverages feature extraction and neural networks to accurately predict user ratings. In addition, the study explores the use of Gallium nitride as a material for neural network hardware, which could lead to improved computational efficiency. The research also investigates collaboration between generative adversarial networks and generators to optimize the recommendation model. To evaluate the proposed method, the researchers conducted experiments on datasets from various domains, such as games and movies, and compared the results to other state-of-the-art algorithms. The findings show that the Adversarial Auto-Encoder outperforms the baseline methods in terms of prediction accuracy and recommendation quality, indicating its potential for practical use in real-world recommendation systems.

The problem of real-time remote estimation in wireless networked control has been a topic of interest for many researchers in the field of control theory. The use of observers, which are algorithms that estimate the state of a system based on output measurements, has been proposed to overcome the challenges of transmitting large amounts of data over a wireless network. However, the time-varying nature of many systems poses challenges for the numerical stability of these observers. This paper explores the stability analysis of observers for time-varying systems and considers the impact of estimation error on overall system performance. Various methods for ensuring numerical stability are discussed, including the use of differential equations to model the system dynamics. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the challenges and solutions for real-time remote estimation in wireless networked control systems.

Financial markets are difficult to predict due to its complex systems dynamics. Although there have been some recent studies that use machine learning techniques for financial markets prediction, they do not offer satisfactory performance on financial returns. We propose a novel one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (CNN) model to predict financial market movement. The customized one-dimensional convolutional layers scan financial trading data through time, while different types of data, such as prices and volume, share parameters (kernels) with each other. Our model automatically extracts features instead of using traditional technical indicators and thus can avoid biases caused by selection of technical indicators and pre-defined coefficients in technical indicators. We evaluate the performance of our prediction model with strictly backtesting on historical trading data of six futures from January 2010 to October 2017. The experiment results show that our CNN model can effectively extract more generalized and informative features than traditional technical indicators, and achieves more robust and profitable financial performance than previous machine learning approaches.

In this paper, an accurate State of Charge (SOC) estimation system is proposed for batteries considering the observation noise of the electric current. The estimation of the SOC is crucial in battery management systems since both overcharging and undercharging can lead to severe consequences such as battery degradation, safety hazards, and reduced reliability. The proposed system utilizes Kalman filters to integrate voltage measurement and current measurement and model the integrated circuit to improve estimation accuracy. The observation noise of the electric current is taken into account to reduce estimation errors caused by measurement noise. The proposed system is validated through experimental tests, and the results show significant improvement in SOC estimation accuracy compared to conventional methods. The proposed system has a high potential to be applied in various battery-related industries such as electric vehicles, renewable energy, and portable devices.

This note investigates the output regulation problem of Boolean control networks (BCNs) under event-triggered control via semi-tensor product of matrices. Firstly, based on an algebraic state-space representation of BCNs, a necessary and sufficient condition is obtained for the solvability of the output regulation problem. Secondly, the feedback event-triggered control laws are obtained by using augmented system approach. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed results.

Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) trade deep and intimate tutor-tutee interactions for large-scale coverage of educational lectures. Therefore, a proper length of student-assistant discussion is particularly precious both for the questioner and the observers in MOOC communities. To investigate the concept conveying characteristics of long and short discussions, this paper collected 32 student-assistant discussion transcripts in MOOC communities. Each discussion thread was randomly chosen in one course. Besides, 32 questions-and-answers (Q&A) transcripts in different science lectures and 31 Q&A transcripts in different press briefings were collected as comparison groups. The nouns in these transcripts were extracted as concepts, and the concept conveying procedure was modelled into a directed graph. We found that if an assistant would like to prolong the discussion in MOOC communities, he or she needs to retain concepts closely connected like political spokesmen on press briefings, and apply properly deep concepts like senior scientists on science lectures.

This paper proposes a heuristic mixed model for viral marketing cost minimization in social networks. The model integrates both computational and analytic approaches, incorporating previous work in integrated circuit modeling and optimization. In particular, the model seeks to minimize costs associated with viral marketing campaigns on social platforms such as Facebook. It achieves this by identifying the key factors and players involved in the social network, and optimizing strategies accordingly. The proposed model presents a novel approach to minimizing marketing costs while maximizing reach and impact. Overall, this study contributes to the ongoing exploration of computational modeling and optimization in the realm of social media marketing.

This paper presents a deep learning based approach for small-signal stability of a single machine connected to infinite bus. The proposed approach is based on an optimal estimation of the synchronizing and damping torque coefficients of the synchronous generator by optimal measurement of the operating conditions including the voltage, real power and reactive power. The proposed approach in this paper is to train deep neural networks to estimate the synchronizing and damping torque coefficients for all examples that the power system may encounter. Hence, a large dataset of more than 310,000 examples is created to cover the full range of the possible operation conditions. The performance of deep neural networks based approach is compared with that of other neural networks reported in the literature. Simulations results show that the proposed approach is robust and training the neural network over a wide range of operating conditions yield fast, yet accurate estimation of the torque coefficients.

This paper studies the problem of adaptive fault estimation and accommodation for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems with unknown time-varying faults. Different from existing fault estimation methods, a novel adaptive prescribed performance fault estimator is designed, which guarantees that the fault estimation error is confined within a pre-set region, and a better estimation accuracy is obtained. The designed fault-tolerant tracking controller is capable of attenuating the effect of faults through using back-stepping techniques. Furthermore, the proposed method guarantees that all the error signals of the closed-loop system be bounded in probability, the fault estimation error and output tracking error both converge to desired neighborhoods of origin in the sense of quadratic mean value. Finally, the simulation results are provided to verify the method proposed in this paper.

With the rapid growth of social media, people are more aware of cyber bullying on the internet. The most important aspect for preventing cyber bullying is to detect the abusive content. In this paper, we build a Long Short-Term MemoryNeural Network-Deterministic Finite Automaton (LND) model which considers not only the language content, but also the user’s characteristics and historical speech on social network. Due to the lack of labeled content, we utilize Douban’s reviewers data by analyzing speech patterns with polarized emotions. Then the learned model is applied to analyze Chinese cyber bully behaviors on Weibo. As a result, the accuracy of detecting cyber bullying increases from 89% (sensitive lexicon filtering method) to 95% by considering user’s behavior features and language emotional polarity scores. Our model is capable of analyze real celebrities’ Weibo webpages and assists prevention of cyber bullying on social media.

Railway detection task produces a large number of images, the lack of effective image classification method makes it difficult to analyze detection image deeply. Using convolutional neural networks (CNN) to realize railway image scene classification is an effective technical means. This paper propose a method to reduce the bias of database by Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping(Grad-CAM) to effectively improve scene classification accuracy, and achieve accuracy of 95.3%(top3) on Railway12 database. Our approach combines two insights: (1) Small quantity of railway scene database make it hard for CNN to achieve high performance, transfer pre-trained ImageNet-CNN to fine-tune on railway scene database (2) Introduce Grad-CAM visualization method to analyze model's classification pattern and intuitively show the possible bias of database, provide an intuitive way to reduce bias of dataset.

In this paper, we present a live demonstration of real-time spoken digit recognition using the DeltaRNN accelerator. The DeltaRNN accelerator is a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a recurrent neural network (RNN) designed for speech recognition tasks. Real-time systems are critical for speech recognition as delays can cause errors in recognition accuracy. Using the DeltaRNN accelerator, we demonstrate real-time spoken digit recognition with a high level of accuracy. We also provide an error analysis of the recognition results and discuss the hardware and microphones used in the demonstration. The results show that the DeltaRNN accelerator is a promising approach for real-time speech recognition tasks on hardware platforms.

This paper proposes a subdictionary-based joint sparse representation framework for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition using multilevel reconstruction. The proposed method utilizes scattering features and radar polarimetry to extract discriminative features of the target. The joint sparse representation is performed by dividing the dictionary into multiple subdictionaries, which enhances the sparsity of the representation. A multilevel reconstruction strategy is applied to improve the accuracy of the recognition results. The proposed method is evaluated on two public SAR target databases and compared with several state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in terms of recognition accuracy and robustness. This approach can be applied in various fields such as target recognition, feature extraction, image reconstruction, and solid modeling.

In this paper, we propose the use of LDHA-BP, a biological neural network inspired by dolphins, to predict atmospheric PM2.5 concentration. The predictive model uses virtual groups to simulate the behavior of dolphins and their ability to navigate using echolocation. By applying prediction algorithms to atmospheric modeling data from various sources, we were able to generate accurate predictions of PM2.5 concentration. This study not only highlights the potential of using biological neural networks in predictive modeling, but also emphasizes the importance of taking inspiration from nature in developing cutting-edge technologies.

With smart and connected IoT systems becoming increasingly prevalent in homes and businesses, ensuring that their `smartness' is up to the mark in making our lives secure is vital. This paper reveals the inadequacy of the `away mode' of smart plugs-which is a feature meant to safeguard a user's home security by mimicking the on-off pattern of appliance usage when a user is away, e.g., on a vacation. Using statistical methods, we show that a third party attacker can easily extrapolate sensitive usage information by analyzing accessible data gained from these commercial, off-the-shelf smart plugs. We recommend that the developers of these smart plugs should focus on implementing rule-based, coordinated, and/or learning-based models to enhance the away-mode behavior of these smart plugs to improve their performance in obfuscating user absence.

The role of various plant traits involved in carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) economy on species balance and total aboveground biomass production in binary mixtures of legumes and non-legumes was evaluated through a modelling approach using the Virtual Grassland model (VGL). A first step allowed us to identify the model parameters most sensible to inter-specific competition trough a sensitivity analysis. A second step consisted in testing the impact of individual traits values (i.e. selected among sensible parameters) on virtual mixture performance. Based on our simulation results, we concluded that maximal overyielding was achieved in cases where trait values were divergent for N acquisition (i.e. allowed complementarity in the use of different N pools) but convergent for light interception (i.e. limiting the asymmetric competition for light). The best combination of traits was not the same in all the pedo-climatic conditions tested and depended on the level of mineral N available into the soil. Random trait combinations could frequently lead to reduced mixture yields (as expected from a neutral situation of competition) and even to under-yielding (i.e. less than the average of monocultures) in some situations.

Given a nonlinear dynamical system, this letter considers the problem of selecting a subset of the total set of sensors that has provable guarantees on standard metrics related to the nonlinear observability Gramian. The key contribution is a simple randomized algorithm that samples the sensors uniformly without replacement, and yields probabilistic guarantees on the minimum eigenvalue or the inverse of the condition number of the nonlinear observability Gramian relative to that of the complete set of sensors. Numerical studies reveal that the utility of the theoretical results lies in the regime of large total number of sensors wherein the combinatorial nature of the problem presents a significant computational challenge. The results are demonstrated numerically on a problem of moving target localization using an extended Kalman filter in two scenarios: one using range sensors and another with time-difference-of-arrival measurements. A graceful degradation of performance with a decreased number of sensors is observed when compared to the use of all of the sensors for localization. It is also observed that for certain metrics, the proposed approach provides an improvement over a heuristic that selects the sensors in a greedy manner based on the contribution of an additional sensor toward the observability Gramian metric.

The combination of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model is investigated in this study to recognize characters of a license plate number without the need for segmentation. The aim of this research is to enhance the character recognition rate and decrease the computational complexity of the system. The proposed approach is trained using optical character recognition software to capture features of the input data model. The multilayer perceptron (MLP) algorithm is used to provide a strong computational modeling framework to the system. The empirical results demonstrate that the combination of CNN-GRU model outperforms existing methods in terms of recognition accuracy for license plate characters. Additionally, the proposed approach can learn the recognition model more effectively than traditional MLP based methods. Overall, the study provides a new perspective to enhance the performance of the character recognition algorithm by combining CNN and GRU models.

Prostate cancer remains a significant concern globally, with early detection being critical for successful treatment. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based system for detecting prostate cancer without segmentation, using magnetic resonance imaging. We utilize support vector machines with a kernel to classify the features extracted from the MRI images. Additionally, we draw inspiration from biological neural networks to design our CNN architecture. Evaluating our proposed method on a publicly available dataset, we achieve excellent classification accuracy, demonstrating that our proposed system can effectively detect prostate cancer without the need for segmentation. Our approach has the potential to significantly enhance early detection of prostate cancer and improve patient outcomes.

Skin lesion segmentation is an important task in biomedical imaging, with applications in computer-aided diagnosis of various skin diseases such as melanoma. In this paper, we propose a new approach to improving skin lesion segmentation through the use of stacked adversarial learning. Our method leverages the power of adversarial networks to learn to segment skin lesions at multiple scales, and we show that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art methods on a benchmark dataset. One of the key contributions of our work is the use of a novel training data augmentation technique, which allows us to train our models in a more robust manner with limited training data. Our experiments demonstrate that our approach can achieve impressive segmentation performance on both melanoma and non-melanoma skin lesions, highlighting the potential for this method to be used in clinical settings. Overall, we believe that our work represents an important step forward in the field of skin lesion segmentation, and we hope that our approach can help improve the accuracy and reliability of computer-aided diagnosis for skin diseases.

This paper proposes a benchmark and evaluation of both handcrafted and learned local descriptors in the context of image matching tasks using the $\mathbb{H}$-Patches dataset. The paper first analyzes the limitations of traditional benchmark testing when it comes to evaluating handcrafted and learned features. It then describes the $\mathbb{H}$-Patches dataset and the protocols and detectors used to extract features from it. The paper evaluates 10 handcrafted and 3 learned local descriptor methods using a variety of metrics such as repeatability and matching accuracy. The results suggest that learned descriptors can outperform handcrafted ones, but the performance of both types of descriptors greatly depends on the training data and the number of parameters. Finally, the paper suggests using a combination of learned and handcrafted descriptors to achieve optimal performance in image matching tasks.

This paper discusses the use of content-based image research, specifically examining the area of image color analysis. The study utilizes databases and support vector machines to aid in the process of feature extraction. Additionally, the use of Gabor filters is explored to assess the effectiveness of feature extraction. The results are then displayed using visualization techniques to reveal the shape of the object being analyzed. The findings of this study indicate that content-based image research can be an effective method for analyzing and understanding visual imagery. By utilizing a combination of advanced techniques, researchers can gain valuable insights into the properties of different images and better understand the relationship between color, shape, and other defining characteristics. Overall, this research provides an important foundation for future studies in the field of content-based image research and the development of more sophisticated techniques for analyzing and interpreting visual data.

The study aims to find out the training of beneficiaries level on the use of databases in the central library of the university Mohamed Bouguerra -Boumerdes, and the most important factors and steps that help in the success of training process on the use of digital information, as well as to detect the most important difficulties facing beneficiaries when searching the databases as the necessity that must be worked on as a result of the rapid developments and in order to ensure as much as possible to achieve their goals, especially with regard to databases that facilitated the access of information to the researcher.

The use of container-based 3-tier service traffic is becoming increasingly popular in cloud computing environments due to its ability to improve efficiency and reduce overhead costs. However, with the rise of this technology comes the need for effective monitoring and protection. This paper proposes a solution to the challenge of protecting the coordination of service mesh for container-based 3-tier service traffic. The proposed approach involves the use of cryptography to encrypt traffic between containers, as well as the implementation of custom computer architecture to support the encryption process. In addition, this paper explores the challenges of stress testing and monitoring in such environments and proposes an approach for handling these challenges using a combination of intelligent monitoring and automated response mechanisms. Overall, the proposed solution provides an effective means of protecting the coordination of service mesh in container-based 3-tier service traffic, while also addressing the challenges of monitoring and stress testing.

This paper presents a method of maximum permitted learning rate calculation for the neural controller of a balancing robot. The robot kinematics are analyzed and a training approach is proposed to update the weights of the neurons in the controller. The proposed method takes inspiration from biological neural networks to enhance the control system of mobile robots. The effectiveness of the proposed method is tested on a balancing robot and the results show improved performance and stability. This method can be applied to other control systems that utilize neural networks to enhance their efficiency and reliability.

This paper addresses the problem of optimal sampling of multiple linear processes that share a common communication medium. The objective is to estimate the processes while minimizing the resource utilization. The authors propose an optimization framework that takes into account stochastic processes and capacitive sensors to achieve efficient resource management. The proposed method is evaluated on a sensor system experiment and shows significant improvement in terms of estimation accuracy and resource utilization compared to other strategies. This work contributes to the development of efficient and effective sampling methods for sensor networks, which can have applications in many fields such as environmental monitoring and industrial control.

The purpose of monitoring the state of the objects of the cloud computing environment is to ensure their effective functioning. With the purpose of developing known statistical methods for monitoring the state of objects, a scientific approach is proposed that makes it possible to minimize errors of the 1st and 2nd kind when assessing the state of objects, compress large amounts of data without losing their informativeness based on the use of the Kulbak information measure. This approach largely allows satisfying the requirements for the implementation of known methods for monitoring the state of objects in the cloud computing environment. These requirements include: processing large amounts of current information to adjust the parameters of the control and management system; decision-making on the results of processing in real time; timely detection of possible precritical conditions of objects that may be associated with great economic damage or even catastrophic consequences.

With the increasing utilization of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, ensuring their security and privacy becomes essential. Address shuffling is a promising approach to address this issue. This method alters the source and destination IP addresses of the packets transmitted between the IoT devices and the servers. By doing so, it makes it harder for attackers to pinpoint the location of the devices and extract sensitive information. In this paper, we propose an easy way to implement address shuffling and improve security in IoT networks. We also analyze the impact of this technique on various protocols commonly used in IoT, including CoAP, MQTT, and HTTP. Additionally, we explore the potential applications of address shuffling in areas such as biomedical imaging, where confidentiality is of utmost importance. Overall, our study provides insights into how address shuffling can enhance the security and privacy of IP networks and IoT deployments, making them safer and more reliable.

This paper proposes a new method for the model-free global stabilization of discrete-time linear systems with saturating actuators using reinforcement learning. The mathematical model considers the system dynamics and linear systems, while the stabilization is achieved through the use of Riccati equations and heuristic algorithms. The reinforcement learning technique is used to learn the optimal control policy of the system, allowing for the achievement of stability without requiring a priori knowledge of the system model. The behavior of the system is analyzed through simulation, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving global stabilization under different operating conditions. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the development of model-free control techniques for linear systems with nonlinear actuators, highlighting the potential of reinforcement learning in solving complex control problems.

As the main logistics carrier of international transportation, the container is the main carrier of import and export goods. The role of containers in modern logistics systems has become increasingly prominent. The reefer container maintains temperature and humidity values within a specified range, which can ensure a safe transportation of food and medicines. Therefore, continuous monitoring and transmission of temperature and humidity in the reefer container is of great significance for ensuring the safety of transported products. In this paper, the WSN-IoT (Internet of Thing based on Wireless Sensor Network ） monitoring system for reefer containers is presented. The system hardware and software and the experimental results are discussed.

Automated wound area segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical diagnosis, as it aids in the identification and tracking of wounds during healing. In this study, we propose a novel approach for superpixel classification using both color and texture features to segment wound areas in skin images. The proposed method involves the extraction of color and texture features from training image samples, which are then used to train a classifier to identify wound areas based on histogram features. Our results show that the proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach for automated wound area segmentation. The proposed method has potential applications in various medical fields, including dermatology, wound care, and plastic surgery, among others.

The integration of cloud computing and mobile devices, known as Mobile Cloud Computing (MCC), allows the adoption of offloading techniques for improving compute intensive applications' performance and minimize the energy consumption. Deciding to offload some computing tasks or not is a way to solve the limitations of battery life and computing capability of mobile devices. In this paper, to alleviate the computational burden of mobile devices, we present a cost estimation weight factor for computation offloading in mobile devices. To make the right decisions as to whether or not to perform task offloading, based on the energy cost of the methods. The experimental results will demonstrate that the proposed cost estimator can significantly reduce energy consumption of mobile device as well as execution time of application.

Neuromorphic systems aim to mimic the structure and function of the human brain to perform tasks that traditional computers struggle to solve. This paper proposes a multilayer-learning current-mode neuromorphic system with analog-error compensation. The hardware architecture uses pulse width modulation to convert digital input signals to analog signals for more efficient computation. The neural networks are modeled using synapses with analog weights for improved energy efficiency. The system demonstrated successful approximation of various functions and exhibited better performance compared to traditional computing methods. The proposed architecture has potential applications in artificial intelligence and can pave the way for developing more advanced neuromorphic systems.

This paper focuses on the comparison of aboveground biomass estimation from InSAR and LiDAR canopy height models in tropical forests. The study is conducted in the context of forestry, where accurate biomass estimation is critical for effective forest management. Both InSAR and LiDAR techniques are commonly used for biomass estimation, but their performances have not been systematically compared before. The study utilizes coherence data models to convert data from both techniques into biomass estimates, and the results are compared. The study also includes discussions on vegetation characteristics, such as canopy height and structure, which can influence the accuracy of biomass estimation. By comparing the performances of InSAR and LiDAR, this study can provide useful insights for forest researchers and managers in choosing the most suitable technique for biomass estimation in their specific forest environments. The findings can also contribute to the development of more accurate biological system modeling in forestry research.

Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANET) are a promising technology for improving road safety through collective perception. One key element of this technology is the ability to efficiently disseminate sensor data from automobiles to others in the network. However, traditional frequency control methods may not be sufficient for VANETs due to their dynamic topology and high mobility. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel method for controlling sensor data dissemination that takes into account the road infrastructure and the vehicles themselves. Specifically, we propose the use of laser radar sensors to measure the distance between vehicles and adjust the dissemination frequency accordingly. Our simulation results show that this method can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of VANETs in terms of safety and overall performance.

Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent cancers among women worldwide, and early detection through mammography is crucial for successful treatment. Gabor filters have proven to be effective in processing mammography images by capturing texture features. However, the effectiveness of these filters is limited when dealing with complex features. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown great promise in image classification tasks. In this paper, we propose a method for suspicious mass classification in mammography images through the combination of Gabor filters and CNNs. The proposed method extracts features from mammography images using Gabor filters and feeds them to a CNN for classification. Experiments are conducted on two publicly available databases, and the results show that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. The proposed method can ultimately aid radiologists in the accurate diagnosis of breast cancer, leading to better outcomes for patients.

This paper proposes an automatic segmentation method for the placenta and its peripheral vasculature in volumetric ultrasound images, aimed at facilitating fetal surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS). The method utilizes three-dimensional displays and biomedical imaging techniques to accurately and efficiently segment the blood vessels surrounding the placenta. The segmented images can be used to guide surgeons during surgery and aid in preoperative planning. The proposed method involves image segmentation algorithms and deep learning techniques, and requires a training dataset for optimization. The segmentation results are promising, with high accuracy and efficiency in both preoperative planning and operative guidance. This method has the potential to greatly improve the safety and efficacy of fetal surgery for TTTS patients.

The advances of cloud and edge computing allow networked robots to acquire supporting information anywhere. Meanwhile, cloud and edge computing give rise to a large amount of data information for user to acquire. This leads to a challenging issue for wireless networks because radio resources is limited. To accommodate a number of robots that download map information from wireless LANs (WLANs), it is important for a robotic wireless network (RWN) to improve the efficiency of using wireless resources. The objective of this paper is to investigate how to efficiently use multiple wireless channels for a multi-layered RWN, which employs local data sharing among robots to save wireless resource consumption. Based on the hierarchical structure of multi-layered RWN, we proposed a multi-channel utilization scheme for local data delivery in robot clusters. The joint design of local data sharing via robot clustering and multi-channel utilization increases the available wireless resources for accommodating of the increasing number of service robots. Quantitative analysis results illustrate that the proposed channel separation-and-sharing system increases significantly the capability of robot accommodation and improve the channel availability. Furthermore, the preliminary experiment results confirm the functionality of the proposed system.

In this paper, we propose an optimal robust state estimator using maximum likelihood optimization with the t-distribution noise model. In robust statistics literature, the t-distribution is used to model Gaussian and non-Gaussian statistics. The influence function, an analytical tool in robust statistics, is employed to obtain the solution to the resulting maximum likelihood estimation optimization problem, so that the proposed estimator can be implemented within the framework of traditional robust estimators. Numerical results obtained from simulations of the IEEE 14-bus system, IEEE 118-bus system, and experiment on a microgrid demonstrated the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed estimator. The proposed estimator could suppress the influence of outliers with smaller average mean-squared errors (AMSE) than the traditional robust estimators, such as quadratic-linear, squareroot, Schweppe-Huber generalized-M, multiple-segment, and least absolute value estimators. A new approximate AMSE formula is also derived for the proposed estimator to predict and evaluate its precision.

Information fusion is an essential part of numerous engineering systems and biological functions, e.g., human cognition. Fusion occurs at many levels, ranging from the low-level combination of signals to the high-level aggregation of heterogeneous decision-making processes. While the last decade has witnessed an explosion of research in deep learning, fusion in neural networks has not observed the same revolution. Specifically, most neural fusion approaches are ad hoc, are not understood, are distributed versus localized, and/or explainability is low (if present at all). Herein, we prove that the fuzzy Choquet integral (ChI), a powerful nonlinear aggregation function, can be represented as a multilayer network, referred to hereafter as ChIMP. We also put forth an improved ChIMP (iChIMP) that leads to a stochastic-gradient-descent-based optimization in light of the exponential number of ChI inequality constraints. An additional benefit of ChIMP/iChIMP is that it enables explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Synthetic validation experiments are provided, and iChIMP is applied to the fusion of a set of heterogeneous architecture deep models in remote sensing. We show an improvement in model accuracy, and our previously established XAI indices shed light on the quality of our data, model, and its decisions.

Video data analysis is a fascinating field since the last few decades. It assists user to find the genre of a video without watching it. In this paper, an application for analysing Pakistani news data based on the scene classification using deep convolution neural network has been presented. For this purpose the dataset has been collected on our own, which consists of 200 videos of different news channels, and covers almost all categories which we possess in our methodology. The results have been evaluated using the 2D convolution neural network on the fine-tuned inception model. The methodology achieved the 92.2% accuracy on the proposed architecture, such a high accuracy on locally prepared dataset of the news for the video data analysis shows the novelty in literature.

In this paper, we present a new architecture for Gaussian Processes Model Reference Adaptive Control (GP-MRAC) trained using a generative network. GP-MRAC is a successful method for achieving global performance in the systems enabling adaptive control. GP-MRAC can handle a broader set of uncertainties without requiring apriori knowledge of the domain of operation. However, existing GP-MRAC work requires estimates of the state-derivate, and this is a primary limitation in the implementation of the controller. In this paper, we alleviate this major limitation by creating Model reference adaptive framework as Generative Network (MRGeN). Our contribution is a generative network architecture for learning Gaussian model to predict system uncertainties without having to estimate the state derivatives while ensuring that the system stability properties are unaffected. We retain the nonparametric nature of the controller by sharing the kernels between GP's and MRGeN, ensuring global performance and stability guarantees. GP-MRGeN can also be viewed as a method of baseline policy transfers, with applications in Reinforcement Learning.

End-to-end speech synthesis has gained a lot of attention in recent years due to its potential to simplify the speech synthesis pipeline. However, training such models can be challenging due to the long sequence length and the complexity of the acoustics of speech. In this paper, we propose a pre-alignment guided attention mechanism to improve the training efficiency and model stability of end-to-end speech synthesis. Our method guides attention to the relevant parts of the input using an analytical model of speech acoustics, which improves decoding accuracy and reduces training time. We perform stability analysis of the proposed method and show that it leads to more stable training compared to traditional attention mechanisms. Our experimental results show that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on a task analysis benchmark dataset while reducing the computational cost by 25% compared to traditional attention mechanisms.

Detection of high-speed maneuvering targets has attracted a great deal of attention recently. There are two main problems to be solved: improving detection ability under the condition of complicated range migration and Doppler frequency migration effects, and reducing computational load. Different from most existing fast algorithms which are at the cost of detection ability, this paper devises a computationally attractive method with excellent detection performance. First, the keystone transform is carried out to remove linear range migration. Thereafter, a fast discrete chirp-Fourier transform (FDCFT) based on radix-4 decomposition is proposed to compensate the undersampled linear Doppler frequency migration and quadratic Doppler frequency migration. Because of exploiting inherent symmetry and periodicity as in the fast Fourier transform (FFT), the FDCFT can largely reduce the computational complexity without performance loss. The novelty of the proposed algorithm lies in combining linear transform with the concept of decimation-in-time FFT, which avoids the demanding multi-dimensional search and severe performance loss via introducing nonlinear transforms. It is shown that the proposed method has an approximately optimal detection performance but with relatively low computational cost.

In recent years, with the increased development of social networking online, rumor spreading has become a common and challenging issue. To address this problem, feature extraction is a crucial step for on-line rumor detection. In this paper, we propose a dynamic slide window-based feature scoring and extraction method with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The proposed method can dynamically select the features with higher scores from the windows and adaptively update the feature set in each iteration, which improves the effectiveness and efficiency of feature extraction. Additionally, the proposed method utilizes semantic information to enhance the feature representation for the task of on-line rumor detection. The experiment results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and F1-measure on the benchmark dataset. Consequently, the proposed dynamic slide window-based feature scoring and extraction with CNN is proven to be effective and efficient for on-line rumor detection with Microsoft Windows.

This paper proposes a novel approach to improving Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) through Adversarial Learning with Knowledge of Image Classification. The traditional GANs are prone to producing low-quality images with poor resolution, which limits their practical applications. To address this issue, the authors introduce an adversarial training strategy that incorporates prior knowledge of image classification. Through this approach, the generators in the GANs are trained to produce images that are not only visually appealing but also accurately classified by the learning system. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through experimental results on Gallium Nitride data models. The proposed method shows significant improvements in terms of image resolution and classification accuracy, which suggests its potential for advancing the state-of-the-art in GANs. In conclusion, this study provides a promising direction for future research on better incorporating domain-specific knowledge into deep learning systems.

Machine-Type Communications (MTC) have recently become an integral part of the rapidly growing Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem. One of the major challenges facing MTC is the identification of Active Users, or those MTC devices that are actively transmitting data. In this paper, a novel solution to this problem is proposed using Dimension Spreading Neural Network (DSNN). The proposed DSNN algorithm is evaluated using Sparse Matrices and Correlation measures to achieve high accuracy in detecting Active Users. The proposed algorithm is also compared with an existing method called Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) to demonstrate its superiority. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DSNN algorithm achieves better performance in terms of detecting Active Users in MTC. Overall, this work establishes the potential of using neural networks to improve the performance of Active User Detection in MTC, which could lead to significant advancements in the field of IoT.

This paper develops an approach for household appliance identification and classification of household activities of daily living (ADLs) using residential smart meter data. The process of household appliance identification, i.e., decomposing a mains electricity measurement into each of its constituent individual appliances, is a very challenging classification problem. Recent advances have made deep learning a dominant approach for classification in fields, such as image processing and speech recognition. This paper presents a deep learning approach based on multilayer, feedforward neural networks that can identify common household electrical appliances from a typical household smart meter measurement. The performance of this approach is tested and validated using publicly available smart meter data sets. The identified appliances are then mapped to household activities, or ADLs. The resulting ADL classifier can provide insights into the behavior of the household occupants, which has a number of applications in the energy domain and in other fields.

This paper proposes a novel Chaotic Type-2 Transient-Fuzzy Deep Neuro-Oscillatory Network (CT2TFDNN) for worldwide financial prediction. The proposed methodology harnesses the power of fuzzy logic, predictive models, oscillators, indexes, linguistics, cryptography, and uncertainty principles to model and predict the complex and dynamic nature of financial markets. The CT2TFDNN takes into account the chaotic and transient behavior of financial data, and employs deep learning techniques to extract hidden features and relationships between various financial parameters. The proposed approach shows superior performance compared to traditional forecasting methods and can be used for both short-term and long-term financial predictions. The results also suggest that the CT2TFDNN can be used to predict potential financial crises and provide useful insights for policy makers and investors.

We introduce a method to classify ghost moving detections in automotive radar sensors for advanced driver assistance systems. A fully connected network is used to distinguish between real and false moving detections in the occupancy gridmaps. By using this architecture, we combine the local Doppler information, along with the spatial context of the surrounding scenario to classify the moving detections. A proof of concept experiment shows promising results with data from a test drive in an urban scenario.

Identification of clinically significant events in electroencephalograms (EEGs) is a time-consuming task for neurologists [1]. EEG signals contain a variety of morphologies which relate to a combination of brain signals and noise/artifacts. Automated classification of such events has the potential to speed up the interpretation process and provide valuable input to other types of EEG decision-making software. Because of the similarities between EEGs and speech signals, both of which contain temporal/sequential information, one of our long-term goals has been to apply well-developed concepts from speech recognition to EEG processing. We have previously approached this by applying hidden Markov Models (HMMs) [2] [3] using a toolkit known as HTK [4]. In this poster, we discuss the application of a new high-performance speech recognition system known as Kaldi [5] to this task. Adaptation of this technology to the EEG problem has not been as straightforward as previously thought.

The spectral efficiency of multiuser massive MIMO communication systems can be maximized using a finite dimensional channel. In this paper, we focus on the uplink scenario, where multiple antennas are equipped on user terminals. We investigate the effects of antenna configurations on the system performance, including the number of antennas and their spatial distribution. Channel estimation is also considered as a crucial aspect in multiuser massive MIMO communication, where a high accuracy is required for reliable data transmission. We propose a novel resource management scheme that optimizes the allocation of resources to different users based on their channel quality. Moreover, we introduce a receiver design that utilizes covariance matrices for channel estimation, achieving a better estimation accuracy compared to the conventional approaches. Our simulation results show that the proposed system design outperforms existing methods in terms of spectral efficiency and error rate performance.

The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), big data and cloud computing technologies has led to the development of Edge and Fog computing, which enables data and application processing close to the source of data. In this paper, we propose an architecture based on oneM2M for Fog computing. The proposed architecture utilizes Edge computing devices such as sensors and gateways to allow data processing at the edge of the network, and to minimize data transmission delays. The architecture includes a Cloud computing component as well, allowing for centralized processing and storage of the data for easy access by multiple users. The proposed architecture has been designed with emphasis on smart cities, which require real time data processing for urban services. We evaluate the proposed architecture using a case study on smart parking, demonstrating that it is capable of efficiently addressing the challenges faced by IoT applications in smart cities. In conclusion, this work presents an innovative approach to tackling the challenges of IoT, Edge and Cloud computing by proposing a novel architecture based on oneM2M, which is scalable, interoperable, and flexible.

Swarm robotics is an emerging field that utilizes a large number of simple robots to perform complex tasks in a coordinated manner. However, the reliability of the robots in the swarm can be compromised due to hardware or software faults. Fault detection and monitoring are essential in preventing system failure in swarm robotics. This paper proposes a mathematical model for statistical fault detection in swarm robots under noisy conditions. The approach integrates principal component analysis to reduce the dimensionality of the robot sensing systems, improving the accuracy of fault detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach can successfully detect faults in a swarm of robots under various noisy conditions. This research contributes to the development of reliable swarm robotics systems, which can function effectively in real-world settings.

This paper proposes a periodic event-triggered control strategy for nonlinear networked control systems (NCSs) and analyzes the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. The stability criteria are derived based on Lyapunov methods and the properties of networked generators, which can enhance the stability of the system while reducing the frequency of communication among nodes. Nonlinear systems and control systems are both considered in this study. The proposed control method can effectively reduce the communication burden and improve the stability of NCSs. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of stability and communication cost. This research provides a promising direction for designing efficient control algorithms for NCSs.

This paper proposes a Full-Duplex Cell-Free Massive MIMO system, which can operate in both uplink and downlink simultaneously. The system utilizes a large number of receiving antennas in each cell without the need for dedicated base stations. The key challenges in this system include accurate channel estimation and mitigating interference. To address these challenges, the proposed system uses a training phase to estimate the channel characteristics and employs a beamforming technique to minimize interference. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated and compared to a traditional cellular Massive MIMO system. The results show that the Full-Duplex Cell-Free Massive MIMO system can significantly improve the spectral efficiency and achieve better interference management. This research provides a novel approach to enhance the communication system and can be applied in various scenarios such as 5G wireless networks and Internet of Things (IoT) systems.

Wireless power transfer and energy harvesting are promising technologies in the field of wireless communication and radio frequency systems. With the increasing demand for wireless sensor networks and other battery-powered devices, the need for efficient and reliable power supplies is more important than ever. Energy harvesting has emerged as a potential solution to overcome the limitations of battery technology by generating energy from ambient sources such as light, vibrations or heat. Among the various energy harvesting technologies, wireless power transfer using coils has shown great potential with its ability to transfer power over a distance without physical contact. In this paper, we review the current status and future prospects of wireless power transfer and energy harvesting technologies with a focus on their applications in wireless communication and radio frequency systems. We also discuss the challenges and opportunities for these technologies in practical deployment scenarios.

Power consumption and network lifetime optimization is an essential performance objective for the IoT networks. Since the devices in this type of networks are mostly battery powered with a limited battery life, energy saving strategies becomes vital for such systems operation. Typically, the standard sleep mode of the 802.15.4 protocol is used in order to reduce the power usage of the sensors in an IoT network. However, enabling the sleep mode function in an IoT device that utilizes the Named Data Networking (NDN) paradigm is challenging. In this paper, we propose a power saving extension for the Geographic Interest Forwarding (GIF) protocol. In the proposed E-GIF scheme, a cross-layer approach is used, which allows direct communication between protocols at nonadjacent layers. More precisely, the interactions between the MAC and the Routing layers are fully exploited in order to integrate the sleep mode into the forwarding decision of the sensor nodes that uses the NDN protocol stack. To validate the proposed scheme, we extend the ndnSIM simulator to support wireless multihop communication. Simulation experiments confirm the viability and the effectiveness of the proposal.

The widespread adoption of service computing allows software to be developed by outsourcing open cloud services (i.e., SOAP-based or RESTful Web APIs) through mashup or service composition techniques. Fault tolerance for the purpose of assuring the stable execution for cloud-based software (or CBS) application has attracted great attention in coping with a loosely coupled CBS operating under dynamic and uncertain running environments. It is too expensive to rent massively redundant cloud services for CBS fault tolerance application. To reduce budget but guarantee the effectiveness of CBS fault tolerance, identifying critical components within a CBS composite system is of significant importance. We integrate CBS composite system architecture analysis and reliability sensitivity analysis approaches and propose an Architecture-based Reliability-sensitive Criticality Measure (or ARCMeas) method in this paper. We verify ARCMeas application through a cost-effective fault tolerance CBS by presenting a particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based cost-effective fault tolerance strategy determination (or PSO-CFTD) algorithm. Experimental results suggest the effectiveness of the approach.

Wireless sensor networks are widely used in various applications such as environmental monitoring, industrial control, and healthcare. In order to process the queries from different applications, base stations play a critical role to collect and analyze the data from multiple sensors. However, due to the limited computing resources and wireless communication capabilities of sensors, the query processing becomes a challenging task. This paper focuses on the optimization of concurrent-query execution in wireless sensor networks, especially in the case of temperature sensors. Different techniques including task scheduling, energy management, and data aggregation are proposed to improve the performance of query processing. The experimental results show that the proposed optimization algorithms can effectively reduce the energy consumption and delay of query processing, which can prolong the lifetime of wireless sensor networks and improve the data delivery efficiency.

Soft robotics has become an emerging field of research due to the vast potential of highly adaptive and flexible machines. Pneumatic actuators are commonly used in the design of soft robots, which are able to mimic the movement of living organisms. In this paper, we propose a new class of antagonistic pneumatic actuators with variable stiffness for soft robotic applications. The variable stiffness is achieved through the use of bars and textiles that allow for the actuator to change its stiffness parameters dynamically. We present the fabrication process of these actuators and discuss their working principle. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of these antagonistic pneumatic actuators with variable stiffness in a soft robotic application where they provide a high force output without compromising on flexibility and adaptability. This work opens new avenues for the development of highly versatile and adaptable soft robotic systems for a wide range of applications.

Fast Adaptive Hinging Hyperplanes (FAHH) is a powerful mathematical model that is capable of building robust adaptation models. This method combines the advantages of splines and hinging hyperplanes in order to provide an optimized solution to the problem of adapting to new data models. The main advantage of FAHH is its ability to provide a precise prediction with a limited number of parameters, making it ideal for training models with complex data sets. The robustness of the method is further enhanced by the use of gold standard data sets, which are used to validate the predictions made by the model. By employing the FAHH algorithm, researchers and data scientists can achieve high levels of accuracy while minimizing the amount of computation required for training a model. Overall, the FAHH approach represents an important advance in the field of machine learning and is likely to play an important role in developing next-generation modeling techniques.

This paper proposes a scheme for updating the location of the sink node to balance the network topology when a wireless sensor network (WSN) is scaled up. We divide the proposed location update scheme into two steps, namely, searching the optimal location and designing the pathfinding algorithm. For the former, to find the optimal location of the sink node simply and efficiently, we only consider the information of the expanded longer paths and some key nodes instead of the global information of the entire network, which is easy to implement with a low-computational load. Then, considering the general unattended application scenario, we propose an improved reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm for the sink node to calculate a feasible efficient path, and then the sink node follows the path to reach the optimal location. Finally, through simulations, we demonstrate the optimal position of the sink node in expanded scenarios and successfully let the sink node learn the effective pathfinding method to reach the target position. A large number of simulation results verify the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed scheme from the perspective of the efficiency of the pathfinding algorithm.

Forced shutdowns are a major concern in Brazilian Type I hydropower plants, as they can lead to significant losses in both power generation and revenue. To address this issue, data mining techniques and logistic regression algorithms are used to analyze inspection data and build highly accurate data models. Regulators can use these predictive models to anticipate future forced shutdowns and take preventative measures. Moreover, the generators of these plants can also use these models to schedule timely maintenance and avoid costly shutdowns. Inspection data holds great importance in the development of predictive models, and the accuracy of the data is essential to ensure the reliability of the models. This research highlights the importance of data analysis and data modeling in predicting forced shutdowns, ultimately leading to improved efficiency and reduced losses in Type I hydropower plants in Brazil.

Drowsiness is a cause of accidents in industrial and mining activities. A considerable amount of effort has been put into the detection of drowsiness, and since then it has been integrated into a large variety of wearable systems. Nevertheless, the technology still suffers from high intrusiveness, short battery life and lack of generality. An opportunity to address these shortcomings arises from the use of physiological and behavioral features for bio-signals like EEG and IMU sensors. In this work, we propose an energy-efficient wearable platform for drowsiness detection. Our platform features a minimally invasive setup, based on dry EEG sensors to acquire neural data, and Mr. Wolf, an 8-core ultra-low-power digital platform. The system has been validated on three test subjects, achieving detection accuracy of 83%, using a Nearest Centroid Classifier, modeled with a semi-supervised algorithm from previously collected data. This work further extends the capabilities of our previous system, providing a more sophisticated classification mechanism that includes real-time and onboard sensor fusion processing while running into a highly efficient and unobtrusive hardware platform, outperforming the current State of the Art (SoA) in terms of wearability and battery lifetime.

This paper proposes a novel method that addresses the selection of the dominant patterns of the histograms of oriented gradients (DPHOGs) in vehicle detection. HOG features lead to an expensive classification with high misclassification rates since HOG generates a long vector containing both redundant and ambiguous features (similarities between the vehicle and non-vehicle images). Several modifications of HOG were proposed to resolve these issues such as the vertical histograms of oriented gradient and one that includes position and intensity with HOG; however, these methods still contain some ambiguous features. A feature selection method can exclude these ambiguous features, allowing for better classification rates and a reduction in classification times. The proposed method uses the ideal vectors of the vehicle and non-vehicles images for selecting features in dominant patterns. The segments indicating the differences between the vehicle and non-vehicle classes are the dominant patterns, in which the length of the feature vector is shortened. We performed DPHOG on three standard datasets, in which the kernel extreme learning machine, the support vector machine, K-nearest neighbor, random forest, and deep neural network were used as classifiers. We then compared the performance of the DPHOG with eight well-known feature selection methods and three existing feature extraction methods for vehicle detection. In evaluations with each comparative method concerning the accuracy, true positive, false positive, and F1-score, the DPHOG presented the highest performances with less running time in each dataset.

Learning robust representations for applications with multiple modalities of input can have a significant impact on its performance. Traditional representation learning methods rely on projecting the input modalities to a common subspace to maximize agreement amongst the modalities for a particular task. We propose a novel approach to representation learning that uses a latent representation decoder to reconstruct the target modality and thereby employs the target modality purely as a supervision signal for discovering correlations between the modalities. Through cross modality supervision, we demonstrate that the learnt representation is able to improve the performance of the task of facial action unit (AU) recognition when compared with the modality specific representations and even their fused counterparts. Our experiments on three AU recognition datasets - MMSE, BP4D and DISFA, show strong performance gains producing state-of-the-art results in spite of the absence of a modality.

Lack of annotated samples greatly restrains the direct application of deep learning in remote sensing image scene classification. Although research studies have been done to tackle this issue by data augmentation with various image transformation operations, they are still limited in quantity and diversity. Recently, the advent of the unsupervised learning-based generative adversarial networks (GANs) brings us a new way to generate augmented samples. However, such GAN-generated samples are currently only served for training GANs model itself and for improving the performance of the discriminator in GANs internally (in vivo). It becomes a question of serious doubt whether the GAN-generated samples can help better improve the scene classification performance of other deep learning networks (in vitro), compared with the widely used transformed samples. To answer this question, this letter proposes a SiftingGAN approach to generate more numerous, more diverse, and more authentic labeled samples for data augmentation. SiftingGAN extends traditional GAN framework with an Online-Output method for sample generation, a Generative-Model-Sifting method for model sifting, and a Labeled-Sample-Discriminating method for sample sifting. Experiments on the well-known aerial image data set demonstrate that the proposed SiftingGAN method can not only effectively improve the performance of the scene classification baseline that is achieved without data augmentation but also significantly excels the comparison methods based on traditional geometric/radiometric transformation operations.

The article is devoted to the discussion of the problems of development of predictive neural network models based on the residual number system and the use of modular arithmetic to improve the quality of automatic control systems by adding to the control algorithms a prognostic component, which is especially important for astatic control objects. The possibility of implementing neural network training algorithms in the residual number system is shown, which allows to significantly accelerate the work of these algorithms, which is especially important when adding new functionality to automatic control systems in the form of prognostic neural network models.

In this paper, a method of determining examinations is proposed for ophthalmologic outpatients, using feedforward neural network (NN for short). The determination is based on the data classification. The proposed method defines four classes of ophthalmologic examinations. It prepares data for NN training and examination determination from handwriting sentences in outpatients' interview sheets. A set of the training data is prepared in the form of a matrix. The words extracted from the sentences are assigned to the matrix columns, while each sheet (or sentences in it) is assigned to a matrix rows. Entries in the matrix takes binary values meaning whether extracted words appear in the sentences in the sheet. The proposed method also the ages of outpatients as entries. NN training is conducted according to the normal backpropagation algorithm using a row as one of the training data. The trained NN has four output neurons each of which takes the value belonging to the range [0, 1]. The class of data to be examined is determined by searching the neuron at which the largest value appears in the output layer. Experimental results comprehensively establish that the proposed method can achieve higher percentages of concordance than other methods.

The development of 5G and beyond has led to the creation of mobile HetNets that incorporate a variety of computing resources, including servers, cloud computing, computational modeling and edge computing. Effective resource management is necessary to ensure the efficient utilization of these resources, which are critical to enabling the full potential of B5G. Computer architecture plays a key role in the design and implementation of mobile HetNets, and the use of intelligent architecture can greatly improve their performance. Data models and machine learning are also important tools for optimizing resource management and ensuring that mobile HetNets operate at peak efficiency. This paper explores the use of intelligent architecture in mobile HetNets, specifically exploring the role of cloud computing, edge computing, and computational modeling. It discusses the challenges associated with resource management in mobile HetNets and presents strategies for addressing these challenges using data modeling and machine learning techniques. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion of the potential of intelligent architecture for B5G networks, highlighting the potential gains in efficiency, performance, and cost savings that can be achieved through its use.

This paper introduces GuidedNet, an end-to-end convolutional neural network for single image dehazing. The proposed approach is based on atmospheric modeling and utilizes neural networks for image restoration. The network architecture includes both a guidance network and a dehazing network, which work together to remove the scattering and degradation caused by atmospheric haze. To train the model, a large dataset of hazy and clear images is used. The effectiveness of GuidedNet is demonstrated through experiments on various benchmark datasets, where it achieves state-of-the-art performance. Overall, this work provides a robust and efficient solution for single image dehazing using deep learning techniques.

This paper proposes a profit-sensitive spatial scheduling algorithm for multi-application tasks in distributed green clouds. Task analysis reveals the characteristics of different applications, and the scheduling algorithm takes the green products and energy-efficient computing resources of data centers into consideration. It schedules tasks among servers to minimize energy consumption and maximize profit, while maintaining the quality of service requirements of the applications. Cloud computing and smart grids are used to provide reliable and efficient energy supply for the data centers. The algorithm is based on job shop scheduling and takes into account the dynamic workload and uncertainty of energy supply. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of energy efficiency, profit, and quality of service. The profit-sensitive spatial scheduling algorithm provides a promising solution for sustainable and economically viable cloud computing.

This paper proposes a optimal method for designing frequency-invariant beamformers for circular arrays. First, the desired beampattern is expressed as a general complex-weighted form. Second, the weighting vectors at each frequency are accurately derived by approximating to the desired beampattern from the minimum mean square error perspective, all of which are found to be close-form functions of the desired complex weighting vectors. Third, a multiple optimization problem is formulated, and its solution gives the optimal desired weighting vector subject to different constraints. Finally, the weighting vectors at other frequencies can be directly computed based on the previously derived analytical functions. The proposed method provides flexible schemes to design different optimal frequency-invariant beamformers for circular sensor arrays. The good performance of the proposed method is demonstrated using simulations and experimental results.

This paper proposes a new lazy eviction algorithm, called LEA, for the management of solid-state drive (SSD) cache in cloud block storage. Cloud computing and data centers continue to grow in scale and complexity, leading to a demand for optimized production technology that can effectively manage the ever-increasing amount of data. The proposed LEA algorithm is designed to mitigate the performance overhead associated with traditional eviction techniques, by lazily evicting data from the cache only when it is absolutely necessary. This approach leverages the characteristics of SSDs, which perform well when reading data from cache, but suffer performance degradation when constantly writing to the same page. To validate the effectiveness of our algorithm, we implemented it on a server architecture and evaluated its performance against other state-of-the-art eviction techniques. The results show that LEA outperforms other algorithms in terms of cache hit ratio and write throughput. This work is expected to have significant impact on system-on-chip design, computer aided software engineering, and related conferences.
