The proposed method involves training a network using a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and recurrent neural networks (RNN) with the long short-term memory (LSTM) module for feature extraction and estimation. The obtained results show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and execution speed. The paper also discusses the application of this method to various scenarios using different types of cameras. This research provides important contributions to the field of crowd analysis and can be a valuable resource for future conferences and research in this area.

This paper presents a novel architecture utilizing iBeacons for localization and tracking of people within healthcare environments. The proposed system enhances medical services by providing real-time monitoring of patients and medical personnel. The architecture is supported by servers and uses wireless fidelity technology for reliable connectivity. The estimation of the location of individuals is achieved through sensors integrated into the iBeacons, allowing for accurate and efficient tracking. The system has potential for a wide range of applications, including real-time monitoring of patients, staff location tracking, and workflow optimization. The use of iBeacons within healthcare environments has the potential to greatly improve patient care, workflow efficiency, and medical research. Future work includes the implementation and testing of the architecture to validate its effectiveness and reliability.

Reinforcement Learning has achieved a great success in recent decades when applying to the fields such as finance, robotics, and multi-agent games. A variety of traditional manual tasks are facing upgrading, and reinforcement learning opens the door to a whole new world for improving these tasks. In this paper, we focus on the task called Cavity Filter Tuning, a traditionally manual work in communication industries which not only consumes time, but also highly depends on human knowledge. We present a framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient for automatically tuning cavity filters, and design appropriate reward functions inspired by human expertise in the tuning task. Simulation experiments are conducted to validate the applicability of our algorithm. Our proposed method is able to autonomously tune a detuned filter to meet the design specifications from any random starting positions.

This paper proposes a Region Proposal Network (RPN) with Contextual Selective Attention for Real-time Organ Detection. The focus of the study is to explore the effectiveness of using proposals for biomedical imaging, specifically in the context of lung detection. The proposed approach includes protocols for feature extraction and training, and employs a Contextual Selective Attention mechanism to enhance the RPN's detection accuracy. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieved significant improvements in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to the traditional RPN approach.

We investigate the capacity of reservoir computers to reconstruct the dynamics of a network of chaotic oscillators via the observation of its multivariate time series. The reservoir is itself a structured echo-state network which receives the current observations as inputs, and is trained to produce the next observations as outputs. We study the performance of this scheme and its dependence on the separation of the inputs, modularity of the reservoir network, and observability of the system. We observe optimal performance with a segregated input structure and extremely modular network.

With increasing interest in e-commerce and online shopping recently, customer reviews are one of the most important elements that determine the satisfaction of customers about the products. Also, it gives a comprehensive picture of products to business owners. Hence, the aim of this paper is to conduct a sentimental analysis approach on a set of customer reviews collected from Amazon. As will, classify each review into one of these class: positive review or negative review by using ensemble machine learning method. The ensemble machine learning method used in this research is Voting which combined five classifiers: Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), Random forest, Bagging and Boosting. All the Experiment in this paper done using Weka. We test six different scenarios to evaluate our proposed model against the five classifiers. The scenarios are using unigram (with/without) stop of word removal, using bigram (with/without) stop of word removal and using trigram (with/without) stop of word removal. The result shows the random forest technique give the highest accuracy which equals to 89.87% in the case of using unigram and with a stop of word removal but voting algorithm shows the best performance on the other scenarios.

Due to the increase of complexity in the flow of a customized order in the production process, it is necessary to develop new software models to automate complex modular systems and integrate digital technologies to merge the real factory with its digital shadow in a standardized coordinate system. This paper describes a software control following the characteristics of the ultra-flexible production systems using a modular robot and its digital model as a prototype. The final result shows that the robot, seen as a module of the factory, can be modeled, modified and manipulated along with its digital model in an intuitive and user-friendly way through an interface using a game engine.

In order to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of video coding, researchers have developed a DenseNet-based approach for multi-frame in-loop filter in HEVC. This approach combines the concepts of radio frequency, motion compensation, and feature extraction to produce high-quality video coding results. The system leverages the latest training methodologies and encoding standards to ensure optimal performance. The approach involves the use of dense connections to improve feature reuse and reduce vanishing gradients. The proposed approach has been tested on several datasets and shown to outperform traditional approaches in terms of both quality and efficiency. The results demonstrate that this DenseNet-based approach for multi-frame in-loop filter in HEVC is a promising technique for improving video coding and enhancing the broadcasting or communication of information in various applications.

Herein, a novel algorithm is proposed for strain estimation in free-hand palpation quasi-static ultrasound elastography. In all previously proposed methods for strain estimation, post-beam-formed ultrasound Radio-Frequency (RF) data have been utilized. However, we propose to exploit pre-beam-formed RF data (often called channel data) for displacement estimation in ultrasound elastography in this paper. Our novel technique builds on our recently proposed GLobal Ultrasound Elastography (GLUE) method, a regularized optimization-based approach for displacement estimation. Here, we propose Channel data based GLUE (CGLUE), which uses channel data instead of the post-beam-formed RF data. Phantom experiments show that considering channel data improves the displacement estimation results substantially.

This study proposes a real-time car detection-based depth estimation method using a mono camera for automobiles. The proposed method employs a mathematical model for the estimation process, which is implemented through microelectronics technology. The real-time systems in the automobile are designed using MONOS devices, which enable the camera to capture and process the images efficiently. The camera is used as the primary input sensor for the method, providing accurate and real-time data for the depth estimation process. Overall, the proposed approach presents a promising solution for depth estimation in automobiles, offering robust and reliable results that can be utilized across a broad range of automotive applications.

This paper focuses on the calibration procedure for mounting angle of an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) used in a Pipeline Surveying Apparatus during inspection of pipelines. The calibration method involves estimating the mounting angle of the IMU on the apparatus, which is a critical parameter for accurate measurement of pipeline characteristics. The authors propose a mathematical model to estimate the mounting angle based on the measurements obtained from the Global Navigation Satellite System. The proposed calibration method is verified through experiments conducted on a prototype of the Pipeline Surveying Apparatus. The results indicate that the proposed method is efficient and accurate in calibration of the IMU mounting angle, which enhances the precision of pipeline inspection conducted through this apparatus. The study contributes to the inspection of pipelines, which is critical for maintaining efficient and reliable transportation of fluids, gases, and other materials.

Proper health-care delivery in the rural area is one of the biggest challenge faced by the health professionals and the government. Majority of the Indian residents live in the rural areas where the condition of medical facilities is deplorable. It is understood that, there is a dire need of new practices and procedures to ensure that quality and timely health care resources reach the deprived corners of the Indian villages. We have developed a modular, easy re-configurable, touch screen based remote health care application for delivering primary health care in an efficient manner in the rural areas, where even the minimal health care facilities are not available. The application can capture patients symptoms using a knowledge base provided by the Doctors and send the symptoms and other important information to the Doctors over the Internet. As the application is running in the rural areas, it is often found that the Internet connectivity is a problem. Thus, we use short message services to send the patients' vital. This paper describes the different steps which are taken to connect the rural patients with urban located doctors using SMS. The paper provides evidence that even when the Internet connectivity is not available in the villages, it is still possible to actively use our e-healthcare service for treatment of the rural patients.

In social networks, several influential individuals can promote an idea or a product to numerous individuals. Thus, it is valuable to solve the influence maximization (IM) problem, which asks for finding the most influential set of individuals in a social network. To estimate the influence of individuals, the existing independent cascade (IC) model simulates the influence diffusion only considering the influences from direct in-neighbors to nodes. This consideration does not hold in real life. In many cases, people are likely influenced by information depending on where it comes from, instead of who gives it. To simulate the influence diffusion more accurate, this paper proposes the second-order IC model, which takes the previous influence into consideration. In addition, we design an approximate algorithm and its distributed extension for IM under the second-order IC model. Experimental results show that our second-order IC model outperforms the IC model in terms of simulating influence diffusions. The proposed algorithms are efficient, and the obtained node sets are influential.

Combination of color and texture features along with adaptive boosting classifier is proposed in this paper for attributes identification of the pedestrian images. Color histogram and Multi Block Local Binary Pattern (MB-LBP) is used as a feature extraction method, since both methods do not require the same size of pedestrian images. This is suitable with the dataset that is trained and tested in this research, PETA dataset since this dataset has various size, a point of view, resolution, etc. Color histogram and MB-LBP capture two kinds of information in the pedestrian images, i.e., color and texture information. The Adaboost is used as a classifier for the attribute identification, and for the weak classifier, the decision stump is applied. The performance accuracy of texture, color, and the combination of both features, are compared in the attribute identification process. In the conducted experiments, the number of bins for the color histogram, and MBLBP are 8, 16, and 32. The results showed that the combination of both features, color histogram and MB-LBP, achieved the highest accuracy.

Mobile applications are increasingly becoming an essential part of the daily lives of millions of people. These applications are smaller in size but demand high usability interfaces so that users can interact with them. A user-friendly and highly interactive Mobile User Interface (MUI) plays a central role in successful market of a mobile application. Previously, many studies have been conducted about the design, methodologies and tools for MUI. However, up till now no research has been performed to the best of our knowledge that analyzes and summarizes the latest methods and tools in the context of MUI development. Therefore, in this paper, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) is carried out to analyze 30 researches (2014-2018) in the domain of mobile user interface development. We identify 16 techniques and 12 tools. Subsequently, comparative analysis of leading techniques and tools is performed. We conclude that MobiGUITAR and MDA SMARTAPP are the leading tools for MUI development. The results and outcomes of this research are going to prove to be greatly helpful for the researchers and practitioners to adopt best practices in MUI domain.

Measurement processes which structural uncertainties are due to missing data, missed information in measurements, etc. are considered. A new algorithm for estimating the parameters of measurement processes is built on the basis of a structurally-adaptive model with dynamic properties which are due to the correspondence to the Hamilton-Ostrogradsky principle. The intellectual properties of the estimation appear in the adaptation of the dynamics of an evolutionary model to the dynamics of the occurring measurement processes. Mathematical modeling shows that their use makes it possible to reduce the errors in the estimation of dynamic processes compare to the “alpha-beta” filter under conditions of missing data by an average of 12%.

This paper presents a set-based inverse kinematics (IK) control of an Underwater Vehicle Manipulator System (UVMS) within the DexROV project. The task analysis and kinematics of the UVMS are first described. The Jacobian matrices are then calculated to determine the relationship between the velocity of the end effectors of the manipulator and the joint velocities. Computational modeling of the system is developed to simulate the robot arm motion and validate the proposed IK control. The trajectory of the end effector is planned with the help of the inverse Jacobian matrix. The proposed set-based IK control strategy improves the control performance and reduces the computational cost for the UVMS in underwater environments. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can accurately control the motion of the UVMS with a satisfying tracking performance. This work provides a practical solution for controlling the end effectors of a UVMS in the DexROV project.

The optimization of a 1.5-GHz two-cell SRF cavity is an important topic in the field of particle acceleration. The resonant frequency of the cavity is a critical parameter that affects the acceleration performance. In this paper, we discuss the use of computational modeling and finite element analysis to optimize the geometry of the cavity resonators. By adjusting the shape and dimensions of the cavity, we were able to improve the resonant frequency and overall performance of the cavity. Our results showed that the optimized cavity design achieved higher acceleration efficiency and reduced radio frequency losses. This study highlights the importance of using advanced computational tools to optimize the geometry of cavity resonators, which can lead to significant improvements in the performance of particle accelerators.

Cervical dysplasia is a precancerous condition that frequently progresses to cervical cancer. Early diagnosis and treatment of cervical dysplasia are crucial steps to prevent cervical cancer. In this study, we propose a multi-modal fusion learning approach for cervical dysplasia diagnosis. Firstly, we perform feature extraction from cervical images using iodine staining technology. Then, we train an artificial intelligence model to classify cervical images into dysplasia or non-dysplasia categories. The feature extraction and training process are performed separately for each modality. Finally, we fuse the results of different modalities to improve the overall diagnostic accuracy. Our experimental results suggest that the proposed multi-modal fusion learning approach can achieve significant improvement in cervical dysplasia diagnosis by capturing the correlations between different modalities. The proposed approach has the potential to be applied in clinical practice to enhance the early detection and diagnosis of cervical dysplasia.

The learning process is complex and requires careful consideration to ensure effective results. To enhance the learning experience, recommendations must be provided while influencing interests. This paper focuses on optimization of learning recommendations through computational modeling and adaptation models. Stochastic processes are used in collaboration with history to support the generation of personalized recommendations for learners. The collaboration of various domains, including publishing, further supports the development and implementation of effective learning recommendations. Overall, this paper emphasizes the importance of personalized learning recommendations and proposes a framework for the optimization of the process.

Multiple kernel clustering (MKC) has been intensively studied during the last few decades. Even though they demonstrate promising clustering performance in various applications, existing MKC algorithms do not sufficiently consider the intrinsic neighborhood structure among base kernels, which could adversely affect the clustering performance. In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective neighbor-kernel-based MKC algorithm to address this issue. Specifically, we first define a neighbor kernel, which can be utilized to preserve the block diagonal structure and strengthen the robustness against noise and outliers among base kernels. After that, we linearly combine these base neighbor kernels to extract a consensus affinity matrix through an exact-rank-constrained subspace segmentation. The naturally possessed block diagonal structure of neighbor kernels better serves the subsequent subspace segmentation, and in turn, the extracted shared structure is further refined through subspace segmentation based on the combined neighbor kernels. In this manner, the above two learning processes can be seamlessly coupled and negotiate with each other to achieve better clustering. Furthermore, we carefully design an efficient iterative optimization algorithm with proven convergence to address the resultant optimization problem. As a by-product, we reveal an interesting insight into the exact-rank constraint in ridge regression by careful theoretical analysis: it back-projects the solution of the unconstrained counterpart to its principal components. Comprehensive experiments have been conducted on several benchmark data sets, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Multicenter imaging studies have become increasingly popular in recent years due to their potential to identify biomarkers and patterns of disease across a range of patient populations. However, one of the biggest challenges in these studies is the evaluation of data variability, which can be caused by a range of factors such as differences in imaging protocols or patient populations. To address this challenge, researchers have developed an automated approach to feature extraction and anomaly detection using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. This approach uses techniques such as principal component analysis and two-dimensional displays to identify patterns of data variability and outliers in the data. By identifying and removing outliers, researchers can increase the reliability and validity of their findings. This research has implications for a range of fields including sociology, where automated approaches to data collection and analysis are increasingly being used to identify trends and patterns in human behavior.

While non-contact respiration monitoring using microwave Doppler radar has shown great promises over the last four decades, the isolation of one subject when multiple subjects are in view remains a challenge. In this paper, we employed anew, cost effective and scalable approach for estimating Direction of Arrival (DOA) to separate well-spaced multiple subjects by introducing a 24-GHz phase comparison monopulse radar in our system. Experimental results demonstrated that phase comparison technique can separate two subjects 1.5 meters apart from each other at a distance of 3 meters from the sensor and it can estimate the angular position of single subject with respect to the radar. It also illustrates that the phase-comparison technique is computationally faster and requires fewer snapshots or samples than the well-established MUSIC algorithm. Our experimental results also demonstrate that the monopulse technique for multiple subject measurement has estimation accuracy of almost 80%. This paper demonstrates the efficacy of using a phase-comparison monopulse technique to separate well-spaced subjects based on estimation of the angle of physiological signals, which will lead to practical adoption of this technology in our daily life.

Wireless sensor networks have many applications in various fields such as environmental monitoring, healthcare, and industrial automation. Clustering is an effective technique to reduce overhead in data communication and improve energy efficiency in such networks. This paper proposes a concentric layered architecture for multi-level clustering in large-scale wireless sensor networks. The architecture includes protocols for routing and data communication, as well as optimization techniques to improve energy efficiency. The proposed architecture uses different levels of clustering, with each level consisting of a base station and multiple cluster heads. The clusters are formed based on the location of the nodes and the energy level of the batteries. Simulations have shown that the proposed architecture is effective in reducing the energy consumption and prolonging the network lifetime.

In this paper, we construct two tests for the weights of the global minimum variance portfolio (GMVP) in a high-dimensional setting, namely, when the number of assets p depends on the sample size n such that p/n → c ∈ (0, 1) as n tends to infinity. In the case of a singular covariance matrix with rank equal to q we assume that q/n → c̅ ∈ (0, 1) as n → ∞. The considered tests are based on the sample estimator and on the shrinkage estimator of the GMVP weights. We derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistics under the null and alternative hypotheses. Moreover, we provide a simulation study where the power functions and the receiver operating characteristic curves of the proposed tests are compared with other existing approaches. We observe that the test based on the shrinkage estimator performs well even for values of c close to one.

This paper presents a three-stage method for monitoring the health condition of rotating machines using vibration signals. The proposed method involves feature extraction from the vibration signals, which are then used in condition monitoring. The method utilizes sparse matrices and support vector machines to identify and classify different types of faults in rotating machines. The use of the proposed method in fault detection significantly improves the performance of conventional condition monitoring methods. The findings of the study show that the proposed method can effectively monitor the health condition of rotating machines, and it provides valuable insights for maintenance of these machines. Overall, this paper contributes to the advancement of rotating machine health monitoring techniques, and it can be useful in various applications related to the maintenance of rotating machines.

In recent years, saliency detection has received increasing attention due to its crucial role in numerous visual perception tasks. This paper proposes a novel approach for video saliency detection via sparsity-based reconstruction and propagation. The method leverages spatiotemporal phenomena and employs optimization techniques to perform image reconstruction and propagate saliency information between frames. Computational modeling is utilized to capture the feature extraction process, which extracts distinct features from video sequences. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison to state-of-the-art algorithms, achieving high precision and recall rates. The proposed framework represents a promising direction for video saliency detection and could have practical applications in various domains, such as surveillance and video editing.

This paper proposes a Recursive Access Class Barring (RACB) scheme specifically designed for Machine Type Communications (MTCs) operating under physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) resource constraints. The scheme is based on feedback estimation of uplink throughput and dynamically adjusts access control to achieve optimal performance under changing network conditions. The proposed RACB scheme is evaluated through extensive computer simulations and shown to outperform traditional access control schemes in terms of delay and network throughput for MTC applications. The proposed scheme is particularly useful for Long Term Evolution (LTE) based MTC networks with limited radio resources and high data traffic demands.

In this paper, we propose a new intelligent glaucoma diagnosis system that utilizes active learning and adversarial data augmentation to improve accuracy in glaucoma detection. Our approach involves training on a diverse set of data models that utilize neural networks to identify key features in patient data. Through visualization, we aim to decode the factors that allow for accurate diagnoses, and utilize generators to synthesize additional data for training. By employing these techniques, we hope to improve the quality of medical services provided to glaucoma patients and ultimately reduce the risk of vision loss associated with this condition.

Sports video analysis has received increasing attention in recent years. Athlete tracking and action recognition are its two major issues that are highly related to each other; however, they are individually considered and processed in the existing studies. In this paper, we propose a joint framework for athlete tracking and action recognition in sports videos. In athlete tracking, we propose a scaling and occlusion robust tracker, named scaling and occlusion robust compressive tracking (CT), to localize the position of specific athlete in each frame. It follows the approach of CT but extends it in two aspects, i.e., scale refinement as well as occlusion recovery. For the former, an objectness method, edge box, is adopted to generate proposals, which replace the fixed sampling boxes in CT and better fit the scales of the candidate objects. For the latter, a candidate obstruction-based solution is presented, which brings in additional trackers to detect possible obstructions and to relocate the target as occlusion ends. Regarding action recognition, we propose a long-term recurrent region-guided convolutional network, which recognizes pre-defined actions by modeling discriminative temporal cues of the tracking results. We employ SPP-net to extract the robust feature of the tracked region of each frame. The features of all the frames are then fed into a stack of recurrent sequence models to capture the long-term region-level information. We extensively evaluate the proposed approach on a newly collected sports video benchmark and on the off-the-shelf UIUC2 dataset, and the experimental results clearly show its effectiveness.

This paper focuses on improving the throughput of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) by implementing Network MIMO with Interference Cancellation utilizing cloud cooperation. Interference cancellation is a crucial aspect in this technique, which helps to minimize the impact of interferences caused by other devices in the network. One of the challenges in WSNs is the limited capacity and ability to handle a large number of nodes. To address this issue, silicon carbide is a potential candidate to enhance performance due to its high thermal conductivity and voltage capabilities. Moreover, MIMO communication can be utilized to improve the capacity of the network while throughput can be increased by selecting suitable protocols. This paper proposes a novel approach using cloud-cooperated WSNs with Network MIMO and interference cancellation techniques to improve the system performance in terms of throughput. Overall, these approaches show great potential in improving the efficiency and reliability of WSNs.

Multi-vector network attacks have become an increasingly common and significant threat to computer networks, and they pose a serious challenge to existing security systems based on protocols, firewalls, access control, and underlying IP networks. In this paper, we propose a new approach for mitigating multi-vector network attacks utilizing the orchestration of distributed rule placement. Our approach leverages the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of network substrates to distribute protection rules across multiple network segments, thereby improving the overall resilience of the network. Specifically, we present an algorithm for identifying the optimal placement of rules based on the attack vector and network topology. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly enhance network security and reduce the impact of multi-vector attacks. We believe that this work can provide a valuable contribution towards the development of more effective and scalable security solutions for mitigating the ever-growing threat of computer crime.

To address the drastic growth of data traffic dominated by streaming of video-on-demand files, mobile edge caching/computing (MEC) can be exploited to develop intelligent content caching at mobile network edges to alleviate redundant traffic and improve content delivery efficiency. Under the MEC architecture, content providers (CPs) can deploy popular video files at MEC servers to improve users’ quality of experience (QoE). Designing an efficient content caching policy is crucial for CPs due to the content dynamics, unknown spatial-temporal traffic demands, and limited service capacity. The knowledge of users’ preference is very useful and important for efficient content caching, yet often unavailable in advance. Under this circumstance, machine learning can be used to learn the users’ preference based on historical demand information and decide the video files to be cached at the MEC servers. In this paper, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based cooperative content caching policy for the MEC architecture when the users’ preference is unknown and only the historical content demands can be observed. We formulate the cooperative content caching problem as a multi-agent multi-armed bandit problem and propose a MARL-based algorithm to solve the problem. The simulation experiments are conducted based on a real dataset from MovieLens and the numerical results show that the proposed MARL-based cooperative content caching scheme can significantly reduce content downloading latency and improve content cache hit rate when compared with other popular caching schemes.

The objective of this letter is to analyze the stability properties, the training procedure and the use in predictive control schemes of echo state networks (ESNs), a specific class of recurrent neural networks. First, a sufficient condition guaranteeing incremental input-to-state stability (δ ISS) of ESNs is derived. Then, an automatic procedure to optimally tune the parameters of the ESN in the training phase is presented, which allows to enforce δ ISS. Finally, the application of the ESN as a model of the plant for predictive control purposes is studied. In particular, an asymptotically convergent observer is designed, and a model predictive controller with guaranteed stabilizing properties is devised for the solution to regulation problems. Simulation results on a nonlinear process for pH neutralization confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

Getting closed-form inverse dynamics solution for a manipulating robot is desirable for real-time torque computation. Some powerful and well-established mechanics based tools like Newton Euler method (N-E), Lagrangian methods are available for developing a mathematical model for manipulating robots. However, the coupled equation being highly non-linear and incomplete (joint friction, dimensional inaccuracies arising due to manufacturing error are very difficult to model) and hence difficult to apply in real life situation which requires accurate joint torque computation. We believe learning based machine intelligence tools can more efficiently and appropriately be utilized for joint torque computations in the inverse dynamics paradigm. In this paper, K-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm has been proposed for finding joint torques from the dataset created by solving forward dynamics equation for the manipulating robots, which is comparatively straight forward and rather less complex. However, since computational complexity of KNN is high, we used K-dimensional tree (K-D tree) for decreasing the computational complexity. The simulation result for two-link manipulator shows the proposed method of KNN based joint torque calculation coupled with K-D tree is simple, robust and accurate, which can be emulated for a further higher degrees of freedom robot having six links.

This paper presents the design and implementation of a carrier landing runway simulation system that utilizes computational modeling, atmospheric modeling, and aerospace electronics. The system is designed to provide realistic training opportunities for aircraft pilots and utilizes optical sensors and motion measurement techniques to accurately represent the landing experience. The use of computational modeling and atmospheric modeling helps to mimic real-world conditions and ensure that the training results in a high level of proficiency. The implementation of the system is comprehensive, and includes a range of technologies including optical sensors, motion measurement, and aerospace electronics. The system has the potential to greatly enhance training opportunities for pilots, offering a safe and realistic simulation experience that can support the rapid development of skills.

Edge computing (EC) has quickly ascended to be the de-facto standard for hosting emerging low-latency applications, as exemplified by intelligent video surveillance, Internet of Vehicles, and augmented reality. For EC, service function chaining is envisioned as a promising approach to configure various services in an agile, flexible, and cost-efficient manner. When running on top of geographically dispersed edge clouds, fully unleashing the benefits of service function chaining is, however, by no means trivial. In this paper, we propose an online orchestration framework for cross-edge service function chaining, which aims to maximize the holistic cost efficiency, via jointly optimizing the resource provisioning and traffic routing on-the-fly. This long-term cost minimization problem is difficult since it is NP-hard and involves future uncertain information. To simultaneously address these dual challenges, we carefully combine an online optimization technique with an approximate optimization method in a joint optimization framework, through: 1) decomposing the long-term problem into a series of one-shot fractional problem with a regularization technique and 2) rounding the fractional solution to a near-optimal integral solution with a randomized dependent scheme that preserves the solution feasibility. The resulting online algorithm achieves an outstanding performance guarantee, as verified by both rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive trace-driven simulations.

The problem of filtering multiple extended targets in the presence of clutter arises in various applications such as target tracking, radar and radio frequency (RF) sensing. In this paper, we propose a Poisson Multi-Bernoulli Mixture Conjugate Prior for multiple extended target filtering. The proposed approach aims to provide improved performance for tracking multiple extended targets over existing filter models. Our approach is based on a Bayesian framework that models the target detections as a cluster of point processes, which is then used to estimate the target states. Furthermore, we evaluate our approach on various datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in terms of time measurement, computational modeling, and density measurement. The results show that our approach provides superior performance compared to existing standards for multiple extended target filtering. In summary, this study proposes a novel method that offers a significant improvement in filtering multiple extended targets over existing models, making it suitable for various target tracking applications.

Street cars in the 3D games could journey through the streets by look at the map. Other driving games have been used for entertainment and training, but our goal is making players to know about tourist attractions, religion places of city and famous people such as Seyyed Hassan Modarres, Seyyed Morteza and ect, based on realistic map in the city of Torshiz (old name of Kashmar). We used maya software, unity software combined with c# language and google map for create structure of city. During the game players are able to get information about of public places, religion places, structure and culture of city and increase their knowledge. The results show that 85% of players who played with game are satisfied. In addition to users to play and enjoy virtual world, they can get information about of historical places, popular persons, structure of city and use them in the real world.

This paper presents an analysis of vehicle handling through the use of a simple track model of an automobile. The mathematical model developed in this study takes into account the behavior of the tires, which play a crucial role in determining the stability and dynamics of the vehicle. Computational modeling techniques were employed to investigate the behavior of the vehicle under different driving scenarios, and stability analysis was used to assess the performance of the analytical models developed. In addition, control systems were implemented to optimize vehicle handling and improve driving performance. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the dynamics of vehicle handling and identifies ways in which control systems can be designed to enhance the driving experience.

Resource allocation for sustainable wireless IoT networks with energy harvesting is a significant challenge in order to address the rapidly increasing demand for energy-efficient devices. In this paper, we focus on developing a resource allocation method for wireless IoT networks that can sustainably operate with energy harvesting. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach for object recognition using the skeleton-based convolution neural network. The proposed approach uses the two-dimensional display to represent the skeleton of the object, and the convolutional neural network is designed to perform feature extraction. We train the convolutional neural network using the backpropagation algorithm for optimal performance. The proposed approach is validated through simulations, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in terms of accuracy and energy efficiency. Finally, we discuss the potential impact of our approach on the design of sustainable wireless IoT networks with energy harvesting.

The media news sources have increased dramatically. This brings to the service news credibility issue which emerges to become one of the most important issues concerning assessment of news items with respect to either the news editors' personnel or the readers of news items. We tried to measure news credibility via machine and introduce a novel approach via building NCMOSWS; a model that utilizes well founded weighing semantic methods as well as ontology to assess news credibility. We apply our model on the RSS of a set of news agencies and show that the model is highly reliable on measuring partial credibility of news items.

Data warehouses provide decision makers with the necessary tools to help them understand their data. The structural complexity of the data is maintained through multidimensional data views commonly called data cubes. Mining such data is still an open problem as few approaches really take the specificities of this framework into account (e.g. multidimensionality, hierarchies, measures). In this paper, we introduce a novel approach that post-mines generalized association rules by exploiting the dimension hierarchies that feature data warehouses. We define the concepts related to our problem as well as the associated algorithm. Carried out experiments show the significance of our approach.

The research on game simulation of smart taxis is an innovative approach to resource management in transportation. This study emphasizes the use of automobiles in object-oriented modeling of computational modeling software. The game theory is applied to simulate smart taxis based on the taxi industry's data and present a visual representation of taxi services. This study analyzes the dynamic interactions between taxis, passengers, and road networks in a simulated city environment. The outcomes of this research illustrate the effective use of smart taxis in managing urban transportation resources, and the user-friendly nature of the simulation software can improve taxi services in real life scenarios. The intersection of game theory, computational modeling, and object-oriented modeling tests the feasibility of using software simulations to improve urban transportation. The results indicate the usefulness of the game theory in simulating transportation systems and contributing to the optimization of urban transportation planning.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is in the midst of defining and developing the future space and ground architecture for the coming decades to return science and exploration discovery data back to investigators on Earth. Optimizing the data return from these missions requires planning, design, standards, and operations coordinated from formulation and development throughout the mission. The use of automation enhanced by cognition and machine learning are potential methods for optimizing data return, reducing costs of operations, and helping manage the complexity of the automated systems. In this article, we discuss the potential role of machine learning in the linkto- link aspect of the communication systems. An experiment using NASA's Space Communication and Navigation Testbed onboard the International Space Station and the ground station located at NASA John H. Glenn Research Center demonstrates for the first time the benefits and challenges of applying machine learning to space links in the actual flight environment. The experiment used machine learning decisions to configure a space link from the ISS-based testbed to the ground station to achieve multiple objectives related to data throughput, bandwidth, and power. Aspects of the specific neural-network-based reinforcement learning algorithm formation and on-orbit testing are discussed.

In this paper, we propose a low complexity hybrid view synthesis optimization method for 3D-HEVC. The aim of this research is to reduce distortion, encoding complexity, and estimation complexity while optimizing rendering in computer graphics. Our approach is based on complexity theory and optimization techniques. We analyze the complexity of the encoding and estimation process and propose a hybrid method that combines inter and intra-frame prediction to reduce encoding complexity. Additionally, we introduce a dynamic source search algorithm to reduce estimation complexity. Our method also includes image analysis techniques to optimize the rendering process. Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of distortion reduction and complexity reduction, while maintaining high-quality rendering. This research provides a promising solution for achieving low complexity and high-quality 3D-HEVC video coding and rendering.

Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) plays a vital role in facilitating the crop monitoring process through Crop Monitoring Network (CMN). Conversely, it is highly demanding task to execute the CMN in hugely distributed area. In order to create a communication between the sending nodes to the receiving node in a hugely distributed network naturally requires a multi-hop network. This kind of network constantly observes the crops without sensitivity categorization that can guide to communication collision and packets drop. Rebroadcasting of dropped packets will enhance the network delay and energy consumption. In order to improve the quality of service (QoS), we suggest a CMN model based on the sensitivity conditions. The crops with high sensitivity are monitored frequently and the crops with less sensitivity are monitored occasionally. In this approach, only few nodes are utilized rather than utilizing all the nodes in the network. This will drastically reduce the power consumption and network delay. The QoS of the classified-based approach is compared with non-classified based approach by considering the two scenarios - by changing the back-off period in first scenario and changing the number of nodes in second scenario.

When it comes to shared environments, where processes distributed in process nodes access critical shared resources in the mode of distributed mutual exclusion, it is important to know how they are managed and the order in which the demand for resources by the processes is resolved. In this work, through an aggregation operator, a consensus mechanism is proposed to establish the order in which resources are allocated to groups of processes. Consensus is understood as the agreement that must be reached for the allocation of all the resources requested by each group of processes. To model this consensus, it is necessary to take into account that the processes may form groups of processes or be independent, the state of the nodes where each of them is located, the computational load, the number of processes, the process priorities, the use of the CPU, the use of the main memory, virtual memory, etc. These characteristics make it possible to evaluate the conditions for agreeing on the order in which resource allocations will be made, ordered by process group.

Mean shift algorithm is a popular method used in clustering algorithms. It involves finding the modes of the probability density function of the data by computing the mean of the data points within a certain bandwidth or kernel. The properties of this algorithm are critical in understanding how it works and how to optimize it. One of the key properties is convergence, which refers to the fact that the algorithm will eventually find the true modes of the probability density function with enough iterations. Another important property is bandwidth, which refers to the size of the area around each data point that is used to compute the mean shift. Estimation of bandwidth is a critical step in the algorithm, as it is used to balance the need for accuracy with the need for speed. Finally, the trajectory of the mean shift vector can be used to visualize the clustering process and gain insights into the structure of the data. Overall, understanding the properties of mean shift is essential in its successful application to clustering problems.

This paper presents a formalization and analysis of a resource allocation security protocol for secure service migration in cloud computing environments. The protocol takes into consideration the security requirements of servers during the allocation process. The use of cryptographic protocols provides an additional layer of security to prevent unauthorized access to the resources. The proposed protocol has been analyzed using the AVISPA tool, which validates that the protocol satisfies the security requirements. This research contributes to the internet security domain by providing a formalization and validation of a security protocol that ensures the confidentiality and integrity of the resources during the service migration process. The results of this research can be applied to enhance the security of cloud computing infrastructure and provide a secure environment for the deployment of sensitive applications. The use of formal methods and analysis tools can assist in the development of robust and secure protocols and systems.

The explosive growth of artificial neural networks (ANNs) has resulted in unprecedented advances in machine learning across various domains. However, the training and decoding of ANNs require high computational resources, leading to long processing times and large energy consumption. To address this, approximate computing techniques have been proposed to reduce the required computation, power and area. The use of tunable floating-point representations in ANNs has been shown to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the computations. This paper explores the benefits of tunable floating-point representations for ANNs, examining the current state-of-the-art methods for training and decoding. It also discusses the potential applications of these techniques in the field of approximate computing, as well as the resulting impact on industry standards. Overall, this paper presents a comprehensive overview of the use of tunable floating-point representations for ANNs and highlights its potential to revolutionize machine learning applications.

Recovering an absolute metric scale from a monocular camera is a challenging but highly desirable problem for monocular camera-based systems. By using different kinds of cues, various approaches have been proposed for scale estimation, such as camera height and object size. In this paper, first, we summarize different kinds of scale estimation approaches. Then, we propose a robust divide-and-conquer absolute scale estimation method based on the ground plane and camera height by analyzing the advantages and disadvantages of different approaches. By using the estimated scale, an effective scale correction strategy has been proposed to reduce the scale drift during the monocular visual odometry estimation process. Finally, the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method have been verified on both public and self-collected image sequences.

This paper examines the modernisation and vision of telecommunications engineering at Macquarie University in Australia. The university is dedicated to providing cutting-edge engineering education that meets the needs of the telecommunications industry. To achieve this goal, Macquarie University has established state-of-the-art laboratories and research facilities that allow students to gain hands-on experience in the latest technologies. Additionally, the university has implemented a strong focus on cloud computing in its telecommunications curriculum to ensure that students have the skills necessary to succeed in the rapidly evolving field of telecommunications. Ultimately, Macquarie University is committed to providing its students with a comprehensive education in telecommunications engineering that will enable them to make significant contributions to the industry and to society as a whole.

In this paper, we propose a coordinated path-following control strategy for multiple autonomous vehicles with communication time delays. The delay effects are introduced to the closed loop systems and addressed by using prediction algorithms. The proposed predictive control strategy enables each vehicle to follow a desired path while maintaining a safe distance from neighboring vehicles. The vehicle dynamics and communication delays are modeled using computational modeling techniques, and the proposed strategy is evaluated through simulations. The results show that the proposed strategy is effective in controlling multiple autonomous vehicles with communication time delays and can improve the overall performance and safety of autonomous systems. This research has practical significance for the development of autonomous vehicles and can be applied to various transportation scenarios that require coordinated control of multiple vehicles.

This paper proposes an extension of the Negative Imaginary Systems (NIS) theory to nonlinear systems. The NIS theory has been widely studied in the context of linear systems, where transfer functions are used to analyze the stability of a system. In this work, the concept of asymptotic stability is introduced to analyze the stability of nonlinear systems. The proposed method is applied to the study of a manganese chemical reactor system using computed tomography (CT) data. The CT data is used to construct a model of the reactor system, and the stability analysis is performed using the extended NIS theory. The results show that the proposed method is effective in analyzing the stability of nonlinear systems and can be used to improve the design and operation of complex chemical reactors.

In this paper, a quadrotor UAV dynamic model with the wind speed factor is established and sliding mode controllers are designed for attitude stabilization. Neural network and fuzzy control are proposed to improve the performance of anti-strong wind controller for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Uncertainty of dynamic model can be approximated by radical basis function (RBF) neural network, and fuzzy control can dynamically correct the coefficients of the symbol function during the state convergence process. The simulation results show that the neural network constructed in this paper can track the uncertainty of the model, combining sliding mode with fuzzy control maintains the advantages of fast response and robustness. At the same time, the chattering problem is greatly reduced, which guarantees the anti-strong wind requirements of UAV and improves the stability of the controllers.

Global surrogate models are presented for antenna elements in large phased arrays, to cheaply and accurately model scan-dependent impedance and radiation responses for systems with wide-angle scanning requirements. Adaptive sampling combined with rational and Kriging interpolation is found to produce accurate, convergent models within 50 full-wave EM simulations of a patch element within a planar PBC unit cell.

This paper presents an efficient and secure fine-grained access control scheme for fog computing, called CCA2. The proposed scheme is publicly verifiable, flexible and robust against various types of attacks. It leverages the advantages of edge computing, cryptography, cloud computing and the Internet of Things to provide a comprehensive solution for access control in fog computing. The scheme operates based on a hierarchical structure, where access policies are defined at different levels to reflect the varying security requirements of different resources. In addition, it employs a unique game-theoretic approach to evaluate the trustworthiness of users, ensuring that only authorized users are granted access to sensitive information. The proposed scheme also demonstrates high efficiency, requiring low computation overhead and minimal communication cost. Overall, the CCA2 scheme provides an effective and practical solution for fine-grained access control in fog computing, enabling secure and efficient sharing of resources across diverse applications.

As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to grow, there is an increasing need for verified programming of embedded devices. These devices, such as those used in buildings or hardware, often interact with physical pins and have strict safety requirements. In this paper, we focus on the challenges of programming IoT devices and propose a solution that utilizes libraries to ensure safety and reduce delays. Our approach involves verifying the correctness of the code and incorporating pre-built libraries to streamline the programming process. By doing this, we hope to improve the overall reliability and safety of IoT devices, making them more suitable for use in a wide range of applications. Our work highlights the importance of reliable programming in the IoT, and points to a potential way forward for future developments in this exciting and rapidly evolving field.

Combined variations such as low-resolution and occlusion often present in face images in the wild, e.g., under the scenario of video surveillance. While most of the existing face enhancement approaches only handle one type of variation per model, in this paper, we propose a deep generative adversarial network (FCSR-GAN) for joint face completion and face super-resolution via one model. The generator of FCSR-GAN aims to recover a high-resolution face image without occlusion given an input low-resolution face image with partial occlusions. The discriminator of FCSR-GAN consists of two adversarial losses, a perceptual loss, and a face parsing loss, which assure the high quality of the recovered face images. Experimental results on several public-domain databases (CelebA and Helen) show that the proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in jointly doing face super-resolution (up to 4×) and face completion from low-resolution face images with occlusions.

This paper proposes an anomaly identification method for a liquid-coffee vending machine using electrical current waveforms. The method consists of preprocessing of a series of current values collected from the machine, training of multiple classifiers corresponding to individual target anomalous operations, and anomaly detection by means of the classifiers. Preprocessing improves detection accuracy by excluding current values that represent non-target operations. Multiple classifiers corresponding to individual target operations are trained using pre-processed data and the ground truth. An operation with the maximum likelihood normalized by the total number of individual operations is identified as the current anomaly. Evaluations using electrical current values obtained from an actual coffee vending machine shows a false positive rate and a false negative rate of, respectively, 0% and 6.7%, for lack of beans and 2% and 0% for water leakage, both of which are major reasons for degraded coffee quality.

Cloud storage has gained increasing attention from the industry and research communities with concerns about data stored in cloud computing environments, despite its many advantages. The reasons come from economic viability to the latency along with behavioral changes that may affect the applications that use data stored remotely. Among those challenges, there is the problem of ensuring the integrity and retrievability of users' data in the cloud. Several schemas have been proposed: proof of data possession (PDP), proof of retrievability (PoR), and proof of ownership (PoW) that differ on the approach to guarantee the effective retrieval of data stored remotely. In this paper, a novel PoR protocol is proposed: hyper-scalability, availability, and integrity layer (Hy-SAIL), where a new PoR scheme adds higher availability to data stored and a flexible manner to perform integrity checks. It is demonstrated that Hy-SAIL leads to an efficient and scalable cryptographic system that meets near-optimal bounds in terms of communication and storage complexities. It is also proposed a new adversarial model that aggregates the main functionalities of a realistic adversary in cloud computing environments. Hy-SAIL operates on data that are not affected by any kind of incremental change or update, which is the characteristic of various file types stored in clouds, such as stored video and audio streams. When compared to other systems, such as HAIL, Hy-SAIL is more scalable and efficient. The results collected with an unoptimized implementation of Hy-SAIL point to a better perspective than other approaches.

We systemically investigated the influence of sidewall morphology change based on TMAH etching on the optical performance of mini-LEDs. The dominant feature of prism structures on the sidewall of mini-LEDs with TMAH etching treatment varied from inhomogeneous to homogeneous as the TMAH etching time prolonged. Such prism structures only appeared on the sidewall along direction owing to the anisotropic TMAH etching. Experimental and simulation results demonstrated that these prism structures can effectively improve the light extraction from sidewall and homogenous prism structures on the sidewall function better in out-coupling light.

In this research work, we propose a novel Quantum Particle Swarm Optimizer (QPSO) with enhanced strategy for the global optimization of electromagnetic devices. The proposed QPSO is a combination of quantum mechanics and particle swarm optimization to optimize the convergence of the algorithm. The primary focus of this study is to optimize the performance of superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) devices and solenoids. The QPSO algorithm is highly efficient and can effectively solve electromagnetic optimization problems in a timely manner. The proposed algorithm is compared with various other algorithms, and the results show that the proposed QPSO algorithm has higher accuracy and faster convergence rate. We conduct extensive experiments on the optimization of various electromagnetic devices such as solenoids and SMES devices. The results confirmed that the QPSO algorithm is highly effective and efficient in solving electromagnetic optimization problems. The proposed algorithm can be relevant in the areas of electromagnetics, optimization, and particle swarm optimization.

This paper proposes Stacon, a self-stabilizing context neighborhood for mobile IoT devices. The authors conduct a task analysis to identify the requirements of the wireless sensor network protocols for mobile IoT devices. They then develop Stacon, a protocol that enables the self-stabilization of the wireless communication between mobile IoT devices by adjusting the payload size dynamically. The authors evaluate Stacon on various sensor systems and applications and show that it significantly improves the network's stability and efficiency. The proposed solution has significant implications for the development of mobile IoT devices and wireless sensor networks in general.

The development of competences related to green tourism requires the awareness and cooperation of relevant stakeholders. This paper focuses on identifying the key stakeholders and their roles in developing green tourism competences. The paper also examines the importance of green products, training, electronic learning, market research, and learning systems in developing these competences. The study emphasizes the need for a collaborative approach among stakeholders to promote sustainable tourism practices. The paper concludes that by improving the knowledge and skillset of stakeholders, the tourism industry can enhance its ability to provide sustainable tourism experiences to consumers.

Three-dimensional visible light positioning (3D-VLP) is capable of achieving superior locating accuracy in comparison with other existing positioning techniques, such as global positioning system (GPS) and Wi-Fi-based method, which draws much attention from the researchers. In this paper, a novel 3D-VLP scheme using regression neural network is proposed to provide accurate and real-time positioning service. In the proposed method, the angle of arrival (AOA) vectors corresponding to the light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are obtained by the image sensor of the receiver and then fed into a regression neural network, which directly outputs the positioning results. Simulations are carried out to validate the superiority of the proposed method. It’s observed that, in spite of the inevitable quantization error in the positioning process, the mean positioning error is still as accurate as 1.1 cm. In addition, the proposed positioning method is more robust to camera’s height, and takes only 0.27ms to calculate the position, which could be used for real-time locating.

As IoT (Internet of Things) has expanded year over year enabling the presence of sensing in almost everywhere. This leads to increase the concerns about authentication and security. In this scenario, the academy is engaged with alternatives to automated recognition of individuals and provide proof of liveness. In this context, the application of physiological features such as ECG (electrocardiography), PPG (photoplethysmography), and EMG (electromyogram) is a promising approach for continuous authentication. Specifically, ECG has been used by many researchers as biometric identification, since it has features that are unique to an individual, such as, statistical, morphological, and wavelet features. In this paper, we proposed a particular feature selection, using only fiducial points related to amplitude and time that can be found directly from the signal acquired, without any kind of complex processing. We also investigate some of the most used machine learning algorithms for user identification. Evaluation results show the potential of the proposed solution, which has reached accuracy higher than 98.2% in the continuous authentication and identification scenario, which seems to be a feasible approach to increase security in many critical applications and services.

For the acceptance of spectral measurement technology for quality assurance and inspection in the industrial sector, the acquisition and processing of spectral images must be adapted to the production cycle. When processing spectral images, variations of the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) are often used as preprocessing steps, for example for segmentation, spectral decomposition or data compression. To speed up this time-consuming algorithm, hardware and software cores were implemented on a system-on-a-programmable-chip (SoPC). This paper deals with the optimization of this implementation to minimize calculation times. Special attention is paid to the cores used to calculate covariances and data derivation. The restructuring of the hardware IP (Intellectual property) cores and fundamental design decisions are discussed. The optimization was implemented and evaluated on a 12-channel spectral camera.

Traditional analog circuit fault diagnosis usually consists of feature extraction, feature selection and fault classifier. However, fault feature extraction and selection take much manual effort, which make the design of the fault diagnosis system complicated and not universal. This paper proposes an analog circuit fault diagnosis method based on Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). The proposed method uses the single pulse as the stimulus signal to circuit-under-test (CUT), and then the raw time domain response of CUT is directly sampled to construct fault samples, which are inputted into the ELM network to obtain fault diagnosis results. The experimental results show that the average diagnostic accuracies reach 100% and 99.5% on the Sallen-key band-pass filter circuit and the four opamp biquad high-pass filter circuit, respectively. The algorithm achieves good diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in the absence of feature extraction and selection.

This paper proposes a novel method for target detection in video feeds using selected dyads and groups assisted by collaborative brain-computer interfaces. The approach focuses on error analysis to identify potential shortcomings of existing methods and improve the overall accuracy of the system. Standards are developed for assessing and comparing performance in this domain. In addition, decision-making processes are analyzed to determine optimal strategies for allocating resources and optimizing performance. Task analysis is used to define the specific requirements for target detection in video feeds. Electroencephalography is utilized to capture brain signals as input, and feature extraction techniques are employed for extracting relevant information from these signals. Finally, the head movements of users are used as an additional input for the system, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the user's intentions and improving the accuracy of the system overall. The proposed method offers promising results and demonstrates the potential for enhancing target detection in video feeds using collaborative brain-computer interfaces.

This paper deals with the problem of adaptive estimation, i.e. the simultaneous estimation of the state and parameters, for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems. A nonlinear adaptive sliding-mode observer is proposed based on a nonlinear parameter estimation algorithm. The nonlinear parameter estimation algorithm provides a rate of convergence faster than exponential while the sliding-mode observer ensures ultimate boundness for the state estimation error attenuating the effects of the external disturbances. Linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are provided for the synthesis of the adaptive observer and some simulation results show the feasibility of the proposed approach.

This paper proposes the EB-Boost method, a medium-long term forecasting approach to estimating the supply of shared electric cars in smart scenic spots. The approach leverages meteorological data to create predictive models that are trained on historical data, predicting future supply levels. The proposed method also involves the use of data models and business estimation tools to further refine the forecasts. The goal of the EB-Boost method is to provide accurate and reliable forecasts that can help businesses in the shared electric car industry make informed decisions regarding fleet management and supply chain logistics. Overall, this paper demonstrates that the EB-Boost method is an effective means of forecasting supply levels, helping businesses optimize their operations and better serve their customers.

Edge detection is a fundamental computer vision problem and has wide applications, Convolutional neural networks (CNN) has been a good fundamental component in many image edge detection systems. But the edge detection accuracy from the detection and extraction of edge features by CNN is still below human visual perception, the edges of lines are fuzzy and the process is time-consuming. Based on the convolutional architecture for fast feature embedding (Caffe) framework and Visual Geometry Group (VGG16) template, a new accurate edge detector is presented in this paper by using visual cross fusion (VCF) network to detect features first. Our VCF model extracts the features of the multi-level hierarchy by parameter dimension reduction and cross-fusion of the fully connected layers respectively to achieve the end-to-end image edge detection. Second, for further improvement, a custom grading weighted cross-entropy loss function is to maximize the use of image pixels set and organize the disputed pixels rationally. Finally, the cross-network fusion layer is used to refine the edge features of images. The experimental results show that the VCF algorithm achieves an ODSF-measure as 0.808 on the Berkeley Segmentation Data Set (BSDS500) classic dataset, which is 2.5% higher than the Holistically-Nested Edge Detection (HED) algorithm, while maintaining fast 30+ FPS. On the NYU Depth Dataset V2 (NYUD V2) dataset, the ODSF-measure is 0.783, improved by 5.66% compared with the HED algorithm, and the FPS is increased by 10+. Therefore, the VCF algorithm is closer to the average human visual perception.

This paper proposes an adaptive computation framework of distributed deep learning models for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. The proposed framework aims to optimize the computational modeling process and improve the performance of the system. To achieve this, the framework utilizes adaptation models and load modeling techniques to dynamically allocate computing resources among servers in the distributed system. The performance evaluation of the proposed framework surpasses that of existing methods. The implementation of this framework has a significant impact on the IoT industry, as it allows for the effective application of deep learning in IoT systems. As the IoT continues to grow, this proposed framework provides a tool for effective deep learning in a scalable and efficient manner.

The recognition of diabetic retinopathy is an important task in healthcare, which can be achieved by leveraging transfer learning techniques in conjunction with artificial intelligence. This involves training neural networks with large volumes of data to enable accurate identification of retinopathy in diabetic patients. The prevalence of diabetes has led to an increased demand for automated systems that can detect and classify the disease. Transfer learning can significantly improve the accuracy of such systems by enabling the reuse of knowledge gained from training on other related domains. This approach has proven effective in reducing the dependence on large datasets and reducing the time required for training. Effective recognition of diabetic retinopathy can lead to timely intervention and treatment, which can help prevent blindness in diabetic patients. Therefore, transfer learning can be considered as a promising approach in the development of effective systems for the recognition of diabetic retinopathy.

The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is a term applied to the industrial application of M2M devices. The security of IIoT devices is a difficult problem and where the automation of critical infrastructure is intended, risks may be unacceptable. Remote attacks are a significant threat and solutions are sought which are secure by default. The problem space may be analyzed using threat modelling methods. Software Defined Networks (SDN) provide mitigation for remote attacks which exploit local area networks. Similar concepts applied to the WAN may improve availability and performance and provide granular data on link characteristics. Schemes such as the Software Defined Perimeter allow IIoT devices to communicate on the Internet, mitigating avenues of remote attack. Finally, separation of duties at the IIoT device may prevent attacks on the integrity of the device or the confidentiality and integrity of its communications. Work remains to be done on the mitigation of DDoS.

This paper proposes the use of Energy Network Theory to model and analyze Integrated Energy Systems. By incorporating the principles of Thermodynamics into a Mathematical model, Energy states can be properly represented and analyzed. The Network theory (graphs) is applied to mimic the interactions within the Energy Systems and to identify and optimize the key pathways of energy flow. The approach is similar to the way the Internet and Local area networks are managed. Analytical models are also employed to enhance the accuracy of the modeling and analysis process. In conclusion, the proposed Energy Network Theory offers a promising approach for modeling and analyzing Integrated Energy Systems, which can lead to improved performance and energy efficiency.

This paper proposes a novel direction of arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm that utilizes the received signal strength (RSS) of directional antennas to achieve higher accuracy in location awareness. The proposed algorithm employs software algorithms to estimate the DOA based on the RSS measurements of multiple directional antennas. By using this method, the DOA can be estimated with higher precision, and the position measurement accuracy can also be improved. The use of directional antennas enables the estimation of multiple DOAs simultaneously, while the software algorithms allow for a more efficient and accurate estimation process. The proposed algorithm has the potential to improve the performance of location-based services and position sensing in various applications that require precise positioning, such as navigation systems and indoor positioning. Overall, the proposed DOA estimation algorithm demonstrates a promising direction for improving the accuracy of position sensing using directional antennas.

Can we predict the words a child is going to learn next given information about the words that a child knows now? Do different representations of a child's vocabulary knowledge affect our ability to predict the acquisition of lexical items for individual children? Past research has often focused on population statistics of vocabulary growth rather than prediction of words an individual child is likely to learn next. We consider a neural network approach to predict vocabulary acquisition. Specifically, we investigate how best to represent the child's current vocabulary in order to accurately predict future learning. The models we consider are based on qualitatively different sources of information: descriptive information about the child, the specific words a child knows, and representations that aim to capture the child's aggregate lexical knowledge. Using longitudinal vocabulary data from children aged 15-36 months, we construct neural network models to predict which words are likely to be learned by a particular child in the coming month. Many models based on child-specific vocabulary information outperform models with child information only, suggesting that the words a child knows influence prediction of future language learning. These models provide an understanding of the role of current vocabulary knowledge on future lexical growth.

The implementation of swarm robotics in supervisory control of heterogeneous robots with varying levels of autonomy poses challenges in establishing trust between humans and the robots. This paper proposes a study on the effects of implementing "switches" in controlling autonomous robots and how they affect the level of trust of humans in supervisory control. It also highlights the importance of task analysis in determining which aspects of robot behavior should be automated and which should be left to human control. Furthermore, the paper discusses the impact of automation on the level of trust in human-robot interactions, emphasizing the need for clear instruction manuals and guidelines for efficient supervisory control.
