Contrary to conventional strategies, which extract the sensor information from the normalized resistance, the proposed algorithm is based on the variation in resistance over time. The results have demonstrated that the time necessary to get the maximum performance of these sensors is reduced around a 25% when compared with the conventional approach for any of the recovery strategies analyzed (passive desorption, external heating, or dc voltage). The hardware implementation of the proposed algorithm in a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) has also demonstrated that, in addition to optimizing the sensor performance in terms of time response and sensitivity, this measurement algorithm yields a significant minimization of the sensor readout circuit resources at both software and hardware levels paving the way for future development of smart sensors for the Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

This paper proposes a method for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of near-field passive sources based on acoustic array and fractional Fourier transform (FRFT). The proposed method is capable of estimating DOA in both azimuth and elevation directions. The estimation accuracy is improved by using the chirp signal and the time-frequency analysis based on FRFT. The algorithm is implemented on a sensor array and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Comparing with traditional Fourier transforms, FRFT provides more comprehensive information on the time-frequency domain, which can capture more subtle changes in the signal. Hence, the proposed method based on FRFT has a higher performance in terms of estimation accuracy and resolution. Overall, this work presents a promising solution for the DOA estimation of near-field sources in the acoustic field.

This paper proposes a trust-based cooperative game model for secure collaboration in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). With the development of IoV, collaboration between vehicles has become an important method to improve traffic efficiency and ensure road safety. However, due to the lack of trust and security issues, vehicles may hesitate to share their data with others, which hinders the collaboration. In this context, game theory is applied to model the interaction between vehicles, and the trustworthiness of vehicles is defined as a key factor to determine the cooperation strategy. Moreover, a computational model is designed to evaluate and optimize the system performance. The proposed model considers the data integrity and authenticity, which ensures the data exchanged between vehicles are reliable and tamper-proof. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model can achieve better performance than traditional methods in terms of traffic efficiency and security. Overall, the trust-based cooperative game model presented in this paper is an effective solution to promote secure collaboration in IoV.

This paper demonstrates a possible application of the Moving Path Following (MPF) motion control approach applied to the marine environment. Specifically, the problem of target estimation and tracking using Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is considered, wherein the robotic vehicle is equipped with a ranging sensor in order to localize a possibly moving target. Such a problem bears a strong resemblance to the single beacon navigation problem, in which the AUV is expected to execute state and input trajectories that renders the target states observable. To this end, control laws are proposed for an AUV to follow a geometric path, that is stationary with respect to the moving target, leading to the MPF problem. The geometric path is chosen such that the target states are observable. An extended Kalman filter is utilized to estimate the target position and velocity using range-only measurements. The efficacy of the MPF approach is illustrated through a source localization and tracking scenario in simulations.

5G networks will be characterized by massive densification of base stations (BSs). To minimize the network power consumption due to the increased BS deployment, we leverage emerging paradigms to propose BS energy-saving strategies applicable to 5G networks. We explore the potentials of virtualized radio access and core networks to enable spectrum sharing among mobile network operators (MNOs) by harnessing inter-band non-contiguous carrier aggregation. We propose the sleep-mode with efficient beamformers and spectrum-sharing (SEBS) strategy, which minimizes BS power consumption of cooperative MNOs. The licensed bandwidth of each MNO is partitioned into private and shared bands to provision active BSs with sufficient spectrum resources for serving all UEs. Moreover, an optimization problem is formulated to obtain the optimal intra- and inter-RAN beamforming vectors for efficient BS transmission power and improved user signal reception. Numerical simulations show that the proposed strategies yield significant reductions of total power consumption as compared to other schemes. We present different bandwidth sharing ratio formulations to motivate the cooperation among MNOs by the spectrum-user support trading. We also show that the trading does not always yield a higher spectral efficiency in the cooperative cellular network.

Traditional web security assessments are evaluated using a single data source, and the results of the calculations from different data sources are different. Based on multi-source data, this paper uses Analytic Hierarchy Process to construct an evaluation model, calculates the weight of each level of indicators in the web security evaluation model, analyzes and processes the data, calculates the host security threat assessment values at various levels, and visualizes the evaluation results through ECharts+WebGL technology.

This research paper explores the impact of graph analysis on the detection of content marketing articles. The study focuses on the use of feature extraction to extract relevant data from social networking sites, frequency measurement to identify patterns, and semantics to aid in context modeling. Writing techniques are also analyzed to determine their potential impact on the success of content marketing campaigns. From the results of the analysis, it was found that graph analysis can significantly improve the accuracy of content marketing article detection. Furthermore, it was found that advertising plays a crucial role in enhancing the success of content marketing campaigns. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of various factors on content marketing article detection and offers an opportunity to improve the effectiveness of digital marketing campaigns.

This paper proposes a discrete-time sliding mode control (DSMC) strategy for linear (possibly multi-input) systems with additive bounded disturbances, which guarantees the satisfaction of input and state constraints. The control law is generated by solving a finite-horizon optimal control problem at each sampling instant, aimed at obtaining a control variable that is as close as possible to a reference DSMC law, but at the same time enforces constraint satisfaction for all admissible disturbance values. Contrary to previously-proposed control approaches merging DSMC and model predictive control, our proposal guarantees the satisfaction of all standard properties of DSMC, and in particular the finite-time convergence of the state into a boundary layer of the sliding manifold.

In this paper the procedure of collision resolution based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) is observed. The efficiency of this procedure in the random multiple access (RMA) systems is estimated considering the imperfection of signal subtraction in the real conditions. The model of the system was developed and the experiments for estimating the system parameters and throughput were held.

With the increasing development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), smart city is becoming an important topic in the field of urban planning. The evaluation of intelligent agents is a fundamental part of designing and implementing smart city solutions. Intelligent agents are autonomous entities that can perform tasks on behalf of humans by making decisions based on specific algorithms. In order to evaluate a smart city system that uses intelligent agents, task analysis is an important tool that can help to identify the tasks that agents can perform and the potential benefits they can bring. Robot kinematics is another crucial factor in designing smart cities. The use of robots can significantly improve the efficiency of various industries and services, such as transportation, manufacturing and healthcare. In addition, cognition plays an important role in enabling intelligent agents to perceive their environment and make decisions accordingly. Overall, the evaluation of intelligent agents in smart cities is a complex and interdisciplinary process that requires a comprehensive understanding of AI, task analysis, robot kinematics, cognition and other related fields.

Hyperspectral image (HSI) consists of hundreds of continuous narrow bands with high redundancy, resulting in the curse of dimensionality and an increased computation complexity in HSI classification. Many clustering-based band selection approaches have been proposed to deal with such a problem. However, a few of them consider the spectral and spatial relationship simultaneously. In this letter, we proposed a novel clustering-based band selection approach using deep subspace clustering (DSC). The proposed approach combines the subspace clustering task into a convolutional autoencoder by treating it as a self-expressive layer, enabling it to be trained end to end. The resulting network can fully extract the interaction of spectral bands based on using spatial information and nonlinear feature transformation. We compared the results of the proposed method with existing band selection methods for three widely used HSI data sets, showing that the proposed method is able to accurately select an informative band subset with remarkable classification accuracy.

This paper describes the development of a web application for learning and training of mouse handling as an interaction device in digital environments. The application, called "Mice," is designed to provide users with a comprehensive understanding of the use of mice and their associated software programs. This training platform is accessible through the Internet which allows anyone with an active online connection to access the application from anywhere around the world. Mice training emphasizes the importance of computer input devices, especially keyboards and mouse for motor coordination. The application can be used as an effective tool for individuals seeking to improve their knowledge and skills in the use of mice as information systems input devices. This research underscores the potential of web-based educational applications in providing practical and affordable ways to learn new skills and improve existing ones.

Though face recognition using traditional (hard) biometrics has attracted massive research interest and received extensive studies, it still confronts degrading variability challenges and notably achieves lower performance compared with other biometric recognition forms like fingerprint and iris. Recently, a number of research studies have been interested in enhancing face recognition performance by all means of supplementary facial biometric traits or other biometric modalities. Thus, soft biometrics have been emerged as a new promising modality of biometrics and highlighted as likely viable and fusible traits for augmenting traditional/hard biometrics. This is due to the expected advantages of soft biometrics over the traditional biometric traits, such as the high collectability and invariance properties. Other than fusing different kinds of traditional traits to augment face recognition, adding soft biometrics to augment various traditional facial traits has yet gained little research attention. Hence, in this research, unlike the majority of existing work, we investigate the viability of global soft face biometrics in supplementing traditional (hard) biometrics and the efficacy of concurrently using absolute and relative descriptions as soft biometrics. We conduct a new soft biometric-based fusion scheme in feature-level for augmenting a traditional Gabor-based face identification/verification in different potential forensic scenarios, considering performance variability evaluation and comparison with the baseline performance of Gabor features in isolation.

The photovoltaic (PV) generation system becomes important as renewable energy sources, due to its advantages such as absence of fuel cost, low maintenance requirement, and environmental friendliness, the integration of the z-source inverter in the (PV) generation system has been very popular among researchers, due to its ability to boost the PV voltage with its single-stage topology. This paper focus on the integration of The Z-source inverter in a photovoltaic (PV) system generation, and the implementation of the Perturb & Observe (P&O) and the fuzzy logic controller algorithm (FLC), to find the Maximum power point (MPPT). At the final we compare the results of the FLC with the Perturb & Observe (P&O) algorithm. A Matlab simulink toolbox and M-file have been used for the simulation, in order to verify the results experimentally. The two algorithm was implemented in a real time with a dSPACE MicroLabBOX, and the I-V curves was programed with Chroma 62150H-600S/1000S Solar Array Simulator.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has seen widespread adoption in recent years, with wireless sensor networks (WSN) being an integral component of its infrastructure. However, conventional WSN-based data gathering methods can be both time-consuming and computationally expensive. In this paper, we propose an optimized data gathering method based on compressive sensing, a technique that aims to minimize the number of samples required to obtain accurate data measurements. With the use of sparse matrices, we can effectively reduce packet loss without compromising the accuracy of data collection. Our method also takes into account correlations between sensors, allowing us to further optimize the data gathering process. Through experimentation, we show that our proposed method outperforms conventional data gathering methods in terms of both computational efficiency and accuracy, making it an attractive solution for IoT applications.

Distributed Trust-Based Multiple Attack Prevention for Secure MANETs is a critical issue in wireless ad hoc networks where nodes are highly mobile and topology can change rapidly. Steady-state networks cannot guarantee secure communication due to the absence of centralized infrastructure, and mobile computing further exacerbates the problem by restricting the ability of nodes to remain connected. This paper proposes a novel approach to multiple attack prevention in MANETs based on trust and distributed intrusion detection methodologies. The proposed system utilizes probes to detect and respond to attacks, and data models for predicting and preventing future attacks. By leveraging trust models based on the behavior of individual nodes, the system can quickly identify and isolate malicious actors, enabling receivers to ignore or discard attack packets. Simulation studies have shown that the proposed system outperforms existing approaches in terms of detection accuracy, false positive rates, and overhead costs. In conclusion, our research presents a practical and effective approach to securing MANETs, which have become increasingly important in a wide range of military, civilian, and commercial applications.

The growing interest in machine learning among business leaders and decision makers demands that researchers explore its use within business organisations. One of the major issues facing business leaders within companies is the loss of talented employees. This research studies employee attrition using machine learning models. Using a synthetic data created by IBM Watson, three main experiments were conducted to predict employee attrition. The first experiment involved training the original class-imbalanced dataset with the following machine learning models: support vector machine (SVM) with several kernel functions, random forest and K-nearest neighbour (KNN). The second experiment focused on using adaptive synthetic (ADASYN) approach to overcome class imbalance, then retraining on the new dataset using the abovementioned machine learning models. The third experiment involved using manual undersampling of the data to balance between classes. As a result, training an ADASYN-balanced dataset with KNN (K = 3) achieved the highest performance, with 0.93 F1-score. Finally, by using feature selection and random forest, F1-score of 0.909 was achieved using 12 features out of a total of 29 features.

The IPIM (Information Propagation Incentive Mechanism) is an innovative approach to address the challenge of effective information propagation in social networking platforms. The mechanism is designed to incentivize content creators to contribute high-quality information on the platform, thus improving the overall accuracy and effectiveness of search results for users. IPIM supports various applications, including object recognition, sensors, games, and computational modeling. By integrating incentive schemes, IPIM provides a framework for creating a self-sustaining ecosystem of content creators and users. With the increase in the usage of online social networking, search problems have become increasingly complex due to the vastness of the data available. IPIM offers a promising solution to these problems by ensuring that users are provided with timely and high-quality information. In conclusion, IPIM represents a significant contribution to the field of social networking and information propagation and has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of search results.

Efficient utilization of energy in energy-constrained mobile devices is crucial to achieve sustainable network connectivity. Computational offloading has been gaining popularity as a technique to minimize energy consumption of individual devices in mobile ad hoc networks. In this study, we propose a multi-hop cooperative network architecture for computational offloading. The architecture utilizes the spread spectrum communication technique to achieve efficient transmission of computational workloads across multiple devices. A set of performance evaluation metrics are defined to quantify the effectiveness of the proposed architecture. These metrics are applied in evaluating the performance of the proposed scheme on various mobile handsets and servers. The results of the evaluation demonstrate the potential of the proposed scheme to achieve improved network connectivity and energy efficiency in wireless fidelity networks. This study presents a promising solution to the energy problem in wireless networks and can be integrated into various applications that demand energy-efficient network communication.

With the increasing application of wireless sensor networks (WSNs), routing has become a crucial issue in ensuring the efficient and effective operation of WSNs. This paper proposes a novel flexible routing computing approach (FRCA) for WSNs. FRCA combines the advantages of traditional routing protocols with the measurement and analysis of mobile computing and computational modeling. It achieves improved energy efficiency, enhances the network’s robustness, and provides greater flexibility in adapting to various network environments. The proposed FRCA has been evaluated using simulations, and the experimental results show that it outperforms existing routing protocols in terms of network lifetime and the ability to cope with varying traffic loads. In conclusion, FRCA presents a promising solution to the routing challenges in WSNs and has the potential to enhance the performance and reliability of WSNs in real-world applications.

To operate under sterilization condition in operating room help to reduce infection rate in patient. Therefore, surgeons cannot control computer by using mouse, or keyboard. In this paper, we proposed a method to controlling images in operating room by using a touchless sensor. This method consists of four step. First, hand motion is sensed by a touchless sensor as Leap motion. Second, hand position is detected. Third, hand gesture is recognized by using movement direction. Finally, image is shown and processed relating with hand gesture command. To test the performance of the proposed method, twenty subjects used this device to control an images. This method controls images with two gestures and eight commands: waiting, selection, searching left image, searching right image, increasing brightness, reducing brightness, zooming in and out, and left or right rotation commends. Accuracy rate of commands interpretation is 87.67%. The performance of the proposed method is effective for real-world applications. This is an alternative method for controlling image in an operation room.

The healthcare industry generates vast amounts of data which can contain valuable insights for improving patient care and reducing costs. In this paper, we propose a novel method for mining abnormal behaviors in social medical insurance using data mining techniques. Our approach involves the analysis of transaction databases from hospitals and insurance companies to identify patterns of abnormal behavior such as fraudulent claims or unnecessary medical procedures. By identifying these abnormal behaviors, our method can be used to reduce waste and promote more efficient use of medical resources. This research has important implications for the insurance and healthcare industries, and demonstrates the potential of data mining techniques to enhance decision-making in these sectors.

This empirical study aims to investigate the acquisition of English vowels by EFL learners in Tianjin and Zibo, both urban areas in China. The study employs a phonetics approach, focusing on the acoustics and production of English vowels by these learners’ tongue movements. The convergence of these findings with previous studies on the acquisition of English vowels by Chinese learners is also examined. Through analyzing the data collected from the learners' speech production, the study provides insights into the difficulties encountered by EFL learners in acquiring English vowels and proposes pedagogical implications for improving vowel production skills among Chinese EFL learners.

Information visualization (InfoVis) is defined as ”the use of visual, interactive and visual representations supported by computer, to increase cognition”. InfoVis tools and methods help us accelerate our understanding of a large amount of data. Datavisualization improves understanding, especially with multidimensional data sets. Visual analysis methods allow decision makers to combine their human flexibility, creativity and knowledgewith the huge storage and processing capabilities of today's computers for information about complex problems. Using advanced visual interfaces, humans can interact directly with the data analysis, adding more to their liking and need. The MLV-Viewer prototype will be described in this article.

This paper proposes a new design scheme of carrier runway simulation system. The system can be used for simulating training for the aircraft of carrier landing, and it can provide pilots with an environment being closer to the actual landing. The carrier runway simulation system mainly includes runway motion simulation system and the ideal landing point simulation system. The simulation system of ideal landing point simulates the height variation of the ideal landing point by using the horizontal variation of optical virtual arresting cable, it can offer crucial movement information to the carrier aircraft pilot. The runway motion simulation system employs a programmable multi-axis controller to control the linear motion guides moving with the infrared cooperative targets, which can simulate the carrier runway movement. And the high-precision magnetic grid measurement sensor collects motion information and transfers the information into the computer. In this paper, an 8:1 scale experiment has been designed and the runway motion simulation system is implemented. The experiment results show that the maximum height error of the targets between actual and setting motion is 0.02m, which meets the requirement of the simulation system and verifies the feasibility of the runway motion simulation system. What's more, the simulation system is beneficial to the later research work of carrier-based aircraft landing ground simulation.

This paper focuses on the investigation of a unified emerging non-volatile memory system-on-chip (SoC) architecture for Internet of Things (IoT) wireless sensor network (WSN) applications. The aim is to improve the performance of WSNs by incorporating random access memory (RAM) and non-volatile memory (NVM) into a single chip. The proposed architecture uses phase change materials to implement NVM and also supports wireless communication. To evaluate the performance of the proposed architecture, the authors conducted simulations and compared the results with existing architectures. The findings indicate that the unified emerging NVM SoC architecture achieves higher performance and reduced power consumption than the existing architectures. Therefore, the proposed architecture has the potential to significantly improve the operations of WSNs in IoT applications.

The classic midpoint method for triangulation is extremely fast, but usually labelled as inaccurate. We investigate the cost function that the midpoint method tries to minimize, and the result shows that the midpoint method is prone to underestimate the accuracy of the measurement acquired relatively far from the three-dimensional (3-D) point. Accordingly, the cost function used in this letter is enhanced by assigning a weight to each measurement, which is inversely proportional to the distance between the 3-D point and the corresponding camera center. After analyzing the gradient of the modified cost function, we propose to do minimization by applying fixed-point iterations to find the roots of the gradient. Thus, the proposed method is called the iteratively reweighted midpoint method. In addition, a theoretical study is presented to reveal that the proposed method is an approximation to the Newton's method near the optimal point and, hence, inherits the quadratic convergence rate. Finally, the comparisons of the experimental results on both synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that the proposed method is more efficient than the state-of-the-art while achieves the same level of accuracy.

Independent mobility of visually impaired people is key to making an inclusive society for them. Unstructured infrastructure in developing countries pose significant challenges in developing aids to address the mobility problem of visually impaired. Most of the assistive devices available internationally assume a structured and controlled environment severely restricting the applicability of such devices. In this paper, we assess the ability of state-of-the-art assistive devices for addressing the independent outdoor mobility needs of the visually impaired in an unstructured environment. We have created realistic datasets for various scenarios and evaluate deep neural networks for object detection on these datasets. We also present a portable prototype for the task. Further, we have also developed a cloud based solution to address the mobility requirements. We compare the local device based and cloud based solutions in terms of accuracy, latency, and energy. We present and discuss results from these two implementations that can provide insights for an effective solution. The results and insights open up novel research problems for embedded systems.

This paper investigates the implementation of green human resource practices in healthcare organizations. The study utilizes a joint application of Balanced Scorecard and SIR Method to measure the effectiveness of green practices in hospitals. The study focuses on two key areas of human resource management- recruitment and training, and examines how green practices are integrated into these areas. The paper also explores the use of green products in healthcare organizations and measures their impact on the environment. The findings of the study suggest that healthcare organizations have made significant progress in adopting green practices. The study recommends the use of specific indexes to measure the effectiveness of green practices in healthcare organizations. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the implementation of green human resource practices in the healthcare sector and highlights the importance of adopting these practices to protect the environment.

The performance of many robust model fitting techniques is largely dependent on the quality of the generated hypotheses. In this paper, we propose a novel guided sampling method, called accelerated guided sampling (AGS), to efficiently generate the accurate hypotheses for multistructure model fitting. Based on the observations that residual sorting can effectively reveal the data relationship (i.e., determine whether two data points belong to the same structure), and keypoint matching scores can be used to distinguish inliers from gross outliers, AGS effectively combines the benefits of residual sorting and keypoint matching scores to efficiently generate accurate hypotheses via information theoretic principles. Moreover, we reduce the computational cost of residual sorting in AGS by designing a new residual sorting strategy, which only sorts the top-ranked residuals of input data, rather than all input data. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in computer vision tasks, such as homography matrix and fundamental matrix estimation.

This paper explores and practices the establishment of a quality management security system for undergraduate capstone design. It discusses how to provide effective training for students to enhance their writing and communication skills, as well as creating a positive atmosphere for innovation and creativity. Technological innovation is also emphasized for better quality management, and atmospheric measurements are taken into consideration to ensure the safety of the design process. A well-implemented quality management security system can not only guarantee the success of the capstone project, but also serve as a guideline for future students to follow.

This paper proposes a new approach to the problem of anti-synchronization for discontinuous reaction-diffusion neural networks with time-varying coefficients and time delay. The study of synchronization among neurons is essential to understanding biological neural networks, and this work contributes to the development of mathematical models that can capture the complexity of these networks. The proposed approach relies on Lyapunov methods for analyzing convergence and delay effects, and it offers a fixed-time solution that avoids the need to specify a synchronization time. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through simulations that show the anti-synchronization of the network under different initial conditions and perturbations. This work provides a significant contribution to the study of synchronization and anti-synchronization in complex neural networks, and it has potential applications in fields such as neuroscience and artificial intelligence.

This paper discusses feature extraction techniques for next-term prediction of poor student performance. Task analysis is conducted to identify relevant factors that contribute to poor academic outcomes. Special issues and sections are considered, including the influence of socio-economic backgrounds, individual learning styles, and other external and internal factors. Predictive models are developed using data mining techniques to analyze students' academic histories, demographic information, and other relevant data. Learning management systems are utilized to collect and manage this data, and tools such as machine learning algorithms are applied to develop more accurate predictive models. The study shows that feature extraction plays a critical role in predicting poor student performance and can be used to identify at-risk students early on, allowing for timely interventions to prevent academic failure.

This paper explores the notions of centralized and decentralized opacity in linear systems, with a particular focus on observers, trajectory, and controllability. Opacity refers to the inability of an observer to determine the internal state of a system based on its inputs and outputs. The study extends to nonlinear systems, discrete-event systems, automata, and computers. The authors examine the potential benefits and drawbacks of both centralized and decentralized approaches to achieving opacity in various settings. They raise important questions about the trade-offs between system complexity, information sharing, and control performance, and they propose a number of theoretical frameworks for addressing these issues. Ultimately, this paper sheds light on the underlying principles and challenges of observable control systems, and offers insights for researchers and practitioners working in related fields.

This paper proposes an incremental online verification approach for dynamic Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) using automata and model checking techniques. The focus of the study is on aerospace electronics CPSs, which are associated with control systems and safety-critical applications. The proposed approach aims to detect computer bugs and erroneous behaviors in such systems by incrementally verifying their models during the runtime. The technique employs labeling to differentiate between controllable and uncontrollable events and maintains a set of feasible states in the automata to improve the efficiency of the verification process. The paper presents experimental results that demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach and its effectiveness in detecting complex errors in aerospace electronics systems. The contribution of this study lies in the design of a scalable and efficient method for online verification of dynamic CPSs, which can provide an early warning of unsafe behaviors in cyber-physical systems.

Video summarization (VS) is to identify important content from a given video, which can help users quickly comprehend video content. Recently, sparse dictionary selection (SDS) has demonstrated to be an effective solution for VS problems, which generally assumes a linear relationship between keyframes and non-keyframes. However, this assumption is not always true for video frames which possess intrinsic nonlinear structures and properties. In this paper, by exploiting the nonlinearity between video frames, a nonlinear SDS model is formulated for VS, in which the nonlinearity is transformed to linearity by projecting a video to a high-dimensional feature space induced by a kernel function. We also propose two greedy optimization algorithms to solve the resulting model, namely the standard kernel SDS (KSDS) greedy algorithm and the robust KSDS greedy algorithm with a backtracking strategy. In order to achieve an intuitive and flexible configuration of the VS process, an adaptive criterion, namely energy ratio, is devised to produce video summaries with different lengths for different video contents. Experimental results on two different benchmark video datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms several state-of-the-art VS algorithms.

This research design an environmental monitoring application for weather monitoring, which aims to monitor environmental conditions around such as temperature and humidity, CO2 and rain intensity and observe data on sensors. This monitoring system is robust to implement realworld environment monitoring and surveillance of several weather sensors such as temperature and humidity sensors, CO2 gas sensor and rainfall sensor. Sensors Network development in environment monitoring system has the ability to monitor the actual state of the environment and can display data from some weather sensors used in the internet.

Conditions for the existence and convergence to zero of numeric approximations with state-depend step of discretization to solutions of asymptotically stable homogeneous systems are obtained for the explicit and implicit Euler integration schemes. It is shown that for a sufficiently small discretization step the convergence of the approximating solutions to zero can be guaranteed globally in a finite or a fixed time, but in an infinite number of discretization iterations. It is proven that the absolute and relative errors of the respective discretizations are globally bounded functions. Efficiency of the proposed discretization algorithms is demonstrated by the simulation of the super-twisting system.

The detection of minor outer-raceway bearing faults is crucial for preventing costly motor failures. This paper presents a study on the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence methods in the detection of minor outer-raceway bearing faults. Specifically, support vector machines and other machine learning algorithms are utilized for fault diagnosis, while feature extraction is carried out on vibration data collected from the induction motors. The results of the study indicate that machine learning algorithms, such as support vector machines, can effectively identify minor faults in the outer raceway of motors. Additionally, artificial intelligence methods, such as feature extraction, can aid in the accurate diagnosis of motor faults. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of machine learning and artificial intelligence methods in detecting minor outer-raceway bearing faults in induction motors.

This paper focuses on the commercialization of eSIM technologies for network operators. With the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), eSIMs have become an essential component for enabling seamless connectivity between billions of devices. The paper delves into the standards and regulations surrounding eSIMs, highlighting the need for network operators to collaborate with other industry players to ensure interoperability and compatibility. Additionally, the paper covers the commercialization of eSIMs and how network operators can leverage this technology to provide new services and revenue streams. The intersection of eSIM technologies and cloud computing is also discussed, presenting opportunities for network operators to enhance their cloud-based offerings. Finally, security and contractual considerations surrounding the deployment of eSIMs in buildings are explored, emphasizing the importance of ensuring data privacy and integrity while also developing robust contractual mechanisms that balance the interests of all parties involved.

This paper presents an approach for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning using a constrained optimization framework. Reinforcement learning is a subfield of artificial intelligence that is concerned with how agents can learn to make decisions based on feedback from their environment. Optimization techniques are used to optimize the performance of the agents by finding the best set of parameters that minimize some objective function. The proposed approach introduces a risk-sensitive objective function that takes into account the impact of risk on the agent's decisions. The framework is shown to be effective in reducing the risk of unfavorable outcomes for the agent in various test scenarios. This research contributes to the field of computer science by providing a framework for incorporating risk into reinforcement learning algorithms. The approach has the potential to be applied in various fields, such as finance, robotics, and control systems, where risk is a significant factor in decision-making processes.

This paper presents a method to enhance Feature-based Visual SLAM by incorporating semantics. The goal of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping is to simultaneously estimate the robot's position and map the environment. By adding Semantics to the feature extraction process, the performance of the system is boosted. The proposed approach detects and recognizes objects in the surroundings, augmenting the visualization of the environment. Additionally, Image color analysis is performed to improve object recognition. The final result is a set of three-dimensional displays that provide a more comprehensive representation of the environment. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing the performance of Feature-based Visual SLAM. The addition of semantics improves the robustness and accuracy of the system, making it suitable for various applications in robotics, such as navigation and exploration.

The development of resistance-based embedded non-volatile memories as synaptic devices has been of great interest in the field of neuromorphics research. These devices, also known as memristors, are capable of emulating the behavior of synapses in biological neural networks. By using non-volatile memory, they are able to retain their state even in the absence of power, making them an attractive option for hardware implementation. The use of memristors as synaptic devices has shown promise in improving the efficiency and performance of spiking neural networks, which are commonly used in the field of neuromorphic engineering. This paper explores the potential of memristors as an alternative to traditional electronic synapses in spiking neural networks, highlighting their ability to perform a wide range of functions, from simple binary operations to more complex learning algorithms. Overall, the development of resistance-based embedded non-volatile memories as synaptic devices represents a promising step towards more efficient and high-performing hardware implementations of neuronal networks.

This paper proposes a sophisticated optimization algorithm for obtaining a group trading strategy portfolio, with a focus on determining stop-loss and take-profit points. The optimization algorithm draws inspiration from various fields, including biology, sociology, statistics, task analysis, and genetic algorithms. A portfolio of different trading strategies is optimized to maximize profitability while minimizing risk. The stop-loss and take-profit points for each strategy are also optimized to ensure optimal risk management. The proposed algorithm advances the optimization techniques used in portfolio management and trading strategy development, providing a more comprehensive and accurate approach. The algorithm's success is demonstrated through backtesting and out-of-sample testing. Overall, this research contributes to the development of more effective trading strategy portfolios and risk management techniques.

Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease. Early diagnosis will considerably decrease the risk of further deterioration. Unfortunately, current studies mainly focus on classifying the states of disease in its current stage, instead of predicting the possible development of the disease. Long short-term memory (LSTM) is a special kind of recurrent neural network, which might be able to connect previous information to the present task. Noticing that the temporal data for a patient are potentially meaningful for predicting the development of the disease, we propose a predicting model based on LSTM. Therefore an LSTM network, with fully connected layer and activation layers, is built to encode the temporal relation between features and the next stage of Alzheimer's Disease. The Experiments show that our model outperforms most of the existing models.

This paper explores Cumulative Citation Recommendation (CCR) for Knowledge Base Acceleration (KBA). The CCR task aims to detect potential citations of a set of target entities with priorities from a volume of temporally-ordered stream corpus. Previous approaches for CCR that build an individual relevance model for each entity fail to deal with unseen entities without annotation. A compromised solution is to build a global entity-unspecific model for all entities without respect to the relationship information among entities, which cannot guarantee achieving a satisfactory result for each entity. Moreover, most previous methods can not adequately exploit prior knowledge embedded in entities or documents due to considering all kinds of features indifferently. In this paper, we propose a novel entity and document class-dependent discriminative mixture model by introducing one intermediate layer to model the correlation between entity-document pairs and hybrid latent entity-document classes. The model can better adjust to different types of entities and documents, and achieve better performance when dealing with a broad range of entity and document classes. An extensive set of experiments has been conducted on two offical datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model can achieve the state-of-the-art performance.

This paper discusses the adaptation of machine learning grid prediction models for forecasting of resources on the clouds. The focus is on predictive models, adaptation models, analytical models, data models, computational modeling, cloud computing, and prediction algorithms. By adapting and applying machine learning grid prediction models to cloud computing, businesses and individuals can forecast more accurately and allocate resources accordingly. This paper provides insight into the various models and algorithms used in cloud computing prediction, and outlines how machine learning models can be used to improve prediction accuracy. It also discusses the challenges faced in adapting these models and provides solutions to overcome them. The research conducted in this paper underscores the importance of machine learning in cloud computing and highlights the potential impact it can have on resource allocation and management.

In this paper, we propose a novel generative model with Bounded-GAN for the reliability classification of gear safety. The model leverages the power of generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create synthetic data that resembles the real data, and introduces a bounding mechanism to ensure that the synthetic data conforms to the characteristics of the real data. We apply this model to the task of gear safety reliability classification with the aim of improving the accuracy of classification results. Our approach involves collecting gear safety data, constructing a data model, and using the generators to generate synthetic data based on the real data. The generators incorporated in our model use a Gallium Nitride (GaN) power amplifier to provide improved coherence and efficiency. By conducting experiments on a benchmark dataset, we demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing methods in accuracy and reliability classification of gear safety. Our proposed model has important implications for improving the safety of gear systems and other related industries.

This paper proposes an expert speed controller based on Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK)-fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for remotely located solar photovoltaic (PV)-wind-battery energy storage (BES) based microgrid system. The TSKFLC tunes the proportional and integral gains of the proportional integral (PI) controller. The conventional PI controller suffers from the drawbacks of high overshoot and narrow bandwidth during dynamic conditions. These issues are resolved by continuously tuning the controller gains. The TSKFLC adapted PI controller takes the speed error and the change in speed error as input and provides the adjusted gain parameters of the PI controller according to the operating conditions. The reference speed of the wind turbine driven synchronous generator (SG) is obtained using perturb and observe (P&O) maximum power point (MPP) technique, which perturbs the generator speed in the direction of optimal power. The double stage solar PV array with an intermediate boost converter, utilizes an incremental conductance (InC) MPP scheme for maximum power extraction. The flexible power flow is allowed by using a battery at the DC link. A prototype is developed in the laboratory and tested in accordance to IEEE519 standard under steady state and dynamic conditions including variable wind speeds, changing insolation and load removal.

Cognitive impairment is one of the crucial problems elderly people face. Tracking their daily life activities and detecting early indicators of cognitive decline would be necessary for further diagnosis. Depending on the decline magnitude, monitoring may need to be done over long periods of time to detect abnormal behaviour. In the absence of training data, it would be helpful to learn the normal behaviour and daily life patterns of a (cognitively) healthy person and use them as a basis for tracking other patients. In this paper, we propose to investigate Recursive Auto-Encoders (RAE)-based transfer learning to cope with the problem of scarcity of data in the context of abnormal behaviour detection. We present a method for generating synthetic data to reflect on some behavior of people with dementia. An RAE model is trained on data of a healthy person in a source household. Then, the resulting RAE is used to detect abnormal behavior in a target house. To evaluate the proposed approach, we compare the results with the-state-of-the-art supervised methods. The results indicate that transfer learning is promising when there is lack of training data.

Text categorization has become a critical task in recent years, especially with the rise of email communication. The use of Naïve Bayes method for classifying text-based email has become increasingly popular, particularly in postal services that require efficient email filtering. The success of this approach depends heavily on the quality of training data used for the model. However, given the vast amount of unsolicited e-mail or spam, many challenges exist in developing accurate text categorization models. Task analysis has played a pivotal role in identifying the important features to consider when building the training data. Despite these challenges, the use of Naïve Bayes method has shown promising results in accurately classifying email with high precision and recall values.

In this paper, we propose a new Perceptually Optimized Embedded ZeroTree Image Coder EVIC and Quality Assessor WVDP. The coder introduces a perceptual weighting to wavelet coefficients prior to control SPIHT encoding algorithm in order to reach a targeted bit rate with a perceptual quality improvement with respect to the coding quality of the SPIHT algorithm only. The paper also, introduces a new objective quality metric based on Daly visual model known as Visible Difference Predictor that integrates the properties of the HVS and plays an important role in our EVIC quality assessment. Our EVIC coder is based on a vision model that incorporates various masking effects of human visual system HVS perception. Thus, our coder weights the wavelet coefficients based on that model and enhances the perceptual quality for a given bit rate and observation distance. The model weights within all wavelet sub bands are computed with respect to 1) luminance masking and Contrast masking deployed to ensure threshold elevation, 2) the contrast sensitivity function CSF to filter invisible frequencies, 3) the Just Noticeable Differences JND used to take into account only wavelet coefficients with respect to that perceptual thresholds. The EVIC coder has the same computational algorithm complexity as the standard SPIHT. However, the experimental results show that it demonstrates very good performances in terms of image coding and quality measurement.

Over the past years, various anomaly detection techniques for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have been proposed in the literature. These detectors are generally only effective against particular security threats and thus many detectors have to be executed to ensure high-level security in WSNs. Due to the hardware limitations, WSNs cannot execute all of these detectors simultaneously. Thus, WSNs have to appropriately schedule when to execute a particular detector and when to execute the others. This paper presents an optimized solution by providing a unified framework that combines the usage of a costly yet highly-accurate detector, called an oracle detector, and a low cost and less-accurate detector, called a partial detector. A detection pattern is created and optimized using a first-order approximation method. Simulation results show that combining several detectors into an optimized pattern is essential to provide low execution time overhead.

Natural disasters are a major threat in Japan. It is convenient to have disaster prevention education as e-learning for distribution to many people each year, but this type of material needs to be revisited and reviewed a number of times before it can be recalled instantly at a later date, for example in an emergency situation. In this research, we apply visual novel design techniques to disaster prevention learning contents and develop an e-learning system with a gamification element for estimating how long it will take for the information learned to be forgotten. That is, we indicate to users not only how well they are progressing with the e-learning units and quizzes, but also how their information retention fitness is regressing if they do not revisit the material for long periods of time.

Piezoelectric shunt damping is a technique for vibration suppression by connecting an external circuit called the shunt circuit to a piezoelectric element attached to a mechanical structure. Many previous studies consider only a single mode for designing shunt circuits. However, the vibration of actual structures typically includes multiple vibration modes. It is consequently necessary to consider multiple modes toward designing a high-performance vibration control system. This paper proposes a method for estimating multiple-mode parameters of a piezoelectric structure, which is composed of a piezoelectric element and a flexible structure. The proposed multiple-mode parameter estimation method is derived by expanding a previously proposed method for single-mode parameter estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed estimation method is verified by experiments.

We propose a scheme for calculation of indoor evacuation routes of a single-floor building in the event of a fire that uses selection of a potentially safe exit before evacuation starts. We refer to potentially safe exits to those that have high probability of being accessible at evacuation time. The scheme pre-calculates whether an exit may be reached by an occupant before being reached by the fire. Among those exits, the one with the shortest distance to the occupant is selected. This exit pre-selection improves evacuation success ratio by avoiding destination changes during evacuation. This approach is applicable to a building where the floor plan is known and analyzable. With such an evacuation routing scheme, we study the applicability of our approach to cases where the floor plan has not been characterized and yet we may be able to perform route calculation in a fast manner. To do so, we use machine learning with data obtained from a floor plan where the evacuation success ratio has been analyzed and apply it on the new floor plan. This approach indicates floor plan similarities and it is used to rapidly estimate evacuation routes with high probability of a successful evacuation. We show how floor similarity accuracy estimation increases with the use of data from an increasing number of analyzed floor plans.

Security of the critical infrastructure of automated process control system under the conditions of the automation level of modern production in the Russian Federation and around the world is becoming an increasing priority and is one of the most important components of the digital economy. The attacks of malicious persons are constantly improving, becoming combined and spread almost instantly. Intrusion detection systems implement monitoring functions and detect attacks that have bypassed the firewall. The means to ensure the information security of process control systems at this stage of their development are not able to withstand such threats. To solve this problem, network attacks detection systems based on the use of artificial intelligence methods is proposed. The research describes the analysis of modern approaches to the network attacks detection, structure of detection system based on data mining methods and comparison between different data mining algorithms.

This paper proposes the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for Hand Gesture Recognition (HGR) using 8 different Electromyography (EMG) signals. EMG Sensors are utilized to record muscle signals and transformed into raw data that is subsequently processed and analyzed. CNNs have been chosen for their ability to learn and recognize patterns in large amounts of data, with Convolution as their key feature for filtration of signal noise. To train the CNNs, a specialized database is constructed, which provides a diverse set of EMG signals as well as their corresponding hand gestures. The results demonstrate high recognition rates indicating the potential of CNN-based HGR systems. Future work will address the expansion of the database and the refinement of the CNN architecture to further improve recognition rates.

This paper proposes an SMS advisory system for medical assistance by using a neuro fuzzy system. The system is designed to assist in the diagnosis of cancer by utilizing fuzzy logic and medical diagnostic imaging. Computer architecture is an integral part of the system, providing the necessary processing power to achieve accurate diagnoses. Training is also crucial, as the system must learn how to properly interpret medical data in order to make accurate suggestions. The implementation of robots within the system enhances its capabilities, allowing for faster and more accurate analysis. Overall, this SMS advisory system offers an innovative approach to medical assistance and has the potential to greatly benefit the healthcare industry.

This paper analyzes the common text clustering algorithm and text representation model for the hot topics found in the campus. Through the use of the word segmentation system, the text word segmentation and keyword extraction are proposed, and a knowledge representation model of the message text is proposed. The study of vector space model uses the word frequency of statistical messages to determine k initial clustering centers and improve the optimization algorithm k-Means. The detailed process and concrete steps of the hot topic discovery algorithm are given, and the topic discovery module is verified. The experimental results show that the intelligent topic clustering process can be processed faster and better, and the clustering accuracy can be kept high when the number of reported messages is large.

In this paper, we propose a new nonconvex design algorithm for optimal polynomial fuzzy control of nonlinear systems. The algorithm aims to find an upper bound on the cost function of the control system using a Takagi-Sugeno model. We use a nonconvex optimization approach to minimize the upper bound of the cost function, which has been shown to be effective in fuzzy control design. Our approach can handle a wide range of nonlinear systems with uncertainties and achieve optimal control performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulation results on a series of benchmark examples. Overall, our algorithm provides a new and efficient method for designing polynomial fuzzy controllers in control systems.

In this paper, we propose an efficient free-form contour packing method based on a code matching strategy. The proposed method utilizes shape and feature extraction algorithms to extract important information from the input layout, shapes, and raw materials. Heuristic algorithms are then used to optimize the packing layout and minimize material waste. Machining is also taken into account during the packing process to ensure efficient and accurate manufacturing. Clustering algorithms are employed to group similar shapes and materials to further improve the packing efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in terms of saving material and reducing manufacturing time, thus providing a practical solution for optimizing packing layout for various manufacturing scenarios.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and software testing has brought significant changes to the software industry. Software testing is a critical phase in the software development process, and the introduction of AI has contributed to its optimization. AI provides software testing with a range of tools and techniques that streamline the process, improving test accuracy and minimizing human error. In software testing, AI has been utilized to develop machine learning algorithms that can analyze data and identify patterns to enhance software algorithms. The use of AI in software testing has become increasingly more prevalent and is expected to become even more pervasive in the future. In conclusion, the impact of AI on software testing has been tremendous, and the benefits of AI-powered testing are undeniable. With software testing being an essential component of software development, integrating AI in the software testing process is a welcome advancement, offering developers and engineers efficient ways to test their software and improve upon their designs.

This paper presents a method for controlling industrial robotic systems based on received visual information. The main focus is to utilize three-dimensional displays and fitting algorithms to accurately estimate the position and orientation of objects in the robot's working space. The proposed method is aimed at developing service robots that can assist humans in a wide range of tasks. Visual information is captured by cameras mounted on the robot, and is processed using libraries such as OpenCV and PCL. The aim is to develop a reliable and efficient method for controlling industrial robots based on visual feedback, which would enable robots to carry out more sophisticated tasks in the manufacturing industry. Overall, the proposed method has the potential to significantly enhance the capabilities of service robots, and improve their adoption in various domains.

This study aims to realize a tactile display which can represent 2D haptic information on the display surface. The tactile display typically consists of a lot of compact linear actuators. In order to represent the haptic information on the display, the motion of the actuator should be controlled. The position sensor is usually attached to the actuator to derive the position information. However, the sensor makes the system large and expensive. Therefore, the sensorless control technique is effective to reduce the size and cost. In our previous works, a position estimation method for a compact dual solenoid actuator was proposed. In this paper, the position control with the estimated position feedback is proposed. Additionally, a disturbance observer is applied to achieve robust position control. The frequency characteristics of the sensorless position control was experimentally investigated. The results indicated that the sensorless position control was accurately achieved when a sinusoidal position command whose frequency was less than 2.0 Hz was applied. This proposal is useful since the compact actuation system is realized.

In this paper, we discuss the application of emerging NVM (Non-Volatile Memory) devices such as Phase Change Memory (PCM), OxRAM (oxide based), and magneto resisitive STT-MRAM memory in System-on-Chip (SoC) used for IoT-WSN (Wireless Sensor Node) applications. We validate the concept of a unified memory architecture relying on all NVM implementation, in particular for IoT-WSN applications. Simulation and analysis for NVM based unified memory architecture are presented on MSP430 platform with Contiki, benchmarked for the Sky-Collect application. Performance parameters such asarea, write hits, write hit rate/evolution, power and latency are considered.

Gas sensor arrays are widely used in various fields like environmental monitoring, food packaging and medical applications. The QBC algorithm is one of the most commonly used techniques for data processing in gas sensor array systems. However, a major challenge in QBC algorithm is the sampling strategy used for data acquisition which can heavily influence the accuracy of the results. In this paper, we propose an improved sampling strategy for the QBC algorithm. The proposed strategy is based on a machine learning technique called data mining and it aims to enhance the Q measurement accuracy in gas detector signal processing. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments using a gas sensor array system. The results show that the proposed method significantly improves the QBC algorithm's performance in terms of accuracy and speed. These findings suggest that the proposed technique could potentially be applied to other information systems with sensor arrays, and could be a promising solution for enhancing the performance of sensor array systems in a variety of applications. This paper is presented at the conference titled "Conferences".

Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems are becoming increasingly popular, encompassing a number of different applications such as electric vehicle charging and medical implants. However, WPT systems can be vulnerable to foreign objects which can cause significant damage or even complete system failure. Therefore, a combined foreign object detection and live object protection technique is proposed in this study via real-time thermal camera analysis. The proposed approach involves image reconstruction, sensor technology, and the use of neural networks trained by real-time system data to detect and protect against foreign and live objects in WPT systems. The system also utilizes specially designed coils to minimize the impact of the foreign object on the system. Results demonstrate that this approach can effectively mitigate the impact of foreign objects on WPT systems and provide real-time protection for live objects.

ACVAE-VC is a technique for non-parallel voice conversion that utilizes the auxiliary classifier variational autoencoder. This algorithm is capable of decoding acoustic features in order to convert speech into a different voice, without requiring parallel data to train. The training process for the ACVAE-VC involves optimizing the objective function, which includes an auxiliary classifier to improve the classification accuracy. This technology has potential applications for speech recognition and other speech-related fields. Additionally, the use of gallium nitride generators in conjunction with artificial neural networks can improve the performance and efficiency of the ACVAE-VC.

This paper presents a robust model predictive controller for discrete-time nonlinear systems, subject to state and input constraints and unknown but bounded input disturbances. The prediction model uses a linearized time-varying version of the original discrete-time system. The proposed optimization problem includes the initial state of the current nominal model of the system as an optimization variable, which allows to guarantee robust exponential stability of a disturbance invariant set for the discrete-time nonlinear system. From simulations, it is possible to verify the proposed algorithm is real-time capable, since the problem is convex and posed as a quadratic program.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly growing field that involves connecting various devices and sensors to the internet in order to enable real-time monitoring and management. However, one of the biggest challenges in this field is the presence of fog, which can disrupt data transmission and cause delays. In order to overcome this challenge, peer-to-peer (P2P) computing can be used as a potential solution. P2P computing involves the distribution of resources and data across multiple devices, thus allowing for efficient data transmission through the fog. In addition, other technologies such as cloud computing, computer architecture, edge computing, wireless sensor networks, and protocols can be used in conjunction with P2P computing to further enhance the performance of IoT systems in foggy environments. Overall, by leveraging P2P computing and other complementary technologies, it is possible to achieve more efficient and reliable IoT systems in foggy environments.

India is a country in which agriculture plays a wide role with around 70% of its population is dependent on agriculture good in direct or indirect way. The agricultural sector contributes about 14% to GDP of India. As the population is increasing, demand for crops is also increasing day by day. About all suicides in India farmer suicide accounts for 11.2%. There are many reasons given for farmer suicides like inadequate monsoon rainfall, interest rate is high, certain government policies are not in welfare, mental health issues, personal and family problems. It is also noticed that even the states are responsible for manipulating certain statistics. this research work uses data mining clustering technique to group attributes that results in low crop production. Case studies are conducted to map and co-relate the low crop production, monsoon factors along with farmer suicidal data. The states are affected most is identified and further analysed.

This paper presents an adaptive sliding mode observer design for a class of T-S fuzzy descriptor fractional order systems. Observers are widely used in control systems to estimate the state variables of a system. However, designing observers for fuzzy systems is challenging due to the nonlinearities inherent in fuzzy models. In this work, the T-S fuzzy model is used to describe the system and the observer is designed using fractional calculus. The proposed observer is adaptive, which means that it is able to track changes in the system's dynamics over time. The design is based on linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), which are tools commonly used in control system design to ensure that a desired set of conditions is satisfied. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for estimating the state variables of nonlinear systems described by T-S fuzzy models.

In this paper, a VLSI design of a bit-serial artificial neuron circuit is proposed. Different from the ordinary bit-serial architectures which usually start from the least significant bit (LSB), the proposed design will start from processing the most significant bit (MSB). For the MSB-first approach, the more significant part of results will be generated earlier, and the intermediate results will be progressively refined by processing the less significant bits. An artificial neuron is equipped with an activation function at the output, and many common used activation functions such as sigmoid, a rectified linear unit (ReLU) etc will saturate to 0 for large negative inputs. Some will saturate to 1 for large positive inputs. Therefore, when the intermediate results are positive or negative enough, the remaining processing of less significant bits can be neglected. Our preliminary results shows that the approximation results due to the proposed early termination can still lead to the same classification accuracy as the full precision, but the processing cycles can be reduced by more than 25%. The proposed methodology can be applied to the design of hardware accelerators for those machine learning networks based on neurons such as neural network (NN) and convolution NN (CNN).

This paper evaluates the effects of using a cartoon-like character with emotions on users' behavior within virtual reality environments. The study aimed to investigate whether the presence of such a character could influence users' engagement and interaction within these virtual environments. The research was conducted through a series of simulation-based experiments, which involved participants interacting with the character within a virtual reality setting. The results show that the use of a cartoon-like character with emotions can have a positive impact on users' behavior, leading to increased engagement and interaction. This research has important implications for the development of virtual reality environments and artificial intelligence technologies, highlighting the potential benefits of incorporating emotional elements into these systems. The findings also have relevance for academic and professional conferences, where virtual reality and artificial intelligence are increasingly becoming important topics of study and discussion.

Epilepsy is one of the most prevalent neurological issues faced by a large population around the globe. Epilepsy is marked by intermittent seizures, the detection of which can be a challenging problem. Therefore, reliably detecting the onset of seizures has evoked the interest of researchers over the last few years. Major leaps in the domain of machine learning, signal processing methods, and computational capabilities have made it a tractable task. In this paper, we apply multi-resolution dynamic mode decomposition (MRDMD), which is a data-driven dimensionality reduction technique, on the problem of epileptic seizure detection. This method can effectively separate a complex non-linear system into a collection of time-scale components at different resolutions. We have applied this algorithm on two different scalp EEG datasets, i.e., CHB-MIT and KU Leaven datasets. We have applied necessary post-processing steps to reduce the false alarm rate and boost the sensitivity and specificity. A detailed analysis of the results has been presented for the proposed method applied to both the datasets. The algorithm achieves a sensitivity of 0.937 and 0.96, a specificity of 0.99 and 0.99, a false alarm rate of 0.587 and 0.413 per hour, and a latency of 3.12 and 2.75 s for CHB-MIT and KU Leuven, respectively. The results indicate that the multi-resolution analysis yields a significant improvement in sensitivity compared with the basic dynamic mode decomposition.

While access to a variety of Internet of Things (IoT) networks can be achieved through end-user devices such as smartphones or tablets, these devices are susceptible to theft or loss, and their use by illicit users could lead to unauthorized access to IoT networks, thus allowing access to user information. Hence, an effective authentication mechanism that continuously authenticates users in the background is required in order to detect unauthorized access. As most access to IoT devices is achieved through end-user devices, a rich set of information can be extracted and used in the background to continuously authenticate users without requiring further user intervention. Several studies have examined mobile app usage in the broader population but failed to consider network traffic patterns during app access for user authentication. This paper presents a model to authenticate users based on the network traffic patterns of accessed apps, with an average F-measure of 95.5%. Overall, the preliminary results are promising and show the effectiveness and usability of the proposed model.

In the past few years, Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) has standardized "lightweight" IPv4/IPv6 protocol variations for Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) on resource constrained devices. In the above approaches, security is considered a strong requirement, however, adapting IP oriented security protocols (like the IETF Data-gram Transport Layer Protocol DTLS) to actual WSN security enabled implementations requires tradeoffs between performance, energy consumption and security level. In this paper, the above tradeoffs are explored for the latest version of the widely accepted Contiki OS (version 3.x) when DTLS security is enabled for the IETF supported Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP). More specifically, the DTLS framework is integrated in the Contiki 3 CoAP stack for 2 different cipher suites and the performance in comparison with non secure CoAP applications is evaluated through simulation, in terms of speed, memory overhead and energy consumption for various WSN clientserver network environment. Finally, tradeoff and recommendation for balanced performance versus security are proposed.

In-memory computing with nanoscale memristive devices such as phase-change memory (PCM) has emerged as an alternative to conventional von Neumann systems to train deep neural networks (DNN) where a synaptic weight is represented by the device conductance. However, PCM devices exhibit temporal evolution of the conductance values referred to as the conductance drift, which poses challenges for maintaining synaptic weights reliably. Based on the mean behavior of 10,000 GST-based PCM devices, we observe that the drift coefficient is dependent on the conductance value. Moreover, we show that PCM drift is re-initialized and the drift history is erased after the application of even partial SET pulses. This is regardless of how much the device has drifted. With models capturing these features, we show that drift has a detrimental impact on training DNNs, but drift resilience can be significantly improved with a recently proposed multi-PCM synaptic architecture.

This paper proposes a method for maximizing the utilization of allocated power for scheduling of smart home appliances. Home appliances play a crucial role in our daily lives, and with the increasing pace of technological advancements, they have become smarter and more connected than ever before. However, the power demand of these appliances could lead to power shortages if not coordinated effectively. Hence, Electromagnetic Compatibility-based (EMC) aggregates are employed to ensure efficient usage of power among these appliances. Artificial neural networks are utilized for the generation of optimized schedules based on the filling of these EMC aggregates. This paper presents the effectiveness of this approach by conducting extensive simulations on a realistic smart home scenario. The results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved maximum utilization of allocated power, leading to efficient power utilization and reduction in electricity bills for homeowners.

Mutual coupling, which is caused by a tight inter sensor spacing in uniform linear arrays (ULAs), will, to a certain extent, affect the estimation result for source localisation. To address the problem, sparse arrays such as coprime array and nested array are considered to achieve less mutual coupling and more uniform degrees-of-freedom (DoFs) than ULAs.
