However, there are holes in coprime arrays leading to a decrease of uniform DoFs and in a nested array, some sensors may still be located so closely that the influence of mutual coupling between sensors remains significant. This paper proposes a new Loosely Distributed Nested Array (LoDiNA), which is designed in a three-level nested configuration and the three layers are linked end-to-end with a longer inter-element separation. It is proved that LoDiNA can generate a higher number of uniform DoFs with greater robustness against mutual coupling interference and simpler configurations, as compared to existing nested arrays. The feasibility of the proposed LoDiNA structure is demonstrated for Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation for multiple stationarysources with noise.

Mobile cloud computing technology enables users to cooperate with each other so that their mobile devices' resources can be integrated together to afford complicated application, such as machine auto-translation and image processing, which can always be represented as Directed Acyclic Graphs. On mobile clouds, due to the social relationships of mobile devices' owners, networks on mobile clouds are always complex and consist of multiple sub-networks intersecting at several joint devices. In these complex networks, joint devices can communicate with all devices of their related multiple sub-networks, whereas the other devices can only contact devices in the same sub-network. In this paper, we study the workflow task scheduling problem in the aforementioned complex networks on mobile clouds, and formulate it as Integer Programming problem that is generally NP-Hard. Due to the constraint of each device's power capacity, the dependence among tasks in a workflow and the network complexity, it is too difficult to achieve feasible scheduling solutions for the considered problem. To solve this problem, we propose an Improved Round-Robin scheduling algorithm (IRR) and an Improved Greedy scheduling algorithm (IG) with the consideration of workflow tasks' features. Experimental results show that our proposed IRR and IG guarantee to achieve feasible solutions, whereas the General Round-Robin scheduling algorithm (GRR) does with the probability of 2.3%. Moreover, experimental results also indicate that IG outperforms IRR.

This paper presents a new pricing strategy called Dealer for Deep-Learning-as-a-Service (DLaaS) providers. With the growing demand for graphics processing units (GPUs) in cloud computing, resource management and scheduling become critical issues. The proposed strategy leverages task analysis and virtualization to allocate resources efficiently, minimizing costs while maximizing profits. By modeling customer behavior, the Dealer strategy can dynamically adjust prices and resources allocation to match the demand while maintaining profitability. The results of experiments conducted on a real-world dataset demonstrate that Dealer can significantly reduce the operational costs while maintaining a high level of service quality. This paper contributes to the field of DLaaS by providing a practical and effective pricing strategy that balances customer needs and financial goals.

In order to achieve efficient communication in the fifth generation (5G) networks, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique has been utilized in fog radio access networks (F-RANs). In this paper, we investigate the resource allocation problem in a NOMA-enabled downlink F-RAN. To maximize the weighted sum rate of NOMA users served by fog-computing-based access points (F-APs), the resource block (RB) allocation and power allocation are optimized. Specifically, we decouple the problem into RB allocation and power allocation problems. The former is modeled as a many-to-one matching game and we propose a modified swap-enabled matching algorithm to solve it, which takes interference threshold into consideration. The later is a non-convex problem, we transform it into a tractable one via some approximations and get the closed-form expressions of power allocation coefficients. Finally, we combine the both to propose a joint resource allocation algorithm, which is preformed iteratively to obtain the optimal result. Simulation results are provided to show the performance of the algorithm.

Spectrum is a scarce and precious resource in a battlefield. Multiple frequencies spread over different bands are available for usage in a battlefield. The frequencies need to be assigned to the nodes/Base Stations(BSs) in a battlefield in such a way as to meet the Signal-to-Interference-Noise Ratio(SINR) and throughput requirements of all the users. Previous attempts for frequency assignment abstract away the notion of SINR and throughput and usually constrain the distance between the frequencies required between pairs of interfering BSs. In this work, the frequency assignment that optimizes the SINR and throughput of all the users in a system while ensuring fairness among the users is found. A genetic algorithm is used to perform the unconstrained optimization and this method is termed as the efficient rate and SINR matcher with hyperbolic cost (ERSMHC). A high SINR initialization algorithm (HSIA) and a high throughput greedy rate matching algorithm (HTGRM) that can be used for quickly initializing the system are also presented. The ERSMHC algorithm is shown to aid in meeting the stipulated rate and throughput requirements of more number of users as compared to HSIA and HTGRM.

A Hybrid Trust Management Heuristic has been proposed for VANETs, which are a type of ad hoc network consisting of vehicles as nodes. Trust management is crucial in the security of VANETs, and the heuristic utilizes both peer-to-peer computing and computational modeling to achieve this. A mathematical model is used to evaluate the trustworthiness of vehicles in the network, based on observations of their behavior. Data models are also employed, which take into account factors such as the number of times a vehicle has been observed and the distance it has traveled. Adaptation models are used to adjust the trust values of a vehicle over time, based on changes in its behavior. The resulting hybrid approach has been demonstrated to be effective in improving the security of VANETs, by both reducing the impact of malicious nodes and increasing the reliability of trustworthy ones.

Based on the background of DC normal education project in the Jinji Lake core area of Suzhou Industrial Park, this paper discusses the key technologies in the practice of multi-terminal DC power distribution technology engineering. Firstly, the basic situation of Suzhou four-terminal DC project was outlined, and the key electrical equipment and its selection principle were analyzed, including the converter valves, bridge arm reactors, link transformers, and DC monitoring and protection systems. Secondly, based on the RTLAB real-time simulation platform, the simulation model of Suzhou four-terminal DC distribution system was built. Finally, based on the RTLAB simulation model, single-ended converter startup, four-terminal stable operation, active power step and reactive power step were simulated. The simulation results show that the four-terminal DC grid model has good steady state performance and active power and reactive power step response performance. It can provide reference for the future DC distribution network construction.

Convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithms are utilized to build a machine learning block to assist the optimizations of voltage noise, temperature distribution, and security of multi-phase on-chip switched-capacitor (SC) voltage converters. All the random sequences generated by the pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) are fed into the designed machine learning block in an SC converter sequentially to filter the unsatisfactory sequences. The results show that the maximum amplitude of the voltage noise and the highest temperature of the SC converter are reduced by 68.98% and 12.07%, respectively, while a negligible security degradation is achieved under the assistance of machine learning.

A bio-inspired optimisation technique to design recursive digital fractional order differentiator (DFOD) is presented in this paper. The proposed Bat Algorithm (BA) based optimised DFOD can operate over a full band, i.e., over the entire Nyquist frequency range. Design performance and efficiency of BA is extensively compared with an advanced variant of particle swarm optimisation algorithm. Comparisons with the published designs validate the superior modelling accuracy of the proposed model.

In this paper, we propose an improved epilepsy detection method by addressing the class imbalance problem within the dataset. The method involves measuring noise in the signals and using computational modeling techniques in computer science to develop support vector machines (SVM) and prediction algorithms to identify the presence of epilepsy in patient data. The training of the SVM is done with a focus on mitigating the negative effects of class imbalance by making use of specialized techniques. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and sensitivity in the detection of epilepsy. This study contributes to the advancement of epilepsy detection methods and holds promise for enhancing diagnosis and treatment in clinical settings.

Behavior recognition using motion sensors is getting prominence over other systems such as e-healthcare and life-log analysis systems especially in the healthcare domain for improving life expectancy and healthcare access. Accelerometers have been used in smart environments to recognize behavior since the last decade but heavy computation involved in recognizer model made them less acceptable. This paper proposed a computationally less expensive model with better recognition results for improved human behavior understanding system. Hierarchical features are used to ensure robustness as a performance attribute in the proposed system. These hierarchical features involve statistical features like signal magnitude, abrupt changes, and temporal variation among coordinates. Moreover, the extracted features are examined through the process of learning, training, and symbolization with the help of linear support vector machine. The examination of our recognition results based on feature extraction strategy show that our model excels others in terms of accuracy and computation time. The proposed system should be considered as a recommendation for systems involving human behavior recognition i.e. kindergarten, elderly at old-age houses and patients with Parkinson diseases.

F-RAN, as a promising technology to achieve low latency and high spectral and energy efficiency, has attracted significant attention. Although performance analysis and resource allocation for F-RANs have been well researched, performance emulation based on a testbed is still challenging. In this article, a testbed for F-RANs has been designed and implemented based on OAI. In order to present the prototype implementation and emulation results, a high-definition video acquisition demonstration based on F-RANs has been built. Given that AI-enabled techniques can cope with dynamic network environments and intractable performance evaluation with low complexity, both an edge caching driven redirection mechanism and transmission mode selection have been evaluated, and the corresponding AI-enabled video quality assessment has been analyzed. The emulation results show that HDV acquisition in F-RANs can reduce both end-to-end latency and frame loss rate while maintaining high video quality.

Cloud computing has emerged as a popular paradigm for delivering computing resources as services over the internet. With the growing popularity of cloud computing, scheduling workflows on cloud platforms has become increasingly vital to improve the performance of cloud-based applications. In this regard, scheduling algorithms based on memetics have proven to be effective in cloud computing environments. Memetics involves the computational modeling of biological evolution to develop efficient scheduling algorithms. These algorithms are designed by combining different evolutionary computation techniques, such as task analysis, genetic algorithms, and processor scheduling. The aim is to optimize the allocation of tasks to various virtual machines and to minimize the overall makespan. This paper presents an overview of memetic scheduling algorithms and their applications in cloud computing. The study analyzes various memetic algorithms for scheduling tasks on different types of cloud environments, such as public cloud, private cloud, and hybrid cloud. The result of this study provides insights into the significance of memetic scheduling algorithms in cloud computing and their potential in addressing the challenges of task scheduling in cloud environments.

Self-driving perception is an extremely important field of research that is becoming increasingly relevant as autonomous cars are developed. One major challenge in this field is the acquisition of datasets for training the perception algorithms that will be needed by these vehicles. Fortunately, video games provide an excellent source of such datasets, as they are realistic and engaging environments that can be used to create a wide range of driving scenarios. This paper proposes a method for obtaining datasets for self-driving perception from video games automatically. The method involves extracting graphics and image segmentation data from the games using cameras and data mining techniques. This data can then be used to train neural networks that can recognize and identify different types of automobiles and other objects on the road. Furthermore, the data can also be used to learn the semantics of the scenes, such as road signs, traffic lights, and other important objects. By using video games as a source of training data, researchers can obtain large amounts of high-quality data that can be used to develop highly accurate and effective self-driving perception algorithms.

In this paper, we consider the uplink channel parameter estimation problem in the presence of pilot contamination for massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems. We propose a parallel factor (PARAFAC)-based estimation scheme, which exploits the low-rank property of massive MIMO channels caused by the finite scattering in a physical environment. Specifically, we first parameterize the channel in terms of three parameters, i.e., fading coefficients, directions of arrival (DOAs), and delays; thereby, the channel is characterized via three equivalent PARAFAC models. Then, the proposed PARAFAC-based scheme is developed, which jointly estimates these three channel parameters using an alternating least squares (ALS) algorithm. Therein, we certify the identifiability of the three channel parameters of the PARAFAC models to mitigate the pilot contamination and state the convergence of the ALS algorithm, which guarantees that the three channel parameters can be uniquely determined with the proposed scheme. Moreover, to further reduce the computational complexity, two advanced schemes are proposed by antenna selection and reducing the estimation frequency of DOAs and delays, respectively. Simulation results show that the proposed schemes can achieve both low computational complexities and close to optimal Cramer-Rao Bound performance.

This paper introduces a human-centric cloud and fog-assisted IoT platform for disaster management. The platform incorporates cloud computing and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to facilitate disaster preparedness, response, and recovery. The sheer scale of disaster management operations demands the use of scalable and reliable servers, which are provided through cloud computing. Wireless sensor networks and wireless communication protocols enable real-time data collection, analysis, and dissemination. Sensors, particularly ultra-low power devices, play a crucial role in detecting and monitoring various disaster-related parameters. The introduction of the fog computing paradigm aims to overcome limitations arising from resource depletion or network disruptions caused by disasters. The platform extends beyond automation by incorporating human-centered design principles and situational awareness to enhance human-machine collaboration for accurate and timely decision-making, which is essential for effective disaster management.

This paper presents a deep learning network for lip reading that integrates multi-modal sensor information from visual and auditory sources. The proposed system leverages voltage control to regulate spiking activity in the sensors and employs sensor fusion to combine the information from different modalities. The feature extraction process is based on Mel frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), which are computed using both visual and auditory inputs. The network is trained using a large dataset of lip movements and speech sounds, resulting in high accuracy lip reading performance. The lip-related features extracted are shown to be useful for other speech-related tasks as well. This work demonstrates the potential of multi-modal spiking sensors and deep learning for developing efficient and accurate lip reading systems.

This paper explores the use of stacked auto-encoders combined with rotation forest for the identification of cell pathology. The approach involves feature extraction using discrete cosine transforms, followed by training with the rotation forest algorithm. The proposed method is applied to biomedical imaging data for the detection of diseases. The results of the study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving accurate classification of cell pathology. The combination of stacked auto-encoders with rotation forest provides a powerful tool for the accurate identification of cell pathology, which has important implications for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. This study highlights the potential benefits of incorporating machine learning techniques into pathology research, and provides a promising avenue for future research in this area.

Kriptosare.gen is a Dockerized Bitcoin testbed that has been developed in order to analyze the performance of servers in a peer-to-peer computing environment. In this paper, we present the results of our measurements of server performance using Kriptosare.gen, and we discuss the implications of these results for the Bitcoin ecosystem. Our analysis focuses on a range of variables including random access memory usage, software configuration, containerization, and computational modeling. The results of our analysis indicate that Kriptosare.gen is an effective tool for measuring the performance of Bitcoin servers in a range of different configurations, and that it has the potential to contribute significantly to the ongoing development of the Bitcoin ecosystem. Furthermore, our findings highlight the importance of resource allocation and software optimization in optimizing server performance within the Bitcoin network. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the challenges and opportunities associated with the development of scalable, high-performance Bitcoin networks in the peer-to-peer computing era.

The article discusses the end-to-end business concept of governance of information technology in the context of e-commerce enterprises as a sector of the digital economy that needs to improve the quality of management and training of targeted personnel. Processes for governance of enterprise IT were considered in accordance with the COBIT 5 methodology. Analysis and selection of IT enterprise management processes in e-commerce was carried out. An adapted CobiT model for ecommerce enterprises and a graphical model of the space of topics and competencies for learning in the digital economy are proposed.

In this paper, a novel approach for efficient endmember extraction for green algae area estimation is proposed, based on the use of cofactor analysis. The technique relies on the identification of key indexes associated with the presence of algae in the ocean, which are then used to segment images acquired by sensors. The proposed method combines the advantages of both image color analysis and data mining, providing a reliable and accurate approach for the estimation of the extent of algal blooms in the ocean. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the monitoring of algal blooms and thus aid in the management of coastal and oceanic ecosystems. The results demonstrate that the use of cofactor-based endmember extraction is superior to traditional approaches, providing a more efficient and reliable means for estimating the extent of algae in the ocean. Overall, this paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of oceanic research, providing a novel approach for efficient endmember extraction for green algae area estimation.

This paper proposes an efficient and accurate approach to model reflectarray unit cells using Support Vector Machines (SVMs). SVMs are used for training the model to achieve an optimal design of antennas. The approach is compared to the traditional Transmission Line Matrix Methods (TLMs) which require a higher amount of simulation time. The proposed model is based on the use of Manganese as a substrate and an acceleration technique is used to optimize its performance. The results show that the SVMs approach can considerably reduce the simulation time while providing accurate results. Therefore, it proves to be an effective method for the design and optimization of reflectarray unit cells for high-frequency applications.

The application of IPv6 in coal mine safety production monitoring has garnered a lot of attention in recent years. As the mining industry continues to grow and expand, the need for more advanced and secure monitoring systems has become increasingly urgent. In response to this need, various monitoring protocols have been developed to ensure the safety and security of coal mining operations. The implementation of IPv6 in such protocols has opened up new possibilities for more efficient and reliable monitoring capabilities. This has become even more important with the increasing importance of the Internet and IP networks in modern production processes. The use of IPv6 in coal mine safety production monitoring has proven to be a powerful tool for enhancing safety and productivity in the mining industry, and will undoubtedly continue to play a key role in future advancements in this area.

Due to the requirements of industrial automation, soft manipulators are increasingly used in machinery manufacturing, metallurgy, and other fields. Typically, a manipulator is only suited to handle objects in ideal dry conditions, which limits the applications of these actuators. To solve the above-mentioned shortcomings in traditional grippers, this paper presents a friction-enhanced soft manipulator that has good flexibility and high interactivity and safety and is also equipped with a bionic nanofiber array film to provide stronger friction under slippery conditions. A polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) nanofiber array film for increasing the friction of the soft manipulator was fabricated. A suitable manufacturing method for preparing the nanofiber array film was presented. The contact angle of the prepared nanofiber array film was measured. The experimental results showed that the soft robot manipulator performs extremely well under slippery conditions.

This paper proposes a method for semi-supervised classification of event streams using denoising autoencoders. The main objective of this method is noise reduction in event streams. The proposed approach uses denoising autoencoders to filter out noise from event streams, enhancing the accuracy of classification. The paper also proposes a training methodology for the denoising autoencoders, which is essential for the effectiveness of the method. This approach is particularly useful for applications such as predictive maintenance, where sensors generate event streams that require classification. The paper also discusses the use of probability distributions and hidden Markov models to further refine the classification. Overall, this paper highlights the potential of machine learning techniques for improving classification accuracy in event stream analysis.

This paper presents a study on text categorization using weighted features with a focus on sports-related texts. The research starts with task analysis, identifying the key requirements for sports text categorization, which include understanding the semantics and extracting relevant features to achieve accurate results. The paper discusses various methods for feature extraction, including traditional approaches and deep learning techniques. The primary focus is on measurement of the effectiveness of different feature extraction methods for sports text categorization. The study shows that deep learning methods outperform traditional methods in terms of feature extraction and categorization accuracy. The findings of this research can be beneficial for the development of efficient text categorization systems for sports-related texts.

Shrinking of device dimensions has undoubtedly enabled the very large scale integration of transistors on electronic chips. However, it has also brought to surface time-zero and time-dependent variation phenomena that degrade system's performance and threaten functional operation. Hence, the need to capture and describe these mechanisms, as well as effectively model their impact is crucial. To this extent, we follow existing models and propose a complete framework that evaluates failure probability of electronic components. To assess our framework, a case-study of packet-switched Network on Chip (NoC) routers is presented, studying the failure probability of its SRAM buffers.

The paper titled "MAIDENS: MIL-STD-1553 Anomaly-Based Intrusion Detection System Using Time-Based Histogram Comparison" presents a novel approach to intrusion detection that focuses on military standards. The proposed system utilizes histograms and time-based comparisons to extract features from network traffic and identify anomalies in real-time. The paper discusses the challenges associated with the MIL-STD-1553 protocol and how they can be overcome using the system. MAIDENS has been tested on a Microsoft Windows based platform and is effective at detecting a variety of network intrusions. This paper makes a significant contribution towards enhancing the security of military networks, and demonstrates the potential of anomaly-based intrusion detection systems for much broader applications.

This paper proposes a novel gradient descent least squares regression (GDLSR)-based neural network (NN) structure for the control of grid-integrated solar photovoltaic (PV) system with improved power quality. Here, a single-layer neuron structure is used for the extraction of fundamental component (FC) from the load current. During FC extraction, GDLSR-based NN structure attenuates harmonic components, noise, dc offsets, bias, notches and distortions from the nonlinear current, which improves the power quality under normal as well as under abnormal grid conditions. This single-layer GDLSR-based NN structure has a very simple architecture, which decreases the computational burden and algorithm complexity. Therefore, it is easy in implementation. In this work, the GDLSR-based control technique is tested on a single-phase single-stage grid-integrated PV topology with the nonlinear loads. The prime objective of the GDLSR-based NN structure is to provide reactive power compensation, power factor correction, harmonics filtering and mitigation of other power quality issues. Moreover, when solar irradiation is zero, the dc-link capacitor and voltage-source converter act as a distribution static compensator, which enhances the utilization factor of the system. The proposed system is modeled, and its performances are verified experimentally on a developed prototype in different grid disturbances as well as solar insolation variation conditions, which performances have satisfied the motive of the proposed technique as well as the IEEE-519 standard.

Ship plate recognition is challenging due to variations of plate locations and text types. This paper proposes an effcient Fully Convolutional Network based Plate Recognition approach FCNPR, which uses a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) to locate ships, then detects plate text lines with the fully convolutional network (FCN). The recognition accuracy is improved with integrating the AIS (Automatic Identification System) information. The actual FCNPR deployment demonstrates that it can work reliably with a high accuracy for satisfying practical usages.

Wireless energy transfer can extend the lifetime of wireless sensor networks deployed in hard-to-reach and/or harsh environments. A number of works have proposed using dedicated mobile chargers (e.g., robots, drones, or vehicles) to transmit Radio Frequency (RF) energy to sensor nodes, which, despite optimal route selection, remains an expensive approach. In this article, we consider a scenario where sensor nodes could be recharged by passing vehicles. This could be the case of a wireless sensor network deployed to monitor the health of a bridge or a dam. We provide exact mathematical modeling of the harvested energy from a moving vehicle over T seconds and over a trip time. This model captures the effect of the vehicle's speed and location. Then, we extend the discussion to the case of multiple vehicles and propose a multi vehicle harvesting protocol. This protocol allows the sensor node to maximize its energy intake by proactively selecting the source vehicle. This work paves the ground for accurate designs of energy harvesting protocols that leverage surrounding sources of RF energy. The accuracy of the derived results is verified using computer simulations.

The design of Wideband MIMO Radar Waveforms has gained significant interest in the field of signal processing. This paper explores the use of convex functions for optimizing the waveform design in Wideband MIMO radar systems. Wideband signals are used in MIMO radar systems to increase the range and resolution of the radar system. The optimization of the radar waveform is important in order to improve the detection and imaging capabilities of the MIMO radar system. Signal processing algorithms are developed to enhance the system performance and mitigate the effects of noise and interference. Convergence is also studied to ensure the effectiveness of the optimization process. The results show that the proposed method is effective in improving the performance of the Wideband MIMO radar system.

This paper proposes a novel approach to design and optimize soft computing based ellipsoidal fractal antenna for wide band applications. The microstrip antenna, which is widely used in modern communication systems, is utilized as a platform to implement the proposed fractal antenna design. Artificial neural networks are integrated into the design process to enhance the optimization efficiency and accuracy. Fractals, a self-similar and non-Euclidean geometric object, are utilized to improve the performance of the proposed antenna. The generated fractal antennas have been tested and confirmed the bandwidth enhancement and satisfactory results. Computational modeling techniques are employed throughout the design process to simulate and analyze the performance of the fractal antennas. These novel antennas have great potential for improving the performance of wireless communication systems.

YAFS (Yet Another Fog Simulator) is a simulator designed for IoT scenarios in fog computing. It allows for large scale integration and analysis of various relays, wireless communication technologies such as OFDM, interference cancellation, and channel estimation. YAFS provides a realistic platform for evaluating the performance of these technologies in real-time systems, which is essential for ensuring that IoT networks function efficiently and are reliable. The use of YAFS can save significant amounts of money and time in the development and testing of IoT systems. Researchers can use it to simulate various IoT scenarios, tweak system parameters, and evaluate the effects of different network configurations, ultimately resulting in better system design and overall improved network performance.

Soil detection using satellite imagery has been a prominent research topic in remote sensing. In this paper, we propose a joint sparsity approach for soil detection using expanded bands of WV-2 images. The method integrates both spectral and terrain factors to achieve accurate soil detection. Multiple dictionaries are created based on training samples, and the joint sparsity model is employed to select the best dictionary for each pixel. The expanded bands of WV-2 images further enhance the spatial resolution, improving the accuracy of soil detection. The proposed approach is tested on different terrains and geology, and the experimental results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the method. The joint sparsity approach provides a novel and effective method for soil detection using satellite imagery, with potential applications in agriculture and environmental monitoring.

In this paper cubic splines are designed as tone correction functions applied to the achromatic component of a spherical color model. Compared with the commonly used color models HSV and HSL, an advantage of the spherical color model is that color changes more perceptually smoothly along its coordinates. However, the spherical color model contains more color points than what can be displayed with the RGB color model, so a tone correction function might cause a gamut issue. The paper demonstrates the gamut issue can be avoided when tone correction functions are well designed and the general tone correction techniques still work well in the spherical color model. A particular type of cubic splines is designed to serve the purpose, and these splines can be adopted by the general tone correction techniques including those for low-key, middle-key and high-key images with correspondingly selected parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that these cubic splines work well for tone correction under the spherical color model.

This paper proposes a novel approach for determining the weights and optimizing the structure of a two-input power-activation neural network using particle swarm optimization. The motivation for this work comes from the complexity of biological neural networks and the desire to mimic their capabilities. The basic building blocks of the network are modeled after neurons, and linear programming techniques are employed to train the network. The structure is then optimized by using particle swarm optimization techniques, which enable a search for the optimal architecture. A detailed comparison with existing approximation algorithms and signal processing algorithms is provided, and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

Exposure to Particulate Matter (PM) has been identified as a major health problem worldwide. Established measurement techniques require equipment costing many thousands of dollars and specialist expertise to maintain. Ongoing research is investigating the use of low cost <;$300 sensors to enable greater temporal-spatial density of readings to be taken. There are questions about the suitability and reliability of these low-cost sensors, which can be addressed by deploying and evaluating the sensors in real world applications. Rather than deploying standalone data loggers for each sensor, each air quality monitor is connected to an IoT device to enable real time transmission of data. We propose festival sites as small scale cities to enable a short term deployments and evaluation of sensors. This work illustrates that, if coupled with higher resolution of wind data, low-cost sensors may enable to follow the evolution of pollution hotspots and help the identification of pollution sources. This study, building upon the body of work focused on the evaluation and best practice of using low-cost sensors for PM monitoring. We present data from these IoT devices and experiences gained from using a festival site as a substitute for a city.

This paper focuses on the evaluation of the naturalness of chatbot applications in the context of task analysis, artificial intelligence, personnel, human computer interaction, and robotics. Naturalness is an essential aspect of chatbot applications since it directly impacts the effectiveness of human-computer interactions. The study discusses several factors that contribute to the naturalness of chatbot applications, including the chatbot's personality, tone, and language. The research examines the use of machine learning and natural language processing algorithms to develop chatbot applications that are more natural in their interactions with humans. The study also highlights the role of personnel in ensuring the naturalness of chatbot applications, emphasizing the need for skilled professionals with expertise in human-computer interaction and artificial intelligence. The results of this evaluation suggest that the naturalness of chatbot applications is a critical component of effective human-computer interaction and that acceleration in technology and integration of cutting-edge AI can contribute to the development of more human-like interactions.

This paper proposes a method called Class-Specific Guided Local Feature Selection for Data Classification, which focuses on feature extraction and optimization to improve the accuracy of classification algorithms. The method utilizes linear programming to select relevant features that are specific to each class, and employs task analysis to guide the feature selection process. The proposed approach allows for personalized training of classification models, thus enhancing their efficiency and accuracy. The results of experiments conducted on several datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in improving the classification accuracy when compared to other state-of-the-art feature selection methods.

Adolescence is a transitional period between the childhood and adulthood with physical changes, as well as increasing emotional development. Studies have shown that the emotional sensitivity is related to a second period of rapid brain growth. However, there is little focus on the trend of brain development during this period. In this paper, we aim to track functional brain connectivity development from late childhood to young adulthood. Mathematically, this problem can be modeled via the estimation of multiple Gaussian graphical models (GGMs). However, most existing methods either require the graph sequence to be fairly long or are only applicable to small graphs. In this paper, we adapted a Bayesian approach incorporating joint estimation of multiple GGMs to overcome the short sequence difficulty, which is also computationally efficient. The data used are the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) images obtained from the publicly available Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC). They include 855 individuals aged 8-22 years who were divided into five different adolescent stages. We summarized the networks with global measurements and applied a hypothesis test across age groups to detect the developmental patterns. Three patterns were detected and defined as consistent development, late puberty, and temporal change. We also discovered several anatomical areas, such as the middle frontal gyrus, putamen gyrus, right lingual gyrus, and right cerebellum crus 2 that are highly involved in the brain functional development. The functional networks, including the salience, subcortical, and auditory networks are significantly developing during the adolescent period.

Artificial neural networks (ANNs) have become a powerful tool for research in cognitive science and psychology. With their ability to model complex systems and learn from data, ANNs are applicable to a wide range of topics in these fields. ANNs have been used to model perception, attention, memory, and decision-making processes, among others. These models can help researchers to understand the nature of cognitive processes and their underlying neural mechanisms. ANNs are also useful for artificial intelligence applications, as they can be trained to recognize patterns in data, make predictions, and classify objects. This paper reviews the use of ANNs in cognitive science and psychology, highlighting their benefits over traditional statistical analysis methods. The paper also presents examples of ANNs implemented in Matlab to demonstrate their effectiveness as a tool for cognitive modeling. Overall, ANNs present a powerful tool for researchers in cognitive science and psychology to gain insights into the workings of the human mind.

This paper proposes a practical approach to track uncertain nonlinear systems via adaptive event-triggered feedback. The approach is designed for adaptive systems with uncertain parameters and aims to achieve greater control accuracy while using fewer control signals. The paper focuses on the use of event-triggered feedback to reduce communication and computation costs in the control loop. The proposed approach works by dynamically adjusting the event threshold and feedback gain to adapt to changes in the system's uncertain parameters. The approach is shown to converge to a bounded tracking error using an upper bound on the system's uncertainty. The paper also includes a detailed analysis of the computer architecture required to implement the proposed approach. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through simulations of a nonlinear system with uncertain parameters and actuator constraints. The results show that the approach provides better tracking performance compared to the traditional continuous-time feedback control.

This paper proposes an online non-negative multi-modality feature template learning approach for RGB-assisted infrared tracking, which aims to improve the reliability and accuracy of target tracking in video surveillance. The proposed methodology incorporates adaptation models and optimization techniques to learn a robust feature template that can handle variations in object appearance and background clutter. By leveraging the complementary information from RGB and infrared modalities, the proposed method achieves superior tracking performance compared to existing approaches. The computational modeling results show that the proposed method can perform well under different challenging scenarios, such as fast motion, occlusion, and illumination changes. Therefore, the proposed method has great potential for practical applications in video surveillance and object tracking domains.

This paper explores the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies as a substitute for reading and to support and enhance the authoring of scientific review articles. The use of bibliographies, text mining, and artificial intelligence, along with databases, systematics, natural language processing, and information retrieval tools, has the potential to optimize the identification and evaluation of relevant literature, as well as the organization and synthesis of ideas. These technologies can also facilitate the automation of the citation process, reducing the time needed for literature search and bibliography creation. The development of intelligent systems that can recognize patterns in scholarly communications, identify gaps in knowledge, and suggest potential research directions could revolutionize the way scientists write and publish their work. However, significant challenges remain, including the accurate interpretation of complex scientific language and the careful calibration of AI systems to avoid biases and errors. Further research is needed to fully evaluate the benefits and limitations of AI technologies in scientific review article writing, and to ensure that their implementation aligns with ethical standards and best practices.

In recent years, wireless sensor networks have been extensively deployed to collect various data. Due to the effect of harsh environments and the limitation of the computing and communication capabilities of sensor nodes, the quality and reliability of sensor data are affected by outliers. Thus, an effective outlier detection method is essential. The existing outlier detection methods have some drawbacks, such as extra resource consumption introduced by the size growth of a local detector, poor performance of combination methods of local detectors, and the weak adaptability of the dynamic changes of the environment, etc. We propose an isolation-based distributed outlier detection framework using nearest-neighbor ensembles (iNNE) to effectively detect outliers in wireless sensor networks. In our proposed framework, local detectors are constructed in each node by the iNNE algorithm. A new combination method taking advantage of the spatial correlation among sensor nodes for local detectors is presented. The method is based on the weighted voting idea. In addition, we introduce a sliding window to update local detectors, which enables the adaption of dynamic changes in the environment. The extensive experiments are conducted on two classic real sensor datasets. The experimental results show our framework significantly improves the detection accuracy and reduces the false alarm rate compared with other outlier detection frameworks.

A metasurface-based thermophotovoitaics system directly converts thermal radiation to electricity through the photovoitaic effect. The efficiency of such a system significantly depends on the thermal stability and efficiency of the spectral reshaping of the metasurface. We couple the generative adversarial network technique with the topology optimization to design a new class of high-efficiency metasurface thermal emitters. Numerical simulations confirm that due to non-trivial metasurface topologies the proposed method generates the close-to-ultimate high-efficiency emitters. Comparison with a conventional global optimization technique shows that our topology-optimized designs demonstrate superior spectral control of thermal blackbody radiation than the regular-shape emitters optimized with conventional optimization.

Billions of devises are expected to be connected to the Internet of Things network in the near future, therefore, a considerable amount of data will be generated, and gathered every second. The current network paradigm, which relies on centralised data-centres (a.k.a. Cloud computing), becomes impractical solution for IoT data due to the long distance between the data source and designated data-center. In other words, the amount of time taken by data to travel to a data-centre makes the importance of the data vanished. Therefore, the network topology have been evolved to permit data processing at the edge of the network, introducing what so-called "Fog computing". The later will obviously lead to improvements in quality of service via efficient and quick responding to sensors requests. In this paper, we are proposing a fog computing architecture and framework to enhance QoS via request offloading method. The proposed method employ a collaboration strategy among fog nodes in order to permit data processing in a shared mode, hence satisfies QoS and serves largest number of IoT requests. The proposed framework could have the potential in achieving sustainable network paradigm and highlights significant benefits of fog computing into the computing ecosystem.

Qualitative simulation and reasoning about change is an essential task in many domains, including engineering, psychology, and biology. This area of study is concerned with predicting the behavior of complex systems and understanding how changes to those systems will affect their behavior. Analytical models, finite element analysis, and computational modeling are some of the approaches used to study dynamic systems. In the engineering domain, one example where qualitative simulation is needed is in designing the brakes of a vehicle. The behavior of the brake system under different conditions, such as wet roads or emergency stops, must be understood to ensure the system meets safety requirements. Switches are another example of a dynamic system where qualitative simulation is necessary for predicting behavior. In the psychology domain, the study of cognition involves modeling how knowledge is acquired and represented in the brain. Water is a complex system where qualitative reasoning about change is important for understanding how it moves through the environment and how it interacts with other systems. Overall, qualitative simulation and reasoning about change is a valuable tool for understanding complex systems across a range of domains.

Pedagogical agents (P A) are lifelike characters presented on a computer screen that guide users through multimedia learning environments. Evidences show that P A has effect on promoting learning. However, P A field still faces common problems to be solved, such as how to promote the trust relationship among P A and learners. Such questions relate to how to make P A behaves more like human. This paper argues that solving these problems requires at least P A to simulate humans better in appearance, speech and motion, a possible solution is to transfer a human tutor's style to P A. Traditional P A production methods rely on the authoring tool, such as Microsoft agent, this type of methods are highly depending on manual production, so it is difficult to transfer the style of human tutor to P A well. Meanwhile, the production cycle is long, the cost is high, and the adaptability is not ideal. Based on the analysis of the achievements of interdisciplinary literature, this paper points out that based on various machine learning technologies, the above problems can be solved to a great extent. The related technologies are more likely to enhance the human-like of PA, such as the establishment of teacher strategy and behavior prediction model.

This paper proposes a free-space estimation technique for self-driving systems using millimeter wave radar and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed technique utilizes the accuracy and reliability of millimeter wave radar detection to estimate the free space around the vehicle. The use of CNNs in this technique enables the system to identify potential obstacles and navigate through them. The study evaluates the proposed technique through several experiments and demonstrates the effectiveness of the system in real-world scenarios. Additionally, the study compares the proposed method with traditional laser radar and spaceborne radar techniques and shows the superiority of the millimeter wave radar-based approach. Overall, the proposed technique has shown great potential for improving the performance and safety of self-driving systems.

Robotic-assisted rehabilitation of the upper limb following neurological injury can achieve best possible functional recovery when patients are engaged in the therapy. However, implementation of active training is still difficult as it's challenging to detect human motion intention online and impose corresponding robot control. This paper introduces a novel upper-limb rehabilitation robot, and proposes a sEMG-driven (sEMG: surface Electromyography) torque estimation model based on artificial neural networks (ANN). The robot has three DOFs, of which the first two DOFs adopt a planar parallel structure, and the wrist module has an exoskeleton form. In this study, we design an impedance controller and an admittance controller for the first two DOFs and the wrist module, respectively. Specifically, for the first two DOFs, the assistance/resistance force at the end-effector was controlled according to its motions and desired interaction impedance; for the wrist module, an sEMG armband was used to collect 8 channels of sEMG signals from the forearm muscles, and a time-delay ANN model was developed to estimate the wrist pronation/supination torque, based on which the wrist rotation was controlled according to the human motion intention. To overcome the overfitting problem, besides the experimental samples of wrist rotation, both resting and co-contraction samples were collected for training. Finally, combining with the design of a virtual reality game and force fields, the proposed methods were implemented and tested experimentally on the upper-limb rehabilitation robot.

The problem of state estimation for unobservable distribution systems is considered. A deep learning approach to Bayesian state estimation is proposed for real-time applications. The proposed technique consists of distribution learning of stochastic power injection, a Monte Carlo technique for the training of a deep neural network for state estimation, and a Bayesian bad-data detection and filtering algorithm. Structural characteristics of the deep neural networks are investigated. Simulations illustrate the accuracy of Bayesian state estimation for unobservable systems and demonstrate the benefit of employing a deep neural network. Numerical results show the robustness of Bayesian state estimation against modeling and estimation errors and the presence of bad and missing data. Comparing with pseudo-measurement techniques, direct Bayesian state estimation via deep learning neural network outperforms existing benchmarks.

Imitation learning has gained huge popularity due to its promises in different fields such as robotics and autonomous systems. A great deal of past research work in the field of imitation learning has been devoted to developing efficient and effective policies using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The performance of CNN-based control policies intimately depends on the network architecture. Determination of the optimal architecture for CNNs is still a hot research topic for the deep learning community. This study comprehensively investigates and quantifies the impact of CNN architecture on the performance of learned policy for an autonomous vehicle. CNN models with different architectures (number of layers and filters) are fed by visual information from multiple cameras obtained from multiple driving simulations. These networks are trained to precisely find the mapping between visual information and the steering angle. Two ensemble approaches are also introduced to further improve the overall accuracy of steering angle estimations. Obtained results indicate that deeper networks show a better performance than less deep networks during autonomous driving. Also it is observed that best results are achieved by ensemble approaches.

Food transformation is an integral aspect of modern gastronomy, and virtual reality has made it possible to visualize the entire process. The CNN-based food transformation on HoloLens technology allows users to transform food in a virtual environment using shape and geometry. This technology incorporates image generation algorithms that provide an accurate simulation of the food transformation process. The HoloLens technology provides a platform for practical training sessions that enhance the creativity and skillset of chefs. The technology has been demonstrated at various conferences, showing its capability in the field of food transformation. In conclusion, CNN-based food transformation on HoloLens presents a new and innovative approach to food transformation, revolutionizing the culinary industry.

With the advancement of medical services, the sharing of medical data has become an important aspect of healthcare. However, the sensitive nature of medical data and the need for data privacy have posed challenges in the data sharing process. This paper provides a review of secure and privacy-preserving medical data sharing techniques, focusing on two main technologies: cloud computing and blockchain. The use of cloud computing has enabled the sharing of biomedical imaging data, while ensuring data privacy through the use of cryptographic techniques. On the other hand, the development of blockchain technology has made it possible to share medical data in a decentralized and secure manner. The use of cryptography in both cloud computing and blockchain technologies ensures secure data sharing and protects the confidentiality and integrity of medical data. Further research is needed to address challenges such as interoperability and regulatory compliance in the implementation of these technologies in medical data sharing.

With the technological advancement in science, education, engineering, and research the scheduling problem is getting more attention to the researchers. Scheduling is a well known Non-deterministic Polynomial(NP)-complete problem. In this paper, we have proposed a solution to the scheduling problem using a well known meta-heuristic approach known as Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA). The proposed GSA based scheduling technique considers multiple conflicting objectives as minimization of makespan, load-balancing, and maximization of resource utilization. The proposed work is extensively simulated on standard benchmark data sets. The simulation result shows better performance of the proposed algorithm than the existing algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm(GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO).

Hyperspectral remote sensing imagery provides valuable and rich information to distinguish the characteristics of materials. However, this advantage of hyperspectral imagery often encounters the problem of a limited amount of training samples, which is caused by the difficulty of manually labeling. Fortunately, the spatial distribution of surface objects can be integrated with the spectral signature to improve the discriminative ability. In this paper, a 3-D Gaussian-Gabor feature extraction and selection framework has been proposed for hyperspectral image classification. First, a bank of 3-D Gaussian-Gabor filters are convolved with the concatenated data of both extended multi-attribute profile (EMAP) features and raw hyperspectral data. Second, an improved fast density peak clustering (IFDPC) method is introduced to select the most representative features from each extracted 3-D Gaussian-Gabor feature cube. Finally, the retained features are combined together to accomplish the classification task. The proposed method is thus named as GG-IFDPC. Three real hyperspectral imagery data sets have been utilized, and the experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed GG-IFDPC approach over the compared ones.

In this paper, we propose a placement-aware soft-error rate estimation method for combinational circuits under multiple transient faults in CMOS technology. The proposed method takes into account the effect of temperature on the soft-error rate and utilizes Monte Carlo methods for error analysis and simulation. We present an estimation algorithm that considers the placement of the circuit components and their proximity to other sensitive components. The proposed method incorporates very large scale integration (VLSI) design tools to accurately estimate the soft-error rate of the circuit. Our results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The placement-aware soft-error rate estimation method can be used in VLSI design to improve the reliability of circuits against transient faults.

For an interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM), parameters mismatching would affect the performance and reduce the output efficiency.In this paper, a variable parameter Maximum Torque Per Ampere(MTP A)control method based on online parameters identification was proposed. Firstly, an adaptive linear neural network algorithm is used to identify the motor parameters, and then the MTPA control is modified by combining the identified parameters. The results show that the proposed strategy has a nice adaptation to parameters mismatching, along with an improved output efficiency which is beneficial to magnetic recording motor.

This study aims to investigate the contribution of Optical Time Division Multiplexing (OTDM) and OTDM/WDM hybrid multiplexing at a bit rate of 160 Gbps. The optimization of optical fibers and wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) technologies has become necessary features in next-generation optical fiber networks. The study focuses on the performance analysis of the OTDM and OTDM/WDM hybrid multiplexing, such as the transmission distance, receiver sensitivity, and resilience to crosstalk. The research shows that the OTDM and OTDM/WDM hybrid multiplexing techniques provide superior performance in high-speed data transmission, enabling higher data rates and greater capacity for information transmission in optical fiber networks. The results demonstrate the potential of utilizing OTDM and OTDM/WDM hybrid multiplexing as a promising solution to meet the growing demand for high-speed data transmission while offering scalability and cost-effectiveness.

In recent years, the field of neural networks has gained widespread attention due to its ability to classify and identify patterns in large sets of data. One application of neural networks is in the task of multi-label classification, where multiple labels are assigned to a single instance. In this paper, we introduce the use of a Neural Tensor Network (NTN) for multi-label classification, which can capture the correlation between labels and improve the overall prediction accuracy. The NTN is a type of neural network that employs tensor transforms to model the relationship between different features, making it particularly suitable for complex datasets such as those found in the field of biology. We also investigate various adaptation models that can be used to improve the performance of the NTN across different datasets. Our findings suggest that the NTN can achieve state-of-the-art results in multi-label classification tasks, and we propose it as a potential standard model for future research in this area.

Congestion control in wireless sensor networks is a challenging area owing to the fact that the resources such as storage capacity, processing capability, sensing capability and power are limited in the sensor nodes building the wireless sensor network. Congestion occurs in wireless sensor networks when data packets flow towards a node where the node buffers are full or nearly full. To address these challenges we propose a newer congestion controlling algorithm which monitors the buffer occupancy and adjusts traffic rate to increase throughput and save energy. It detects the level of congestion based on two different thresholds. It also takes care that more number of higher priority packets are received at the destination and the life of the network is increased.

This paper proposes an efficient time-shifted random access scheme for cellular-based IoT networks. By strategically shifting the access time of IoT devices, the proposed scheme aims to optimize the network performance and reduce access collisions, ultimately improving the overall efficiency of the network. The scheme is evaluated through numerical models and performance evaluation, and the results show significant improvements in the synchronization and access performance of IoT devices. The proposed scheme also makes use of indexes to streamline the access process and improve the overall network efficiency. The optimization strategies proposed in this paper can be applied to various Internet of Things scenarios, making it a valuable contribution to the field of IoT network optimization.

Naturalistic driving studies seek to perform the observations of human driver behavior in the variety of environmental conditions necessary to analyze, understand and predict that behavior using statistical and physical models. The second Strategic Highway Research Program (SHRP 2) funds a number of transportation safety-related projects including its primary effort, the Naturalistic Driving Study (NDS), and an effort supplementary to the NDS, the Roadway Information Database (RID). This work seeks to expand the range of answerable research questions that researchers might pose to the NDS and RID databases. Specifically, we present the SHRP 2 NDS Video Analytics (SNVA) software application, which extracts information from NDS-instrumented vehicles' forward-facing camera footage and efficiently integrates that information into the RID, tying the video content to geolocations and other trip attributes. Of particular interest to researchers and other stakeholders is the integration of work zone, traffic signal state and weather information. The version of SNVA introduced in this paper focuses on work zone detection, the highest priority. The ability to automate the discovery and cataloging of this information, and to do so quickly, is especially important given the two petabyte (2PB) size of the NDS video data set.

Breast cancer is one of the most common types of cancer amongst women globally. Traditional diagnosis and prognosis of breast cancer involve the analysis of histopathological images of breast tissue specimens. However, this process can be time-consuming and subjective. In this study, we propose a novel approach to improve the classification of breast cancer by utilizing the image pyramids of whole-slide imaging and multi-scale convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed method uses deep learning techniques for feature extraction from pathology images of breast tissue specimens. The extracted features are then used to train multi-scale CNNs to classify the breast cancer condition. The proposed method achieves improved classification results compared to traditional methods. Additionally, the study also investigates the impact of image resolution on the classification performance. The findings of this research demonstrate the potential of utilizing deep learning techniques with whole-slide imaging for the accurate classification of breast cancer, which can aid in early detection and effective treatment.

Around 6-8% of people are affected by rare genetic disorders in the world. Due to unavailability of proper identification of gene variants causing these rare disorders, the genetic tests for many of them do not exist with an exception to some common conditions like Down’s Syndrome. A limited number of individuals have the proper training and ability to recognize these disorders and have to depend on the pronounced facial features which occur in about 30-40% of these diseases. Fine-tuning of the pre-trained model VGGFace(with ResNet50 network architecture) on our dataset comprising of 12 classes of rare genetic syndromes leads to a top accuracy of 97.66% and an F1 score of 0.86. On using a smaller dataset with 8 classes of syndromes same as Clinical Face Phenotype Space, the state-of-the-art, our model produces a top accuracy of 98.1% and an F1 score of 0.92. This could be used to screen for rare genetic diseases in newborns.

In this paper, we propose a computational modeling approach for predicting associations between microRNAs and human diseases. The proposed approach is based on multiple similarities and arbitrarily-order proximity network embedding. To extract effective features, we employ the kernel method and semantic analysis. Furthermore, matrix decomposition is used to reduce the dimensionality of the feature vectors. Finally, we build predictive models to predict the associations between microRNAs and diseases. The proposed approach is evaluated on a dataset containing microRNA and disease associations, and the experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of predictive accuracy. Overall, our approach provides a promising direction for predicting associations between microRNAs and human diseases, which could facilitate the discovery of new therapeutic targets and lead to improved clinical outcomes for patients.

It is well-known that the classical proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller plays a fundamental role in various engineering systems. However, up to now a theory that can explain the rationale why the linear PID can effectively deal with nonlinear uncertain dynamical systems and a method that can provide explicit design formula for the PID parameters are still lacking. This motivates our recent study on the theoretical foundation of the PID control. The main purpose of this letter is to extend the 1-D results to higher dimensional nonlinear uncertain systems and to improve the results significantly by a refined method. We will also consider a class of multi-agent uncertain nonlinear systems where each agent is controlled by a PID controller using its own regulation error. We will show that a parameter manifold can be constructed explicitly so that when the PID parameters are chosen from this manifold, the multi-agent systems will be globally stable and the tracking error of each agent will coverage to zero exponentially fast.

A growing number of user applications rely on the computing resources of edge cloud data centers (ECDCs). The efficient management of ECDC resources has a positive impact on the cloud service providers' profitability and on the stringent quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of user applications. This paper proposes a resource allocation framework of interconnected ECDCs using software-defined networking (SDN). SDN technology is used to ensure QoS and to efficiently embed user applications into the ECDCs. The proposed framework, called infrastructure as a service provisioning using SDN (IaaSP-SDN), includes the two-phase coordinated IaaS requests. Provisioning approach and a set of SDN management modules to set up accepted IaaS. The performance of IaaSP-SDN is evaluated in two steps: 1) a prototype is compared with generalized multi-protocol label switching (GMPLS) and 2) the impact of SDN controller physical location on the performance of the IaaSP-SDN framework is evaluated. The results illustrate that the SDN framework is more stable and scalable than GMPLS. We also show that SDN controller location attributes have a significant effect on the acceptance ratio of IaaS requests.

This paper proposes a Wasserstein metric based distributionally robust approximate framework for unit commitment to address the uncertainties associated with wind power generation. The proposed method measures the uncertainty through probability distributions and employs optimization techniques to minimize the discrepancy between the distributional uncertainty set and the true probability distribution. This approach provides a computationally efficient solution to handle the complex nature of the unit commitment problem, which involves random variables and nonlinear constraints. The proposed approach is validated through case studies on different scenarios to demonstrate its effectiveness in managing uncertainties and providing robust unit commitment solutions. Overall, this framework offers a promising solution to address the challenges posed by uncertainty in the field of wind power generation and provides a useful computational modeling tool for optimization problems involving random variables.

Bone age assessment is one of the most important problems to assess Pediatric growth. Various methods have been investigated to develop bone age assessment. The study of bone age assessment helps to diagnose disorders in growth progress. It is very common to monitor growth progress with left hand x-ray images. There are many method such as Tanner-Whitehouse [TW], Greulich and Pyle (G&P) methods. In this paper, we applied convolutional neural network resnet50 by preprocessing the images using different filters based on edge detection to compare effects on CNN accuracy. The main purpose of the paper is to compare the effect of DoG filtering and à trous wavelet as preprocessing techniques on bone-age assessment. It has been proved that suggested methods improved the accuracy of CNN (resnet50) in filtered images compared to the result of the non-filtered ones. The ages between 0 and 7 are analyzed to assess bone for female, male, and female male together. It is observed that there is over% 14 improvement for Female for Male %11 and for male and female %10 percent between filtered images and non-filtered images. The proposed method reached% 87.78 female and% 80 for male within 7.9 month.

Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have been widely utilized in the field of Artificial Intelligence and are now considered as one of the primary technologies for pattern recognition and classification problems. However, the actual mechanisms that ANNs employ to achieve these goals are still not well understood. This paper proposes a new perspective for interpreting ANNs as network flows, inspired by the physical properties of iron. By redefining the nodes and connections of ANNs in the context of network flows, we can identify the contributions of each node to the final output, which provides a more intuitive way of interpreting the behavior of ANNs. Moreover, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in the context of 5G mobile communication, where ANNs can be used for various applications such as channel estimation and interference cancellation. Our results suggest that the network flow interpretation can help improve the performance and explainability of ANNs in practical scenarios.

The development of a cognitive machine learning system for phrases composition and semantic comprehension is a promising area of research in the field of linguistics. This system focuses on utilizing machine learning algorithms that can identify patterns in language semantics and syntactics through algebraic models. The system aims to provide a more sophisticated approach to language learning based on cognitive systems, which can process large amounts of data and generate meaningful insights into language patterns. The system's success is dependent on its ability to accurately capture the complexities of language and apply them to real-world applications. Further research is needed to validate the system's effectiveness and optimize its performance. Overall, this cognitive machine learning system has the potential to greatly improve our understanding of language and pave the way for more advanced language applications.

Flatfoot is a common disease in children and juveniles. If the disease is not controlled and treated in time, it may last into adulthood, which can bring a great deal of inconvenience and even pain to daily life. In addition to the diagnosis of the disease simply by doctors and medical equipment, artificial intelligence has become a very promising auxiliary diagnostic tool. In this paper, a neural network with a simple structure is used to classify the foot data to achieve the function of diagnosing flatfoot. The presented neural network is termed as modified weights-and-structure-determination neural network (MWASDNN), of which the input weights are analytically determined by the pseudo-inverse method, while the output weights are randomly generated within a specified interval, and the number of hidden-layer neurons is determined by an incremental method. In addition, the stratified cross-validation method is introduced to choose the model structure that best fits the features of the data set, thereby improving the generalization performance and robustness of the MWASDNN. Utilizing the MWASDNN models to classify the foot data we collected, we finally get the accuracy of 84.31% and 85.29% on the left and right foot data, respectively. Besides, MWASDNN achieves the highest classification accuracy on our foot data set compared to some traditional neural networks, pattern classification methods, and two improved neural networks. These excellent results indicate that the MWASDNN is expected to be designed as a practical flatfoot diagnostic tool.

We propose a time series prediction system of agricultural products price based on recurrent neural networks and their time alignment. The purpose of the system is to provide a way to make the price movements stable by sharing the information of price between producers and consumers of agricultural products. For the purpose, we designed a time alignment mechanism of recurrent neural networks to predict time series of prices, where each predicted results is evaluated not only by the accuracy but also by probability distribution of price movement (statistical characteristic). For the stability of agricultural products, price movements have the same importance as accuracy of predicted prices. This is the reason why we focus on not only the accuracy but also probability distribution. Although we show the results where only past price information is used as input of learning for the first step, the framework is designed to reflect other related information such as meteorological and social information on learning in future.

Internet of Things (IoT) security becomes of great importance, as IoT is the foundation for many emerging services. To safeguard IoT security, cryptosystems at upper layer relying on sophisticated key management alone can face many challenges due to the massive deployment of resource constrained machine-type communication (MTC) devices. Physical layer (PHY) security can complement and enhance IoT security, by exploiting the characteristics of the bottom layer. In PHY security, channel state information (CSI) estimated through reverse pilot training is essential for the sender to select appropriate beamforming/precoder, which however is also vulnerable to adversaries. An adversary can actively launch pilot contamination attacks to affect the channel estimation and improve its signal reception quality. In this paper, we propose a relay-aided vectorized (RAV) secure transmission scheme, to safeguard the downlink communication in IoT networks under potential pilot contamination attacks. The proposed scheme does not distinguish the pilot sequences sent from an adversary and the receiver; and the sender utilizes what it receives to estimate the CSI for beamforming/precoder design. Then, a set of data symbols are presuperposed using a random complex matrix to form signal vectors to send. Through cooperation with a relay, the signal vectors can be recovered by the intended receiver whereas the adversary or the relay cannot, as proved through security analysis. The simulation results also demonstrate that the bit error rate (BER) of the adversary is 0.5 regardless of its channel quality, indicating perfect secrecy is achieved.

This research method is motivated by Rat Grimace Scale(RGS) method in [1]. Their approach indicates the utility of quantifying spontaneous pain in mice via blinded coding of facial expression, but there is a general concern about rating with subjective criteria of mice experts. Therefore, this research utilizes a supervised parameter linear SVM classifier for long-term monitor of pain face. The contributions are summarized in two points. First, a statistical analysis of pain face has been done for exploring facial patterns before training SVM classifier.
