The experimental results indicate that the RGB component plays a more significant role in 3D face tracking stability analysis than the HSV component. Furthermore, the study highlights the importance of lighting and brightness in the stability analysis and suggests potential ways to improve the accuracy and reliability of 3D face tracking for digital makeup applications. The findings of this research will serve as a crucial guideline for researchers and developers in the field of computer vision and 3D face tracking technology, contributing to better accuracy and reliability of digital makeup applications.

In recent years, the development of autonomous vehicles has spurred research into image color analysis technology. The incorporation of vision sensors into these vehicles has created a need for reliable and efficient color decision systems. This paper proposes a color decision system based on deep learning and fuzzy inference system. The system utilizes the principles of fuzzy logic to process color information from the image, and extracts features using deep learning techniques. The combination of these two approaches provides a robust and reliable color decision system for autonomous vehicles. The system is able to effectively distinguish colors in environments with varying levels of colored noise, improving the overall performance of the autonomous vehicle. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the system's implementation and validation, and demonstrates its effectiveness through experimentation.

Real-time fall detection is a critical part of ensuring the safety of individuals, particularly the elderly and those with disabilities. Microwave Doppler sensors have emerged as a promising approach for fall detection due to their non-invasive nature and ability to operate in complex environments. However, the computational cost associated with the sensors can be a significant drawback, leading to an increased risk of missed falls. In this paper, we present a computational cost reduction method based on genetic algorithms. The method utilizes time-frequency analysis and microwave measurement techniques to optimize the processing of the Doppler signal. Through the use of genetic algorithms, we are able to achieve real-time fall detection with reduced processing requirements. Our approach provides a promising solution to the challenge of resource-efficient fall detection using microwave Doppler sensors.

The emergence of modern web frameworks, microservices, and cloud architectures requires testers to generate and maintain test cases, scripts, and data in short agile sprints, sometimes in as little as a few hours. It is impossible to produce these assets in a comprehensive manner using legacy DevOps approaches that largely depend on the subjective judgement of test engineers. In this paper, we demonstrate the implementation of ATARI, an autonomous testing framework that uses a combination of search algorithms, page-rank heuristics, and reinforcement learning techniques to radically improve the completeness and velocity of testing to meet the needs of modern software engineering practices.

In this paper, a discussion on the minimization of torque ripple in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) based on robust Iterative Learning Control (ILC) via Adaptive Sliding Mode Control (ASMC) is presented. The authors focus on the challenges associated with torque measurement and minimization in nonlinear systems with uncertainty. To address this, a sliding mode control approach that utilizes ASMC is proposed. The proposed approach is capable of effectively reducing torque ripple and enhancing the performance of the PMSM. Moreover, the authors analyze the convergence of the proposed method and provide theoretical guarantees of its effectiveness. The study concludes that the proposed approach has desirable features, including the ability to operate in the presence of uncertainty, incorporating adaptive control and learning, and guaranteeing convergence.

Road segmentation is an important task in computer vision for intelligent transportation systems. In this paper, we propose a novel method for road segmentation using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Distributed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Our approach involves feature extraction using the Kernel method which is followed by segmentation using distributed LSTM. We have evaluated our method through benchmark testing on publicly available datasets and our results show that our proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. The advantage of our method lies in its ability to learn spatial and temporal dependencies of roads from a video dataset captured by cameras mounted on vehicles. We achieve this through training the CNN and distributed LSTM together. Our method has important applications in autonomous driving and intelligent transportation systems.

This paper proposes a chance-constrained scheduling approach for underground pumped hydro energy storage (UPHES) systems in the presence of model uncertainties. The study considers the uncertainty in the UPHES system's hydraulic and turbine dynamics, as well as the magnetic head losses. The goal is to determine the optimal schedule that maximizes the UPHES system's available power, while ensuring the system remains within the uncertainty constraints. The proposed approach includes a computational modeling framework, which utilizes stochastic programming and chance-constrained optimization techniques. The study also introduces a set of indexes to evaluate the scheduling results and to compare the performance of different UPHES system configurations. The results show that the proposed approach can improve the UPHES system's performance under uncertainty and provide a practical and robust solution for UPHES system operators.

In this paper, we consider a device-to-device (D2D) communications underlaying cellular network where Long Term Evolution (LTE) and D2D users are allowed to communicate over both licensed and unlicensed bands for spectrum efficiency improvement. LTE users utilize spectrum orthogonally and share it with D2D users. To maximize the total throughput of this D2D system, we leverage stochastic geometry to derive the throughput for each kind of users by modeling the deployment of users as Poisson point processes (PPPs), and investigate the mode selection problem for D2D users. Since the problem is NP-hard, we propose a sequential quadratic programming (SQP) based algorithm to obtain the corresponding suboptimal solutions. Theoretically, we evaluate the system performance by analyzing the throughput regions. Simulation results validate the accuracy of the geometric analysis and verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

This paper proposes a novel approach to program the blockchain of things using macroprogramming techniques. The blockchain technology has revolutionized the way we share and store information, and it is now being extended to the internet of things (IoT). In this context, blockchain plays a crucial role in ensuring the security and privacy of IoT devices. However, writing smart contracts for IoT applications is not an easy task, and it requires a deep understanding of blockchain technology, programming, and cryptography. In this paper, we introduce a set of libraries and program processors that enable developers to write IoT applications using high-level programming languages. Our approach enhances the programmability and usability of blockchain technology by enabling developers to build sophisticated IoT applications with ease.

This paper presents a novel bit-slicing field-programmable gate array (FPGA) accelerator for quantized neural networks. The aim is to improve the computational efficiency of neural networks, which are increasingly utilized in various fields including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. The proposed architecture leverages the parallel processing capability of FPGAs, which are reconfigurable hardware devices, to speed up the computations. Moreover, the bit-slicing technique enables the representation of weights and activations using only binary values. This reduces the memory requirement of the system and allows for faster data access. The proposed accelerator is evaluated on several datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in performance, with up to 30x speedup for some tasks. This work contributes to the field of computer architecture by providing an efficient and scalable hardware solution for implementing neural networks on system-on-chip (SoC) platforms.

This paper presents a study on student eye gaze tracking during MOOC teaching. The research focuses on using face and iris recognition technology for feature extraction to track student gaze. The experiment was conducted using special glasses equipped with eye tracking sensors. The goal of the study was to analyze the effectiveness of gaze tracking technology in education and its potential impact on student learning. The results showed that eye tracking technology can be an effective tool for tracking student attention and identifying areas where they may be struggling. However, there were also limitations to the technology, such as difficulty in capturing precise eye movements and issues with accuracy in identifying specific features of the eye. Overall, the study suggests that gaze tracking technology has promising potential in improving the quality of MOOC teaching, but further research and development are necessary to ensure its full effectiveness.

This research proposes a novel Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) Ultra-Wideband (UWB) based system for Real-Time Spectrum/Clear-to-Send (RTS/CTS) collaboration in industrial Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The system is designed to improve the performance of industrial wireless networks by addressing some of the challenges like signal to noise ratio, propagation losses, and timing. The proposed system utilizes multiple transmitters and receivers to enhance the network capacity and reliability. The collaboration between the transmitters and receivers enables the estimation of the channel capacity, allowing the system to predict scalable data rates based on the channel quality. The system's performance was evaluated in terms of throughput and energy efficiency, and results showed that it outperforms existing systems in both metrics. The proposed MIMO-UWB based RTS/CTS collaboration system is a significant contribution to industrial WSNs, improving their scalability and reliability.

This paper proposes a personalized emotion detection system called sEmoD that utilizes a smart holistic embedded IoT system. The system comprises temperature sensors, Bluetooth, and skin monitoring technologies, among other biomedical monitoring tools, to detect and track emotions in individuals. The Internet of Things (IoT) provides a platform for connecting these sensors through software, which enables the system to analyze and evaluate the collected data to determine an individual's different emotional states. The system thus provides a personalized approach to emotion detection, as sensors collect data unique to each individual, and the software is capable of analyzing and interpreting these unique data sets. The proposed system has numerous practical applications, including mental health treatment, human resources management, and even market research. The potential of sEmoD to revolutionize emotion detection and management underscores the importance of continued research in this field.

The recent success of neural networks has significantly advanced the performance of 3D human pose estimation from 2D input images. However, the diversity of capturing viewpoints and the flexibility of the human poses remain some significant challenges. In this paper, we propose a view-invariant 3D human pose estimation module to alleviate the effects of viewpoint diversity. The proposed framework consists of a base network, which provides an initial estimation of a 3D pose, a view-invariant hierarchical correction network (VI-HC) on top of that to learn the 3D pose refinement under consistent views, and a view-invariant discriminative network (VID) to enforce high-level constraints over body configurations. In VI-HC, the initial 3D pose inputs are automatically transformed to consistent views for further refinements at the global body and local body parts level, respectively. For the VID, under consistent viewpoints, we use adversarial learning to differentiate between estimated 3D poses and real 3D poses to avoid implausible results. The experimental results demonstrate that the constraint on viewpoint consistency can dramatically enhance the performance of 3D human pose estimation. Our module shows robustness for different 3D pose base networks and achieves a significant improvement (about 9%) over a powerful baseline on the public 3D pose estimation benchmark Human3.6M.

With the advances in hand-held devices (smart-phones and tablets, etc.) and high speed wireless networks, users have an explosive growth demand for live streaming service. Due to the diversity of user equipments (UEs), the live streaming has to be transcoded as different versions. However, transcoding is a computationally expensive and time consuming process. Since the shortage of computational resources and unstable of wireless networks, providing strict delay requirement and high quality live videos for wireless UEs is a big challenge. In this paper, we investigate user scheduling, transcoding decision, computational and wireless spectrum resources allocation problem in software-defined networking (SDN) based cloud-aided of heterogeneous networks (HetNets). Our research focuses on improving UEs' quality of experience (QoE) while guaranteeing time-delay requirement for live streaming services. Different from existing literature, to approach the real wireless environment, the available computational and wireless spectrum resources are modeled as random processes in our research. Considering dynamic characteristics of wireless networks and the available resources, the above problem is modeled as a Markov decision problem (MDP). Since the action space of the MDP is multi-dimensional continuous variables mixed with discrete variables, traditional learning algorithms are powerless. Therefore, an online actor critic algorithm is proposed to resolve the problem. Simulation results show the proposed algorithm has superior performances compared with the policy gradient algorithm and deep Q-learning network (DQN).

This paper explores the use of kinetic energy harvesting for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Kinetic energy is a promising energy source for IoT devices as it can be harvested from vibrations and acceleration. Energy harvesting transducers play a crucial role in converting the kinetic energy into electrical energy. However, there are challenges to be addressed in the next decade, such as improving energy conversion efficiency and understanding the impact of different environments on energy harvesting. This paper provides perspectives on the potential of kinetic energy harvesting for IoT devices and highlights the challenges that must be overcome to make this technology viable for widespread use.

This paper aims to provide insight into attempts of solving the problems of data cleaning in big data wireless sensor networks that could be used in smart cities. We focus on data cleaning algorithms and case studies of some of the more specialized problems that occur in this field, like error models, benchmark datasets, impact of certain components in datasets and the proposed order of data cleaning.

In recent years, the application of big data in industrial electrical equipment has become increasingly popular due to its enormous and complex data. However, extracting useful features from such large data sets is a challenging task. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a solution that combines the strengths of long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks and edge computing for big data feature recognition in industrial electrical equipment. The proposed solution uses the edge computing technology to avoid the limitations of traditional centralized computing by processing the data closer to the source. It trains and optimizes the LSTM model to automatically recognize the key features of big data, such as smart meters data. Additionally, we conduct a computational modelling based on artificial neural networks to evaluate the performance of the proposed solution. The results show that our solution has high accuracy and superior efficiency in handling large volumes of big data. Therefore, this research provides a promising technological innovation for big data feature recognition in industrial electrical equipment, which can significantly improve the energy efficiency and reduce cost in the manufacturing industry.

In this paper, we propose the use of Amplitude Modulation and Frequency Modulation (AM-FM) features for replay detection task. In AM-FM signal, AM component is known to be severely affected by noise (in this case, due to replay mechanism) which is exploited in proposed feature extraction. In particular, we explore this damage in AM component to corresponding instantaneous frequency. Thus, the novelty of proposed Amplitude Weighted Frequency Cosine Coefficients (AWFCC) feature set is the use of frequency components along with weighted amplitude components that are degraded due to replay noise. The AWFCC features have the information of AM-FM and hence, gave discriminatory information in the spectral characteristics. The experiments were performed on ASVspoof 2017 Challenge database using AWFCC feature set that gave an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 6.37 % (dev) and 11.72 % (eval) set. We have compared our results with CQCC, LFCC and MFCC using Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) classifier and found that proposed AWFCC feature set performed better than the other feature sets on both dev and eval datasets. In addition, we have used score-level fusion of CQCC and AWFCC to obtain a lower EER of 3.60 % and 11.22 % on dev and eval set.

This paper proposes a Document Categorization Engine that utilizes machine learning techniques to categorize documents accurately and efficiently. The engine employs various classification algorithms and machine learning algorithms that are commonly used in computer science and information technology. The categorization task is accomplished through training the engine with a set of labeled documents. Our approach differs from traditional rule-based engines, as it learns from the data and makes predictions based on the learned insights. The paper discusses different aspects of the engine, including machine learning algorithms used, training and evaluation of the engine, and its application in document categorization. The proposed engine provides an efficient and effective solution for document categorization tasks with potential applications in various fields, including information technology and machine learning.

We considered the issues of synthesis of the algorithms for adaptive nonlinear signal processing using feed-forward blocks of nonlinear transformation under the influence of non-Gaussian noise with unknown density of distribution of instantaneous values or its envelope. It is shown that to plot the adaptive feed-forward blocks of nonlinear transformation, the algorithms for estimating the parameters of linear model of probability density function of noise can be used. This model is presented in the form of a generalized polynomial of decomposition in a series of linearly independent functions, and, also, in the form of nonlinear models, such as generalized Gaussian distribution and abnormally cluttered distribution.

This paper discusses the improvement of frequency estimation for single-phase phase-locked loops using a digital RST controller. The phase locked loop is a widely used control system in power electronics applications that requires accurate frequency estimation for optimal performance. This study proposes a new approach to frequency control based on time-frequency analysis and transfer functions. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulation results which show improved frequency estimation and reduced tracking error compared to traditional PI control methods. These findings suggest that the use of the digital RST controller can significantly enhance the performance of single-phase phase-locked loops and offer a promising avenue for future research in power electronics control systems.

Analog filters design depends strongly on the appropriate selection of discrete components (Resistor and Capacitors). The challenge is to find the values which allow an optimal filters sizing with high accuracy. Some metaheuristics have proved a capacity to treat such problem effectively. In this paper, we present an application of two metaheuristic-based optimization techniques in order to select optimal values of resistors and capacitors from different manufactured series (E12, E24, E48, E96 and E192) to satisfy the filters design criteria. The Ant Colony Optimization technique (ACO) and the Genetic Algorithm (GA) are applied for the optimal sizing of two analog filters named a second order low-pass state variable filter and a high pass sallen-key filter. PSPICE simulations are given to validate the obtained results/performances.

This article surveys a stream of work in reinforcement learning (RL) focussed on the online objective. The traditional objective in RL has been to identify a good behavioural policy with as few interactions with an unknown environment as possible, but without explicitly accounting for reward earned along the way. Many sequential decision-making settings, however, require algorithms that can ensure high cumulative reward or low regret during the learning horizon. We discuss regret minimizing learning algorithms in a variety of RL settings, including the basic multi-armed bandit or stateless Markov Decision Process (MDP), structured (parametric and nonparametric) bandits, online learning in the tabula rasa MDP setting, and in structured (parametric and nonparametric) MDPs.

A design of scientific analysis service based on container technology in data cloud is presented: resource nodes are scaled up by means of automatic registration; resource nodes can be physical hosts or virtual hosts. When the utilization rate of computing resources reaches the threshold, the management node starts resource registration, subsequently, a resource host is to be registered and the available container instances are into the pool. The health of the container instance pool is maintained inside of the host. The instance lifecycle management is performed according to the maximum usage time and maximum silent time from each instance. A user can not only do analysis jobs through the interactive component, the interactive programming component or the interactive application component, which is in a separate container instance for efficient isolation of the resources, but also use data storage clusters and the high-performance computing clusters in data cloud.

Natural disasters such as earthquakes often leave post-disaster environments with severely limited resources and damaged infrastructures such as poles and towers, roads, and wireless communication networks. To mitigate the effects of these conditions, a novel network architecture for resource-constrained post-disaster environments is proposed in this paper. This architecture incorporates ad hoc networks with wireless communication and efficient resource management techniques to provide reliable and effective communication services. The proposed architecture provides a flexible and scalable solution that can easily adapt to the changing conditions of the post-disaster environment. The effectiveness of the proposed architecture is demonstrated through a simulation study, which shows that it provides better network connectivity and stability compared to existing architectures. The proposed architecture can be leveraged to facilitate the recovery and rescue operations in post-disaster environments by ensuring reliable communication services. Overall, this novel network architecture holds great potential for improving disaster response and management strategies in resource-constrained environments.

In this paper, we consider the simultaneous connectivity of primary and secondary networks forming a cognitive model. It is assumed that the cognitive model includes guard zones that prevent the nodes of the secondary network from being active in the vicinity of primary nodes to limit interference. Under these assumptions, we characterize the region of densities, the transmission radii of the nodes in each of the networks, and the guard zones for which the two networks have a unique unbounded connected component. We prove that this model is feasible, that is, there exists simultaneous connectivity with the unique unbounded connected component in each of the networks. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the simultaneous connectivity of this cognitive model.

Human action recognition for automated video surveillance applications is an interesting but a daunting task especially if the videos are captured in unfavourable lighting conditions. These situations encourage the use of multi-sensor video streams. However, simultaneous activity recognition from multiple video streams is a difficult problem due to their complementary and noisy nature. This paper proposes simultaneous action recognition from multiple video streams using deep multi-view representation learning. Furthermore, it introduces a spatio-temporal feature based correlation filter, for simultaneous detection and recognition of multiple human actions in low-light conditions. We evaluated the performance of our proposed filter with extensive experimentation on nighttime action datasets. Experimental results indicate the effectiveness of deep fusion scheme for robust action recognition in extremely low-light conditions.

This paper discusses the use of artificial neural networks and deep learning techniques to analyze sentiment in social networks for the purpose of personalized advertising in video games. The authors propose using tagging and analytical models to process the data gained from analyzing sentiment in social networks like Twitter. Through this process, robots can then be utilized to determine the most effective ads to place in video games based on user preferences and sentiment. In addition, the authors suggest that personalized advertising can be achieved through deep sentiment analysis of social networks, allowing for more precise targeting of advertising efforts. Overall, this paper provides important insights into the role of deep learning and analytical tools for personalized advertising in video games through social network sentiment analysis.

Accurately describing and classifying driving style is crucial for driving safety intervention strategies in the design of advanced driver assistance systems (ADASs). This paper presents a novel driving style classification method based on constructed driving operational pictures (DOPs) which map sequential data from naturalistic driving into 2-D pictures. By using the nested time window method, 798/1683/1153 DOPs sized 42 (features) × 60 (seconds) were generated for three different driving styles (low-risk, moderate-risk, and high-risk), respectively. The three kinds of neural network algorithms, i.e., convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and pretrain-LSTM were applied to recognize driving styles based on DOPs. The results showed that CNN performed the best with an accuracy of 98.5%, better than the traditional support vector machine (SVM) method. This study provides a new perspective to classify driving style which may help design ADASs operating characteristics to improve driving comfort and safety.

Selecting the number of assents to obtain the maximized expected return under the possible lowest risk is the main concern of portfolio optimization problems. Optimization algorithms -multi/many-objective- are evaluated to find the desired/possible level of investment. Converging to the best possible asset set and -if possible- distribution of the many possible solution sets for an efficient frontier is expected as the result of the multi/many-objective optimization algorithms. Obtaining an accurate and well-distributed set of solutions is the main motivation. Hence, in this paper, two initialization approaches are proposed for multi/many-objective optimization algorithms to obtain a better convergence and distribution solution set for the portfolio optimization problem. The initial population set is composed of the assets with the largest income and binary combinations of the assets where their sum returns the maximum income. These proposed approaches are integrated with eight different optimization algorithms and the performance of the algorithms is compared with respect to the convergence and diversity metrics.

The problem of identifying heavy hitters in IP networks has been an area of active research in recent years. In this paper, we propose a new approach known as Volumetric Hierarchical Heavy Hitters (VHHH) for identifying heavy hitters based on both the frequency and volume of traffic. We present an approximate algorithm for VHHH that achieves high throughput while accurately measuring both the frequency and volume of traffic. We evaluate the performance of VHHH under a variety of scenarios and show that it outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Our results demonstrate that VHHH is a promising approach that can be applied to a wide range of computer crime scenarios, including identifying sources of DDoS attacks, detecting network anomalies, and monitoring network traffic.

This paper proposes a robust LQR-based ANFIS control approach for the x-z inverted pendulum system. The system is challenging to control due to its highly nonlinear and unstable nature. To tackle this, a fuzzy logic-based ANFIS controller is utilized, taking into account the robustness of the system against parametric uncertainties and external disturbances. The ANFIS controller is trained using the well-known LQR technique to achieve optimal control performance. The proposed control system is tested in real-time simulations, and its effectiveness is demonstrated by achieving stabilization of the inverted pendulum while preserving robustness against disturbances. The proposed approach can be applied to various systems, including aircraft control systems, where accurate and robust control is necessary for the safe operation of the aircraft. Overall, the results obtained from this work show promising potential for the use of robust LQR-based ANFIS control in various real-world applications.

The number of containers is usually far greater than the number of virtual machines in data center. In order to avoid the energy waste caused by the frequent migration of container after initial deployment, an efficient container initial deployment strategy is particularly important. Therefore, this paper studies a many-to-one stable matching algorithm and proposes a container placement strategy MLSM. We start at an initial hosting solution for containers to reduce their migration times by using a stable matching algorithm. This algorithm uses the similarity methods as the matching preference strategy for containers and virtual machines. The virtual machine preference list is sorted by the resource utilization rate. The simulation results show that the algorithm can reduce the energy consumption by an average of 12.8% compared with using FirstFit algorithm.

This work presents a work-in-progress report on the development of a real-time smart city communication system using software defined wireless mesh networking. The research focuses on routing protocols for wireless communication in smart cities, which are becoming increasingly prevalent as a means to enhance urban sustainability and quality of life. The proposed system employs software defined networking (SDN) principles to create a highly efficient and flexible communication framework capable of adapting to varying traffic conditions in real-time. The system is designed for smart cities, which rely on wireless communication networks to support various services such as environmental monitoring, traffic management, and public safety. In addition, the system leverages IP networks for seamless integration with existing communication infrastructures. The research has the potential to contribute to improved urban planning and management by addressing the challenges of real-time communication in smart cities.

This paper compares the performance of different deep learning algorithms for indoor monitoring using bioelectric potential of living plants, which is a form of bioelectric phenomena. The study focuses on using deep learning methods, such as convolutional neural networks, for monitoring biological systems. The main goal of this research is to estimate the electric potential generated by plants in response to various indoor environmental stimuli. The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset of bioelectric potentials collected from different indoor environments, and their performance is compared based on metrics such as accuracy and computational efficiency. The results show that deep learning algorithms can effectively capture complex patterns in bioelectric signals and outperform traditional methods in terms of accuracy and speed. This study contributes to the field of electrical engineering and biological system modeling by demonstrating the potential of deep learning algorithms for indoor monitoring using bioelectric signals from living plants.

Involving consumers as influencers of the video game development process is the main feature of Steam's early access model. This has led to the exponential increase in the popularity of Steam's early access games. Steam being the most widespread digital distribution platform for video games on computers is part of the reason for the success of the early access model. Another part is the abundance of possibilities for game developers to communicate with end users and vice versa. The model is considered a success by the game development community as numerous games using Steam's early access as their distribution platform have gained a large user base (game owners) and high sales, even though, on principle early access games are not complete and are offered for sale in alpha and beta stages with no guarantees on release date or development schedule. Hence, the success of such a model cannot just be measured with owner and sale numbers. This paper aims to explore the interconnection between employing Steam's early access model and the satisfaction of consumers.

Periodic event-triggered control (PETC) is an appealing paradigm for the implementation of controllers on platforms with limited communication resources, a typical example being networked control systems. In PETC, transmissions over the communication channel are triggered by an event generator, which depends solely on the available plant and controller data and is only evaluated at given sampling instants to enable its digital implementation. In this paper, we consider the general scenario, where the controller communicates with the plant via multiple decoupled networks. Each network may contain multiple nodes, in which case a dedicated protocol is used to schedule transmissions among these nodes. The transmission instants over the networks are asynchronous and generated by local event generators. At given sampling instants, the local event generator evaluates a rule, which only involves the measurements and the control inputs available locally, to decide whether a transmission is needed over the considered network. Following the emulation approach, we show how to design local triggering generators to ensure input-to-state stability and $\mathcal {L}_p$ stability for the overall system based on a continuous-time output-feedback controller that robustly stabilizes the network-free system. The method is applied to a class of Lipschitz nonlinear systems, for which we formulate the design conditions as linear matrix inequalities. The effectiveness of the scheme is illustrated via simulations of a nonlinear example.

Computational thinking is a necessary skill for human life. However, promoting this competency in primary school students sometimes is hard and difficult for instructors. This article proposes a learning approach based on the use of a platform as part of a strategy of computational thinking to enhance learning of geometry. A case study was performed with primary school children from fourth grade at the Comfacor School (Montería-Colombia). The aim of the study was to analyze the effects of the approach in the children's motivation and performance.

This paper investigates the near optimality of linear strategies for static teams with "big" non-Gaussian noise. Specifically, it compares the performance of linear strategies under "Gaussian noise" with that under "big" non-Gaussian noise to determine their effectiveness in the latter scenario. The study finds that "Linearity" still provides a good approximation for optimal performance under "big" non-Gaussian noise with the help of "Kalman filters". Moreover, "Periodic structures" and "Covariance matrices" used in linear strategies can be optimized to better handle "big" non-Gaussian noise. The paper also discusses "Rotation measurement" and "Estimation" techniques that can be used to further improve the performance of linear strategies in these scenarios. Overall, the study shows that linear strategies can achieve near-optimal performance even in the presence of "big" non-Gaussian noise.

This paper proposes a new method for achieving variable stiffness in soft robotics, called Electrostatic Layer Jamming. The technique employs the principles of jamming via the use of electrostatics and electrodes to create friction and force between layers of material. By applying strain to the layers, the electrostatic force can be adjusted, resulting in variable stiffness. The approach offers promise for implementing soft robotic systems that can adapt to a range of environments and tasks. Key to the approach is the ability to control the behavior of the electrostatic layer, as well as the mechanical properties of the materials used. The results of this study provide a foundation for future research exploring the use of electrostatics in soft robotic applications.

Satellite attitude control system is an important subsystem that ensures the normal operation of the satellite. Aiming at the problem that the model-based fault detection method relies on modeling accuracy, an actuator fault detection method based on neural network observer is proposed. The neural network is trained with the error back propagation algorithm including a correction term to ensure the accuracy and weight bounded. The neural network is used to identify and estimate actuator failure. The stability of the observer is proved by Lyapunov method. Simulation results show that this method can effectively detect and estimate actuator failure.

The papers in this special section provide a series of high quality papers which significantly contribute to new theories, applications, and algorithms about uncertain multicriteria decision making. It not only reports recent significant developments but also highlights potential, growing research directions, and future trends, which will benefit researchers in studying theories, applications, and algorithms about uncertain multicriteria/ multiobjective/multiattribute decision making.

Recognizing human actions from the video streams has become one of the very popular research areas in computer vision and deep learning in the recent years. Action recognition is wildly used in different scenarios in real life, such as surveillance, robotics, healthcare, video indexing and human-computer interaction. The challenges and complexity involved in developing a video-based human action recognition system are manifold. In particular, recognizing actions with similar gestures and describing complex actions is a very challenging problem. To address these issues, we study the problem of classifying human actions using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and develop a hierarchical 3DCNN architecture for similar gesture recognition. The proposed model firstly combines similar gesture pairs into one class, and classify them along with all other class, as a stage-1 classification. In stage-2, similar gesture pairs are classified individually, which reduces the problem to binary classification. We apply and evaluate the developed models to recognize the similar human actions on the HMDB51 dataset. The result shows that the proposed model can achieve high performance in comparison to the state-of-the-art methods.

Leveraging high-performance software-defined networks (SDNs) to manage industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices has become a promising trend; the SDN is expected to be the next generation as a unified and virtualized network platform that provides unprecedented automation, flexibility, and efficiency. As the core of business applications and sensitive data storage, the SDN is vulnerable to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks in IIoT environment that numerous requests are sent to the SDN to interrupt its services. In the traditional defense systems, honeypots have shown great promises in resisting DDoS attacks. In this paper, we reveal a new attack that can identify honeypots to invalidate their protection. In addition, we analyze the optimal strategies of attackers, so that they can find the best time to carry on attacks. To protect SDN from such a kind of anti-honeypot attacks, we propose a pseudo-honeypot game (PHG) strategy with theoretical performance guarantee. We prove several groups of Bayesian-Nash Equilibrium in the PHG strategy. Moreover, we show that these strategies can achieve the optimal equilibrium between legitimate users and attackers. The proposed honeypot strategies can provide dynamic protection for SDN. Hence, malicious attacks under our strategies can be effectively controlled. Finally, we evaluate our proposals on a testbed, and experimental results show that our proposals can effectively resist DDoS attacks with lower energy consumption compared with the existing methods.

This paper proposes a Gaussianity-preserving event-based state estimation technique with an FIR-based stochastic trigger. The proposed approach utilizes sensors and receivers to accurately measure and examine current measurement data, while applying Kalman and Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters to reduce the estimation error. The main contribution of this work is the development of an FIR-based stochastic trigger that can effectively capture and estimate the state of a system. The proposed method is experimentally validated on a benchmark system to demonstrate its superior performance over conventional approaches. In summary, the proposed approach offers an effective solution for preserving Gaussianity while estimating the state of a system, which can have important implications in various applications such as robotics, automation, and control.

This paper presents a new hybrid heuristic algorithm for the job shop scheduling problem with maintenance, delay and setup costs, and setup times. A mathematical model was initially developed to solve the problem composed of up to 10 orders. Solving large-scale problems, however, proved to be extremely time-consuming due to existing limitations and variables within the model; therefore, the hybrid simulated annealing (HSA) method was presented for large-scale problems. HSA efficiently solved the large-scale problems with a large number of orders in a proper minimized time.

For a popular class of nonlinear systems, an observer can be constructed by rendering estimation error dynamics linear in unmeasured state variables. However, measurement disturbance violates the structure of the error dynamics and brings in undesirable terms in which the estimation error and the plant state are often coupled and multiplied by the measurement disturbance. This is why local analysis and semi-global design have been performed in many cases. This paper introduces new flexibility into the iISS small-gain framework to accommodate such terms. It is demonstrated how the flexible framework enables global analysis of observer-based output feedback control systems to achieve convergence and boundedness in the presence of measurement disturbance.

This paper presents a comparative research study on various swarm intelligence clustering algorithms for analyzing medical data. Clustering algorithms play a vital role in data mining, and in this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of different algorithms, such as particle swarm optimization, in optimizing the process. The mathematical model of the algorithms and their time complexity are studied and compared to determine which algorithm performs the best for analyzing medical data. This research is valuable because it helps to identify the most efficient and effective swarm intelligence clustering algorithm for solving search problems within medical data analysis.

There is a sheer growth of attention on the issue of deep learning attacks launched by adversaries. Especially with the spread of edge computing devices that cooperate with the central cloud, how to protect the neural network models and private data from being attacked becomes a hot topic. In this paper, we consider two collaborative edge-cloud deep learning scenarios. The first is that deep learning models are trained on resource-rich cloud and deployed on the terminal deep learning accelerators for delay-sensitive tasks. While in the second scenario, edge collected data is offloaded to the cloud for computationally-intensive tasks. In both scenarios, the valuable pre-trained neural network models and the private data are exposed to the risks of being attacked if they are transmitted and processed in an unencrypted way. To tackle this security problem, we present a lightweight protection scheme towards data-oriented attacks and model-oriented attacks. With the use of on-chip memory Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and Processing-In-Memory (PIM), our method limits the model execution only on specific edge devices and also prevents the unauthorized analysis of private data. Experiments on state-of-the-art deep learning networks show that our method secures edge deep learning models and user-data with a negligible performance overhead.

This paper studies the use of drone-base stations to enhance the performance of heterogeneous cellular networks. In particular, we analyze the impact of deploying drone-base stations on the bit rate, signal to noise ratio, and overall performance of these cellular networks. Through simulations and experiments, we demonstrate that the use of drone-base stations can significantly improve the quality of service provided by these networks, especially in areas with poor or nonexistent coverage. We also investigate the potential benefits of satellite broadcasting in conjunction with drone-base stations. Our findings suggest that the use of drone-base stations can be a promising solution for improving the coverage and performance of cellular networks, and we discuss the implications of our results for future research and development in this area. This work was presented at several conferences and is an important contribution to the ongoing efforts to improve wireless communication systems and services.

The diagnostic systems of aphasia are tools that allow the specialist to recognize the degree of the disorder that a patient possesses, in this way facilitate and follow up the treatment that allows the patient to recover speech through therapies. This article shows the development of a computational platform that allows the configuration and execution of tests to make a diagnosis in patients with aphasia. The activities that the doctor can configure and design on the platform include different levels of difficulty that will be stored in a database, which depending on the agility and ability of the user, will give the specialist support to generate their diagnosis.

This paper presents an adaptive time-delay control method to handle the balance of a class of biped robots. Considering model uncertainties and unknown external disturbances, a high-dimensional integral Lyapunov function has been developed, then time-delay estimation technique (TDE) is utilized, and in order to compensate for the errors produced by TDE, an adaptive control law is designed. Based on the evolution of the error trajectories, the adaptive control law can automatically regulate the control gains without any threshold value. By the Lyapunov synthesis, the semiglobally uniformly ultimately boundness (UUB) of the closed-loop control system has been theoretically proved. We have conducted the experimental studies on biped robot to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

This paper proposes an adaptive network fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) based decision support system that can provide European policy makers with systematic guidance in allocating and prioritizing scant public resources, whilst accomplishing the best growth performance at a regional level. We do so by taking the stance of the Smart Specialization Strategies, which aim at consolidating the regional strengths and make effective and efficient use of public investment in R&D. By applying the ANFIS method, we were able to understand how - and to what extent - the competitiveness drivers promoted technological development and how the latter contributes to the economic growth of European regions. We used socio-economic, spatial, and patent-based data to train, test, and validate the models. What emerges is that an increase of R&D investments enhances the regional employment rate and the number of patents per capita; in turn, by taking into account the several combinations of specialization and diversification indicators, this leads to an increase of the regional gross domestic product (GDP).

The Internet of Things (IoT) is a rapidly growing area with a substantial number of interconnected devices, sensors, and actuators providing data and services to various domains, including medical services. Programming such a diverse and complex infrastructure requires lightweight and adaptive technologies to manage the heterogeneity of IoT devices and their communication patterns. The Fluidware approach presents an adaptive flow programming model that abstracts the IoT devices as fabrics, providing an easy-to-use programming interface for users interested in designing IoT services. The fluidware platform uses these fabrics to construct dynamic service flows that can be deployed, reconfigured and composed based on the context of the deployment environment, thus increasing system resilience and flexibility. The approach has been evaluated in various domains and continues to attract significant attention in the research community, with many conferences dedicated to the topic. This article presents the Fluidware approach and its potential use in the IoT domain.

This paper proposes a joint exploitation of Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) and Phase Comparison Localization (PCL) techniques for two-dimensional target localization. A mathematical model is presented to formalize the problem, which enables the derivation of signal processing algorithms. The research is particularly relevant in the domains of aerospace and electronic systems, where the detection and tracking of targets are of utmost importance. Two dimensional displays are leveraged to visualize the estimated target location. The estimation algorithm relies on radio transmitters and the use of linear matrix inequalities to solve the optimization problem. Such a methodology could lead to greater precision in target localization, which in turn may facilitate early detection of danger and improved situational awareness.

This paper is based on genetic algorithm to solve the target assignment problem in the course of target reconnaissance. In order to increase the efficiency and improve the local search ability of the genetic algorithm, a hybrid algorithm of genetic algorithm and hill-climbing algorithm is adopted in this paper. And population catastrophe is also used to improve the performance of hybrid algorithm. The simulation results show that the improved algorithm has faster solution speed, better optimization capability, and can solve target assignment problem effectively.

This paper considers mobile computation offloading where task completion times are subject to hard deadline constraints. Hard deadlines are difficult to meet in conventional computation offloading due to the stochastic nature of the wireless channels involved. Rather than using binary offload decisions, we permit concurrent remote and local job execution when it is needed to ensure task completion deadlines. The paper addresses this problem for homogeneous Markovian wireless channel models. An online energy-optimal computation offloading algorithm, OnOpt, is proposed. Its energy optimality is shown by constructing a time-dilated absorbing Markov process and applying dynamic programming. Closed form results are derived for general Markovian processes, and the Gilbert-Elliott channel model is used to show how the particular structure of the Markov chain can be exploited in computing optimal offload initiation times more efficiently. It is shown that job completion time probabilities can be computed recursively, which leads to a significant reduction in the computational complexity of OnOpt. The performance of the proposed algorithm is compared to three others, namely, Immediate Offloading, Channel Threshold, and Local Execution. Performance results show that the proposed algorithm can significantly improve mobile device energy consumption compared to the other approaches while guaranteeing hard task execution deadlines.

Although traffic sign detection has been a well investigated area of topic for researchers, since the data itself is so region-specific, it demands further exploration. This paper focuses on the 10 most common Thai traffic signs using a dataset derived from the combination of our own dataset via Google Street View and the BTSD as well as the GTSRB dataset. Our aim is real-time detection at a much less processing time. We employ the use of YOLO version3 as our state-of-the-art recognition system that uses global instead of local features in its detection. With the use of logistics regression, it ensures accurate prediction of bounding boxes. Our dataset has been properly augmented and tested to account for disturbances such as occlusion, damage and perspective changes. In addition, we apply convolutional neural networks to detect and recognize Thai traffic sign and demonstrate that the average precision of 0.93 and above.

With the current significant penetration of mobile devices (i.e. smartphones and tablets) and the tremendous increase in the number of the corresponding mobile applications, they have become an indispensable part of our lives. Nowadays, there is a significant growth in the number of sensitive applications such as personal health applications, personal financial applications, home monitoring applications, etc. In addition, with the significant growth of Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, smartphones and the corresponding applications are widely considered as the Internet gateways for these devices. Mobile devices mostly use wireless LANs (WLANs) (i.e., WiFi networks) as the prominent network interface to the Internet. However, due to the broadcast nature of WiFi links, wireless traffics are exposed to any eavesdropping adversary within the WLAN. Despite WiFi encryption, studies show that application usage information could be inferred from the encrypted wireless traffic. The leakage of this sensitive information is very serious issue that will significantly impact users' privacy and security. In addressing this privacy concern, we design and develop a lightweight programmable privacy framework, called PrivacyGuard. PrivacyGuard is inspired by the vision of pushing the Software Defined Network (SDN)-like paradigm all the way to wireless network edge, is designed to support of adopting privacy preserving policies to protect the wireless communication of the sensitive applications. In this paper, we demonstrate and evaluate a prototype of PrivacyGuard framework on Android devices showing the flexibility and efficiency of the framework.

In recent years, two-way MIMO relay systems have gained significant attention in wireless communication due to their remarkable features. However, channel estimation remains a challenging task, especially in a relay network. To address this issue, various channel estimation methods have been proposed, among which training-based algorithms have shown promising results. In this paper, we propose an efficient channel estimation algorithm for two-way MIMO relay systems based on the training method. The proposed algorithm utilizes a relay to estimate the channel parameters between two nodes and operates with a low complexity. Additionally, our algorithm considers the effects of the relay on the channel estimation, which improves the accuracy of the estimates. The performance of our proposed scheme is analyzed in terms of bit-error rate and shows a superior performance compared to existing methods. The proposed algorithm offers a simple and effective solution to channel estimation in two-way MIMO relay systems, making it a practical choice for wireless communication systems. Finally, we provide a complexity theory analysis to show that the proposed algorithm has a low computational complexity, which makes it suitable for real-time applications.

Barrett's esophagus is a condition characterized by abnormal changes in the cells lining the lower end of the esophagus. Early detection of this condition is crucial for effective treatment and management. In recent years, image color analysis using techniques such as color co-occurrence matrices has become an increasingly popular method for identifying Barrett's esophagus. This approach involves the extraction of features from images using specialized algorithms and the subsequent use of databases containing gray-scale histograms to identify patterns associated with the condition. Various protocols have been developed for the use of these techniques in clinical settings, with promising results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Overall, the use of image color analysis for Barrett's esophagus identification represents a promising avenue for improving the detection and treatment of this condition.

The fourth industrial revolution has spurred the development of 5G mobile communication, enabling seamless connectivity for the internet of things and catering to high-bandwidth applications. Resource management in 5G networks poses challenges, particularly in the realm of radio resource scheduling, which requires intelligent scheduling algorithms. Reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, provide a means for dynamic scheduling of resources in 5G networks. This algorithm learns through trial and error, enabling it to make decisions based on experience and optimize resource allocation based on dynamic user behavior. The use of DDPG in radio resource scheduling allows for better management of Quality of Service (QoS) and ensures that user requirements are satisfied while minimizing resource waste. In summary, the use of reinforcement learning algorithms such as DDPG is a promising approach to resource scheduling for 5G NR networks, particularly in the context of dynamic scheduling and QoS management.

This paper presents a cloud-based architecture designed to implement an electronic health record (EHR) system in hospitals in Pakistan. The system utilizes cloud computing technologies to store and manage medical records in a centralized database. The overall architecture is based on a distributed server infrastructure that ensures high availability and scalability of the system. The design emphasizes on security and privacy measures, ensuring the confidentiality of data transmission and storage. The proposed system also makes use of medical diagnostic imaging, allowing for easy and rapid access to patient medical imaging records. The use of electronic medical records in the cloud provides a streamlined approach to managing patient data, enabling health professionals to make timely and informed decisions about patient care. The study presents a new approach to managing medical records in Pakistan and other developing countries by utilizing cloud computing technologies and computer architecture to achieve efficiency, scalability, and security.

In this paper, a novel approach for designing fused helico-spiral coils is proposed using both neural network and generic algorithms. Genetic algorithms have been used for optimizing the performance of the helico-spiral coils through coupling with the biological neural networks. The spiral geometry of the coils has been optimized to maximize the Q-factor, which determines the quality of the signal transmission. The proposed approach has been shown to outperform conventional methods for designing helico-spiral coils. The results of the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its potential in optimizing the performance of helico-spiral coils for various applications. This paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of coil design by offering a powerful and efficient method for achieving optimal performance through the integration of genetic algorithms and neural network coupling.

In this paper, we propose a method of carrier frequency estimation for time-frequency overlapped MASK signals in underlay cognitive radio networks. Time-frequency analysis is employed to reveal the characteristics of the signals in both time and frequency domains. By exploiting these characteristics, the frequency estimation is carried out using a peak searching algorithm with the signal to noise ratio taken into consideration. The proposed method is verified through simulation experiments under different scenarios, including frequency shift keying and temperature measurement. The results show that the proposed method can effectively estimate the carrier frequency even in the presence of interference. The proposed method is a promising solution to improve the performance of cognitive radio networks.

This paper considers automatic clinical workflow description of full-length routine fetal anomaly ultrasound scans using deep learning approaches for spatio-temporal video analysis. Multiple architectures consisting of 2D and 2D + t CNN, LSTM, and convolutional LSTM are investigated and compared. The contributions of short-term and long-term temporal changes are studied, and a multi-stream framework analysis is found to achieve the best top-l accuracy =0.77 and top-3 accuracy =0.94. Automated partitioning and characterisation on unlabelled full-length video scans show high correlation (ρ=0.95, p=0.0004) with workflow statistics of manually labelled videos, suggesting practicality of proposed methods.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey on Human-centered Reinforcement Learning (HCRL). The main focus of HCRL is to incorporate human feedback and preferences in the reinforcement learning process, enabling agents to learn from more informative signals when compared with traditional reinforcement learning methods. One of the main contributions of this paper is the analysis of task requirements and potential applications of HCRL. In addition, the authors discuss various reinforcement learning algorithms and techniques that have been proposed for HCRL, including exploration-exploitation trade-offs, priority sampling, and model-based approaches. The paper also addresses the challenges of defining standards and evaluation metrics for HCRL, as well as the use of search methods and man-machine systems for developing effective HCRL approaches. Lastly, the authors touch upon the emerging field of robot learning and its implications for HCRL, as well as the importance of programming interfaces and frameworks for enabling researchers and practitioners to leverage the power of HCRL in their respective fields.

This paper proposes a novel credit scoring framework for auto loans, which utilizes an imbalanced-learning-based reject inference approach. The framework incorporates semisupervised learning, which allows for the use of a mix of labeled and unlabeled data to enhance prediction accuracy. Inference algorithms and classification algorithms are also employed to improve the performance of credit scoring. The proposed framework is validated using a dataset of auto loan applications from companies in the financial industry. Additionally, the framework is compared to traditional credit scoring methods, and it shows improved results in terms of prediction accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed framework, similar to biological system modeling, involves a training process that involves analyzing multiple data models to build a comprehensive credit scoring model. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for improving credit scoring in the auto loan industry.

In this paper, we apply the NetFV and NetVLAD layers for the end-to-end language identification task. NetFV and NetVLAD layers are the differentiable implementations of the standard Fisher Vector and Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors (VLAD) methods, respectively. Both of them can encode a sequence of feature vectors into a fixed dimensional vector which is very important to process those variable-length utterances. We first present the relevances and differences between the classical i-vector and the aforementioned encoding schemes. Then, we construct a flexible end-to-end framework including a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture and an encoding layer (NetFV or NetVLAD) for the language identification task. Experimental results on the NIST LRE 2007 close-set task show that the proposed system achieves significant EER reductions against the conventional i-vector baseline and the CNN temporal average pooling system, respectively.

This paper investigates the use of multilayer perceptron (MLP) models for predicting band diagrams in bi-dimensional photonic crystals. The proposed approach involves training MLP models using computational modeling techniques to accurately predict the band diagrams of these structures. The paper also explores the use of two dimensional displays to visualize the predicted band diagrams. Furthermore, the authors discuss the implications of computer architecture and the significance of the dielectric constant in generating accurate predictions. Overall, the study suggests that MLP models, which are inspired by neurons in the human brain, offer a promising approach to predicting band diagrams in bi-dimensional photonic crystals.

Image registration is an important task in the field of remote sensing, particularly when different types of images, such as optical and radar, are acquired. This paper proposes a deep fully convolutional neural network (FCN) for the registration of multimodal remote sensing images. The proposed method achieves accurate measurement and feature extraction through the use of optical imaging and optical sensors, enabling precise alignment of different modalities. Task analysis is carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed method, and its superior results compared to existing methods are demonstrated. The application of the proposed method will provide improved data quality and more effective use of remote sensing data, particularly in areas such as environmental monitoring, emergency response and urban planning.

This paper presents LENTA, a Longitudinal Exploration tool for Network Traffic Analysis from Passive Data. LENTA utilizes clustering algorithms coupled with machine learning techniques to analyze big data for malware and security threats. The scalability of LENTA is achieved by a distributed computation model, and its ability to handle large volumes of data is crucial for effective network traffic analysis. By using data mining techniques, LENTA can identify patterns in network traffic, providing insight into potential security breaches. Overall, LENTA serves as a valuable tool for network administrators in their efforts to maintain the security of their systems.

This paper presents a practical methodology for traveling wave (TW)-based fault location on homogeneous transmission lines. It provides improvements in the fault location accuracy in real-world scenarios by eliminating the influence of uncertainties in line parameters and data time synchronization errors, which are potentialities not readily available in actual micro-processed fault location devices. A commercially available software for TW analysis is proposed to be used as a support tool to compute auxiliary variables, from which the accurate fault distance is estimated. Real and simulated TW fault records are assessed, from which the proposed fault location procedure is evaluated, highlighting its step by step. The obtained results show that the proposed methodology is straightforward and reliable, being quite useful for field applications.

In this paper, we propose an efficient entropy-based causal discovery method for linear structural equation models with independent and identically distributed (IID) noise variables. The aim is to detect the underlying causal relationships between variables, while accounting for measurement errors. We introduce a simple mathematical model and derive an entropy-based criterion to identify candidate causal structures using Markov processes. The proposed method can handle large-scale distributed databases and is robust to different data models. We also present an estimation algorithm that can efficiently compute the likelihood of each candidate structure. Our experiments show that our proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency in discovering the causal structure of data.

Facial expression recognition is an important area of research in computer vision and artificial intelligence. In this paper, we explore the effectiveness of local learning using both deep and handcrafted features for facial expression recognition. Our approach involves training computational models using support vector machines and convolutional neural networks. We analyze the task of facial expression recognition and experiment with different feature combinations to improve recognition accuracy. Our results show that the combination of deep learning and handcrafted features can significantly improve recognition accuracy, especially for complex expressions. Our study contributes to the ongoing effort to develop more accurate and efficient facial expression recognition systems.

We consider a spatial vector field estimation problem with vehicles modeled as unicycles. The vector field is assumed to affect the motion of the vehicles in an additive fashion. We investigate whether the position information of the vehicles can be used to simultaneously estimate the unknown field parameters and the heading information of the vehicles. Starting with a single vehicle case, we design a stable nonlinear observer and reveal a persistence of excitation (PE) condition on the vehicle's motion that guarantees the convergence of the field parameter estimates and the heading estimates almost globally. We next extend the observer for multiple vehicles with a strongly connected communication topology and provide a PE condition to ensure filter convergence. The effectiveness of the designed observers is demonstrated with simulations of vehicles estimating a rotational field.

High speed vehicles or driving by consuming alcohol is one of the main reasons of accidents. So, the number of accidents can be decreased by controlling the vehicles moving at higher speed. In this paper, we proposed a Position Based High Speed Vehicle Detection Algorithm (PHVA) for detecting the higher speed vehicles in a Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) by using a vehicular cloud server, where the cloud server is used as computing as a service. The proposed algorithm calculates the speed of a vehicle based on the data directly received from the Road Side Units (RSUs). When a vehicle comes under the coverage of an RSU, RSU receives the time, position and other information about the vehicle. RSU then sends the received information to the Cloud Server (CS). Based on the information received from the nearby RSUs, the CS calculates the average speed for that vehicle in a particular lane. The calculated speed is then compared with that of the permitted speed on that lane. If it is greater than the permitted limit, then the CS increments the speed violation counter for that vehicle. Depending upon the frequency of violation and with the help of Certification Authority (CA), appropriate action will be taken on that high speed vehicle. To check the efficiency of our PHVA algorithm, we simulated our work in Vehicles in Network Simulation (Veins) hybrid simulation framework. Veins uses Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) as the road traffic simulator and OMNeT++ as the network simulator. Both simulators are connected via a TCP socket which has been standardized in Traffic Control Interface (TraCI). The results show that our algorithm has better detection accuracy over ReVISE scheme in this environment.

This paper proposes a single fault diagnostic method for regenerative permanent magnet synchronous machine drives with the ability to handle multiple insulated gate bipolar transistor faults, single current sensor fault, and rotor-position disconnection. The considered faults are discriminated, and the faulty device is correctly identified in each case. The robustness against false alarms is improved by using adaptive thresholds and normalized diagnostic variables. The proposed algorithm requires the information given by current sensors and the rotor position sensor that are already available from the drive system, without requiring a high computational burden. Simulation and experimental results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the considered algorithm for both motoring and regenerative operations.

This position paper proposes an extension of the codelet model for dataflow software pipelining using software-hardware co-design. The paper focuses on the optimization of software pipeline processing and computational modeling by incorporating hardware components into the software design. The proposed model utilizes data models to enhance the efficiency of software-hardware co-design for pipeline processing. With the integration of hardware components, the codelet model can achieve higher throughput and reduced latency, even in complex processing tasks. The paper concludes that the extended codelet model is a promising approach for optimizing pipeline processing in dataflow software, and has the potential to revolutionize software-hardware co-design in the field of computing.

This paper proposes an adaptive Type-2 FNN-based dynamic sliding mode control approach for DC-DC boost converters under uncertainty. The approach integrates fuzzy control, voltage control, fuzzy neural networks, inductors, capacitors, and perturbation methods to deliver robust and accurate control. The proposed control method consists of a sliding mode controller with a Type-2 fuzzy neural network-based adaptive system, which is capable of handling uncertain and dynamic situations. The fuzzy neural network allows for the identification of the system's dynamics and the estimation of uncertain parameters. The proposed adaptive control approach is tested on a DC-DC boost converter under different uncertain scenarios, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the system's transient response, robustness, and stability. Overall, this study presents a promising approach towards enhancing DC-DC boost converter control under uncertainty.

The constrained command tracking problem for the cloud robotic system with unknown bounded time-varying delays is considered. Based on a novel predictor-observer approach, a command governor is proposed to modify the received command in order to guarantee the constraint enforcement of remote robot. We firstly use a prediction algorithm in the forward channel to generate a virtual command, which is close to the original one as much as possible when the danger of constraint violation exists. Then, to deal with the measurement delay and disturbance in the backward channel, interval estimations of the system states are applied instead of delayed measurements in the prediction algorithm of the command governor. The constraints can be rigorously enforced with the upper and lower estimations. The efficiency of the proposed approach is demonstrated by simulations in the case of a single-degree-of-freedom manipulator.

Mobile position estimation is critical for wireless communication applications. In this paper, a novel hybrid location algorithm based on chaotic particle swarm optimization (CPSO) is proposed to improve the accuracy of position measurement. The algorithm is based on the mathematical model of particle swarm optimization and incorporates chaos theory to better handle the problem of delays in obtaining location information. The chaotic behavior of particles is employed to increase their diversity and explore more search space. The proposed algorithm is compared with traditional particle swarm optimization algorithms and simulation results show that it achieves better localization accuracy, especially in the presence of delays. The effectiveness and applicability of the algorithm in real wireless communication systems are also demonstrated. Overall, the proposed CPSO-based algorithm provides a promising approach for accurate mobile position estimation in wireless networks.

Chatbots, i.e., systems that can interact with humans in a more appropriate way using natural language, have been of increasing importance. This is due the fact of the availability of computational means for natural language interaction between computers and humans that are becoming closer to the interaction between humans alone. Consequently, there are more and more chatbots available that are intended to support humans organizing tasks or making decisions. In this paper, we focus on how to verify the communication capabilities provided by chatbots. In particular, we introduce an automated approach for generating communication sequences and carrying them out. The approach is based on AI planning where each action can be assumed to be a certain question that is given to the chatbot. The answer of the chatbot should make the action post-condition true, in order to proceed with the plan. In cases of deviations between the actual chatbot behavior and the expected one, re-planning is required.
