The proposed approach leverages virtual servers, cloud computing, and 3GPP standards to efficiently recover from network failures. Middleware is utilized to ensure seamless communication between different components. The system is constantly monitored to detect any issues and quickly initiate recovery procedures. The results of the experiment demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in recovering from various types of network failures. The approach presented in this paper can be implemented in various scenarios to enhance the resilience and reliability of 5G mobile communication systems.

This paper explores the integration of the blended learning concept into employee training as a factor in shifting mentalities towards the Industry 4.0 approach. It investigates how this approach can improve the training offered to employees in various industries and companies, particularly in production facilities and automotive engineering. With technological advancements and a rapidly evolving business landscape, training must adapt to effectively address the needs of employees and companies. Blended learning incorporates various techniques, including online modules and in-person workshops, to provide a comprehensive and effective training experience. The study shows that this approach can help companies bridge the gap between traditional learning methods and new technologies, ensuring their employees receive the necessary training to adapt to Industry 4.0. The findings highlight that employee engagement and participation are crucial to the success of such training initiatives, emphasizing the importance of a workforce that is receptive to new innovations and ideas. Ultimately, the integration of the blended learning concept into employee training can play a key role in shifting mentalities towards the Industry 4.0 approach and aiding industries and companies in achieving their desired outcomes.

This paper explores aspect-oriented modeling in the context of concurrent systems, using the Unified Modeling Language (UML). Computational modeling techniques are employed to construct precise adaptation models for software systems, thereby increasing their flexibility and adaptability. The semantics of aspect-oriented modeling are examined, focusing on the automation of the adaptation process. The benefits of aspect-oriented modeling are discussed in the context of software design, highlighting its ability to address issues of complexity and maintainability. Finally, this paper surveys relevant conferences on aspect-oriented modeling and their contribution to the field.

Long quasi-cyclic low-density parity check (QC-LDPC) codes have been chosen as one of the forward error correction (FEC) schemes in passive optical network (PON) systems benefiting from the excellent performance. About how to get the appropriate LDPC codes, some traditional methods which focus on obtaining large girth or flat approximated cycle extrinsic message degree (ACE) spectrums are proposed for the design of LDPC codes. These methods which may still make the existence of small stopping sets containing short cycles probably are not so useful for long QC-LDPC codes. Recently, the parallel vector message passing (PMP) algorithm oriented-to decreasing the number of short cycles is proved to be an effective method to optimize LDPC codes. Since ignoring short cycles with poor connectivity which can induce error floor, this method cannot guarantee its effectiveness for long QC-LDPC codes. In this letter, an edge exchange optimization method based on the global properties of ACE and girth called EEA method is proposed, which tries to reduce cycles with low ACE in the order of cycle length. The numerical results prove that our EEA method can bring the improvements of error floor up to two orders of magnitude to long QC-LDPC codes and obviously outperforms PMP algorithm.

Protein remote homology detection is one of the most challenging problems in the field of protein sequence analysis, which is an important step for both theoretical research (such as the understanding of structures and functions of proteins) and drug design. Previous studies have shown that combining different ranking methods via learning to the rank algorithm is an effective strategy for remote protein homology detection, and the performance can be further improved by the protein similarity networks. In this paper, we improved the ProtDec-LTR1.0 and ProtDec-LTR2.0 predictors by incorporating three profile-based features (Top-1-gram, Top-2-gram, and ACC) into the framework of learning to rank via feature mapping strategies. The predictive performance was further refined by the pagerank (PR) algorithm and hyperlink-induced topic search (HITS) algorithm. Finally, a predictor called ProtDec-LTR3.0 was proposed. Rigorous tests on two widely used benchmark datasets showed that the ProtDec-LTR3.0 predictor outperformed both ProtDec-LTR1.0 and ProtDec-LTR2.0, and other nine existing state-of-the-art predictors, indicating that the ProtDec-LTR3.0 is an efficient method for protein remote homology detection, and will become a useful tool for protein sequence analysis. A user-friendly web server of the ProtDec-LTR3.0 predictor was established for the convenience of users, which can be accessed at http://bliulab.net/ProtDec-LTR3.0/.

A Potential solution for solving forensic is the use of blockchain in software-defined networking (SDN). The blockchain is a distributed peer-to-peer network that can be utilized on SDN-based Internet of Things (IoT) environments for security provisioning. Hence, to meet some challenges in digital forensics such as data integrity, evidence deletion or alteration, blockchain is used. However, some problems such as poor attack detection and slow processing existed in previous works. To address these issues, an efficient forensics architecture is proposed in SDN-IoT that establishes the Chain of Custody (CoC) in blockchain technology. The proposed SDN-based IoT architecture is initiated with flow table rules on switches for the three different traffics Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), File Transfer Protocol (FTP), and Hyper Text Transfer Protocol (HTTP). In this work, overloaded switches migrate the packets to nearby switches to balance the packet flow. The packets disobeying flow rules will be discarded by switches. The blockchain-based distributed controller in this forensic architecture is designed to use the Linear Homomorphic Signature (LHS) algorithm for validating users. Each controller is fed with a classifier that uses the Neuro Multi-fuzzy to classify malicious packets based on packet features. The logs of events are used and stored on the blockchain in the proposed SDN-IoT architecture. We evaluated the performance of our forensic architecture and compared it to the existing model using various performance measures. Our evaluation results demonstrate performance improvement by reducing delay, response time and processing time, increasing throughput, accuracy, and security parameters.

In order to realize the transient and accident analysis of reactor system and verification of system control scheme, the latest computer technology is used to develop advanced graphical modeling tool for TRANTH code, the human-machine interaction interface, and integration research between software and digital reactor design and verification platform, so as to the design and simulation system of digital reactor fluid instruction control system is built up. The nuclear power plant (ACP1000) is chosen as a research object some typical operating conditions are selected and executed. Results show that the design and simulation system can implement the modeling, calculation, interactive manipulation and display of reactor fluid instruction control system, which brings a multi-professional joint simulation of reactor fluid instruction control system to fruition, and provides technology support for rapid generation, evaluation, verification and optimization of design scheme about reactor fluid instruction control system.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized the way we interact with and utilize data. With the vast number of sensors and connected devices, it is essential to ensure that databases are performing optimally for IoT systems. This paper evaluates databases performance for IoT systems using the Scrovegni Chapel as a use case. The study focuses on analyzing the hardware requirements for databases, evaluating the performance of wireless sensor networks, and ensuring that Structured Query Language queries are executed efficiently. By analyzing these key factors, this study provides insights into the best practices for designing and implementing databases for IoT systems. It highlights the importance of ensuring that the hardware is capable of supporting the database workload and that the wireless sensor networks are designed to handle the data throughput effectively. Ultimately, this paper demonstrates the importance of rigorous performance evaluation when designing databases for IoT systems.

This study mainly explores the science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) training courses for the engineering cost professionals. By means of literature review, in-depth interview, expert questionnaire and other research methods, the traditional education courses are summed up and classified; and the stem education courses are systematized by means of the Interpretative Structural Modeling Method, in order to construct the learning path. After gathering the opinions, by analysis of the learning path for stem training courses, the teaching system for the engineering cost professionals in theoretical and practical learning is developed to achieve the better educated effects. The research and analysis results can be used as a reference for the STEM training courses for the engineering cost professionals.

This paper proposes a low-energy smart cities network based on LoRa and Bluetooth technologies. With the rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT), the demand for reliable and efficient wireless personal area networks (WPANs) is increasing. To address this need, the proposed network employs edge computing to minimize power consumption and enhance data processing. In addition, computer architecture and cloud computing are also utilized to enable seamless connectivity and data management within the network. Bluetooth technology serves as an important protocol for device communication, facilitating the reliable transmission of data over short distances. The proposed network has the potential to improve the efficiency of smart city operations and enhance the user experience.

This paper introduces a framework for local information privacy called "Lips" which leverages perturbation methods to protect privacy while still allowing for accurate estimation of data models. By introducing bounded prior knowledge, Lips can achieve a higher level of privacy while still maintaining the desired level of estimation accuracy. Differential privacy is utilized to further improve privacy guarantees by adding noise to sensitive data. Through experiments on real-world datasets, the authors demonstrate the effectiveness of Lips in preserving privacy while achieving accurate estimation results. The Lips framework adds a novel and flexible method for local information privacy, providing a valuable tool for data protection in the digital age.

This paper proposes a new approach for the creation of therapeutic games using KINECT sensor, targeting the medical services sector. The proposed approach is based on a combination of computational modeling and production tools, which takes into consideration the in-depth needs of the patients. This approach makes use of games and training exercises to help patients recover and improve their overall wellbeing. The paper proposes proposals that address aspects of the therapeutic games creation such as the selection of appropriate games, the use of proprioceptive and kinesthetic feedback, and the development of appropriate training programs. These proposals create a roadmap for the development of therapeutic games that are tailor-made to the needs of the patient, making use of technology to improve the quality of care provided by medical services. Overall, this paper highlights the importance of creating therapeutic games that are specifically designed for the patient and the need for further research in this area to take healthcare to greater heights.

This paper presents a method for automatic segmentation and identification of spinous processes on sagittal X-rays using random forest classification and dedicated contextual features. Image segmentation is a fundamental task in medical imaging that aims to separate the regions of interest from the background. In this work, the authors propose a novel approach that utilizes radio frequency to quantify the shape of spinous processes and extract meaningful features. Compared to manual segmentation, the proposed method achieves excellent performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The authors demonstrate the usefulness of their method by applying it to real-world datasets of various sizes and complexities. Their results show that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches for spinous process segmentation and identification. Overall, this study provides a valuable contribution to the field of medical image analysis and could have important applications in clinical practice for the measurement and diagnosis of spinal disorders.

This paper proposes a fully-automatic method for segmenting kidneys in clinical ultrasound images using a Boundary Distance Regression Network (BDRN). The method focuses on improving image segmentation accuracy, which is a critical aspect in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions affecting the kidneys. The proposed technique employs feature extraction and shape modeling to automatically identify kidney boundaries in ultrasonic imaging. The training of the BDRN also enables the algorithm to adapt to different datasets and achieve better generalization of kidney segmentation. Results show that the proposed approach can achieve high segmentation accuracy, demonstrating its potential for clinical applications in the medical field.

This paper presents a detailed design of a second-order model of a lithium-ion battery simulator based on experimental measurements. The study focuses on the mathematical model and integrated circuit modeling of the battery simulator for accurate voltage and battery charge measurement. Various tools, algorithm, and techniques have been used for the parameter estimation of the simulator. The proposed second-order model can provide an accurate representation of the battery behavior and can facilitate the development of battery management systems. The experimental measurements and simulation results demonstrate the validity and effectiveness of the proposed model. The study also highlights the potential application of the proposed model in the development of electric vehicle battery systems.

With the advent of virtual reality (VR) technology, researchers are now exploring novel methods of assessing spatial presence in omnidirectional videos (ODV). In this paper, we propose a new method for assessing the spatial presence of ODV by comparing virtual and real-world experiences. The approach involves testing the quality of stereoscopic streaming media against the video recordings of real-world experiences. The study aims to better understand how different factors such as headphones, Intserv networks, and standards can impact the spatial presence of ODV. Furthermore, the proposed method may have far-reaching applications in fields such as quality assessment and virtual reality.

This paper presents the design and implementation of a real-time face tracking humanoid robot. The robot's neck was developed to enable it to track human faces in real-time, employing feature extraction and classification algorithms. The robot kinematics were also considered in the design process to ensure smooth and natural movements. The developed system is capable of detecting and tracking faces in real-time and can adjust its head and neck movements based on the detected facial features. The proposed methodology includes the use of relevant classification algorithms, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), to classify the detected features and significantly improve accuracy. The results from the evaluation of the developed system show that the proposed methodology could be useful in developing real-time face tracking humanoid robots that can interact with humans and perform tasks that require facial recognition. The study shows that the developed system can track faces while reducing the occurrence of errors and prolonged reaction times, making it a valuable tool in robotics research and development.

Binary code analysis is crucial in various software engineering tasks, such as malware detection, code refactoring, and plagiarism detection. With the rapid growth of software complexity and the increasing number of heterogeneous computing platforms, binary analysis is particularly critical and more important than ever. Traditionally adopted techniques for binary code analysis are facing multiple challenges, such as the need for cross-platform analysis, high scalability and speed, and improved fidelity, to name a few. To meet these challenges, machine learning-based binary code analysis frameworks attract substantial attention due to their automated feature extraction and drastically reduced efforts needed on large-scale programs. In this paper, we provide the taxonomy of machine learning-based binary code analysis, describe the recent advances and key findings on the topic, and discuss the key challenges and opportunities. Finally, we present our thoughts for future directions on this topic.

Cloud computing and its computing as a utility paradigm offers on-demand resources, enabling its users to seamlessly adapt applications to the current demand. With its (virtually) unlimited elasticity, managing deployed applications becomes more and more complex raising the need for automation. Such autonomous systems leverage the importance to constantly monitor and analyse the deployed workload and the underlying infrastructure serving as knowledge-base for deriving corrective actions like scaling. Existing monitoring solutions, however are not designed to cope with a frequently changing topology. We propose a monitoring and event processing framework following a model-driven approach, that allows users to express i) the monitoring demand by directly referencing entities of the deployment context, ii) aggregate the monitoring data using mathematical expressions, iii) trigger and process events based on the monitoring data and finally iv) attach scalability rules to those events. We accompany the modelling language with a monitoring orchestration and distributed complex event processing framework, capable of enacting the model in a frequently changing multi-cloud infrastructure, considering cloud-specific aspects like communication costs.

The swinging posture of floating objects plays an important role in improving the simulation degree of oceanic scenes. In this paper, we study the influence factors of swinging posture of floating objects in oceanic scenes, including the environment and its own influences. For the problem that the traditional floating model only applies to regular objects, such as boxes, we propose a floating model with multi-center force, including the confirmation of the center of the corner block, the distribution of weights, the vector synthesis of forces, and the determination of resistance problems. This model analyzes the shape of floating objects and allocates a branch center of gravity for the more prominent corner blocks, which makes the corner block contribute to the swing posture. In this way, the swing posture of irregular floating objects is more in line with reality. Through experimental comparison, a floating model based on multi-center force shows swinging posture which is more consistent with practical mechanics than the traditional single-center floating model on the irregular floating objects with more corner blocks.

In recent years, indoor navigation has become an increasingly important research area due to the growing popularity of navigation systems for pedestrians. This paper proposes an indoor pedestrian navigation algorithm based on smartphone mode recognition. The algorithm estimates the user's current location using a combination of neural networks and acceleration sensors. Additionally, switches are used to distinguish between different modes of locomotion, including walking and running. Legged locomotion is also considered in the algorithm to accurately estimate the user's position. While global positioning systems (GPS) have been a popular method for outdoor navigation, they are not as effective in indoor environments due to signal interference. Thus, this proposed algorithm shows potential for improving indoor navigation solutions. Future research could focus on further improving the accuracy and usability of the algorithm for practical applications.

Cloud computing has paved the way for efficient processing and storage of data in various fields of computer science, including vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs). In order to further enhance the performance of VANETs, proposals for the utilization of mobile brokers have been put forward. These brokers act as intermediaries between vehicles and the cloud, enabling efficient and timely access to cloud resources. Routing protocols are also being developed to enable seamless integration of mobile brokers into the VANETs. Such developments are especially crucial in urban areas where automobiles are abundant, and efficient management of data and resources is vital. Furthermore, the integration of semantics into the mobile broker architecture can further enhance the performance of the vehicular cloud system. In summary, the integration of mobile brokers and routing protocols into the vehicular cloud system can boost its efficiency and reliability, especially in urban areas, leading to the development of more sophisticated and better-performing vehicular cloud systems.

LLLCancerCare is a proposed framework for guiding the development of intelligent cancer care systems. Cancer is one of the leading causes of death around the world, and while there have been many advances in cancer care, there is still much work to be done to improve patient outcomes. The proposed framework is informed by the fields of informatics, system of systems, internet of things, big data, sustainable development, and education. By leveraging these areas of expertise, LLLCancerCare aims to create a comprehensive system that can adapt to the evolving needs of cancer patients and healthcare providers. The framework emphasizes the importance of incorporating machine learning and other intelligent technologies to improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment efficacy. It also promotes the use of big data analytics to optimize cancer care delivery and support sustainable development of healthcare systems. Finally, LLLCancerCare recognizes the importance of education and training in promoting a culture of continuous learning and innovation in cancer care. By providing a strong foundation for intelligent cancer care, this framework has the potential to transform the field and improve outcomes for patients worldwide.

As the dynamics of cyber warfare continue to change, it is very important to be aware of the issues currently confronting cyberspace. One threat which continues to grow in the danger it poses to cyber security are botnets. Botnets can launch massive Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks against internet connected hosts anonymously, undertake intricate spam campaigns, launch mass financial fraud campaigns, and even manipulate public opinion via social media bots. The network topology and technology undergirding each botnet varies greatly, as do the motivations commonly behind such networks. Furthermore, as botnets have continued to evolve, many newer ones demonstrate increased levels of anonymity and sophistication, making it more difficult to effectively counter them. Increases in the production of vulnerable Internet of Things (IoT) devices has made it easier for malicious actors to quickly assemble sizable botnets. Because of this, the steps necessary to stop botnets also vary, and in some cases, it may be extremely difficult to effectively defeat a fully functional and sophisticated botnet. While in some cases, the infrastructure supporting the botnet can be targeted and remotely disabled, other cases require the physical assistance of law enforcement to shut down the botnet. In the latter case, it is often a significant challenge to cheaply end a botnet. On the other hand, there are many steps and mitigations that can be taken by end-users to prevent their own devices from becoming part of a botnet. Many of these solutions involve implementing basic cybersecurity practices like installing firewalls and changing default passwords. More sophisticated botnets may require similarly sophisticated intrusion detection systems, to detect and remove malicious infections. Much research has gone into such systems and in recent years many researchers have begun to implement machine learning techniques to defeat botnets. This paper is intended present a review on botnet evolution, trends and mitigations, and offer related examples and research to provide the reader with quick access to a broad understanding of the issues at hand.

This paper proposes an improved low-bitrate High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) technique by utilizing deep learning based super-resolution and adaptive block patching. The method aims to enhance the video quality by optimizing the motion estimation, reducing the bit rate, improving the image reconstruction, and achieving superresolution. The proposed technique applies a deep learning model to predict high-resolution frames which are then used to improve the quality of the reconstructed frames. Additionally, the adaptive block patching technique is employed to enhance the accuracy of the motion estimation and the encoding efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art HEVC algorithms in terms of visual quality, bit rate reduction, and compression efficiency.

This paper aims to explore the implementation of artificial intelligence in the operational support system and business support system context. The integration of AI into these systems is expected to enhance their functionality and efficiency through advanced computer architecture and loss measurement capabilities. The paper investigates the potential use cases of AI in these systems, specifically in the areas of business operations and logic gate support. This is based on an analysis of current developments and trends in AI research, as well as discussions at relevant conferences. The findings suggest that AI can be successfully applied in a range of operational and business support scenarios, providing benefits such as improved decision-making and system optimization. Overall, this paper highlights the importance and potential of incorporating artificial intelligence into operational and business support systems architecture.

This paper proposes an asynchronous and distributed tracking approach for time-varying fixed points. The main focus is on achieving convergence through iterative methods, taking into account the challenges posed by approximation algorithms and noise measurement. The proposed approach relies on information exchange between nodes in the network, with each node utilizing local indexes to optimize its tracking task. The efficacy of the proposed approach is evaluated through simulations, which show promising results in terms of both tracking accuracy and convergence speed. Overall, this work presents a practical and effective solution for the challenging problem of tracking time-varying fixed points in distributed systems.

This paper discusses recent improvements in the software tool Feko, specifically with regards to its capabilities in finite element analysis (FEA) for various applications including antennas, dielectrics, automotive components, cable shielding, power cables, and computational modeling. Feko is a powerful and versatile FEA tool that has seen significant upgrades in recent years, particularly with regards to its ability to accurately model electromagnetic phenomena. The improved performance of Feko in antenna simulation and analysis is particularly noteworthy, as it allows for detailed analysis of both simple and complex antenna designs. Additionally, Feko’s ability to model the behavior of dielectrics and cable shielding is key for the design and optimization of high-performance electronic systems, particularly those used in the automotive industry. The paper also highlights the use of Feko in computational modeling, which can be used to simulate complex systems and predict their behavior under a variety of conditions, allowing for more accurate and informed design decisions. Overall, the recent improvements in Feko have greatly enhanced its capabilities for a wide range of FEA applications, making it an invaluable tool in the field of electromagnetic design and analysis.

Use of mobile health (mHealth) systems has increased with the advancement and proliferation of mobile computing and related technologies. It has improved efficiency and effectiveness of healthcare services. Non-invasive pain level detection from facial images is one of the promising mHealth applications. Effective pain treatment requires regular and continuous pain assessment. Most of the pain research tools are study or disease specific while some are pain (lumbar pain, cancer pain, etc.) and patient group specific (neonatal, adult, woman, etc.). This results in recurrent but potentially avoidable costs such as time, money, and workforce to develop similar services or software research tools for each research study. In this study, we have proposed, designed, and implemented a customizable personalized pain study platform that offers real-time data collection, research participant management, role-based access control, research data anonymization etc. It is also used to investigate pain level detection accuracy using evidence-based continuous learning from the facial expression data, collected from Bangladesh, Nepal and USA, which yielded about 71% classification accuracy.

The visual data, which are acquired from the ubiquitous visual sensors deployed in metropolitans, are of great value and paramount significance to enhance the effectiveness and pursue the future development of smart cities. In this paper, the essential building blocks of the unified visual data management and analysis infrastructure that serve as the foundation for the economical visual system in the city brain, are introduced to facilitate the utilization of the visual signal in the artificial intelligence era. In particular, we start by the discussion of the front-end smart visual sensing in the context of economical communication and service with the heterogeneous network, and the functionalities and necessities of compact visual feature and deep learning model representations are detailed. Subsequently, the utilities of the infrastructure are demonstrated through two intelligent applications at the back-end, including vehicle re-identification and person re-identification. The standardizations regarding compact feature and deep neural network representations, which are regarded as the key ingredients in this infrastructure and greatly facilitate the construction of the visual system in the city brain, are also discussed. Finally, we envision how the potential issues regarding the economical visual communications for future smart cities might be pragmatically approached within this unified infrastructure.

This paper focuses on consensus-based distributed optimization in multi-agent systems with a particular emphasis on convergence and differential privacy. The convergence study explores the convergence properties of the algorithms and identifies the necessary conditions under which convergence can be reached. Meanwhile, differential privacy is incorporated into the framework to address privacy issues that arise in the optimization process. The concept of cost function is introduced to quantify the privacy cost of the optimization algorithm, and the privacy preservation is optimized with respect to this cost function. Additionally, the use of radio frequency in multi-agent systems is discussed as a potential approach to improve the overall performance of the algorithm. Overall, this paper presents a comprehensive analysis of consensus-based distributed optimization in multi-agent systems, taking into account both the convergence and privacy aspects of the problem.

In recent years, the concept of "Smart Cities" has emerged and gained significant attention from all stakeholders, including governments, businesses, and citizens. The development of Smart Cities relies heavily on emerging technologies, such as Big Data, Cloud computing, and data centers. These technologies create opportunities for governments to collect, store, process, and analyze large sets of data, allowing for a better understanding of city operations. In this context, the paper offers an analysis of the development path of Smart Cities in the era of Big Data, discussing the crucial role of government in fostering the creation of Smart Cities. The paper examines the challenges and opportunities that arise when implementing Smart City initiatives using Big Data and highlights how Cloud computing and data centers can significantly support the development of such projects. The paper concludes by providing recommendations on how governments can best implement Smart City projects using these technologies, taking an integrated approach to their implementation to ensure their effectiveness and ultimate success.

In this paper, a novel approach is proposed for the segmentation of overlapping cytoplasm in cervical smear images. The approach utilizes adaptive shape priors extracted from contour fragments to accurately segment the cytoplasmic regions. The use of shape priors enhances the segmentation process while minimizing errors caused by overlapping regions. The proposed approach combines the use of shape priors with level set methods to achieve greater precision and accuracy in the segmentation process. The results of the task analysis indicate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional image segmentation methods. Feature extraction is also used to further enhance the accuracy of the segmentation process. The proposed approach is particularly relevant in the context of cervical cancer, where accurate segmentation of cytoplasmic regions is critical for proper diagnosis and treatment. Overall, this paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation with potential for significant impact in the field of medical image analysis.

Visible Light Communication (VLC) is a complementary solution for fifth generation (5G) heterogeneous mobile networks with the advantages such as high speed transmission and no frequency regulation. This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates an indoor hybrid system that integrates VLC and WiFi to exploit the advantages of both networks. Downlink VLC channels are proposed to supplement an existing RF channel to mitigate the data traffic bottlenecks in high density environments. The design of joint resource management algorithm is described for the optical wireless network to dynamically allocate network resources to users. Experiments show the system works well with the goal to avoid service disconnections.

This paper investigates the worst-case cause-effect reaction latency in systems with non-blocking communication. The authors perform a task analysis and develop protocols for real-time systems that incorporate both semantics and estimation techniques. They examine the impact of communication delays on system performance and utilize harmonic analysis to study potential sources of delay. The findings of this study highlight the importance of careful consideration of communication protocols and delay estimation in the design of real-time systems. It is concluded that effective communication protocols, accurate delay estimation techniques, and careful system design planning are essential for ensuring optimal system performance in non-blocking communication systems.

This paper discusses various techniques to improve color segmentation in the task of identifying objects on aerial images. Image color analysis and image segmentation are employed to extract different regions of interest. Object recognition is then performed by merging these regions and analyzing their shape, texture, and other features. In addition, image edge detection and feature extraction are used to improve the accuracy of object identification. The proposed techniques aim to increase the efficiency and accuracy of object recognition on aerial images, which have wide-ranging applications in fields such as agriculture, urban planning, and monitoring natural disasters.

In this paper, an optimum broadband Conformal Strongly Magnetic Resonance (CSCMR) is designed which provides simultaneously high efficient power transfer and high data-rate communication through the same link. This wireless power transfer system is able to achieve 20 MHz bandwidth at the operating frequency of 115 MHz maintaining over 80% power transfer efficiency. The integrated planar broadband strongly coupled magnetic resonant system is able to deliver 30% of the given power to a 50 Ω load. Utilizing the large bandwidth, a high data rate digital communication through the same link is achieved, using backscattering modulation. The data transfer is accomplished with 6 Mbps data-rate and 30% overall system efficiency.

In the field of network traffic classification, accurate identification of traffic types is of great concern to network administrators and researchers. In recent years, graph convolutional neural network (GCN) has emerged as a powerful tool for traffic classification due to its ability to extract features from graph data. In this paper, we propose a novel traffic classification framework called GCN-TC, which combines trace graph with statistical features to improve the accuracy of traffic classification. Specifically, we use the trace graph to represent the network traffic and extract graph features, while statistical features are extracted from the payloads. To classify the traffic types, we adopt both classification and machine learning algorithms based on sparse matrices and convolution. The performance evaluation results demonstrate that our proposed GCN-TC outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on a real-world dataset of peer-to-peer computing and telecommunication traffic.

The edge detection is yet a critical problem in many computer vision and image processing tasks. The manuscript presents an Holistically-Nested Edge Detection based approach to study the inclusion of Near-Infrared in the Visible spectrum images. To do so, a Single Sensor based dataset has been acquired in the range of 400nm to 1100nm wavelength spectral band. Prominent results have been obtained even when the ground truth (annotated edge-map) is based in the visible wavelength spectrum.

This paper proposes a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC)-based VANET Data Offloading technique that uses a staying-time-oriented k-hop away offloading agent. Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) are a type of wireless network that enable communication between vehicles and infrastructure. With the increasing number of connected vehicles, the amount of data generated by VANETs is also growing rapidly. This data can be offloaded using servers located in the Long Term Evolution (LTE) cellular networks or the Internet. However, the traditional offloading methods may not be efficient enough to handle the large volume of data generated by VANETs. This is where the staying-time-oriented k-hop away offloading agent comes into play, which can select the optimal offloading path based on the staying time of the vehicles in the area and the number of hops between the source and destination. This technique is based on edge computing, as it utilizes the vehicle-to-infrastructure communication and offloading capabilities of the MEC environment. The proposed technique can significantly reduce the data traffic on LTE cellular networks and the Internet, and improve the overall performance of VANETs.

There are different types of arc may occur depending on the arcing conditions and involved surfaces. The severity of the arc is determined by the involved arcing surface and the arcing current flowing path. In this study, arc in Sphere-Gap and Rod-Gap surfaces is considered for the time-frequency domain analysis. The voltage characteristics for both the arc events are recorded in different voltage levels and gap length. A Stockwell Transform (ST) based approach is applied on the arc signals for the harmonic decomposition. Further, K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) machine learning algorithm is applied on the ST coefficients for the classification of real-time arc signals of different arcing conditions. The results obtained using ST and KNN algorithm successfully classifies different arc faults due to rod-gap and sphere-gap by their harmonic signature.

The integration of blockchain technology into the Internet of Things (IoT) has opened up new opportunities for secure and efficient data exchange in various domains. This paper presents Hybrid-IoT, a hybrid blockchain architecture for IoT systems that leverages both Proof-of-Work (PoW) sub-blockchains and traditional blockchain structures. By utilizing a hybrid approach, Hybrid-IoT enhances security and enables faster transaction processing. The architecture also employs peer-to-peer computing protocols to ensure seamless communication between IoT devices. Moreover, the paper evaluates the performance of Hybrid-IoT and highlights its advantages over existing blockchain-based IoT solutions. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach improves transaction throughput, reduces network latency, and enhances overall system performance. Overall, Hybrid-IoT provides a promising solution for enhancing the security and efficiency of IoT systems through blockchain technology.

The aim of this study is to assess the performance of a hardware-implemented machine learning technique under neutron irradiation. The technique relies on support vector machines as the machine learning algorithm and field programmable gate arrays for circuit implementation. The authors describe the training process for the support vector machine and the methodology for assessing its performance. Circuit faults are introduced to the system to simulate the effects of neutron irradiation and transient analysis is carried out to identify the faults. A mathematical model is also developed to analyze the system's behavior. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the hardware-implemented machine learning technique under neutron irradiation, providing valuable insight for the development of reliable machine learning systems in harsh environments like those encountered in space exploration.

Cheating and abnormal activities like- whispering, impersonation or hand contact are widely involved in offline examination around the globe, this hinders the integrity and morality of fair conduction of examination. Video Surveillance systems embeds image and video processing algorithms to monitor, analyse and process various activities and even detection of crime, suspicious activities. The purpose of this research is to design a robust video surveillance system model to monitor and analyse activities during examination, this will allow the academic institutes to detect and identity unfair or suspicious activities during examination. This system model will use automated video as feed to monitor students activities during examination in real-time. We have discussed about various video analytics or video processing and image processing methods and tools involved in surveillance model. We throughout the paper have walk through about the various processes- pre-processing, segmentation, classification, feature extraction and its related video processing algorithm in sequential manner. The proposed model is effective, efficient and requires relatively less processing power.

This paper presents the use of a neural network for the development of a process system "Torque Controller - Synchronous Motor". The focus of the study is on the application of the neural network in controlling the torque output of synchronous motors. A mathematical model was developed for the system and implemented into a biological neural network. The network was then trained using data from a physical synchronous motor to optimize the control of torque output. Results of the study show that the use of a neural network can significantly improve the control of torque in synchronous motors, leading to more efficient operation of the motor. The study concludes that the application of neural networks in process control can have significant benefits in industrial applications where precise and efficient control is critical. Future work could focus on the implementation of the system in an industrial setting with actual synchronous motors.

Estimation errors caused by perspective distortions are a long-standing problem in the domain of crowd counting. In this paper, we propose a novel loss function to allow filters in convolutional neural networks to learn features that are adaptive to the scale and perspective variation of individuals in crowd images. By exploring the crowd count error from regions close to the vanishing point of a perspective distorted image, we are able to penalize under-estimations. This is useful to train a network that is robust against perspective distortion for accurate density estimation. The proposed method is scene-independent and can be applied effectively to crowd scene with a variety of physical layout. Extensive comparative evaluations demonstrate that our proposed method achieves significant improvement over the state-of-the-art approaches on the challenging ShanghaiTech and UCF-QNRF datasets.

This paper proposes a self-organization smart protocol for mobile wireless sensor networks (WSNs) that incorporate drones for efficient data collection. Wireless sensor networks have gained importance due to their ability to collect and transmit data wirelessly, however, there is always a concern on how to efficiently manage the data collected by these networks. This protocol integrates drones as mobile base stations that collect data from the sensors and transfer it to data collection centers, thus improving network efficiency. The proposed protocol allows for the drones to self-organize and dynamically select the most suitable base station to route data, based on the location and the data being transmitted. This self-organization of the protocol enables more efficient network management and reduces packet loss. The results of this research indicate that the self-organization smart protocol for mobile wireless sensor networks improves the network's efficiency and reliability, which is essential for their reliable deployment in real-world scenarios.

Mass spectrometry is a powerful analytical technique used in various fields, including chemistry and biology. However, the complexity of mass spectral data poses a challenge in detecting and identifying substances accurately. To address this challenge, long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, which are a type of biological neural network, have been applied to mass spectral substance detections. LSTMs are particularly suitable for time series analysis, allowing the networks to extract relevant features from the mass spectral data and detect anomalies. This paper reviews the use of LSTMs in mass spectral substance detections and discusses their potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of mass spectrometry. The study highlights the importance of feature extraction and anomaly detection in mass spectral data analysis and demonstrates the effectiveness of LSTMs in ion identification and quantification. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in mass spectral substance detections using LSTMs, and highlights future research directions in this field.

The Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) is a well-known challenge in optimization. In recent years, Genetic Algorithms (GAs) have been used to find optimal solutions to this problem. This paper proposes the use of biological cell mechanisms to enhance the performance of Genetic Algorithms in solving the TSP. The biological cell mechanisms utilized in this paper include cellular division, mutation, differentiation, and death. These mechanisms are integrated in the GA to improve the optimization process. The GA with the biological cell mechanisms is applied to TSP in urban areas. The results show that the proposed method yields better results than the traditional Genetic Algorithm. This study contributes to the fields of genetics, optimization, sociology, and statistics. The proposed method can be applied to other optimization problems to improve the efficiency of Genetic Algorithms.

Online anonymity is considered as one of the great gifts of the Internet, but it also brings dangers to society, such as cybercrime, online sexual abuse and bullying, and love scams. Many people are fond of chatting online to make new friends, but how can they be sure that the person sitting behind the other computer is really the person they claim to be? By studying stylometry and keystroke dynamics features from chat data, it is feasible to reveal the actual gender of an online user. In this paper, we examined stylometry and keystroke dynamics features from chat data, and proposed a Random Forest based gender prediction approach by analyzing these features. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a data acquisition was conducted to capture the keystroke dynamics and text information when participants were chatting remotely via Skype. All participants were invited to chat freely on any topic they prefered in order to get to know each other. Based on our experimental result, the proposed approach achieved 72% prediction accuracy by analyzing on this free-text data captured only in 15 minutes.

This paper proposes an approach to integral quality control of service profile of traffic, focusing on "Time measurement," "Communication networks," "Ethernet," "Bandwidth," "Quality of service," "Monitoring," and "Communication channels." The research aims to optimize the quality of service (QoS) in communication networks, specifically through the active monitoring of communication channels to analyze the traffic conditions and provide real-time feedback to the QoS management system. By analyzing the bandwidth usage, time measurement, and other key factors of the traffic, the proposed method provides a comprehensive approach to QoS management. Additionally, by leveraging the capabilities of Ethernet technology, the research presents a framework for efficient and effective QoS monitoring and control. The proposed approach represents a significant step forward in the field of QoS control for communication networks, and has the potential to significantly improve the overall performance of these networks in terms of reliability, efficiency, and effectiveness.

Symbolic regression aims to find mathematical expressions of functions that can fit a finite set of given data. This problem is a typical problem for evaluating performance in the field of Genetic Programming (GP). Cartesian GP (CGP) is one of the extensions of GP, which generating the graph structure programs. By using the graph structure, the solutions can be represented by more compact programs. Therefore, CGP is widely applied to the various problems. In standard symbolic regression problem, the sample data is expressed by a simple function, which is continuous and smooth. On the other hand, In a complex system appearing in the real world, they can be produced by a discontinuous or non-smooth function. When conventional GP or CGP is applied to this complex system's modelling, it is difficult to obtain good performance. In this paper, we propose a new CGP framework for complex symbolic regression problem. The proposed CGP modularizes the output nodes, and module mutation is introduced to increase or decrease the number of modules during the search. Each module consists of a node corresponding to the output of the network and a node for selecting the output to be used. By switching the output node for each input, it is possible to output appropriate values for each section of the objective function. We have examined its effectiveness by applying it to symbolic regression problem where the objective function is divided into several different sub-function fields. Experimental results have shown that it outperforms conventional CGP.

Due to rapid changes in the environment, vehicular communication channels no longer satisfy the assumption of wide-sense stationary uncorrelated scattering. The non-stationary fading process can be characterized by assuming local stationarity regions with finite extent in time and frequency. The local scattering function (LSF) and channel correlation function (CCF) provide a framework to characterize the mean power and correlation of the non-stationary channel scatterers, respectively. In this paper, we estimate the LSF and CCF from measurements collected in a vehicle-to-infrastructure radio channel sounding campaign in a suburban environment in Lille, France. Based on the CCF, the stationarity region is evaluated in time as 567 ms and used to capture the non-stationary fading parameters. We obtain the time-varying delay and Doppler power profiles from the LSF, and we analyze the corresponding root-mean-square delay and Doppler spreads. We show that the distribution of these parameters follows a lognormal model. Finally, application relevance in terms of channel capacity and diversity techniques is discussed. Results show that the assumption of ergodic capacity and the performance of various diversity techniques depend on the stationarity and coherence parameters of the channel. The evaluation and statistical modeling of such parameters can provide a way of tracking channel variation, hence, increasing the performance of adaptive schemes.

In order to achieve efficient management of microgrids, it is essential to develop accurate prediction systems for distributed generation. In this paper, we propose a neural network based prediction system for forecasting the production of microgrids. We conduct time series analysis on the data and utilize the complex computer architecture of neural networks to develop predictive models. By leveraging the power of microprocessors, our system is capable of providing accurate and timely predictions which can be used to optimize the management of microgrids. Our proposed system demonstrates significant improvements when compared to traditional forecasting methods, and has the potential to greatly enhance the performance of microgrids.

The growth and increasing complexity of modern communication systems have made the design and management of network control critical. Optical fiber networks are becoming increasingly popular as they offer more bandwidth and are less susceptible to signal interference than traditional copper networks. Optical switches and amplifiers are integral components of these networks, and their effective management is vital to maintaining high levels of network performance. In recent years, protocols based on stimulated emission have been developed to increase the efficiency of these networks. Additionally, adaptive optics and other optical devices are being developed to improve the accuracy of optical signal transmission over longer distances. This paper reviews the current state of network control and management for optical fiber networks, highlighting the role of optical switches, amplifiers, and devices, and discusses the latest research trends in the field.

The solution of electromagnetic (EM) inverse scattering problems is hindered by challenges, such as ill-posedness, nonlinearity, and high computational costs. Recently, deep learning was shown to be a promising tool in addressing these challenges. In particular, it is possible to establish a connection between a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) and iterative solution methods of EM inverse scattering. This led to the development of an efficient CNN-based solution to EM inverse problems, termed DeepNIS. It has been shown that DeepNIS can outperform conventional inverse scattering solution methods in terms of both the image quality and computational time. In this letter, we evaluate the DeepNIS performance as a function of the number of layers using structure similarity index measure and mean square error metrics. In addition, we probe the dynamic evolution behavior of DeepNIS by examining its near-isometry property and show that, after a proper training stage, the proposed CNN has near-optimal stability properties.

In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly popular as a platform for wireless communication, especially in areas where there is no existing infrastructure. One of the major challenges in UAV-based wireless communication is to find the optimal placement of base stations to ensure maximum coverage and quality of service (QoS) for different types of users. In this study, we propose a 3D placement of UAV base station using multi-population genetic algorithm for maximizing users with different QoS requirements. The genetic algorithm is used to search for the optimal combination of base station locations and transmit powers to achieve the desired QoS for each user while minimizing interference and power consumption. The proposed approach is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing placement algorithms. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of users with different QoS requirements and higher network throughput. This study provides a promising approach in addressing the placement problem of UAV base stations for wireless communication.

Human pose estimation has received significant attention recently due to its various applications in the real world. As the performance of the state-of-the-art human pose estimation methods can be improved by deep learning, this paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep learning based human pose estimation methods and analyzes the methodologies employed. We summarize and discuss recent works with a methodology-based taxonomy. Single-person and multi-person pipelines are first reviewed separately. Then, the deep learning techniques applied in these pipelines are compared and analyzed. The datasets and metrics used in this task are also discussed and compared. The aim of this survey is to make every step in the estimation pipelines interpretable and to provide readers a readily comprehensible explanation. Moreover, the unsolved problems and challenges for future research are discussed.

This paper delves into the field of deep learning for domain adaptation, with a focus on exploiting semantics as a tool in adversarial training. It discusses techniques for using semantics to aid in image-level domain adaptation, particularly in the context of image segmentation tasks. The authors analyze the effectiveness of these techniques, which make use of generators and task analysis, in improving domain adaptation accuracy. This work has important implications for the use of deep learning in practical applications, particularly in the semiconductor industry, where the authors have demonstrated the efficacy of their approach using gallium nitride data. Ultimately, this paper provides valuable insights into how semantics can be leveraged to enhance adversarial training for successful image-level domain adaptation.

The uncontrollable weather conditions can cause a serious problem to remote sensing imaginary. One of the weather conditions is a resulting from cloud contamination. As a result, this paper proposed the use of the convolutional autoencoder neural networks to remove clouds from cloud-contaminated images by training on a multi-temporal remote sensing dataset. Here, the observations from different spectral bands are assumed to be independent since their spectral responses are usually nonoverlapped. From this assumption, each convolutional autoencoder neural networks are trained with the observation from only one spectral band. In our method, we have three convolutional autoencoder neural networks for red, green and blue spectral bands. The experiments were conducted on both synthesis and real dataset derived from the actual LANDSAT 8 images from the central part of Thailand where our algorithm has shown to have a superb performance.

Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) segmentation has been a glaring medical imaging issue for the past decades. The existing convolutional networks used for CMR segmentation lack adequate communication between semantic and spatial information. In this paper, we propose an aggregated parallel cross-scale pyramid network (APCP-Net) for CMR segmentation, which adopts parallel cross-scale spatial pyramid to enhance the ability of multi-scale feature fusion. To alleviate the computational complexity of the network without losing performance and increasing time consumption, we present a convolution decomposition strategy which decomposes a regular convolutional layer into several lightweight ones. Furthermore, deep aggregation is used among parallel spatial pyramids to promote the representation ability of our APCP-Net. We evaluate our APCP-Net on the segmentation dataset of ACDC 2017 Challenge. Experimental results demonstrate that our APCP-Net is comparable to the state-of-the-art methods in the case where the parameter amount is 54 times less than the existing methods.

We consider the large graphs as the object of study and deal with the problem of escape probability estimation. Generally, the required characteristic cannot be calculated analytically and even numerically due to the complexity and large size of the investigation object. The purpose of this paper is to offer the effective method for estimating the probability that the random walk on graph first enters a node b before returning into starting node a. Regenerative properties of the random walk allow using an accelerated method for the cycles simulation based on the splitting technique. The results of numerical experiments confirm the advantages of the proposed method.

Social media is extensively used nowadays and is gaining popularity among the users with the increasing growth in the network capacity, connectivity, and speed. Moreover, affordable prices of data plans, especially mobile data packages, have considerably increased the use of multimedia by different users. This includes terrorists who use social media platforms to promote their ideology and intimidate their adversaries. It is therefore very important to develop automated solutions to semantically analyse given multimedia contents to assist law enforcement agencies in the preventive policing of online activities. A major challenge for the social media forensic analysis is to preserve the privacy of citizens who use online social networking platforms. This paper presents results of European H2020 project RED-Alert that aims to enable secure and privacy preserving data processing; hence the malicious content and the corresponding personality can be tracked while the privacy of innocent citizens can be preserved. We have mined seven social media channels for content and providing support for ten languages for analysis. Our proposed solution is designed to ensure security and policing of online contents by detecting terrorist material. We have used speech recognition, face and object detection besides audio event detection to extract information from multimedia files. We have applied anonymization techniques to ensure the privacy of citizens using social media. We have discussed the challenges and prospects of this work especially the need of using digital forensic techniques while respecting European and national data protection laws notably GDPR.

Network motifs bring a great interest to many fields, because they are a perfect candidate to speed up the applied research in the understanding of complex networks dynamics. One of the biggest problems raised in the process of finding these motifs is the performance. Starting from splitting the initial network into subgraphs to the subgraphs clusterization, each algorithm used addresses an NP problem. Hence there are many algorithms that are trying to solve network motifs discovery, however there is no perfect approach talking from a time performance perspective, but only solutions that are faster than others. This paper presents a redesign of one of the most competitive algorithms for subgraphs enumeration found in the literature called ESU. In the proposed approach a given network can be processed by using parallel programming, either with a process-driven model, or a hybrid one (process-driven and thread-driven). Finally, the existing and proposed models are compared using benchmark graphs, revealing competitive results.

This paper proposes a method for calibrating dynamic hand-wrist EMG-force models using a minimum number of electrodes. The study focuses on the use of electrodes in electromyography, which measures the electrical activity of muscles. The goal is to create accurate models for biological systems, specifically the wrist, that can be trained with limited resources. The key aspect of the proposed method is the use of filtering techniques to improve the accuracy of the models without using a large number of electrodes for calibration. By reducing the number of electrodes required for calibration, this method can make dynamic hand-wrist EMG-force models more accessible, practical, and cost-effective in various applications.

Early detection and prediction of cardiac anomalies play an important role in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. In medicine, electrocardiography provides valuable information for the doctors since they can accurately determine what is happening concerning the heart activities. Nevertheless, electrocardiography classification is a non-trivial challenge due to the specialties of these data as well as the reliability of manual data collection methods. With the recent advancement of the IoT technologies, some wearable IoT devices for electrocardiography monitoring have been developed. However, the data collected from those devices, though possibly automatic, pose more challenging issues for the problem of electrocardiography classification. In this paper, we propose a novel solution for electrocardiography signal classification based on Deep Learning by combining Auto Encoder and Long-Short Term Memory models to handle data collected from intelligent IoT devices Shimmer and VitalSigns Holter.

Saliency detection plays an important role in computer vision systems, allowing for the identification of important or relevant information within an image. This paper proposes a new approach for saliency detection using global and local information under multilayer cellular automata. The proposed method employs feature extraction and encoding techniques, allowing for the identification of important visual features and their association with specific semantic contexts. By incorporating nonhomogeneous media and convolutional codes, the proposed method achieves improved accuracy and efficiency in saliency detection tasks. The results of experiments conducted on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison to existing techniques. The proposed approach has the potential to enhance various applications, such as object recognition and visual tracking systems.

This paper proposes a solution for improving the effectiveness of higher order mutation testing in software testing. The approach is focused on syntactic analysis of computer languages, and the use of classification algorithms and genetic algorithms for sorting and selecting the most appropriate test cases. The study highlights the need for higher order mutation testing in software development as traditional testing methods may miss critical errors. The proposed method aims to address the limitations of other mutation testing techniques to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of software testing. The results of the study demonstrate that the proposed approach provides better solutions by identifying critical test cases that traditional testing methods may miss. The approach is flexible and adaptable to different software development scenarios and can be easily integrated into existing software testing processes. Overall, this paper provides important insights and practical solutions for improving the effectiveness of higher order mutation testing in software testing.

This paper focuses on time scheduling for Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) connection events, specifically the central BLE. The efficient scheduling of connection events is crucial for effective communication in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT). The paper discusses various scheduling strategies and proposes a new scheduling method that takes into account the timing of advertising and the processor scheduling. The proposed method is based on the BLE standards and is designed to optimize the scheduling of connection events while minimizing power consumption. The authors note that efficient scheduling of central BLE connection events will contribute to the overall effectiveness of the IoT, making it more responsive and reliable.

To provide reliability of flash memory, error-correcting codes are usually used which can be further enhanced by moving on from hard-decision to soft-decision decoders. This requires multiple readings to obtain a reliability measure of the stored data, which is complicated by the fact that a posteriori probability distributions change as the memory ages through retention and wear-out. The existing methods for reading a flash memory either assume knowledge of these distributions or require a large number of readings for accurate estimation. In this letter, we propose a low-complexity algorithm that tracks the soft-decision boundaries and estimates the corresponding log-likelihood ratios (LLRs). It does not require any additional readings and only involves simple calculations using already available variables. The efficacy is verified through the simulations and is shown to provide near-optimal performance.

This article describes the Versatile Tensor Accelerator (VTA), a programmable DL architecture designed to be extensible in the face of evolving workloads. VTA achieves “flexible specialization” via a parameterizable architecture, two-level Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), and a Just in Time (JIT) compiler.

This paper introduces CUDA au Coq, a novel framework for machine-validating GPU assembly programs. GPUs, also known as graphics processing units, have become increasingly important in various fields due to their high computational power. However, verifying the correctness of GPU programs can be challenging because of their complex instruction sets and the large number of registers used. The CUDA au Coq framework provides a formal semantics for GPU assembly instructions, which enables the computer-aided verification of GPU programs. The framework is based on the Coq proof assistant and provides a computational model of the GPU architecture. It also includes prototypes for verifying several GPU programs, demonstrating the effectiveness of CUDA au Coq in practical settings. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for ensuring the correctness of GPU programs, which is important for the reliable and efficient use of GPUs in various applications.

With the increasing popularity of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs), safety concerns have become a major issue of concern. In order to ensure the safety of vehicles and their drivers, it is essential to develop effective Misbehavior Detection (MD) systems. In this study, we propose a novel approach to MD by integrating plausibility checks with machine learning algorithms. Specifically, we focus on the use of Support Vector Machines (SVM) for feature extraction and classification of misbehavior in VANETs. Our approach has shown promising results in detecting various types of malicious activities, including intrusion and safety violations. Overall, the proposed method represents a significant advancement in the field of MD for VANETs and has the potential to enhance the safety and security of vehicular networks.

Cloud computing has become an integral part of many companies today who seek to take advantage of the flexibility, scalability and low costs that it affords. However, with the use of cloud computing comes the challenge of secure data storage, transmission and access control. Encryption is an important tool for securing data but traditional encryption methods do not allow for fine-grained control over who has access to specific data. This is where Attribute-Based Encryption (ABE) comes in. In this paper, we propose an Updatable Ciphertext-Policy ABE scheme with traceability and revocability in order to provide a more fine-grained access control mechanism for cloud computing. Our scheme enables the production of ciphertexts that can be updated over time to include additional attributes. This makes it suitable for scenarios where complex and evolving user access control policies are required. Additionally, our scheme also includes traceability and revocability features, which make it possible for cloud providers to track and revoke access to data in case of unauthorized access or misuse. Overall, our proposed scheme offers a comprehensive solution to the challenges of secure data storage, transmission and access control in cloud computing.

This paper handles the problems of identification and equalization. To recognize the impulse response for frequency radio, we focus on positive kernel algorithm and we proceed to the equalization MC-CDMA systems. In this paper, we employ a broadband radio access network channels (BRAN A and BRAN E) standardized by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) and Proakis channels (channels A, B and C). Through theoretical analysis and the experimental simulation, it shows the appropriateness of the kernel algorithm using different SNR. To indicate the robustness of the algorithm, we have done a comparison with the RLS method. In the equalization part, we used the Zero Forcing algorithm (ZF) and Minimum Mean Square Error Algorithm (MMSE). Simulations results show that the proposed algorithm is efficient and effective for practical channels.

The present work proposes the use of a nonlinear inversion technique for the extraction of the directional ocean wave spectrum from bistatic High-Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR) Doppler data. The extraction method is combined with empirical expressions, solely based on the Doppler data, to retrieve wind speed and direction. Once the initialization parameters have been defined using these empirical expressions, a blind iterative algorithm based on Tikhonov regularization in Hilbert Scales is used to extract the nondirectional spectrum. The extracted spectrum is then used to determine the directional factor, which is assumed to be described by a cosine-power model. The proposed method yields good results with synthetic noise-contaminated HFSWR data with a priori regularization parameters.

In uncertain environments, it is crucial to accurately estimate risks to ensure safe and efficient operation of systems, such as robots. The Moment-Sum-of-Squares (MSS) approach is a powerful tool for risk estimation that utilizes probability distributions and Chebyshev approximation to efficiently compute risk metrics. This approach leverages optimization techniques and probabilistic logic to estimate risk with speed and accuracy. By utilizing MSS, risk estimation in uncertain environments can be streamlined and optimized. This paper discusses the advantages of using the MSS approach for risk estimation, and highlights its potential applications in fields such as robotics, where quick and accurate risk assessment is critical for ensuring the operational safety of robots.

In recent years, mobile devices and their connectivity have been growing exponentially, which has led to an increase in the demand for the mobile data services. To meet this ever-increasing demand, the Mobile D2D Cellular Network has emerged as a new paradigm for mobile communication. The Residual Energy-Aware Caching technique is one of the efficient ways to manage the enormous amount of data and reduce the network latency. The integration of Cloud Computing has proven to be beneficial in improving the storage, processing, and data management efficiencies of Mobile D2D Cellular Network. Service robots are becoming an attractive option for many industries, and their use in Mobile D2D Cellular Network can be very promising for efficient data management. Robot Sensing Systems are being developed to enhance the capabilities of Service Robots, and they can also be utilized in the Mobile D2D Cellular Network for better data collection. With the increasing need for efficient and secure data transfer, Protocols and Logic Gates play a vital role in protecting the information and ensuring seamless communication. The advancements in Computer Architecture have also contributed to the development of newer technologies and techniques for improving the Mobile D2D Cellular Network.

In this paper, we propose a sequential training-based receiver for On-OFF-keying diffusion-based molecular communications. The receiver is designed based on Monte Carlo methods and biological neural networks. By training the receiver, we aim to improve the throughput of the system. The proposed receiver is based on a mathematical model of a biological system and is designed to mimic biological neural networks. The receiver is trained using an iterative process to improve the accuracy of the received signals. Our simulation results show that the proposed receiver can significantly improve the throughput of the system. Overall, our approach provides a promising way of using biological system modeling to design efficient receivers for diffusion-based molecular communications.

This paper proposes a method for speech emotion classification using attention-based LSTM (long short-term memory) model. The system comprises several key components including speech recognition, emotion recognition, feature extraction, and harmonic analysis. The proposed model is based on a combination of the LSTM and attention mechanisms, which allows for more effective processing of speech signals and improved accuracy in extracting emotional features.
