Additionally, the system utilizes logic gates to classify emotional states into discrete categories. The proposed method has been tested on a dataset of speech recordings from various speakers, and the results show the effectiveness of the proposed model in accurately recognizing emotions in speech signals. The proposed system is expected to have practical applications in a wide range of fields, including speech processing, task analysis, and automated emotional support systems.

Team sports have always required players and coaches to analyze their opponents' tendencies and attack patterns to gain a competitive advantage. In recent years, advancements in technology have allowed for the collection and analysis of large amounts of data, leading to the development of new visualization methods for attack patterns. This paper proposes an improvement in the visualization method, utilizing encoding techniques and machine learning algorithms. Specifically, dictionaries of attack patterns will be created using image color analysis and training data. The resulting visualizations will allow for quicker and more accurate analysis of attack patterns, providing valuable insights into team sports. Further research into this method may lead to improved performance and strategic decision making for teams and coaches.

Rectified linear unit (ReLU) plays an important role in today’s convolutional neural networks (CNNs). In this paper, we propose a novel activation function called Rectified Exponential Unit (REU). Inspired by two recently proposed activation functions: Exponential Linear Unit (ELU) and Swish, the REU is designed by introducing the advantage of flexible exponent and multiplication function form. Moreover, we propose the Parametric REU (PREU) to increase the expressive power of the REU. The experiments with three classical CNN architectures, LeNet-5, Network in Network, and Residual Network (ResNet) on scale-various benchmarks including Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny ImageNet demonstrate that REU and PREU achieve improvement compared with other activation functions. Our results show that our REU has relative error improvements over ReLU of 7.74% and 6.08% on CIFAR-10 and 100 with the ResNet, the improvements of PREU is 9.24% and 9.32%. Finally, we use the different PREU variants in the Residual unit to achieve more stable results.

Live TV production, due to its distributed nature, requires broadcasters to deploy equipments and human resources to several different places. This increases production costs. The traditional method through outside broadcasting vans is expensive. Migrating this type of application onto clouds is a promising method to reduce the cost. However, the Quality of Experience (QoE) can hardly be assured because of the cloud performance uncertainty. Auto-scaling the infrastructure based on dynamic workloads at runtime is also difficult. The feasibility of CloudsStorm framework, which is the core component of SWITCH (Software Workbench for Interactive, Time Critical and Highly self-adaptive Cloud applications) workbench, handling the lifecycle of the time critical application development and performance monitoring, infrastructure planning and provisioning, etc., is demonstrated with the aspect of live events broadcasting. It makes a significant attempt to fill the DevOps gap when migrating applications from legacy systems onto clouds. A live streaming application is demonstrated as a use case example.

Dynamic Computing in Memory (DCIM) is a promising approach to overcome the power and latency issue associated with the transfer of data between memory and processor. This paper presents the implementation of DCIM in Resistive Crossbar Arrays, which offers high density arrays with high speed and low power demand. The paper discusses the underlying principle of Resistive Crossbar Arrays and how it can be utilized for DCIM. The proposed computational model for DCIM demonstrates the significant reduction in power consumption compared to Random Access Memory. Furthermore, a detailed analysis of the power-saving potential of various DCIM logic gates has been presented. The overall results suggest that Resistive Crossbar Arrays can be an efficient solution for computing close to memory and offers an exciting opportunity for future system designs.

Computation offloading is a proven successful paradigm for enabling resource-intensive applications on the mobile devices in multi-access edge computing (MEC) network. Moreover, in view of emerging mobile collaborative application (MCA), the offloaded tasks can be duplicated when multiple users are in the same proximity. This motivates us to design novel collaborative offloading schemes. In this context, we first consider the MEC offloading scenario, where multiple mobile users offload duplicated computation tasks to the network edge servers, and share the computation results among them. Our goal is to develop the optimal fine-grained collaborative offloading strategies with data caching enhancements to minimize the overall execution delay at the mobile terminal side. Next, we extend the MEC offloading to hybrid offloading (i.e., joint MEC and Device-to-Device (D2D) offloading) with social relationship consideration, and propose a hybrid D2D multicast-based task execution framework to achieve an energy-efficient task assignment policy for mobile users. To overcome the great complexity for the deployment problems, we then formulate the offloading decision problem as a multi-label classification problem and develop the Deep Supervised Learning (DSL) method to achieve a rapid offloading decisions making, as well as minimize the computation and offloading overhead. Last but not least, we evaluate their performance through extensive numerical study, which shows the superior performance of the proposed scheme.

This paper proposes a novel algorithm named Complexity Reduced OMP for the reconstruction of sparse propagation environment. The algorithm reduces delays and complexity, overcoming the shortcomings of Matching Pursuit algorithms. Using Channel Estimation and OFDM, the algorithm can effectively estimate the propagation environment and reduce the Bit Error Rate. The proposed algorithm has been tested and analyzed, and the results show that it outperforms traditional algorithms in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This makes it a promising candidate for sparse channel estimation in communication systems. Overall, the Complexity Reduced OMP algorithm shows great potential in improving the accuracy and efficiency of estimation in wireless communication systems.

This paper aims to develop an algorithm for economic evaluation between a diesel-generator set (DGS) and a PV solar system according to Iraqi conditions and market. The criteria of economic evaluation is based on estimation of the life cycle cost (LCC) by determining of the initial cost, periodic maintenance cost, replacement cost, diesel fuel cost and the total energy yield over 25-year lifetime. A cost comparison between a conventional 125 kVA DGS (e.g. low-quality and high-quality types) and a 100kW PV solar system using the proposed algorithm. It is found that LCC (over 25-year lifetime) for the PV solar system is 44,430$ which is cheaper than the low-quality and the high-quality DGSs, which are 388,910$ and 436,380$, respectively. In order to highlight the effects of diesel fuel cost and energy yield on LCC, the percentage-profit (profit%) and percentage-loss (loss%) are demonstrated. It is concluded that over 25-year lifetime, the total profit% of the PV solar system is 112%, whilst the total loss% for both low-quality DGS and high-quality DGS are 86% and 76%, respectively.

Smart connected health is a vital Internet of Things (IoT) application proposed to improve the efficiency of healthcare systems and reduce healthcare costs. However, there are many complex security and privacy-preserving concerns in medical services. Blind batch encryption provides a solution for the tradeoff between privacy and security. We propose an efficient blind batch encryption scheme from the CDH assumption, which can be proven to be suitably secure and blind. Based on this scheme, we design a protocol for secure and privacy-preserving medical services in smart connected health. We analyze our protocol in the context of six typical attacks and implement the prototype over the Intel Edison platform. The experiments show that our protocol is efficient for resource-limited devices and “cheap” communication protocols.

The interconnection of sensors into a wireless body area network (WBAN) is critical for emerging health monitoring and medical intervention technologies. However, wireless transmission currently limits the energy efficiency and security of body networks because of its inherently low energy efficiency and vulnerability to eavesdropping. We report a method to create robust and highly efficient wireless body area networks by confining radio-frequency (2.4-2.5 GHz ISM band) electromagnetic waves on clothing that support spoof surface plasmons (SSPs). Such textile-based networks, created by patterning clothing with low-cost conductive textiles, enables high-efficiency propagation of wireless signals by guiding propagation around the curved and dynamic environment of the human body. We experimentally demonstrate more than 30 dB enhancement in signal transmission between wearable Bluetooth devices and improved signal stability during physical activity. Our results enable miniaturized and longer-lasting wireless body sensors and point to potential of clothing in molding wireless signal propagation.

The embedded and real-time systems are the main motivation for this research where the computations are critical to be reduced as much as possible. Face recognition method using eigen-faces yields good accuracy if enough eigen-faces are considered in the classification process. The more eigen-faces used, the more computation power is needed. In this paper, the main goal is to investigate the trade-off between the used number of eigen-faces and the accuracy and the needed computation power of face recognition. Three different distance measures are studied. Namely: Euclidean, block-city, and chess board distances are used. It is concluded that there is some optimum number of eigen-faces that provides the highest recognition rate and acceptable execution time. Moreover, the best number of eigen-faces highly depends on the selected distance measure.

It is common the use of the sonar technology in order acquire and posteriorly control the distance of an underwater vehicle towards an obstacle. Although this solution simplifies the problem and is effective in most cases, it might carry some disadvantages in certain underwater vehicles or conditions. In this work it is presented a system capable of controlling the altitude of an underwater vehicle using computer vision. The sensor capable of computing the distance is composed of a CCD camera and 2 green pointer lasers. Regarding the control of the vehicle, the solution used was based on the switching of two controllers, a velocity controller (based on a PI controller), and a position controller (based on a PD controller). The vehicle chosen to test the developed system was a profiler, which main task is the vertical navigation. The mathematical model was obtained and used in order to validate the controllers designed using the Simulink toolbox from Matlab. It was used a Kalman filter in order to have a better estimation of the state variables (altitude, depth, and velocity). The tests relative to the sensor developed responsible for the acquisition of the altitude showed an average relative error equal to 1 % in the range from 0 to 2.5 m. The UWsim underwater simulation environment was used in order to validate the integration of the system and its performance.

Inchworm locomotion is comprised of a simple anchor-slip gait which has inspired a wealth of mobile robots spanning rigid, soft, composite, and foldable mechanisms. Here, we expand upon that work by introducing centimeter-scale, inexpensive, simple, and soft robots capable of forward and backward motion, as well as tight turns. The robots are based on partially antagonistic fluid elastomer actuators; using a low fidelity model and experimental verification, we reason about actuator geometry. We introduce a simple two-step manufacturing process, and test actuator longevity and payload capacity. To enable stand-alone operation, we design a lightweight, low volume electro-mechanical backpack, capable of driving up to 3 actuators. We then show how differential friction can be used to enable forward and turning motion in a single actuator, and how three actuators can be combined to additionally enable backwards motion and on-axis turns. Due to the use of miniature pumps, inflation and corresponding motion is slow. However, the robot cost, durability, and ability to maneuver in confined spaces may be beneficial in applications such as duct mapping and maintenance.

This paper proposes a parameter variation insensitive method for estimating armature temperature in a surface-mounted permanent magnet servo motor (SPMSM) system. The proposed method utilizes the resistance and inductance parameters of the motor, which are characterized by a mathematical model that incorporates the harmonic analysis of the motor's current waveform. The method is able to accurately estimate the armature temperature of the motor without relying on external temperature sensors. This is particularly advantageous as temperature sensors are often unreliable and expensive. The proposed method is demonstrated through simulation and experimental results, showing that it is robust to parameter variations and can be used in practical applications without sacrificing accuracy. Overall, this method provides a promising new approach to armature temperature estimation for SPMSM servo systems.

Anti-wear property (AWP) is one of the critical characteristics that define the lubrication performance of the lubrication oil. The AWP deterioration is characterized by the wear rate variation and is often related to the operating environment. Since a low AWP can lead to system failure, proactive means to predict the remaining useful life (RUL) considering the environmental factors is an important practical relevance. This paper presents a stochastic model to determine the oil AWP deterioration in order to predict the RUL of the related system. The model assumes that the operating environment behaves as a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). A Bayesian methodology using three sources of information (online degradation information, observed degradation, and environmental data) is applied to update dynamically the RUL. In order to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed model, a case of study is presented. Furthermore, to show the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach, a comparative study is conducted with a previously developed model, which does not consider the operating environment.

This paper presents a restructured intelligent Model-Free Control (MFC) algorithm that is designed for Multi-Input-Multi-Output (MIMO) system. In the literature, MFC is designed for Single-Input-Single-Output (SISO) system, where MIMO system is controlled by decomposing it into multi-SISO systems, and then MFC controller is applied on each one of them. The complexity of implementing multi-MFC controllers can be reduced by using the proposed MIMO-MFC controller. Moreover, the ultra-local model gain matrix in the MIMO-MFC structure will be computed using Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) to ensure the system stability, while in the classical MFC technique, the controller gain is found empirically by the means of trial and error. The unmodeled system dynamics and the different uncertainties can be compensated by the MIMO-MFC where various feedback controllers are failing to cope with. A real-time comparison between the PID controller and the proposed MIMO-MFC controller will be implemented and tested on a Twin Rotor MIMO System (TRMS). The robustness of the proposed algorithm will be tested against an actuator-fault and induced-disturbance during the real-time tests to validate the claims about the control performance enhancements.

Many existing data is inconsistent due to various reasons, such as noise, missing data, or repeated errors. Previously, the CDP clustering algorithm has been shown as an effective method to detect data anomalies. Yet, single computational processor or sequential version of the CDP algorithm demands lengthy computational times and often not acceptable in practice when dealing with voluminous data. In this paper, we propose the PCDP algorithm on detecting data anomalies by parallelizing the CDP algorithm with the support of multiple machines. Through preliminary experiments, the PCDP algorithm has demonstrated its fast computation performance as well as retaining the anomaly detection accuracy for customer data of a commercial bank.

In this paper, we propose a Transferable Environment Model With Disentangled Dynamics for predictive models, adaptation models, reinforcement learning, data models, training, and decoding. Our model disentangles the dynamics of different state factors, which allows for more efficient transfer between different tasks and environments. We also introduce a method for training the model using a combination of unsupervised and supervised learning, which further improves its flexibility and adaptability. In addition, our model incorporates a decoding component that allows for a more robust representation of the state space. Our experimental results show that our proposed model outperforms existing methods in both transfer learning and reinforcement learning tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for real-world applications.

This qualitative cross-comparison study aimed to explore the feasibility and potential of emerging technologies for software-defined systems. Specifically, the study focused on six technologies, including containers, tools, open source software, cloud computing, engines, and load management. Through a comprehensive evaluation of these technologies, the study aimed to provide insights into the benefits, challenges, and trends associated with their implementation in software-defined systems. The study employed a qualitative research approach, using interviews, case studies, and expert opinions to collect data. The findings revealed that each technology offers unique advantages and limitations for software-defined systems. Containers, for example, enable more efficient application deployment and management, while tools and open source software provide developers with greater flexibility and cost-effectiveness. Cloud computing, on the other hand, offers scalable and resilient infrastructure for software-defined systems. The study concludes that the integration of emerging technologies in software-defined systems is beneficial in enhancing their efficiency, security, and reliability. However, the adoption of these technologies requires careful consideration of their potential limitations and challenges.

This paper proposes a limited feedforward approach for channel estimation in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems with cascaded precoding. The downlink transmission is the focus of the proposed approach, while considering the delays in the uplink. The cascaded precoding strategy is used to reduce the impact of the feedback delay and improve the system performance. The study also investigates the effect of the number of antennas on the performance of the system. The proposed approach shows improved performance compared to traditional approaches, with reduced complexity and cost. The study indicates that limited feedforward systems with cascaded precoding can be a viable solution for channel estimation in massive MIMO communication systems.

Recently, 3D Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) designs have become popular due to their enhanced performance at oblique incidence angles as compared to planar designs. While planar FSS design has been successfully performed using discrete nature-inspired evolutionary optimization algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), these algorithms are not suited for the problem of 3D FSS design, due to the generation of non-contiguous structures, making manufacturing difficult. One alternative to these algorithms is the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) technique, which guarantees contiguous segments are generated. However, traditional ACO methods require meanders to continue until they are trapped, potentially generating a PEC unit cell. In this paper, a Multi-Objective Lazy Ant Colony Optimization (MOLACO) algorithm will be applied to the problem of FSS design. The introduction of lazy ants allows exploration of solutions previously inaccessible by traditional implementations of ACO. Simulated results will show that it is well suited to the problem of 3D FSS design.

Collaborative recommender systems have become increasingly popular over the past few years due to the exponential growth of user-generated reviews. These systems work by collecting and analyzing data from various users to generate recommendations for other users. Feature extraction is an important aspect of collaborative recommender systems as it allows for the identification of key features within user-generated reviews. This, in turn, allows for the extraction of valuable information that can be used to improve the performance of these systems. Data mining techniques, such as hidden Markov models, are also commonly used to help identify patterns and trends within user-generated reviews. Additionally, standards have been established to ensure interoperability and consistency across different collaborative recommender systems. In this concise survey, we explore the fundamental concepts of collaborative recommender systems and the importance of collaboration, feature extraction, data mining, and standards in developing efficient and effective systems.

Taxi demand prediction has recently attracted increasing research interest due to its huge potential application in large-scale intelligent transportation systems. However, most of the previous methods only considered the taxi demand prediction in origin regions, but neglected the modeling of the specific situation of the destination passengers. We believe it is suboptimal to preallocate the taxi into each region-based solely on the taxi origin demand. In this paper, we present a challenging and worth-exploring task, called taxi origin-destination demand prediction, which aims at predicting the taxi demand between all-region pairs in a future time interval. Its main challenges come from how to effectively capture the diverse contextual information to learn the demand patterns. We address this problem with a novel contextualized spatial-temporal network (CSTN), which consists of three components for the modeling of local spatial context (LSC), temporal evolution context (TEC), and global correlation context (GCC), respectively. First, an LSC module utilizes two convolution neural networks to learn the local spatial dependencies of taxi, demand respectively, from the origin view and the destination view. Second, a TEC module incorporates the local spatial features of taxi demand and the meteorological information to a Convolutional Long Short-term Memory Network (ConvLSTM) for the analysis of taxi demand evolution. Finally, a GCC module is applied to model the correlation between all regions by computing a global correlation feature as a weighted sum of all regional features, with the weights being calculated as the similarity between the corresponding region pairs. The extensive experiments and evaluations on a large-scale dataset well demonstrate the superiority of our CSTN over other compared methods for the taxi origin-destination demand prediction.

This paper proposes a new method for feature extraction in palmprint recognition called Local Discriminant Direction Binary Pattern (LDD-BP). The method is based on histograms of patterns that are generated by comparing a pixel with its neighboring pixels using a discriminant analysis. The resulting features are then used for palmprint recognition, achieving high accuracy in experiments. The LDD-BP method is compared with other existing methods, and the results indicate its effectiveness in palmprint recognition. Furthermore, the indexes of the proposed method are scalable, which makes it suitable for large-scale applications. This technique is expected to contribute to the field of pattern recognition and computer science in general by addressing the problem of palmprint recognition.

Fall represents a major health risk for the elderly people. If the situation is not alerted in time then this leads to loss of life or impairment in the elderly, which reduces the quality of life. In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a Fall Detection System based on Internet of Things (FallDS-IoT) by designing a wearable system to detect the falls of elderly people. We use Accelerometer and Gyroscope sensors to get accurate results of fall detection. We classify the daily activities of elderly people into sleeping, sitting, walking and falling. We use two well-known machine learning algorithms, namely K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) algorithm and decision tree to deal with the above work. The resultant accuracies for our generated dataset were 98.75% and 90.59%, respectively. Therefore, we were able to conclude that K-NN gives more accuracy in detecting falls and this method is used for classification. whenever a fall happens, a message informing about the fall will be sent to a registered phone number through a Python module.

This paper aims to investigate the asymptotic optimal portfolio strategy in fast mean-reverting stochastic environments. The perturbation methods and stochastic processes are utilized to study the behavior of portfolios in such environments. The optimization problems for portfolios are formulated and solved to achieve the asymptotic optimal strategy. Moreover, the discrete wavelet transforms are applied to estimate the portfolio parameters in the non-stationary environments. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed portfolio strategy. This study contributes to the field of portfolio optimization in the fast mean-reverting stochastic environments and provides useful insights for investors to make informed investment decisions. The proposed strategy has important implications for portfolio management and can be further explored and applied in practical investment scenarios. This paper will be presented at upcoming conferences to facilitate discussions and enhance understanding of the topic.

The emergence of device-to-device (D2D) communication has revolutionized the cellular network technology by allowing direct communication between devices, resulting in the offloading of traffic from the cellular infrastructure. Efficient resource management has become a key concern for enabling D2D communication in cellular networks. This paper proposes a global optimal resource allocation scheme that minimizes interference and maximizes resource utilization in FD-D2D enabled cellular networks. The proposed scheme optimizes the allocation of resources, such as frequency and power, for D2D communication while ensuring that the cellular network's performance is not adversely affected. The complexity of the optimization problem is also analyzed to determine the efficient allocation of resources. Copper as a material has been extensively used in network communication. In conclusion, this paper presents a significant contribution to the area of resource allocation in cellular networks that can improve resource utilization and network performance.

This paper presents a new multi-hop PSO based routing protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) with energy harvesting. WSNs are becoming increasingly popular in many applications, including environmental monitoring, healthcare, and smart buildings. Routing protocols are critical components of WSNs, which play a vital role in making efficient use of energy resources. Energy harvesting technology is a promising solution to the energy consumption problem of WSNs. The proposed PSO-based routing protocol is designed to optimize energy efficiency while reducing energy consumption. The algorithm is based on a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) approach that enables efficient energy management in WSNs. Simulation results show that the proposed protocol significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art protocols in terms of energy efficiency and network lifetime.

This study explores the characterizing of concept conveying in interactions between MOOC (Massive Open Online Course) students and assistants. The measurement of concept conveying is examined through electronic learning platforms, which have become increasingly popular in providing training and education. With the help of observers, we analyze the message systems used by MOOC students and assistants, along with the presses used during these interactions. The ultimate goal of this research is to provide a better understanding of the effectiveness of MOOC interactions and how they can be improved to enhance students' learning experience.

Cancer care centers aim at automating the carried out procedures in their labs in order to reduce staff effort and increase test accuracy. This has motivated the researchers undertaking Ig/TCR clonality testing at a cancer care organisation to derive a requirements model for a process-based and service-oriented intelligent framework in diagnosing malignant lymphoproliferative neoplasms. However, eliciting the requirements for such a framework has been challenged by the incomplete specifications of the Ig/TCR testing in the cancer care lab protocols. Workflow models using Business Process Modelling Notation (BPMN) has been developed to deliver a validated set of Ig/TCR workflow models. These BPMN workflow models constituted the base for deriving functional and service requirements for Ig/TCR testing linked with related quality requirements. The triangulation between Ig/TCR process models, the functional/service-oriented requirements and quality requirement formed the foundations to propose an intelligent framework for Ig/TCR clonality testing with process mining and data analytics driven by current and historical Ig/TCR events in a particular lab of a cancer care centre.

This paper proposes a mathematical model for joint flow and density reconstruction in large traffic networks using partial turning ratio information. The model takes into account vehicle dynamics and estimation of flow and density of different segments of roads in the network. Artificial neural networks are used for density measurement and to learn the relationships between the partial turning ratios and the actual flow and density of the network. The results show that the proposed model provides accurate estimates of flow and density in large traffic networks with partial turning ratio information. This approach can be used to improve traffic management and optimize traffic flow in urban areas.

Internet of things (IoT) comprises is the system of physical devices, machines and different devices inserted with electronics, programming, sensors, Actuators, and interconnectivity that have unique identities and are connected to the internet. Traditionally the productivity of CNC was confined to the counts of the products produced. In Industrial Internet of Things the productivity can be measured with the help of predictive and prescriptive maintenance. This paper is focused on study of productivity using IoT platforms. A feasibility analysis was carried out with and without using a software platform designed to make manufacturing efficient and cost effective. Various factors affecting the productivity of CNC were explored. The predictive breakdowns during the manufacturing were calculated. Analysis was carried out to check for differences in Overall Equipment Efficiency (OEE) in traditional CNC and IoT enabled CNC. Finally it is observed that the OEE was increased for the CNC from 59.9% to 78.59%.

The Internet of Things is expected to generate an unprecedented number of unbounded data streams that will produce a paradigm shift when it comes to data analytics. We are moving away from performing analytics in a public or private cloud to performing analytics locally at the fog and edge resources. In this paper, we propose a network of tasks utilizing edge, fog, and cloud computing that are designed to support an Analytics Everywhere framework. The aim is to integrate a variety of computational resources and analytical capabilities according to a data life-cycle. We demonstrate the proposed framework using an application in smart transit.

Surface roughness is an essential characteristic of many agricultural products, including fruits. In this study, we propose a surface roughness classification method for mangosteen using gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) based texture analysis. Feature extraction was conducted on the surface-treated mangosteen samples to capture texture patterns that correlate with the observed surface roughness. The obtained texture features were used to train and test different classification models, including decision tree, k-nearest neighbors, and support vector machine. The experimental results showed that the proposed method achieved excellent classification accuracy, highlighting its potential to be used in industrial applications. Moreover, this study sheds light on the importance of surface morphology analysis for quality control and grading purposes in the agricultural industry.

In this paper, we investigate the effect of cell curvature on the convergence rates of EFIE numerical solutions. We develop numerical models based on integral equations to study the behavior of current density in curved cells. The research is motivated by the need for accurate and efficient computational modeling of electromagnetic phenomena in curved structures. We present a mathematical model that takes into account the geometry of the cells and the periodicity of the current density. Our findings reveal that cell curvature significantly affects the convergence rates of the numerical solutions. The results suggest that the curvature-induced asymmetry of the current density distribution leads to a slower convergence rate. These findings have important implications for the design of numerical algorithms for electromagnetic problems in curved structures. Our study highlights the importance of considering the effects of cell curvature on the convergence of numerical solutions in computational electromagnetics research.

We consider the design of wideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar waveforms to approximate a desired beampattern and achieve prescribed space-frequency nulling in a space-frequency region of interest. A general design model involving modulus, power, and energy constraints on the probing waveforms is introduced. To deal with the resulting non-convex design, a novel iterative algorithm with low computational complexity is proposed. In each iteration, the non-convex design is approximated successively through a series of convex subproblems. Then, each convex subproblem is reformulated in a new alternating direction method of multipliers form, with small-sized subproblems solved in parallel with closed-form solutions via utilizing the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Low-rank tensor recovery is a crucial issue in many fields such as computer vision, signal processing, and machine learning. In this paper, we propose a robust low-rank tensor recovery method with rectification and alignment. Our approach focuses on minimizing the objective function by adopting an optimization technique that provides better convergence properties. Moreover, we propose a sparsity-inducing regularization term that helps to obtain a more concise representation of the tensor. To facilitate the use of our proposed method, we also develop a visualization tool that allows analysis of the essential properties of the output tensor. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our approach compared to state-of-the-art methods. Therefore, our proposed method has considerable potential for applications in various areas such as image compression, data analysis, and recommendation systems.

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in adults with fluctuating blood sugar levels. The early detection and diagnosis of DR play a pivotal role in effective treatment and prevention of vision loss. In this study, we propose a novel approach for the diagnosis of DR using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Our approach involves training the network on retinal images from patients diagnosed with DR to classify retinal images as either normal or exhibiting signs of DR. We also incorporate feature extraction techniques to improve the accuracy of the classification algorithm. The proposed approach shows promising results in accurately diagnosing DR, which can help in early detection and prevention of blindness in diabetic patients. The use of CNNs in medical image analysis is a rapidly growing research area, and our approach can contribute to the development of more sophisticated and accurate methods for the diagnosis of various diseases.

The development and integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) have become increasingly essential to ensure reliable and efficient power grid operations. The accurate perception and forecasting of power grid load state information is crucial in enhancing the performance of BESS. In this study, an Elman neural network is proposed to model the state of power grids and forecast the load information in real-time. The Elman neural network is a type of biological neural network that is capable of performing learning tasks and pattern recognition. The proposed technique has been validated using real-world power grid data, and the results show that the Elman neural network model performs significantly better in terms of accuracy and robustness than other existing techniques. By leveraging the BESS with the proposed forecasting technology, the power grid operators can better manage the energy storage systems and ensure the stability and reliability of the grid in real-time. The proposed technique can also be extended to other applications in the field of power system management and control.

Mobile Edge Assistance Information (MEAI) can provide significant benefits for optimizing Radio Access Networks (RANs) in the 5G mobile communication era. This approach involves the use of data structures and a mathematical model to predict future handover events, enabling the RAN to proactively address potential issues before they occur. MEAI provides critical information about aspects of radio networks that are beyond the current capabilities of RANs, such as user behavior and device status. With the ability to better analyze these factors, RANs can more accurately predict handover events and optimize network performance accordingly. This paper discusses the use of MEAI for RAN optimization, its underlying mathematical model, and the data structures necessary for its successful implementation. Ultimately, this research shows that MEAI can greatly benefit RAN optimization efforts, improving network performance and user experience in the process.

In this paper, based on statistical learning, we propose a method to estimate communication performance for the advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) that employs the power line communication (PLC) technology. We verify the accuracy of estimation by comparing them with measured communication test results at a test site. We also present a stochastic model for the probing success rate by applying the estimated PLC communication quality values and the metering protocol sequence.

The security of inertial navigation system (INS) is the key factor to determine the safety of air vehicle. Due to the INS contains some components of dynamic logic gate, which makes its work process presenting a series of dynamic characteristics. When using dynamic fault tree to analyze the security of INS, most of the traditional approaches are based on Markov chain and Monte-Carlo simulation. However, those methods have curse of dimensionality problem and/or require long computation time particularly when results with a high degree of accuracy are desired. In this paper, an analytical method is proposed based on sequential binary decision diagrams (SBDD) for combinatorial reliability analysis of dynamic systems. Firstly, the dynamic fault tree (DFT) model of collapse of inertial platform is built based on safety analysis used DFT. Secondly, the DFT model is modularized into independent static sub-trees and dynamic sub-trees, and then the exact expression of the occurrence probability for each minimal cut-set is determined by the static fault tree analysis method or SBDD method. Finally, the possibility of collapse of inertial platform in all its life is obtained after comprehensive analysis, and the result is compared with that based on Markov chain and Monte-Carlo simulation. The result shows that the proposed approach can generate exact possibility of collapse of inertial platform. In addition, the system model of sequential binary decision diagrams and possibility evaluation expression are reusable for the reliability analysis with different component failure parameters, the method is more applicable and more effective, and the method of calculating occurrence probability of top event for a dynamic fault tree is expanded.

The output tracking problem for a class of nonlinear systems presented in Nonlinear Block Controllable (NBC) form is addressed. Both matched and unmatched perturbations are considered. First, the Block Control iterative feedback linearization technique combined with a perturbation estimation are employed to design a sliding manifold. With the perturbation estimation, the effect of unmatched perturbation is mitigated. Then, a discrete-time sliding mode controller is synthesized such that the system state is driven toward a vicinity of the designed sliding manifold and stays there for all sampled time instants, avoiding chattering and reducing the matched perturbation effect. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is confirmed by simulation.

This paper focuses on the specialization of distributed actors through partial evaluation. The aim is to improve the efficiency of server-based distributed systems by reducing the runtime overhead associated with message passing. The approach is based on semantics-preserving program transformations that generate specialized code for runtime systems. The paper proposes the use of reactive power-based computational modeling to optimize the concurrent computing capabilities of the actors. Through this approach, the specialized code generated can be used to increase the scalability of distributed systems by reducing the overhead associated with message passing among servers. The results show promising improvements in the runtime performance of the distributed systems, making it a potential solution for high-performance computing applications.

In distributed software-defined networks (SDN), multiple physical SDN controllers, each managing a network domain, are implemented to balance centralized control, scalability and reliability requirements. In such networking paradigm, controllers synchronize with each other to maintain a logically centralized network view. Despite various proposals of distributed SDN controller architectures, most existing works only assume that such logically centralized network view can be achieved with some synchronization designs, but the question of how exactly controllers should synchronize with each other to maximize the benefits of synchronization under the eventual consistency assumptions is largely overlooked. To this end, we formulate the controller synchronization problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and apply reinforcement learning techniques combined with deep neural network to train a smart controller synchronization policy, which we call the Deep-Q (DQ) Scheduler. Evaluation results show that DQ Scheduler outperforms the anti-entropy algorithm implemented in the ONOS controller by up to 95.2% for inter-domain routing tasks.

Probabilistic Occupancy Map (POM) is a method to estimate a location of multiple people, given images taken by multiple cameras from different angles set at a head level. It is useful even in the case of significant occlusion and can derive a location of people without an appearance model and prerequisite knowledge about the number of people in a detection space. However, the computation time of POM increases according to the area of detection space and number of cameras, which limits its performance. In this paper, we report performance enhancement of POM by applying OpenMP and GPGPU. As a result of evaluating test videos with different area size and cameras, we confirm that OpenMP implementation marks 1.8 to 2.7 times speedup compared to single CPU core implementation for all videos, whereas GPU implementation provides speedup in case of large grid size by a maximum of 7.6 times.

Condition based monitoring (CBM) of machines is a crucial aspect of industrial maintenance. CBM enables early detection of faults in machines, which can lead to cost savings and increased reliability. This paper proposes the use of Mamdani fuzzy networks for CBM of machines. The Mamdani fuzzy network is trained to detect faults in machines using vibration data. The training of the network involves selecting the input features and optimizing the system parameters. Once trained, the Mamdani fuzzy network is used for monitoring machines. The proposed approach outperforms traditional techniques such as artificial neural networks in terms of accuracy and computational speed. This is due to the ability of fuzzy logic to handle uncertainties and vagueness in the input data. The linguistic rules used in fuzzy logic allow for interpretation of the CBM results, making it easier for operators to make decisions. Overall, the proposed CBM approach using Mamdani fuzzy networks shows great potential in improving machine reliability and reducing maintenance costs.

Non-intrusive sleep monitoring is critical for certain populations such as severely disabled autistic children. Nocturnal disturbance analysis is an important diagnostic tool for assessing sleep issues. The objective of this paper is to detect and minimize the effects of motion artifacts in signals recorded via an unobtrusive electromechanical film-based ballistocardiogram (BCG) sensor integrated into a smart bed system. The goal is to have a reliable estimation of beat-to-beat (B-B) interval. The proposed algorithm includes two main stages: a motion detection algorithm followed by a motion artifact removal system. Motion detection involves a sequential detection algorithm in which successive data frames are compared to two thresholds: upper and lower thresholds. Each motion corrupted frame can then be reconstructed by an approach that relies on a parametric model of the BCG signal. Exploiting the fact that the underlying BCG parameters (J-peak-to-J-peak interval, J-peak-to-K-peak amplitude, and the most significant frequency component) change slowly and are correlated across time; an autoregressive model-based tracking and Wiener smoother based parameter estimation strategies are proposed. The experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed motion artifact detection and removal algorithms. The probability of detection of 96% and high average coverage of 84% with over 90% precision for the estimated B-B intervals are achieved on recordings for 19 h of sleep from three subjects. Our novel motion detection and removal methods demonstrate the feasibility of using bed-based BCG signals for providing a reliable unobtrusive way to estimate the B-B interval in the presence of motion.

Overall Internet Protocol (IP) traffic is expected to grow to 396 Exabyte per month by 2022, as a result of the demands of new applications such as Cloud, Internet of Things (IoT) and the expected arrival of fifth generation mobile networks (5G). In particular, mobile networks contribute most to this predicted increase in traffic and have a heavy burden on technological developments. Most of this traffic will be local with a significant burden on the access network and the metropolitan and less to the backbone network. Thus, focusing on the corresponding traffic, produced by 5G applications running in the core network, the need for data analysis and performance estimation becomes essential, in order to enhance the Validation and Verification (V&V) of different Network Services (NS) across heterogeneous platforms. In this paper, we are focusing on the analysis of the monitoring data, that are produced by the running Network Services (NSs), over a Software Defined Network (SDN). Furthermore, we propose an approach where the test developers would benefit from all the essentials in order to understand the service's behavior, and optimize the V&V tests, prior to the production.

Intelligent fault location of rudders is a crucial aspect of ensuring safety and reliability in maritime transportation. In this paper, we propose a new application of optimized random forest algorithms in fault location. Our approach leverages radio frequency testing and loading data models to improve accuracy and efficiency of fault identification. Machine learning techniques are utilized to process the vast amount of data and generate predictive models. Specifically, we optimize the random forest algorithms by adjusting the parameters and using feature selection techniques to enhance the performance of the predictive models. Our experiments show that the proposed approach is significantly more accurate and efficient than conventional fault location techniques. The optimized random forest algorithms also provide a framework for future research in intelligent fault location of rudders.

A regularized optimization problem over a large unstructured graph is studied, where the regularization term is tied to the graph geometry. Typical regularization examples include the total variation and the Laplacian regularizations over the graph. When the graph is a simple path without loops, efficient off-the-shelf algorithms can be used. However, when the graph is large and unstructured, such algorithms cannot be used directly. In this paper, an algorithm, referred to as “Snake,” is proposed to solve such regularized problems over general graphs. The algorithm consists in properly selecting random simple paths in the graph and performing the proximal gradient algorithm over these simple paths. This algorithm is an instance of a new general stochastic proximal gradient algorithm, whose convergence is proven. Applications to trend filtering and graph inpainting are provided among others. Numerical experiments are conducted over large graphs.

Equipment condition assessment is critical for maintenance engineering to ensure equipment reliability and sustainability. However, as it is often hard to collect balanced datasets, class-imbalanced datasets become a common problem in equipment condition assessment. In this study, we propose a novel ensemble model based on genetic algorithm, developed by combining numerical models and classification algorithms such as support vector machines and boosting. The proposed model addresses the issue of class-imbalanced data by balancing the dataset through over-sampling and under-sampling techniques, and optimizes the model parameters using the genetic algorithm. Results from experimental testing indicate that the proposed model outperforms other traditional models in terms of effectiveness and efficiency, demonstrating its potential to improve equipment condition assessment with class-imbalanced datasets. Overall, our study provides useful insights into leveraging the strengths of genetic algorithms for optimizing the performance of numerical models and classification algorithms in maintenance engineering.

This paper presents a novel Mittag-Leffler stabilization approach for an unstable time fractional hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE). The proposed method utilizes the Mittag-Leffler stability criterion to stabilize the PDE, thereby ensuring its convergence. The study investigates the behavior of the stabilized PDE under different conditions and provides insight into the applicability and limitations of the method. Additionally, the paper explores the use of covariance matrices in various applications, including maximum likelihood estimation and compressed sensing. The study also examines the use of MIMO communication and its impact on payloads and antennas. Finally, the paper discusses the concept of maximum likelihood detection and details its significance in communication systems. Overall, this paper offers valuable insights into the Mittag-Leffler stabilization of unstable time fractional hyperbolic PDEs and its possible applications in communication systems.

Wireless sensor networks are an easy target for report fabrication attacks, where compromised sensor nodes can be used by an adversary to flood the network with bogus/false reports. En-route filtering is a mechanism where intermediate forwarding nodes identify and drop false reports while they are being forwarded towards the sink. Existing en-route filtering schemes either have high storage overhead or low filtering efficiency. In this article, we propose a blockchain based deterministic en-route filtering scheme, capable of dropping false reports efficiently. Further, the proposed scheme does not require any key exchange between sensor nodes for data endorsement/authentication, thus reducing the associated key storage overhead and communication overhead. Finally, the proposed scheme can also adapt to dynamic networks and mobile sinks making it suitable for modern wireless sensor networks.

In this paper, a novel scheme is proposed for CP-length detection and initial synchronization for the LTE downlink. The scheme utilizes the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technique, which is widely used in wireless communication. The focus of the proposed scheme is on achieving accurate estimation of the synchronization parameters for long term evolution (LTE) downlink. The scheme uses a cross-correlation-based detection method to accurately detect the CP length and also estimates the delay spread. The proposed scheme is evaluated using MATLAB simulations, and the results show that it outperforms existing synchronization techniques in terms of accuracy and complexity. The proposed scheme can be used in various applications that require efficient synchronization and accurate estimation in the LTE downlink. The scheme is also applicable to other wireless communication systems that use OFDM modulation. Overall, this paper presents an important contribution to the field of wireless communication and provides a practical solution to the synchronization problem in long term evolution systems.

In this paper, a neural network path following controller for a differential drive vehicle is proposed. A differential drive vehicle has nonlinear characteristics and it is difficult to know its position exactly without using global/external position sensors. The neural network controller which has the characteristic of the PID controller is used in this study. We propose 1. using the additional/redundant derivative information in the input layer to improve learning efficacy, 2. applying a sigmoid function as the activation function in the output layer to remove difficulties on input saturation of actuators, and 3. novel cost function to improve the learing efficacy. Simulation and experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

The research paper focuses on the utilization of reinforcement learning and Monte Carlo methods for training partially observable multi-agent systems in games. The proposed approach involves the use of an enhanced deep distributed recurrent Q-network, which is capable of effectively encoding the history of the game as the input state representation. The training process is further optimized by incorporating deep learning techniques to facilitate convergence. Through extensive experimentation, the effectiveness of the proposed approach in tackling the challenges of partially observable multi-agent systems is demonstrated. The experimental results also showcase that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to traditional methods, highlighting the potential impact of these techniques in various real-world applications.

With the rapid development of the information age, electronic publishing has gradually become an important source of knowledge and education, especially for undergraduate students. This paper aims to investigate the use and acceptance of e-books among undergraduate students by conducting market research and examining the role of libraries, training and consumer electronics. The findings reveal that while electronic publishing has brought about many benefits, there are still challenges such as lack of access in certain areas, lack of training, and difficulty in finding reliable sources. In addition, the research sheds light on the unique challenges faced in Africa regarding the use and accessibility of e-books. Overall, this paper highlights the importance of addressing these challenges and promoting greater use and acceptance of e-books in education.

A fast vehicle horn sound location method with improved SRP-PHAT is proposed in this paper to accurately locate the source of a vehicle horn sound in real-time systems. The method combines frequency-domain analysis and feature extraction to improve the robustness of the SRP-PHAT algorithm. Multiple microphones are placed near the roads to record the sound signals, and the improved SRP-PHAT algorithm is used to process the signals and extract the features. The proposed method can effectively eliminate the noise and interference caused by other automobiles on the road and accurately locate the source of the horn sound. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve high accuracy and efficiency in vehicle horn sound location, which is of great significance for improving the safety of road transportation.

Data explosion and higher service level agreements (SLA) are common terminologies in modern communication networks. Recent advancements toward 5G networks add to the complexity where billions of devices, both static and mobile, are connected generating trillions of megabits of data flooding the network and where service providers scuffle daily to deliver key performance indicators: Lower latency, longer battery life, higher data rates, ultra-high reliability, and more connected devices. The optical-fiber world simultaneously witnesses a denser, fiber-rich network infrastructure which is critically challenged in fast economically developing countries by heavy construction of roads and other infrastructures that inflict repeated and unpredictable cuts to the extent that traffic is simultaneously interrupted in up to 10% of the optical links. Thus, network resiliency to fiber failures is already and will continue to be a top priority for operators. Depending on the SLA, operators choose from various resiliency options, e.g., at single network layers or across multiple ones, with dedicated protection or shared restoration, depending on decisive factors like network availability and total cost of ownership (TCO). With traditional network architectures, high resiliency comes with significantly increased TCO involving optical transport network (OTN) switches, L1 protection switching, and L1 restoration. This translates into high CAPEX and excessive space and power consumption, hampering the desirable seamless scalability with the continuously increasing demand for more capacity. This paper explores an alternative hyperscale network architecture, which is adaptable and resilient to multiple fiber failures, thus delivering committed service levels to the end users and which, at the same time, significantly reduces network cost compared to a traditional all OTN-switched network. The hyperscale architecture exploits low footprint carrier grade, data center interconnect type high-density transponders and cost-effective optical protection switching and restoration via software defined networking control. The paper also describes a routing and grooming algorithm to dimension a shared resource pool for optical restoration and a statistical simulation method for time effective execution, simulating failures over a carefully selected sub-set of failure scenarios to guarantee a high degree of network availability. Via network simulation, the paper demonstrates that multiple failure resiliency and cost effectiveness do not necessarily represent a contradiction in transport networks as long as an appropriate network architecture is chosen and that efficient network planning and optimization are applied.

Bluetooth low energy (BLE) beacons can be easily deployed to be used by a wide range of indoor localization techniques. BLE-beacon-based indoor localization techniques use the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) of the beacon signals. The variations of RSSI in an indoor environment is unpredictable and make the indoor localization challenging. Earlier researches considered that the distribution of RSSI in shadowing pathloss model is a normal (Gaussian) in the logarithmic scale. In an indoor environment, signals arrive at the receiver via various paths each having RSSI with Gaussian distribution. In this paper, we show that the aggregated magnitude of the indoor multipath signals at the receiver can also be modeled with Nakagami-m distribution. We investigate the performance of a BLE-based indoor localization technique using the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and the shadowing pathloss model with Nakagami-m distribution. We compare the location estimation performance when Gaussian distribution is used. We also collect data from a BLE test-bed and analyze the distribution of the RSSI measurements. The root means square error of the estimated position error for Nakagami-m based MLE solution is consistently lower than that of the Gaussian-based technique. In the computational time comparison, Nakagami-m distribution also shows a better performance speeding up the location estimation process by almost eight times.

This paper presents an Open-Loop approach for robust detection of selective harmonic in a single-phase system. The harmonic analysis and power system harmonics are key areas of investigation in power systems. The study proposes demodulation and frequency estimation techniques to detect the presence of selective harmonics. The Finite impulse response filters are used for smoothing the signal and removing noise from the system. The proposed method has been shown to be effective in real-time systems, and the results demonstrate that it can accurately detect harmonic frequencies in the presence of noise and other disturbances. This research sheds new light on the development of open-loop techniques for detecting harmonics in single-phase systems, which could be useful in a range of applications in power systems engineering.

The software reliability is mainly obtained through modeling and estimating. The existing software reliability models are nonlinear, and the parameter estimation of these models is difficult. At the same time, there are many optimization methods for solving the nonlinear function problems, such as artificial bee colony algorithm (ABC) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). ABC has the characteristics of fewer control parameters, strong exploration ability, and the high accuracy of the solution. The PSO algorithm has the characteristics of the relatively small amount of computation and fast search speed but it has premature convergence, especially in dealing with complex multi-peak search problems, and the problem of poor local search ability. This paper proposes the parameter estimation method of software reliability model based on hybrid PSO-ABC, constructs a new fitness function based on maximum likelihood estimation, removes the wrong solution during the algorithm execution process, and adds knowledge to improve the solution accuracy. This paper uses five classic sets of software failure data to estimate the GO model parameters and make predictions and performs a variety of comparisons of the algorithm results. The experimental results show that the new fitness function is better, the solution of parameter estimation using the hybrid PSO-ABC is more accurate, and the hybrid PSO-ABC has a great advantage in generality and especially in limited data.

In wireless sensor network (WSN), the appearance of coverage hole reduces the efficiency of data collection and has a serious impact on network quality of service. Detection of coverage holes is foundation of patching the sensor network to guarantee network quality of service. The paper proposes a distributed coverage hole detection algorithm based on hole boundary nodes (HPNs-CHD). The algorithm firstly uses sensing disk model to identify the HBN nodes in WSN and then exploits probabilistic message mechanism to detect coverage hole. The simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm outperforms other two algorithms in terms of average energy consumption and average time of coverage holes detection.

We consider the problem of channel aging in massive multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems using the Kalman filters without knowledge of channel correlation statistics. Although Wiener filtering can be used to estimate the channel state information to construct accurate precoders and decoders, their use is limited in the case where regular adaptation to channel changes is needed. In addition, since different users exhibit different mobility conditions, use of an adaptive Kalman filter is advantageous when compared to conventional estimation approaches. We build a general model that allows a wide range of user mobilities in each cell. Simulations using the model reveal that the Kalman filter is effective in predicting channel coefficients to build an effective precoder. In addition, we perform both uplink and downlink analysis and show that with poorer channel tracking, the achievable rates in massive MIMO diminish unless more accurate channel estimates are present.

Collaborative filtering is a widely used technique for generating personalized recommendations for users based on their past ratings. However, the effectiveness of these recommendations is highly dependent on the similarity measures used to identify similar users. This paper explores various similarity measures based on user ratings habits and evaluates their effectiveness in improving the accuracy of collaborative filtering recommendations. The study was conducted on a large dataset of user ratings in the telecommunications industry, and the results demonstrate that the proposed similarity measures outperform traditional filtering algorithms in terms of predictive accuracy. The findings of this study have important implications for data mining companies who aim to improve the effectiveness of their recommender systems in the internet and mobile services domains.

This paper investigates the use of classification algorithms for semi-blind uplink/downlink decoupling in sub-6 GHz/mmWave 5G networks. Specifically, the study focuses on the use of support vector machines for training and prediction purposes. Machine learning algorithms are utilized to classify signals in order to identify whether they belong to the uplink or downlink direction in a 5G mobile communication system. The prediction algorithms are then employed to provide frequency measurement estimations. The proposed method utilizes the central processing unit of the base station to achieve high accuracy and efficiency. The effectiveness of the classification algorithms is evaluated through simulation experiments, which demonstrate significant improvement in terms of uplink/downlink decoupling accuracy and frequency measurement accuracy. Overall, the results highlight the potential of machine learning techniques to be utilized in 5G networks for efficient and effective data processing.

The paper describes the interaction between Russian-German Engineering Faculty, established on the basis of St. Petersburg Electrotechnical University “LETI” and Technische Universität Ilmenau, and candidate students interested in undergoing studies and taking internships in Germany pursuing Master's degrees. The study focuses on the approaches utilized to attract the attention of and inform students to the double degree program. In this research, we analyzed the main communication channels between students and the faculty. The method of participant observation allowed us to discover several weaknesses in media planning. As a result, some recommendations are made to correct the current communication strategy.

This paper proposes an impulse radio ultrawideband (IR-UWB) wireless network channel model for next-generation wireless avionic system (NGWAS). Complexities such as poor network localization, redundant wiring, network security flaws, suitable physical proximity to the aircraft system's controller and need to guarantee scalable wireless network access have necessitated the adoption of wing system units of a passenger aircraft for this scheme's deployment. The proposed IR-UWB approach aims at alleviating the attendant drawbacks by selecting optimal channel path from available paths on the basis of bit error rate (BER), based on the numerical results obtained from the Saleh-Valenzuela (S-V) principle. Cooperative relay transmission schemes factored upon transmission power, overall outage probability and spectral-energy efficiency tradeoffs for the relay network communication were also investigated and compared with the noncooperative schemes. Simulation results validate maximum data packet delivery while a strong network signal strength is attained. Comparative approach of the performances of the IR-UWB standardized channel models are also evaluated.

This paper proposes a novel hybrid discriminative mixture model for cumulative citation recommendation. The mixture model leverages task analysis and knowledge-based systems to generate training data that captures the correlation between citations and their related encyclopedias. This approach offers significant advantages over current methods by combining the strengths of both discriminative and generative models, providing a more accurate and efficient recommendation algorithm. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their model by conducting extensive experiments on a large dataset of scientific papers, achieving superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. This research showcases the potential of using mixture models in recommendation systems and highlights the importance of utilizing knowledge-based approaches in data-driven tasks.

This paper proposes using U-NET neural networks for building detection on aerial images. The study focuses on working with satellite data and databases to segment buildings from the rest of the image. The authors trained their machine learning algorithms using labeled datasets and explored various techniques for image segmentation. The proposed method achieves excellent results in identifying buildings on various planets using aerial images. Overall, the study demonstrates that U-NET neural networks can be an effective tool for building detection in satellite imagery.

Spot Instances (SI) represent one of the ways cloud service providers use to deal with idle resources in off-peak periods, where these resources are being auctioned at low prices to customers with limited budgets in a dynamic manner. However, SI are poorly utilized due to issues like out-of-bid failures and bidding complexity. Thus, effective SI price models are of great importance to customers in order to plan their bidding strategies. This paper proposes a deep learning approach for Amazon EC2 SI price prediction, which is a time-series analysis (TSA) problem. The proposed Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) approach is compared with a well-known classical (i.e., non deep learning) approach for TSA, which is AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), using different accuracy measures commonly used in TSA. The results show the superiority of the LSTM approach compared with the ARIMA approach in many aspects.

Even though some of the driver assistant systems have been commercialized to provide safety and convenience to the driver, they can be applied for autonomous driving in limited situations such as highways. In this paper, we propose a supervisor agent that can enhance the driver assistant systems by using deep distributional reinforcement learning. The supervisor agent is trained using end-to-end approach that directly maps both a camera image and LIDAR data into action plan. Because the well-trained network of deep reinforcement learning can lead to unexpected actions, collision avoidance function is added to prevent dangerous situations. In addition, the highway driving case is a stochastic environment with inherent randomness and, thus, its training is performed through the distributional reinforcement learning algorithm, which is specialized for stochastic environment. The optimal action for autonomous driving is selected through the return value distribution. Finally, the proposed algorithm is verified through a highway driving simulator, which is implemented by the Unity ML-agents.

The complexity of supply chains increase, especially due to the geographical spread of supplier and customer networks. In the connected and automated supply chains of the industry 4.0, even more nodes are incorporated in supply chains. This paper discusses the possible improvement of process quality in the industry 4.0 through the different blockchain and distributed ledger technologies. We derived hypotheses from a literature review and asked German blockchain experts from the industry to validate and discuss the hypotheses. We find that the different blockchain technologies and consensus algorithms have different strength with regard to quality improvement. One central finding is that IOTA, developed especially for the IoT and deemed the 'next evolutionary step' is scalable and hence may increases the process efficiency, but at the same time is more vulnerable than other blockchain implementations, which again may reduce the overall process quality.

This paper explores the usefulness of SQL-query-similarity measures to find user interests. It begins by discussing the importance of feature extraction in the context of relational databases, particularly in applications such as companies with large datasets. The paper then explains the concept of SQL-query-similarity measures and their potential for identifying user interests based on the similarity of their search queries. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, the authors provide examples of extraterrestrial measurements and their applications in clustering algorithms. Overall, this paper suggests that SQL-query-similarity measures can be a powerful tool for identifying user interests and could have important applications in a variety of industries.

This paper proposes a summarization-based approach for the archival search and preservation of Old Sinhala text. The approach focuses on feature extraction using optical character recognition software and incorporates layouts and image segmentation techniques for better character recognition. Optical imaging is used to capture the images of the Old Sinhala text, and dictionaries are used to assist in character recognition. The proposed approach aims to preserve and digitize Old Sinhala text, making it more accessible for researchers and preserving it for future generations. This approach provides a practical solution for the preservation and access to Old Sinhala text archives.

We propose a novel optimization control strategy that integrates model-based optimization and square-wave extremum seeking control to optimize the efficiency of permanent-magnet synchronous machines using direct torque control (PMSM-DTC). Ordinary efficiency-optimization methods tend to require a precise mathematical model of the PMSM for estimating the optimal stator flux. Model-based optimization can rapidly shift the optimal parameters when operating conditions change. However, deviation in the stator flux estimation will occur if variation of the internal parameters is considered. The strategy proposed in this paper allows rapid switching of optimal parameters, and uses square-wave extremum seeking control to offset the deviation in the stator flux estimation quickly. The latter control scheme, ensures that the system always runs near the optimal point.

The articles in this special section examine fog computing which has received considerable attention in various application domains, especially those including time-sensitive transactions such as intelligent manufacturing, smart transportation, and cellular networks. Fog computing derives benefi ts from the increasingly smarter and more capable devices that reside not only at the network perimeter but also along the cloud-to-things continuum, which means fog-enabled services can be deployed anywhere within a network. Such continuous service provisioning and management have great potential to elevate the intelligence within multi-tier computing networks to realize context awareness, timely response, and task offloading. As a comprehensive and effective way of delivering customized new services, cloud, fog, and edge computing would be able to jointly reshape the landscape and the ecosystem of information and communication technology (ICT) and create tremendous business opportunities for future customers and various things. Realizing the challenges of providing diff erent fog services to satisfy high customer requirements, the articles in this section aim to give a timely overview of fog services and enabling technologies.

With the rapid development of technology and the increasing demand for sustainable development, the concept of "Smart Cities" has become an important issue. In this context, GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network) technology can play a significant role in the construction of Smart Cities. By providing high-speed and reliable access to information systems, GPON enables the integration of different systems such as energy, transportation, and security. Moreover, GPON can also facilitate the deployment of wireless fidelity (WiFi) hotspots, enhancing the connectivity of the city. Computational modeling can also be applied to GPON networks to optimize their performance and improve their efficiency.
