The system utilizes electrocardiography to extract feature information related to the myocardium and heart beat. Decision trees are used to classify the features and determine the presence of myocardial infarction. The proposed system was tested on a database of patients undergoing monitoring for cardiac disease, achieving high accuracy in detecting and localizing myocardial infarction. This system has the potential to be a valuable tool in clinical settings, providing automated and accurate diagnosis of cardiac disease.

The aim of this study was to develop a 3D-to-2D architecture for paraseptal emphysema segmentation using the SR-NET approach. The proposed method utilizes computed tomography (CT) images to accurately detect and segment lung lesions associated with paraseptal emphysema. This architecture involves a combination of three-dimensional and two-dimensional displays to effectively capture the spatial information of the lung tissue. The proposed method was trained using a dataset of chest CT images, and it achieved promising results in terms of accuracy and specificity. This study demonstrates the potential of the SR-NET approach for the segmentation of paraseptal emphysema, which has important clinical implications for the diagnosis and management of lung diseases.

In this paper, we focus on the resource management in a heterogeneous small cell network implemented in a Content Centric Network (CCN), where a hierarchical innetwork caching framework is formed with small cell base stations (SBSs) and macro base station (MBS) taking the role of the CCN router. In the hierarchical network structure, SBSs in the same hot spot cooperate and serve as the first hop routers, handling the Interest packets issued by the users. While the MBS works as the next hop router when a cache miss occurs at the small cell layer. Taken into consideration the feature of content request and content retrieving in CCN, we establish the link between SBSs and users on the request level rather than adopt the fixed connection regime. This means different SBSs may come to serve the same user in terms the content request it generates. In this context, we model a cooperative game among SBSs with transferable utility, in which the SBSs in a hot spot collaborate to maximize their overall revenue by selecting the best one to respond to each content request. In the meantime, a certain amount of spectrum resource is bought from the operator to satisfy the user's QoS requirement. Finally, the payoff is divided among SBSs via a bankruptcy game, and the solution is found exploiting the Nucleolus fairness concept. A decentralized Nucleolus calculation algorithm is adopted here so that the network can work in a distributed manner.

Breast cancer is a common type of cancer that affects millions of women worldwide. As the use of biomedical imaging in breast cancer diagnosis increases, the need for accurate and efficient classification methods becomes more critical. In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown great promise in analyzing biomedical images. However, the issue of low image resolution has created challenges in developing effective deep learning models for breast cancer classification. In this paper, we propose a deep hybrid attention method that combines the strengths of multiple deep learning architectures to overcome this challenge. We employ visualization techniques to examine the performance of the proposed method, which includes logic gates designed to help identify the most important features of the images. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to existing deep learning models, achieving high levels of accuracy in breast cancer classification. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the quality of breast cancer diagnosis, making it a promising tool for clinicians and researchers alike.

The variant of recurrent neural networks (RNN) such as long short-term memory (LSTM) is successful in sequence modelling such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) framework. However the decoded sequence is prune to have false substitutions, insertions and deletions. We exploit the spectral flatness measure (SFM) computed on the magnitude linear prediction (LP) spectrum to detect two broad manners of articulation namely sonorants and obstruents. In this paper, we modify the posteriors generated at the output layer of LSTM according to the manner of articulation detection. The modified posteriors are given to the conventional decoding graph to minimize the false substitutions and insertions. The proposed method decreased the phone error rate (PER) by nearly 0.7 % and 0.3 % when evaluated on core TIMIT test corpus as compared to the conventional decoding involved in the deep neural networks (DNN) and the state of the art LSTM respectively.

Wireless sensor network to create for water supply distribution network which have many issue, approaches and limitations. I have reviewed 120 research papers regarding this topic but particular 48 papers reviewed in table on leak detection and localization.we implement a comparison table. In the comparison table to create two parts first is the leak detection and second is localization. Main issue is on the localization. This paper contains objective, solution approaches, sensors, hardware, technique, parameters, results and limitations.

This paper presents a Markov decision process based model for a socially assistive robot. Problem addressed by the model is one to one correspondence of a robot with a human where robot has to convince the human about completing certain tasks. In this regard, emotions of the human and those of the robot are incorporated in the model. Furthermore, emotion transition probabilities and probabilities of robot being able to successfully convince the human are also incorporated. The resulting model however involves large state space. Computational complexity involved in calculation of optimal decision policy from the proposed model is discussed. Consequently, a computational complexity reduction technique is proposed that uses decomposition of the tasks to be performed into sub groups. An online learning framework is also proposed to account for un-modeled parameters in the problem. Behavior of decision making optimal policy obtained from the proposed model has been demonstrated with the help of a simulation based case study.

This study aims to investigate the factors causing ischemic stroke transformation into hemorrhagic stroke. The method used in this study is PLS-GA (Partial Least Square-Genetic Algorithm) and Swarm Algorithm. To conduct this study, data from various databases were collected on patients who have experienced stroke. It was found that blood pressure, medication intake and extent of brain damage were among the major causes of hemorrhagic transformation. Furthermore, genetic factors also contributed to this transformation. This study has important implications for insurance companies and healthcare providers. Understanding the causes of this transformation can help in the development of more effective treatments and preventative measures. Overall, this study provides a valuable contribution to the field of medical research, particularly in the area of stroke-related diseases.

Motion estimation is a crucial task in modern image and video processing applications such as streaming media, motion tracking, and image registration. In this work, we propose a new method for object-based motion estimation using the Estimated Point Density (EPD) similarity measure and Demons algorithm. The EPD similarity measure is used to detect image edges which are critical for accurate motion measurement. Prediction algorithms are used to estimate the object's motion. The optimization process is based on the Demons algorithm, which allows for efficient motion estimation. The proposed method is compared with other state-of-the-art algorithms, and it is shown to be more accurate and reliable. The results of the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for object-based motion estimation. This work presents a valuable contribution to image and video processing research and has practical applications in many areas.

Switched Reluctance Motors (SRM) are known for their inherent fault tolerance and rugged design. However, the use of external position sensors compromises the reliability of the machine. A sensorless control method is proposed in this paper which tries to eliminate the need of an extensively computed magnetization characteristic, and utilize the variation of phase inductance with rotor position. The inductance profile is modeled by a simplified trapezoidal function whose coefficients can be easily determined, with minimal offline measurement. The method was implemented on a 50 V, 1 HP 4-Phase SRM. Experiments verified that the method is capable of characterizing the inductance variation and estimate the rotor position.

RTS (Real-time Strategy) games require sophisticated AI (Artificial Intelligence) to provide a challenging and immersive gameplay experience. This paper proposes a framework for improving the game AI by utilizing supervised policy learning, tactical search, and deep reinforcement learning. In particular, the authors leverage the power of neural networks to facilitate these techniques in order to address the inherent complexity and uncertainty of RTS games. Specifically, supervised learning is used to improve the capabilities of the AI agents in making tactical decisions in real time. Tactical search is employed to optimize decision-making at a strategic level, while deep reinforcement learning is used to improve the agents' ability to learn from experience and adapt to changing conditions. These techniques are evaluated using benchmark datasets and demonstrate that the proposed framework is effective in improving the performance of RTS game AI. In conclusion, the proposed approach provides a promising direction for advancing the state-of-the-art in game AI and may lead to new frontiers in the development of engaging and challenging RTS games.

In this paper we propose a general framework in which the robustness properties and requirements of output regulation schemes can be formally described. We introduce a topological definition of robustness relative to arbitrary steady state properties, extending the usual notion of robustness relative to the existence of a steady state in which the regulation error vanishes. We review some of the main control approaches for linear and nonlinear systems, by re-framing their robustness properties within the proposed setting. We show that the celebrated robustness property of the linear regulator, namely the “internal model principle” stated by Francis, Wonham and Davison in the 70's, can be generalized to nonlinear systems in a robustness property relative to the Fourier expansion of the regulation error. We then focus on nonlinear regulation, where we show that only practical regulation can be achieved robustly, while asymptotic regulation is achieved in a quite fragile way. The paper concludes with a conjecture stating that, in a general nonlinear context, asymptotic regulation cannot be achieved in a robust way with a finite dimensional regulator.

Wireless sensor networks have become increasingly popular over the years, bringing wireless communication to a wide range of applications. Security is a major concern in wireless sensor networks, and communication system security has become a key challenge. Ad hoc networks are particularly vulnerable to security breaches and the presence of eavesdropper nodes can pose a significant risk to the confidentiality of transmitted data. Nickel is a commonly used material for sensor nodes in wireless sensor networks, but its low strength limits its ability to withstand intentional collisions. Therefore, it is important to develop effective mechanisms for preventing illegal overhearing by eavesdropper nodes in wireless sensor networks. This paper proposes using intentional collisions between sensor nodes to prevent eavesdropping. Time division multiple access is used in combination with the proposed mechanism to ensure that only authorized nodes are allowed access to the network. The effectiveness of the proposed mechanism is evaluated through simulations and the results show that intentional collisions can be an effective method for preventing illegal overhearing by eavesdropper nodes in wireless sensor networks. The proposed mechanism can improve the security of wireless sensor networks, and is a promising area for future research in robot sensing systems.

This study explores the influence of the forgetting factor on tracking non-stationary neural dynamics. The adaptation models, eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, brain modeling, adaptive systems, and prediction algorithms are taken into consideration to investigate the effect of the forgetting factor. The research is based on the biological neural network and heuristic algorithms, which represent the brain's function and simulate the human computational process. The findings indicate that the forgetting factor plays a vital role in the accuracy of adaptive systems and prediction algorithms. The results suggest that choosing an appropriate forgetting factor is crucial in tracking non-stationary neural dynamics. These findings contribute to the development of better adaptation models and prediction algorithms for analyzing human brain activity in various contexts.

This paper proposes a novel approach called HitBoost for survival analysis using a multi-output gradient boosting decision tree method. This approach is designed to model the hazards and predict outcomes associated with various diseases. The boosting technique is utilized to improve the accuracy of predictive models, enabling the development of personalized treatment plans. Stochastic processes are incorporated to account for uncertainties in the data, and decision trees are used to construct the models. HitBoost outperforms traditional methods such as neural networks and Cox regression, demonstrating its superior performance in the analysis of medical data. Ultimately, this method could have significant applications in the development of precision medicine, facilitating more effective diagnosis, treatment, and ultimately better patient outcomes.

This paper proposes a feature extraction method for underground object detection using B-scan images from GprMax, a ground penetrating radar simulator. The focus is on detecting landmines, which can be made of various materials including plastics and metals. The proposed method involves calculating histograms of the amplitudes of the B-scan images to extract features that can distinguish between the object and clutter in the surrounding soil. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments using simulated data. The results show that the method achieved high accuracy in detecting objects buried at various depths and with different sizes and materials. This method has the potential to be applied in real-world landmine detection scenarios, where the accurate and efficient detection of buried objects is crucial for ensuring the safety of people in conflict-affected areas.

This paper presents a multi-band vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) channel characterization technique in the presence of vehicle blockage. Antenna measurements, frequency measurement, and loss measurement were performed to measure the signal propagation characteristics of V2V links in different frequency bands. The presence of automobiles as blockages in the V2V channels was also taken into consideration. The fading channel characteristics and associated delays were studied for different frequency bands, which is of great importance for the design and evaluation of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs). This study demonstrates that the use of multiple frequency bands can mitigate the effects of vehicle blockage and improve the reliability of V2V communications. Overall, this research provides a deeper understanding of the V2V wireless communication channel and lays the foundation for the development of more robust and efficient VANETs.

Protection coordination is an essential task for ensuring the reliable and secure operation of power systems. In this paper, an improved optimal solution for the directional overcurrent relays coordination is proposed using a hybridized whale optimization algorithm. This algorithm combines the features of genetic algorithms and mathematical models to achieve a better performance in complex power systems. The optimal relay settings are obtained by minimizing the cost function, which considers the coordination time and the sensitivity of the relays. The proposed method is tested on a benchmark power system and compared with existing techniques. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the coordination among the relays and reducing the fault clearing time. This study reveals that the whale optimization algorithm can be applied to the protection coordination problem, and the hybridization with other optimization techniques can enhance its performance. The proposed method has the potential to enhance the security and stability of power systems and improve the reliability of protective relaying.

This paper presents a performance comparison of automated EEG enhancement algorithms utilized for mental workload assessment of ambulant users. The study focuses on Feature extraction, Electroencephalography, Electrodes, Task analysis, Classification algorithms, Support vector machines, and Monitoring. EEG is a non-invasive method that records electrical activity in the brain from the scalp. In this study, different feature extraction techniques have been used to capture important characteristics of EEG signals. Various electrodes placement methods were also tested to analyze which has the most significant impact on the outcome. Moreover, task analysis was performed to investigate the effectiveness of the methods in detecting mental workload changes during cognitive tasks. Different classification algorithms, including support vector machines, were investigated to examine their accuracy in detecting mental workload levels. Finally, monitoring of the results was conducted to assess the usability of the proposed algorithms for practical applications. The experimental results showed that the proposed methods are effective in assessing mental workload levels of ambulant users.

The audit industry has undergone significant changes over the years, from traditional methods to technologically influenced approaches. This paper explores the shift towards technology-based auditing from a compliance perspective, with a focus on monitoring, tools, data mining, and ontologies. Additionally, this paper takes an in-depth look at the economic implications of these changes for organizations operating in various industries. The adoption of technology in auditing has enabled auditors to improve the quality of their work, identify potential issues more efficiently, and reduce the risk of fraud. However, this shift also presents new challenges and requires the implementation of new strategies to effectively manage the data and tools involved. As a result, organizations must continuously adapt to keep pace with technological advancements and remain competitive in their respective industries.

Mobile cloud computing systems, or simply mobile clouds, have attracted tremendous attention because they allow mobile devices with limited computational resources to offload complex computations. However, due to the channel uncertainty and the complexity of a computation task, mobile computation offloading may suffer from poor outage performance that the offloaded task cannot be completed within the desired delay constraint. Thus, how to efficiently identify and overcome the outage bottleneck, which could be used to optimize resource allocation schemes and improve the system performance effectively is an open problem. In this paper, we shall develop a unified framework that minimizes the overall outage probability in various mobile computation offloading scenarios. More specifically, the outage bottleneck is defined and identified by adopting asymptotic analysis, without any need of the accurate outage probabilities in both transmissions and computations. To overcome the outage bottleneck, resource pairing, matching, and allocation policies are investigated. Both theoretical analysis and numerical results show that the outage bottleneck relies on not only the availability of spectrum and computation resources but also the probability distributions of computation complexities of the computation tasks.

Individuals with cochlear implants (CIs) experience more difficulty understanding speech in reverberant environments than normal hearing listeners. As a result, recent research has targeted mitigating the effects of late reverberant signal reflections in CIs by using a machine learning approach to detect and delete affected segments in the CI stimulus pattern. Previous work has trained electrode-specific classification models to mitigate late reverberant signal reflections based on features extracted from only the acoustic activity within the electrode of interest. Since adjacent CI electrodes tend to be activated concurrently during speech, we hypothesized that incorporating additional information from the other electrode channels, termed cross-channel information, as features could improve classification performance. Cross-channel information extracted in real-world conditions will likely contain errors that will impact classification performance. To simulate extracting cross-channel information in realistic conditions, we developed a graphical model based on the Ising model to systematically introduce errors to specific types of cross-channel information. The Ising-like model allows us to add errors while maintaining the important geometric information contained in cross-channel information, which is due to the spectro-temporal structure of speech. Results suggest the potential utility of leveraging cross-channel information to improve the performance of the reverberation mitigation algorithm from the baseline channel-based features, even when the cross-channel information contains errors.

In recent years, Neural Network (NN) is developed as an optimal technique for the prediction of tasks which include image classification, speech recognition and also useful in biomedical analysis. Biomedical data consists of diverse modalities like X-ray, CT, MRI, PET, EEG and ECG signals. There are several NNs techniques such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) that are used for various prediction applications in handling multimodal heterogeneous data. However, learning and prediction of such multimodal data limits the scope of existing neural techniques. One of the limitations of ANN observes that addition of layer cause back propagation stuck in local minima and reduction of learning speed. Where, DNN causes higher computational complexity in training the features which are based on contrastive divergence. In CNN there is loses of spatial information due to the weight factors variation. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes a novel learning technique in which the weight factor of DNN is integrated with CNN for handling multimodal heterogeneous data. The simulation results prove that the integrated learning technique (IDCNN) obtains better learning performance than ANN, CNN and DNN models in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and efficiency in terms of cross entropy.

A high amount of stress is experienced by people of all ages nowadays and is affecting their physical and mental health adversely. Traditionally, Perceived Stress Score (PSS-14) questionnaire is used to calculate the stress score, which requires manual intervention of people. In this work, we look into the usage of Electroencephalography (EEG) to help predict the stress level of people without manual intervention and recording by a Brain-Computer Interface(BCI) instrument. EEG can estimate and record the electrical signals in brains utilizing sensors exhibited over the scalp. We propose the design of a brain mapping based stress identification system using a single electrode EEG device. Here we have taken EEG recording of 63 students using a single electrode EEG device NeuroSky Mindwave Mobile. A novel feature combination of bandpower ratios of alpha, beta, delta and theta bands are extracted and fed to the classifiers. We evaluate the performance of Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbour machine learning algorithms. Target class of the training set is assigned using the stress score calculated from the response of the PSS-14 questionnaire. We achieve the highest average classification accuracy of 74.43 % using K-NN algorithm. We observe that there exist a correlation of bandpower ratios of different bands obtained from recorded EEG signals from the frontal portion of the brain with the stress level of subjects.

This paper proposes a fast motion estimation algorithm with efficient memory access for HEVC hardware encoders. The algorithm is designed to optimize memory management and reduce the complexity of the encoding process. The implementation of the algorithm in hardware can be beneficial for various applications, including Microsoft Windows. The proposed method provides a solution for the motion estimation problem, which is a key component in video encoding. The algorithm focuses on reducing memory access time, which is a major bottleneck in hardware encoders. The method is compatible with the current encoding standards and can be easily integrated into existing hardware designs. Overall, the proposed algorithm offers an efficient solution for motion estimation that can enhance the performance of HEVC hardware encoders.

The increase in number of cellular users had lead to the evolution from the traditional cellular networks to the more efficient heterogeneous cellular networks (HetNet) to handle the traffic. Offloading plays a vital role in handling the traffic from the congested macro base station by handing users to the less congested femto base stations (FBS). Further, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has proved to be efficient for the future generation networks. In this work, we study the offloading in HetNets, where the FBS tier serves the users using NOMA. Imperfect channel state information (CSI) is considered to analyze the outage probability of offloaded user, since, in practice CSI estimation requires significant system overhead, especially when the number of users are large. Hence, for practical systems, the analyses with imperfect CSI is more relevant. Some important observations regarding offloading to FBS tier with NOMA based on imperfect CSI are drawn. The analytical results are validated using Monte Carlo simulations.

This paper proposes an adaptive approach to sensor bias fault diagnosis and accommodation for a class of input-output nonlinear systems. The approach involves estimation, adaptation models, and fault diagnosis to overcome the uncertainty that arises from nonlinear systems. In particular, the proposed method is designed to handle the issue of sensor bias fault diagnosis and accommodation. Through stability analysis and noise measurement, the proposed method is shown to be effective in tackling the challenges posed by nonlinear systems. By applying the proposed adaptive approach, the system can adjust to changes in the environment and maintain its stability, thus improving its overall performance. Overall, this study highlights the importance of using an adaptive approach to handle uncertainty and nonlinearities in applications that involve sensor bias fault diagnosis and accommodation.

A large number of mobile multimedia terminals are prominent features of smart cities. Device-to-device (D2D) communication takes advantage of the limited bandwidth resources of cellular networks to accommodate more mobile devices. However, when D2D pairs reuse cellular users channels, serious interference leads to energy consumption, which dissatisfies the requirements of green communication. This paper focuses on energy efficiency maximization of D2D communication under the constraints of both D2D pairs and cellular users quality of service. The formulated resource allocation problem is NP-hard, which is usually difficult to solve within polynomial time. To make the problem easy to handle, we divide it into power control and channel allocation sub-problems. In particular, we propose a power control algorithm based on the Lambert W function to maximize the energy efficiency of a single D2D pair. The preference values of D2D pairs and cellular users are calculated using the power control results, respectively. A channel allocation scheme based on the Gale-Shapley algorithm utilizes preference values to match two sides, which aims at maximizing the signal to interference plus noise ratio of cellular users and the energy efficiency of D2D pairs. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm could not only guarantee the transmission rate of cellular users but also improve the system and D2D pairs energy efficiency.

In recent years, there has been an increasing interest in the unsupervised image translation task, which aims to learn a mapping between different image domains without paired training data. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Show, Attend, and Translate (SAT) that incorporates self-regularization and attention mechanisms into generative adversarial networks (GANs) for unsupervised image translation. The proposed approach not only improves the artistic quality of the generated images, but also achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods on various benchmark datasets. Furthermore, we also investigate the task of adapting SAT to new domains with limited training data, and propose adaptation models that enable effective transfer learning. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach and adaptation models in achieving high-quality and diverse image translations, which have promising applications in computational modeling, task analysis, and other related fields.

In this paper, we describe a method for representing a behavioral dynamical system as a Generalized Synchronization Tree (GST). The method of representation we propose is analogous to the “unrolling” of a Labeled Transition System (LTS) into a bisimilar Synchronization Tree (ST). Thus, for behavioral systems endowed with state maps, we are able to establish conditions under which bisimilar behavioral systems result in bisimilar GST representations and conversely. Preservation of bisimulation equivalence is critical to future study of composition operators for behavioral systems and GSTs. Additionally, we define a composition operator for GSTs constructed from behavioral systems, and prove a congruence result for strong bisimulation.

In today's social media, especially twitter is very important for the success and destruction of one's image due to the many sentences of opinion that can compete the users. Examples of phrases that mean evil refer to hate speech to others. Evil perspectives can be categorized in hate speech, which hate speech is regulated in Article 28 of the ITE Law. Not a few people who intentionally and unintentionally oppose a social media that contains hate speech. Unfortunately, social media do not have the ability to aggregate information about an existing conversation into a conclusion. One way to draw conclusions from aggregation results is to use text mining. In this Final Project to classify whether the text in the sentence contains elements of hate speech or not. The author hopes in this final project can make how to classify element of hate speech in text by computer, which later speech of hate can be recognized. By using an Artificial Neural Network method optimized with Backpropagation algorithm. The author hopes after this application the computer can know and classify the existence of hate speech on a text from social media twitter. From the results of tests that have been done the average precision of 80.664%, recall 90.07%, and Accuracy of 89.47%.

As we saw in the previous chapters, we learn from games—how to play them and almost certainly other skills as well. We can also develop algorithms that learn to play games. But let's turn this statement around. Can games learn from us? And if so, what could they learn? Can we develop algorithms that use our interactions with games to learn about us?

Successful solution of the problem of digital transformation of the national economy will require a large-scale restructuring, and in some cases, and reengineering, business processes of most organizations of the industrial sector, the introduction of new approaches to the formation and development of infrastructure support of production. One of the fundamental factors for solving this problem is the availability of highly qualified specialists with a set of professional competencies not only in highly specialized areas, but also capable of applying interdisciplinary knowledge at the intersection of technical, economic, managerial and humanitarian training. Training of such specialists requires revision of existing educational programs and approaches to their implementation, including the introduction of distance learning technologies, modernization of laboratory facilities, strengthening the practical orientation of the educational process.

The paper presents a method for representing the instruction set truth tables of microprocessors with High-Level Decision Diagrams (HLDD). A behavior level fault model is defined for the microprocessor control parts on the basis of instruction level truth tables (TT). Two methods are proposed for creating HLDDs from TTs with minimization of the edges on graphs: greedy algorithm, and branch and bound algorithm (B&B). A simple and fast computable lower bound is proposed to be used for pruning the search space of the B&B algorithm. Experimental data of using the fault model for several microprocessors and comparison data are provided to show the efficiency of the proposed high-level fault model over the gate-level Stuck-at-Fault (SAF) model.

The relational database service in cloud usually achieves energy efficiency by using virtualization technology, in which it consolidates multiple independent database systems into a single physical machine while enforcing the hardware-level isolation among them. However, the disk I/O performance is inevitably hurt due to the resource contention on the shared device. We propose VMSQL, a novel disk I/O model for the virtualized relational database management system (RDBMS). VMSQL has two innovations over the original disk model of virtualized database systems. First, VMSQL enforces the synchronous operation in guest operating system to handle with the transaction commitment. Due to its simplicity, a portion of CPU cycles is decoupled from I/O buffer management and then used to serve the upcoming requests, thereby improving their response times. Second, in host system, VMSQL asynchronizes the storage path of transactions which are committed from the different co-located guest databases. An obvious advantage of this procedure is that systems can apply host-level improvements into the disk I/O performance of virtualized RDBMS, relieving the random I/O and enhancing the throughput of whole system. We implement a prototype of this Sync-Async model in QEMU-KVM hypervisor, in which the InnoDB engine is deployed in the guest operating system. Extensive experiments are conducted to verify its advantages and the results are positive without any loss of ACID-compliance. In the meanwhile, VMSQL incurs moderate overhead at the hypervisor layer.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the development of predictive models for traffic flow prediction. In particular, autoregressive processes and computational modeling techniques have been widely used in this domain. However, these models often suffer from the limitation of not effectively capturing the influence of temporal information on traffic flow patterns. To address this issue, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have been proposed as a powerful approach for modeling time-series data. Among RNNs, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has been shown to be effective in capturing temporal dependencies in various applications. In this paper, we propose a novel neural network model called T-LSTM, which is an LSTM enhanced by temporal information for traffic flow prediction. Our experimental results demonstrate that T-LSTM outperforms several state-of-the-art models in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness. This model can benefit a wide range of applications such as data models, market research, and more.

The paper explores the utilization of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) cells, which belong to the family of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), for mapping Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) dialogs and analyzing their security. The proposed method leverages machine learning algorithms, specifically anomaly detection, to identify abnormal behavior in SIP dialogs. The study highlights the importance of securing servers that use SIP for communication, given the significance of SIP in modern communication standards. The implementation and evaluation of the proposed approach are discussed, demonstrating the effectiveness and feasibility of the LSTM-based approach for SIP dialog analysis and security. Finally, the paper concludes by offering potential future extensions and applications of the proposed method.

In recent years, nonvolatile memory has become an increasingly critical component of computing systems. One promising nonvolatile memory technology is Spin-Orbit Torque MRAM, which has shown potential for low-power and high-density applications. Binary Neural Networks (BNNs) are another area of research that has the potential to revolutionize computing systems. PXNOR-BNN is a novel concept that combines the advantages of Spin-Orbit Torque MRAM and BNNs. The PXNOR-BNNs perform preset-XNOR operations, enabling efficient Convolution Neural Network (CNN) computation without requiring conventional multiplication operations. This leads to significant improvements in memory management and power consumption. This paper provides an overview of this promising technology, highlighting its potential impact on computing systems.

Unknown input estimation have a major importance in real-time monitoring, diagnosis and fault-tolerance control. Consequently, this paper concentrates on state estimation for nonlinear system where a part of its inputs is unknown. In particular, the problem is oriented towards an experiential application for laboratory three tank system affected by actuator faults. Our objective is to perform the fault detection (FE) by the synthesis and the implementation of the unknown input observer (UIO). Simulation and experimental results confirm the performance of the suggested observer.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has started to make a real impact with many IoT-based services in agriculture, smart farming, smart cities, personal health, and critical infrastructures. Sensor/IoT devices form one of the indispensable elements in these IoT systems and services. An effective IoT system requires the interoperability among its heterogeneous physical devices, but this presents a significant challenge regarding various communication protocols, networking management policies, as well as data processing approaches. Software-defined paradigm is considered essential for managing and provisioning IoT services on demand. An emerging solution is the application of software-defined networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) in programming WSN/IoT systems. However, these technologies cannot be directly deployed due to the differences in the functionality of SDN network devices and sensor/IoT devices as well as the limitation of resources in IoT devices. We proposed the software-defined IoT(SD-IoT) model in our earlier work. This paper focuses on the S-MANAGE protocol that enables an SD-IoT controller to control and manage sensor/IoT devices via their virtual representation, called software-defined virtual sensors (SDVS). The paper presents in detail the design and the implementation of the S-MANAGE southbound protocol.

Mobile crowd sensing is emerging as a new paradigm for collecting and analyzing large-scale sensor data. However, the efficiency of task allocation poses a significant challenge to its widespread adoption. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an efficient task allocation approach based on evolutionary computing. The proposed approach leverages task analysis to identify tasks that are suitable for crowd sensing and assigns these tasks to available sensors based on resource management. The genetic algorithms are used to optimize the allocation of tasks to sensors while ensuring data integrity. The allocation approach is designed to support different types of smart devices and is tested on a simulated platform. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves significant efficiency gains in task allocation for the mobile crowd sensing systems. Specifically, the approach reduces the time required for task allocation, improves sensor utilization, and enhances the overall system performance. The proposed approach has the potential to enable the widespread adoption of mobile crowd sensing in various domains such as environmental monitoring, urban planning, and transportation.

This work proposes a sensor fault isolation scheme for co-existence of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) current sensor and non-sensor imbalance faults. The proposed method examines DC link battery current residuals to determine the location of machine current sensor and non-sensor imbalance faults. Power conservation evaluation, phase current signals estimation and sensor information recovery are performed in the proposed method to derive DC link battery current residuals which reflect different features of various fault scenarios for fault isolation. The proposed scheme is capable of isolating complicated fault scenario of a machine current sensor fault and a non-sensor imbalance fault co-existence, which is a challenging issue in PMSM and is not well addressed in existing literature. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is confirmed by simulation results in MATLAB for a PMSM under both phase current sensor fault and non-sensor phase imbalance fault.

In the last years, spammers have taken advantage of the popularity of electronic media to spread undesired text messages. These may cause direct and indirect damages, such as dissatisfaction and exposure of users to misleading information and malicious content that can result in significant financial losses. Automatic filtering short text messages is a challenging problem nowadays because labeled datasets generally contain few instances and messages may have an insufficient amount of terms to be classified. In addition, the messages are rife with abbreviations, slang, and misspelled words making it difficult to generate a good computational representation. In this study, we propose an automatic data augmentation technique to increase the number of labeled instances and to improve the quality of the computational representation of short and noise text messages. We also proposed an ensemble approach to combine the predictions obtained by the classifiers using the messages generated by this technique. Experiments with three text representation techniques demonstrated that the ensemble approach improves the results obtained in the detection of undesired short text messages when the number of training instances is small.

This paper presents a machine-learning-based approach for predicting diffraction loss variation caused by the human body. The study focuses on the diffraction phenomenon in wireless communication and explores ways to accurately measure loss in a frequency-dependent manner. The proposed method involves using machine learning and biological system modeling to predict variations in diffraction loss. The approach is validated through a series of antenna measurements and training experiments. The results show that the machine-learning-based method is effective in predicting diffraction loss variation and could potentially be used to improve wireless communication performance in complex scenarios involving the human body. Overall, this study highlights the significant role that machine learning can play in predicting and modeling complex biological systems.

In recent years, significant progress has been made in the field of speech synthesis through the application of deep neural network techniques. This study focuses on Dungan speech synthesis, utilizing hidden Markov models and neural networks in the training process to improve the accuracy and naturalness of synthesized speech. Acoustic and context modeling are also employed to better capture the nuances of Dungan speech. Data models are developed to account for the unique characteristics of the Dungan language, leading to more effective synthesis. This research highlights the potential of deep neural network techniques in the field of speech synthesis and provides important insights into improving the accuracy and naturalness of synthesized speech in a specific language context.

This paper considers utility optimal power control for energy-harvesting wireless devices with a finite capacity battery. The distribution information of the underlying wireless environment and harvestable energy is unknown, and only outdated system state information is known at the device controller. This scenario shares similarity with Lyapunov opportunistic optimization and online learning but is different from both. By a novel combination of Zinkevich's online gradient learning technique and the drift-plus-penalty technique from Lyapunov opportunistic optimization, this paper proposes a learning-aided algorithm that achieves utility within O(ϵ) of the optimal, for any desired ϵ > 0, by using a battery with an O(1/ϵ) capacity. The proposed algorithm has low complexity and makes power investment decisions based on system history, without requiring knowledge of the system state or its probability distribution.

Gaussian frequency shift keying (GFSK)is a digital modulation scheme with both attractive spectra and high power efficiencies. Modulation schemes with these characteristics often require a maximum likelihood sequence estimator (MLSE)implemented by means of Viterbi Algorithm (VA). The main drawback of VA is complexity implementation due to the filter bank needed to calculate the metrics, the large number of states required to describe the signal and the employment of squaring and multiplication operations in calculating metric cost. This paper discusses alternative metrics for VA in GFSK schemes that avoids the use of multiplication and squaring operations, achieving a reduction in implementation complexity. Moreover, the tradeoff between complexity and performance (in terms of bit error rate, BER)for the proposed metrics is shown under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN).

With the increasing popularity of robots, the need for efficient data sharing in multi-layered wireless robotic networks has become a critical issue. This paper proposes a new approach called Multi-Channel Utilization to address this challenge. The proposed approach utilizes the capabilities of edge computing and wireless LAN to create a reliable and efficient multi-channel communication system. By utilizing multiple channels, the proposed approach can reduce data transmission delays and improve the overall network performance. Additionally, multiple servers are deployed to further optimize data sharing and ensure the robustness of the system. The proposed approach is evaluated using two different monitoring scenarios, and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing approaches in terms of delay, packet loss, and network utilization. Overall, this paper provides a new and effective solution for local data sharing in multi-layered wireless robotic networks.

Industrial communication systems represent one of the most important innovations of the last decades in the context of factory and process automation systems. They are networks specifically designed to cope with the tight requirements of these challenging application fields such as real time, determinism, and reliability. Moreover, industrial networks are often deployed in environments characterized by strong electromagnetic interference, mechanical stress, critical temperature, and humidity. Over the last three decades, different classes of industrial networks have been developed according to changing requirements and available communication and information technologies. In this paper, we first provide an account of the state of the art, reviewing classical fieldbuses, real-time Ethernet networks, and industrial wireless networks, along with their most relevant features, applications, and performance figures. We introduce the complex standardization framework and analyze the market status and assumptions for future development. In the second part, we address the future perspectives focusing on new technologies, standards, and fields of application. In particular, we consider the time-sensitive networking (TSN) family of standards, Industrial Internet-of-Things (IIoT) systems, high-performance wireless LANs, industrial applications of cellular networks, and Ethernet networks for automotive communication.

The smart monitoring system (SMS) vision relies on the use of ICT to efficiently manage and maximize the utility of network infrastructures and services in order to improve the quality of service and network performance. Many aspects of SMS projects are dynamic data driven application system where data from sensors monitoring the system state are used to drive computations that in turn can dynamically adapt and improve the monitoring process as the complex system evolves. In this context, a research and development of new paradigm of Distributed Big Data Driven Framework (DBDF) for monitoring data in mobile network infrastructures entails the ability to dynamically incorporate more accurate information for network monitoring and controlling purposes through obtaining real-time measurements from the base stations, user demands and claims, and other sensors (for weather conditions, etc.). The proposed framework consists of network probes, data parsing application, Message-Oriented Middleware, real-time and offline data models, Big Data storage and Decision layers., and Other data sources. Each Big Data layer might be implemented using comparative analysis of the most effective Big Data solutions. In addition, as a proof of concept, the roaming users detection model was created based on Apache Spark application. The model filters streaming protocols data, deserializes it into Json format and finally sends it to Kafka application. The experiments with the model demonstrated and acknowledged the capacities of the Apache Spark in building foundation for Big Data hub as a basic application for online mobile network data processing.

This paper aims to estimate the time derivative of the horizontal geomagnetic component in Malaysia during a quiet period for the assessment of geomagnetically induced currents (GIC). The study focuses on the magnetosphere and the effects of storms on GIC, as well as the correlation between observed data and the utilization of data mining techniques. By examining data collected from observatories in Malaysia, this paper looks at the impact of electric fields on the conductivity of the surrounding regions. The results of this study could have significant implications for GIC assessments in Malaysia during quiet periods, and could potentially inform the development of effective mitigation strategies.

Computation offloading is an effective way to address the limited resources of mobile handsets and the demands of cloud computing. In this paper, we propose a cost solving model for the computation offloading decision algorithm. We perform a task analysis and evaluate the performance of the algorithm in terms of energy consumption and bandwidth. We also consider the limitations of batteries in mobile handsets. The proposed model takes into account the costs associated with computation offloading and provides an optimal solution based on different parameters. Our experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the energy consumption while improving the system performance. The model can be applied to various scenarios to optimize the computation offloading decision algorithm in a cost-effective manner.

Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed the way physical layer devices are being monitored and controlled. However, IoT networks are vulnerable to malicious attacks, which can lead to catastrophic consequences. The use of authentication schemes in IoT networks has become indispensable to ensure security and privacy of data communication. In this paper, we propose a light-weight authentication scheme for Air Force IoT networks, which uses sensors for data communication and surveillance. The proposed scheme offers robust security against various attacks, including impersonation, replay, and man-in-the-middle attacks. We evaluate the proposed scheme on different parameters such as security, overhead, and energy consumption. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme not only provides high security but also has low overhead and energy consumption, making it practical for Air Force IoT networks. Overall, the proposed authentication scheme can enhance the security and privacy of Air Force IoT networks, making it suitable for critical and sensitive applications.

This paper explores the use of deep learning based beamforming neural networks in downlink MISO systems with the intention of improving signal processing. Specifically, the paper discusses the use of neural networks as a means of minimizing delays in the downlink process through the use of iterative optimization methods. By optimizing the beamforming weights, the neural networks aim to improve the overall performance of the downlink system. The paper also touches on the importance of minimizing delays in the downlink system and discusses various techniques for achieving this optimization. Ultimately, the study concludes that deep learning based beamforming neural networks can significantly improve downlink MISO systems and that their potential applications are numerous.

In order to realize the differentiation and refinement management of power users, the paper proposes a power user load classification method based on k-means and FSVM. The method takes the power use daily load curve index as the original sample, extracts the typical industry category by k-means clustering algorithm, combines the FSVM classification algorithm to train and test the samples of the known industry labels, and obtains the FSVM classification model of power user load. The simulation experiments show that the power user load classification model implemented by this method has higher classification accuracy and can effectively identify users in unknown industries.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are widely used in various fields, and localization is a critical part of WSNs. In this research, we propose a multi-objective three-dimensional DV-Hop localization algorithm with NSGA-II for WSNs. The proposed algorithm is based on the popular DV-Hop algorithm but with the enhancement of a three-dimensional display. The algorithm considers multiple objectives, including minimizing localization error and maximizing energy efficiency. The NSGA-II algorithm is applied to optimize these objectives by using the solid modeling concept. The proposed algorithm is compared with existing localization algorithms, and the results show that it has better estimation accuracy and requires less energy. The genetic algorithm approach used in this algorithm enables the selection of optimal sensor placement which reduces the localization error. In summary, the proposed algorithm provides a more efficient and accurate solution to the localization problem in WSNs, thereby improving the performance and reliability of the overall system.

This paper proposes an Attacker Behavior-Based Metric for Security Monitoring, specifically applied to Darknet Analysis. The metric considers the semantics of IP networks to capture and analyze the behavior of potential attackers. In doing so, it allows for monitoring the security of these networks and detecting any suspicious or malicious activity. The proposed metric can be applied to various security monitoring scenarios, including those involving extraterrestrial measurements, and can be particularly useful in identifying and mitigating threats before they cause any damage. Moreover, the study suggests that this metric can be further enhanced by incorporating data from telescopes for a more comprehensive and accurate analysis. Ultimately, the Attacker Behavior-Based Metric for Security Monitoring has the potential to significantly improve the effectiveness of security monitoring systems and prevent potential cyber-attacks.

Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has obtained growing attention during the past years. For this purpose, various methods have been proposed. Feature extraction is the major part of SER methods and aims to attain effective emotional features from speech signal. One of the most important features in speech processing task is Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). The vocal production mechanisms of speakers at different emotional states can improve the discrimination abilities of the aforementioned features for SER task. This work aims to propose a novel feature extraction scheme for SER task that integrates this particular information through the decomposition of emotional speech spectra and providing an improved spectral representation of various emotions. By employing this scheme, two novel procedures are represented. In the first procedures, cepstral-like features are obtained by a filter bank which is computed by Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) technique on emotional speech spectra. In the second procedures, the activation coefficients of NMF technique which are achieved by decomposition of speech spectrums, are considered as the new features. Finally, to increase the discrimination abilities of features among emotion classes, each of the feature vectors is normalized to its mean value. According to experiments on Emo-DB database, fusion of the proposed features with MFCCs outperforms the performance of an SER system compared with conventional MFCC as the baseline or the simple unsupervised NMF-based features derived from the speech spectra.

Cognitive radio (CR) systems have to be able to detect the presence of a primary user (PU) signal by sensing the spectrum area of interest. Due to radiowave propagation effects like fading and shadowing, spectrum sensing is often complicated, because the PU signal can be attenuated in a particular area. In this paper, we explore a distributed spectrum sensing approach that exploits the largest eigenvalue of correlation matrices (CMs) that are adaptively estimated, based on the combine and adapt least (CTA) type of diffusion method with no fusion center (FC). More specifically, CR nodes exchange also observations with a subset of neighbouring nodes and combine the neighbouring observations based on the locally estimated signal to noise ratio (SNR) values. We analyse the resulting detection performance and verify the theoretical findings through simulations.

We present a 77 GHz cooperative radar system, which uses two standalone FMCW radar sensors for vector velocity and positioning measurements. The system is based on a decentralized signal processing approach, where sampled data from only one sensor is used for full 2-dimensional localization and velocity measurement of a target. The information is also used for direction-of-movement (DOM) estimation. Frequency and phase calibration for the bistatic beat responses is accomplished by using a known reference target and corresponding signal processing algorithms. Measurement results show the applicability of the proposed system for target tracking, localization and 2-dimensional velocity measurements. The average deviation for DOM estimation is better than 1.1 degree and an average velocity error of approximately one percent is achieved.

With the growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), massively connected devices are exposed to cyber-attacks and are becoming active as bots. To protect IoT devices efficiently from increasing threats, in addition to honeypot-based approaches, we need to gain more complete understanding of IoT botnets and potential victims including purposes of attacks and events which they are participating in. In this paper, we propose a two-step subspace clustering method to cluster botnets and clarify their types (functionalities). For each target host, the proposed method separates features into several subspaces and generates a sub-label in each subspace to represent partial characteristic (e.g., low-size flows or high TCP-SYN rate). Major combinations of sub-labels presents different partial characteristic, and the proposed method classify bots and interprets the whole behaviors for each bot group. In the evaluation, we reveal the scale and variety of botnets in the wild through two real-world datasets.

Cloud computing has recently gained significant attention because of the emergence of new internet-based applications which utilize cloud computing infrastructure in the data centers (DCs). Therefore, Internet traffic and traffic generated within a data center has also increased exponentially. Traditional data center networks, which are based on the electrical switches, are not adequate to handle increasing bandwidth demands of these applications. They are also not power efficient. A new optical switch architecture, based on optical switches, for data centers is presented in this paper. Optical switches are more power efficient and they can support larger bandwidths. The proposed architecture, namely, extended-hybrid optical switch architecture (E-HOSA), relies on software defined network (SDN) networking paradigm. Similar to SDN, E-HOSA has a separate control plane and a data plane. We perform analytical modelling of E-HOSA to evaluate its cost and power consumption. The comparative analysis of E-HOSA is performed with other famous electrical / optical networks for data centers. The results have shown significant improvement in power consumption as compared to other networks on the cost of increased capital expenditures (CAPEX). However, this increased CAPEX is mitigated to some extent due to its increased power efficiency. We also perform scalability analysis of E-HOSA. The analysis shows that E-HOSA is scalable to thousands of servers which is suitable for a very large scale data center.

In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised transfer learning model that utilizes genetic algorithm to optimize transformation and novel label transfer mechanism. The model is applied to robot sensing systems, and can improve the training accuracy with limited labeled data by transferring knowledge from a related domain. Our method uses a kernel function to transform the data, and the parameters of the kernel function are optimized by genetic algorithms. We also introduce a novel label transfer mechanism that takes into account the probability distribution of unlabeled data to improve the accuracy of transfer learning. The cost function is designed to integrate both labeled and unlabeled data, and a probabilistic logic is used to propagate the labeled data to the unlabeled data. The experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms traditional transfer learning methods in terms of accuracy and convergence speed.

It is expected that a highly-safe intelligent system which makes risk avoidance in the real-world environment where human lives. In order to detect dangerous situations, it is indispensable to accurately recognize risk events from the input image information, i.e., high-accuracy scene recognition. In this paper, it is clarified that the high-accuracy scene recognition can be achieved by combination of the convolution neural network which extracts the feature of an input image and the support vector machine for classification. In the scene recognition of a single danger event, it is not possible to recognize multiple event occurrences (multi-class classification). We propose a method to realize multi-class classification without decreasing the recognition accuracy by selectively using an individual classifier generated for each event.

This paper investigates the existence of the optimal step-stress accelerated life test under progressive type-I censoring. The study focuses on the stress level and life estimation in reliability engineering. The loading conditions and the use of linear programming techniques are considered to optimize the test designs. The acceleration factor is also taken into account as an important parameter in this study. The results of this research are useful in developing efficient experimental plans for accelerated life tests in the field of reliability engineering.

Based on the analysis of the fault characteristics of the inverter interfaced distributed generation under PQ control and the influence of the distributed generation access on the traditional protection technology, an active distribution network protection scheme considering the capability of regional measurement is proposed. The protection scheme based on the direction of zone current is proposed for the region with enough capability of measurement. The distribution network is divided into zones, and the fault zone is judged by collecting the fault component of current at breakers. As for the region with poor capability of measurement, an reclosing scheme coordinated with DG re-grid timing is proposed. The proposed scheme effectively solves the influence of distributed generation access on traditional protection and reclosing of distribution network. The simulation results of the examples in PSCAD/EMTDC prove the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

This paper presents a method for Cross-Spectral Image Dehaze through a Dense Stacked Conditional GAN Based Approach. Atmospheric modeling is used to simulate the haze in images and Gallium nitride based LEDs are employed to capture the images in multiple spectral regions. Image color analysis is performed to determine the degree of haze in the images. Generative adversarial networks are utilized to accelerate the dehazing process. The proposed method uses a dense stacked generator network to effectively remove haze from images. The training procedure is optimized to reduce the loss and improve the quality of the dehazed images. Experiments show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of image quality metrics. The proposed method can be used in a variety of applications, such as autonomous driving, aerial photography, and surveillance.

This paper presents a method for guiding interceptor missiles using deep learning techniques. The proposed approach uses atmospheric modeling and trajectory analysis to optimize missile trajectories and increase the chances of a successful interception. Deep learning algorithms, such as artificial neural networks, are used to train predictive models that can accurately predict the movement of incoming missiles. The training process involves feeding the algorithm with large amounts of missile trajectory data to enable it to make accurate predictions. The proposed method has the potential to enhance the performance of interceptor missiles and improve their overall efficiency. Further research is needed to evaluate its effectiveness in practical applications.

In this paper, we explore the application of ensemble methods to model the power consumption of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) used in cellular communications. Specifically, we investigate the efficacy of the bagging technique in training predictive models for UAV power consumption. This research combines methods from sociology, statistics, and machine learning to develop a robust learning system. We employ different training datasets to analyze the influence of the bagging method on predictive accuracy. Our results suggest that the bagging approach can effectively enhance predictive performance, especially when the training datasets suffer from high variance or bias. Our work contributes to the field of UAV power modeling and demonstrates the potential of ensemble methods in developing stable and accurate predictive models.

This paper proposes a novel approach for enabling adaptive intelligence in cloud-augmented multiple robots systems. The increasing complexity of robotic systems calls for more advanced and flexible approaches to task analysis, deep learning, and adaptation models. By leveraging the power of cloud computing and servers, we can provide robots with the computational modeling capabilities they need to better perform their tasks in dynamic environments. The proposed system includes a distributed architecture that allows robots to communicate with each other and access cloud resources on-demand, enabling real-time adaptation and decision-making. The system's adaptation models learn from the robots' behaviors and adjust their operation accordingly, leading to increased efficiency and effectiveness. The proposed approach has the potential to greatly enhance the capabilities of multiple robots systems and pave the way for future advances in robotics technology.

This paper presents a dynamic estimation method for model parameters of in-pipe walking robots. Legged locomotion has been proven effective for traversing uneven surfaces, and can be particularly useful in navigating pipes for inspection or maintenance. However, accurately estimating the robot's position and orientation in 3D space is a challenge due to the robot's complex geometry and limited sensory data. The proposed method uses robot sensing systems to obtain input data, and applies estimation algorithms to improve the accuracy of the robot's kinematic and mathematical models. The results of experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the robot's performance in terms of stability, motion accuracy, and control precision. Overall, the dynamic estimation approach presented in this paper provides a promising solution for improving the functionality of in-pipe walking robots.

The Coach Ing model, applied to professionals in the engineering field, continues to be enriched through training experiments. After a careful evaluation of the results of the Coach-Ing path [1], this paper shows the results of a further experimentation performed in SAPIENZA - University of Rome. The experimentation was focused on the identification of a numerical evaluation technique of the skill level acquired by the students participating in the program. This was achieved through the guided validation of the set of 16 reference skills defined by the Coach-Ing model. During the training process a double level activity was carried out: on the one hand, the participants were taught about the possible working scenarios to which they could orientate themselves and, at the same time, assessed the personal strategies - observation and evaluation of the 16 parameters - more coherent to effectively propose itself in different working contexts. Further two steps (a unconventional final exam and a follow-up on the interview) integrated the students' training path and at the same time enriched the Coach-ing model with further reference indicators with communicative-relational indicators. The results of the complete experimentation confirm that the Coach-Ing model has excellent performances as a methodological lever within the training path. Moreover, the use of Mentor-Ing techniques allows to accompany the participants in the consolidation of the acquired skills.

Auscultation of heart sounds is usually used as an important way to identify symptoms of heart disease. In this case the experts need to concentrate on diagnosing heart sound abnormalities in humans. Finding various characteristics to classify heart sounds according to the group is a very important part. This research was made to improve the results based on previous research which still had an accuracy rate of 92%. Heart collection obtained from the Michigan Sound Heart Database. Data used only on the apex. The Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) method is used to extract heart sound features, while for classification from the results of heart sound extraction using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method. Based on the results of this study, the accuracy reaches 100%.

Monolithic 3D (M3D) integration offers significant performance, power, and area benefits. However, the design of a reliable M3D power-delivery network (PDN) is challenging due to high power density and current demand per unit area. We propose a framework to design a reliable PDN for M3D ICs using accurate electrical and reliability models. We leverage genetic programming to explore the design space to optimize the PDN for M3D. We also analyze power-supply noise (PSN) during scan-based testing and compare it with that observed during functional operation. We quantify the impact of PSN during scan-based testing on yield loss. Our results show that the PDN obtained using the proposed approach significantly increases the reliability of at least 40% of the wire segments in the PDN. In addition, the proposed PDN design reduces the worst-case power-supply droop by 50.5% compared to a baseline PDN. The yield loss due to power-supply droop for the proposed design is also significantly lower compared to the baseline.

In metropolitan areas, common traffic issues include traffic congestion, traffic accidents, air pollution, and energy consumption occur. To resolve this issues, Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) have been evolved by many researchers. One of the important sub-systems in the development of ITS is a Traffic Management System (TMS) which attempts to reduce a traffic congestion. In fact, TMS itself relies on the estimation of traffic flow, therefore providing such an accurate traffic flow prediction is needed. For this reason, we aim to provide an accurate traffic flow prediction to facilitate this system. In this works, a Supervised Deep Learning Based Traffic Flow Prediction (SDLTFP) was proposed which is a type of fully-connected deep neural network (FC-DNN). Timely prediction is also a major issue in guaranteeing reliable traffic flow prediction. However, training a deep network could be time-consuming, and overfitting is might be happening, especially when feeding small data into the deep architecture. The network is learned perfectly during the training, but in testing with the new data, it could fail to generalize the model. We adopt the Batch Normalization (BN) and Dropout techniques to help the network training. SGD and momentum are carried out to update the weight. We then take advantage of open data as historical traffic data which are then used to predict future traffic flow with the proposed method and model above. Experiments show that the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for our traffic flow prediction is within 5 % using sample data and between 15% to 20% using out of the sample data. Training a deep network faster with BN and Dropout reduces the overfitting.

This paper focuses on the development of a multimodal profiling tool for digital job analysis and matching of requirements competences frameworks. The tool is intended to be used in the field of information and communication technology (ICT), and will aid in the training and evaluation of individuals seeking to work in the digital job market. The project is being developed in accordance with existing standards and regulations within Europe. This includes the creation of a taxonomy for the tool, which will enable the classification and organization of various competences and skills. Overall, this engineering solution will serve as a powerful asset to those seeking to improve their skills and qualifications in the ever-evolving world of digital technology.

This work presents a simulation environment for embedded control systems that are designed to leverage the processing power of multi-core processors. The simulation environment enables designers to assess the performance of their systems on a variety of processing architectures before implementation. The proposed simulation environment has particular relevance to the emerging field of the Internet of Things (IoT), as it allows designers to optimize their designs for low-power consumption and enhanced connectivity. Additionally, the simulation environment has potential applications in the areas of green computing and social computing, where energy efficiency and social interactions are critical factors. Finally, the proposed simulation environment could be leveraged to explore the use of blockchain technology in embedded systems, as blockchain is being recognized as a potentially transformative technology in the field of information technology. Overall, this work presents a valuable contribution to the field of embedded systems and provides a useful toolset for designers of multi-core processors.

Nowadays, the application of pattern recognition methods in power systems protection and control is becoming more and more prevalent. The pattern recognition methods are widely used owing to their high precision and speed in signal processing algorithms. In this paper, we discuss the use of pattern recognition methods in the context of power system protection and control, focusing on correlation, task analysis, and training. Specifically, we delve into the use of artificial neural networks in the protective relaying, which involves monitoring and controlling power systems. By leveraging artificial intelligence, we can optimize the protective relaying by accurately detecting faults and reducing the probability of a blackout occurring. Our analysis shows that the combination of task analysis and artificial neural networks for power system protection can improve the accuracy of fault detection and reduce the cost of system operation. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future directions of applying pattern recognition methods to the field of power systems.

This paper proposes a novel spectrum sharing based cognitive UAV network system which adopts optimal beamwidth allocation for efficient communication. The system aims to enhance mission planning and execution for UAVs by intelligently leveraging available spectrum resources. The system uses handwriting recognition technique which involves the use of feature extraction, task analysis, training, data mining, character recognition and writing.
