This is implemented by utilizing cognitive UAV networks to extract data from the environment with advanced sensing capabilities, which are then used to identify and track handwriting by drones. The optimal beamwidth allocation strategy has been used to optimize spectrum sharing to ensure efficient and secure communication. The proposed system has shown promising results in terms of improved accuracy rates for handwriting recognition and better resource utilization, which makes it a viable solution for efficient cognitive UAV network systems.

We offer a microservice-oriented multi-agent approach for solving computationally complex problems arising in the course of scientific and applied research in some subject areas. The computational experiments specificity of a considered class of problems is stipulated by the exponential increasing runtime due to increasing dimension, multivariate calculations of the different input data of the problem, as well as the variability of a mathematical model and algorithm for solving the problem. The use of microservices provides reusability, ease of updating the components of a distributed application and its cross-platform and allows operating with modularity properties in new conditions of distributed computing when inter-module communication is provided only through the message passing mechanism. The designed software platform for the offered approach automatizes both the development of a distributed microservice application based on an applied program package and the organization of decentralized management of microservices composition. New mechanisms for deploying and updating microservices support the synchronization of cloud knowledge bases and one installed on a user's computer, providing an additional opportunity using Dew computing paradigm that combines the concept of Cloud computing with the capabilities of the user's local computers. The practice of scientific computational experiments has shown the effectiveness and convenient in the usage of the offered approach.

This work proposes an intelligent bearing fault diagnosis system using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in deep learning to achieve the abnormal identification of bearing vibration. In this system, the convolutional kernel in CNN can automatically extract the features of input signals and no human feature extraction and other data pre-processing are required. As a result, comparing to the traditional signal processing methods, this work has the advantages of automated end-to-end, high-accuracy and intelligent machine troubleshooting in vibration fault diagnosis of bearings.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep face recognition, a rapidly growing area of research in computer vision. The focus of the survey lies in reviewing the recent advances in face recognition accomplished through the use of deep neural networks. The paper starts by introducing the basics of face recognition and its challenges. It then discusses the different techniques used for face detection and feature extraction, highlighting the most popular approaches in deep learning. The survey further outlines the various types of deep neural networks used to train face recognition systems, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, and siamese networks. The paper concludes by providing insights into the current state of the art and future directions of deep face recognition research.

This paper proposes a novel approach of Fuzzy Stochastic Petri Net with Uncertain Kinetic Parameters for Modeling Tumor-Immune System. The proposed model is designed based on Kinetic theory and Mathematical model, and serves as a Computational modeling tool for simulating the dynamics of the complex biological system through incorporating the essential elements such as Tumors and Immune system. The model takes into account the Uncertainty associated with the kinetic parameters, which is a common phenomenon in biological system modeling. The proposed approach provides an efficient framework for exploring the intricate interactions of Tumor-Immune system and gaining deeper insights into the underlying mechanisms of the disease progression, thus aiding in the development of effective treatment strategies. Overall, this approach offers a promising avenue for advancing the field of computational biology and has the potential to contribute to the better understanding and management of cancer.

This research paper proposes a Context-Aware Co-attention Neural Network for Service Recommendations to enhance the accuracy of recommender systems. The authors employ feature extraction and context modeling to develop a two-layer co-attention mechanism that is incorporated into the neural network model. This mechanism is designed to extract and highlight the most informative features of the users and services to improve recommendations. The study involves computational modeling, and the results show the improved performance of the proposed model compared to the state-of-the-art models. The authors also provide a task analysis of the proposed model and recommend its use in real-world settings. This research aims to contribute to the development of efficient recommender systems that can dynamically adapt to the users' context and provide more accurate recommendations.

In this paper, we propose a no-reference video quality estimation approach based on machine learning for passive gaming video streaming applications. With the increasing popularity of streaming media, measuring quality assessment has become a crucial task. However, the traditional methods heavily rely on video recording, which is inconvenient and time-consuming. Instead, we focus on estimating the quality of experience (QoE) of passive gaming videos without relying on any reference. To do so, we adopt machine learning techniques to extract features from the input videos and build a regression model to estimate QoE. Experimental results show that our method achieves high accuracy in estimating QoE and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of efficiency and effectiveness. Our approach has great potential for practical applications in passive gaming video streaming, making quality assessment more convenient and accurate at the same time.

The Control of Useless Interests Flooding in Vehicular Named Data Networks (CUIF) is a proposed method for managing the flow of data within vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) on roads. VANETs are a type of ad hoc network where vehicles communicate directly with each other through the dedicated short-range communication (DSRC) protocol, allowing for efficient sharing of information in real-time. However, the decentralized nature of VANETs and their interconnection with the Internet and IP networks present significant security challenges. The CUIF proposes a set of protocols and strategies to combat issues such as useless interest flooding, where excessive queries for data can consume network bandwidth and degrade performance. By utilizing servers and applying security measures, CUIF aims to optimize the flow of data in VANETs, facilitating communication between vehicles and improving overall network efficiency.

As next generation networking, 5G technology promises to revolutionize the way we connect and communicate. However, the efficient management of wireless resources remains a major challenge for 5G networks, requiring practical and innovative solutions. Blockchain and artificial intelligence techniques present promising avenues to address these challenges, and in particular, the coupling of deep reinforcement learning with blockchain technology holds the potential to empower intelligent 5G networks beyond current capabilities. By leveraging the power of these two technologies, 5G networks can be optimized to better manage resource allocation, improve network scalability, and enhance overall performance. Additionally, deep reinforcement learning can enable dynamic and automated network management, allowing 5G networks to adapt to changing conditions and requirements. Ultimately, the integration of blockchain and deep reinforcement learning in the design of 5G networks presents exciting opportunities for the further development of computer architecture and resource management techniques in wireless networking.

Targeted marketing strategies use market segmentation for insight into the heterogeneity of the customer purchase lifecycle, but this often ignores the evolution of customer behavior over time causing retailers focus on unprofitable customers. By pairing the Recency, Frequency, Monetary scores with the Customer Lifetime Value model to segment customers of a medium-sized clothing and fashion accessory retailer in Kuwait. A modified regression algorithm investigates the customer purchase curve gaining knowledge from point-of-sales data to help the retailer make informed decisions. Clustering is by K-means and by Expectation Maximization. Cluster quality analysis reveals the former outperforms the latter to discover and suggest relevant market segments and appropriate marketing strategies.

Current harmonics generated by Adjustable Speed Drives (ASDs) due to the use of power electronics devices are one of the main power quality concerns in distribution networks. These harmonics affect the grid quality and lead to power losses in the grid. Therefore, different harmonic mitigation strategies using active front end had been proposed to tackle this issue. However, due to the cost effectiveness, conventional front end such as Diode Rectifier is still recommended in industries for a broad range of three phase power electronics systems. Thus, in this paper, a new grid harmonic elimination approach is proposed using three-phase diode rectifier with controlled DC link current (boost converter). Simulation results validates the proposed concept that a selective harmonic can be eliminated from the grid using the developed strategy.

The emerging technology of Blockchain has shown a great potential in enhancing the security and reliability of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs). However, the implementation of Blockchain in VANETs faces unique challenges in terms of mobility of vehicles and lack of dedicated infrastructure. This paper explores the impacts of mobility on the performance of Blockchain in VANETs, focusing on peer-to-peer computing, roads, security, and unmanned aerial vehicles. The study provides insights into the feasibility of using Blockchain for VANETs and highlights the need for additional research to overcome the challenges and further improve the performance of this technology. Ultimately, the findings of this research can contribute to the development of more efficient and secure VANET systems to support the growing demands of modern transportation.

In-band full-duplex wireless communication systems have received considerable attention because of their potential to double the capacity of existing wireless networks. However, one of the biggest challenges in achieving this goal is the residual self-interference (RSI) which occurs when the transmitted signal leaks into the receiving antenna. To address this problem, interference cancellation and channel estimation techniques have been proposed. In addition, radio frequency (RF) impairments such as phase noise can further degrade the performance of these systems. In this paper, the authors investigate the distribution of the RSI power in in-band full-duplex wireless systems. They propose a Monte Carlo method to model the RSI power distribution and analyze the impact of phase noise on the system performance. The simulation results show that the proposed method accurately captures the behavior of the RSI power distribution and can be used for evaluating the performance of in-band full-duplex wireless systems under different RF impairments. This work has important implications for the design and optimization of future wireless communication systems.

Segmented Autoencoders for Unsupervised Embedded Hyperspectral Band Selection is a research paper focused on feature extraction from hyperspectral imaging data using deep learning techniques. The authors propose a method for unsupervised band selection through image reconstruction using segmented autoencoders. Mutual information is utilized for measuring the relevance of each band in the hyperspectral image, and autoencoders are used for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction. The proposed method is compared to existing methods using real hyperspectral datasets, and the results show that the segmented autoencoders approach outperforms other methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research demonstrates the potential of deep learning techniques in hyperspectral image processing, and can be useful in various applications such as vegetation monitoring, mineral exploration, and object detection.

This paper discusses the performance study and enhancement of access barring for massive machine-type communications in 3GPP. With the increasing number of connected devices in the Internet of Things, access control mechanisms must be able to handle a large number of devices. Several proposals have been made for access barring, but their performance needs to be analyzed to ensure optimal use. The study focuses on analyzing the delays and switches that occur during message exchange and estimates the effect of these parameters on performance. The proposed enhancements aim to reduce the delays and switches and improve access barring performance. Overall, this study provides insight into the efficient use of access control mechanisms for massive machine-type communications.

This paper proposes a model-based concept for real-time operating system (RTOS) portability, which aims to facilitate the development and deployment of RTOS-based systems across different computer architectures and hardware platforms. The kernel plays a central role in this concept, acting as an intermediary layer between the hardware and the higher-level software components. The proposed model considers both hardware and task analysis factors, taking into account the specific characteristics of the target platform and the requirements of the intended application. This approach enables the design of efficient and flexible RTOS-based systems, which can adapt to different contexts and support diverse functionalities. The proposed model is particularly relevant in the context of the Internet of Things (IoT), where interoperability and portability are crucial aspects. Overall, this paper contributes to the development of innovative RTOS-based solutions that can meet the requirements of a dynamic and heterogeneous computing environment.

This paper presents a research study on the overall framework of cloud support platform for electricity trading. Power markets are facing challenges in terms of accommodating new electricity generation sources, intermittent renewable energy sources, and rising energy demands. In order to meet these challenges, new computer architectures and distributed databases are required. Cloud computing offers a scalable and cost-efficient solution for realizing a cloud support platform that can handle large volumes of data and numerous transactions. Security is also an important consideration for cloud support platform, and measures should be taken to ensure secure data storage and transmission. Finally, software architecture is critical in achieving an efficient and effective cloud support platform that can streamline electricity trading and improve power markets' operation. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the infrastructure and key features of a cloud support platform for electricity trading that can address the challenges facing power markets.

In order to improve the accuracy and efficiency of tunnel geological-type prediction, a data-driven framework based on TBM operating data is proposed in this paper. The framework utilizes various indexes and real-time systems to collect and analyze data and applies neural networks and predictive models to generate predictions. The geological factors are classified into several types, and the corresponding indexes and monitoring meters are selected accordingly. The framework is tested on practical tunnel projects, and the results show that it can significantly improve the accuracy of geological-type prediction and provide valuable guidance for tunnel construction. The proposed framework has a wide range of applications and provides a new approach for tunnel geological-type prediction.

Objective: Powered assistive devices need improved control intuitiveness to enhance their clinical adoption. Therefore, the intent of individuals should be identified and the device movement should adhere to it. Skeletal muscles contract synergistically to produce defined lower limb movements, so unique contraction patterns in lower extremity musculature may provide a means of device joint control. Ultrasound (US) imaging enables direct measurement of the local deformation of muscle segments. Hence, the objective of this study was to assess the feasibility of using US to estimate human lower limb movements. Methods: A novel algorithm was developed to calculate US features of the rectus femoris muscle during a non-weight-bearing knee flexion/extension experiment by nine able-bodied subjects. Five US features of the skeletal muscle tissue were studied, namely thickness, angle between aponeuroses, pennation angle, fascicle length, and echogenicity. A multiscale ridge filter was utilized to extract the structures in the image and a random sample consensus (RANSAC) model was used to segment muscle aponeuroses and fascicles. A localization scheme further guided RANSAC to enable tracking in a US image sequence. Gaussian process regression models were trained using segmented features to estimate both knee joint angle and angular velocity. Results: The proposed segmentation-estimation approach could estimate knee joint angle and angular velocity with an average root mean square error value of 7.45° and 0.262 rad/s, respectively. The average processing rate was 3-6 frames/s that is promising toward real-time implementation. Conclusion: Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of using US to estimate human lower extremity motion. The ability of the algorithm to work in real time may enable the use of US as a neural interface for lower limb applications. Significance: Intuitive intent recognition of human lower extremity movements using wearable US imaging may enable volitional assistive device control and enhance locomotor outcomes for those with mobility impairments.

This research explores the application of selected Artificial Intelligence (AI) models to reconstruct the noise levels at thoroughfares during a specific year. The study focuses on data models, training, regression tree analysis, computational modeling, vegetation, and noise levels. The research primarily aims to determine the effectiveness of AI models in reconstructing noise levels and identify the relevant factors affecting noise levels at thoroughfares. The study utilizes regression tree analysis to identify the main variables that contribute to noise levels. It also uses computational modeling to generate predictions and identify the potential effects of vegetation on reducing noise levels. Overall, the application of AI models in reconstructing noise levels is relevant to urban planning and environmental management, particularly in identifying effective strategies to reduce noise pollution. The findings of this research can potentially contribute to enhancing the quality of life of individuals living in urban areas.

In non-contact heart rate (HR) monitoring via Doppler radar, the disturbance from respiration and/or body motion is treated as a key problem on the estimation of HR. This paper proposes a blind source separation (BSS) approach to mitigate the noise effect in the received radar signal, and incorporates the sparse spectrum reconstruction to achieve a high-resolution of heartbeat spectrum. The proposed BSS decomposes the spectrogram of mixture signal into original sources, including heartbeat, using non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) algorithms, through learning the complete basis spectra (BS) by a hierarchical clustering. In particular, to exploit the temporal sparsity of heartbeat component, two variants of NMF algorithms with sparseness constraints are applied as well, namely sparse NMF and weighted sparse NMF. Compared with usual BSS, our proposed BSS has three advantages: 1) clustering-induced unsupervised manner; 2) compact demixing architecture; and 3) merely requiring single-channel input data. In addition, the HR estimation method using our proposal delivers more satisfactory precision and robustness over other existing methods, which is demonstrated through the measurements of distinguishing people's activities, gaining both smallest absolute errors of HR estimation for sitting still and typewriting.

The regression method proposed in this paper determines a regression function for noisy inputs. We represent noisy inputs by using noise and latent noise-free constituent of the noisy input. Given an observed noisy input, the proposed method estimates the posterior of the latent noise-free constituent of it, and represents the posterior using the noise distribution. For the value of the regression function for the noisy input, the method produces the expected value of the Nadaraya-Watson estimator for noiseless inputs, which is constructed from a training dataset consisting of noiseless explanatory values and the corresponding objective values. In addition, a probabilistic generative model is presented for estimating the noise distribution. This enables us to determine the noise distribution parametrically from a single noisy input, using the distribution of the noise-free constituent of the noisy input estimated from the training dataset as a prior. Experiments conducted using artificial and real datasets show that the proposed method suppresses the overfitting of the regression function for noisy inputs and that the root mean squared errors of the predictions are smaller compared with those of an existing method.

With the impact of disasters in developing countries,this study looks into how disaster response needs and processes can be modelled to help decision makers in the Philippines. This research examines how humanitarian needs are defined given disaster-related data, existing literature, best practices by developed countries and organizational bodies. Relevant disaster response processes are identified in order to address these humanitarian requirements. A design science research methodology is used in creating a decision metamodel of these disaster response processes and humanitarian needs. Disaster data from a leading non-governmental organization for disaster response is used as a baseline. Two cycles are done using design science. A final evaluation with a prototype dashboard is done to validate the disaster response model.

Deep learning neural networks have revolutionized the field of artificial intelligence, but their performance is limited by the traditional activation circuits used in these networks. This paper proposes a novel memristive activation circuit that can improve the efficiency and accuracy of deep learning neural networks by using memristors as the basic building blocks. Memristors are electronic devices with a memory effect that can store resistance values, and their behavior is similar to the neurons in biological neural networks. The proposed circuit architecture can be used to train neural networks by adjusting the threshold voltage and resistance values of memristors, which can effectively adjust the intensity of signals and enable them to pass through the network layers. Experiment results demonstrate that the proposed memristive activation circuit can reduce the computational complexity of deep neural networks and improve their accuracy. This innovative circuit architecture provides a promising method for developing highly efficient and effective neural networks, which can have significant practical applications in various fields.

By sensing wirelessly the radio propagation environment and analyzing the channel state information (CSI), one can extend human senses beyond our traditional reach and enrich the insight into the surrounding environment and activities, with or without line-of-sight. On one hand, different indoor activities bring distinctive perturbations to wireless radio propagations. On the other hand, thanks to the nature of multipaths, indoor environmental information is contained and embedded in the wireless CSI. Since the occurrence of an indoor event lasts for a certain period of duration and repeats a similar transition pattern among different realizations, information is embedded not only in each instantaneous CSI sample, but also in how CSI changes along time, e.g., the CSI time series. Inspired by that, this paper proposes an indoor monitoring system that monitors the occurrence of different indoor events in real time with commercial WiFi devices, by exploiting the temporal information embedded in the CSI time series. Through extensive experiments, this paper studies the robustness of the proposed system to variabilities in event instances and human motion interference, and its long-term performance in a one-month test.

This paper presents the development of a Minimum Interference Leakage (MIL) based Interference Aligned Network (IAN) in the presence of jammers. The proposed network addresses the challenges posed by interference and jamming in wireless networks. By utilizing energy harvesting techniques, the network enhances the reliability of the system and minimizes interference. The MIL approach is used to find the optimal path between receivers, in order to further improve the effectiveness of the network. The IAN is designed to align the interference signals, thus reducing the effect of jamming on the network. This approach provides a robust and efficient solution for wireless networks in the presence of jamming and interference signals. The proposed network implementation is evaluated through simulation experiments, which demonstrate significant improvements in network performance over existing methods. The results indicate that the MIL based IAN can improve the network's reliability and reduce interference to a great extent in radio frequency communication systems.

Coordinated head-neck movement is a challenge for patients with neurological disorders, such as cerebral palsy and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Neck collars are commonly used to stabilize the head-neck in these patients. These collars are mostly rigid and uncomfortable to wear for extended periods of time. We have developed a robotic neck brace to assist head-neck motion. In this letter, we focus on using the robotic neck brace for training of the head-neck motion using forces applied on the head. A force controller is implemented to deliver a moment to correct the head motion in an `assist-as-needed' fashion. A human study was designed to assess the performance of the robotic neck brace with the force controller. Ten young healthy adults participated in the experiment. They were asked to perform a lateral bending motion in the coronal plane of the head-neck with and without the assistance of the brace. The motions were conducted under two conditions: i) with visual feedback, ii) with visual and force feedback. We found that the rotational movement errors were significantly reduced (p<; 0.05) during training with the force field when compared to visual feedback alone. As expected, this change was not retained during post-training. We conclude that the force controller is able to provide the desirable force assistance to help coordinate the head motion.

Cloud computing provides organizations with computing resources featuring easy deployment, connectivity, configuration and scalability. Multi-tenancy permits cloud providers to establish collaborative relationships among cloud users, especially at the storage service level. To satisfy security requirements among collaborating tenants, each tenant may define a set of access control policies to secure access to its shared data. However, tenants may enforce their policies using heterogeneous access control models (e.g RBAC and ABAC), which may be difficult to manage by cloud providers. Hence, There is a need of a cloud system that acts as an intermediary access control model in order to resolve the heterogeneous structure of other models. This paper presents a novel unified access control model for heterogeneous multi-tenancy architectures in the cloud environment. This model, called XBAC, can manage heterogeneous access control policies. The proposed model uses a learning automata to represent access policies and requests. XBAC is integrated in the cloud environment using a cloud broker. In addition, the paper defines a basic architecture that defines the interaction between the main components of heterogeneous cloud systems. Initial simulation results show that the proposed model meets the requirements of the heterogeneous access models environment, by preventing access of unauthorized users to the resources of multi-tenancy cloud services.

Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation with a co-prime linear array, composed of two uniform linear arrays with inter-element spacing larger than half-wavelength of incoming signals, has been investigated a lot thanks to its high-resolution performance. For better computational efficiency, one class of methods treat the co-prime linear array as two sparse uniform linear subarrays. From each of them, high-precision but ambiguous DOA estimation is obtained, and the ambiguities are eliminated according to the co-prime property. However, the existing methods of this kind suffer from the insufficient reliability and high complexity. In this paper, the potential problems associated with the DOA estimation with two co-prime subarrays are discussed, and a reliable and efficient DOA estimation method is proposed. For each subarray, the true DOAs are treated as their equivalent angles and the pair matching of them is accomplished by exploring the cross-correlations between the equivalent signals associated with the equivalent angles. Compared with other existing methods, the proposed method is able to achieve a better estimation performance in all situations, in terms of accuracy and complexity.

This paper presents a novel approach for estimating the path of a spinning magnet marker using hyperbolic functions on a smartphone platform. The proposed mathematical model uses magnetic resonance principles and incorporates a new approach to estimate short-range distance measurements made using magnetic sensors. With the increasing pervasiveness of computing power in smartphones, this approach shows great potential for improving the accuracy of path estimation for a variety of applications, such as navigation systems, autonomous vehicles, and virtual reality simulations. The proposed method was evaluated using spinning magnets attached to belts, and the results showed promising accuracy compared to existing methods. Hence, this approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of path estimation by improving localization accuracy in indoor and outdoor environments.

This paper investigates creativity of students in the context of engineering education. The main goal is to get new insights on how to motivate engineering students to express more creativity in solving their assignments. The research included a crowdvoting contest on a sample of was 28 students in the area of information technologies at Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade. Results point out that a crowdvoting competition can be used to induce students' creativity in engineering education. Additionally, we discuss how students creativity styles relate to the design of creative-based educational tasks.

This paper presents a novel M2M (machine-to-machine) learning environment for electric applications that incorporates blockchain technology. Blockchain is a decentralized, distributed ledger system that provides secure and transparent data storage and transmission capabilities. Proof of work is used to validate transactions within the blockchain, ensuring that they are genuine and are not the result of fraudulent activities. The M2M learning environment uses databases to store and retrieve data, allowing for seamless integration with existing data systems. The use of blockchain and M2M learning environments in electric applications has the potential to revolutionize the industry by enabling better monitoring and analysis of energy usage, which can ultimately improve efficiency and reduce costs. The influence of internet of things on this environment is also discussed, as IoT devices play a crucial role in creating a comprehensive and interconnected system. The economics behind the adoption of blockchain technology in electric applications are evaluated and the implications for the industry are explored. The paper concludes with a call for continued research in this promising area.

In multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems that employ pilot-symbol aided channel estimation, the pilot-to-data power ratio (PDPR) has a large impact on the system performance. In this paper, we consider the problem of setting the PDPR in multi-cell MU-MIMO systems in the presence of channel estimation errors, intercell interference and pilot contamination. To analyze and address this problem, we first develop a model of the multi-cell MU-MIMO system and derive a closed-form expression for the mean squared error of the uplink received data symbols. Building on this result, we then propose two decentralized PDPR-setting algorithms based on game theoretic approaches that are applicable in multi-cell systems. We find that both algorithms converge to a Nash equilibrium and provide performance improvements over systems that do not properly set the PDPR, while they maintain different levels of fairness.

This paper proposes a Security Framework for IoT Cloud Services, which addresses security concerns related to the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing. The proposed framework includes four main components: training, monitoring, feature extraction, and computer architecture. The training component focuses on educating and training users about potential security risks and best practices for IoT devices and cloud services. The monitoring component involves continuous monitoring of IoT devices and cloud services to detect any suspicious behavior. The feature extraction component helps identify relevant security features from the collected data, while the computer architecture component optimizes the resources and performance of the security framework. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive approach to address security concerns and enhance the overall security of IoT and cloud services. Further research is needed to test and validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in real-world scenarios.

With the rapid development of the Internet, more and more users expressed their views on the Internet. Therefore, the big data of texts are generated on the Internet. In the era of big data, mining the sentiment tendencies contained in massive texts on the Internet through natural language processing technology has become an important way of public opinion supervision. In this paper, the sensitive information topics-based sentiment analysis method for big data is proposed. This method integrates topic semantic information into text representation through a neural network model. The attention mechanism is introduced into the neural network, and context-aware vector is introduced to calculate the weight of each word. In addition, in order to make the model more adaptable, the method of sentiment dictionary tagging is used to obtain the training data. The experimental results show that the proposed model can effectively improve the accuracy of sentiment analysis results.

Scientific workflows are complex computational tasks involving a large number of interdependent tasks. Scheduling these workflows on cloud environments presents several challenges, including data transfer delays, processor scheduling and load balancing. In this paper, we propose a task duplication approach to scheduling scientific workflows on clouds. We first perform task analysis to identify critical tasks and their relationships. We then generate schedules based on the duplication of critical tasks to ensure timely execution while reducing the impact of data transfer delays. Finally, we evaluate our proposed approach and compare it with existing workflow scheduling methods on various case studies. The results show that our approach significantly reduces the execution time of scientific workflows on clouds, while improving resource utilization and minimizing delays. Overall, the proposed task duplication approach offers a promising solution for optimizing scientific workflow scheduling on cloud environments.

Computer Tomography (CT) is the gold standard technique for brain damage evaluation after acute Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). It allows identification of most lesion types and determines the need of surgical or alternative therapeutic procedures. However, the traditional approach for lesion classification is restricted to visual image inspection. In this work, we characterize and predict TBI lesions by using CT-derived radiomics descriptors. Relevant shape, intensity and texture biomarkers characterizing the different lesions are isolated and a lesion predictive model is built by using Partial Least Squares. On a dataset containing 155 scans (105 train, 50 test) the methodology achieved 89.7% accuracy over the unseen data. When a model was built using only texture features, a 88.2% accuracy was obtained. Our results suggest that selected radiomics descriptors could play a key role in brain injury prediction. Besides, the proposed methodology is close to reproduce radiologists lesion labelling. These results open new possibilities for radiomics-inspired brain lesion detection, segmentation and prediction.

This paper proposes a modified state-queuing model for optimizing the control parameters of thermostatically controlled loads. The model is used to aggregate and analyze data from switches and analytical and computational models of linear systems. The proposed model offers an optimization procedure that enables the selection of control parameters in order to minimize energy consumption while maintaining thermal comfort levels. The method's feasibility is demonstrated through experimental results. The results show that the modified state-queuing model provides a feasible means of optimizing control parameters of thermostatically controlled loads. These findings could have broad implications for the development of more energy-efficient HVAC and building systems.

With the development of cloud server, reversible data hiding in encrypted domain has received widespread attention for management of encrypted media. Most of existing reversible data hiding methods are based on stream ciphers, which are mainly concerned with data storage security. While homomorphic ciphers focus on data processing security, which is popular in cloud and other third-party platforms. Reversible data hiding with homomorphic cryptography has been an active topic in the research filed. In this paper, we propose a new lossless data hiding method based on homomorphic cryptosystem. After a content owner generates encrypted media with homomorphic ciphers, a data hider embeds secret data by establishing a mapping between secret bits and losslessly modifying encrypted media. At the receiver side, the embedded data is extracted from encrypted domain with a little auxiliary message. And original media is recovered by directly decrypting marked encrypted media. During the embedding process, the modification of encrypted media does not change the corresponding original media owing to homomorphic and probabilistic properties. Thus, no distortion is introduced in the whole procedures of data embedding. And directly decrypted media containing embedded data is the same as the original media. Meanwhile, the proposed method achieves a high embedding rate through efficient mapping and skillful use of expanded pixel values. The experimental results show that compared with state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method has higher embedding rate without distortion.

Embedded systems are used in various applications such as medical devices, automobiles, and communication systems. However, these systems are prone to attacks and external threats which can lead to system malfunctioning. Anomaly detection is a key approach to detect such threats in real-time systems. This paper proposes a Hierarchical Attention-based Anomaly Detection Model for Embedded Operating Systems. The proposed model incorporates feature extraction, kernel and data models to enhance the performance of anomaly detection. The hierarchical approach leverages attention mechanisms to model complex relationships between features, to better detect anomalies. The proposed model is evaluated on datasets collected from real-world embedded systems, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness over existing state-of-the-art methods. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to detect anomalies in embedded operating systems in real-time, which can help enhance the security and reliability of these systems.

In the Internet of Things and smart environments data, collected from distributed sensors, is typically stored and processed by a central middleware. This allows applications to query the data they need for providing further services. However, centralization of data causes several privacy threats: The middleware becomes a third party which has to be trusted, linkage and correlation of data from different context becomes possible and data subject lose control over their data.Hence, other approaches than centralized processing should be considered. Here, Secure Multiparty Computation is a promising candidate for secure and privacy-preserving computation happening close to the sources of the data.In order to make SMC fit for application in these contexts, we extend SMC to act as a service: We provide elements which allow third parties to query computed data from a group of peers performing SMC. Furthermore, we establish fine-granular access control on the level of individual data queries, yielding data protection of the computed results. By adding measures to inform data sources about requests and the usage of their data, we show how a fully privacy-preserving service can be built on the foundation of SMC.

Despite the emergence of many soft-bodied robotic systems, model-based feedback control for soft robots has remained an open challenge. This is largely due to the intrinsic difficulties in designing controllers for systems with infinite dimensions. This work extends our previously proposed formulation for the dynamics of a soft robot from two to three dimensions. The formulation connects the soft robot's dynamic behavior to a rigid-bodied robot with parallel elastic actuation. The matching between the two systems is exact under the hypothesis of Piecewise Constant Curvature. Based on this connection, we introduce a control architecture with the aim of achieving accurate curvature and bending control. This controller accounts for the natural softness of the system moving in three dimensions, and for the dynamic forces acting on the system. The controller is validated in a realistic simulation, together with a kinematic inversion algorithm. The paper also introduces a soft robot capable of three-dimensional motion, that we use to experimentally validate our control strategy.

Global utilities deploy smart meters as foundation for smart grids and smart cities, thereby providing more energy options and choices for customers to save energy. Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) deployment involves business process review, technology evaluation, system and network design, customer engagement, workforce management and technology applications. CLP Power Hong Kong Limited (CLP) will upgrade all conventional meters of residential, and small and medium business customers to smart meters starting from end 2018. This paper aims to describe the deployment and technical challenges when developing a full roll-out AMI deployment programme.

This case study evaluated the performance of OnPrem and Azure SQL Server in cloud computing environments. Performance metrics were measured on databases and servers, taking into consideration various computer architectures. Testing was conducted using Microsoft Windows, with results indicating that Azure SQL Server outperformed OnPrem in most cases. The study concludes that the use of cloud computing can significantly improve database server performance, providing a viable solution for businesses looking to improve their publishing capabilities. Overall, the study highlights the importance of considering cloud computing as a viable solution for businesses looking to improve their database server performance.

Efficient path calculation scheme is a critical task in resource management for hierarchical optical path networks, which consist of multiple layers of optical switches and fiber networks. In this study, we propose a novel approach to represent the state of optical switches using continuous variables, which can significantly reduce the computational complexity of path calculation. We also develop a heuristic algorithm to efficiently explore the network topology and find optimal paths for advance reservation requests. Our simulation results show that the proposed scheme can achieve significant improvement in terms of path setup time and resource utilization compared with existing methods. This study provides a promising solution to advance reservation and resource management in hierarchical optical path networks, which can facilitate the development of future optical communication systems.

This paper attempts to investigate novel Text-to-Speech algorithm based on Deep voice which is an attention based, fully convolutional mechanism. The procedure of producing speech synthesis involves with learning statistical model of the human vocal production mechanism which is eligible of taking some text and vocalize that as speech. This paper would reveal the route of the attempt where there is the destination of accuracy and realism. Serenity and fluency are the most important qualities which expect from a TTS. The idea is to give an outline of discourse amalgamation in the Sinhala language, compresses and replicates about the characteristics of different blend procedures utilized. The proposed TTS synthesizing with the neural network based approach to perform phonetic-to-acoustic mapping has described by the purpose of applying for multilingual synthesizers.

We propose a 2D Encoder-Decoder based deep learning architecture for semantic segmentation, that incorporates anatomical priors by imitating the encoder component of an autoencoder in latent space. The autoencoder is additionally enhanced by means of hierarchical features, extracted by an UNet module. Our suggested architecture is trained in an end-to-end manner and is evaluated on the example of pelvic bone segmentation in MRI. A comparison to the standard U-Net architecture shows promising improvements.

As genome sequencing continues to become more cost-effective and affordable, more raw and aligned genomic files are expected to be generated in future years. In addition, due to the increase in the throughput of sequencing machines, the size of these files is significantly growing. In particular, aligned files (e.g., SAM/BAM) are used for further processing of the data, and hence efficient representation of these files is a pressing need. In this work we present AliCo, a new compression method tailored to the aligned data represented in the SAM format. We demonstrate through simulations on existing datasets that AliCo outperforms in compression ratio, on average, the state-of-the-art compressors for SAM files, achieving more than 85% reduction in size when operating in its lossless mode. AliCo also supports a variety of modes for lossy compression of the quality scores, including for the first time the recently proposed lossy compressor CALQ, which uses information from the aligned reads to adjust the level of quantization for each location of the genome (achieving more than 10× compression gains in high-coverage datasets). AliCo also supports optional compression of the reference sequence used for compression, hence guaranteeing exact reconstruction of the compressed data. Finally, AliCo allows to stream the data as it is being compressed, as well as to decompress the data as it is being received, potentially providing significant time savings. AliCo can be accessed at: https://github.com/iochoa/alico.

A physically unclonable function (PUF) is a circuit of which the input-output behavior is designed to be sensitive to the random variations of its manufacturing process. This building block hence facilitates the authentication of any given device in a population of identically laid-out silicon chips, similar to the biometric authentication of a human. The focus and novelty of this paper is the development of efficient impersonation attacks on the following five Arbiter PUF-based authentication protocols: 1) the so-called Poly PUF protocol of Konigsmark et al. as published in the IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems in 2016; 2) the so-called OB-PUF protocol of Gao et al. as presented at the IEEE Conference PerCom 2016; 3) the so-called RPUF protocol of Ye et al. as presented at the IEEE Conference AsianHOST 2016; 4) the so-called LHS-PUF protocol of Idriss and Bayoumi as presented at the IEEE Conference RFID-TA 2017; and 5) the so-called PUF-FSM protocol of Gao et al. as published in the IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems in 2018. The common flaw of all five designs is that the use of lightweight obfuscation logic provides insufficient protection against machine-learning attacks.

This paper presents a novel approach to control an autonomous wind-battery based microgrid using natural genetics adapted control (NGAC) methodology. The proposed method employs genetic algorithms to optimize the PI controller parameters of the battery and wind turbine converters, and also optimizes the ON/OFF status of the switches for maximum efficiency. Microgrid operation in standalone mode requires an effective management of power conversion and control of the battery as the primary energy source. NGAC methodology is a highly effective control strategy for microgrids with unpredictable and intermittent energy sources. The experimental results show that the proposed approach can enhance the performance of the microgrid by improving its voltage and frequency stability, and reducing the fluctuations of the renewable energy sources. Furthermore, the proposed method outperforms the other existing control strategies reported in the literature. Therefore, the proposed approach can be considered as a promising solution for the effective management of renewable energy-based microgrids.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become an indispensable tool for image classification. However, existing learning methods often suffer from overfitting to the training data, which leads to poor generalization performance. To address this problem, we propose a novel feature correlation loss (FCL) for CNNs, which encourages the correlation between feature maps to be maximized during training. By considering the correlation among different feature maps, the proposed FCL can effectively guide the optimization process and make the learned representations more discriminative. Moreover, we show that FCL can be interpreted as a variant of principal component analysis (PCA), and hence can be easily integrated into existing CNN pipelines. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FCL can significantly improve the convergence speed and achieve state-of-the-art performance for image classification tasks.

This paper proposes an enhanced brain-inspired model for face categorization using mutual information maximization. The approach utilizes computational modeling techniques and feature extraction methods such as Gabor filters, as well as brain modeling principles, to create a system capable of accurately categorizing faces. The proposed model also incorporates visualization techniques to facilitate understanding of the face categorization process. Additionally, the concept of entropy is employed to maximize the mutual information between the extracted features and the categories. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in accurately categorizing faces with high accuracy. The enhanced brain-inspired model holds promise for advanced face categorization applications, and can potentially be extended to other areas of computer vision and machine learning.

This paper proposes a 3D model-based approach for estimating the trajectory of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using object detection and databases. The method employs Kalman filters and covariance matrices to estimate the position and orientation of the UAV in real time. The system uses solid modeling techniques to create a detailed 3D model of the UAV, which is used as a reference for tracking. The proposed approach can estimate the position and orientation of the UAV with high accuracy and is robust to changes in the environment. The study presents experimental results that demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in UAV tracking applications. This new approach will contribute to the advancement of the UAV tracking technology and will have practical applications in various fields like military or civilian purposes, such as emergency response, surveillance, and transportation.

This paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the tracking methodology using kernelized correlation filter. The methodology utilizes convolution and correlation operations to track the target object in a video sequence. The kernel plays a crucial role in determining the similarity between the target and the candidate regions. The paper also discusses the feature extraction process and its implications on the tracking performance. The proposed visualization approach enhances the interpretability of the tracking results, improving the user's understanding. The experiments conducted by the authors manifest the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in various scenarios. Overall, this paper serves as a guideline for utilizing kernelized correlation filter in target tracking applications.

In the transportation industry, the proper selection of taxi drivers is vital to maintain the quality and reliability of services offered to customers. To address this issue, social network analysis models have been developed and utilized for the pair selection of appropriate taxi drivers. These models utilize the principles of social network services, allowing for the identification of key drivers who possess essential knowledge and skills for delivering quality services. Furthermore, knowledge engineering techniques are also used to develop algorithms for data mining and analysis, allowing for the identification and selection of suitable drivers based on their abilities and performance. Such models have been implemented in various companies offering public transportation services and have provided remarkable benefits in the selection of skilled and experienced taxi drivers. Overall, incorporating social network analysis and knowledge engineering techniques in the pair selection of appropriate taxi drivers leads to the enhancement of public transportation services and ensures that the high standards of quality and reliability are maintained in the automobile transportation industry.

In this paper we address the problem of Community Question Answering (CQA) for Arabic language. We mainly explore the direction of combining both lexical and semantic features for enhancing the retrieval task of possible answers to a posted question. We show a comprehensive evaluation on the SEMEval2017 CQA dataset for Arabic language. Our Mean Average Precision (MAP) achieves 62.85% when using a supervised machine learning approach (linear SVM). We outperformed best reported results on such dataset. This is achieved by defining a mix of word embedding, latent semantic similarity features and other lexical similarity features.

The purpose of the investigation presented in this paper is to obtain the optimal restructure of radial distribution system under the impact of contingencies, with and without the scope of distributed generation. Firstly, solution to occurrence of contingency is proposed by finding out the best switching sequence of a specified number of tie lines and sectionalizes with an objective to improve the continuity of power flow in radial system. Secondly genetic algorithm (GA) has been used to find the optimal location and size of embedded distribution generation (DG), to improve voltage profile and to reduce losses for given load demand. The outcome of the proposed study is illustrated through simulations of loaded 69-bus radial distribution system. The obtained results suggest that the investment is distribution generation is attractive when reconfiguration is used to minimize load curtailment.

Anomaly detection is a crucial task in Cyber-Physical Production Systems (CPPS) to ensure the security and stability of production systems. The identification of decision boundaries is one of the most challenging aspects of anomaly detection. The shape of the decision boundary is highly dependent on the data models and machine learning algorithms used for anomaly detection. Probabilistic logic is often employed to identify anomalies in CPPS. Dimensionality reduction techniques are also incorporated to reduce the computational complexity of anomaly detection. Overall, the identification of decision boundaries for anomaly detection in CPPS is a complex task that requires careful consideration of data models, machine learning algorithms, probabilistic logic, and dimensionality reduction techniques.

In recent years, stem cell research has become increasingly important due to its potential applications in regenerative medicine. A key aspect of this research is the use of computational modeling to understand stem cell behavior and guide the production of desired cell types. The issue of robustness in stem cell production is particularly relevant, as it determines the reproducibility and reliability of stem cell therapies. To address this issue, researchers have utilized spatial-temporal pattern synthesis in a network of locally interacting cells. Through this approach, it has been possible to achieve greater control over stem cell differentiation and production, while also gaining insights into the underlying biology of these processes. In addition to its applications in stem cell research, this approach has also been used in fields as diverse as sociology, statistics, and support vector machines, highlighting its versatility and potential for future research. Overall, spatial-temporal pattern synthesis represents a promising methodology for advancing the field of stem cell research and unlocking its full potential.

In wireless sensor networks (WSN), data gathering is a critical issue due to the limited energy and communication capabilities of the nodes. Compressive sensing has emerged as a promising technique to reduce the amount of data transmission by encoding and compressing the data at the source. Additionally, embedding techniques have been proposed to provide security and privacy in data transmission. In this paper, we propose a novel privacy-preserving data gathering scheme in WSN based on a combination of compressive sensing and embedding. The proposed scheme uses matching pursuit algorithms for encoding the data and cryptography-based embedding techniques to ensure privacy in the transmission. The simulations results show that the proposed scheme outperforms existing data gathering schemes in terms of energy consumption, delay, and privacy preservation. Our proposed scheme is a significant contribution to the WSN community, as it addresses the data gathering challenges while preserving the privacy of data transmission.

This paper proposes a Deep Learning-Based Constellation Optimization approach for Physical Network Coding in Two-way Relay Networks. The goal is to improve the performance of demodulation and reduce the system complexity while maintaining high reliability. In order to achieve this, the authors introduce entropy as a measure of the optimization objective and utilize deep learning algorithms to search for the optimal constellation designs. Different protocols are explored and evaluated, and the results show that the proposed approach outperforms other methods in both bit error rate and computational complexity. This research contributes to the field of network coding in relay networks by providing a promising direction for constellation optimization through deep learning techniques.

The concept of the smart city has been created in response to the increasing numbers of people living in cities. Just as the development of technology has evolved rapidly, smart life has also emerged. The goal of the smart city is one day to enable all affairs of daily life to be completed with the single touch of a finger through cutting-edge technology. New and innovative information must be applied effectively to the industry. With the industrial revolution, propelled by the Internet of Things (IoT), big data and the cloud platform have birthed the “smart city,” integrating the IoT and the cloud through mobile devices and applying technology to fields like logistics, finance, healthcare, recreation, surveillance, and traffic transportation, thus providing people with greater well-being and convenience. Following the era of the big data knowledge economy, the IoT has become an important pillar of national economic development. The IoT is expected to provide substantial support for continued and sustainable development of the smart city. Therefore, effective use of the IoT has become an important topic in smart city development. The purpose of this paper is to build a conceptual framework of service innovation, relying on the smart city case of Taiwan. Based on a literature review, in-depth interviews, and case interviews, the proposed conceptual framework of IoT is rooted in the market, policy, and technical aspects. It incorporates eight steps: composition of the project team, service idea generation, service idea screening, development concept selection, design and development, service testing, commercialization, and service quality, to generate new service value and thereby create customer satisfaction. In fact, the IoT is designed to support the smart city vision; thus, this paper describes the various innovation modes of the smart city. Furthermore, the paper presents and discusses the technical solutions and best-practice guidelines adopted in the Taiwan Smart City project. Finally, it discusses the meaning and future research direction of the smart city through the use of the IoT. With wave after wave of digital development civilizing the city's evolution and with the phenomenon of Internet access through mobile phones for each person, the smart city of human factors is clearly coming.

The length of an inverted L shaped antenna (ILA) which is three-quarters of the wavelength is studied. The ILA is placed on metallic objects or human bodies. The desired direction of radiation is at right angles to the objects. The gain in this direction without matching loss is enhanced, where the antenna is bent at a point that is approximately a quarter of wavelength from the feeding point. Because the current vector reverses near this bending point, the offsetting of current vectors is avoided and the combined current vector of this bent antenna is longer than that of the unbent antenna and that of the one quarter of wavelength ILA. As a result, the gain of the optimized three-quarters of wavelength ILA is enhanced.

This work presents a K-NN feature matching for monocular visual odometry (VO) system that can perform in realtime. By feeding a monocular video sequence, the proposed method continuously determines the instantaneous 6-DOF camera pose. After obtaining binary descriptors for image features, we adopt k-nearest neighbor algorithm with Hamming distance calculation as a novel method for feature matching. Then, with our designed robust motion estimation, the system can operate in real-time scenario for a large-scale outdoor environment without utilizing GPU or reducing input image size. The experimental result shows a successfully built trajectory path without non-linear optimization and loop closure for a challenging video sequences of KITTI dataset. Moreover, the comparison in terms of root mean square error with ORB-SLAM and Semidirect Visual Odometry (SVO) are also presented.

The estimation of interval weight vector is a fundamental problem in Interval Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The convergence property of the estimated interval weight vector is crucial for the validity of the solution. In the paper, the authors propose a relaxation method to solve the estimation problem with improved convergence. Specifically, they introduce a concept of "phase change materials" and apply it to the estimation problem to enhance the convergence of the solution. The proposed method shows significant improvement over the existing methods in terms of convergence speed and accuracy. Moreover, the authors also provide an extensive analysis of the convergence performance of the proposed method, including a comparison with other existing methods in terms of the convergence indexes. Overall, the proposed method provides a promising solution for the estimation of interval weight vector, which has broad applications in decision-making problems.

Direct monocular simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) methods, for which the image intensity is used for tracking and mapping instead of sparse feature points, have gained in popularity in recent years. However, feature-based methods usually have more accurate camera localization results than most direct methods, though direct methods can work better in a textureless environment. To tackle the localization issue, we develop a novel real-time large-scale direct SLAM model, namely, GCP-SLAM, by integrating the learning-based confidence estimation into the depth fusion and motion tracking optimization. In GCP-SLAM, a random regression forest is trained off-line with pre-defined confidence measures for learning confidence and detecting the ground control points (GCPs). Then, the confidence value along with the selected GCPs is utilized for depth refinement and camera localization. Our proposed method is shown experimentally more reliable in tracking and relocalization than the previous state-of-the-art direct method when compared with feature-based and RGBD SLAMs.

Peer-to-peer systems are well-known patterns of distributed systems which created several revelations in designing ultra-scalable systems. Recently, these types of systems are evolved into cognitive peer-to-peer networks. Because of the distributed nature of Internet of Things (IoT), peer-to-peer systems such as blockchain can be used to design management mechanisms in IoT. Therefore, we need an architecture which facilitates the utilization of peer-to-peer systems in IoT based systems. To the best of our knowledge, there is no general architecture based on cognitive peer-to-peer networks. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an architecture for managing IoT based on cognitive peer-to-peer networks. In order to study the potential of the proposed architecture, we suggest an adaptive search mechanism and also a topology management algorithm utilizing the proposed architecture. The results show the efficiency of the suggested algorithms. The proposed architecture may facilitate a new evolution from peer-to-peer systems to thing-to-thing systems.

Edge deep learning systems have become increasingly popular with the advent of technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile devices. The security of these systems, however, has become a major concern due to their vulnerability to attacks. This paper proposes the use of Memory Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) and Processing-in-Memory (PIM)-based encryption as a means to secure edge deep learning systems. Computational modeling and deep learning algorithms are utilized to implement this security mechanism, which does not rely on cloud computing for encryption and data modeling. Instead, it leverages Random Access Memory (RAM), which is already available on most devices, to create a unique encryption key. The proposed method ensures a higher level of data security at the edge and reduces the risk of data theft and unauthorized access. The paper sheds light on the potential of this approach to enhance the security of edge deep learning systems, paving the way for a more secure and efficient era of IoT and mobile devices.

Mobile devices, along with wearable sensors, allow patients to access healthcare services from anywhere at any time. The longstanding constraints of computational capability and storage space on mobile devices can be alleviated by outsourcing computation- or data-intensive tasks to remote cloud centers. Thus, mobile cloud computing (MCC) has been recognized as a promising approach to provide pervasive healthcare services to people in their daily life. As the development and adoption of MCC techniques in healthcare, new optimization strategies have been explored and studied to help mobile cloud healthcare services to be deployed in a more effective and efficient manner. In this survey, we demonstrate how MCC techniques have been extensively deployed in various healthcare applications and, specifically, describe the general architecture and design considerations one should take into account while designing an MCC for healthcare scenarios. Given a large number of factors that may affect the performance of the MCC and even result in catastrophic consequences in healthcare, this paper presents the state-of-the-art optimization methods on the MCC for meeting the diverse priorities and achieving the optimal tradeoff among multiple objectives. Finally, the security and privacy issues of the MCC in healthcare are also discussed.

This paper explores the effect of prenatal organic solvent exposure on structural connectivity during childhood. The study focuses on the exposure of solvents, which can have a negative impact on pregnancy outcomes. The research relies on magnetic resonance imaging and optical fiber networks to assess the changes to structural connectivity in the brain. The biomedical imaging techniques used in the investigation show that prenatal exposure to organic solvents can lead to reduced structural connectivity in childhood. This study highlights the importance of vigilant monitoring of pregnant women who work with organic solvents and the potential long-term effects on the brain development of their offspring. The findings of this study have implications for healthcare providers and policymakers in developing occupational safety guidelines to reduce the risk to pregnant women and their children. The research contributes to a growing body of literature on the importance of the prenatal environment and its long-lasting impact on children's health and development.

Nowadays, the number of mobile netizens continues to grow, mobile life continues to infiltrate people's lives. Mobile applications play an increasingly important role in major industries (financial consumption, travel, education, and entertainment). High dependence and complexity make network communication become an important attack surface of mobile applications. How to quickly and efficiently discover security threats in the process of network interaction has become an urgent problem. This paper proposed a test method based on network packets fuzzing for Android applications. The scheme uses middleman technology to obtain the interaction data sent by servers to applications, adopts different mutation strategies to mutate the original data of different types, returns the mutated response data to applications, uses log monitoring technology to monitor crash information, thereby discovers potential security threats. 10 popular applications were tested based on the proposed method, and four kinds of problems were discovered. The problems contain unresponsiveness, crashes caused by JSON data exception, HTML content replacement, and URL redirection. The results indicated that the proposed method was effective in exposing bugs of mobile applications in the process of network data interaction.

In this paper, we have proposed a novel architecture for citizen security using deep learning based edge computing device. The proposed system comprises of an end- device which can be connected to every street light pole in an area. The gateway device can be connected at a large distance from the end-devices. LoRa physical layer is used as the main communication interface which enables large distance transmission. CNN based algorithm is used to identify the expression of the person who pressed the panic button on the device to reduce false alarm. A very low complex Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture has been developed, to recognize the expression on the end device itself. A data logging server is used for logging the node-id everytime it is pressed. An android application is also developed which shows the real-time location of the pressed node and provides navigation routes to reach that node.

This paper proposes a Covariance Matching Kalman Filter approach for Observable Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Systems. The proposed method involves the matching of the covariance matrices to achieve optimal convergence. The approach accounts for the measurement uncertainty and noise measurement through the Q measurement technique. The study highlights the importance of observability in Kalman filters, which is maintained through the proposed method. The implementation of the Covariance Matching Kalman Filter is presented and its effectiveness is evaluated through simulations. The results demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach, as compared to the traditional Kalman filter, especially for systems with large measurement uncertainty. In conclusion, the Covariance Matching Kalman Filter is a promising approach to enhance the performance of observable LTI systems.

This empirical study examines the impact of decision maker’s risk attitude on inventory policy, specifically in the context of raw materials and safety in companies. The authors use computational modeling to investigate the effects of different risk attitudes on decision making and resulting inventory policies. Results indicate that decision makers who exhibit risk aversion tend to hold more inventory at higher levels of safety, while those who exhibit risk seeking behavior tend to hold less. The study contributes to the development of standards for inventory management in industrial engineering, as it highlights the importance of considering decision makers’ risk attitudes in policy formation. Overall, this research sheds light on the integral role that decision making plays in inventory policy and offers valuable insights to managers seeking to optimize their inventory management practices.

As heterogeneous computing systems have become increasingly common, researchers have been focusing on optimizing offload programming for these systems. One promising approach is reverse offload programming, where tasks are offloaded from the CPU to specialized coprocessors. This approach can be particularly effective when coupled with computational modeling to optimize task allocation. In this paper, we explore the use of reverse offload programming on heterogeneous systems using microwave integrated circuits. To achieve optimal performance, we conduct a thorough task analysis to identify which tasks should be offloaded, and to which coprocessors. We then develop kernel-level programming techniques that allow for seamless communication between the CPU and coprocessors. Finally, we evaluate our approach through extensive experimentation on a prototype system, demonstrating the ability to achieve significant performance gains and energy savings compared to traditional offload programming techniques. Overall, our work provides valuable insights into the design and optimization of reverse offload programming for real-time applications on heterogeneous systems, and has important implications for computer architecture research.

In this paper, a simulation of the effects of approximation errors on multiple signal classification for direction of arrival estimation is presented. The focus lies on computer approximations of sine and cosine. Two possible error sources are highlighted, discussed and their effects estimated by constraining the approximation precision. The simulation results are then evaluated with an emphasis on optimized calculation times while maintaining good angle estimation results.

Identity verification is an important aspect in biometrics, and the use of hand geometry has been gaining attention due to its unique features. In this study, we propose a method for identity verification using the geometry of human hands, specifically focusing on the thumb. The proposed approach involves feature extraction of palmprints and thumbprints followed by transformation techniques to analyze the geometry of the thumb. The use of palmprint recognition adds an additional layer of security to the verification process. The transforms used in this approach include Fourier Transform (FT), Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), and Wavelet Transform (WT). The results of our experimentation demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in identity verification using the geometry of human hands, and pave the way for further research in the field.

Recent advancements in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology hold immense potential for improving the quality of life for individuals with motor disabilities. However, designing a robust BCI system that accurately interprets the user's motor imagery signals requires a significant amount of training data, which may not always be feasible to obtain. In this paper, we propose a method for transferring common spatial filters between subjects without the need for additional training data. We utilize semi-supervised learning techniques to derive effective feature extraction and estimation models from a limited amount of labeled data. Additionally, we employ support vector machines for calibration to further enhance the performance of the system.
