Its features have inspired the capstone project and project-based learning method. This article starts with a survey and clarifies the two major issues of the current capstone project. Afterwards, the systematic design of the capstone project based on the CDIO model is proposed, and some suggestions are made on the equipment and learning space. Finally, we analyze current issues of project-based learning method in universities and make some inspiring suggestions.

Muscle thickness is an important parameter used for quantifying musculoskeletal function. At present, the muscle thickness measurement relies on the manual method, which is subjective, time-consuming, and prone to error. In this paper, a novel automatic calculation method was proposed to achieve the continuous and quantitative measurement for the muscle thickness of biceps brachi in ultrasound images. The proposed method includes three steps: the detection and tracking of the seed point in the superficial aponeurosis, the detection and tracking of the feature line in the deep aponeurosis, and the muscle thickness estimation. The performance of the proposed method was firstly compared to the manual measured results, which demonstrates that they have a good agreement during the experiment and can be used for efficiently estimating the muscle thickness of biceps brachi in the musculoskeletal ultrasound images. Then, the validated method was employed to investigate the relationship between the muscle thickness and the joint angle. The results show that, the elbow flexion and extension angle has an approximately linear relationship with muscle thickness change.

This work proposes a new Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation for traffic grooming, routing and spectrum allocation to be used in the design of Elastic Optical Networks (EON). In order to compare our method with classic Routing and Spectrum Allocation (RSA) formulation without grooming, the evaluation of the benefits of exact traffic grooming and RSA formulation are presented over three small networks. For each network, the objective function is set as minimizing the maximum slot index among all fibers. Then, the collected results show the benefits of traffic grooming in EON networks. Due to the NP characteristic of the MILP proposed, we propose a heuristic algorithm for large networks, and the benefits of the grooming using this algorithm are investigated.

The modeling of Lithium-Ion batteries is an important task in designing efficient and long-lasting batteries. In this paper, we propose the use of a NARX Nonlinear model for battery modeling that takes into account the complex characteristics of Lithium-Ion batteries. The proposed mathematical model utilizes Artificial Neural Networks and Integrated circuit modeling to build an accurate model that can effectively predict the behavior of the battery under different conditions. Training of the NARX Nonlinear model is done using various data models and databases to ensure that the model is accurate and reliable. The results of our study show that the proposed model can accurately predict the behavior of Lithium-Ion batteries and can be used in the development of efficient and reliable battery systems. Overall, our research highlights the importance of battery modeling using advanced mathematical models and machine learning techniques to improve the design and development of batteries for various applications.

Node importance evaluation is an important task in information systems, with various applications in fields such as image reconstruction and feature extraction. In this research, we propose a novel approach for evaluating node importance based on background error reconstruction. Our method takes advantage of the sparsity of the underlying matrix to efficiently estimate the importance of each node. We also evaluate the computational complexity of our approach and compare it with existing methods, demonstrating our method's superior performance. Our experimental results indicate that our approach can effectively capture the importance of nodes in sparse matrices and achieve high accuracy with low computational cost. Overall, our method provides a promising solution for node importance evaluation in various information systems applications.

Noncontact penetrating detection and classification of human activities based on micro-Doppler signatures (MDs) using ultrawideband (UWB) bio-radars are valuable tasks in various practical applications such as post-disaster search-and-rescue operations and urban military operations. However, for all classifiers, MD features of different-magnitude activities at different positions are likely to result in classification errors due to MD attenuation and confusions. This letter proposes a classifier improving method called position-information-indexed classifier (PIIC). It aims at enhancing the performance of various classifiers in terms of recognition and classification. This method fully exploits the position information acquired by UWB bio-radar to create a position-labeled modularized database of MD features. It also guides searching adaptively for optimal predict submodel of PIICs for activity classification at a random position. We report through-wall detection and classification experimental results related to five activities within a range of 6 m. These results, based on four typical classifiers, demonstrate that PIIC-based classifiers can avoid those classification errors in an effective manner. Moreover, all PIIC-based classifiers present a better classification performance with an average accuracy rise of 8.16% compared with those of overall-model-based classifiers. These performance evaluation experiments suggest that this method is strongly robust and stable, presenting wide applicability to various classifiers.

This paper presents a technique for an efficient and accurate characterization of dual-polarized reflectarray unit cells by means of Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to accelerate the analysis and optimization of this type of antenna. The goal is to accurately obtain the matrix of complex reflection coefficients using geometrical data of the unit cell. To this end, SVMs are employed to obtain surrogate models of those coefficients in an efficient fashion by employing a novel grid search which accelerates by three orders of magnitude the training process with regard to an exhaustive grid search. In addition, the precision of the surrogate model is tested against full-wave simulations assuming local periodicity obtaining a high degree of agreement.

With the development of machine learning technology, numerous studies have been proposed to diagnose the open circuit (OC) faults in the pulse width modulation (PWM) voltage source rectifier (VSR) systems. However, most methods require system signals of more than one current period, which show poor real-time performance. Aiming at this problem, this paper presents an improved diagnosis system based on deep belief networks (DBN) and least square support vector machine (LSSVM). First, the double chain quantum genetic algorithm (DCQGA) is employed to obtain the proper length of measured signals and DBN structure parameters. Then, the fault features are extracted from the signals through DBN. Finally, these features are used to train the LSSVM fault classifier to construct the diagnosis model. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve the fault diagnosis including six kinds of single switch faults and 15 kinds of different double switches faults correctly. Besides, the proposed method also shows the superior anti-interference performance and high robustness on abrupt load transient conditions, unbalanced, and/or distorted grid voltage conditions, as well as, different power factor conditions. Furthermore, the average diagnostic time of this method is only 2.57 ms.

The rise of smart cities has led to an increasing demand for efficient content distribution systems. Cognitive radio, which allows for dynamic spectrum access, can greatly improve the performance of ad hoc networks. In this paper, we propose an information-centric cognitive radio network (ICCRN) for content distribution in smart cities. The ICCRN leverages both the content-centric networking (CCN) architecture and cognitive radio technology to enable efficient content retrieval and dissemination in a self-organized manner. We also propose a delay-aware routing protocol for ICCRN to minimize content retrieval delays. Additionally, we show how sensors can be integrated into ICCRN to improve network performance. Our simulation results demonstrate that ICCRN can significantly reduce content retrieval delays and improve network throughput, especially under heavy traffic loads. The proposed ICCRN is a promising solution for content distribution in smart cities, demonstrating the potential for cognitive radio to enable efficient and reliable communication in the era of the internet of things.

This paper proposes a microservice-oriented approach to automation of distributed scientific computations. The approach is aimed at improving computational modeling by leveraging the benefits of software, cloud computing, knowledge-based systems, synchronization, and tools. These technologies have the potential to facilitate problem-solving in distributed scientific computations. The proposed approach involves breaking down complex scientific computations into smaller, more manageable microservices that can be easily distributed across a computing network. This enables the efficient use of cloud computing resources and the easy scaling of computational resources to meet changing needs. Moreover, the approach allows for software tools to be developed and integrated into the microservices, enabling the use of knowledge-based systems for improved problem-solving. The synchronization of microservices also increases efficiency and reliability in distributed computations. Overall, the microservice-oriented approach presented in this paper has the potential to significantly enhance the automation of distributed scientific computations.

ID card recognition is an application scenario in image recognition. As an important identity certificate for citizens, ID card identification and information management has also become a hot issue of concern. Chinese ID card images recognition mainly faces the following problems: Firstly, the shadow grid lines and the noise interference caused by the camera hardware conditions and illumination, together with the useful information in the picture, cause a huge problem of extracting useful information in the ID card. Secondly, the way to extract the foreground part in a complex context is also important for recognition. In response to these problems, this paper proposes an ID card region location method based on face detection and national emblem detection. This method can locate the foreground target area of the ID card in a complex context. In addition, the method of rotation correction of ID card region based on Hough transform is proposed, which can correct the tilt target within the range of tilt angle less than 45 degrees. In the text localization stage, the morphological method of the image is used to locate the text area. The deep convolutional neural network is then used to implement character segmentation and recognition. The recognition process proposed in this paper achieves a better recognition effect, and the recognition of Chinese and digital characters reaches 99.7% recognition rate, and can cope with the rotation tilt and the image containing the background.

The language study and automatic processing require the availability of large raw and annotated corpora. Collecting data and constructing such language resources are non-trivial tasks in the NLP field, especially when it comes to deal with low-resource languages. In this paper, we are concerned with the Tunisian dialect (TD) and propose to survey the availability of corpora for its automatic processing. From the study of the main works that have been carried out in TD language processing, we were able to identify and categorize the different types of corpora that were constructed as part of these works. We present, in this paper, a summary of the identified TD corpora characteristics as well as an inventory of those which are accessible online.

This paper presents the modeling and simulation of a spherical autonomous underwater vehicle. The robot was developed under the European Union H2020 innovation action UNEXMIN for the exploration of underground flooded mines, and is a small spherical robot with thrusters and an internal pendulum for pitch control. A model of the vehicle is presented, initially without the pendulum, then an extended formulation is derived accounting for a multibody dynamic description of the system. Experimental identification results for the determination of drag parameters are presented as well. A Modelica based simulator is developed for dynamic simulation of the vehicle, and is integrated with the Matlab/Simulink environment. The simulator is then validated based on preliminary experimental results.

Nonlinear optimization problems with dynamical parameters are widely arising in many practical scientific and engineering applications, and various computational models are presented for solving them under the hypothesis of short-time invariance. To eliminate the large lagging error in the solution of the inherently dynamic nonlinear optimization problem, the only way is to estimate the future unknown information by using the present and previous data during the solving process, which is termed the future dynamic nonlinear optimization (FDNO) problem. In this paper, to suppress noises and improve the accuracy in solving FDNO problems, a novel noise-tolerant neural (NTN) algorithm based on zeroing neural dynamics is proposed and investigated. In addition, for reducing algorithm complexity, the quasi-Newton Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) method is employed to eliminate the intensively computational burden for matrix inversion, termed NTN-BFGS algorithm. Moreover, theoretical analyses are conducted, which show that the proposed algorithms are able to globally converge to a tiny error bound with or without the pollution of noises. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the superiority of the proposed NTN and NTN-BFGS algorithms for the online solution of FDNO problems.

This paper proposes a method for seismic events estimation under noisy environments using multiple model particle filter. The method takes into account the noise measurement and uses probability density function and mathematical models to estimate the seismic events with high accuracy. The approach is based on Bayes methods, which allow for more accurate estimation and prediction. The proposed method can be used in different fields of information technology and provides a valuable tool for estimating seismic events. The method can also be used in conjunction with additives to further enhance its accuracy and efficiency. Overall, this paper provides a promising solution for estimating seismic events under noisy environments using multiple model particle filter.

Optimal Health Monitoring via Wireless Body Area Networks is an emerging technology that has garnered considerable interest in recent years. The advent of wireless communication and advancements in sensor systems have made it possible to monitor patients' health remotely. Body area networks allow for continuous monitoring of vital physiological signs and provide real-time feedback to healthcare professionals. This paper discusses the use of heuristic algorithms in optimizing the monitoring process in wireless sensor networks. The proposed approach involves the use of intelligent routing and data fusion techniques that can reduce the energy consumption of the sensors and prolong the battery life of the network. The research focuses on the design and development of efficient algorithms for healthcare applications. The results demonstrate that the use of heuristic algorithms in wireless sensor networks can significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of health monitoring systems. Overall, the study suggests that the deployment of wireless body area networks in healthcare settings can revolutionize the way patients are monitored and treated.

This paper proposes a local adaptive observer for linear time-varying systems with parameter-dependent state matrices. The observers are designed to estimate the state variables of the system and the estimation error converges to zero asymptotically. To achieve this, the observer gain matrix is designed in a way that ensures the symmetry of its matrix product with the state matrix. This approach is applicable to both observable and unobservable systems with unknown parameters that are linear in the state variables. The proposed scheme is shown to be effective in estimating state variables for time-varying systems with parameter-dependent state matrices. The convergence of the estimation error is analyzed and the theoretical results are supported by simulations. The proposed observer provides a practical solution for estimating state variables in linear systems with varying parameters.

This paper deals with the description of a newly practiced method of teaching in EI. CESI, a French engineering school. This method called "The Active Project-Based Learning" (APBL) belongs to an emergent trend of innovative and active learning methods. The APBL approach has as a goal to eliminate the drawbacks of the classical education methods, which are often based on an almost unidirectional teacher speech, an unbalance in the amounts of information exchange and interaction between the transmitter (the teacher) and the receiver (the learner). Moreover, clearly, the great quantity of knowledge flow, the inactivity of the learner, a certain monotony of the teacher speech and finally the abstract character of some scientific fields are critical factors of risk and failure of the conventional method. This is more and more true face to a new generation growing in a digital environment where media and digital tools are preponderant. Consequently, the "old" conventional method has reached its limitation. In opposition to the conventional method, the APBL puts the student in the center of the learning mechanism. The learning is based rather on a flexible and dynamic interaction between the teacher and the student. he teacher ensures a role of coaching and accompanying the learner to reach the preplanned pedagogical goal with an easier and a faster way on a hand and with a greater chance of success on the other hand. The student can trust more and more in his capacities and can manage better, organize and customize his own learning process. Organizing studies by project will increase the student autonomy and will set up a similar context of professional work of an engineer in a company. Finally, elementary steps of the project are defined to ensure a continual improvement process, by following the PDCA process (P-Plan, D-Do, Check, A-Act), a widely used management method in industry. These are the great outlines of the APBL method, its expected results and impacts on the quality and efficiency of learning.

This paper presents a new technique for analog performance locking using neural network-based biasing. The proposed method utilizes the principles of biological neural networks to model the behavior of transistors and integrated circuits. Instead of using traditional analytical models, this approach relies on dynamic measurements of the system in order to generate biasing inputs. By effectively learning the system through a neural network, it is then possible to optimize performance and reduce variability across different circuit designs. This technique can be applied to a range of different applications, including logic gates, amplifiers, and other analog circuits. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential for this approach to improve the performance and accuracy of analog circuits, particularly in applications where variability is a critical concern.

This paper introduces a novel distributed stopping criterion for consensus algorithms operating in the presence of delays. Delays constitute one of the major challenges in the design and implementation of distributed protocols, and can considerably impact the convergence properties of iterative algorithms used in control systems. The proposed criterion leverages the analysis of the flow of information across the network, and allows for the incorporation of stringent convergence requirements while accounting for the inevitable delays in communication. The theoretical framework is based on a distributed algorithm that employs a set of standard messages to exchange information between nodes. The proposed criterion can be implemented in a variety of consensus protocols, and is shown to significantly improve the convergence rate compared to previous approaches. The applicability of the proposed framework is demonstrated using numerical simulations for various control systems, highlighting its robustness and versatility in real-world scenarios. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of distributed algorithms by offering a practical and effective solution for distributed consensus in the presence of delays.

This paper proposes a discrete time trajectory following sliding mode control strategy, which utilizes switches to achieve convergence of generators in the presence of uncertainty. The trajectory following component ensures that the system tracks a specified trajectory accurately, while sliding mode control is used to guarantee robustness to parametric uncertainties. The switching mechanism restricts the generator to a predefined sliding mode manifold and allows for accurate tracking of the reference trajectory. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations on a nonholonomic mobile robot. Results show that the trajectory following sliding mode control strategy is able to provide accurate tracking of the desired trajectory even in the presence of uncertainties, and the switching mechanism ensures that the system remains stable and converges to a desired equilibrium point. Overall, this method presents a promising approach for the control of systems with complex dynamics and uncertain parameters.

This article presents the results obtained from the collaboration and participation of the Spanish University for Distance Education (UNED) and the renewable energy company INOMA, both based in Spain, in the Microelectronics Cloud Alliances Project (MECA project). As part of this project, three open courses were created, two of microelectronics and one of maintenance in renewable energies systems. These courses were integrated into a cloud architecture, which are accessible to everyone. After three years of project, which involved the development and design of cloud architecture; the contents and implementation of the three courses; and a small pilot test. This article presents the results and conclusions reached, as well as points to take into account in the future.

This paper proposes a testing method called datamorphic testing, which is specifically designed for testing intelligent applications such as face recognition software using artificial intelligence. The method involves modifying the input data used in testing and observing the output results to detect any unexpected behavior. The proposed method is especially useful for testing complex software that is difficult to test using traditional methods, such as those incorporating artificial intelligence algorithms. The use of datamorphic testing is demonstrated via testing of face recognition software running on glass, highlighting the benefits of this approach for testing intelligent applications. Ultimately, this method represents an important step towards improved software testing for intelligent applications, where accuracy and reliability are crucial for ensuring successful performance.

Over the last decade, Passive Optical Networks (PONs) have emerged as an ideal candidate for next-generation broadband access networks. Meanwhile, machine learning and more specifically deep learning has been regarded as a star technology for solving complex classification and prediction problems. Recent advances in hardware and cloud technologies offer all the necessary capabilities for employing deep learning to enhance Next-Generation Ethernet PON's (NG-EPON) performance. In NG-EPON systems, control messages are exchanged in every cycle between the optical line terminal and optical network units to enable dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) in the upstream direction. In this paper, we propose a novel DBA approach that employs deep learning to predict the bandwidth demand of end-users so that the control overhead due to the request-grant mechanism in NG-EPON is reduced, thereby increasing the bandwidth utilization. The extensive simulations highlight the merits of the new DBA approach and offer insights for this new line of research.

Reliability is nowadays considered a key requirement in wireless sensor networks for their increasing diffusion in various Internet of Things applications. However, radio interference from various sources may heavily affect the performance of wirelessly connected embedded devices, resulting into increased packet collisions and congestions. There is therefore a widely recognized need of both theoretical and practical investigations capable of shedding light on the factors affecting the operativeness of sensor networks subject to interference. In this paper, we investigate the role of packet length into the reliability and energy efficiency of low-power medium access protocols. Specifically, we propose a mathematical model to explore the functional dependence of the reliability of a pair of sensor nodes under interference from packet length. We also present a wide range of experimental evaluations aimed at validating the model and at providing novel insights on dependability issues. In particular, we assess the performance of Contiki's default medium access control layer (together with that of an always listening receiver, as a baseline) in terms of packet loss rate and energy efficiency for varying payload lengths. Experimental results highlight the interplay between packet size and interference and in particular the tradeoff between the robustness against interference and the overhead imposed to communication as a function of the length of data packets. The Pareto curve describing the energy efficiency as a function of the packet loss rate, demonstrates the existence of intermediate packet size representing an optimal choice for balancing energy consumption and communication reliability, enabling adequate system dimensioning at design-level.

This paper proposes a non-task-oriented dialogue system that is capable of controlling the length of utterances to improve the conversational efficiency. The system is developed through a combination of decoding, task analysis, and neural networks. Control systems are used to achieve optimal dialogue management by selecting appropriate responses based on the context of the conversation. The training of the system is achieved through supervised learning from training data, which is pre-processed by encoding techniques. The proposed system is tested in a real-world scenario and shows promising results in terms of both conversation quality and efficiency. Overall, this non-task-oriented dialogue system represents a significant advance in the development of conversational systems and opens up new possibilities for various applications, including customer service, educational instruction, and entertainment.

This paper studies some challenges in Internet of Things-based remote healthcare and smart environment sensing domains. A cloudlet architecture with virtual sensors is proposed and its advantages are discussed in the context of resolving certain issues. The issues are handled by applying sensor virtualization techniques in cloudlet and developing a PaaS platform to support relatively expensive computation at the edge. The utility of our design has been summarized with a number of use case implementations, test results, and performance metrics, based on the challenges we initially faced.

Intelligent intrusion detection systems have gained significant attention due to the increasing rate of cyber-attacks. Classification algorithms have been widely used in intrusion detection as they effectively classify network traffic into normal and malicious traffic. This paper proposes the use of a Decision Tree Classifier in combination with Bootstrap Aggregation, also known as bagging, for intrusion detection in IP networks. The proposed system involves feature extraction from incoming network traffic, followed by the classification process. The decision tree classifier is used to classify the network traffic as normal or malicious based on the extracted features. Bootstrap aggregation is then used to improve the accuracy of the detection by training multiple decision trees on different subsets of the training data. Experimental results show that the proposed system provides a high accuracy rate in detecting intrusion attempts in IP networks. This is achieved by combining the power of decision trees with the effectiveness of bagging during the training phase. The proposed system can be considered as a reliable and efficient solution for intrusion detection in IP networks.

Opening Range Breakout (ORB) is a fairly intraday trading strategy. We set the resistance and the support levels by the price in opening interval to follow the trend in the futures market. However, such kind of strategies is not profitable for most commodities in recent years in the changing market. In this paper, we attempt to improve the original ORB strategy by considering the effect of trends continuity on the event. We adjust the predetermined threshold for upper bound and lower bound. This strategy is called Threshold Adjusting ORB or TA_ORB. We implement this modified ORB strategy on the Taiwan Index Futures from 2008 to 2012. Compared with the original ORB strategy, we got 145.98% return in 2008 (bear market), 81.86% return in 2009 (bull market) and 32.25% annual return in 2008-2012 (five-year period) which are 4.0 times, 1.4 times, and 2.6 times more than original ORB, respectively. TA_ORB performs outstanding in large fluctuation, especially in the bear market. Performance can verify that the observations of TA_ORB improve the stability of the breakthrough signal, enhance the return, and reduce strategic risk. Further, we plan to use neural network to make more precise predictions and implement these strategies in different commodities.

Soft robotics has gained increasing attention in recent years due to its unique properties in achieving high compliance and adaptability. This paper introduces a new type of actuator, the inflatable toroidal bellows, which enables high force generation in soft robots. The topology of the toroidal bellows is optimized to enhance its force output capabilities. Furthermore, a force measurement setup is designed to evaluate the performance of the actuators. The results demonstrate that the inflatable toroidal bellows can generate significantly higher force compared to other soft robotic actuators. This new actuator provides a promising solution for applications in which high force generation is required, such as locomotion and manipulation tasks.

This paper focuses on the prediction of stealthy watermarks in files using deep learning techniques. The authors propose a predictive model based on watermarking and deep learning, which is trained to detect the presence of watermarks in files. The training process involves the measurement of certain key metrics, which are used to feed the neurons in the deep learning model. By using these metrics, the model can predict the presence of stealthy watermarks with high accuracy. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting the importance of using deep learning techniques for watermarking. Overall, the findings suggest that deep learning can be an effective tool for predicting the presence of stealthy watermarks in files, and can help to improve the security and protection of digital content.

This paper proposes the use of a Cascade Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Recurrent Neural Network architecture for the automatic classification of Indian languages into tonal and non-tonal categories. The paper focuses on feature extraction from spectrograms and task analysis for speech recognition. Several databases are used to train and test the system. The proposed architecture utilizes the convolution operation to extract meaningful features from spectrograms, which are further processed by LSTM recurrent neural networks to model temporal dependencies in the data. The results of the experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed system for accurate classification of Indian languages into tonal and non-tonal categories. The paper outlines the potential of the proposed architecture in computer architecture for speech recognition in Indian languages.

We live today in a highly competitive world in many areas, for instance, in the business world. Thus, strategic business partnerships become important for a business to succeed, especially for those exposed to a dynamic and uncertain market. Therefore, this study aims to identify expressive virtual relationships among businesses that are generated spontaneously by users in social media. To this end, a business similarity model based on common spontaneous reactions of users in social media, particularly Facebook, is proposed, as well as a new algorithm for detecting business communities within the proposed model. To demonstrate the proposed approach, the study uses more than 280 million user reactions on Facebook about businesses in Curitiba, Brazil. Exploring these data and the proposed approach, this study shows the possibility to identify non-trivial relations between businesses, which might enable the development of new mechanisms for recommending strategic business partnerships for entrepreneurs and business owners.

This paper proposes a human mixed strategy approach to deep reinforcement learning applied to games. The training is designed to enhance the task analysis and improve the simulation of the game, which helps to achieve a better performance. To create a comprehensive model, this approach uses the history of the game and reinforcement learning, which makes the learning process more efficient. The proposed method also employs MIMICs, which are a combination of human and computer components acting as a single agent. The MIMICs are used to replicate human-like behaviors, and they can learn from both the human and the computer's decisions. The results of the experiments show significant improvements in the performance of the agents trained with this approach compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods. Therefore, this approach provides a valuable contribution to the field of AI, particularly in developing more sophisticated strategies for game agents.

In this paper, we propose a rigorous macromodeling approach for efficiently simulating large arrays of complex scatterers. The approach is based on integral equations and the method of moments, which are widely used in the field of electromagnetics. With this approach, we are able to accurately model the behavior of antenna arrays and other complex structures, while also achieving a significant reduction in computational time and resources. Our method is particularly useful for large-scale computational modeling, where efficiency is paramount. Overall, our results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach for a wide range of applications in the field of computational electromagnetics.

In recent years, mobile robots have become increasingly popular in exploring unknown environments. One essential aspect of mobile robot navigation is the usage of fuzzy logic methods, which allow the robot to navigate in an uncertain environment. This research aims to conduct a comparative study of hybrid fuzzy logic methods for mobile robot navigation in unknown environments. Specifically, the study focuses on the integration of genetic algorithms and linguistic fuzzy logic for improving navigation performance. The proposed hybrid fuzzy logic methods involve the combination of linguistic expressions and genetic algorithms for generating optimum control parameters for the mobile robot's wheels. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid fuzzy logic methods offer promising outcomes compared to the conventional fuzzy logic methods. Therefore, it is concluded that the hybrid fuzzy logic methods can significantly enhance the robot's navigation performance in unknown environments.

In this paper, a novel fault isolation scheme for coexisting permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) current sensor and non-sensor imbalance faults is proposed. As the use of PMSM in various applications continues to increase, it is important to have a reliable fault detection and isolation mechanism. The proposed scheme utilizes battery charge and phase measurements to estimate the rotor and stator currents, which can be used to detect and isolate faults. The algorithm also accounts for sensor faults and non-sensor faults, such as rotor imbalance. Overall, this scheme improves the reliability and safety of PMSM systems, making them more suitable for use in various applications.

This paper discusses the development and application of a Saint-Venant Reduced Order Model (ROM) for water level control in open channels. The mathematical model is derived using transfer functions and is designed to capture the dynamics of water level control in open channels. This model is then reduced to a lower order using numerical models, which greatly reduces the computational modeling requirements. The model is capable of accounting for delays and high frequency effects, which are critical in water level control. The results show that this model is highly effective in level control and can be used as a tool for design and optimization of control systems in open channel flow.

This paper explores the topic of crowd management in urban areas, particularly in the context of smart cities. With the widespread use of smart phones and the increasing availability of big data and the Internet of Things, crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising approach for managing crowds during large events or crises. This paper highlights specific issues and sections related to crowd management, such as emergency response, transportation, and security. By analyzing case studies and discussing best practices, this paper presents a framework for effective crowd management in smart cities. The results suggest that leveraging information and communication technologies (ICT) in crowd management can foster better resource allocation, improved situational awareness, and more timely decision-making. Ultimately, this paper provides insights into the challenges and opportunities of managing crowds in the era of smart cities, setting the stage for future research in this area.

This paper proposes a knowledge oriented framework using the Axiomatic Design Theory to facilitate the development of new services, with a focus on hotel business models. The framework integrates multiple aspects such as the biological system modeling, technological innovation, and product development. The use of the Axiomatic Design Theory allows for a systematic approach to service development with a clear focus on meeting customer needs and business goals. The proposed framework emphasizes training as an important component to ensure the successful implementation and adoption of the new service. This framework can be applied in various business industries to enable efficient and effective service development, aiding in the overall growth and success of businesses.

EEG signals could reveal unique information of an individual's brain activities. They have been regarded as one of the most promising biometric signals for person identification and verification. Steady-State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEPs), as EEG responses to visual stimulations at specific frequencies, could provide biometric information. However, current methods on SSVEP biometrics with hand-crafted power spectrum features and canonical correlation analysis (CCA) present only a limited range of individual distinctions and suffer relatively low accuracy. In this paper, we propose convolution neural networks (CNNs) with raw SSVEPs for person identification and verification without the need for any hand-crafted features. We conduct a comprehensive comparison between the performance of CNN with raw signals and a number of classical methods on two SSVEP datasets consisting of four and ten subjects, respectively. The proposed method achieved an averaged identification accuracy of 96.8%±0.01, which outperformed the other methods by an average of 45.5% (p-value <; 0.05). In addition, it achieved an averaged False Acceptance Rate (FAR) of 1.53%±0.01 and True Acceptance Rate (TAR) of 97.09%±0.02 for person verification. The averaged verification accuracy is 98.34% ± 0.01, which outperformed the other methods by an average of 11.8% (p-value <; 0.05). The proposed method based on deep learning offers opportunities to design a general-purpose EEG-based biometric system without the need for complex pre-processing and feature extraction techniques, making it feasible for real-time embedded systems.

The proposal of an e-learning system integrated P2P model with client-server model is an innovative approach to incorporating peer-to-peer computing into the design of electronic learning systems. This model involves the use of servers and IP networks to support the computational modeling and sharing of educational resources. The peer-to-peer aspect of the model allows for more efficient distribution and access to these resources. By integrating both client-server and P2P models, this e-learning system offers the benefits of both centralized and distributed approaches, resulting in a more flexible and effective platform for online education. With the increasing demand for online learning, this proposal offers a promising solution for enhancing the accessibility and scalability of learning systems.

This paper presents an extensive comparative study of four neural network models, including feed-forward networks, convolutional networks, recurrent networks and long short-term memory networks, on two sentence classification datasets of English and Vietnamese text. We show that on the English dataset, the convolutional network models without any feature engineering outperform some competitive sentence classifiers with rich hand-crafted linguistic features. We demonstrate that the GloVe word embeddings are consistently better than both Skip-gram word embeddings and word count vectors. We also show the superiority of convolutional neural network models on a Vietnamese newspaper sentence dataset over strong baseline models. Our experimental results suggest some good practices for applying neural network models in sentence classification.

Mobile computing has enjoyed rapid growth over the past decade, with an increasing number of smart phone users and a proliferation of applications available for download. However, this growth has also created new challenges for software developers and businesses, including the problem of cloning. Cloning occurs when an individual or group creates a copy of an existing app with the intent of presenting it as their own. To address this issue, the authors have developed a new technique called RomaDroid that uses a tree structure and components of each app's manifest file to efficiently detect app clones. This technique is robust, efficient, and provides accurate results even in the presence of distortion created by cloud computing. The use of RomaDroid and other similar detectors can help businesses protect their intellectual property and enhance the security of their software development efforts.

Electroencephalogram (EEG) has been widely used to study cortical connectivity during acquisition of motor skills. Previous studies using graphical models to estimate sparse brain networks focused on time-domain dependency. This paper introduces graphical models in the spectral domain to characterize dependence in oscillatory activity between EEG channels. We first apply a transformation based on a copula Gaussian graphical model to deal with non-Gaussianity in the data. To obtain a simple and robust representation of brain connectivity that explains most variation in the data, we propose a framework based on maximizing penalized likelihood with Lasso regularization utilizing the cross-spectral density matrix to search for a sparse precision matrix. To solve the optimization problem, we developed modified versions of graphical Lasso, Ledoit-Wolf (LW) and the majorize-minimize sparse covariance estimation (SPCOV) algorithms. Simulations show benefits of the proposed algorithms in terms of robustness and accurate estimation under non-Gaussianity and different structures of high-dimensional sparse networks. On EEG data of a motor skill task, the modified graphical Lasso and LW algorithms reveal sparse connectivity pattern among cortices in consistency with previous findings. In addition, our results suggest regions over different frequency bands yield distinct impacts on motor skill learning.

Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation, also known as a natural extension of general POI recommendation, is recently proposed to predict user's next destination and has attracted considerable research interest. It focuses on learning users’ sequential patterns of check-in behavior and on training personalized recommendation models using different types of contextual information. Unfortunately, most of the previous studies failed to incorporate the spatiotemporal contextual information, which plays a critical role in analyzing user check-in behavior, into recommending the next POI. In recent years, embedding learning and recurrent neural network (RNN) based approaches show promising performance for modeling sequential patterns of check-in behavior in next POI recommendation. However, not all of the historical check-in records contribute equally to the next-step check-in behavior. To provide better next POI recommendation performance, we first proposed a spatiotemporal long and short-term memory (ST-LSTM) network. By feeding the spatiotemporal contextual information into the LSTM network in each step, ST-LSTM can model the spatial and temporal information better. Also, we developed an attention-based spatiotemporal LSTM (ATST-LSTM) network for next POI recommendation. By using the attention mechanism, ATST-LSTM can focus on the relevant historical check-in records in a check-in sequence selectively using the spatiotemporal contextual information. Besides, we conducted a comprehensive performance evaluation using large-scale real-world datasets collected from two popular location-based social networks, namely Gowalla and Brightkite. Experimental results indicated that the proposed ATST-LSTM network outperformed two state-of-the-art next POI recommendation approaches regarding three commonly-used evaluation metrics.

We present a simple and quick method to estimate a network centrality measure. Our method, called QuickCent, is inspired in so called fast and frugal heuristics, which are heuristics initially proposed to model the human quantitative estimation process. The centrality index that we estimate is the harmonic index which is a measure based on shortest-path distances, so infeasible to compute on large networks. We compare QuickCent with known machine learning algorithms on synthetic data. Our experiments show that QuickCent is able to make robust estimates compared with alternative methods achieving low-error variance estimates even with a small training set. Moreover, QuickCent is comparable in efficiency -accuracy and time cost-to more complex methods. Our initial results show that simple heuristics and biologically inspired computational methods are a promising line of research in the context of network measure estimations.

Brain tumour identification is a very crucial step that is required to diagnose and identify the degree of severity. The identification of tumor and classification helps the radiologist to diagnose properly and treat in according with that. Therefore, this paper presents a multi-class brain tumor classification in MR neurological images using random forest (RF) classifier with three different approaches. In the proposed approach, gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM), shape and local binary pattern (LBP) features are computed and further principal component analysis (PCA) is used for dimensionality reduction of the computed feature vector. All the features are extracted into the small patches having size of 3 ×3 in a local window. Several experiments are performed on a brain tumor dataset having 3064 T1-weighted contrast-enhanced images and comparative analysis of RF, RF-PCA and RF-PCA with random selection is presented. The experiment results show that RF-PCA with random selection performs better than the other approaches with a testing and validation accuracy of 88.72% and 85. 56%.

In this work, particle swarm optimization (PSO) based approach to the synthesis of a cylindrical-rectangular ring microstrip conformal antenna using support vector regression (SVR) models is presented. Resonant frequency of the antenna is obtained by PSO of trained SVR models. Radial basis function (RBF) and wavelet kernel functions are used in SVR models. Simulation examples are given and the results are compared.

Internet of Things (IoT) has gained tremendous attention in recent years due to its potential to revolutionize various sectors. IoT is essentially an ecosystem that interconnects various sensors, devices, and networks to gather and transmit data to facilitate efficient decision-making. One of the critical components of the IoT ecosystem is protocols. Protocols govern the way in which devices communicate with each other and exchange information. Another essential element of IoT is web pages, which serve as an interface for users to access and monitor IoT devices. These web pages are hosted on computers and servers and can be accessed using Uniform Resource Locators (URLs). Understanding the IoT ecosystem and its various components is crucial for developing efficient and sustainable IoT solutions.

Effective utilization of resources in hospitals is one of the most critical factors that impact patient care and hospital efficiency. The allocation of time for surgeries in operating rooms is a crucial aspect of resource management in hospitals. This paper proposes a new method for block allocation in two-stage operating rooms scheduling that aims to optimize the use of resources and minimize patient waiting times. The proposed method employs sequential analysis and processor scheduling techniques to allocate blocks of surgeries in a way that minimizes idle time and ensures the availability of resources for every patient. The method was evaluated using real data collected from a hospital in China, and the results showed that the proposed method outperformed the existing scheduling methods. This study provides insights into how hospitals can benefit from the use of innovative scheduling methods that optimize the use of resources such as operating rooms, and ensure that patient care is delivered efficiently.

Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory is a potentially transformative technology in the non-volatile memory market. Its viability depends, in part, on one's ability to predictably induce or prevent switching; however, thermal fluctuations cause small but important errors in both the writing and reading processes. Computing these very small probabilities for magnetic nanodevices using naive MC simulations is essentially impossible due to their slow statistical convergence, but variance reduction techniques can offer an effective way to improve their efficiency. Here, we provide an illustration of how importance sampling can be efficiently used to estimate low read and write soft error rates of macrospin and coupled-spin systems.

Coronary MRI is a non-invasive radiation-free imaging tool for the diagnosis of coronary artery disease. One of its limitations is the long scan time, due to the need for high resolution imaging in the presence of respiratory and cardiac motions. Machine learning (ML) methods have been recently utilized to accelerate MRI. In particular, a scan-specific ML technique, called Robust Artifical-neural-network for k-space Interpolation (RAKI) has shown promise in cardiac MRI. However, it requires uniform undersampling. In this study, we sought to extend this approach to arbitrary sampling patterns, using coil self-consistency. This technique, called SPIRiTRAKI, utilizes scan-specific convolutional neural networks to nonlinearly enforce coil self-consistency. Additionally, regularization terms can also be incorporated. SPIRiT-RAKI was used to accelerate right coronary MRI. Reconstructions were compared to SPIRiT for different undersampling patterns and acceleration rates. Results show SPIRiT-RAKI reduces residual aliasing and blurring artifacts compared to SPIRiT.

Cancer is a disease which causes increasing of human death rate in each year. Normally cancer can occur anywhere in human body. A major class of problems in medical sciences involves the diagnosis of disease based upon various tests performed upon patient. When several tests are involved the ultimate diagnosis may be difficult to obtain, even for medical expertise because of lot of different parameters obtained from the subject to be diagnosed. This has given rise, over the past few decades, to computerized diagnostic tools, intended to aid physicians in making sense out of the confusion of data. Clinical oncologists create diagnostic selections concerning cancer patient supported by past skilled experiences and information, intelligent techniques area unit probably the sole category of automatic technique powerful enough to emulate the expert's selection because of their stable behavior within the presence of noise in preciseness and uncertainty, the ANN and ANFIS techniques may doubtless get higher results than classical ways.

This paper proposes the development of an augmented reality ecosystem for learning environment that harnesses the transformative potential of novel technologies such as augmented reality, games, and the Internet of Things. Leveraging mobile handsets and real-time systems, this ecosystem aims to create an immersive learning experience that fosters engagement, motivation, and knowledge retention. Augmented reality technology provides the means to seamlessly integrate the physical and digital worlds, enabling learners to explore and interact with virtual objects within a real-world context. Games offer a compelling and entertaining means of engaging learners while simulating real-world scenarios. Connecting these technologies with the myriad sensors and devices embedded in our environment through the Internet of Things facilitates a richer and more personalized learning experience. By creating an ecosystem that harnesses these technologies, we can create an environment that is both joyful and effective in developing lifelong learners.

Current techniques of knowledge management have some common defects in efficiency, scalability, and applicability. Knowledge graph provides a new way for knowledge management and is a more flexible knowledge management method. Considering the specific features of crop diseases and pest data, this paper analyzed and classified the key techniques and methods of knowledge graph technology in the field of crop diseases and pest in recent years. We introduced the definition and connotation of the crop diseases and pest knowledge, and the current construction method of it was analyzed in detail from four aspects: knowledge representation, extraction, fusion, and reasoning. Furthermore, the application of crop diseases and pest knowledge graph was introduced in detail in the expert system, search engine, and knowledge question-answering system. At last, this paper summarized the challenges and important problems of diseases and pest knowledge graph and forecasted the prospect of knowledge graph according to the key points and difficulties of current knowledge graph research.

This paper proposes a Fuel Level Indication and Mileage Calculator system that utilizes the Internet of Things (IoT) technology. This system is designed to provide drivers with accurate and real-time information about their fuel levels and mileage, through the use of Liquid Crystal Displays (LCD) and various sensors. By leveraging the capabilities of IoT, this system can enable reliable and efficient monitoring of fuel levels and enable drivers to calculate the optimal fuel consumption. Additionally, the proposed system can incorporate acoustics and cloud computing to further enhance the user experience. By enabling drivers to better manage fuel storage, this system has potential to reduce accidents related to fuel shortage or overloading. In summary, this Fuel Level Indication and Mileage Calculator system represents an innovative use of IoT technology in the automotive industry, which could significantly improve fuel consumption and driving safety.

This paper presents a loop antenna for deep implant powering in an intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring application. This work is continuation of our on-going development of a wirelessly powered implantable system for ICP monitoring. Experimental results indicate that the implant can be activated until the depth of 19 mm from the skin. This is 8 mm more than our previous work where we were able to activate the implant until 11 mm depth from the skin. Moreover, we have also presented pressure readout experimental results with the proposed antenna.

This article presents a medical simulation solution. This solution allows a physician to train a clinical scenario by interacting with a graphical interface. The aim is to instigate the learning and internalization of clinical procedures. Currently these resources have been intensifying in the most diverse areas, being our focus, Medicine. Within this area, the focus is on medical simulation. There are numerous biomedical simulation centers, whose main objective is to create realistic simulations to aid health professionals. Thus, it is intended to optimize its performance, to meet the needs detected and to anticipate unexpected situations (critical or complex events). However, current simulation systems face some limitations, since they have enough difficulties in the development of new scenarios, since they are restricted to the level of modularity and the number of simulated situations. The training of these professionals is limited to simulation centers. The goal is to create a platform to simulate real scenarios and develop serious games that simulate various clinical situations, in order to facilitate access to this type of training and training.

The Multi User-Multiple Input Multiple Output (MU-MIMO) technique offers big advantages over traditional MIMO solutions. Nevertheless, Nonlinearity of High Power Amplifier (HPA) presents a crucial role in the performance of MU-MIMO systems.This paper investigates the performance of Massive MIMO system in the presence of nonlinear HPA over Rayleigh fading channel. Different receivers and algorithms are used in order to illustrate this fact, such as LS, MMSE, ZF and AMP, are evaluated and mutually compared. Specifically, we assess the effect of the nonlinear distortion on the BER. Numerical results are provided and show the impacts of several system parameters, such as type of receivers, number of antennas, number of users and values of IBO, on system performance.

The Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm involves the connection of billions of devices, leading to unprecedented amounts of data generation and analytics. As a result, the demand for cloud computing resources has skyrocketed. Resource management is a key challenge in this context, and traditional hardware-based approaches are not agile enough to deal with the dynamic nature of IoT workloads. Network Function Virtualization (NFV) has emerged as an attractive paradigm for managing IoT resources. NFV-based systems can easily provision, allocate, and manage resources on demand. In this paper, we propose analytical models and load modeling techniques to enable data-driven resource allocation for NFV-based IoT systems. Our approach focuses on optimizing resource allocation for efficiency, scalability, and reliability. We demonstrate our approach using a set of experiments, showing the effectiveness of our approach in terms of workload distribution and resource usage. Our research highlights the importance of data-driven resource management in NFV-based IoT systems and offers new insights into cloud resource management for IoT applications.

This paper studies the problem of emptying small satellite networks using in-network data aggregation. Small satellite networks are becoming increasingly popular due to their low cost and feasibility for various applications. However, these networks rely on node-to-node communication which can cause network congestion and energy depletion. In-network data aggregation is proposed as a solution to this problem. The paper discusses various data aggregation techniques and evaluates their performance in terms of energy efficiency and network lifetime. The proposed approach is compared with existing approaches used in wireless sensor networks and ad hoc networks. The results show that in-network data aggregation can significantly improve the energy efficiency of small satellite networks and extend their lifespan. This research is particularly relevant for low earth orbit satellites that require efficient data transmission and processing capabilities to support various remote sensing and Earth observation applications.

Human identification by gait from event-based camera is a promising approach for recognition tasks in scenarios where traditional cameras are not suitable. The use of artificial neural networks in combination with event-based cameras provides a reliable and efficient method for human identification. The system is trained by using data from different individuals and applying machine learning algorithms, which enable the system to differentiate between distinctive human gait patterns. Additionally, the implementation of MIMO communication and the Global Positioning System (GPS) in the system can improve the accuracy of human identification, especially in large-scale environments. Channel models and fading channels are also considered in the design of the system to account for the impact of environmental factors on data transmission. Overall, the proposed system provides a promising approach for human identification using gait analysis with the use of advanced technologies such as artificial neural networks, GPS, and MIMO communication.

The linear decreasing weight particle swarm optimization algorithm (LDWPSO) is mentioned in the concept of a center particle, and then puts forward center particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO). The linear decreasing weight particle swarm optimization algorithm, unlike other general center particle, particle velocity center is not clear, and is always placed in the center of the particle swarm. In addition, the neural network training algorithm compared to particle swarm optimization algorithm and the linear decreasing weight particle swarm optimization algorithm, results show that: the performance is better than the linear optimization center particle swarm decreasing weight PSO algorithm. algorithm.

In this paper, we investigate a recently proposed opinion dynamics model which considers a network of individuals simultaneously discussing a set of logically interdependent topics. The logical interdependence between the topics is captured by a “logic matrix”. Previous works have investigated the model under the assumption that all individuals have the same logic matrix, or that individuals have different logic matrices but each individual has some stubbornness, which are restrictive assumptions. In contrast, we investigate heterogeneous logic matrices for the individuals, and assume that no stubborn individuals are present. We show that such heterogeneity can lead to a stable system with persistent disagreement among the final opinions. This indicates heterogeneity in individuals' logical interdependence structures, and not just the stubbornness of individuals (as in the Friedkin-Johnsen model), may explain the phenomenon of strong diversity of opinions often observed in a strongly connected network: the opinions at equilibrium are not at a complete consensus and opinions in any cluster are similar but not equal.

This paper addresses the problem of optimal DoS attacks on remote state estimation with a router in wireless sensor networks. Denial-of-service attacks are a significant threat, disrupting the channel estimation and data communication between the nodes in the network. In this paper, the optimal DoS attack strategy is formulated as a maximum-likelihood estimation problem. The results show that the optimal attacker can effectively degrade the estimation accuracy of the remote state while minimizing the attack energy. The proposed scheme can be applied to different types of wireless communication systems and is robust to fading channels. Overall, this work sheds light on the importance of considering DoS attacks in the design of wireless sensor networks and presents a practical solution to mitigate such attacks.

Cognitive radio is an efficient spectrum sharing mechanism to solve the contradiction between spectrum shortage and spectrum underutility, where secondary users (SUs) are allowed to access the spectrum licensed to primary users (PUs) in an opportunistic manner. In cognitive radio networks with multiple access points (APs), due to the information exchange cost and system flexibility, APs may not cooperate with each other and there usually does not exist a central controller in practice. We propose a distributed user association scheme based on multi-agent reinforcement learning to achieve load balancing for cognitive radio networks with multiple independent APs. In our proposed scheme, APs execute reinforcement learning process independently to derive optimal policies on user association. In each iteration, APs make decisions on choosing SUs for association and then SUs choose the optimal AP for association based on the offers of all APs, the behaviors of APs and SUs is modeled as a dynamic matching game. Simulation results show that the proposed multi-agent reinforcement learning approach can highly improve the system performance with excellent robustness, compared to the conventional max-SINR method.

Social health and emotional wellness is a matter of concern in today's urban world. Being the part of a metropolis has an effect on mental health through the influence of increased stressors and factors such as overcrowded and polluted environment, high levels of violence, and reduced social support. It is important to realize that only healthy citizens can constitute together a smart city. In this paper, we present a fuzzy-based approach for analyzing the well being of a person. We track the general day to day activities of a person and analyze its performance. To do so, we divide the factors affecting the wellness of a person into three components which are the physical, productive and social. Using these parameters, we output a coefficient for the overall well being of a person.

The 5G mobile communication technology is believed to be the foundation of the Internet of Things (IoT). However, ensuring massive connectivity in the 5G uplink is a challenging issue. This paper proposes a scheme called Flex-NOMA that exploits buffer-aided relay selection to enhance the performance of the 5G uplink. In the Flex-NOMA scheme, relays are used to assist in improving the connectivity of the uplink. Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is used as a multiple access scheme in the system. The proposed scheme is evaluated through performance evaluation, and the results show that it achieves significant performance improvements compared to existing schemes. Also, the use of new materials such as silicon carbide can lead to even better results. Overall, the Flex-NOMA scheme provides a promising solution to the problem of massive connectivity in the 5G uplink, contributing to the development of the IoT.

Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks are a special type of Ad-Hoc network that supports communication between highly mobile vehicles and stationary Roadside Units or base stations. As the demand for more bandwidth increases with the introduction of autonomous vehicles and Multi-Media entertainment, the network size must scale to accommodate the demand. However, when deploying any additional networking resources, energy consumption should be taken into account. Existing works target routing as a means to reduce the energy consumed in end-to-end communications, but little work has been directed towards energy-aware infrastructure planning. In this work, we present a spatio-temporal clustering approach that models the connection time for potential Roadside Unit deployment sites. Our techniques leverage crowdsourced data, which is collected at the vehicle, and accurately represents the trends of users in the network. Modeling the connection time of deployment sites allows for transmission power to be adjusted based on traffic flow. We also present a technique to model the signal strength in deployment sites, thus identifying areas with sufficient coverage and selecting sites with weak connectivity from existing networking infrastructure. Combined this information allows infrastructure to be deployed in a manner that matches the real-time traffic and operate with an optimal transmission power.

In recent years, the use of through-silicon vias (TSVs) has become increasingly important in the semiconductor industry due to its high integration capability. However, TSVs are prone to clustering faults, which can significantly affect the performance and reliability of the system. In this paper, we propose a 3-D rotation-based redundancy architecture to address clustering faults in TSVs. Our proposed architecture uses a rotation-based approach to distribute redundancy across multiple TSVs, which effectively mitigates the impact of clustering faults. To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed architecture, we perform extensive simulations using various benchmarks and real-world applications, such as databases, smart grids, Zigbee, cloud computing, batteries, electric vehicles, and base stations. Our results show that our proposed architecture achieves an average of 25% improvement in reliability compared to existing redundancy architectures for TSVs.

By applying low power wide area network (LPWAN) to communication between a machine and the cloud, it can be anticipated that communication costs and the amount of power consumed by the machine can both be reduced. However, considering the addition of functions to the machine, it is necessary to have a technology able to transfer a large amount of data, which cannot be transferred by LPWAN, to the machine from the cloud at low cost. In this paper, a novel large data download method by Wi-Fi from cloud to machine using the terminals of general users is proposed. In the proposed method, the cloud selects the delivery terminals satisfying the data arrival rate requirement by analyzing the correlation of the movement history between the terminals. It guarantees a data arrival rate with a higher degree of accuracy than the existing DTN and CC-DTN, and at the same time minimizes the number of delivery terminals. In addition, this paper shows an authentication procedure that prevents DoS attacks on LPWAN by a spoofing terminal, which cannot be prevented by existing network authentication technology. Also, we report the effectiveness of the proposed method, which is confirmed by numerical calculation.

In this paper, a lightweight security solution is proposed for the Internet of Things (IoT) systems. In fact, this proposed solution is called TrioSec, and can ensure the basic security requirements such as Authentication/Authorization, Intrusion Detection System (IDS), and System Monitoring with minimum computation and resources overhead. The proposed solution uses optimized open source software agents that can be implemented in the Gateway node of the IoT network layer. In fact, several recent interesting security solutions were being presented in the literature to tackle these security requirements. However, there is not yet any complete security solution for IoT systems that integrates multiple software agents. The advantage of the proposed solution is its ability to combine the best existing and customized security tools to reach a maximum level of security with a minimum overhead level in terms of computation and resources.

This paper proposes a method for detecting botnet attacks at the edge of the Internet of Things (IoT) using sparse representation. The Internet of Things has made it easier for botnets to launch attacks, which can be a major security threat. Sparse representation and matching pursuit algorithms are used to extract features and detect botnet attacks. The method is based on image edge detection and can be used for intrusion detection. This research shows that with the use of sparse representation and matching pursuit algorithms, it is possible to detect botnet attacks at the IoT edge, providing a more secure environment for IoT devices.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have been widely deployed for various applications due to their flexibility and low cost. However, the energy limitation of WSNs poses a significant challenge, as the power demand of nodes varies depending on the operating system, protocol, and energy measurement methods used. In this study, we aimed to explore the suitable node number for WSNs based on energy consumption, using the Cooja simulator. We measured the power consumption of nodes under different protocols and operating systems, and implemented Java-based scripts to collect energy consumption data. Our results showed that the suitable node number varied depending on the protocol and operating system. Specifically, the ZigBee protocol and Contiki operating system were found to be the most energy-efficient combination. Our study highlights the importance of carefully selecting the appropriate protocol and operating system for WSNs to minimize energy consumption and prolong network lifetime. Future work should focus on optimizing energy consumption through algorithmic and hardware design improvements.

This paper proposes a novel approach for Energy Theft Detection through the use of Gradient Boosting Theft Detector equipped with Feature Engineering-Based Preprocessing. The proposed system leverages the power of Feature Extraction to identify relevant features from raw meter data, and then uses the Boosting algorithm to optimize the selection and combination of these features. Furthermore, Classification Algorithms such as Support Vector Machines are employed to train detectors that flag unusual patterns indicative of energy theft. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms several alternative methods in terms of detection accuracy and processing speed. The system also proves to be versatile in its applicability, showing good performance across different types of theft scenarios. Computer Aided Software Engineering tools have been used for implementing the system, making it an efficient and scalable solution for Energy Theft Detection.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing analytical and computational models for manufacturing processes. These mathematical models can provide insights into the behavior of unit manufacturing processes, and ultimately aid in the development of more advanced process control and optimization strategies. The use of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) has facilitated the creation of more structured and standardized models, making it easier for researchers and practitioners to exchange and compare models. However, there is still much work to be done towards making these models more user-friendly and accessible for operational use. This paper presents a review of the current state of unit manufacturing process modeling, with a focus on the tools and techniques being employed towards making these models more useful for real-world applications. Future research directions and practical considerations are also discussed.

ICT technology is widely applied to various industries including agriculture. In the agricultural sector, most of the devices and greenhouses still use very old serial communication technologies. Nowadays, many ICT technologies such as ZigBee, Bluetooth and the Internet are spreading but still not interoperable. A set of standards is under development in Korea to ensure interoperability between different vendors. In particular, core interoperability can be provided by standardizing the LCP protocol independent of the underlying network infrastructure. In this paper, we designed service control protocol based on LCP protocol and implemented it using Python. We have deployed the implementation to Raspberry PI with actual physical devices.

This paper proposes a new consensus algorithm called Proof of Previous Transactions (PoPT) for the JCLedger. The JCLedger is a blockchain-based system that supports peer-to-peer computing and cloud computing. The PoPT algorithm is designed to be more efficient than previous consensus algorithms, which have been criticized for their lack of scalability. The paper argues that the PoPT algorithm is capable of addressing this issue, making it a viable option for large-scale blockchain-based systems such as Bitcoin. The PoPT algorithm is based on the idea of using previous transactions as a means of verifying new transactions. This approach eliminates the need for mining and other resource-intensive activities, which can slow down the verification process. The authors also discuss some of the challenges that need to be addressed when implementing the PoPT algorithm, such as security and privacy concerns. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to consensus for blockchain-based systems that have to deal with scalability issues.

This paper proposes a linearization technique for third-order input intercept point (IIP3) improvement in subthreshold low noise amplifiers (LNAs). The proposed LNA is designed for 2.4 GHz radio-frequency wireless receiver front-ends for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. A novel modified derivative superposition technique is presented for the linearization of subthreshold LNAs.
