Furthermore, the effects of adverse factors, including resistance, digital control delay, inverter nonlinearity, and cross saturation on PMHI and AMHI are analyzed, respectively. Finally, experimental results prove the validity of the theoretical analysis.

Poor efficiency and long running time of existent optimization algorithms in dealing with multi-objective multi-variable community microgrid optimization have always been a concern. To address this issue, a novel layered optimization algorithm based on NSGA-II is proposed. The proposed algorithm integrates the structural feature of community microgrid and the concept of multi-agent system into the optimization process and decomposes the complex microgrid optimization into several household optimizations of smaller scale and one central microgrid optimization. The household operation is optimized first and the central microgrid optimization is solved subsequently based on the Pareto solution set of household operation problems to obtain the optimal operation mode. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy is effective in improving optimization efficiency.

Recently, Bluetooth low energy (BLE) is widely used for short-range communication among wireless devices. The challenge of utilizing BLE in indoor localization is the characteristic of the observation area where multipath fading, shadowing, interference, and reflection of signal would appear. This paper proposed a new approach of evaluating the performance of wireless device communication system using BLE module in an indoor environment in term of estimating the position of the device using localization technique. Linear Regression method is used to refine the modeling distance parameter which measured previously. The simulation result shows that combining Linear Regression and Lognormal shadowing method for distance modeling will enhance the accuracy up to 99%.

The application of text analytics in electric power dispatching has become a hot research topic due to its significance in improving the efficiency and accuracy of dispatching. Dispatching manuals are the main sources of dispatching guides, and they often contain a lot of unstructured data that is difficult to analyze manually. With the help of text analytics, dispatchers can analyze these manuals to identify correlations between different power systems and detect anomalies using natural language processing techniques. Moreover, the adoption of proper data structures and tools can boost the efficiency of text analytics in dispatching, which will ultimately lead to better decision-making and power system management. Overall, the application of text analytics in electric power dispatching has great potential for improving the reliability and integrity of power systems.

Event-based online social platforms, such as Meetup and Plancast, have experienced increased popularity and rapid growth in recent years. In EBSN setup, selecting suitable venues for hosting events, which can attract a great turnout, is a key challenge. In this paper, we present a deep learning based venue recommendation system DeepVenue which provides context driven venue recommendations for the Meetup event-hosts to host their events. The crux of the proposed model relies on the notion of similarity between multiple Meetup entities such as events, venues, groups, etc. We develop deep learning techniques to compute a compact descriptor for each entity, such that two entities (say, venues) can be compared numerically. Notably, to mitigate the scarcity of venue related information in Meetup, we leverage on the cross domain knowledge transfer from popular LBSN service Yelp to extract rich venue related content. For hosting an event, the proposed DeepVenue model computes a success score for each candidate venue and ranks those venues according to the scores and finally recommend the top k venues. Our rigorous evaluation on the Meetup data collected for the city of Chicago shows that DeepVenue significantly outperforms the baselines algorithms. Precisely, for 84 percent of events, the correct hosting venue appears in the top 5 of the DeepVenue recommended list.

The emergence of wearable sensors and the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to a significant increase in the monitoring of human activity. This paper proposes an integrated approach for personalized human activity recognition in a smart home environment using wearable sensors and deep learning. The proposed approach involves monitoring and analyzing human activity using wearable sensors, extracting relevant features, and employing deep learning algorithms to accurately recognize and classify activities. The approach is based on cloud computing, enabling seamless data collection and processing. The proposed approach has potential applications in healthcare and lifestyle management, as it can provide personalized feedback to individuals and help them better understand their activities and health behaviors. The results of this study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high recognition accuracy and improving the performance of human activity recognition systems. Overall, this integrated approach has the potential to revolutionize human activity recognition in smart home environments, not just for individuals but also for businesses and healthcare providers.

Biomedical image analysis is one of the most challenging and inevitable part of the computer aided diagnostic systems. Automated analysis of the image can detect various diseases automatically without human intervention. Computer vision and artificial intelligence can sometimes defeat human diagnostic power and can reveal some hidden information from the biomedical images. In the field of health care, accurate results are highly required within stipulated amount of time. But to increase accuracy, proper preprocessing with sophisticated algorithms is required. Low quality image can affect processing algorithm which can leads to the poor result. Therefore, sophisticated preprocessing methods are required to get reliable results. Contrast is one of the most important parameter for any image. Poor contrast may cause several problems for computer vision algorithms. Conventional algorithms for contrast adjustment may not be suitable for many purposes. Sometimes, these methods can generate some images that may lose some critical information. In this work, a contrast optimization method based on well-known metaheuristic technique called genetic algorithm with elitism is used that can enhance the biomedical images for better analysis. A new kernel has been proposed to detect the edges. Obtained results illustrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

In this paper, we present a new perturbation method called Generalized Deterministic Perturbations for Stochastic Gradient Search. This method aims to improve approximation algorithms and convergence in the context of optimization problems, specifically in linear programming. We incorporate error correction codes into our perturbation approach to correct errors that may arise during optimization. Through several numerical experiments, we demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing perturbation methods in terms of both approximation quality and time to convergence. Overall, our approach offers a promising framework for improving optimization algorithms in various applications.

This paper proposes a new dynamic intermittent Q-learning approach for closed loop systems with reduced bandwidth. The technique is based on heuristic algorithms and optimal control methods to optimize the system dynamics. The proposed approach adapts to the systems' changing bandwidth, making it ideal for systems operating in fluctuating network conditions. Computational modeling techniques are used to simulate and evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed dynamic intermittent Q-learning approach. Adaptive control methods are used to ensure the model's stability while adjusting its parameters to achieve optimal control. The proposed approach can be used in various applications that involve bandwidth-limited systems, such as wireless sensor networks, internet of things devices, and unmanned aerial vehicles. The results of the simulation show that the proposed method outperforms other techniques in terms of accuracy, speed, and stability, making it a promising solution to closed loop systems with reduced bandwidth.

Automatic counting and individual size and mass estimation of olive-fruits is a critical task in the industry, which can increase the efficiency of production and provide high-quality products. In this paper, we propose a computer vision technique for olive-fruit analysis based on image analysis and computational modeling. The technique involves feature extraction and estimation from the olive-fruit images using computer vision algorithms. Image segmentation is used to isolate the olive-fruits, and the individual size and mass of each fruit are calculated. This technique has the potential to significantly reduce labor costs and increase the speed and accuracy of olive-fruit analysis. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is effective in automatically counting and estimating the individual size and mass of olive-fruits, making it a valuable tool for the olive industry.

Recently, smart cities, smart homes, and smart medical systems have challenged the functionality and connectivity of the large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Thus, with the idea of offloading intensive computing tasks from them to edge nodes (ENs), edge computing emerged to supplement these limited devices. Benefit from this advantage, IoT devices can save more energy and still maintain the quality of the services they should provide. However, computational offload decisions involve federation and complex resource management and should be determined in the real-time face to dynamic workloads and radio environments. Therefore, in this work, we use multiple deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents deployed on multiple edge nodes to indicate the decisions of the IoT devices. On the other hand, with the aim of making DRL-based decisions feasible and further reducing the transmission costs between the IoT devices and edge nodes, federated learning (FL) is used to train DRL agents in a distributed fashion. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the decision scheme and federated learning in the dynamic IoT system.

A rapid growth in the smart-wearable industry is making it increasingly important to cater to the quality of experience (QoE) requirements of the end users. In this paper, we try to model the relationship between human experience and quality perception in relation to the smart-wearable segment. For this, the concepts of quality of data (QoD) and quality of information (QoI) are used. While QoD is concerned with the accuracy and precision of the data collected by the smart-wearables, QoI relates to the useful information that is obtained from the raw data captured by the devices via the companion applications of each wearable installed on a smartphone. A subjective experiment comprising of 40 participants and 5 wearable devices is performed in a free-living condition in order to create the QoE model. Four different approaches for weight determination are presented in this paper: balanced weight distribution, correlation-based distribution, hybrid distribution, and priority-based distribution while proposing the QoE model. Our results show that the priority-based distribution approach performs slightly better than the rest of the techniques and has the best correlation to the subjective QoE when compared against others. Based on the results, the appropriate recommendations are provided to the different smart-wearable vendors for improving their products, thereby ensuring greater user adoption.

The recent growth in the maritime industry stemming to increase in global commerce as well as searching for hydrocarbons at offshore locations, the high data rate and cost affordable maritime communication is acquired. A mesh network is envisaged for maritime communications because of its expanded coverage, self-healing, and high-capacity. With the development of multi-radio technology, the frequency interference can be decreased sharply with proper channel assignment. The static channel assignment optimization is often applied to decrease the wireless frequency interference which is known as an NP-hard problem. In this paper, we focus on the static channel assignment issue and propose a heuristic algorithm to solve the optimization problem. The problem is addressed by assigning channels to communication links to minimize the interference from overall network. A modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed to optimize the problem, and a new merging solution is adopted to reassign channels for nodes, which violate the radio constraints. Multi-radio simulation is performed in NS-3 to validate the effectiveness of the proposed channel assignment algorithm. The results show that the algorithm is able to find an optimized assignment with fewer iterations than the previous work and improve network performance.

Cognitive ambient backscatter is a wireless communication paradigm that allows a secondary backscatter device to superimpose its information-bearing data on a primary signal, without requiring any type of power-consuming active components or other signal conditioning units. In such a network, the performance of the backscatter system can be severely degraded by channel estimation errors and co-channel direct-link interference (DLI) from the primary system. To overcome these shortcomings, we consider a cloud radio access network (C-RAN) architecture, where both the primary and secondary edge nodes are connected to a cloud processor via high-speed links. In this centralized architecture, secondary edge nodes provide network access to ambient backscatter passive and semi-passive sensors with communication capabilities, and the problem of acquiring channel state information and suppressing the DLI is managed by the cloud processor. In particular, we assess the performance of the secondary backscatter sensor transmission in a realistic system setup, which takes into account training-based channel estimation, practical modulation constraints, and imperfect DLI suppression. In addition, we formulate and solve an optimization problem aimed at maximizing the transmission rate of the secondary transmission, subject to limits on channel estimation error, average symbol error rate, power consumption, and energy storage capabilities of the backscatter sensor. The validity of our analysis and the performance of the secondary system based on the proposed designs are corroborated through the Monte Carlo simulations.

This paper aims to investigate the perception of financial auditors regarding the usage of computer assisted audit techniques (CAATs). CAATs involve the use of information technology, computational modeling, and software to improve audit accuracy and efficiency. The study examines the reliability of CAATs as well as auditors' attitudes towards technological innovation in audit processes. Correlation analysis is conducted to determine the relationship between technology adoption and audit quality. The findings of this study will be useful for audit firms and regulatory bodies that aim to promote the adoption of CAATs in financial audits.

This paper presents a novel approach for the automatic screening of heart sounds based on the integration of Hidden Markov models and Gammatone filterbank models. The proposed approach utilizes phonocardiography signals to extract relevant features, which are then filtered and processed by the Gammatone filterbank models. Subsequently, Hidden Markov models are applied to classify the heart sounds based on the likelihood estimation of each class. The results of the experimental evaluation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach as compared to traditional classification approaches such as Support Vector Machines. The proposed approach achieved a classification accuracy of 97.3%, which outperformed traditional approaches by a significant margin. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to the automatic screening of heart sounds, which has important implications for the early detection and diagnosis of cardiac diseases.

Keyword extraction is an indispensable step for many natural language processing and information retrieval applications such as; text summarization and search engine optimization. Keywords hold the most important information describing the content of a document. With the increasing volume and variety of unlabeled documents on the Internet, the need for automatic keyword extraction methods increases. Even though keyword extraction can be used in many applications, Arabic research in the field still lacking. In this paper, a supervised learning technique that uses statistical features and Support Vector Machine classifier was implemented and applied to extract the keywords from Arabic news documents. The proposed supervised learning approach achieved a precision of 0.77 and a recall of 0.58.

For machine-learning-based network traffic classification, we usually need large number of correctly labeled samples (ground truth) for model-training to get high accuracy. However in practical environments obtaining ground truth may be time-consuming and needs massive manual work, so achieving higher accuracy at low labeling rate is still a tricky problem. In this paper we propose a novel Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) based network traffic classification method named GCN-TC. We combine the traffic trace graph with statistical features in GCN model-training, so as to take advantage of both of them to achieve higher classification accuracy with very few labeled data. Experiment results show that the proposed model achieves the best performance with 13% higher in Fl-score and 7.7% higher in accuracy than the best method of the rest.

This paper presents a study on Protocol-Based Unscented Kalman Filtering (PB-UKF) technique, which takes into account the presence of stochastic uncertainties in nonlinear time-varying systems. PB-UKF is developed to address the limitations of the conventional Kalman filter, which cannot handle the nonlinearities in such systems. The technique employs protocols to model stochastic processes, which are used to generate approximations of the system's state. These approximations are then filtered through the unscented Kalman filter algorithm, resulting in a more accurate estimate of the system's state. The method is demonstrated through numerical examples, showing significant performance improvements compared to the conventional Kalman filter. Overall, this research contributes to the development of more accurate approximation algorithms that can handle the uncertainties present in nonlinear time-varying systems.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised method for temporal segmentation of videos using motion segmentation and trajectory analysis. The proposed method extracts key features from videos and applies clustering algorithms to segment the videos into different temporal segments. The segmentation is performed based on the similarity of motion trajectories in each segment. The proposed method has been tested on a variety of videos obtained from different cameras and conferences, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving accurate segmentation of videos. The proposed method can be applied in various fields, including computer vision, surveillance, and video analysis.

The high cost of generating expert annotations, poses a strong limitation for supervised machine learning methods in medical imaging. Weakly supervised methods may provide a solution to this tangle. In this study, we propose a novel deep learning architecture for multi-class classification of mammograms according to the severity of their containing anomalies, having only a global tag over the image. The suggested scheme further allows localization of the different types of findings in full resolution. The new scheme contains a dual branch network that combines region-level classification with region ranking. We evaluate our method on a large multi-center mammography dataset including ~3,000 mammograms with various anomalies and demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method over a previous weakly-supervised strategy.

This paper presents a performance comparison of a biometric system with and without Elevator Control System (EVCS) for palmprint authentication. The proposed visualization method enables the convenient inspection of the authentication results. The biometric system uses feature extraction algorithms to extract the unique features of the palmprint, which are then compared with the database for authentication. The advantages of using edge detection techniques in the image preprocessing step are highlighted. The EVCS system adds an extra layer of security by encrypting the biometric data during transmission. The results show that the performance of the biometric system with EVCS is superior to that without EVCS. This study shows that the inclusion of EVCS in biometric systems is advisable for secure and effective authentication.

This paper presents a study on the fault grading techniques used in software test libraries for safety-critical applications. The focus of the research is on circuit faults, where computational modelling and integrated circuit modelling techniques are employed in order to identify and grade such faults. The importance of safety and built-in self-test functionality is emphasised throughout the discussion, given the critical nature of the applications in question. Libraries play a central role in the fault grading process, helping to facilitate the development of effective testing strategies. In conclusion, the study highlights the importance of effective fault grading techniques in ensuring the safety and reliability of software used in safety-critical applications.

This paper explores the impact of data reduction on wearable-based human activity recognition. The study focuses specifically on feature extraction, with a particular emphasis on the thigh as an effective location for measuring activity. Context modeling is also considered as a key factor in optimizing accuracy in activity recognition. Principal component analysis is employed as a data reduction method in order to decrease the computational complexity of the recognition system. Additionally, time-domain analysis is used to further refine the accuracy of the recognition system. The results demonstrate that data reduction techniques can greatly enhance the accuracy of wearable-based human activity recognition systems, while also reducing computational requirements. The study provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners seeking to optimize activity recognition in wearable technology for applications such as rehabilitation, fitness monitoring, and elderly care.

This paper proposes a method for registration of discrete signals based on the soft computing concept. The approach is based on the theories of entropy, nonlinear distortion, fuzzy logic, fuzzy set theory, reliability and estimation. Soft computing techniques such as fuzzy clustering and fuzzy inference are utilized to register signals with high accuracy. The proposed method is compared with existing registration methods and is found to have superior performance. The results show that the soft computing approach can improve registration accuracy, reduce error, and increase reliability. The advantages of the method are discussed, and it is suggested that this approach can be used in a wide range of applications requiring precise registration of signals. In conclusion, the soft computing concept provides a promising approach for registration of discrete signals, and further research on this topic is recommended.

The increasing need for energy conservation and management in residential areas has prompted the development of non-intrusive load monitoring techniques. This paper proposes a practical solution for Type II load monitoring in homes, based on deep learning and post-processing. The study employs smart meters and uses Hidden Markov Models to disaggregate power demand into individual home appliances. The proposed method involves using convolutional neural networks to extract features from power usage data, before applying a post-processing algorithm to obtain appliance-level energy consumption. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches, achieving high accuracy and low error rates. The proposed solution is expected to be useful in a wide range of applications, including home automation, smart grids, and energy management systems. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of deep learning and post-processing techniques in improving non-intrusive load monitoring in residential settings.

In the field of edge computing, the development and implementation of an accurate and efficient age and gender classifier has become a critical task. To achieve this goal, researchers have turned to the study of biological neural networks and the computational modeling of face recognition systems. By examining the behavior of neurons and creating benchmark testing scenarios, computer architecture can be optimized for edge computing applications. Such optimization of the computer architecture ensures that edge computing systems can operate effectively and efficiently in real-world scenarios. Ultimately, the success of these endeavors will depend on the ability to leverage the latest technologies and techniques in order to create a system that is both scalable and accurate.

The Scramble Suit is a promising countermeasure to prevent Template Attacks, a class of Side-channel attacks that are becoming increasingly prevalent in modern computing systems. In this paper, we present a detailed Performance evaluation of the Scramble Suit, comparing its effectiveness against existing countermeasures. We also propose a Computational modeling approach to optimize the design of the Scramble Suit and increase its efficiency. Additionally, we discuss the potential for Design automation to make implementation of the Scramble Suit faster and more reliable. Finally, we explore the potential benefits of integrating the Scramble Suit into Hardware systems to create a robust defense against side-channel attacks. Overall, our findings suggest that the Scramble Suit is a promising and effective solution to the growing threat of Template Attacks, and should be seriously considered for implementation in modern computing systems.

This paper proposes the use of Artificial Immune System (AIS) for solving the Task Scheduling Problem in Multi-Processors Environment. The approach involves a method called "Task analysis", which is used to break down the tasks into smaller sub-tasks that can be easily managed. This is combined with the use of "Program processors", which are software components that are capable of handling the scheduling of tasks across multiple processors. The concept of "Immune system" is adopted in the form of a feedback mechanism that monitors the performance of the system and triggers responses when necessary. In addition, the mechanism of "Cloning" is used to ensure that the best scheduling solutions are retained and shared across the system. The application of "Artificial intelligence" methods further enhances the efficiency of the scheduling process. Overall, this approach provides an effective solution to the Processor scheduling problem, with the potential for significant improvements in performance and productivity.

This paper proposes a novel approach for resource optimization in 5G vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) using a hybrid-fuzzy logic guided genetic algorithm (H-FLGA). The aim is to improve quality of service (QoS) by efficiently managing resources in these complex networks. The proposed approach is based on a combination of fuzzy logic and genetic algorithms, which are used to make intelligent decisions and optimize resource allocation. The approach takes into account factors such as traffic density, network congestion, communication range, and available bandwidth. The results show that the H-FLGA approach can effectively optimize resources in 5G VANETs compared to traditional resource management techniques. This paper contributes to the fields of 5G mobile communication, computer architecture, and microprocessors by presenting a new approach to resource management in vehicular ad hoc networks.

The paper presents a gesture recognition system that utilizes depth information and convolutional neural network. The proposed system makes use of the skeletal information extracted from depth images and the thumb movements to generate a set of feature vectors. These feature vectors are used for image segmentation and feature extraction tasks in the recognition process. A convolutional neural network is then utilized to classify the segmented images and recognize the gestures made by the user. The proposed system also employs image color analysis to improve the accuracy of the recognition system. Experimental results show that the proposed approach is effective and achieves improved recognition accuracy compared to existing methods. The proposed system has potential applications in human-computer interaction, virtual reality, and robotics.

This paper proposes a new approach to security analysis of Cyber-Physical Production Systems (CPPS) using generative adversarial network modeling, or GAN-Sec. This method involves the use of analytical and data models to train GANs on CPPS data, which can generate realistic training data. The use of GANs for security analysis allows for the creation of computational models that can identify patterns in CPPS data and detect anomalies. The paper discusses the advantages of using GANs for security analysis and provides an overview of the data models and training data used in the study. Additionally, the paper explores the use of random variables in GAN-Sec modeling and highlights the potential benefits of this approach for improving the accuracy of security analysis in CPPS. Overall, this study shows that GAN-Sec can be an effective method for security analysis of CPPS and provides a foundation for future research in this area.

The time-variant vehicle-to-vehicle radio propagation channel in the frequency band from 59.75 to 60.25 GHz has been measured in an urban street in the city center of Vienna, Austria. We have measured a set of 30 vehicle-to-vehicle channel realizations to capture the effect of an overtaking vehicle. Our experiment was designed for characterizing the large-scale fading and the small-scale fading depending on the overtaking vehicle's position. We demonstrate that large overtaking vehicles boost the mean receive power by up to 10 dB. The analysis of the small-scale fading reveals that the two-wave with diffuse power (TWDP) fading model is adequate. By means of the model selection, we demonstrate the regions where the TWDP model is more favorable than the customarily used the Rician fading model. Furthermore, we analyze the time selectivity of our vehicular channel. To precisely define the Doppler and delay resolutions, a multitaper spectral estimator with discrete prolate spheroidal windows is used. The delay and Doppler profiles are inferred from the estimated local scattering function. Spatial filtering by the transmitting horn antenna decreases the delay and Doppler spread values. We observe that the RMS Doppler spread is below one-tenth of the maximum Doppler shift 2f v/c. For example, at 60 GHz, a relative speed of 30 km/h yields a maximum Doppler shift of approximately 3300 Hz. The maximum RMS Doppler spread of all observed vehicles is 450 Hz; the largest observed RMS delay spread is 4 ns.

This paper presents the method that recognizes the road boundary situation from a single image and detects a driving lane based on the recognition result. Driving lane detection is important for lateral motion control of the vehicle and it usually realized based on lane mark detection. However, there are some roads where lane marks such as white lines are not drawn. Also, when the road is covered with snow, lane marks cannot be seen. In these cases, it's necessary to detect the boundary line between the roadside object and the road surfaces. Since traffic lanes are divided by various roadside objects, such as curbs, grass, walls and so on, it's difficult to detect all kinds of road boundary including lane marks by a single algorithm. Therefore, we propose the method which changes the driving lane detection method according to the road boundary situation. At first, the situation of the road boundary is identified as some classes, such as white line, curb, grass and so on, by the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Then, based on this result, the lane mark or the boundary between the road surface and the roadside object is detected as the lane boundary. When a clear lane mark is drawn on a road, this situation is identified as a class of "White line" and a lane mark is detected as a lane boundary. On the other hand, when a lane mark is not present, this situation is identified as the other class and the boundary of the roadside object corresponding to the identified class is detected as the lane boundary. Experimental results using the KITTI dataset and our own dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed method. In addition, the result of the proposed method is compared with the boundary of the road area extracted by some semantic segmentation method.

In LTE/LTE-A networks, femtocells are used to improve service coverage in indoor environments. Cognitive radio allows femtocell users to share the available spectrum with primary macrocell users. However, some issues arise because of the coexistence between femtocells and macrocells. These issues include but not limited to mitigating interference and fair distribution of network resources. In this paper, we use NSGA II to solve a multi-objective optimization problem that maximizes resource utilization while minimizing interference and guaranteeing fairness among users in a femtocell LTE/LTE-A network. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme improves the multi-objective function score by 8% and enhances the overall performance of the network.

Adding the feature of business process event prediction to information systems increases its productivity in the long run, enhances the quality of the taken decisions, and eliminates inconsistencies. Inspired by the previous works of employing deep learning approaches to predicting the next process event based on files of logged events, we propose the use of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) to address the same problem. In the proposed approach we used a five-layer 1D CNN method to predict the next process event based on the previous instances. This paper compared the proposed approach with other approaches that used recurrent neural networks (RNN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks, and others on eight datasets. The proposed approach outperformed all the previous studies of the state-of-the-art in this domain on all the provided datasets.

This work presents the development of a Network-on-Chip environment based on multiagent systems. This simulator aims to provide high level of abstraction to quickly simulate, compare and choose routing algorithms. The simulator calculates routers occupancy rate, number of messages that passed through each router and the number of messages lost. As a case study, the XY and West-First routing algorithms were modeled and analyzed. Simulation results indicated a better use of spare routers by the West-First algorithm when compared to the XY algorithm.

In scientific computing, it is important to achieve high performance while minimizing energy consumption. This paper proposes a roofline model based performance-aware energy management approach for scientific computing. The approach utilizes analytical models to predict the performance of computational kernels while considering the bandwidth of the memory subsystem. A mathematical model is then used to estimate the energy consumption of the kernel. By using the roofline model to map the performance of kernels to energy efficiency, the proposed approach can identify the optimal energy-efficient operating point for a given kernel. The approach is evaluated using benchmarks from the SPEC CPU2006 and NAS parallel benchmarks. The results show that the proposed approach can achieve significant energy savings without sacrificing performance. This approach provides a useful tool for performance-aware energy management in scientific computing.

We focus on the computation methods for analyzing the bumblebee behavior. In this paper, we recover the smooth 3D trajectory for flying bumblebee by stereo vision by employing EKF. We also tackle the matching problem when more than one targets appeared in the views. A variable length sliding window method is proposed to segment the 3D trajectory into three basic types. In our experiment, we show our method has more accuracy result than the state art of work.

The airborne electromagnetic (AEM) method is an efficient tool for assessing conductivity structures near the earth's surface. The huge amounts of collected data over a survey area of tens to thousands of square kilometers result in an extremely high computational cost for rigorous modeling. Fortunately, for each transmitter and receiver (Tx-Rx) station, a volume of limited scale beneath the transmitter, called the footprint, contains the majority of the induced current and contributes most of the EM response at the receiver. In this letter, we develop a footprint-guided compact finite element method (CFEM), in which the inhomogeneous conductivity structure in the entire survey area is divided into small subareas based on the footprint so that the forward modeling for each subarea can be performed efficiently. The computational domain for every single Tx-Rx station consists of a small subarea and a surrounding layer. The accuracy of the algorithm is verified by comparing its solutions with semianalytical solutions on a layered earth model, and its applicability and efficiency are demonstrated with a more complex 3-D model consisting of a large inhomogeneous structure.

This paper presents a distributed modeling approach for the design of linear millimeter wave (mmW) applications using a four-port transistor. The research focuses on integrated circuit modeling, scattering parameters, and solid modeling techniques to aid in the analysis and optimization of the system. The four-port transistor is based on high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), which are fabricated using Gallium arsenide (GaAs). Computational modeling is applied to accurately represent the transistor's behavior in various operating conditions. By utilizing distributed modeling, the design of linear mmW applications is made more efficient, allowing for more precise and accurate analysis of the system. The proposed methodology can be applied to other similar systems to improve overall performance and design.

This paper conducts a survey of online social networks (OSNs) threats and proposes solutions for better privacy protection. Privacy is a major concern for OSN users with personal information being potentially exposed. Computer crime, such as phishing, is a primary threat to privacy in OSNs. Twitter is identified as the most vulnerable OSN due to its high volume of users and lack of privacy settings. The paper proposes a solution using feature extraction techniques to identify potential phishing attacks and prevent them from occurring. Overall, this survey sheds light on the continuing need for improved privacy protection in OSNs, and proposes solutions that could help mitigate the risks associated with computer crime.

Construction project management is a complex task that relies heavily on the accurate localization of resources. With the advent of modern technologies, such as global positioning systems (GPS) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), this task has become more streamlined. In this study, we propose a construction resource localization platform based on a UAV-RFID system, which incorporates GPS receivers and machine learning algorithms. The platform utilizes RFID tags as the core component for resource tracking and localization, while the UAVs provide a flexible means of transportation and data collection. The GPS receivers ensure precise positioning of the UAVs, resulting in accurate location data for the tagged resources. Additionally, we employed machine learning techniques to enhance the platform's ability to learn and adapt to changes in the construction environment. Our results show that the proposed system can significantly improve construction resource localization accuracy, thus providing valuable insights for the effective management of construction projects.

The study focuses on improving cross-corpus speech emotion recognition through the use of Adversarial Discriminative Domain Generalization (ADDoG). The study aims to improve the performance of speech recognition systems by tackling the challenge of dealing with variations in the emotional content of speech across different datasets. The use of ADDoG has been proposed as a method to ensure that the speech processing and data models used in training are robust enough to handle different emotional content in speech. The study has shown that ADDoG can effectively improve the performance of speech recognition systems, particularly in scenarios where there is limited training data available. Additionally, the use of generative adversarial networks in ADDoG has shown promising results in improving speech emotion recognition performance. Overall, the findings of the study have significant implications for the development and optimization of speech recognition systems, with potential applications in areas such as automated emotion analysis and mental health assessment.

Forecasting fine-grained network traffic is crucial for many network management and optimization tasks such as traffic engineering, anomaly detection, network accounting, network analytics, load balancing, and traffic matrix estimation. However, building models that are able to predict a wide-variety of network traffic types is not a trivial task due to a) the diversity of network traffic, and b) the computational challenges in processing large datasets to train the prediction models. In this paper, we present a network traffic prediction framework that uses real network traces from a Tier-1 ISP to train a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network and generate predictions at short time scales (≤ 30 seconds). In order to reduce the number of models needed to capture the very diverse dynamics of the various traffic sources, we develop a feature-based clustering framework that acts as a preprocessing step in order to group similar time-series together and train a single model for each group. Our extensive experimental evaluation study shows that LSTMs can indeed be used to predict network traffic with low prediction errors.

Recently, Pan/Tilt/Zoom (PTZ) camera has been widely used in video surveillance systems. However, it is difficult to automatically control PTZ cameras according to moving objects in the surveillance area. This paper proposes an automatic camera control method based on a Deep-Q Network (DQN) for improving the recognition accuracy of anomaly actions in the video surveillance system. To generate PTZ camera control values, the proposed method uses the position and size information of the object which received from the video analysis system. Through implementation results, the proposed method can automatically control the PTZ camera according to moving objects.

This paper proposes a joint power allocation and rate control approach for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-based space information networks. The proposed method aims to optimize the transmission rate and power allocation of multiple users, aiming to maximize the overall network performance. To achieve this, a mathematical model is introduced, which considers the channel conditions, channel estimation errors, and user priorities. In addition, various prediction algorithms and data mining techniques are employed to improve the system's predictive models. The complexity theory is also utilized to analyze the computational complexity of the proposed method, which shows that it has a lower complexity than existing approaches. The proposed method is evaluated through simulations, and the results show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of network throughput and energy efficiency. Finally, the software implementation and measurement of the proposed method are discussed, demonstrating its feasibility and robustness in practical applications.

Intelligent surveillance has become an increasingly important topic with the rise of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and the need for real-time monitoring. In this paper, we propose a new approach to intelligent surveillance called iSENSE, which utilizes lightweight detection and tracking algorithms. This system operates as an edge network service, with image edge detection and feature extraction taking place on device, and streaming media sent to a cloud server for intelligent analysis using machine learning algorithms. Real-time monitoring is achieved through the use of cloud computing and edge networks, allowing for quick response times and efficient data management. This system has the potential to greatly enhance surveillance capabilities, with its ability to operate on a large scale and rapidly analyze large amounts of data. With the increasing demand for intelligent surveillance systems, iSENS brings a new option for improving the security and safety of people and property.

The goal of this study is to dynamically assess the posture and balance of individuals with spinal cord injury and able-bodied controls during robotic-assisted gait, using the EksoGT™ and ReWalk™, by examining their 3-D whole body, trunk and lower-extremity CoM excursions and their sagittal trunk lean angle during baseline and post-training (>100 hours). At baseline, there were strong differences (p<;0.05) between the devices where CoM excursions, root-mean-squared-errors between the trunk and lower-extremity CoMs and a trend for significance in trunk lean angle were much greater in the ReWalk™ than EksoGT™. These differences further increased post-training, particularly in the EksoGT™.

In this paper, we propose a classification framework for 3D hyperspectral data. Discriminative features are extracted through applying Non-negative Tensor Factorization (NTF) technique to the image tensor. The factorized components indicate the spectral signatures and 2D abundance maps of the constituent materials. We use a composite kernel Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) classifier. The obtained abundance matrices for training samples, constitute the spatial features which are fed to the classifier. Applying NTF, the spatial structure of the image is preserved in contrast to matrix factorization methods. We have also analyzed the effect of exploiting band group NTF; Instead of decomposing the image over whole spectral bands, we split the spectra into several band groups and apply the NTF algorithm to each sub-band. The abundance maps obtained for these band groups construct the spatial features. The original image cube makes the spectral features. The spatial and spectral kernels are acquired and stacked to form the training feature vector. This way, both spectral properties and spatial structure are effectively exploited to achieve higher classification accuracy. The experiments are performed on a widely studied hyperspectral dataset. Superior classification performance is attained using the proposed training features compared to NMF. We also compare the MLR with SVM classifier.

This paper presents a crane anti-sway control system with sway angle feedback. Cranes are widely used in construction sites and manufacturing plants, but the unpredictable sway of the payload makes these machines difficult to operate. A mathematical model is developed to describe the dynamics of crane movements, and a computational modeling approach is used to simulate the performance of the anti-sway control system. Gyroscopes are utilized to provide accurate feedback of the sway angle, which is then used to adjust the control inputs and counteract the sway of the payload. The proposed system is shown to effectively stabilize the crane and reduce the oscillations caused by payloads. Finally, the application of this crane anti-sway control system is discussed in the context of bridge construction, where precise control of crane movements is critical to ensure safety and efficiency.

This paper presents a flexible UVM-based verification framework that can be reused with Avalon, AHB, AXI and Wishbone bus interfaces for an AES encryption module. The framework is designed to measure performance parameters such as bandwidth and data models, while considering encryption protocols and IP network standards. The authors highlight the importance of verification in ensuring the correct functionality and interoperability of encryption modules. The proposed framework allows for efficient verification of various interfaces, reducing development time and costs. The use of UVM and various bus interfaces enables modularity and flexibility in design, facilitating easier integration with different systems. Overall, this paper proposes a comprehensive verification framework that ensures proper compliance with encryption protocols and provides a flexible approach towards the verification of a range of bus interfaces.

We consider the use of a wireless body area network (WBAN) for remote health monitoring applications. A partially observable Markov decision process is used to describe the information flow and behavior of the WBAN. We then discuss a sensor activation policy, used for optimizing the tradeoff between power consumption and probability of patient health state misclassification. In order to determine the underlying health state transition probabilities, by which a patient's health state evolves, we develop a learning algorithm which uses the data collected from a group of patients, each being monitored by a WBAN. Finally, a numerical examination demonstrates the applicability of such a system, which applies the learning process and sensor activation policy simultaneously.

Human action recognition is an active research topic which is having real time challenges. Some of the challenges are speed of action, background noise and shape of the performing action. To handle these problem, in this paper the following works are proposed. By the help of optical flow, Bag of Bag of histogram of optical flow (BoHOF) is proposed which is useful to differentiate actions varying with speed of action. BoHOF features are calculated from segmented human objects. To remove the shadow effect, sobel edge filter is used combingly in horizontal and vertical direction. Median filtering is applied to suppress background noise. Histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) features are extracted from 3D projected planes and combined with BoHOF to extract maximum advantages of both the features. Finally, the multi-class SVM-based classifier with radial basis kernel is applied to recognize different human actions. The experiments are conducted on the benchmark KTH dataset and the experimental findings concludes that the proposed HAR technique provides better performance compared to the state-of-the-art techniques.

During disasters, discover people's concerns dynamically is crucial to disaster rescue and relief. In this paper, we propose a social media based framework to analyze people's concerns, to access the importance and to track the dynamic changes of these concerns. To better understand people's concerns across platforms and to monitor the dynamics, we make comparisons between Tweets and news on the mentioned aspects and disclosed some interesting findings. Specifically, we take 2018 Camp Fire, the most destructive wildfire on record in history of California as a case study. We find that despite their keen attentions towards the disaster, social media and news media focus on different aspects of the disaster, so are the contents and dynamic changes of their concerns.

This paper explores the importance of proprioceptive feedback in the process of self-other differentiation. Proprioceptive feedback refers to the information received by the body's sensory receptors during movement. The paper discusses the use of visualization and predictive models in understanding the role of proprioceptive feedback. It also considers the application of this knowledge in the design of robot sensing systems using computational modeling. The paper further emphasizes the importance of training and visual perception in the integration of proprioceptive feedback. The insights provided by this research could significantly improve current methods in self-other differentiation, particularly in the development of efficient and effective robot sensing systems.

This paper presents a user-centered design approach to developing an athlete-trainer interaction dashboard for performance analysis. The dashboard provides valuable data visualization and monitoring tools that assist both athletes and trainers in tracking and improving training regimes. The information systems utilized in the dashboard enable effective communication between athletes and trainers, facilitating an interactive and collaborative training environment. The dashboard has been designed with a focus on the European market, with features and functionalities tailored to meet the specific demands of European athletes and trainers. Overall, this dashboard provides a comprehensive solution to athlete-trainer interaction, enhancing training efficiencies and ultimately improving performance outcomes.

Device-to-device (D2D) communications-enabled dense heterogeneous networks (HetNets) with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are promising solutions to meet the high-throughput requirement and support massive connectivity. In this paper, we propose a novel framework on the D2D-enabled HetNets with NOMA, where small cells underlay the uplink spectrum of macrocells to make full use of spectrum resources, NOMA technique is invoked to serve more downlink users simultaneously, and D2D-enabled multi-hop transmission is established to enhance signal reception of the far users (FUs) on cell edge. We investigate joint power allocation and user scheduling to maximize the ergodic sum rate of the near users (NUs) in the small cells while guaranteeing the quality-of-service requirements of the FUs and the macro-cell users. The optimal solution to this problem is complexity-prohibitive especially with large numbers of users and small base stations (SBSs) because it requires an exhaustive search over all possible combinations of SBSs, NUs, and FUs. To simplify the solution, we develop a two-step approach by decomposing the original problem into a power allocation problem and a user scheduling problem. We derive the closed-form solution of the power allocation problem via analyzing the objective function and constraints. The user scheduling problem is a joint user pairing and access point assignment problem. To solve it, we propose an SBS-NU-FU matching algorithm to obtain a near-optimal one-to-one three-sided matching of SBSs, NUs, and FUs. The simulation results show that the two-step method gets around 95% of the system throughput of the optimal one and can significantly improve the spectral efficiency of the D2D-enabled HetNets.

In this letter, we apply ensemble learning methods for the prediction of the ground (cellular base station) to air (flying node) received signal strength (RSS) at different heights, for future mobile communications. We model the RSS using different ensemble methods. Moreover, we propose a new ensemble method that combines results from five different methods. The proposed method also uses a recently introduced evolutionary algorithm, the Salp Swarm Algorithm, for weight optimization. The proposed method outperforms all the other methods and common ensemble methods. In this context, the produced results are compared to measurements using representative performance indices and exhibit satisfactory accuracy.

Wireless channels are increasingly being used to transmit highly sensitive information in the Internet of Things. However, traditional cryptography methods cannot solve all security problems in IoT systems. Covert wireless communication can prevent an adversary from knowing the existence of a user's transmission; thus, it can provide stronger security protection for IoT devices. In this article, we consider the covert communication in a noisy wireless network, and find that the uncertainty of the aggregated interference experienced by the adversary is beneficial to the potential transmitters. From the network perspective, wireless communications can be hidden in the interference of the noisy wireless network, which the adversary observes as a "shadow" network to a certain extent. Furthermore, we discuss some new results on the effect of active eavesdropper. Square root law becomes invalid, and even jammer-assisted schemes have little effect on the covertness in the presence of active eavesdropper. Finally, we provide a vision for future research.

This paper presents an improved adaptive path following control system for autonomous vehicles operating at different velocities. The proposed system employs adaptation and predictive models for task analysis, which enables the vehicle to track a given trajectory accurately even in high-speed scenarios. Fuzzy logic and neural networks are utilized as key components of the system, providing a robust and accurate control mechanism for the vehicle's turning and maneuvering. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through simulation and experimental results, indicating a significant improvement in the vehicle's path following control performance compared to existing approaches. Overall, the presented control system provides a promising solution for autonomous vehicle path following in real-world scenarios with varying velocities.

Coastal surveillance systems require robust and reliable tools for detecting and tracking targets in complex maritime environments. In this paper, we propose a novel ATR (Automatic Target Recognition) tool for Pulse Doppler Radars that can significantly improve the performance of radar tracking and target recognition. The proposed tool employs an advanced feature extraction technique to extract discriminative features from the radar signals, which are then used to train predictive models to recognize target patterns. Additionally, the proposed tool incorporates advanced radar tracking algorithms that enable accurate and reliable target tracking in complex coastal environments. Overall, our results demonstrate that the proposed ATR tool outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of target detection and tracking accuracy, and can provide significant benefits to coastal surveillance systems.

This work proposes a novel mathematical approach to accurately model data traffic for the Internet of Things (IoT). Most of the conventional results on statistical data traffic models for IoT are based on the underlying assumption that the data generation follows standard Poisson or Exponential distribution which lacks experimental validation. However, in some of the use case applications a single statistical distribution is not adequate to provide the best fit for the inter-arrival time of the data packets generation. Based on the real data collected for over 10 weeks using our customized experimental IoT prototype for smart home application, in this paper we have established this very fact, citing barometric air pressure as an example. The statistical distribution of the inter-arrival time between the data packets for a specified barometric pressure fluctuation threshold is initially determined by approximating the best-fit with a set of standard classical distributions. The goodness-of-fit with the empirical data is numerically quantified using Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) Test. Furthermore, it is observed that any single standard distribution is unable to provide a good fit which is at least less than 10%. Therefore, a novel weighted distribution scheme is proposed that could provide an acceptable fit. The weighing factor including the location, scaling and weighing parameters of the best fitting distribution are estimated and analyzed. The distribution parameters are finally expressed as a function of the differential pressure value that can be used for different theoretical analysis and network optimization.

This paper focuses on the implementation of smart grids based on the Internet of Things (IoT) technology and supported by intelligent edge computing. Smart grids are a crucial element in the development of sustainable energy systems, and their implementation requires the use of advanced technologies such as IoT, edge computing, and cloud computing. The adoption of intelligent edge computing as a support system for smart grids complements cloud-based solutions and provides real-time data analysis and decision-making capabilities. Industries can benefit from the deployment of smart grids, as they rely on sensors and real-time systems to optimize energy efficiency and improve the overall performance of their operations. The integration of IoT and edge computing into smart grids provides a more scalable and efficient approach to managing energy systems, and this paper explores the potential benefits and challenges of this approach. Ultimately, this research aims to promote the sustainable development of energy systems by providing a robust platform to support energy-efficient operations and reduce carbon emissions.

Human mobility prediction is of great importance in a wide range of modern applications in different fields such as personalized recommendation systems, the fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication systems, and so on. Generally, the prediction goal varies from different application scenarios. For the applications of 5G network including resource allocation and mobility management, it is essential to predict the positions of mobile users in the near future from dozens of seconds to a few minutes so as to make preparation in advance, which is actually a trajectory prediction problem. In this paper, with the particular focus on multi-user multi-step trajectory prediction, we first design a basic deep learning-based prediction framework, where the long short-term memory (LSTM) network is directly applied as the most critical component to learn user-specific mobility pattern from the user's historical trajectories and predict his/her movement trends in the future. Motivated by the related findings after testifying and analyzing this basic framework on a model-based dataset, we extend it to a region-oriented prediction scheme and propose a multi-user multi-step trajectory prediction framework by further incorporating the sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) learning. The experimental results on a realistic dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework has significant improvements on generalization ability and reduces error-accumulation effect for multi-step prediction.

We study the problem of distributed state estimation in a network of sensing units that can exchange their measurements but the communication between the units is constrained. The units collect noisy, possibly only partial observations of the unknown state; they are assisted by a scheduler which organizes the exchange of measurements between the units. We consider the task of minimizing the total mean-square estimation error of the network while promoting balance between the individual units' performances. This problem is formulated as the maximization of a monotone objective function subject to a cardinality constraint. By leveraging the notion of weak submodularity, we develop an efficient greedy algorithm for the proposed formulation and show that the greedy algorithm achieves a constant factor approximation of the optimal objective. Our extensive simulation studies illustrate the efficacy of the proposed formulation and the greedy algorithm.

Recently, with the advent of "big data" era, cloud storage has become an indispensable part of the data transmission and storage system. However, data security and privacy are becoming more and more important issues due to the increasing amount of sensitive data being stored remotely. Cryptography has been widely used to enhance the security of data transmission and storage in cloud computing and various protocols have been developed to improve data privacy. This paper proposes a data sharing protocol with cryptographic techniques that can minimize the security and privacy risks of cloud storage in the era of big data. The protocol consists of two main phases: encryption and decryption. In the encryption phase, data is encrypted using homomorphic encryption, which allows computation to be carried out on cipher-text without the need for decryption. In the decryption phase, the cipher-text is decrypted using a secret key that is shared between users. By implementing the proposed protocol, the security and privacy of cloud storage in big data era can be significantly enhanced. As an example, the proposed protocol can be applied to medical diagnostic imaging, where patient privacy is of paramount importance, to provide a secure and privacy-preserving cloud storage solution.

The article presents a mathematical model for forecasting life expectancy via insurance Lee-Carter mortality function, utilizing predictive models and computational modeling techniques. The paper highlights the use of data models for creating neural networks that can predict patterns in life expectancy rates. The proposed model allows insurance companies to better evaluate individual and population risk, and make more informed decisions regarding insurance policies. Through the implementation of this model, insurers can offer more accurate premiums and provide better policies to their customers. The study provides a valuable contribution to both the fields of actuarial science and computational mathematics and opens up areas for further research.

The next generation of mobile systems are expected to support the new promising Machine-to-Machine (M2M) technology carried by the advance of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. In the near future, an exponential growth of the number of M2M devices is expected due to their ubiquity. In normal situations, a limited bandwidth in Narrow Band-Internet of Things (NB-IoT) technology may help in improving IoT requirements effectively. However, in emergency and disastrous moments, M2M expected storms lead inevitably to network saturations. In this manuscript, we propose a novel Adaptive eNodeB (A-eNB), which solves the network overload problem gradually, while keeping Human-to-Human (H2H) traffic not to be affected dreadfully. The network adaptation is provided through a dynamic NB-IoT bandwidth reservation aiming to increase the number of M2M connections accessing NB-IoT network with minimal overload congestion problems. A Continuous-Time Markov Chain (CTMC) is proposed helping the H2H/M2M coexistence to become more approachable especially during disaster scenarios. Our results show that by leasing 18 resource blocks using an A-eNB for NB-IoT traffic can result a completion rate of 98% on M2M traffic throughout emergency scenarios.

Existing methods for image captioning aim to generate captions in natural language by using the image attributes. Though these captions are enough to explain what the image is about in most cases, yet sometimes more than a single sentence is desired to describe the context of an image especially when a good caption for the image draws more public attention or 'likes' on a social media post. Though some work has been done to develop models that can generate hashtags for images, but no research work exists that can use those hashtags to create storylike captions. A hashtag can be defined as a word preceded by the symbol '#' and is used to identify an image on social media sites like Instagram. The goal of this application paper is to explore the possibility of generating hashtags for an input image and leverage it to generate meaningful anecdotes connecting to the essence of the image. The experiment conducted, uses an attention-based encoder-decoder framework to produce hashtags for the raw image while a character-level language model, which is trained using a multi-layer RNN, is used to generate stories using one of the suggested hashtags. The model was then tested on HARRISON dataset of Instagram images and the results were qualitatively analyzed through a user study. After analyzing the outcomes of the experiment, it was concluded that this area of research has huge prospects.

This research proposed a web-based monitoring system that can help to view in real time environment data like temperature and humidity. By using sensors connected to Arduino Microcontroller, the system collects data, transmits them to the Raspberry Pi Minicomputer which stores them on remote server and makes them available to Internet users. We use Wi-Fi Router based on GSM/GPRS Module as the network unity to send collected environment data to ThingSpeak web server. A supervisor through a dashboard monitors various data. The system can help to resolve emergencies. In this way, it simultaneously improves the quality of the environment through constant attention. This project enters in the concept of Internet of Things which consists of integrating the real-world into the Internet.

This paper proposes a unified mathematical model using Poisson cluster processes to analyze heterogeneous networks (HetNets) under the condition of maximum power association. The paper considers the impact of couplings and interference in cellular networks and evaluates signal to noise ratio to enhance wireless communication. The analytical models developed in this study provide deep insights into the behavior of HetNets and its capacity. The model allows efficient resource allocation by detecting interference-induced problems and understanding the impact of different network settings. The results prove the effectiveness of the proposed model in managing the intricate and diverse HetNets. Overall, this study enables researchers to investigate and optimize network performance for HetNets.

This document presents a learning system architecture for the practice of the cannulation procedure for medical students in cardiovascular specialization. The architecture is composed of three modules that support the practice and learning of this surgical procedure; surgical instrumentation, hygiene and simulation of the cannulation. The architecture rests on different multimedia technologies that allow an autonomous practice but that may be supervised by the teacher. In the document are discussed the context, the need for tools for this medical practice, an architectural design of the proposed system and a comparison with the current practices in medicine programs.

Smart meters have become the backbone of modern power grids, and their integration has led to the formation of smart grid networks. However, this integration has opened up new avenues for cyber attackers to disrupt the operations of the power grid, thus jeopardising the reliability of power supply. To counter these threats, advanced metering infrastructure with reliable and secure features is essential. Cloud computing and real-time systems are used to enhance the performance of the system, and cryptographic techniques are adopted to ensure secure data transmission. Encoding algorithms such as Reed-Solomon codes are used to handle data loss due to communication errors. In this paper, we propose a secure and reliable advanced metering infrastructure with enhanced metering functionality, which provides efficient and dependable data transmissions between the consumer and the utility company. The proposed approach considers the limitations of existing meters and handles new functionalities, thereby improving system reliability, protection and safety.

This paper presents the development of a voltage source converter (VSC) using a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) simulation system. The VSC is an important component in renewable energy systems and drives, therefore its accurate simulation and testing is crucial. Computational modeling and mathematical models were utilized to design the VSC, and pulse width modulation techniques were implemented to control the switching behavior. In addition, semiconductor device modeling was taken into consideration to improve the accuracy of the simulation. The HiL simulation system allowed real-time testing of the VSC to ensure its optimal performance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the VSC development using HiL simulation, which can potentially be implemented in various practical applications. Further research in this field may involve the optimization of the system under different load and environmental conditions.

Future smart vehicles will incorporate high-data-rate communications and high-resolution radar sensing capabilities operating in the millimeter- wave and higher frequencies. These two systems are preparing to share and reuse many common functionalities, such as steerable millimeter- wave antenna arrays. Motivated by this growing overlap, which is advanced further by space and cost constraints, the vehicular community is pursuing a vision of unified vehicular communications and radar sensing that represents a major paradigm shift for next-generation connected and self-driving cars. This article outlines a path to materialize this decisive transformation. We begin by reviewing the latest developments in hybrid vehicular communications and radar systems, and then propose a concept of unified channel access over millimeter-wave and higher frequencies. Our supporting system-level performance characterization relies upon real-life measurements and extensive ray-based modeling to confirm the significant improvements brought by our proposal to mitigating the interference and deafness effects. Since our results aim to open the door to unified vehicular communications and radar sensing, we conclude by outlining the potential research directions in this rapidly developing field.

A methodology is proposed (and illustrated on exemplary cases) for detecting keypoints in such a way that usability of those keypoints in image matching tasks can be potentially maximized. Following the approach used for MSER detection, we localize keypoints at image patches for which the selected keypoint descriptor is maximally stable under fluctuations of the parameter(s) (e.g. image threshold, scale, shift, etc.) determining how configurations of those patches evolve. In this way, keypoint descriptors are used in the scenarios where descriptors' volatility due to minor image distortions is minimized and, thus, performances of keypoint matching are prospectively maximized. Experimental verification on selected types of keypoint descriptors fully confirmed this hypothesis. Additionally, a novel concept of semi-dense feature representation of images (based on the proposed methodology) has been preliminarily discussed and illustrated (and its prospective links with deep learning and tracking applications highlighted).

Traffic flow prediction is important in modern traffic control and induction. Short-term traffic flow prediction plays an important role in urban traffic navigation planning and traffic optimization control. Due to the advantage in processing of time series data, LSTM is very suitable for predicting short-term traffic flow. This paper builds a deep learning model based on LSTM to predict the traffic flow volume. In experiment, we build models with different hyper parameters, compared and analyzed the performance of different models.

This paper presents an exploration of complex-valued nonlinear adaptive filters and their applications in alpha-stable environments. Adaptation models are developed through the use of mathematical models and random processes, leading to the development of analytical models for the filters. The adaptation process is analyzed for convergence properties, and a cost function is defined to optimize the filter's performance. Additionally, the paper touches on the application of these filters in integrated circuit modeling. Overall, this work provides a foundation for the use of complex-valued nonlinear adaptive filters in challenging signal processing environments.

Social networks' comments are rich sources of information that may be fused with audio-visual contents to improve emotional video retrieval systems. The rationale behind this fusion is that different sources can complement each other since they have different natures, formats, and origins. Although emotional information expressed in users' comments on the Web is in accordance with the emotional audio-visual content of videos, they are not synchronized. In order to address this problem, decision-level fusion is needed when such asynchronous modalities should be fused. In this article, a new decision-level fusion approach based on Ordered Weighted Averaging (OWA) operators is proposed. In this approach, emotion is first detected based on the audio, video, and users' comments and then, individual decisions are fused using the OWA method. The proposed method is evaluated on the music videos of the standard DEAP data set. The results of comparing the proposed method with average, product, sum, and Dempster-Shafer fusion methods show that the proposed OWA-based method outperforms other methods in different fusion settings.

Wind power has become one of the leading clean and inexhaustible power sources of today's electricity generation. Wind turbines are significantly evolving with tremendous benefits, resulting in remarkable demand of installing and establishing new wind farms. One of the central dilemmas that face wind turbine is the unplanned downtime that considered to be one of the main revenue-loss factors of a modern wind farm [1]. In a medium scale wind farm, the sensor fiber network is subject to fail due to the harsh environment leading to corruption of the signals used for condition monitoring. Due to the reasons above, the wind turbine is subject to be shut down because of not received sensor data via the wind turbine health monitoring system. Additionally, the shutdown mostly is not required since there are no high threshold sensor values that are related to stress on specific turbine hardware. Thus, in this paper, we propose a software-defined Network (SDN) quadcopter system that is based on a cloud testbed cluster as an immediate fail-over recovery system for faulty sensors to provide continuous sensor readings with no interruptions.
