Our proposed system helps in preventing the unnecessary shutdown of a wind turbine which will result in continuous revenues with no losses and reduce any power shortage overhead that may affect the power grid. The SDN controller is virtualized on the cluster with full topology management on sensor nodes. We have used Real-time wind turbine sensor data to simulate the failure scenario and, extensive testing showed the reliability of our proposed SDN testbed to assess the wind turbine condition and to maintain continuous power generation.

This paper describes and evaluates the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for path planning in support of smart mobility applications such as indoor and outdoor navigation applications, individualized wayfinding for people with disabilities (e.g., vision impairments, physical disabilities, etc.), path planning for evacuations, robotic navigations, and path planning for autonomous vehicles. We propose an architecture based on GANs to recommend accurate and reliable paths for navigation applications. The proposed system can use crowd-sourced data to learn the trajectories and infer new ones. The system provides users with generated paths that help them navigate from their local environment to reach a desired location. As a use case, we experimented with the proposed method in support of a wayfinding application in an indoor environment. Our experiments assert that the generated paths are correct and reliable. The accuracy of the classification task for the generated paths is up to 99% and the quality of the generated paths has a mean opinion score of 89%.

This paper proposes a new grouping-based grant-free random access scheme for wireless communication systems, based on the statistical distribution of user rates. The proposed scheme adopts a closed-loop control design and utilizes several adaptive control techniques, including Lyapunov methods and backstepping, to improve performance and ensure stability of the system. Additionally, the proposed scheme employs tuning techniques to adapt to changing network conditions and optimize performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms existing grant-free random access schemes based on conventional approaches, highlighting its potential for use in future wireless communication systems.

This paper proposes a Deep Learning AI Application to an Electroencephalography (EEG) driven Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Smart Wheelchair. The wheelchair is designed to provide an alternative mobility solution for individuals who are unable to use traditional wheelchairs due to physical disabilities. The EEG signals generated from the user's brain are captured by electrodes placed on the scalp and processed by a Deep Learning algorithm. The algorithm is trained to recognize specific patterns in the EEG data and translate them into control signals for the wheelchair's DC motors. The wheelchair is also equipped with headphones and sensors to allow for real-time feedback and monitoring of the user's cognitive state. The proposed system shows promising results in terms of accuracy and speed of control, indicating a potential for future development and commercialization.

In this research, we proposed a feature selection based serial SVM ensemble classifier for cancer detection. Support vector machines were employed as the primary classification algorithm, and the proposed framework allowed for the selection of optimal features through feature extraction and optimization processes. The measurement of feature relevance was based on a correlation-based feature selection metric. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we applied it to a dataset containing nickel-related cancer patients. Results demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed algorithm compared to existing methods. Specifically, our method achieved an accuracy of 90.4% with only 8 features, while existing methods required 10 or more features to achieve comparable accuracy. Overall, the proposed framework is a promising method for developing accurate and efficient cancer detection systems.

In recent years, Event-based Social Networks (ESNs) have been widely used for communication and information sharing. The popularity of groups in these networks plays a critical role in determining the overall success of a social network. In this paper, we focus on predicting the popularity of new groups in ESNs using a combination of feature extraction, measurement, and mathematical modeling techniques. Our proposed model utilizes chemical reactions to simulate the growth of groups and factor in various factors such as group size, activity levels, and social interactions. We experimentally validate our model on two well-known ESNs, Facebook and Twitter, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately predicting group popularity. Our research contributes towards a better understanding of group growth mechanisms in ESNs and provides insights for developing effective group recommendation systems.

This paper presents a methodology for accurate state of charge estimation for ternary batteries in electric vehicles. The approach utilizes a Spherical Simplex-Radial Cubature Kalman Filter to estimate the state of charge of the batteries. The mathematical model of the battery is integrated with circuit modeling and computational modeling to simulate different driving conditions and estimate state of charge more accurately. The proposed methodology is compared with traditional methods and is found to be significantly more accurate in state of charge estimation. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is a promising tool for the state of charge estimation of ternary batteries in electric vehicles, leading to better utilization of energy and improved efficiency of the vehicle.

Automated driving is expected to improve road safety and traffic efficiency. Host vehicle onboard sensing systems typically sense the environment up to 250 m ahead of the vehicle. Today's LiDARs can see approximately 120 m, and recognition of small objects, such as animals or dropped cargo, however, today reliably drop when range is more than 50m. Connected driving adds an electronic horizon to the onboard sensing system which could extend the sensing range and greatly improves the efficiency. Therefore, collaborative sensing in which the vehicle exchanges not only status messages but also real data has recently been intensively discussed. Current cellular 3G/4G networks have enhanced the downlink capacity for sharing large data blocks. However, uplink is limited and therefore vehicles are unable to share point clouds of what they see in front. This article investigates the opportunities of 5G-based cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) collaborative sensing based on the results of trials conducted at test sites in China and Finland. The results indicate that the round-trip is stable (<; 60 ms) even when exchanging 1 MB/s between vehicles. Finally, the automotive industry perspective is taken into account in identifying and prioritizing potential use case scenarios for utilizing 5G based connected driving applications.

Workflow systems promise scientists an automated end-to-end path from hypothesis to discovery. However, expecting any single workflow system to deliver such a wide range of capabilities is impractical. A more practical solution is to compose the end-to-end workflow from more than one system. With this goal in mind, the integration of task-based and in situ workflows is explored, where the result is a hierarchical heterogeneous workflow composed of subworkflows, with different levels of the hierarchy using different programming, execution, and data models. Materials science use cases demonstrate the advantages of such heterogeneous hierarchical workflow composition.

Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) has been widely used in blind source separation (BSS) for non-contact heartbeat detection. The use of NMF allows for the separation of heart sounds from other environmental noise sources, which is a common challenge in non-contact detection. The effectiveness of this technique can be evaluated using entropy measurements and prediction algorithms. To optimize the performance of the NMF-based BSS, training with a large dataset and data compression techniques are often applied. Machine learning algorithms can also be incorporated to enhance the accuracy of heartbeat detection. Loss measurement is an essential step in estimating the effectiveness of the separation technique. Overall, the use of NMF-based BSS for non-contact heartbeat detection has shown promising results in accurately separating and detecting heart sounds from noisy background signals.

The emerging Fifth Generation (5G) mobile networks have been attracting enormous attention from various stakeholders around the world. In particular, in the research community, prototyping 5G infrastructures and deploying 5G services have gained gears recently towards realising market-oriented 5G trials. However, accessing to and programming on real-world 5G infrastructure is almost prohibitive for most 5G researchers especially in academia. Therefore, it is critical to build realistic yet cost-efficient 5G infrastructure emulators for 5G research labs to enable credible 5G research activities. This paper proposes such a 5G infrastructure emulator that is able to emulate a realistic 5G network in a lab setting based on a small number of commercial-off-the-shelf servers by leveraging virtualization and other technologies. Moreover, this emulator allows a service provider to automatically deploy 5G services from `empty' machines through advanced automation. The emulation platform is described in details with the 5G infrastructure and service deployment procedure highlighted. Empirical results are presented to show the performance of the proposed emulator.

In this paper, a new observer is presented for discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems. The designed observer is a modified version of the recently developed regularized least square (RLS) observer. It leads to an estimator with almost zero or very small overshoot while keeping the settling time of the estimation error very short, a case which cannot be satisfied by the well-known observers available in the literature. The predicted estimate of the developed estimator is calculated from a weighted average of a set of predicted estimate of a set of points to be generated around the filtered estimate of the state vector at a given sampling instant of time. Through this approach, we get a highly accurate result of the predicted state vector, which intuitively leads to highly accurate filtered estimates of the states. The developed estimator can deal with highly nonlinear systems, does not need any state transformation, has no restrictions on the output measurement model, leads to a unique solution, and last but not least avoids the computation of the Jacobian matrices. The convergence of the proposed observer is analyzed, and the results show its superior performance when compared with the RLS observer. Moreover, a modified version of the developed observer is proposed to reduce the computational time while maintaining its main features. Illustrative examples of highly nonlinear power systems are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its superiority when compared with other well-known observers.

This study aims to categorize mergers and acquisitions (M&A) in Japan using corporate databases, with a focus on predicting M&A trends in companies, industries, and finance. The study utilizes principal component analysis and artificial intelligence techniques to analyze a large dataset of corporate M&A data from various sources. The results of this study provide valuable insights into the categorization of M&A in Japan, which can be beneficial for both investors and policymakers in predicting future M&A trends. Additionally, this study also highlights the importance of corporate databases and the potential for advanced analytical techniques to enhance M&A research. Overall, this study contributes to the growing body of research on M&A and provides a foundation for further research in this field.

CoMP transmission and reception have been considered in cellular networks for enabling larger coverage, improved rates, and interference mitigation. To harness the gains of coordinated beamforming, fast information exchange over a backhaul connecting the cooperating BSs is required. In practice, the bandwidth and delay limitations of the backhaul may not be able to meet such stringent demands. These impairments motivate the study of cooperative approaches based only on local CSI that require minimal or no information exchange between the BSs. To this end, several distributed approaches are introduced for CB-CoMP. The proposed methods rely on the channel reciprocity and iterative spatially precoded over-the-air pilot signaling. We elaborate how F-B training facilitates distributed CB by allowing BSs and UEs to iteratively optimize their respective transmitters/receivers based on only locally measured CSI. The trade-off due to the overhead from the F-B iterations is discussed. We also consider the challenge of dynamic TDD where the UE-UE channel knowledge cannot be acquired at the BSs by exploiting channel reciprocity. Finally, standardization activities and practical requirements for enabling the proposed F-B training schemes in 5G radio access are discussed.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have recently attracted considerable attention due to their outstanding accuracy in applications, such as image recognition and natural language processing. While one advantage of the CNNs over other types of neural networks is their reduced computational cost, faster execution is still desired for both training and inference. Since convolution operations pose most of the execution time, multiple algorithms were and are being developed with the aim of accelerating this type of operations. However, due to the wide range of convolution parameter configurations used in the CNNs and the possible data type representations, it is not straightforward to assess in advance which of the available algorithms will be the best performing in each particular case. In this paper, we present a performance evaluation of the convolution algorithms provided by the cuDNN, the library used by most deep learning frameworks for their GPU operations. In our analysis, we leverage the convolution parameter configurations from widely used the CNNs and discuss which algorithms are better suited depending on the convolution parameters for both 32 and 16-bit floating-point (FP) data representations. Our results show that the filter size and the number of inputs are the most significant parameters when selecting a GPU convolution algorithm for 32-bit FP data. For 16-bit FP, leveraging specialized arithmetic units (NVIDIA Tensor Cores) is key to obtain the best performance.

Use of electromagnetic modeling tools has significantly helped in analyzing human vital signs and gait. The paper will briefly discuss modeling efforts; radars used, and some recent simulated and measured results. This is a very important step in developing a practical 24/7 activity tracking system.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has been a popular method for decision making using computational modeling. However, the standard RL algorithms are risk-neutral in nature and do not adequately take into account the uncertainty and risk associated with the outcomes of decision making. Inverse Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning (IRLRL) is a novel approach that incorporates the risk sensitivity of human decision makers into the RL algorithm. This paper presents a comprehensive review of IRLRL, its convergence properties, and measurement techniques to assess its effectiveness. Furthermore, this paper examines the application of IRLRL to Markov processes and explores the potential for an integrated biological system modeling framework that could incorporate IRLRL into cognitive and neural modeling. The paper concludes by discussing the potential future research directions for incorporating risk sensitivity into decision making using IRLRL.

Fault detection of nonlinear processes using Kernel Principal Component Analysis(KPCA) method has recently prompt a lot of interest due to its industrial practical importance. However, this method cannot be applied for data sets with a large amount of samples. To overcome this deficiency, this paper proposes a reduced KPCA method based on K-means clustering. This method aims to find a reduced data set among the training data in the input space and uses this reduced data set to built the reduced KPCA model in the feature space. The relevance of the proposed method is illustrated on an air quality monitoring network. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new method when compared to the classical KPCA technique.

Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is a fundamental problem in robotics which involves estimating the movement of a robot relative to its environment while simultaneously creating a map of that environment. In this paper, we present a real-time direct monocular SLAM system which utilizes learning-based confidence estimation to improve the accuracy of the estimation process. Our system uses cameras as the only sensor and extracts features directly from the image stream. By incorporating machine learning, our system is able to track the movement of the camera with high precision and confidence. The system employs an optimization approach to improve its accuracy and is designed to perform in real-time. Our experimental results show that our system performs favorably against existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and reliability.

It is critical to obtain stability certificate before deploying reinforcement learning in real-world mission-critical systems. This study justifies the intuition that smoothness (i.e., small changes in inputs lead to small changes in outputs) is an important property for stability-certified reinforcement learning from a control-theoretic perspective. The smoothness margin can be obtained by solving a feasibility problem based on semi-definite programming for both linear and nonlinear dynamical systems, and it does not need to access the exact parameters of the learned controllers. Numerical evaluation on nonlinear and decentralized frequency control for large-scale power grids demonstrates that the smoothness margin can certify stability during both exploration and deployment for (deep) neural-network policies, which substantially surpass nominal controllers in performance. The study opens up new opportunities for robust Lipschitz continuous policy learning.

This paper examines the potential usability of text-to-speech synthesis as a tool to bridge the digital divide in South Africa, from the perspective of language practitioners. The authors focus on the challenges faced by individuals who lack access to electronic publishing or dictionaries due to low literacy levels or limited language proficiency. The study investigates the usability of text-to-speech synthesis tools in addressing these challenges, including the effects of stress and intonation on the accuracy and effectiveness of the technology. The authors discuss the importance of accurate training data and benchmark testing in evaluating the usability of these tools for bridging the digital divide in South Africa. Overall, the study suggests that text-to-speech synthesis has the potential to play a valuable role in promoting digital inclusion and access to educational resources for underserved communities in South Africa.

This paper introduces a low power packet detection algorithm designed for the FM-UWB PHY for IEEE 802.15.6 WBANs, which are wireless communication networks specifically designed for body area networks. The IEEE 802.15 standard is used to establish a universal standard for wireless communication networks. The proposed algorithm is based on correlation and takes into account the frequency modulation properties of the FM signal. The algorithm is optimized for low power consumption and is effective for detecting packets in environments with high interference. The results show that the algorithm is able to achieve a packet detection rate of over 90% while consuming less than 1mW of power. This algorithm is a promising solution for packet detection in WBANs and has the potential to be applied in various wireless communication applications.

UAV-enabled data gathering in wireless sensor networks has been gaining increasing attention in recent years. Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have been extensively used for monitoring and surveillance applications in various domains. However, the inherent limitations of WSNs such as limited battery power, processing capabilities, and communication range, have resulted in the development of drone-based solutions. Drones, also known as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), offer several advantages over the traditional WSN-based monitoring and surveillance systems. They can provide reconfigurable and dynamic monitoring capabilities, mobility, and can efficiently cover a large area. Protocols and sleep schedules have been proposed to enable effective communication between the drones and the sensors, without compromising the battery life of the sensors. Additionally, the use of drones can eliminate the need for base stations in the network. In conclusion, UAV-enabled data gathering in WSNs has the potential to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of monitoring and surveillance tasks in various domains.

In this paper, the achievable rate of the multi-cell multi-user generalized spatial modulation uplink is analyzed in the presence of realistic pilot contamination. A practical channel model associated with arbitrary transmit and receive correlation matrices is assumed for each user and base station (BS). Imperfect channel estimation is assumed with pilot contamination. The performance of a single-cell based minimum mean squared error (SMMSE) combiner is analyzed and compared to the ubiquitous zero forcing (ZF) combiner as well as matched filtering (MF). The transmit antenna (TA) index detection and the classic amplitude/phase modulation signal detection process are carried out separately for the sake of low complexity. Moreover, an algorithm based on order statistics is proposed for calculating the antenna detection probability conditioned on the actual TA. Finally, an approximation of the achievable rate is derived by exploiting the characteristics of massive multiple-input multiple-outputs (MIMO). Simulation results show that SMMSE has the best performance, followed by ZF, and then MF. Furthermore, the relationships between the system's achievable rate and three systems' parameters, namely the number of BS antennas, the signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), and the interference factor of pilot contamination, are presented. The performance of different number of activated antennas is also compared.

This paper proposes a collaborative generative adversarial network (CGAN) for recommendation systems. CGAN utilizes generative adversarial networks (GANs), which consist of two models: generators and discriminators, to generate realistic data samples that can be used for training. The training process is optimized with the use of Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology to enhance the robustness of the model. Furthermore, the proposed CGAN model enables collaboration between multiple generators which improves the overall performance of the recommendation system. In addition, feature extraction is applied to enhance the quality of the generated data. The results of experiments show that CGAN can outperform existing state-of-the-art recommendation systems. Thus, the proposed method has great potential for enhancing recommendation systems in various domains.

Both wrapper and hybrid methods in feature selection need the intervention of learning algorithm to train parameters. The preset parameters and dataset are used to construct several sub-optimal models, from which the final model is selected. The question is how to evaluate the performance of these sub-optimal models? What are the effects of different evaluation methods of sub-optimal model on the result of feature selection? Aiming at the evaluation problem of predictive models in feature selection, we chose a hybrid feature selection algorithm, FDHSFFS, and conducted comparative experiments on four UCI datasets with large differences in feature dimension and sample size by using five different cross-validation (CV) methods. The experimental results show that in the process of feature selection, twofold CV and leave-one-out-CV are more suitable for the model evaluation of low-dimensional and small sample datasets, tenfold nested CV and tenfold CV are more suitable for the model evaluation of high-dimensional datasets; tenfold nested CV is close to the unbiased estimation, and different optimal models may choose the same approximate optimal feature subset.

There is a great number of image applications, where the first step in the analysis is to associate the same point in two or more images that were taken from different viewpoints or at different times. This procedure is called image registration (IR). This work proposes a new efficient method for IR based on tensor calculus that overtakes the usual assumption of brightness consistency among the involved images. The main idea is to define transformations in serial images by using tensor behavior on coordinate transformations. It combines the simplicity and efficiency of the computer implementation with the correctness and elegance of the physic foundations. Moreover, it introduces a complete different way for management of this very important application of image processing: the use of the principal axis idea. The significant advantage of the proposed method is its promptitude and robustness for use in medical images in a way the as far as we known have never considered before. Experimental results in real examinations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is highly accurate and outperforms a combination of the most updated IR approaches.

The work described in this paper aims at the development of a networkable, intelligent embedded system application, which is used for data acquisition and analysis in traffic flows. The main components of the sensor system and their interaction are explained. The sensor system is constructed in such a way that, in addition to the use of magnetic field sensors, further sensors which are useful for the respective detection task can be added. Furthermore, measuring procedures in the laboratory and in field trials on the road are described and illustrated. A selection of the results is presented.

This paper presents a kinematics analysis and simulation of a series-parallel hybrid haptic handle designed for use in surgical simulators. The use of haptic interfaces and robots in surgery training has become increasingly prevalent in recent years, as they provide a safe and controlled environment for learning and improving surgical skills. The device studied in this paper incorporates a series-parallel hybrid structure, and focuses on wrist movement and manipulation. Using a mathematical model, the kinematics of the handle were analyzed and optimized to provide a realistic and effective training tool. Furthermore, simulations were conducted to validate the performance of the handle, demonstrating its ability to accurately replicate human wrist movement. This research contributes to the development of advanced haptic handles for surgical simulators, with potential uses in medical training and other related fields.

We propose a battery-less location tracking system that enables 3-D positioning of an Internet of Things (IoT) device powered by the radio frequency (RF) wireless power transfer (WPT). In the proposed system, a power beacon is equipped with a phased antenna array that has the dual purposes of high-efficiency WPT and phase-based accurate positioning. In order to enhance the efficiency of the RF WPT, we propose a beam focusing algorithm that dynamically controls the respective phases of antenna elements to place the focal point of the electro-magnetic (EM) wave onto the target IoT device. We also propose a phase-based positioning algorithm that requires only one multi-antenna anchor point for determining the distance as well as the direction from the anchor point. We analyze the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) of the phase-based positioning with a single multi-antenna anchor point, and show that the distance from the anchor point can be estimated as long as the IoT device lies within the radiative near-field region. We propose a joint location tracking and WPT algorithm that performs 3-D positioning and beam-focused WPT in a unified way. We have built a real-life testbed with a large-scale antenna array with 64 antenna elements for testing the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in a real environment.

The statistical delay of a path is traditionally modeled as a Gaussian random variable assuming that the path is always sensitized by a test pattern. Its sensitization in various circuit instances varies among its test patterns and the pattern induced delay is non-Gaussian. It is modeled using probability mass functions. The defect coverage is improved by test pattern selection using machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate accuracy in defect coverage when comparing to existing methods.

In this paper, we introduce Deep Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (DCFA) to identify complex nonlinear transformations of two variables for information fusion. DCFA is able to represent the coupled patterns between two different sets of variables by minimizing the Frobenius norm distance in the transformed domain. Unlike previous kernel methods, the feature mapping of DCFA is achieved with deep networks (DN) instead of the traditional kernel method. Therefore, the representation of DCFA method is not limited by the fixed kernel. Moreover, DCFA can be considered as a nonlinear extension of the linear Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (CFA), and an alternative to the nonparametric method Kernel Cross-Modal Factor Analysis (KCFA) and the recently proposed Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis (Deep CCA) method. The performance of DCFA is evaluated on MNIST handwritten digit dataset and two audio emotion datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed solution outperforms the methods of KCCA, KCFA, Deep CCA and the deep learning based method-Alexnet, in terms of accuracy.

This paper is aimed at evaluating the reliability indices of a distribution network (DN) considering the rerouting of the interrupted customers during outages. The DN is represented by its circuit graph that is used to analyze the effect of the failure mode (FMEA method) and compute the reliability of the system. To have a more accurate estimation, the capacity of the feeder and the voltage deviation when the rerouting occurs, are also considered. After the occurrence of an outage, the problem is finding the optimum tree by interchanging the status of normally open (NO) and normally closed (NC) switches to restore as many as interrupted customers subject to defined constraints. The proposed algorithm presents a systematic method to find the optimum solution of the restoration problem, and by decreasing the search space is suitable for analyzing the big size DN. To obtain the impact of each NC switches in the reliability improvement, a ranking method is also introduced.

This paper discusses the use of Machine Learning (ML) techniques to automate classroom observation in low-resource environments. The study focuses on the development of ML models through the process of feature extraction, followed by classification algorithms for classifying different observations. The primary aim is to reduce the burden on observers by automating the task of classroom observation using ML. The models are developed through training and time-frequency analysis, which involves identifying and analyzing the patterns and frequencies of classroom activities. The effectiveness of the developed models is tested across different buildings to evaluate its usefulness in different low-resource environments. Overall, the study presents a novel approach to automate the classroom observation process and offers valuable insights on the use of machine learning techniques in low-resource environments.

In this work, we explore efficient parallelization methods for the Parameter-less Population Pyramid (P3) and show their computational effectiveness. First, in this paper, we present one possible implementation of parallel P3. Next, we analyze effects of sharing solutions between sub-populations of parallel P3 on some benchmarks. By sharing solutions, the parallel P3 finds optimal solutions faster than the simple parallelization. On the deceptive trap and discretized Rastrigin problems, the more solutions parallel P3 shares among sub-populations, the faster it finds optimal solutions. On the other hand, on the Nk problem, too much sharing prevents parallel P3 from performing good search. Finally, we propose guidelines for future research on parallel P3.

This paper proposes a knowledge-poor machine learning approach for assertion detection in clinical natural language processing. The task analysis includes identifying assertive statements related to medical conditions, treatments and procedures. The proposed approach relies on a set of measurements such as precision, recall, and F1-score to evaluate the performance of the machine learning model. The study focuses on medical diagnostic imaging and pain assessment in clinical settings. Knowledge engineering is utilized to identify key features and patterns in the clinical text data. The training set is used to train the machine learning model, which is subsequently tested on a validation set. The results of the study demonstrate that the knowledge-poor approach was effective in detecting the assertion status of clinical text records. Machine learning techniques proved to be helpful in improving the accuracy of assertion detection in clinical natural language processing. This approach can potentially be extended to other clinical domains and incorporated into clinical decision support systems to improve patient care.

For the problem of remaining useful lifetime (RUL) prediction of nonlinear system, the existing methods have not systematically carried out the studies on nonlinear degradation modeling with measurement error and random effect, priori parameter estimation and the corresponding RUL prediction. In this paper, a nonlinear Wiener process is used to establish a nonlinear degradation model with the consideration of measurement error and random effect to describe the implicitness, personality difference and nonlinearity of degradation process of a class of device. The expectation maximum (EM) algorithm is used to obtain the estimates of the fixed coefficient and the priori distributions of the random coefficients in the degradation model. Using the current monitoring data of the target device, the posteriori distribution of random coefficients is iteratively updated based on Bayesian inference. Using the full-probability formula, the remaining useful lifetime distribution of device is derived based on the first hitting time (FHT) distribution. A simulation example is analyzed to verify the correctness and advantage of this method.

This paper proposes an MRAM (Magnetic Random Access Memory) based architecture for deep neural networks, which is able to perform computation within the memory itself, thus reducing the delays caused by data transfer between the memory and the processor. MRAM technology is used due to its inherent non-volatility and fast write speed, as well as its compatibility with established standards for random access memory. The architecture uses magnetic tunneling junctions for computing, which can be programmed to mimic the behavior of neurons in a neural network. Barium is proposed as a material to enhance the performance of the magnetic tunneling junctions. The proposed architecture is evaluated through simulations and shows promising results in terms of performance and energy efficiency. This MRAM-based deep in-memory architecture is a major step towards achieving high-speed, low-power processing for deep neural networks.

This paper proposes a novel approach to realize bimanual coordination for trans-humeral prosthesis users in a box-lifting task with various box configurations. The approach utilizes support vector machines to classify electromyography signals from sensors attached to the user's residual arms, and extracts relevant features for task analysis. By analyzing the task and the user's muscle movements, the system can accurately predict the user's intentions and provide suitable control signals to the prosthetics for coordinated movement. The proposed approach provides a promising solution to improve the functionality and usability of prosthetics for trans-humeral amputees, by enabling them to perform complex bimanual tasks with ease and fluidity.

The Hierarchical Cloud-Fog Platform for Communication in Disaster Incident Coordination is a system designed for efficiently managing communication during disaster incidents. This platform leverages the power of cloud computing and integrated circuits to provide real-time communication and decision-making capabilities. The system also utilizes smart devices and advanced data collection techniques to gather critical information related to the incident. The hierarchical structure of this cloud-fog platform is designed to facilitate collaboration between different personnel involved in the disaster response effort, enabling effective coordination and data sharing. With its ability to provide real-time insights and data analysis, this platform is poised to revolutionize disaster management practices across the globe.

The performance evaluation of primary frequency regulation (PFR) of generator is helpful to improve the frequency stability of power grids. Existing research cannot comprehensively and accurately evaluate the PFR performance of generators, and the research methods have the disadvantage of poor adaptability. Based on the simulation model of PFR of generator, this method takes vertiginous rate, regulation limit, dead zone and response delay time of the PFR as model key parameters. The improved genetic algorithm is used to find the model parameters which have the smallest error comparing with the generator actual output. Those parameters are used as the evaluation index of the PFR performance of the generator. Thus the method can more comprehensively and accurately evaluate the performance indexes of the generator primary frequency regulation. Finally, based on the measured data of the primary frequency regulation of the generator in Northwest Power Grid, the response output of the primary frequency regulation model and identified parameters are compared with the actual output, the validity and accuracy of the evaluation method are verified.

Optimization problem is which mainly focuses on finding feasible solution out of all possible solutions. Travelling salesman problem belongs to this one. As it is not possible to find its solution in definite polynomial time that is why it is considered as one of the NP-hard problem. This paper utilizes the optimization capability of genetic algorithm to find the feasible solution for TSP. The algorithm starts with the calculation of Euclidean distance between the towns to be visited by the salesman. Initial chromosome pool is generated using value encoding. Then best fit chromosomes are selected by applying roulette wheel selection which then goes through m-point crossover. Now we apply interchange mutation on the offsprings generated before. Now this whole process is repeated until the convergence of genetic algorithm.

Generative models have become increasingly popular in the area of CNC toolpath generation owing to their flexibility and the ability to generate toolpaths directly. Among the different methods used in CNC toolpath generation, interpolation is a widely used technique. With the emergence of generative adversarial networks (GANs) and their ability to generate realistic images, they have been used in the field of CNC toolpath generation too. This has resulted in major advancements in the field of artificial intelligence and computer numerical control. One of the primary materials in the manufacturing industry is gallium nitride, and its use has also been studied in the context of CNC toolpath generation. Through a combination of GANs and gallium nitride, one can generate toolpaths that can be used for the production of various products. Splines (mathematics) are another important tool used in CNC toolpath generation that have been integrated with GANs to improve the quality of generated toolpaths. Overall, the use of generative models and artificial intelligence in CNC toolpath generation has opened up new possibilities for the manufacturing industry.

Image segmentation is a significant and challenging task in the field of computer vision, especially when it comes to semantic segmentation. Feature extraction, classification algorithms, and convolutional neural networks have all been used successfully to tackle this problem. However, these approaches are often limited by their inability to take into account the contextual information present in the scene being segmented. In order to address this limitation, researchers have proposed the use of Scene-Aware Deep Networks for Semantic Segmentation of Images. This framework effectively integrates contextual information by combining global and local scene features, which provide a more comprehensive representation of the image. Additionally, the training of these networks is augmented by using a novel loss function that encourages the segmentation to be consistent with the scene layout. Experimental results demonstrate that Scene-Aware Deep Networks outperform several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. This approach holds great potential for advancing the field of semantic segmentation for real-world applications.

As new radiotherapy treatment systems using MRI (rather than traditional CT) are being developed, the accurate calculation of dose maps from MR imaging has become an increasing concern. MRI provides good soft-tissue but, unlike CT, lacks the electron density information necessary for dose calculation. In this paper, we proposed a generative adversarial network (GAN) using a perceptual loss to generate pseudo-CTs for prostate MRI dose calculation. This network was evaluated and compared to a U-Net network, a patch-based (PBM) and an atlas-based methods (ABM). Influence of the perceptual loss was assessed by comparing this network to a GAN using a L2 loss. GANs and U-Nets are rather similar with slightly better results for GANs. The proposed GAN outperformed the PBM by 9% and the ABM by 13% in term of MAE in whole pelvis. This method could be used for online dose calculation in MRI-only radiotherapy.

This paper proposes a fast hyperspectral classification method which integrates rotational invariant linear discriminant analysis and nearest regularized subspace techniques. The method is an effective approach to feature extraction and training in hyperspectral imaging, where accurate and efficient classification of image data is critical. The proposed method ensures high classification accuracy in testing, while also reducing computational complexity. With the increasing importance of data mining techniques in modern scientific research, the integration of these two algorithms is a promising development for the field of hyperspectral imaging.

In the last 20 years, the IEEE 1451 standards family has been present throughout the changes in the world of smart sensors. One of the most important evolution in this field was the Internet of Things, mainly because of the popularity of light-weight and simple methods to implement communication protocols among human, machines, and sensors. In particular, one of its protocols is very important to enable this interconnection: the MQTT. It has become synonymous with large cloud service providers for the Internet of Things, such as Amazon AWS, IBM Watson and Microsoft Azure. Despite MQTT protocol being traditionally used in controlled networks within server centers, nowadays this protocols is largely used on IoT and is part of IEEE 1451 family, having the number IEEE 1451.1.6. Following the motivation to adopt IoT' standards protocols in the IEEE 1451 standard family, this paper proposes the use of a specific and potential variant of MQTT, the MQTT for Sensors Networks, or MQTT-SN. It introduces a more efficient protocol for the Common Architectures and Network services found in the IEEE 1451 Family of Standard, and shows how services and applications based on MQTT can be integrated.

A waveform design procedure for improving the estimation of Doppler frequencies in active remote sensing applications is presented. The bound on frequency estimation is analyzed in terms of a continuous waveform, and the optimal waveform is inferred. Several waveform designs are analyzed, showing that a near-optimal dual-pulse waveform can achieve greater estimation accuracy than a single-pulse waveform using the same signal energy.

This paper presents a Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) approach using the Iterative Steepest Descent (ISD) algorithm to control an inverted pendulum. Optimal control is achieved by minimizing a cost function using predictive control. Nonlinear systems pose significant challenges in control theory due to their unsteady and often unpredictable behavior. However, the NMPC approach allows for the use of prediction algorithms, which can help to make effective control decisions. The ISD algorithm is a powerful optimization technique that enables the control of nonlinear systems by iteratively adjusting the control input. By using this technique in the control of an inverted pendulum, it is possible to achieve both stability and accurate tracking of the pendulum's motion. Overall, this study demonstrates the effectiveness of the NMPC and ISD algorithm in controlling nonlinear systems with predictive control.

In the promising time of the Internet, connected things have the ability to communicate and share information. The Internet of Things (IoT) cannot be implemented unless the security-related concerns have been resolved. Sharing information among different devices can compromise the private information of users. Thus, a suitable mechanism is needed to exclude the risk of malicious and compromised nodes. As follows, trust has been proposed in the literature as a useful technology to maintain users' security. Prior studies have proposed diverse trust management mechanisms to achieve adequate trust. The approach of cross-domain trust management is neglected that requires enormous considerations to address the difficulties related to cross-domain communication. In this paper, a cross-domain robust distributed trust management (RobustTrust) system is proposed, which makes a device fit for assessing trust towards different devices locally. In this system, the trust is divided into three components of security that help IoT nodes to become robust against compromised and malicious devices/nodes. The novelty of the proposed mechanism can be summarized in these aspects: A highly scalable trust mechanism, multiple components of evaluation to enhance robustness against attacks, and use of recommendations along with the feedback to build knowledge. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism is event-driven that helps nodes to evaluate trust more effectively as well as enhance the system efficiency. The proposed work is compared with the available trust evaluation schemes by concentrating on various attributes, such as trustworthiness, usability, and accuracy among others. The RobustTrust is validated by the extensive simulations considering absolute trust value's performance, the accuracy of trust estimation, and several potential attacks.

In order to solve the problem of state estimation and fault detection for a class of stochastic switched nonlinear system with unknown characteristics of observation noise change, a system state estimation algorithm based on interactive multiple model and unscented Kalman filter (IMM-UKF) is proposed. The algorithm uses the UKF to estimate the state of each subsystem at different time points, then fuses the state estimation results of different subsystems to obtain the final state estimation, and realizes the estimation of the real state of the system. In order to achieve real-time tracking of system observation noise, a fuzzy controller is established to adjust the observation noise of IMM- UKF in real time, and a fuzzy adaptive IMM-UKF algorithm (FAIMM-UKF) is proposed. For actuator failure in a class of stochastic switched nonlinear systems, FAIMM-UKF is used to estimate the system state. Based on the result of the state estimation, residual and residual evaluation functions are established to detect the actuator fault. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation experiment.

This paper investigates the use of wavelet functions in intelligent direct adaptive control of uncertain nonlinear systems. The proposed approach utilizes neural networks to learn the system dynamics and generate control signals based on the trajectory of the system. The closed loop system is designed to adapt to the uncertainty in the nonlinear system and maintain a stable trajectory. The performance of the approach is evaluated through simulation using adaptation models to test the robustness of the proposed method. The results show that the use of wavelet functions in the adaptive control of nonlinear systems provides superior performance compared to other control strategies. This approach provides a promising solution for controlling complex and uncertain nonlinear systems in real-world applications.

Cloud storage system is a distributed storage system which stores data in many disks on the Internet. In order to achieve more reliable data and improve performance of the storage system, an erasure code is invented and applied to cloud storage system wherein the user's data will be stored online through the Internet. This paper applies the complete graph of ring (CGR) codes [7], which is a maximum distance separable (MDS) code, and implements in cloud storage system. Moreover, the maximum likelihood decoder (MLD) is also applied and implemented on the receiver to detect and correct errors due to noisy channel. In this paper, the grey-scale images/files are randomly stored on distributed cloud storage, then sent via communications channel, and finally read by receivers. The result shows that the receiver operated with the MLD outperforms by giving the lower BER.

In this paper, a multi band planner circular patch antenna is designed with compact size of 30 mm X 20 mm. The proposed antenna is designed with ring resonators having stub and a circular patch. This antenna operates at 1.8 GHz, 5.2 GHz, 7 GHz, 7.86 GHz and 8.53 GHz which belongs to RFID, WLAN and C band that can be used in IoT application and satellite communication. The fractional bandwidth possessed by this proposed antenna corresponding to each frequency are 32.22%, 4.80%, 2.57%, 2.54% and 2.27% respectively. The results are analyzed and discuss in term of return loss, fractional bandwidth and gain.

Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is considered to be one of the best candidates for future networks due to its ability to serve multiple users using the same resource block. Although early studies have focused on transmission reliability and energy efficiency, recent works are considering cooperation among the nodes. The cooperative NOMA techniques allow the user with a better channel (near user) to act as a relay between the source and the user experiencing poor channel (far user). This paper considers the link security aspect of energy harvesting cooperative NOMA users. In particular, the near user applies the decode-and-forward (DF) protocol for relaying the message of the source node to the far user in the presence of an eavesdropper. Moreover, we consider that all the devices use power-splitting architecture for energy harvesting and information decoding. We derive the analytical expression of intercept probability. Next, we employ deep learning based optimization to find the optimal power allocation factor. The results show the robustness and superiority of deep learning optimization over conventional iterative search algorithm.

Clustering also called cluster analysis is the task of data objects grouping where group objects are similar. Simultaneously, they should be different from other groups objects. Such groups are termed as Clusters. We are study in this paper several clustering algorithms applied in E-learning systems. Our objective lies in performing a deep analysis of clustering data mining techniques both theoretically and experimentally and to do a comparative study in order to distinguish which technique is more suitable to identify e-learners profile and also to evaluate better student performance in engineering education. A good clustering method is able to yield high quality clusters. The algorithms under investigation are: Canopy algorithm, Cobweb algorithm, EM algorithm, FarthestFirst algorithm, FilteredClusterer algorithm, MakeDensityBasedClusterer algorithm. The performance of clustering the six algorithms is compared through the use of clustering tool WEKA (version 3.7.12) as an open source tool.

The integration of cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), and advanced sensing technologies is rapidly transforming the status of the human body in society. Biomedical monitoring tools are becoming increasingly connected to cloud-based platforms, enabling real-time tracking of various human parameters. This paper discusses the current status and future prospects of the integration of these technologies, often referred to as the Body within the Internet of Things. The revolution or evolution is focused on the potentials of IoT in economical, environmental, and social aspects, with all possible areas of its impact being markedly increased with sensors and monitoring tools. The sociological impact of these advances is also analyzed, with particular attention given to the ethical issues posed by constant body monitoring. Finally, the statistical implications of this new technology are explored, revealing a significant potential in the field of data analytics and personalized healthcare programs.

This paper proposes a method for vehicle classification in drone imagery by combining deep and handcrafted image features. The proposed approach involves feature extraction using histograms, which takes into account both texture and color information. The extracted features are then fed into a training process, where the system learns to recognize different vehicle types. The use of drones in this context allows for versatile and efficient data gathering. Furthermore, visualization techniques are explored to improve the interpretation of the results. The combination of deep learning and handcrafted features proves to be effective in the classification of vehicles in drone imagery, making it a promising approach for image recognition tasks.

This paper proposes a fault diagnosis and estimation method for electric scooters based on Double-Scale UKF. The study focuses on the estimation and diagnosis of faults related to the motorcycle's wheels. The Double-Scale UKF approach is employed in this research due to its capability of estimating the parameters and covariance matrices in real-time systems. Compared to the conventional UKF, the Double-Scale UKF has better estimation accuracy, higher computational efficiency, and lower convergence time. The proposed method is validated using experimental data, indicating its effectiveness in identifying and estimating faults related to the wheels of electric scooters. The results obtained show that the proposed method provides a promising approach for fault diagnosis and estimation in real-time systems.

We study a mobile wireless sensor network (MWSN) consisting of multiple mobile sensors or robots. Three key factors in MWSNs, such as sensing quality, energy consumption, and connectivity, have attracted plenty of attention, but the interaction of these factors is not well studied. To take all the three factors into consideration, we model the sensor deployment problem as a constrained optimization problem. Our goal is to find an optimal sensor deployment (or relocation) to optimize the sensing quality with a limited communication range and a specific network lifetime constraint. We derive necessary conditions for the optimal sensor deployment in both homogeneous and heterogeneous MWSNs. According to our derivation, some sensors are idle in the optimal deployment of heterogeneous MWSNs. Using these necessary conditions, we design both the centralized and distributed algorithms to provide a flexible and explicit tradeoff between sensing uncertainty and network lifetime. The proposed algorithms are successfully extended to more applications, such as area coverage and target coverage, via properly selected density functions. The simulation results show that our algorithms outperform the existing relocation algorithms.

This paper proposes a geometrically conformal quadrilateral surface-reconstruction method for MoM-SIE simulations. The surface reconstruction technique is based on the method of moments and integral equations, which is commonly used in computational modeling. A mathematical model is established to ensure the consistency of the reconstructed surface with the original one. Moreover, the proposed method applies conformal mapping to improve the accuracy in reconstructing the surface. The method incorporates histograms to optimize the selection of quadrilateral patches for reconstructing the surface. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and efficiency in surface reconstruction, making it a valuable tool for MoM-SIE simulations.

Auto-Retoucher (ART) is a framework designed for the purpose of improving image quality. The framework has been tailored towards background replacement and foreground adjustment through various processes such as feature extraction, logic gates, anomaly detection, target tracking, and cyberattack monitoring. The framework converts input images into mathematical models that are manipulated through specific algorithms to improve or replace the foreground or background. Its ability to detect anomalies and track targets contributes to its overall effectiveness as an image enhancer. The framework's design also includes advanced cyberattack monitoring capabilities, providing security measures to protect sensitive images. Overall, ART has proven to be a reliable and efficient tool for image enhancement and manipulation.

This paper focuses on the selection of variables for discriminating radiated magnetic field signals of electrical discharges using the F-Score algorithm. The dataset was divided into training and testing sets, and the F-Score algorithm was used to determine the most significant input variables for discriminating the signals. Support vector machines and other classification algorithms were then used to classify the signals based on the selected input variables. The results of the study showed that the F-Score algorithm was effective in selecting the most significant input variables for discriminating the radiated magnetic field signals of electrical discharges. The classification accuracy of the support vector machine and other classification algorithms was greatly improved with the selected input variables. This study provides a method for selecting the most important variables for discriminating radiated magnetic field signals of electrical discharges, which can be used in various applications related to electromagnetic compatibility.

Small cells (SCs) mounted on top of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are a promising solution to boost the capacity in hotspot areas. However, the adoption of UAV-SCs involves the planning of their missions over time, which includes the scheduling of recharging actions of each UAV-SC at ground sites. Typically, the energy needed to recharge UAV-SCs is derived from the grid, which can be coupled with microgeneration exploiting renewable energy sources (e.g., solar panels). In this architecture, the energy that is locally produced can be either sold to the grid or used to recharge the UAV-SCs. On the other hand, when the energy from microgeneration is insufficient for recharging the UAV-SCs, additional energy can be bought from the grid. In this paper, we investigate the trade-off between maximizing the throughput provided by the UAV-SCs over a set of areas, maximizing energy sold to the grid, and maximizing energy bought from the grid. The proposed model, MaxUAVProfit, is designed to (i) plan the UAV-SCs missions as a sequence of positions and actions in 3D space vs. time, (ii) manage the grid-connected microgeneration, and (iii) control the amount of throughput received by each hotspot. We then evaluate the MaxUAVProfit in a realistic scenario, which is based on the measurement of real cellular metrics and a realistic UAV-SC energy consumption model. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of the MaxUAVProfit with respect to other competing solutions, which include either optimization of microgeneration or maximization of the area throughput.

With the technologies for machine learning and big data handling new opportunities for classification and prediction tasks have arisen. On the other hand the technology of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) has become indispensable in aviation in the last ten years. Putting these items together paves the way for new applications for real-time radar surveillance systems. That applies to both the civil environment and the world of military systems. This paper describes the complete processing chain to prepare ADS-B data for machine learning and training, which finally leads to applications that can be applied to real-time systems.

In recent years, steganography has emerged as a popular technique to secure and hide information within an image. However, the problem of introducing distortion in the image while hiding information presents new challenges. This paper focuses on CNN-based adversarial embedding for image steganography by exploring various perturbation methods. Through deep learning, the approach utilizes feature extraction to embed the desired information while minimizing distortion in the image. The proposed method not only enhances the security of the message but also provides good image coding with lower distortion. Overall, the paper presents a novel approach for efficient and secure image steganography.

A virtual reality based training and assessment system for hand rehabilitation has been developed to improve hand function in individuals with hand injuries. The system incorporates training and games, utilizing virtual reality and data gloves to enhance engagement and provide real-time feedback. Task analysis is performed to provide individualized treatment plans and calibration of the system. The software allows for progression tracking and data analysis. This system shows promise in improving hand rehabilitation outcomes and providing an engaging and effective rehabilitation option.

Cloud computing has revolutionized the way in which software is designed and deployed, and has brought about a shift towards Platform as a Service (PaaS) solutions. This paper proposes a PaaS solution for large scale deployment of student projects. The solution incorporates various features including databases, scalability, containers, security, and software, which would ensure a holistic approach to the development and deployment of student projects. We argue that the proposed solution is not only effective but also efficient in terms of cost and management. We also discuss the use of containerization, which would enable students to deploy their projects seamlessly and with minimal dependency on the underlying system. Additionally, we outline various security measures that would ensure the integrity and confidentiality of data stored on the platform. We conclude that this PaaS solution is well-suited for large scale deployment of student projects in the field of computer science.

This paper discusses the staffing needs in the regional economy, particularly under the modern conditions of labor market. Training and task analysis are important tools in identifying and addressing these needs in order to increase economic efficiency. In addition, economics play a significant role in personnel and employment decisions made by organizations. Through a comprehensive understanding of these factors, businesses and employers can make informed decisions that promote growth and success. Ultimately, this paper emphasizes the importance of considering the wider economic context when developing staffing and HR strategies in order to maximize productivity and competitiveness.

The recently proposed posit number system is more accurate and can provide a wider dynamic range than the conventional IEEE754-2008 floating-point numbers. Its nonuniform data representation makes it suitable in deep learning applications. Posit adder and posit multiplier have been well developed recently in the literature. However, the use of posit in fused arithmetic unit has not been investigated yet. In order to facilitate the use of posit number format in deep learning applications, in this paper, an efficient architecture of posit multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit is proposed. Unlike IEEE754-2008 where four standard binary number formats are presented, the posit format is more flexible where the total bitwidth and exponent bitwidth can be any number. Therefore, in this proposed design, bitwidths of all datapath are parameterized and a posit MAC unit generator written in C language is proposed. The proposed generator can generate Verilog HDL code of posit MAC unit for any given total bitwidth and exponent bitwidth. The code generated by the generator is a combinational design, however a 5-stage pipeline strategy is also presented and analyzed in this paper. The worst case delay, area, and power consumption of the generated MAC unit under STM-28nm library with different bitwidth choices are provided and analyzed.

Cloud computing has revolutionized the way businesses operate by providing a flexible and cost-effective IT infrastructure. Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) have been quick to adopt cloud-based solutions to stay competitive. However, the prediction of a future dominated by edge computing where users rely on nearby cloudlets to support their computation and storage needs is gaining momentum. This paper provides a value perspective to deploying a cloudlet business model for SMEs in the era of edge computing. The stakeholders involved such as cloudlet providers, SMEs, and end-users are analyzed, focusing on the quality of experience (QoE) and the benefits it offers. A brief history of the cloudlet model and its evolution is presented, along with the importance of prefetching research in improving QoE. Furthermore, the concept of brain modeling is introduced to determine the optimal resource allocation based on user behavioral patterns. The proposed model suggests that cloudlets have a promising future in the SME sector; it presents a cost-effective solution, and its small-scale, localized nature is well-suited for SMEs. This paper highlights the benefits of a cloudlet deployment strategy and provides essential guidance on how to unlock its full potential for SMEs.

Traditional dictionary learning based CT reconstruction methods are patch-based and the features learned with these methods often contain shifted versions of the same features. To deal with these problems, the convolutional sparse coding (CSC) has been proposed and introduced into various applications. In this paper, inspired by the successful applications of CSC in the field of signal processing, we propose a novel sparse-view CT reconstruction method based on CSC with gradient regularization on feature maps. By directly working on the whole image, which need not to divide the image into overlapped patches like dictionary learning based methods, the proposed method can maintain more details and avoid the artifacts caused by patch aggregation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method has better performance than several existing algorithms in both qualitative and quantitative aspects.

Sustainable manufacturing has gained increasing attention in recent years due to its significant impact on environmental preservation and social responsibility. Collaboration among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) has been identified as a key strategy to achieve sustainable manufacturing. This paper examines the impact of collaboration on SMEs' sustainable manufacturing practices, with a focus on three technological aspects: iron, frequency modulation, and IP networks. The study finds that collaboration among SMEs can result in significant benefits such as improved resource efficiency, reduced waste, and enhanced innovation. The use of iron as a sustainable material in manufacturing, the application of frequency modulation technologies in production processes, and the use of IP networks to support collaboration are identified as effective ways to promote sustainable manufacturing among SMEs. The paper concludes by highlighting the need for more research to identify and develop sustainable manufacturing practices that can benefit both SMEs and the environment.

In recent years, the increasing number of fires and their devastating impacts have called for the development of effective methods for early detection and control. This paper proposes a dual convolution network using dark channel prior for image smoke classification. The proposed method utilizes feature extraction and image color analysis coupled with deep learning techniques such as image edge detection and data mining to accurately distinguish between natural backgrounds and smoke. The dual convolution network also includes a fuse mechanism to enhance classification accuracy. The proposed method has been tested on various fire smoke datasets, and the results confirm its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed dual convolution network has tremendous potential to be deployed in real-time fire monitoring and prevention systems, thereby improving public safety and minimizing the devastating impact of fire incidents.

Determination of model order is an important task in many problems such as sinusoidal parameter estimation. In this paper we consider the data matrix corresponding to the given sequence and introduce the Ratio of Cumulative Sums (RCS) of eigenvalues. We then exploit the structure of RCS to obtain a performance that is comparable to the Cumulative Sums based method of Shah and Tufts (ST). However the advantage is that we do not require knowledge of the noise level; moreover, our method is computationally cheaper. RCS can also be used in conjunction with existing methods to improve performance: we showcase improved results for Cheng and Hua's least-squares (LS) method when RCS information is used. When there are three closely spaced sinusoids, our method outperforms both the ST and LS methods.

Wearable devices have become essential in our daily activities. Due to battery constraints, the use of computing, communication, and storage resources is limited. Mobile cloud computing (MCC) and the recently emerged fog computing (FC) paradigms unleash unprecedented opportunities to augment the capabilities of wearable devices. Partitioning mobile applications and offloading computationally heavy tasks for execution to the cloud or edge of the network is the key. Offloading prolongs the lifetime of the batteries and allows wearable devices to gain access to the rich and powerful set of computing and storage resources of the cloud/edge. In this paper, we experimentally evaluate and discuss the rationale of application partitioning for MCC and FC. To experiment, we develop an Android-based application and benchmark energy and execution time performance of multiple partitioning scenarios. The results unveil architectural tradeoffs that exist between the paradigms and devise guidelines for proper power management of the service-centric Internet-of-Things applications.

Recent advances in wireless communication, sensing, computation and control technologies have paved the way for the development of a new era of Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Demanded by the requirements of information-centric and data-driven intelligent transportation systems (ITS), it is of great significance to explore new paradigms of IoV in supporting large-scale, real-time, and reliable information services. In this article, we propose a hierarchical system architecture, which aims at synthesizing the paradigms of software defined networking and fog computing in IoV and best exploiting their synergistic effects on information services. Specifically, a four-layer architecture is designed, comprising the application layer, the control layer, the virtualization layer, and the data layer, with objectives of enabling logically centralized control via the separation of the control plane and the data plane; facilitating adaptive resource allocation and QoS oriented services based on network functions virtualization and network slicing, and enhancing system scalability, responsiveness, and reliability by exploiting the networking, computation, communication, and storage capacities of fog-based services. On this basis, we further analyze newly arising challenges and discuss future research directions by presenting a cross-layer protocol stack. Finally, for the proof of concept, we implement the system prototype and give two case studies in real-world IoV environments. The results of field tests not only demonstrate the great potential of the new architecture, but also give insight into the development of future ITS.

Leukemia is a type of cancer that affects the blood and bone marrow. The early diagnosis of leukemia is crucial for effective treatment, and digital image processing techniques have shown great potential in this area. In this study, we propose a novel approach for the diagnosis of leukemia and its types using support vector machines and shape-based feature extraction from microscopy images. The proposed method involves image segmentation and extraction of morphological features from blood smears for classification using support vector machines. The results obtained from this approach show promising accuracy rates in the detection and classification of leukemia types. The proposed technique can be used as an effective tool for the automated diagnosis of leukemia and can aid medical professionals in providing timely and accurate diagnosis and treatment for patients. Overall, our study highlights the importance of digital image processing techniques in the field of medical diagnosis and provides a valuable contribution to the diagnosis and treatment of leukemia.

Electroencephalography (EEG) signals have been proven to be effective in evaluating human's cognitive state under specific tasks. Conventional classification models utilized for EEG classification heavily rely on signal pre-processing and hand-designed features. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end deep neural network which is capable of classifying multiple types of cognitive workload of a vehicle driver and the context of driving using only raw EEG signals as its input without any pre-processing nor the need for conventional hand-designed features. Data used in this study are collected throughout multiple driving sessions conducted on a high-fidelity driving simulator. Experimental results conducted on 4 channels of raw EEG data show that the proposed model is capable of accurately detecting the cognitive workload of a driver and the context of driving.

An automated multi-resolution simulation (MRS) framework based on model order reduction (MOR) for accelerating simulation of high-fidelity power electronic circuits (PECs) is presented in this paper. The wide span of eigenvalues of PECs makes their simulation prohibitively slow. This problem is tackled using the proposed approach. Singular perturbation approximation (SPA) is used to derive the reduced order models. The transient contribution of the non-dominant eigenvalues is ignored, retaining the steady-state contribution of all the eigenvalues. Reduced models of different orders or resolutions, each corresponding to a particular level of accuracy are derived. Then, the simulation engine is set such that it dynamically changes the resolution of the simulation. Initially, the original high-resolution model is simulated. As the transients of the fast-states die down, the simulation shifts to a lower resolution. The approach has an advantage that instead of simulating the original system over the entire time-range, a combination of the full and reduced models are simulated. The high-fidelity model is simulated for only a fraction of the simulation cycle. This accelerates the simulation considerably and at the same time ensures that the complete response of the system is obtained with negligible approximation error.

This paper presents a range accuracy analysis for Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar systems with source nonlinearity. The estimation of frequency modulation is critical for accurate range measurement. The study focuses on the effects of source nonlinearity on frequency estimation and range accuracy. The analysis demonstrates that the bandwidth of the hardware and the phase noise of the system play crucial roles in determining the accuracy of range measurement in FMCW systems with source nonlinearity. Moreover, the paper contains a method to correct frequency estimation errors incurred by source nonlinearity using dynamic phase locked loops. Experimental results show that the proposed method can successfully reduce the range error caused by source nonlinearity. Overall, the presented analysis and method provide significant insights into FMCW radar systems and offer a promising approach for improving range accuracy in practical systems.

In a multiuser downlink cellular network with radio frequency (RF) impairments, relay selection and antenna selection have significant effects on system performance. In this paper, a training-based joint antenna and relay selection scheme is proposed. The scheme utilizes channel estimation training sequences to estimate the channel distortion caused by RF impairments. Relay selection is achieved by selecting the relay with the smallest distortion. Antenna selection is performed by ranking the antennas based on the received power level and selecting the top antennas.
