The proposed scheme requires low hardware complexity as only a limited number of training sequences are required for channel estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves significant performance gains in terms of system throughput and error rate compared to other selection schemes. It is concluded that the proposed training-based joint antenna and relay selection scheme can effectively mitigate the effects of RF impairments and improve system performance in a multiuser downlink cellular network.

With the growing popularity of the Internet of Things, the use of smart devices has increased dramatically in a variety of fields, ranging from smart homes to smart cities. One of the key challenges associated with the proliferation of these devices is efficient resource utilization. Virtualization has emerged as a promising solution to this problem, allowing multiple IoT devices to run on a single physical device. In particular, virtualization can improve resource management and enable efficient use of resources. In this paper, we present a performance evaluation of IoT device virtualization for efficient resource utilization. We study the impact of virtualization on performance and resource utilization using cameras as an example use case. Our results demonstrate that virtualization can effectively manage resources and improve performance, making it an attractive solution for managing IoT devices in a variety of applications. Additionally, we explore how cloud computing can be integrated with virtualization to further improve resource utilization in IoT systems. Our work highlights the benefits of adopting virtualization as a resource management technique for smart cities and other IoT applications.

This paper proposes a method for fine-grained lesion annotation in CT images using knowledge mined from radiology reports. The focus is on the annotation of lesions in various organs such as the lung, liver, and lymph nodes. The proposed method includes a two-stage training process that utilizes both the radiology reports and CT images to improve the accuracy of the lesion annotation. The method uses a deep learning approach to automatically identify and annotate lesions in CT images. The experimental results showed that the proposed method achieved high accuracy in lesion annotation, especially for small or hard-to-detect lesions. The proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of lesion annotation in clinical practice, and is expected to have broad applications in the field of radiology and computed tomography.

This paper proposes an efficient starting point to adaptive holomorphic embedding power flow methods, which can greatly improve the runtime and convergence of load flow calculations in power systems. The proposed method utilizes iterative methods to construct a mathematical model that can accurately capture the behavior of power system components, including generators and loads. By incorporating adaptive holomorphic embedding techniques, the proposed approach can effectively improve the computational modeling of power systems and accelerate the convergence of load flow calculations. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy, runtime, and convergence, and can be applied to a wide range of power system scenarios.

With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT), the security of data transmitted through constrained devices has become increasingly important. The Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) is a key protocol in IoT networks and its security is of utmost concern. In this paper, we propose a deep en-route filtering approach for CoAP messages on 6LoWPAN Border Routers, aiming to improve the security of data transmission in CoAP-based IoT networks. Our method is based on deep packet inspection, which allows border routers to analyze messages in real-time and filter out any malicious traffic before it reaches the servers. Our approach is highly effective, with a low false positive rate, and can be easily integrated into existing IoT networks. Overall, our proposal provides a reliable solution for data security in CoAP-based IoT networks and can help ensure the smooth and secure operation of IoT systems.

This paper proposes a natural scene text recognition method based on an encoder-decoder framework. The proposed method involves three main steps: feature extraction, decoding, and character recognition. Convolutional neural networks are used for training and the method is tested on optical character recognition software. The encoder-decoder framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on the recognition of natural scene text, especially on curved and distorted text. The results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach for text recognition in natural scenes.

This paper presents an analysis of the convergence rate of a decentralized asynchronous stochastic gradient descent algorithm. The algorithm utilizes message passing and resource management to optimize a solution. The authors perform an analysis of the effects of delays in the message passing system and resource allocation on the convergence rate. The study focuses on linear programming problems, and the results demonstrate that the algorithm can achieve optimal convergence rates, even in the presence of large message passing delays. The analysis also provides insights into the trade-offs between resource allocation and convergence rate. Overall, the study highlights the importance of careful resource management and message passing in decentralized optimization algorithms.

This paper presents a novel neural sequence model for word sense disambiguation that incorporates multiple attentions. The proposed model combines techniques from computer architecture, decoding, and computational linguistics to improve the accuracy of identifying word senses in natural language processing tasks. This study examines the tasks analysis of computational modeling, aiming to provide a better framework for word sense disambiguation in various contexts. The use of multiple attentions in the model allows for a more comprehensive analysis of sentences and helps to improve the overall accuracy of disambiguation. The model is evaluated on several datasets and outperforms a range of other state-of-the-art models. The proposed method has potential implications for computational linguistics and offers a new direction for research in this area. Additionally, this study offers new insights into the use of indexes for word sense disambiguation in natural language processing tasks.

This research focuses on tracking event-related potentials during BMI (brain-machine interface) driven rehabilitation. The study involved the use of electrodes to measure and record the electric potential generated in the brain during training with a robot sensing system. The aim was to investigate the correlation between the EEG (electroencephalography) signals and the rehabilitation processes. The results of this experiment provide insights on the feasibility of using EEG signals to monitor and assess the effectiveness of BMI-driven rehabilitation in patients with motor dysfunctions. This research contributes to the field of neurorehabilitation and holds potential for the development of more effective treatments for patients with neurological disorders.

The behavior of APT attack has been the hot topic in recent network security study. It is critical to understand the implementation principle of APT attack. In this paper, we analyze the behavior of APT attack in the Ngay campaign from two aspects: network traffic and code implementation. We first set up the attack chain by using network traffic analysis. Then, the vulnerability exploitation process is detailed through reverse code analysis. After that, we illustrate the process of building back door. Lastly, we introduce the obfuscation technology applied in the APT malware samples.

There is no doubt that cloud computing provides a simple but efficient way to share computational resources we have for an information system. Developing a highly effective method for solving the workflow scheduling problem (WSP) is one critical issue for enhancing the performance of such a system that requires to minimize the execution time, rent costs of resources, and transmission costs of data in a cloud workflow management system. This paper presents an efficient search algorithm, which is an extended version of search economics (SE), to solve WSP in a cloud computing environment, called search economics for workflow scheduling algorithm (SEWSA). The proposed algorithm inherits the distinguishing features of SE that uses not only the objective value to make a decision for the later search directions but also the potential of the subsolution space. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can find a better scheduling strategy to optimize the makespan time and to reduce the total cost than other metaheuristic algorithms.

This paper presents an electromagnetic strike action system with self-adjustment of output energy that utilizes batteries, sensors, windings, mechanical energy, soil, and IP networks. The system is designed to be able to strike a target using a remote control, with the output energy of the strike being self-adjusted based on the target's characteristics. The system's design enables it to effectively target a variety of materials, including those with different levels of resistance. It also utilizes sensors to detect the soil and wind conditions that could affect its performance. The system's output energy is generated through the use of windings and mechanical energy, and is controlled through an IP network. This allows for greater precision and accuracy in targeting, making the system ideal for use in military and security applications. Overall, this paper describes a highly effective and adaptable electromagnetic strike action system that is capable of self-adjustment of output energy, making it a valuable tool in many different scenarios.

In recent years, there has been considerable research into developing effective approaches for speech emotion recognition. This paper proposes a new parallelized convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) with spectral features for speech emotion recognition. The proposed approach involves feature extraction through time-frequency analysis, which is then used for speech recognition using convolutional networks. The CRNN model then integrates the spectrally extracted features with hidden Markov models to recognize different emotions from speech data. The approach involves parallelizing the CRNN model, which allows for faster and more efficient processing of large datasets. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through extensive experiments using real-world speech data. The experimental results indicate that the parallelized CRNN model with spectral features achieves superior performance in speech emotion recognition compared to other state-of-the-art approaches. This shows the potential of the proposed method for developing accurate and efficient speech emotion recognition systems, which can be useful for various applications, such as human-machine interaction and data mining.

These days, based on the recent development in IoT technologies, a large number of innovative healthcare applications should be created. Health Internet of Things (HIoT) is a novel technology that used to connect many diver's medical sensors to IoT devices. The HIoT facilitates remote data collection and monitoring in healthcare fields. This paper is a review study that addresses the impact of HIoT on healthcare applications. In this regards, we investigated the most important technologies used in HIoT and describe the main strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of HIoT-based applications. Based on the results, the potential strengths and opportunities of the HIoT technology is very different and widespread; however, it has some significant weaknesses and threats including complexity of handling a huge number of heterogeneous objects, achieving scalability, reliability, efficiency, availability, security, and interoperability with IoT systems across healthcare applications.

With the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), the demand for Massive Machine Type Communications (mMTC) has become increasingly important. This has led to the development of ultra-dense cellular IoT networks that can support millions of machine-type devices (MTDs) in a small area. However, there are still many challenges to overcome in order to provide high-quality service in these networks. One of the main challenges is the limited capacity of the wireless communication channels, which can lead to congestion and degraded quality of service. To address this challenge, machine learning-assisted solutions are proposed to optimize the allocation of wireless resources in the network. In this paper, we provide an overview of the current issues in ultra-dense cellular IoT networks and discuss the potential solutions, including machine learning-assisted protocols and tutorials. We also highlight the importance of using 5G mobile communication technology to achieve better quality of service and network performance in mMTC scenarios. Overall, this paper serves as a roadmap for achieving massive machine type communications in ultra-dense cellular IoT networks through the use of machine learning-assisted solutions.

This paper presents a thermal monitoring and protection system for distribution transformers in residential areas using Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The system utilizes a wireless sensor network for monitoring temperature and humidity levels in the environment surrounding the transformer. The system includes sensors that are installed at different points throughout the distribution transformer to obtain relevant temperature data. The wireless communication network between these sensors and a central control unit allows for continuous temperature measurement and data gathering. In the event of an overheating situation, the system activates cooling mechanisms, such as automated fans or water cooling systems, to provide protection for the transformer. With the advancement of IoT technology, this thermal monitoring and protection system offers a promising solution for enhancing the safety and durability of household distribution transformers.

The internet of things (IoT) plays an important role in our lives and this role is significantly increasing. The combination operation of a device or a NodeMCU is used to reduce cost, gather information, and command and control devices. The most beneficial use of the IoT is to help smart farms, home automation, smart factories, smart cities and big data. The aim and contribution of this research are to reduce costs and increase the effectiveness of the use of the IoT. This study uses NodeMCU to make a composition model-driven automation using a choreography architecture. The Contained Application Protocol (CoAP) is used to the reduce costs of the interface between the compositions. The advantage of using the CoAP composition is that it can be made in the limited condition of the devices. For the precision and accuracy of the composition, we carry out experiments with 5 to 20 compositions.

This paper proposes a new tone correction method for images using quasi-cubic splines in a spherical color model. The approach involves fitting a smooth mathematical model to the color values of the image, which can then be manipulated to adjust overall tone. The spherical color model is used to represent colors as vectors in three-dimensional space, which allows for more accurate analysis of color relationships. The use of splines allows for adjustments to be made without introducing sharp transitions, resulting in smoother and more natural-looking tonal changes. The method is evaluated using computational modeling techniques, and results indicate that it is effective in achieving tone correction with minimal artifacting. Additionally, the approach involves the use of azimuthal angle measurements, which may be useful in applications such as safety analysis. Overall, this paper presents a promising new method for image tone correction that could have a broad range of applications in color analysis and image processing.

Image segmentation is a crucial step in text recognition and document analysis. In this paper, we propose a new approach for graph-based page segmentation using machine learning techniques. Our approach is based on a graph representation of the image, where nodes represent connected components of the image and edges represent spatial relationships between these components. We use layout information and image edge detection to construct the graph-based representation of the image. Our approach employs machine learning algorithms, specifically convolutional neural networks, to train a segmentation model for the graph-based representation. We experimentally evaluate our approach on benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness for accurately segmenting text regions in various document types. Our results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher segmentation accuracy and improved performance across different document layouts and image types.

This paper explores the urgent need for blue-collar workers to receive training in the realities of the digital revolution. As production and service industries increasingly integrate artificial intelligence and technological innovation, it is crucial for workers to adapt to these changes in order to remain relevant in the workforce. The focus of the training would be on the utilization of production and service robots, as they become more prevalent in the day-to-day operations of these industries. In order to remain competitive in the global market, it is essential for companies to invest in the training of their blue-collar workforce, as it will improve productivity and overall efficiency. This paper discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with this transformation, and suggests potential solutions to bridge the technological divide between blue-collar workers and the digital revolution.

Today's software complexity makes developing defect-free software almost impossible. Consequently, developing classifiers to classify software modules into defective and non-defective before software releases have attracted great interest in academia and software industry alike. Although many classifiers have been proposed, no one has been proven superior over others. The major reason is that while a research shows that classifier A is better than classifier B, we can find other research that shows the opposite. These conflicts are usually triggered when researchers report results using their preferable performance evaluation measures such as, recall and precision. Although this approach is valid, it does not examine all possible facets of classifiers performance characteristics. Thus, the performance evaluation might improve or deteriorate if researchers choose other performance measures. As a result, software developers usually struggle to select the most suitable classifier to use in their projects. The goal of this paper is to apply the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP) as a popular multicriteria decision-making technique to reliably evaluate classifiers' performance. This evaluation framework incorporates a wider spectrum of performance measures to evaluate classifiers performance rather than relying on selected preferable measures. The results show that this approach will increase software developers' confidence in research outcomes and help them in avoiding false conclusions and infer reasonable boundaries for them. We exploited 22 popular performance measures and 11 software defect classifiers. The analysis was carried out using KNIME data mining platform and 12 software defect data sets provided by the NASA metrics data program (MDP) repository.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIB) have found a wide range of applications in many consumer products in the last 25 years. The United States Navy and Marine Corps have various applications using LIB, and safe battery technologies are critically needed. While many consumer applications typically utilize smaller, high volume cells, military applications can utilize specialty large-format cells in their LIB packs. One of the most important safety considerations for LIB cells is their thermal stability under various abuses such as exposure to heat, nail penetration, external short circuit, crushing, and so on. Several exothermic reactions can occur as the inner cell temperature increases, and if the heat generation is larger than the dissipated heat to the surroundings, this leads to heat accumulation in the cell and acceleration of the chemical reactions, which can then lead to a thermal runaway. Since the behavior of batteries is strongly affected by the interaction of physics on varying length and time scales: a multi-physics and multi-scale model is needed to simulate this process. While many approaches have been reported in literature, they are not directly applicable in large-format LIB cells and the development of multi-scale and multi-physics models are relatively limited and still computationally expensive. For example, in large formatted battery cells, the uniformity of the electrical potential along the current collectors in the cell composites is no longer given. Additionally, due to the inhomogeneity of the distribution of the temperature field with respect to the cell geometry, thermal dynamics must also be taken into account. This study reports the recently developed multi-scale and multi-physics models for simulating the thermal runway inside a lithium-ion battery using COMSOL software. For the electrochemical processes, the porous electrode theory with contributions coming from exothermic side reactions is used to model abuse mechanisms, which could lead to a thermal runaway. For the thermal-mechanical processes, models of thermal abuse reactions that occur at specific elevated temperatures have been simulated. Prior experimental data on a large-scale lithium-ion battery tested at NSWCCD has been used to construct and validate the model with good agreement.

Growth, invasion, and metastasis of cancers are directly linked to the cancer's stiffness and the solid stress (SSg) that develops inside the cancer. Currently, there are no non-invasive methods to assess the SSg distribution in cancers. In this paper, we develop an analytical model for the compression-induced solid stress (SSc) distribution that generates inside a tumor in a poroelastography experiment. We theoretically prove that the SSc has the same spatial distribution as the SSg inside the tumor. We also demonstrate that it is possible to estimate the spatial distribution parameter of SSg α and the ratio between vascular permeability (VP) and interstitial permeability (IP) from the computed SSc. The developed analytical model is validated using finite element and ultrasound simulations. The technical feasibility of the proposed technique is demonstrated in a small animal model study in vivo. Based on the influential role of solid stress in modulating the cancer microenvironment, the proposed methodology may be useful in cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.

This paper proposes a set of protocols for the Energy Internet that enable universally composable key bootstrapping and secure communication. The Energy Internet is a rapidly growing field that combines energy resources, computational modeling, and smart grids to optimize energy usage and distribution. Cryptography plays a crucial role in ensuring that communications within the Energy Internet are secure and protected from adversaries. The proposed protocols allow for the secure exchange of keys between different entities in the Energy Internet, ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity of data transmission. The use of these protocols is expected to enhance the security of the Energy Internet and promote the wider adoption of smart grid technology. Future work includes testing the proposed protocols in real-world scenarios to evaluate their effectiveness in securing communications within the Energy Internet.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the fusion of multiple convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for fine-grained dog breed categorization. The study focuses on dogs as the primary subject and explores the effectiveness of CNNs fusion techniques for categorizing fine-grained dog breeds. The authors propose a training and visualization methodology for feature extraction and model optimization, and investigate the use of streaming media to streamline the data collection process. Additionally, the paper explores the impact of the kernel and computer architecture on the performance of the CNNs fusion model. The findings of this study provide insights into the potential of CNNs fusion techniques for fine-grained categorization tasks and can be applied to other domains beyond dog breed classification.

Memory-augmented neural networks (MANNs) are designed for question-answering tasks. It is difficult to run a MANN effectively on accelerators designed for other neural networks (NNs), in particular on mobile devices, because MANNs require recurrent data paths and various types of operations related to external memory access. We implement an accelerator for MANNs on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) based on a data flow architecture. Inference times are also reduced by inference thresholding, which is a data-based maximum inner-product search specialized for natural language tasks. Measurements on the bAbI data show that the energy efficiency of the accelerator (FLOPS/kJ) was higher than that of an NVIDIA TITAN V GPU by a factor of about 125, increasing to 140 with inference thresholding.

This paper introduces a new approach for face detection, called R-FCN based deformable convolutional networks. The proposed method utilizes a combination of feature extraction and detectors, including deformable convolution layers, to achieve high accuracy in face detection. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, benchmark testing was conducted, and the results have shown that the performance of the R-FCN based deformable convolutional networks is superior to other state-of-the-art face detection methods. Additionally, this paper outlines the training process for the proposed network, providing important insights into the development of deep learning networks for vision-based applications. These findings demonstrate the potential of the R-FCN based deformable convolutional networks in face detection and provide a solid foundation for future research in this area.

VIMO, which stands for Simultaneous Visual Inertial Model-Based Odometry and Force Estimation, is a promising approach for improving robot sensing systems. In this approach, force and dynamics are incorporated into the vehicle dynamics model, which enables the estimation of external forces acting on the vehicle. By optimizing the model, VIMO can achieve accurate and reliable estimation results. This paper discusses the benefits of using VIMO in robot sensing systems and presents its key features, including force estimation and optimization. The results of experiments conducted to test the effectiveness of the VIMO approach are presented, demonstrating its accuracy and potential for practical applications. Overall, this study highlights the importance of incorporating force and dynamics into robot sensing systems and suggests that VIMO is a valuable tool for achieving this goal.

The identification of persons through earprint and voice print is one of the basic biometric matters. The context of use is situated in smart homes. The main issue is the lack of databases containing voice records and ear images from the same persons collected with a smart phone. In this paper, we propose a new database for the persons identification through ear and voice print in degraded conditions. The database contains 111 subjects with more than 12 samples for each one. The new database is collected in degraded conditions, the ear images have different occlusion as scarf, hair, glasses, earrings while the voice records are collected with different types of noise in the background as music, cars, street, conversation. Interested researchers could contact the author to acquire the database.

This paper proposes a method for stabilizing second-order memristive neural networks with mixed time delays by utilizing nonreduced order. Artificial neural networks have shown great potential in various applications, but delay effects can hinder their stability. The proposed method provides stability criteria for these networks and ensures asymptotic stability and synchronization. The incorporation of mixed time delays in the networks is an important aspect that allows for a more realistic representation of neural activity. The use of nonreduced order helps to simplify the stabilization process and make it more computationally efficient. The results of this study demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach and its potential usefulness in real-world applications.

In order to offer end users an efficient multi-service access, it is necessary to implement high quality network access. This paper analyzes the next generation of passive optical networks. It gives a summary view of current researches conducted in the area of passive optical networks, which are directed towards capacity increase using different technologies.

This survey paper presents a comprehensive overview of fault diagnosis in wireless sensor networks (WSNs), with a specific emphasis on fault detection and fault tolerance techniques. The paper discusses the importance of monitoring and diagnosing faults in WSNs, given their widespread applications in areas such as biomedical monitoring. The paper covers different approaches to fault detection and presents a range of fault tolerant systems, including those based on virtual error masking and ellipsoids. The paper also highlights some of the challenges in developing effective fault diagnosis mechanisms for WSNs and outlines potential areas for future research. Overall, this paper provides a useful resource for researchers and practitioners working in the field of WSNs, showcasing different approaches and techniques for diagnosing faults and ensuring robust and reliable wireless networks.

This paper presents an autonomous intersection management scheme using reservation-based scheduling. The scheme coordinates the access of the autonomous vehicles to an intersection without a traffic light such that all vehicles can travel across the intersection without collision. In this paper, we make our model applicable to real-world system by allowing the vehicles to move within a predefined speed range while in the intersection. Simulation shows the effect of the speed range size to the efficiency of the system.

This research paper explores the use of low precision dynamic fixed-point in training neural networks. The training of neural networks is a crucial area of research and the use of low precision dynamic fixed-point brings a new perspective to this field. The paper discusses the error analysis associated with this approach and presents the benefits of using this technique, including reduced requirements for Graphics processing units (GPUs) and efficient usage of computational resources. The use of heuristic algorithms is also discussed, and their effectiveness in optimizing the training process is highlighted. The paper concludes by presenting findings from market research on the potential impact this technique may have on the future of training neural networks.

In this paper, we evaluate the communication efficiency in the data processing system of a distribution network through various indexes and entropy analysis. We also propose a computational modeling approach to measure the collaboration between different components in the network. Additionally, we analyze the communication networks in the system and suggest areas for improvement in planning to enhance the overall performance of the distribution network. Through our evaluation, we have identified several key areas where improvements can be made to increase the communication efficiency and collaboration within the network. Our proposed approach provides a valuable tool for monitoring and enhancing the performance of data processing systems in distribution networks.

The use of wireless sensor networks has become increasingly popular in the monitoring of physical structures. In this paper, we propose a real-time slope monitoring system using time-domain reflectometry with wireless sensor network. The system utilizes coaxial cables to measure the strain on the slope in real-time. By analyzing the reflection coefficient of the coaxial cable, the system is able to determine the strain and deformations of the slope. Wireless communication is used to transmit the data collected by the sensors to a central processing unit, allowing for real-time monitoring of the slope. The proposed system offers a cost-effective and efficient solution for monitoring the condition and stability of slopes.

The goal of this paper is to perform an experimental research and show that simple statistical predictors can reveal usage patterns of the electrical appliances from smart meter and sensor readings. We used an open data set of Smart* project and its real power and apparent power variability to accomplish this goal. We generated the predictors using block-based statistical information of the real power and apparent power associated with each appliance class type. We constructed five machine learning models using these predictors and evaluated them using random forest classification and the qualitative measures - classification accuracy, out-of-bag error, and misclassification error. Our finding is that the simple statistical predictors that reveal smart home occupants appliance usage patterns and energy consumption details can be obtained through smart home data analytics. Our finding includes that the statistical predictors generated from apparent power can improve the accuracy of the significantly-imbalanced smart home data classification.

This research focuses on determining the optimal window parameters for accurate and reliable decoding of multiple classes of upper limb motor imagery tasks. The study employs electroencephalography (EEG) and frequency-domain analysis to extract features and determine the decoding performance. The research also takes a closer look into task analysis and the use of Microsoft Windows in the analysis process. The findings of this study have important implications for prosthetics design and development, as well as for the further advancement of motor imagery-based brain-computer interface (BCI) technology.

Trends in processor and system architecture, driven by power and complexity, point super-computing landscape toward very high and heterogeneous core count designs. As the number of cores inevitably increase traditional ways of performing large scale computations will also need to evolve from legacy models like OpenMP & MPI. However, such models are very much wedded to a control-flow vision of parallel programs, making it difficult to express asynchrony in programs. To address these challenges, codelet model was developed which is fine-grained, event-driven asynchronous program execution model. In-spite of its initial design goals, the Codelet model is rife with opportunities for further improvements to provide high-performance for both data and control regular applications. The major inspiration behind this work is to leverage the decades of research done to exploit instruction level parallelism (ILP) for the machine instructions inside codelet while build upon the dataflow software pipelining principals at codelet graph level to further enhance performance. In this paper, we propose hardware assisted extensions to the original codelet program execution model in order to implement efficient dataflow software pipelining and extend capabilities of the codelet model. This hardware-software co-design focuses on efficient implementation of data FIFO buffers leveraging proposed optimizations like - FIFO ring buffers and multiple-head FIFO buffers and single owner FIFO buffers to further exploit advantages of dataflow software pipelining. The wide range of scientific, machine learning and specially streaming applications should be able to take advantage of techniques proposed in this paper. Identifying these kernels and bench-marking them are the next anticipated steps for us.

This paper aims to find the optimal cross-subject EEG data alignment method for analysis and BCI. The study focuses on Electroencephalography (EEG), a non-invasive method of recording electrical activity in the brain. Various alignment methods were evaluated and compared using visualization, covariance matrices, task analysis, stability analysis, correlation, and training. The results indicated that a time-shift based approach provides the best alignment across subjects. This approach enables more accurate analysis and interpretation of EEG data, which is essential for developing effective BCI systems. The findings of this study have important implications for the design and implementation of EEG-based BCI technology, as well as for the advancement of neuroscience research.

Quantum data structures, methods, algorithms and software applications for parallel solution of combinatorial problems, including design and test, on classical computers by using extra memory are proposed. Quantum models and methods for design and test of specific logic functionalities are developed based on the use of vector qubit data structures and memory-driven architectures for parallel computing algorithms, in order to significantly improve the performance of testing and deductive simulation of digital systems-on-chips. A new quantum method of test generation for single stuck-at faults of logic functions through taking Boolean derivatives with respect to their qubit coverages is proposed. The quantum method of deductive simulation of stuck-at faults of logical functions through the synthesis of matrices of Boolean derivatives with respect to their qubit coverage has been developed. The performance of methods for test synthesis and their analysis has no analogues in algorithmic performance.

This paper presents a joint multi-view hashing method for large-scale near-duplicate video retrieval, with a focus on feature extraction, hash functions, time complexity, indexing, and error analysis. The proposed approach leverages multiple views of the video data to improve retrieval performance, using a combination of visual and textual features. Hash functions are used to efficiently map the high-dimensional feature vectors to compact binary codes, which are then used for indexing and retrieval. The time complexity of the method is carefully optimized to ensure scalability to large datasets. An error analysis is conducted to evaluate the performance of the method and identify areas for improvement. The proposed approach has important implications for computer science and economics, enabling efficient and accurate video retrieval for a range of applications.

The development of smart cities demands a comprehensive and integrated system that can economize the visual system of city brain. In this context, this paper proposes a unified infrastructure that combines front-end smart visual sensing and back-end intelligent analysis. The proposed infrastructure provides a comprehensive solution for efficient visualization, feature extraction, and deep learning analysis of data generated by camera-based sensors. The integration of visualization and feature extraction allows the identification of patterns and trends within complex data sets, while the application of deep learning algorithms enhances this process by enabling the development of higher-level models. The advantages of this unified infrastructure are significant, as it creates a system that can enhance the performance of city brain by reducing the processing time and improving the accuracy of its decisions. Ultimately, this infrastructure exemplifies the potential of integrating various forms of technology to revolutionize the way we perceive and understand our urban environments, and shows great potential for advancing the field of smart cities in the future.

This paper proposes an adaptive sampling process for automated multivariate macromodeling based on Hamiltonian-based passivity metrics. The computational modeling of integrated circuits requires the adaptation models, solid modeling, data models, numerical models and standards. However, the complexity and dimensionality of the models pose challenges for efficient simulation. The proposed sampling process selects an optimal subset of the original data points which can represent the entire dataset with acceptable error bound. The Hamiltonian-based passivity metric is used to evaluate the quality of the subset and ensure the passivity of the resultant macromodel. The proposed method is compared with other state-of-the-art methods showing its superior performances. The proposed process can significantly reduce the computational cost while maintaining the accuracy of the simulation results. This research provides a practical solution for the development of macromodels in integrated circuit modeling.

Integrating hashing into collaborative filtering (CF) has been a promising solution to address the efficiency problem of large-scale recommender systems, i.e., hashing users and items into binary codes and then making recommendations in Hamming space. However, most of the existing hashing methods for CF solely focus on modeling the user-item similarity (a.k.a. preference) but omit the user-user and item-item similarities, which cannot well preserve the original geometry in the vector space. Another tough issue is how to effectively tackle the encoding loss from the continuous vector space to the discrete Hamming space. In this paper, we propose a neural binary representation (NBR) learning approach by combining hashing with a neural network for the large-scale CF tasks. Our NBR problem is formulated as a Hamming similarity loss plus two anchor smoothing terms, which jointly preserve the intrinsic user-item, user-user, and item-item similarities. To compensate the encoding loss introduced by hashing, the anchors for users and items are pre-learned using both user-item interactions and the side-information of users and items through an AutoEncoder model. In particular, to solve the NBR problem, we develop a computationally efficient algorithm, which learns the binary codes in a fast bit-by-bit way and achieves less quantization deviation than the conventional CF hashing schemes. The extensive experiments on three benchmarks validate the superiority of our NBR approach in comparison to the state-of-the-art CF hashing methods.

Domination number is of practical interest in several theoretical and applied scenes. In the problem of wireless networking, the dominating idea is used to deduce an efficient route within the adhoc mobilenetworks. It has also been used for the summarization of documents and making a design of secure web-systems for electrical recursive grids. In this paper, we explore an important class of domination numbers, which is the 2-rainbow independent dominating function (2RiDF) on graphs. The minimum weight of a 2RiDF on a graph G is called the 2-rainbow independent domination number of G. A graph G is 2-rainbow independent domination stable if the 2-rainbow independent domination number of G remains unchanged under removal of any vertex. As a result, we characterize 2-rainbow independent domination stable tree-networks and study the effect of edge removal on 2-rainbow independent domination number in trees.

Utilisation of light emitting diodes (LEDs) and printed electroluminescent elements for manufacturing of flexible displays to be integrated in textile items was analysed. The comparative investigation focused on the necessary manufacturing processes, on the architecture of driver electronics, on achievable display brightness, on lifetime expectations and reliability aspects of the systems. Printed electroluminescent display demonstrators were manufactured and integrated in jackets for the currently running field test. Description of the produced systems as well as the results of the comparative analysis are presented.

Desktop and application virtualization suffers from delay. Opening sessions and remote applications implies to load a non-negligible amount of data, parameters and services. This can be solved by predicting the future activities of the users and pre-loading the required resources. We thus propose a complete approach that automatically discovers the periodical patterns of the users and that automatically builds a probabilistic model of user's behaviour. A kernel density estimator is exploited to estimate the probability density function of an application to be launched by a user. Using the probabilistic approach allows to predict the application a user will open and to reduce the launching time. The efficiency of the proposed approach has been verified by an implementation in a virtualization tool under real operating conditions.

In recent years, serverless computing platforms have gained momentum as a popular choice for deploying applications. However, the migration to such platforms can often result in increased latency due to the cold start of functions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to mitigate this issue by incorporating keep-alive workloads that maintain a warm state of functions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through computational modeling and present results that show significant reductions in latency. Furthermore, we explore the use of containers and load management techniques to optimize the deployment of these keep-alive workloads. Our approach has implications for cloud computing providers and organizations seeking to improve their application performance in a serverless computing environment. We use Java as a case study to evaluate our approach and validate the feasibility and effectiveness of our proposed solution. Finally, we discuss the potential future directions for research in load modeling and optimization for serverless computing platforms.

This paper proposes a novel approach to hyperspectral image classification based on multiple feature learning. The technique makes use of edge-preserving features for feature extraction and image edge detection. The approach also utilizes a kernel-based data mining approach, which allows the identification of relevant features for classification. The technique includes filtering of the hyperspectral image data to extract relevant information for detection and classification. The proposed method is compared to traditional approaches in hyperspectral image classification, and results show that the proposed approach outperforms these traditional approaches in terms of classification accuracy. The approach demonstrates the effectiveness of edge-preserving features in hyperspectral image classification, and the potential for kernel-based approaches to data mining for this application. Overall, the study highlights the importance of feature selection and image filtering in hyperspectral image classification, and provides a promising approach for future research in this area.

Robot navigation through crowds poses a difficult challenge to AI systems, since the methods should result in fast and efficient movement but at the same time are not allowed to compromise safety. Most approaches to date were focused on the combination of pathfinding algorithms with machine learning for pedestrian walking prediction. More recently, reinforcement learning techniques have been proposed in the research literature. In this paper, we perform a comparative evaluation of pathfinding/prediction and reinforcement learning approaches on a crowd movement dataset collected from surveillance videos taken at Grand Central Station in New York. The results demonstrate the strong superiority of state-of-the-art reinforcement learning approaches over pathfinding with state-of-the-art behavior prediction techniques.

The Cloud computing in simple terms is storing and accessing data through internet. The data stored in the cloud is managed by cloud service providers. Storing data in cloud saves users time and memory. But once user stores data in cloud, he loses the control over his data. Hence there must be some security issues to be handled to keep users data safely in the cloud. In this work, we projected a secure auditing system using Third Party Auditor (TPA). We used Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm for encrypting user’s data and Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-2) to compute message digest. The system is executed in Amazon EC2 cloud by creating windows server instance. The results obtained demonstrates that our proposed work is safe and takes a firm time to audit the files.

In the field of image processing and computer vision, the denoising of noisy images is an important and challenging task. The BM3D algorithm has shown promising results in image denoising, but the choice of its parameters can significantly affect its performance. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for selecting the optimal parameter values for BM3D denoising algorithm using no-reference metric. We use a set of image databases with different types and levels of noise to evaluate the performance of our method. Our approach relies on the estimation of noise levels and the use of Laplace equations for image edge detection. The proposed method provides accurate and reliable noise measurement and estimation, which allows the selection of appropriate parameter values for BM3D algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of PSNR and image quality.

To determine an appropriate trading time for buying or selling stocks is always a difficult task. The common way to deal with it is using trading strategies formed by technical or fundamental indicators. Lots of approaches have been presented on how to form trading strategies and how to set suitable parameters for those strategies. Furthermore, some approaches were also designed to optimize a trading strategy portfolio, which is a set of strategies where the return and risk of the portfolio can be maximized and minimized, respectively. To provide a more useful trading strategy portfolio, we first define a group trading strategy portfolio (GTSP). Then, an algorithm that utilizes the grouping genetic algorithm is designed for solving the GTSP optimization problem. In the chromosome representation, the grouping, strategy, and weight parts are employed to encode a possible GTSP. The fitness value of a chromosome is calculated by the group balance, weight balance, portfolio return, and risk to assess the quality of every possible solution. Genetic operators, including crossover, mutation, and inversion, are applied on the population to form a new offspring. Evolution is continued until the stop conditions are reached. Lastly, experiments were conducted on two real datasets with different trends to show that the advantages and the effectiveness of the presented approach.

With the development of aviation, the air traffic density in the terminal area is high and the traffic situation is relatively complex, which brings challenges to the flight deployment. In order to fully understand the air flight situation and provide decision-making basis for controllers, this paper proposes a key conflict aircraft identification method based on complex network theory and node deletion method. First, an aircraft state network is constructed with an aircraft as nodes and airborne collision avoidance system (ACAS) communication relations as edges. Network efficiency, network robustness, connection density, and largest component were used as the indexes of network performance. The weight of each index is determined by using AHP-entropy weight method. A multi-attribute decision-making method was introduced to quantify network performance. Then we used a node deletion method to determine key conflict aircrafts. The simulation and experiment are respectively carried out on the artificial network and the aircraft state network of a certain day in the terminal area of Kunming Changshui Airport. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can identify the key conflict points in the aircraft state network. The deployment of selected nodes can not only effectively reduce the complexity of the flight state network, but also provide a reference for air traffic control services and reduce the control difficulty of the controller.

In this paper, we describe the development and evaluation of a low-cost WiFi Media Access Control (MAC) scanner as a traffic sensor. The scanner was designed to monitor wireless fidelity (WiFi) traffic and collect data for analysis. It operates by capturing packets transmitted on the WiFi network and extracting information on the Media Access Protocol (MAP) used. The collected data is then stored in databases and can be accessed through cloud computing platforms for further analysis. The scanner also supports Bluetooth monitoring, providing a more comprehensive view of wireless traffic. However, the privacy concerns associated with the collection and storage of WiFi traffic data are also addressed. Overall, the low-cost scanner provides a valuable tool for understanding wireless traffic patterns and can be used by researchers, network administrators, and other interested parties.

In recent years, the development of distributed computation frameworks has significantly contributed to the advancement of circuit evolutionary design under CS network architecture. This paper presents a comprehensive review on the use of distributed computation frameworks in circuit evolutionary design. Specifically, we focus on task analysis, computational modeling, integrated circuit modeling, circuit synthesis, genetic algorithms, computer architecture, and sociology in the context of circuit evolutionary design. Through this review, we highlight the key benefits and challenges associated with the use of distributed computation frameworks in circuit evolutionary design. Our findings suggest that distributed computation frameworks offer a promising approach to optimizing circuit design, and that their successful implementation requires careful consideration of various factors such as network topology, communication protocols, and algorithmic design. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the current state-of-the-art in distributed computation frameworks for circuit evolutionary design under CS network architecture, and highlights important areas for future research.

Template attack is a popular side-channel attack method in cryptography. One way to improve the success rate of template attack is to use clustering algorithms to group similar traces together. In this paper, we propose the application of Gaussian mixture clustering algorithm in template attack. We first extract features from the power traces, such as Hamming weight, and then use the correlation coefficient to measure the similarity between the traces. The clustering is performed using the covariance matrices of the features. We experimented with several different prediction algorithms and found that the combination of Gaussian mixture clustering and prediction based on linear regression achieved the best performance. Our results demonstrate the potential of using Gaussian mixture clustering algorithm for improving side-channel attacks in cryptography.

This paper studies a predictive modeling for cutting energy consumption in CNC turning process by using deep learning methods. An analysis of energy consumption in cutting period is firstly presented, based on which the impact factors of energy are clarified. Then the data collection platform and data pre-processing are introduced, followed by a brief review of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Stacked Auto-Encoder (SAE) and Deep Belief Network (DBN). These modeling methods are tested by k-fold cross-validation. The obtained results show that SAE is the most suitable method to model the relationship between process parameters, machining configuration and cutting energy.

This paper presents a modelling and simulation study of glass frit bonding of silicon wafers for micromechanical devices. The semiconductor device modeling is used to investigate the bonding process through the use of computational modeling. The glass frit bonding process achieves high bonding strength, while minimizing the introduction of residual stresses to the device. The simulation results show that the bonding process increases the homogeneity and uniformity of the interface between glass and silicon. The glass frit bonding process is a promising technique for the fabrication of micromechanical devices, and the results of this study provide a valuable insight into the mechanics and properties of the bond.

This paper investigates the controller design problem of networked control systems subject to cyber attacks. A hybrid-triggering communication strategy is employed to save the limited communication resources. State measurements are transmitted over a communication network and may be corrupted by cyber attacks. The aim of this paper is to design a controller for a new closed-loop system model with consideration of randomly occurring cyber attacks and the hybrid-triggering scheme. A stability criterion is obtained for the system stabilization by employing Lyapunov stability theory and stochastic analysis techniques. Moreover, the desired controller gain is derived by resorting to some matrix inequalities. Finally, a numerical example is exploited to demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed scheme.

The paper proposes a novel approach for skin lesion segmentation using a Decision-Augmented Generative Adversarial Network (DA-GAN). The method involves image segmentation to isolate specific regions of interest, namely skin lesions, by enhancing the accuracy of mask creation using Gallium Nitride (GaN) based Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs). In addition, the DA-GAN architecture utilizes generators and discriminators to generate high-quality skin lesion segmentation maps. The proposed method also incorporates decision layers to enhance the accuracy of lesion segmentation by providing more control over the training process. Results indicate that the proposed DA-GAN architecture outperforms previous methods for skin lesion segmentation, demonstrating its potential as an effective tool for skin lesion detection and diagnosis. Overall, the study offers an innovative solution for accurately detecting and segmenting skin lesions, which could ultimately aid in the development of more efficient and accurate diagnostic and treatment methods.

This paper proposes an application of the continuous deep reinforcement learning approach to the pursuit-evasion differential game. The study focuses on developing a mathematical model to solve the game, approximating optimal policies, and enhancing decision making of the agents involved. Training algorithms are utilized to improve performance and maneuverability of the agents based on vehicle dynamics. The findings of the research demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in solving the pursuit-evasion differential game, which has numerous applications in various fields including surveillance, military, and security systems. The study contributes to the existing literature on reinforcement learning and its applications to game theory, highlighting the potential benefits of utilizing deep reinforcement learning techniques in complex decision-making scenarios.

IoT devices generate an enormous amount of data that needs to be processed efficiently for effective decision making. Peer-to-peer computing has been proposed as a way to leverage unused computing resources of IoT devices for data processing. However, this approach requires efficient data caching mechanisms to reduce the data transmission and processing latencies. In this paper, we propose a middleware-based data caching approach that utilizes machine learning techniques for efficient data caching. We show that our approach offers significant improvements in scalability and resilience compared to traditional data caching approaches. The proposed approach leverages the sensor data for real-time monitoring of cache performance and dynamically adjusts the caching policies based on the data characteristics. Our simulation results validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed approach, demonstrating its potential to address the challenges of IoT data caching.

In the field of semiconductor manufacturing, process faults can have a significant impact on yield and product performance. The ability to quickly and accurately detect and diagnose these faults is critical to maintaining high-quality production. In this paper, we propose a Denoised Residual Trace Analysis (DRTA) approach for monitoring semiconductor process faults. Our approach utilizes feature extraction, fault detection, and semiconductor device modeling techniques to identify abnormal behavior in the production process. Furthermore, we employ noise reduction methods to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of collected data, which enhances the accuracy of fault detection. To classify and evaluate the collected data, we also utilize classification algorithms and data models. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DRTA approach for accurately identifying and diagnosing process faults in semiconductor manufacturing, providing valuable insights for improving production efficiency and quality.

This paper proposes a method for word recognition in captured images by using a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained with synthetic images. The synthetic images were created by combining characters and backgrounds to simulate real-world images. Feature extraction was used to identify key elements in the image and image edge detection was applied to improve accuracy. The network was trained using a deep learning approach, resulting in high accuracy in word recognition. Three-dimensional displays were used to visualize the performance of the CNN, showing its ability to accurately recognize words in various orientations and lighting conditions. Overall, this study presents a promising method for word recognition in real-world images using synthetic image training with CNN and deep learning techniques.

Frequency-modulated differential chaos shift keying ultrawideband (FM-DCSK UWB) system has attracted more and more attention in recent years because of its low-complexity and low-power advantages. Nevertheless, its system performance is severely degraded in the presence of narrowband interference (NBI), which further limits its practical applications. In this paper, an enhanced energy-based detector (EED) is proposed for the FM-DCSK UWB system to tackle this problem. Compared with the conventional energy detector (ED), the proposed EED significantly enhances the anti-NBI capability while maintaining the low-power and low-complexity feature. As a further insight, the analytical bit-error-rate (BER) expression of the proposed EED-based FM-DCSK UWB system is derived over additive white Gaussian noise as well as IEEE 802.15.4a multipath fading channels. Moreover, simulation results are carried out to demonstrate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the merit of the proposed EED. It is illustrated that the proposed EED achieves better performance than the conventional ED in various transmission scenarios. Thanks to the above-mentioned advantages, the proposed EED-based FM-DCSK UWB system appears to be an excellent candidate for low-power and low-complexity tactile Internet-of-Things applications, e.g., wireless sensor networks and wireless body area networks.

Aiming at the problems of premature convergence and easily falling into local optimums of the antlion optimization algorithm, a chaos antlion optimization algorithm based on the chaos search is proposed. Firstly, in the algorithm, the population is initialized by using the tent chaotic mapping, and the self-adaptive dynamic adjustment of chaotic search scopes is proposed in order to improve the overall fitness and the optimization efficiency of the population. Then, the tournament strategy is used to select antlions. Finally, the logistic chaos operator is used to optimize the random walk of ants, which forms a global and local parallel search mode with the antlion's foraging behavior. The performance algorithm is tested through 13 complex high-dimensional benchmark functions and three dimensional path planning problems. The experimental results of six complex high-dimensional benchmark functions show that the presented algorithm has a better convergence speed and precision than the standard antlion algorithm and other optimization algorithms, and is suitable for the optimization of complex high dimensional functions. The trajectory planning experimental results show that compared with the antlion optimizer (ALO) algorithm, grey wolf optimizer (GWO), particle swarm optimization (PSO) and artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm, it has advantages in speed and accuracy to obtain a specific path, and it is of great value in actual problems.

This paper proposes a traffic-aware dynamic container migration approach for real-time support in mobile edge clouds. It focuses on using container technology in cloud computing environments to achieve better resource utilization and QoS. Traffic-awareness is achieved by monitoring network bandwidth usage and dynamically migrating containers to nodes with sufficient resources to handle incoming traffic. The proposed approach also takes into account the availability of random access memory and load modeling to assist in migration decisions. The goal is to maintain quality of experience for users of real-time systems while optimizing resource utilization in mobile edge clouds. The results of experiments conducted on a prototype system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving QoS and reducing resource waste.

In this paper, the authors present a delay analysis of a gated service MAC protocol for fiber-wireless 5G MmWave C-RANs. The study focuses on analyzing the delays incurred due to the protocol operation and proposes solutions to reduce them. The authors discuss different protocols and techniques such as optical buffering, passive optical networks, and logic gates, that can be employed to ensure efficient and low-latency communication in 5G mobile networks. The results of the study indicate that the proposed MAC protocol reduces the delays significantly when compared to other protocols. The findings of this research can be helpful in designing and developing efficient MAC protocols for future 5G mobile communication systems, particularly for those using MmWave C-RANs.

This paper presents the design and implementation of an IoT-based accident detection system for smart cars. The proposed system uses Global Positioning System (GPS) technology to track the location of automobiles in real-time and detect accidents by analyzing sudden changes in acceleration and deceleration. The system also utilizes Internet of Things (IoT) principles to transmit accident information to remote servers, where it is stored in databases and analyzed using cloud computing resources. This approach allows for faster and more accurate accident detection, which can help to reduce response times and potentially save lives. The results show that the proposed system is effective in detecting accidents and can be easily integrated into existing smart car technologies. Overall, the study demonstrates the potential of IoT-based accident detection systems to improve road safety and advance the development of smart transportation networks.

To overcome the slacking effect and motivate the patients to actively participate into the training therapy, it is crucial to achieve online assessment of patients’ neural engagement and functional performance in robot-assisted rehabilitation. In this work, a fine motor control task has been designed for functional training of the upper limbs. The subject needs to control the hand position and gripping force, with visual and haptic feedback. Then subjects’ neural engagement and functional performance were assessed online based on the measured EEG and motion information. Experiments with healthy subjects have been conducted, and the relationship between subjects’ neural engagement and functional performance with the task configuration parameters was studied through statistical analysis.

Quite a few physiological measures have been shown to correlate with psychological stress, and used to design some stress detection algorithms. As most of them are also known to react to non-affective mental states as well, physiology-driven stress models based on these features may lack from specificity. This article tackles this issue by looking for physiological features that are both responsive to affective stress load and minimally sensitive to cognitive activity. A laboratory experiment was designed in such a way that activity-related variations in physiological measures can be isolated during exposure to common tasks. A pressure component was defined and extracted from our data. Its relevance as a predictor of features' ability to distinguish between the stressful and control conditions was shown from descriptive statistics. A feature selection procedure was applied on usual heart rate, heart rate variability and skin conductance-based features, to identify the most pressure-specific ones in a between-subjects perspective. Finally, a simple model built from the selected features succeeded in detecting 87.5% of stress examples among instances of stressless task performance.

Radar technology for at home health-care has many advantages such as safety, reliability, privacy-preserving, and contact-less sensing nature. Detecting falls using radar has recently gained attention in smart health care. In this paper, CapsFall, a new method for fall detection using an ultra-wideband radar that leverages the recent deep learning advances is proposed. To this end, a radar time series is derived from the radar back-scattered matrix and its time-frequency representation is obtained and used as input to the capsule network for automatic feature learning. In contrast to other existing methods, the proposed CapsFall method relies on multi-level feature learning from radar time-frequency representations. In particular, the proposed method utilizes a capsule network for automating feature learning and enhancing model discriminability. The experiments are conducted using a set of radar signals collected from ten subjects when performing various activities in a room environment. The performance of the proposed CapsFall method is evaluated in terms of classification metrics and compared with those of the other existing methods based on convolutional neural network, multi-layer perceptron, decision tree, and support vector machine. The results show that the proposed CapsFall method outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity values.

Biomarker inference from biomedical images is one of the main tasks of medical image analysis. Standard techniques follow a segmentation-and-measure strategy, where the structure is first segmented and then the measurement is performed. Recent work has shown that such strategy could be replaced by a direct regression of the biomarker value in using regression networks. While achieving high correlation coefficients, such techniques operate as a 'black-box', not offering quality-control images. We present a methodology to regress the biomarker from the image while simultaneously computing the quality control image. Our proposed methodology does not require segmentation masks for training, but infers the segmentations directly from the pixels that used to compute the biomarker value. The network proposed consists of two steps: a segmentation method to an unknown reference and a summation method for the biomarker estimation. The network is optimized using a dual loss function, L2 for the biomarkers and an L1 to enforce sparsity. We showcase our methodology in the problem of pectoralis muscle area (PMA) and subcutaneous fat area (SFA) inference in a single slice from chest-CT images. We use a database of 7000 cases to which only the value of the biomarker is known for training and a test set of 3000 cases with both, biomarkers and segmentations. We achieve a correlation coefficient of 0.97 for PMA and 0.98 for SFA with respect to the reference standard. The average DICE coefficient is of 0.88 (PMA) and 0.89 (SFA). Comparing with standard segment-and-measure techniques, we achieve the same correlation for the biomarkers but smaller DICE coefficients in segmentation. Such is of little surprise, since segmentation networks are the upper limit of performance achievable, and we are not using segmentation masks for training. We can conclude that it is possible to infer segmentation masks from biomarker regression networks.

The Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm and its applications have been gaining popularity recently. The Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) is a major area of IoT applications. With ITS the transportation infrastructure is supported with advanced networking and computing technologies to better manage traffics on the roads. The Vehicular Ad-Hoc Network (VANET) stands out as an important technology under the ITS. The VANET technology supports different architectures for data communication, namely, vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V), vehicle-to-road-side (V2R), vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I), and infrastructure-toinfrastructure (I2I). In V2R communication, data flow between vehicles and roadside units (RSUs) to convey important information about the road traffic and emergency situations. This data should be transferred with high probability of successful delivery. Also, the sensitivity of this data requires reducing the end-to-end communication delay. The IEEE 802.15.4 standard is one of the important candidate standards that supports the V2R communications. In this paper, we propose the Dynamic Window Algorithm (DWA); a backoff algorithm that targets improving the performance of V2R communications in terms of throughput and delay. This is attained by proposing changes to the operation of the standard Binary Exponent Backoff (BEB) algorithm (in IEEE 802.15.4 MAC). A Java-based simulation tool has been developed to simulate both BEB and DWA algorithms and conduct a comparison study between them. Our results show that in clusters of 20 nodes, the performance in terms of throughput and delay is improved by 32% and 88%, respectively, with DWA.

Scattering properties of multiple-layer anisotropic metasurfaces are characterized based on generalized boundary conditions. Once surface susceptibilities of all layers are determined, reflection and transmission coefficients could be readily derived for arbitrary incident angles and polarizations. The validity of this analytical method is demonstrated through comparison between computed results and full-wave simulations.

The development of intelligent sensors and the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the emergence of navigation solutions that allow individuals to navigate unfamiliar environments with ease. However, the challenge remains in ensuring optimal performance of such algorithms while minimizing the occurrence of disorientation, a key symptom of certain types of diseases. To address this challenge, there is a need for a framework-supported mechanism of testing algorithms for assessing memory and detecting disorientation from IoT sensors. This paper proposes a novel approach that utilizes three-dimensional displays and task analysis to evaluate the performance of navigation algorithms in detecting disorientation. The approach provides a systematic way of examining the behavior of individuals in unfamiliar environments and allows for the optimization of navigation solutions to reduce the occurrence of disorientation in high-risk individuals. The proposed framework would be valuable for researchers and practitioners in developing and testing navigation algorithms for use in healthcare and other settings where disorientation can have serious consequences.

Convergecast scheduling is a crucial aspect of industrial wireless sensor networks. Job shop scheduling algorithms are used to schedule the various tasks that need to be performed by the network. The topology of the network also plays a significant role in determining the best scheduling algorithm to be used. Interference between nodes is an important factor that must be taken into account when scheduling tasks. Local available channel sets must be considered when scheduling tasks, as they can greatly affect the efficiency of the network. Overall, an effective convergecast scheduling algorithm is essential for the smooth operation of industrial wireless sensor networks.

This paper presents an Internet of Things (IoT) based intelligent industry monitoring system for monitoring pollution, gases, and temperature in various industries. The system incorporates a wide range of sensors, including temperature sensors, to collect real-time data on the levels of pollutants and gases emitted by industries. The gathered data is then analyzed using machine learning algorithms to provide insights and recommendations to industries and regulatory authorities regarding their environmental impact. The proposed system aims to provide an efficient and effective solution for monitoring industrial pollution and reducing its hazardous impact on the environment.

This paper proposes a new energy-efficient routing framework for Wireless Nanosensor Networks (WNSNs) with a focus on the field of Nanobioscience that utilizes nanoscale devices. The proposed framework addresses the challenges of energy efficiency and delays in WSNs, which are critical factors that affect the overall energy consumption and performance of the network. The design framework includes a novel routing algorithm that considers energy consumption, remaining energy level, and communication delay. By implementing this algorithm within the WNSN, the proposed framework can optimize energy consumption, prolong network lifetime, and reduce delays. The proposed framework uses routing optimization techniques that allow for energy-efficient routing without sacrificing performance. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can enhance energy efficiency and reduce delays in WNSNs, making it highly suitable for the energy-efficient routing in the field of Nanobioscience.

Non-coherent multiuser massive MIMO-OFDM with differential modulation is an innovative approach for improving the efficiency of wireless communication systems.
