This approach employs OFDM to enable efficient signal transmission, and also adopts differential phase shift keying modulation to achieve better data rate and tolerance to non-coherent transmission. The technique also involves frequency-domain analysis to ensure robustness in interference-prone environments. Additionally, channel estimation is performed to enhance signal to noise ratio and receivers are implemented to enable successful decoding of signals even in the presence of noise and interference. These techniques remarkably improve the overall performance and reliability of multiuser MIMO-OFDM systems, making them an excellent candidate for next-generation wireless communication systems.

The paper proposes a hybrid fast motion estimation approach for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) which is a new standard for video encoding. The goal of this approach is to reduce the bit rate required to encode video while maintaining a high quality. This is achieved by combining two existing fast motion estimation algorithms, namely Merge mode and Diamond Search mode, into a single hybrid algorithm. The paper evaluates the hybrid algorithm by comparing it with both the Merge mode and Diamond Search mode in terms of bit rate and complexity. Experimental results show that the proposed hybrid algorithm achieves significant improvements in encoding efficiency and complexity reduction. This approach has implications for video encoding standards as it offers an efficient solution for achieving high quality video at lower bit rates, which is particularly useful for mobile devices and networks with limited bandwidth.

This paper proposes a new approach for diagnosing electrical and mechanical faults in induction motors by utilizing principal component analysis (PCA) and two-stage Bayesian sensor fusion. The proposed approach aims to address the challenges associated with identifying faults in induction motors, such as the complexity of the motor system and the variety of potential fault sources. The approach involves using PCA to extract features from the vibration data generated by the sensors, which are then used to construct the Bayesian models for fault detection. The two-stage fusion approach involves fusing the data from multiple sensors in a hierarchical fashion, which enhances both the accuracy and confidence of the fault diagnosis. The proposed approach is evaluated using experimental data, and the results show that it outperforms several other commonly used fault detection methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings of this study provide insights into the development of more effective and efficient techniques for diagnosing faults in induction motors, which can improve the reliability and safety of motor-driven systems.

In this paper combines the artificial neural network (ANN) method and the internal resistance measuring method, which is designed for the lithium-ion battery state of charge (SOC) estimation. It is different from the general neural network research that only uses voltage and current as parameters. The input layer adds important parameters: the battery voltage and current, and the internal resistance of the battery as external inputs. We design a recurrent neural networks (RNN) model with non-linear autoregressive with exogenous input (NARX). The network compares the difference between the simulation results under the same benchmark with the back-propagation neural networks (BPNN). Experiments show that this architecture not only improves the convergence speed of the neural network, but also shortens its average execution time, and the mean-square error is improved. It is a good indicator of the accuracy of the measurement. This paper also discusses the application of this architecture to the difference between DC internal resistance and AC internal resistance.

Accurately modeling and predicting wireless channel quality variations is essential for a number of networking applications such as scheduling and improved video streaming over 4G LTE networks and bit rate adaptation for improved performance in WiFi networks. In this paper, we propose an encoder-decoder based sequence-to-sequence deep learning model that is capable of predicting future wireless signal strength variations based on past signal strength data. We consider two different versions of the deep learning model; the first and second versions use LSTM and GRU as their basic cell structure, respectively. In contrast to prior work that is primarily focused on designing models for particular network settings, the deep learning model is highly adaptable and can predict future channel conditions for different networks, sampling rates, mobility patterns, and communication standards. We compare the performance (i.e., the root mean squared error of future predictions) of our model with respect to two baselines-i) auto-regression(1), and ii) linear regression for multiple networks and communication standards. In particular, we consider 4G LTE, WiFi, an industrial network operating in the 5.8 GHz range, Zigbee, and WiMAX networks operating under varying levels of user mobility and observe that the deep learning model provides significantly superior performance. Finally, we provide detailed discussion on key design decisions including insights into hyper-parameter tuning of the model.

End-to-End Cascade CNN for Simultaneously Face Detection and Alignment is a deep learning model developed for the task of face detection and alignment. The model is trained using a large dataset of faces and is capable of simultaneously detecting faces and aligning them for further processing. The training process involves cascading multiple Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in order to achieve higher accuracy in face detection. The model is able to generate proposals for face detection and uses calibration techniques to improve accuracy. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the task of face detection and alignment and the challenges associated with it. The proposed model is evaluated on the Microsoft Windows Dataset and achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of detection accuracy and speed. Overall, the End-to-End Cascade CNN presents an effective approach for simultaneously detecting and aligning faces, which could be useful in a variety of applications such as surveillance systems and facial recognition technology.

This paper presents a study on the use of Business Intelligence (BI) for analyzing department unit performance in eProcurement systems. The research focuses on the utilization of data warehouses, procurement data, and databases in the BI process. The study outlines key challenges in implementing BI models for eProcurement systems and discusses the benefits of using data mining techniques to extract insights from procurement data. The paper also presents a case study of a large organization that implemented BI solutions to improve its procurement process. Overall, the research contributes to a better understanding of the role of BI in analyzing department unit performance in eProcurement systems and highlights the importance of integrating BI solutions into procurement systems to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

The FHIR data model presents a promising approach for developing intelligent multimodal interfaces in medical services. This model has gained popularity due to its ability to provide a comprehensive and flexible platform for healthcare data exchange. Moreover, it offers an effective solution for training and software development in medical services. The FHIR data model adheres to ISO standards and ensures the interoperability of diverse user interfaces. It provides a standardized and uniform approach for developing data models that can improve medical services by facilitating the exchange of information between various healthcare systems. Consequently, the FHIR data model can be utilized as a foundation for developing intelligent multimodal interfaces that can improve medical services and enhance overall patient care.

Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects millions of people worldwide. Accurate diagnosis of PD is essential for timely treatment and management of the disease. In this paper, we propose a longitudinal and multi-modal data learning approach for PD diagnosis using stacked sparse auto-encoder (SSAE). The proposed approach involves task analysis, diffusion tensor imaging, encoding, feature extraction, biomedical imaging, and support vector machines (SVM). We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach using longitudinal and multi-modal data from patients with PD. Our results show that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy and outperforms several state-of-the-art methods for PD diagnosis. This study offers a promising direction for improving the accuracy and reliability of PD diagnosis through longitudinal and multi-modal data analysis using advanced machine learning techniques.

This paper proposes the application of dynamically constructed macro basis functions to antenna arrays with interconnected elements. The use of Jacobian matrices in the construction of macro basis functions is explored to improve the convergence of the method of moments. Iterative methods are utilized to solve the scattering problem of the antenna arrays. A mathematical model is developed to incorporate the interconnected elements in the antenna array. Simulation results show that the proposed method provides accurate results with faster convergence compared to the traditional method of moments. The use of dynamically constructed macro basis functions can provide a more efficient approach to the design and optimization of antenna arrays.

Ground penetrating radar (GPR) has been widely used in the field of buried object detection due to its non-destructive and high-resolution imaging capabilities. However, the interpretation of GPR images for object identification remains a challenge. This paper proposes a deep learning approach for object identification from GPR images. The proposed method utilizes time-domain analysis and finite difference methods to preprocess GPR data and extract features. Then, a neural network model is trained using a large dataset of GPR images for object identification. The proposed method achieved high accuracy in identifying buried objects from GPR images, and it was able to distinguish between objects with different permittivity values. The results suggest that deep learning can be a powerful tool for improving the accuracy and efficiency of buried object detection using GPR technology.

In recent years, wireless communication has revolutionized the way we communicate with one another and access the internet. With the advent of 5G mobile communication, we can expect even faster, more reliable connectivity. This has created new opportunities for the development of wireless sensor networks, which are instrumental in a range of applications from environmental monitoring to healthcare. A particularly interesting application of wireless sensor networks is in the field of diabetes management, where user-centric sensing can provide real-time monitoring of blood glucose levels, reducing the risk of complications. However, reliability is a major concern when it comes to wireless sensor networks, and research is ongoing to improve sensors and network accuracy. By leveraging the power of 5G-based wireless communication and developing more advanced sensors, we can expect to see significant improvements in the reliability of wireless sensor networks in the years to come.

The paper considers technologies of increasing energy efficiency of technological modes at robotized productions. The project of trajectories optimization module of industrial manipulator is put forward. The module is integrated into an informative space of robotized section and analyzes operating programs of CAM - system. It defines the volume of associated energy costs of technological process, puts forward corrective actions, which are aimed at increasing energy efficient of technological process while changing the program code without going beyond the limitations of the technology. The base of the computing part includes intellectual algorithms of identifying non-linear dependencies and output decisions. Results of the research are proved by experiment that was made at robotized machining section with industrial robot KUKA KR - 60.

Multi-label text classification is the machine learning task wherein each document is tagged with multiple labels, and this task is uniquely challenging due to high dimensional features and correlated labels. Such text classifiers need to be regularized to prevent severe over-fitting in the high dimensional space, and they also need to take into account label dependencies in order to make accurate predictions under uncertainty. Many classic multi-label learning algorithms focus on incorporating label dependencies in the model training phase and optimize for the strict set-accuracy measure. We propose a new pipeline which takes such algorithms and improves their F1-performance with careful training regularization and a new prediction strategy based on support inference, calibration and GFM, to the point that classic multi-label models are able to outperform recent sophisticated methods (PDsparse, SPEN) and models (LSF, CFT, CLEMS) designed specifically to be multi-label F-optimal. Beyond performance and practical contributions, we further demonstrate that support inference acts as a strong regularizer on the label prediction structure.

Complex networks have received significant attention due to their widespread applications in various fields. In particular, the complexity of equipment support networks has been a topic of study in recent years. This research focuses on developing indexes to measure the complexity of equipment support networks based on complex networks theory. The study also examines the correlation between complexity indexes and network topology. Furthermore, the complexity theory is applied to analyze the behavior of the network, and a manganese supply network is used as an example to illustrate the application of the method. The results show that the proposed indexes are effective in measuring the complexity of the equipment support network, and the study provides a new perspective for the analysis of complex systems.

The noise effect during training and inference for deep artificial neural network hardware acceleration is analyzed in this paper. The noise effect is extremely important when designing hardware for machine learning due to non-ideal devices and circuits. We found that both forward propagation noise and weight update noise can have detrimental effect on the inference, but may not necessarily harm the training result. Pipelining approach supporting redundant runs for each input image is proposed to address the forward propagation noise, and an additional approach of using parallel memory weight cells to represent one synaptic weight is proposed to address the weight update noise. By using these approaches, MNIST classification accuracy on a deep neural network can be improved close to the ideal accuracy when no noise is present.

Cloud computing has emerged as one of the most important technological revolutions globally. However, the rapid growth of cloud computing has imposed a massive financial burden and resulted in environmental side effects due to excessive energy consumption. The high power consumption is not only attributed to the size of data centers but also to the ineptitude of resource usage. Most of the extant research has focused on reducing power consumption by an aggressive VM consolidation, which leads to the violation of the service level agreement (SLA). Furthermore, the unbalanced resource consumption exacerbates the unavailable wasted resources that are referred to as unavailable resource fragmentation. In this paper, we propose the use of a balanced resources consumption algorithm called BRC-IBMMT in order to enhance the efficiency of resource consumption while achieving an acceptable balance between conflicting correlation objectives of power consumption as well as SLA violation. The extensive simulation results of different types of workload validate and lend credence to the significance of the proposed method in reducing power consumption and SLA violation of the cloud data center.

A secure data hiding scheme based on visual secret sharing and histogram shifting is proposed. Visual secret sharing is used to encrypt the secret image before hiding it into the host image. Encryption is performed by dividing secret image into n shares. Out of these shares, n-1 are embedded in the host image, and one is stored as a secret key share with Trusting Authority. At the receiver side, the k out of these n-1 shares are extracted from the image. The complete secret data can be revealed only when the key share would be superimposed with the k retrieved shares. Random grid technique along with XOR operation has been used to create shares, resulting in no pixel expansion and maximum contrast for the extracted image. The shares have been embedded in the cover image by using the concept of histogram shifting.

This article describes the design and application of a speech emotion recognition system. The system is trained in Czech emotionally coloured speech. The output of the system is the evaluation one of the four emotional states. Classification of emotion from extracted features is performed by a multi-classifier whose structure consists of three sub-classifiers fusion by Bayes Believe rule. The proposed system was deployed in the Secure Mobile Communication Infrastructure developed for the Czech Republic Security Components.

The current trends in industry require more interconnectivity, interoperability and flexibility to adapt to continuous optimization of the production processes. In this landscape, industrial evolution prompts the need for a management concept capable of dealing with the heterogeneity. In the future with the incoming Industrial Internet of Things and other disruptive approaches, this demand will grow dramatically. The comprehensive function models for the management of heterogeneous industrial networks represent a domain specific abstraction. This abstraction enables the development of holistic management approaches that can deal with the heterogeneity in the management plane. In this way, they offer a solution for the future problems of the management of industrial networks regarding of the enhancement needed to perform the new trends driven by the Factories of the Future and the “Industrie 4.0”.

To ensure that humans and robots can safely coexist, the ability to recognize human behavior is a prerequisite for robots and a fundamental technical challenge for researchers. Current research can only recognize relatively simple cases of human behavior due to the lack of enough data and archetypally designed experiments. Our study elucidates human behavior in a systematic manner by observing the behavior of human subjects under more complex situations where they are surrounded by other people or objects to address the challenge. We focus on the following common situation that people pass each other through a narrow passage. We constructed a motion capture room with a narrow passage environment and measured the motion of human subjects performing different tasks. In addition, during the narrow passage experiment, we made subjects hold different daily necessaries (such as a backpack) to observe influences on human behavior. Our study found that passing and avoidance behavior exhibited by each of our subjects were significantly influenced by what kind of daily necessaries subjects carry. This research provides novel findings on human behavior in complex environments: in the case where subjects holding a handbag (a type of daily necessaries that stays next to one's body), they showed the tendency to be affected by the other subject and move more dynamically compared to the subject without anything or with other daily necessaries; in the case where subjects carrying a backpack (a type of daily necessaries on one's back) and looking at a smartphone, they also showed the tendency of being affected by others, but their motion is restricted compared to the subject without anything.

This paper proposes a novel approach for skin lesion segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders with aggregated multi-resolution skip connections. The aim is to accurately identify and segment lesions in images to aid in the diagnosis and treatment of skin diseases, particularly melanoma. The method employs an encoding network to capture features of the image followed by a decoding network to generate a binary mask of the lesion. The aggregated multi-resolution skip connections facilitate the integration of contextual information from different levels of the network, improving the segmentation performance. The model is trained using a combination of data augmentation and weighted loss functions to achieve optimal accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in uncovering various types of skin lesions, suggesting its potential for use in clinical practice.

In this paper, we propose a Super-Resolution Integrated Building Semantic Segmentation approach for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Imagery. The proposed approach is focused on building segmentation and semantics in remote sensing images, which is a challenging task. The spatial resolution in remote sensing images is low and the training data can be limited. We propose to integrate super-resolution techniques with semantic segmentation to overcome these challenges. Our approach is able to enhance the spatial resolution of the images and improve the performance of building segmentation and semantic understanding. We also propose a training strategy to improve the accuracy and robustness of the deep learning model used for segmentation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves higher accuracy and outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. Our approach has the potential to be applied to various remote sensing applications such as land-use classification, urban planning and disaster management.

This paper proposes a novel approach for lossless data compression at the edge of cellular networks, which takes user preferences into account. The compression algorithm is based on Bayes methods and prediction algorithms, with an emphasis on estimation and probabilistic logic. The predictive models used are tailored to reflect user behavior and preferences, resulting in significant reduction in data size while maintaining data integrity. Cellular networks are becoming increasingly sophisticated and capable of handling massive amounts of data, but bandwidth constraints continue to pose a challenge. Computational modeling is used to simulate network conditions and evaluate the efficiency of the proposed compression method. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of compression ratio and preservation of data fidelity. This work has potential implications for the development of edge computing and the optimization of network resources.

This paper presents a heart rate monitoring system that utilizes electrocardiography to track a patient's heart beat. The system is designed to continuously monitor the patient in order to detect any abnormalities that may lead to cardiac arrest. The system is built using microcontrollers and utilizes cloud computing to analyze the data captured by the electrocardiography. By analyzing the data, the system is able to provide real-time alerts to medical practitioners enabling prompt action. The proposed system is low-cost and has the potential to revolutionize patient care by enabling early detection and timely intervention for cardiac events.

Daily rainfall data is a vital element for weather prediction and forecasting. In this study, we discuss the construction of daily rainfall data and its application in weather prediction. We focus on "Meteorology" as the key area of application, and explore various "Prediction algorithms" that can be used for improving prediction accuracy. Additionally, we discuss the importance of "Training data" for machine learning algorithms and examine the role of "Vegetation" in influencing rainfall patterns. We also explore the use of "Temperature measurement" for improving prediction accuracy and discuss the importance of continuous "Training" for developing accurate and reliable weather prediction models. The findings of this study can contribute to improved weather prediction models and better preparedness for extreme weather events.

The paper considers the new possibilities that Fourth industrial revolution brings to everyday life and inclusion in the world of work for people with disabilities and the elderly (persons with special needs). Technological responses to the challenges of this involvement have been in the market for some time now. However, they are currently very limited to mostly static functions, so their application, though useful and necessary, is relatively limited. Cloud, M2M, IoT and especially 5G networks bring a new dimension and open new perspectives for developing applications tailored to the needs of such people. The paper provides an analysis of linkages between applications for people with special needs with upcoming technological possibilities and the perspective of such applications in the new ICT environment.

The paper studies an important problem how to increase the efficiency of electric energy transportation in distribution networks with the voltage range of 6-20 kV by reducing losses while transmitting electricity and ensuring its quality at the consumer nodes in accordance with the deviation criterion from nominal in the network in modern Russian electric power industry. A description of the distribution network model is given. The results of distribution networks modeling with the voltage range of 6-20 kV and the use of intelligent control devices based on the thyristor regulator of booster voltage (TRBV) are presented. The high laboriousness of applying precise control algorithms for intelligent control devices for reducing transmission losses in networks with the voltage range of 6-20 kV is shown. The comparative characteristics of the operation of the distribution electric networks before and after the adjustment of intelligent control devices are given.

Star centroiding accuracy is a critical issue in the field of astronomical imaging. Stray light and other sources of interference can significantly impact star centroiding accuracy, leading to errors in the determination of celestial positions. In this study, we propose a novel method to improve star centroiding accuracy in the presence of stray light, based on background estimation and fitting. Our method utilizes optical filters and attitude control to minimize interference, while also addressing the computational complexity of the problem. By estimating and subtracting the background, we are able to more accurately determine the centroids of stars, improving overall imaging accuracy. Our results show significant improvements in star centroiding accuracy, even in scenarios with high levels of stray light and interference. This research has important implications for the field of astronomy, as it provides a more robust and accurate method for determining celestial positions in challenging imaging environments.

Water is a scarce resource, which needs to be managed optimally. A reservoir is a key water storage source in water management, where they are utilized by various sectors for different purposes. Therefore, there is an essential need in taking the best decision in releasing water from reservoirs not only to manage water as a resource, but also to mitigate floods, which has been one of the most expensive natural disasters causing an increased impact on human causalities and property damage. Research on predicting the future water height of reservoirs, when the reservoir receives a significant amount of rainfall and the water inflow is uncertain due to human intervention, are very limited. Hence, this research proposes a prediction model to forecast the future water height of a reservoir, when the reservoir receives a significant amount of rainfall and the water inflow is uncertain. It presents the effectiveness of applying K-Medoids clustering on top of regression model in predicting the future water height on next three days, while identifying the most effective set of features of the model.

This research investigates the impact of window conditioning parameters on the classification performance and stability of electromyography (EMG)-based feature extraction methods. The study employs both time-domain analysis and frequency-domain analysis to extract features from EMG signals obtained from amputee patients for prosthetics control. The experiment utilizes the Microsoft Windows platform to perform the feature extraction using different window sizes and delay factors. The results demonstrate that the window size and delay factor significantly influence the performance of EMG-based feature extraction methods. The study reveals the optimal window conditioning parameters for each method, which can improve the classification accuracy and stability of EMG-based feature extraction methods. The findings shed light on the crucial role of window conditioning parameters in the development of robust and reliable EMG-based prosthetics control systems.

The development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has brought about various challenges to enable the interoperability between different devices and services. In order to overcome such interoperability issues, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution due to its secure and decentralized nature. This paper proposes a new blockchain-based architecture for service interoperations in IoT. The proposed architecture utilizes smart contracts to enable automated and secure transactions between different IoT devices and services. Furthermore, it adopts a distributed database approach to ensure the availability and consistency of data among IoT devices. To achieve optimal performance, the proposed architecture is designed to take advantage of modern computer architectures that are capable of handling massive amounts of data. Overall, this new architecture provides a reliable and efficient solution for facilitating the interoperability of IoT devices and services.

Dynamic Service Reallocation (DSR) in Network Function Virtualization (NFV)-based Transport Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) Optical Networks is essential to optimize resource management and improve network performance. Optical fiber networks are widely implemented in communication systems, and with the advent of NFV and WDM technology, the service reconfiguration and routing has become possible. The computer architecture of such networks depends on the design of the optical cross-connects and switches that provide a flexible and transparent medium for data transmission. In this paper, we propose a dynamic service reallocation scheme that utilizes NFV to manage the allocation of resources and services. This enables the network operator to optimize resource utilization and increase service capacity by reallocating resources to high-priority services on demand. We measure the performance of our proposed scheme using different scenarios that demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. Finally, we discuss the suitability of copper cables for service reallocation in NFV-based transport WDM optical networks.

Making decisions during a disaster can be challenging when human lives and infrastructures are exposed. An important factor to consider when allocating resources, in these situations, is the critical infrastructures' interdependencies. i2Sim, the Infrastructures' Interdependencies Simulator, is a tool build for that purpose. As a layered architecture, i2Sim includes a dedicated decision-making layer. The use of Reinforcement Learning (RL), a machine learning approach based on an agent learning from experience, has been successfully tested with some dimensionality constraints. This paper introduces two improvements to our previous tests aiming at increasing speed and allowing larger dimensionality problems. The first addition is an improved reward scheme for speeding up convergence while guaranteeing it. The correct application of shaping rewards requires a deep understanding of the problem and extensive convergence tests. The second improvement added is the implementation of a scheduler programmed to trigger multiple instances of the same model using different parameters. This scheduler partitions the state space, enabling the agent's training to be done in parallel via a distributed RL algorithm. With this idea, the state/action matrix representing knowledge is partitioned for training, assigned to computing nodes, populated with knowledge (trained) and collected/reconstructed for use. This work has tested on an IBM cluster with 24 computing nodes. The test model is an aggregated model of the City of Vancouver configured for a disaster with numerous consequences over the different critical infrastructures. Based on the model's configuration, 24 scenarios were identified, created and solved simultaneously. The scheduler automates the training by setting up model and learning parameters, looping execution of instances and gathering results from all nodes. The results verify a proof of concept and enable applicability to new models with highly increased dimensionalities.

Transfer learning can train a neural network for a target task's small dataset using a source task's pre-trained network; however, catastrophic forgetting, where the knowledge of the pre-trained network disappears during transfer learning, is problematic in this setting. PathNet was proposed to address this problem. However, PathNet can only be applied to modular neural network cases:thus, a non-modular pre-trained neural network is unavailable. Consequently, PathNet cannot be used to improve network structure versatility. Therefore, we propose Stepwise PathNet to improve versatility by considering the layers of a non-modular pre-trained neural network as modules. The performances of the proposed Stepwise and original PathNet methods were compared using the CIFAR-10 dataset (10 classes, and 60,000 images), and the results confirm the proposed method's potential to stabilize learning curves and accelerate learning to 45%.

This paper proposes a rekeying-based moving target defence mechanism to enhance the security of encryption against side-channel attacks. The mechanism involves constantly changing the encryption key in order to make it difficult for attackers to extract critical information by monitoring the side-channels. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed mechanism, the authors conducted computational modeling experiments which demonstrated its potential in improving the security of encryption against side-channel attacks. Additionally, the paper discusses the scalability of the proposed mechanism, and highlights its potential to be integrated with machine learning techniques for even more improved security. Overall, the rekeying-based moving target defence mechanism represents a promising approach in defending against side-channel attacks in the context of cryptographic systems.

This paper focuses on the data analysis and modeling of users' behavior on the web, particularly in relation to web browsers and internet usage. The effective monitoring of user behavior is essential for developing accurate analytical models, particularly those that incorporate machine learning and decision trees. However, privacy concerns must be carefully considered when collecting and using user data. The use of analytical models and decision trees enables deeper insight into user behavior, allowing for the development of more effective strategies for improving user experiences and increasing engagement on the web. Overall, this paper highlights the importance of data analysis and modeling in understanding and enhancing user behavior on the web.

Network functions virtualization (NFV) architecture enables quick and cost-effective response of mobile network operators to various Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications, where the crux is to effectively and efficiently allocate resources to virtual network functions (VNFs). However, a systematical approach for resource allocation in virtualized mobile core network is still unavailable. In this paper, we propose a synthetic approach based on analysis of both network processing procedures and users' behaviors. Inspired by the static user behavior model adopted by equipment manufacturers' load test procedures, we construct a more practical user behavior model by analyzing over 20TB real data from an operator. With the model, we propose a matrix mapping-based dynamic resource allocation mechanism for the virtualized mobile core networks. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct experiments using application and signaling records of millions of real users. Results show that the new approach significantly increases the resource utilization and system capacity of the mobile core networks.

In recent years, sleep monitoring systems have gained popularity as a useful way to track sleep patterns and promote healthy sleep habits. This paper proposes a novel contactless and fine-grained sleep monitoring system that leverages WiFi channel response. The system utilizes wireless sensor networks to collect data on a user's sleep patterns based on delays, schedules, topology, and monitoring protocols. By analyzing the energy consumption of the WiFi channel response, this system can identify the user's sleep stages without the need for direct contact or invasive measures. With the ability to track sleep patterns on a fine-grained level, this system has the potential to promote healthier sleep habits and improve overall well-being. Additionally, this system may have applications in healthcare, allowing healthcare providers to monitor the sleep patterns of patients remotely. Overall, this system represents a promising approach to contactless sleep monitoring and may have significant implications for the field of sleep monitoring and management.

The Space-Ground Integrated Network (SGIN) plays an important role for the future development of the country. The cyber-attacks against it are the focus of the research. In this paper, an association analysis algorithm based on knowledge graph of cyber security attack events is proposed to present the attack scenario for the Space-Ground Integrated Network. The construction of knowledge graph and association analysis can show the scene of cyber-attacks in the form of graphs. During the build process, the construction of an event ontology is an important part of it. Event ontology is used to represent various relationships in the network attack procedure. At last, we present a space-ground integration network security analysis system based on the knowledge graph of cyber security attack events, and uses the association analysis algorithm to analyze the attack scenario.

Compositional models are meant for human pose estimation (HPE) due to their abilities to capture relationships among human body parts. Deeply learned compositional model (DLCM) utilizes deep neural networks to learn compositionality of human body parts and has achieved great improvements in human pose estimation. The DLCM has a hierarchical compositional architecture and bottom-up/top-down inference stages. The previous works have proven that multi-scale deep features are beneficial for computer vision tasks, such as classification and human body keypoints detection. However, learning multi-scale feature pyramids in DLCM has not been well explored. In this paper, we propose a new method to apply the multi-scale feature pyramid module to further improve the performance of the DLCM, which is named as deeply learned multi-scale compositional model (DLMSCM). We design multi-scale residual modules as the basic blocks to learn multi-scale deep features which can capture the scale variations of different body parts. With the multi-scale mechanism in the framework of the DLCM, the model can not only deal with scale variations of body parts but also find joints dependencies, therefore enforce the entire body joints structural constrains. As a result, more precise body keypoints detection can be acquired. Our approach outperforms the other state-of-the-art methods on two standard benchmarks datasets MPII and LSP for human pose estimation.

With the rise of the Internet of Things (IoT), the importance of processing data in near real-time has become increasingly crucial. This paper explores a new approach to this challenge by facilitating near real-time analytics on the edge. This approach provides several benefits, including improved performance, reduced network latency, and enhanced energy efficiency. The use of cloud computing and data centers has traditionally been the go-to solution for real-time systems, but this approach is not always feasible, especially in Europe where energy costs are high. By utilizing the edge, organizations can perform real-time data analysis without relying heavily on cloud resources, potentially lowering energy costs and improving efficiency. The paper discusses potential use cases and benefits of this approach and explores various technologies available to facilitate this model.

In recent years, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become increasingly popular due to their widespread applications in various fields. One of the major challenges in WSNs is the energy consumption of sensor nodes, which limits the network's lifetime. Data aggregation is a popular technique to reduce energy consumption in WSNs. In this paper, we propose an integrated divide and conquer with enhanced k-means technique for energy-saving data aggregation in WSNs. Our approach optimizes the battery charge measurement of sensor nodes by dividing the network into smaller clusters and utilizing enhanced k-means clustering algorithms. The proposed method not only reduces energy consumption but also improves the accuracy of data aggregation. The proposed technique is compared to conventional data aggregation methods, and the results show that our approach outperforms them in terms of energy measurement and correlation. Furthermore, our approach utilizes base stations to gather data, which further improves the accuracy of data aggregation. The proposed technique can be used in various WSN applications, including environmental monitoring, health monitoring, and industrial control systems, among others.

This paper explores the strategies and benefits of deploying ultralow-loss fiber links in an elastic optical network (EON). Optical fiber networks play a significant role in telecommunications, and their performance is dependent on various factors such as signal to noise ratio (SNR), optical noise, optical fiber cables, optical fiber amplifiers, and optical fiber dispersion. The deployment of ultralow-loss fiber links can significantly improve the performance of optical fiber networks as this technology can mitigate signal degradations caused by the aforementioned factors. Therefore, the benefits of deploying ultralow-loss fiber links are numerous, including increased throughput, extended transmission distances, and improved signal quality. Furthermore, ultralow-loss fiber links can also reduce the operational costs of optical fiber networks. Therefore, deployment of ultralow-loss fiber links is a promising method to improve the performance and cost-effectiveness of elastic optical networks.

This paper focuses on the long term forecasting of wind speed for wind energy application using time series analysis, forecasting, neural networks, and maximum likelihood estimation techniques. The study aims to predict the wind speed that is necessary for wind energy production using various data sources, including meteorological data and other environmental parameters. The proposed methodology involves training and validation of the neural network models based on the market research to obtain accurate forecasting outcomes. The findings of the study indicate that the neural network-based approach provides an efficient and effective solution for wind speed forecasting that can be utilized in wind energy production. The results of this study have critical implications for producers of renewable energy who rely heavily on the availability of wind energy to meet their production targets. Implementing long term wind speed forecasting will result in improved energy production forecasts, allowing producers to plan their production and pricing strategies more effectively.

Network traffic analytics has always been an important field for cybersecurity and network operations. The analysis could be done on the stream of data (network traffic) in an on-line mode for real-time network operations or on the captured traffic data in an off-line mode for forensic analysis. In this paper, we aim to shed light into using machine learning based network analytics on traffic flows both for network operations and forensic analysis purposes. In doing so, our goal is to design and develop systems that could assist the human expert in analyzing "unknown background" traffic.

Cloud Technology is a most challenging modern area in the field of modern technologies in which assets (e.g., CPU and capacity) can be rented and discharged by the clients through internet on-demand basis. The cloud computing has been giving virtual computing services to a little, medium and extensive industries, and services, for example, infrastructure as a service (IaaS), platform as a service (PaaS), and software as a service (SaaS). Cloud computing has a great combination with the agile software development as a research area. Many researchers worked in Agile Cloud field. The software industries are using the agile methodology for efficient software development need some platform to get quick feedback from the client. Therefore, the agile-cloud is a great combination for it but due to security reasons that directly influence the less adoption of cloud in software industries. This paper reports the survey results of software industries. The total of seven IT industries and many professionals was involved in this paper. However, this paper also contributes and reveals how existing issues can affect agile-cloud adoption for efficient software development. Furthermore, we do not find any type of survey conducted in Pakistan's software industries-related to cloud-agile adoption.

This paper presents a novel approach for handwritten Arabic word spotting using the Speeded Up Robust Features (SURF) algorithm. The proposed method includes various steps such as image segmentation, feature extraction and character recognition. The SURF algorithm is used to extract key points from the input image which are then processed by a set of detectors to identify regions of interest. A Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is implemented to recognize the characters in the identified regions. The proposed method has been evaluated on a dataset of handwritten Arabic words and compared to other Optical Character Recognition (OCR) software. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research contributes to the field of computer vision by providing an efficient and accurate algorithm for handwritten Arabic word spotting.

Ultrasound (US) beam can be focused at multiple locations to increase the lateral resolution of the resulting images. However, this improvement in resolution comes at the expense of a loss in frame rate, which is essential in many applications such as imaging moving anatomy. Herein, we propose a novel method based on Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) for achieving multi-focus line-per-line US image without a reduction in the frame rate. Results on simulated phantoms as well as real phantom experiments show that the proposed deep learning framework is able to substantially improve the resolution without sacrificing the frame rate.

In this paper, secure, remote estimation of a linear Gaussian process via observations at multiple sensors is considered. Such a framework is relevant to many cyber-physical systems and Internet-of-things applications. Sensors make sequential measurements that are shared with a fusion center; the fusion center applies a filtering algorithm to make its estimates. The challenge is the presence of a few unknown malicious sensors which can inject anomalous observations to skew the estimates at the fusion center. The set of malicious sensors may be time varying. The problems of malicious sensor detection and secure estimation are considered. First, an algorithm for secure estimation is proposed. The proposed estimation scheme uses a novel filtering and learning algorithm, where an optimal filter is learned over time by using the sensor observations in order to filter out malicious sensor observations while retaining other sensor measurements. Next, a novel detector to detect injection attacks on an unknown sensor subset is developed. Numerical results demonstrate up to 3-dB gain in the mean-squared error and up to 75% higher attack detection probability under a small false alarm rate constraint, against a competing algorithm that requires additional side information.

Recently, linear wireless sensor networks (LWSNs) have been eliciting increasing attention because of their suitability for applications such as the protection of critical infrastructures. Most of these applications require LWSN to remain operational for a longer period. However, the non-replenishable limited battery power of sensor nodes does not allow them to meet these expectations. Therefore, a shorter network lifetime is one of the most prominent barriers in large-scale deployment of LWSN. Unlike most existing studies, in this paper, we analyze the impact of node placement and clustering on LWSN network lifetime. First, we categorize and classify existing node placement and clustering schemes for LWSN and introduce various topologies for disparate applications. Then, we highlight the peculiarities of LWSN applications and discuss their unique characteristics. Several application domains of LWSN are described. We present three node placement strategies (i.e., linear sequential, linear parallel, and grid) and various deployment methods such as random, uniform, decreasing distance, and triangular. Extensive simulation experiments are conducted to analyze the performance of the three state-of-the-art routing protocols in the context of node deployment strategies and methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the node deployment strategies and methods significantly affect LWSN lifetime.

This paper proposes a method for controlling the two-phase Stefan problem through a single boundary heat input. The estimation of the temperature distribution between the liquid and solid phases is crucial in this problem. Temperature measurement plays a vital role in this estimation process. The proposed method employs heating systems to measure the temperature of two phases and control the heat input to achieve the desired temperature distribution. This method is particularly useful in sea ice research for better understanding its behavior and optimization of its utilization. The results of this study indicate that the proposed control method is effective in controlling the two-phase Stefan problem and can be optimized for different applications.

In the last few years, a new form of Internet-based services has started, which is called Online Social Networks (OSNs). The impact of OSNs on human lives is foreseen to be very large with unprecedented amount of data and users. OSN users share their ideas, photos, daily life events, feelings and news. Since OSNs' security and privacy challenges are more potential than ever before, it is necessary to enhance the protection and filtering approaches of OSNs contents. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of OSNs' threats and challenges, and categorize them into: account-based, URL-based and content-based threats. We analyze the existing protection methods and highlight their limitations and weaknesses. Finally, we provide a set of recommendations for a security system that fill the gaps of the currently applied methods.

Skin lesion classification is a vital but challenging task for dermatologists. In recent years, deep learning has shown remarkable performance in image classification tasks. Feature extraction from pre-trained deep network layers has been widely used to improve the classification accuracy. In this study, we propose a robust feature space extraction method for skin lesion classification. We use the pre-trained deep network layers to extract features from skin lesion images. The extracted features capture the important information in the images, such as image color, texture, and structure. We also employ image color analysis to further enhance the classification accuracy. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in classifying various skin lesions, including benign and malignant lesions. Our method has great potential in assisting the diagnosis of skin cancer and other skin diseases in clinical practice.

Vein recognition is an important task in image recognition and has many practical applications, such as access control and security verification. To achieve accurate and efficient recognition, feature extraction is a critical step. In this paper, we propose a novel method that combines multi-layer convolutional features concatenation with a semantic feature selector. This method integrates both low-level and high-level image features to capture the unique characteristics of veins, while the semantic feature selector selects the most informative features and reduces the effect of redundant information. We conduct extensive experiments on several databases and demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on both training and testing sets. Furthermore, we perform a task analysis to show the effectiveness of our method in different scenarios. In conclusion, our proposed method provides an effective solution for vein recognition and can be widely applied in real-world applications.

Sarcasm is a special category of figurative language, which is mainly used in online social media to convey messages with implicit semantics and criticism. Such messages are used for sarcastic remarks using contemptuous, ridicule, bitter, taunt, and mock related words or phrases. Though sarcasm detection is a well-considered problem by the researchers, to the best of our knowledge, none of them has considered the problem of self-deprecating sarcasm, which is a special category of sarcasm, mainly used by the users to deprecate or criticize themselves using sarcastic phrases. In this paper, we propose a novel self-deprecating sarcasm detection approach using an amalgamation of rule-based and machine learning techniques. The rule-based techniques aim to identify candidate self-around tweets, whereas machine learning techniques are used for feature extraction and classification. A total number of 11 features, including six self-deprecating features and five hyperbolic features are identified to train three different classifiers - decision tree, naïve Bayes, and bagging. The proposed approach is evaluated over a Twitter dataset containing 107536 tweets, and compared with some state-of-the-art methods for sarcasm detection.

With the advent of network densification and the development of other radio interface technologies, the major bottleneck of future cellular networks is shifting from the radio access network to the backhaul. The future networks are expected to handle a wide range of applications and users with different requirements. In order to tackle the problem of downlink user-cell association, and allocate users to the best cell, an intelligent solution based on reinforcement learning is proposed. A distributed solution based on Q-Learning is developed in order to determine the best cell range extension offsets (CREOs) for each small cell (SC) and the best weights of each user requirement to efficiently allocate users to the most appropriate SC, based on both backhaul constraints and user demands. By optimizing both CREOs and user weights, a user-specific allocation can be achieved, resulting in a better overall quality of service. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms current solutions by achieving better user satisfaction, mitigating the total number of users in outage, and minimizing user dissatisfaction when satisfaction is not possible.

Aircraft are becoming increasingly connected to other systems or networks, introducing attack vectors and posing a threat to their operational effectiveness. Many military aircraft function using the MIL-STD-1553 protocol in order to communicate information across its systems. Previous intrusion detection research on this type of data bus is unable to detect spoofing attacks where only data words are manipulated. This paper presents the design of a MIL-STD-1553 anomaly-based intrusion detection system able to identify those attacks through the use of a novel histogram comparison approach and time-based features. The approach includes optimizations for improved time resolution in threat identification. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in identifying threats quickly and accurately.

This paper presents a comparative analysis of two DC optimal power flow methods for analyzing power transmission networks. The first method, Load Flow, is a traditional technique used to analyze power flow in power transmission lines. The second method, Propagation Losses, is a computational modeling technique used for analyzing power generation and transmission. The mathematical model used in both methods is based on the physical laws of electricity and has been implemented in Matlab. The analysis aims to compare the accuracy and computational efficiency of both methods, considering their application to real-world power systems. The results suggest that while both methods are effective for analyzing power flow, the Propagation Losses method is more accurate and efficient for large-scale power systems. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the practical applications of DC optimal power flow techniques in power system analysis.

Moving object detection (foreground and background) is an important problem in computer vision. Most of the works in this problem are based on background subtraction. However, these approaches are not able to handle scenarios with infrequent motion of object, illumination changes, shadow, camouflage etc. To overcome these, here a two stage robust and compact method for moving object detection (MOD) is proposed. In first stage, to generate the saliency map, background image is estimated using a temporal histogram technique with the help of several input frames. In the second stage, multiscale encoder-decoder network is used to learn multiscale semantic feature of estimated saliency for foreground extraction. The encoder is used to extract multi-scale features from multi-scale saliency map. The decoder part is designed to learn the mapping of low resolution multi-scale features into high resolution output frame. To observe the efficacy of proposed MsEDNet, experiments are conducted on two benchmark datasets (change detection (CDnet-2014) [1] and Wallflower [2]) for MOD. The precision, recall and F-measure are used as performance parameter for comparison with the existing state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show a significant improvement in detection accuracy and decrement in execution time as compared to the state-of-the-art methods for MOD.

In the field of near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy, information extraction is an important task that is often carried out using various mathematical and computational techniques. In this paper, we propose a method for information extraction based on entropy theory and genetic algorithm in the frequency domain using wavelet packets. The proposed method involves first performing frequency-domain analysis and then calculating the entropy of the spectra. Subsequently, a genetic algorithm is used to optimize the calibration of the model. Our experimental results show that this method is effective in capturing important information from NIR spectra, including chemical compositions and other valuable features. This method has practical applications in a wide range of fields such as agriculture, food, and biochemistry. Overall, our proposed method provides a reliable and efficient way of extracting important information from NIR spectra, which can be used to improve the accuracy of various analyses and measurements.

This paper presents a fast and broadband surface method for skin effect modeling in multiscale lossy conductors. The mathematical model is based on integral equations, which accurately capture the skin effect phenomenon in conductors. The skin effect is a well-known phenomenon that occurs when high-frequency currents flow through conductors, resulting in reduced conductivity at the surface of the conductor. In order to accurately model the skin effect, it is necessary to take into account the conductivity of the conductor as well as the frequency of the current. This method is able to model the skin effect in conductors with a range of scales, from small inductors to large conductors. The approach uses admittance matrices to model the skin effect, allowing for efficient computation of the electrical characteristics of the conductor. Computational modeling is used to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method. Overall, this method provides a fast and accurate approach for modeling the skin effect in a range of conductors, which has important implications for the design and optimization of electrical devices and systems.

Accurate abstracted behavioral modeling of analog circuits is still an open problem, especially when the abstraction process is automated. In this paper we present an automated abstraction technique of transistor level circuits with full SPICE accuracy alongside a significant simulation speed-up. The methodology computes a hybrid automaton which is transformed into a behavioral model in Verilog-A. The resulting hybrid automaton exhibits linear behavior as well as the technology dependent nonlinear e.g. limiting behavior. The accuracy and speed-up of the methodology is evaluated on several transistor level circuits ranging from simple operational amplifiers up to a complex industrial OTA-based Gm/C filter. Finally, we formally verify the equivalence between the generated model and the original circuit.

This paper presents a deep learning model generation framework for virtualized multi-access edge cache management. The framework is designed to develop predictive models for cache storage to effectively handle the increasing demand for video caching in virtualized networks. The proposed model uses III-V semiconductor materials like Indium phosphide to create efficient and effective virtualization of the cache, which is then trained using deep learning techniques. The predictive models generated using this framework are capable of predicting the performance of the cache storage, enabling the efficient allocation of resources for video caching. This approach can significantly improve the performance of virtualized networks and reduce the bandwidth consumption. The paper outlines the proposed framework and evaluates its effectiveness through various experiments carried out on real-world datasets. The results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over existing solutions without the deep learning component. The presented framework offers an efficient, adaptable, and scalable solution for virtualized multi-access edge cache management using deep learning techniques.

The advent of 5G technology along with the high proliferation of mobile devices entail an explosion of mobile traffic. Due to their resource-limitation constraint, mobile devices resort to connect to Cloud servers so as to offload computational tasks and improve, hence, resource usage. Unfortunately, the conventional Mobile Cloud Computing (MCC) solution involves high transmission latency. Recently Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) is envisioned as a promising technique for enhancing the computation capacities of mobiles and reducing latency. The key insight of MEC is to push mobile computing and storage to the network edge (i.e., base stations and access points). The main challenge of MEC solution is to find an efficient assignment of tasks with local or edge devices, while minimizing energy consumption and latency. In this paper, we propose a new joint task assignment and resource allocation approach in a multi-user WiFi-based MEC architecture. The main novelty of our work is that optimal offloading decision is jointly performed with the radio resource allocation. The objective of our scheme is to minimize the energy consumption on the mobile terminal side under the application latency constraint. To do so, we first formulate the problem as a new online Reinforcement Learning problem while considering both delay and device computation constraints. Then, we propose a new strategy based on a Q-Learning algorithm, named QL-Joint Task Assignment and Resource Allocation (QL-JTAR) to solve it. Based on extensive simulations conducted in NS3 simulator and using real input traces, we show that our approach outperforms the related prominent strategies in terms of energy consumption and delay, while ensuring near-optimal solution.

The increasing prevalence of computer crimes has raised concerns over the security of Internet Protocol (IP) networks. In recent years, the use of WhatsApp has become a notorious platform for the planning and execution of cybercrime. This paper proposes a method for extracting suspicious IP addresses from WhatsApp network traffic to aid in cybercrime investigations. Leveraging ISO and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards for communication protocols, this approach can identify and classify telecommunication traffic that may be associated with illegal activities, such as hacking or data theft. The proposed method enables law enforcement agencies to effectively identify and track the movement of cybercriminals, ultimately increasing the accountability of those responsible for online crimes. As computer crimes continue to escalate in our digitized society, this paper highlights the importance of proactive measures to enhance internet security and prevent malicious activity on IP networks.

The detection algorithm of existing traffic signs was improved, and the implementation of traffic sign detection and recognition was described in detail. This article mainly contains the following: Through targeted feature extraction, a trained cascaded classifier is used to obtain the location of traffic signs. Combined with the previous detection results, feature extraction is performed on the specified part of the target. The results are analyzed according to the location of detection or the results of the trained support vector machine are used to classify, and the classification results are obtained to realize the recognition of traffic signs. The total number of samples used for goal training in this article has reached thousands. The test results show that the detection rate of the traffic sign under the trained scene has been more than 90%. The algorithm has been optimized by the multi-thread method and combined with augmented reality to achieve real-time feedback.

This paper proposes a planar multifunctional four-port antenna system that is suitable for sub-urban mobile tablet applications. The antenna system is designed with the aim of enhancing the performance of satellite antennas, mobile ad hoc networks, dipole antennas, satellites, antenna radiation patterns, and antenna feeds. The four-port antenna system is equipped with a compact size and is composed of four meandered-dipole antennas that are positioned on a rectangular ground plane. The proposed antenna system is capable of providing high gain, wide bandwidth, and low profile performance. The simulation results indicate that the proposed four-port antenna system is capable of achieving an impedance bandwidth of 37.8% at 1.75 GHz with a peak gain of 8.14 dBi. Overall, the proposed planar antenna system appears to be a promising solution for sub-urban mobile tablet communication applications.

This paper proposes a deep neural network based approach for disease discrimination learning using small medical image training sets and user feedback. The method utilizes deep learning and neural networks to transform the original medical diagnostic imaging data into a higher dimensional feature space, allowing for better separation of disease classes. The approach also incorporates user feedback to modify the network's training process and improve its discriminative ability. The results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in learning disease-specific features from small training sets and demonstrate its potential for improving medical diagnostic accuracy. Future work will focus on investigating the robustness and generalization of the proposed approach on larger and more diverse datasets.

Emotional arousal (EA) denotes a heightened state of activation that has both subjective and physiological aspects. The neurophysiology of subjective EA, among other mind-brain-body phenomena, can best be tested when subjects are stimulated in a natural fashion. Immersive virtual reality (VR) enables naturalistic experimental stimulation and thus promises to increase the ecological validity of research findings i.e., how well they generalize to real-life settings. In this study, 45 participants experienced virtual rollercoaster rides while their brain activity was recorded using electroencephalography (EEG). A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network (RNN) was then trained on the alpha-frequency (8-12 Hz) component of the EEG signal (input) and the retrospectively acquired continuous reports of subjective EA (target). With the LSTM-based model, subjective EA could be predicted significantly above chance level. This demonstrates a novel EEG-based decoding approach for subjective states of experience in naturalistic research designs using VR.

The author introduces the top picks selection of papers in computer architecture that were published in 2018. This is the 16th year of publication of what has now become a tradition in the computer architecture community. Each year, the MICRO Top Picks selection committee, which I chaired for this year, selects 12 papers for this special issue, to highlight for the IEEE Micro readership, a sample of the papers published in 2018 that have architectural contributions of potentially high impact and significance. After a short review of the selection process the papers are briefly summarized.

This paper investigates the optimal filter design for CCD readout, taking into consideration the charge transfer characteristics. Charge coupled devices (CCDs) are widely used in image sensors and spectroscopy applications, where the measurement of charges is crucial. The charge transfer process in CCDs is crucial for the accuracy and precision of measurements. Computational modeling and mathematical models are employed to study the charge transfer and design optimal filters. The logic gates in CCDs are also analyzed, which play a critical role in determining the performance of CCDs. The clocks used in CCDs are also studied in detail, which play a vital role in synchronizing and coordinating the charge transfer process and readout. The proposed filter design shows improved performance in terms of accuracy and precision compared to existing approaches. The study provides useful insights for the optimization of CCD readout systems, which have broad applications in imaging and sensing technologies.

The characterization of handwriting skills has become an important biomarker for detecting Parkinson's disease. Task analysis helps to identify different aspects of handwriting that can be impacted by the disease. Feature extraction techniques are used to extract useful features from the handwriting samples for further analysis. Kinematics analysis provides information about the movement patterns of the hand and can provide insights into the progression of the disease. The use of databases facilitates the organization and management of large amounts of handwriting data. Parkinson's disease is one of the many diseases that can be identified using handwriting as a biomarker. Support vector machines can be used as a classification technique to accurately classify and diagnose Parkinson's disease. Writing is an essential human communication skill and the assessment of handwriting skills can serve as a useful tool for the early detection and management of diseases such as Parkinson's.

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is an important disease leading to blindness in humans, attracting a lot of research interests. Previous breakthrough research findings rely on deep learning techniques to diagnose diabetic retinopathy in patients with medical imaging. Although the medical imaging achieves reasonable recognition accuracy, the application of mass, easy-to-obtain and free electronic health records (EHR) data in life can make an early diagnosis of the DR more convenient and quick. In this paper, we used a set of five machine learning models to diagnose the DR in patients with the EHR data and formed a set of treatment methods. Our experimental data set is formed by processing the data provided by 301 hospitals. The experimental results show that random forest (RF) in the machine learning model can get 92% accuracy with good performance. Subsequently, the input features were analyzed and their importance graded to find that the predisposing factors triggering the human DR disease were associated with renal and liver function. In addition, disease diagnosis methods based on readily available the EHR data will become an integral part of smart healthcare and mobile healthcare.

Kernel methods have become increasingly popular for solving classification problems in machine learning. Specifically, multiple kernel learning (MKL) has emerged as a promising approach for combining multiple features in multi-class classification problems. However, the scalability of MKL remains a major concern due to its high computational complexity. To address this issue, the concept of stochastic variance reducing gradient (SVRG) has been introduced to accelerate the optimization process in MKL. This paper proposes a new algorithm called SVRG-MKL that utilizes SVRG to efficiently learn the kernel weights for feature combination in multi-class classification problems, with the aim of achieving faster convergence and better scalability. The proposed approach achieves improved computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art MKL algorithms, while maintaining competitive performance in terms of classification accuracy. The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the proposed algorithm's complexity theory, memory management, and task analysis, demonstrating its practical relevance and effectiveness. This study contributes to the development of fast and scalable MKL solutions for real-world applications.

The use of handheld combat support tools equipped with Internet of Things technologies and data fusion algorithms has great potential for enhancing reconnaissance and surveillance capabilities on the battlefield. These tools offer new opportunities for gathering and analyzing critical intelligence data in real-time, providing valuable situational awareness to military personnel. In particular, temperature sensors utilizing IoT technologies are useful for detecting and alerting soldiers to the presence of potential threats, such as enemy troops or vehicles. By integrating these tools into military operations, commanders can make more informed decisions and respond to threats quickly and effectively. The development and implementation of such tools will require a concerted effort from government agencies, military organizations, and technology firms, but the benefits they offer in terms of increased safety and effectiveness on the battlefield are well worth the investment.

One of the significant problems in Social Net-works (SN) analysis is how to find the best influential members. This problem was proved to be non-deterministic polynomial (NP-hard). The influence maximization (IM) problem in SNs aims to maximize the spread of influence in the network. It represents an optimization problem. IM is a fundamental research problem in social networks. Influence maximization problem is the problem of assigning a subset of k users as (seed nodes) in a graph that could maximize the spread of influence by maximizing the expected number of influenced users. It represents a key algorithmic problem in social influence analysis. In this study, centrality-based methods are utilized to select top k nodes of high centrality values. The degree centrality is used to select the opinion leaders, while the between-ness and Eigenvector centrality is used to select the early adopters. The degree discount (as a heuristic approach) is proposed to replace the Greedy algorithms applied in other studies to avoid the time complexity. A mixed diffusion model (replacing the linear threshold and independent cascade) is utilized to be main diffusion model in this study.

Conventional fault models define their faulty behavior at the IO ports of standard cells with simple rules of fault activation and fault propagation. However, there still exist some defects inside a cell (intra-cell) or between two cells (dual-cell) that cannot be effectively detected by the test patterns of conventional fault models and hence become a source of DPPM. In order to further increase the defect coverage, many research works have been conducted to study the fault models resulting from different types of intra-cell and dual-cell defects, by SPICE-simulating each targeted defect with its equivalent circuit-level defect model. However, it was considered computationally infeasible to simulate every possible defective scenario for a cell library and obtain a complete set of cell-level fault models. In this paper, we present a new dual-cell-aware (DCA) framework based on examining the layout of two adjacent cells (i.e., a dual cell) to identify potential defects, where time-consuming RC extraction can be avoided and the runtime for SPICE simulation can be reduced. Experimental results and silicon data on a SoC product show that the proposed DCA framework can not only save runtime significantly but also maintain the promising efficacy of DCA tests for the objective of lowering DPPM.

This paper proposes a dynamic selection and estimation method for digital predistorter parameters to linearize power amplifiers. The method employs principal component analysis and correlation techniques for feature extraction and estimation.
