The research involves analyzing information systems and their related processes to better understand the interplay between tasks and control-flow constructs. The results show that the proposed method can effectively identify and classify complex control-flow constructs accurately, which can be used to optimize process performance, reduce error rates, and improve overall system efficiency. Overall, the study provides valuable insights into the application of data mining and classification algorithms to identify complex control-flow constructs and enhance the performance of information systems.

Radix Path is a reduced bucket size Oblivious RAM (ORAM) which provides secure cloud storage. The proposed scheme uses binary trees that are modified to create a non-repeating pattern of access to the buckets in the ORAM structure. This arrangement significantly reduces the number of items that can be accessed by an adversary trying to discover the position of an item in the ORAM structure. The reduction in the bucket size enhances the performance of the ORAM scheme. The proposed approach is secure against sophisticated adversaries with access to multiple servers. The cryptographic primitives employed in the scheme provide guaranteed confidentiality and integrity of the data. The approach is well-suited for cloud computing environments where security is a major concern. The proposed mechanism effectively reduces the time factor associated with the ORAM scheme due to the reduced size of the buckets. This paper recommends Radix Path as an effective ORAM scheme for secure storage in cloud computing.

This paper proposes a method for effective State of Charge (SOC) estimation of Lithium-Ion batteries by learning the battery model bias. Traditional SOC estimation methods have relied on predictive models and computational modeling, both of which are prone to uncertainty and errors. The proposed method integrates an integrated circuit model with a machine learning algorithm to learn the battery model bias and improve the accuracy of SOC estimation. The experiments conducted using real battery data demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness. This research has significant practical implications for the development of reliable battery management systems, which can play a key role in the sustainable use of energy in various applications.

Recently, visible light communication (VLC) networks have emerged as a promising alternative for indoor data access, due to high data rate, low implementation cost, and immunity to radio frequency (RF) interference. However, the co-existence of VLC with the RF access points as well as the dependence of VLC to room illumination compel both technologies to work in parallel and thus, to form a hybrid heterogeneous VLC/RF network. This network offers the advantages of both technologies, namely increased capacity and ubiquitous coverage. Furthermore, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a very promising candidate technique for the next generation of wireless networks, mainly due to its increased spectrum efficiency compared to orthogonal access schemes. However, the optimal user grouping in NOMA is a combinatorial NP-complete problem, which calls for low complexity techniques. To this end, in this paper, we propose the use of coalitional game theory, where the users served by the same access point (VLC or RF) form a single coalition, while the users can switch through coalitions based on their payoff. A novel utility function is proposed that takes into account the peculiarities of the NOMA hybrid VLC/RF network. Finally, a coalition formation algorithm is presented as well as an efficient power allocation policy. Computer simulations validate the presented analysis and reveal the effectiveness of the proposed user grouping scheme compared to an opportunistic approach.

Uncertainty quantification is a vital part of mathematical modeling that helps to better understand the behavior of computational models. In this paper, we present a study on uncertainty quantification of vector parabolic equation based wireless channel models using polynomial chaos expansion. The study focuses on the impact of uncertainties related to antennas, transmitters, and other environmental factors on wireless communication. The use of polynomial chaos expansion helps to efficiently capture the impact of uncertainties and allows for a more accurate prediction of system performance. Our results suggest that including uncertainty quantification in wireless channel models can greatly improve the reliability of wireless communication systems. This study highlights the importance of considering uncertainty in computational modeling and may lead to further advancements in the field of wireless communication.

Iterative learning control (ILC) has been extensively studied to improve the tracking performance of control systems. This paper proposes a learning-gain adaptive ILC method for linear discrete-time-invariant systems subject to unknown and time-varying uncertainties. The proposed method updates the learning gain in each iteration based on a performance index that measures the tracking error and the uncertainty level. The convergence of the proposed method is analyzed using the theory of Markov processes. It is shown that the tracking error converges exponentially to zero under mild assumptions on the system and the uncertainties. Moreover, a tuning algorithm is provided to choose the design parameters of the proposed method. Simulations on a trajectory tracking problem are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of tracking performance and robustness to uncertainties.

In this paper we report our study involving an early prototype of TAPESTRY, a service to support people and businesses to connect safely online through the use of a Machine Learning generated visualization. Establishing the veracity of the person or business behind a pseudonomized identity, online, is a challenge for many people. In the burgeoning digital economy, finding ways to support good decision-making in potentially risky online exchanges is of vital importance. In this paper, we propose a Machine Learning method to extract temporal patterns from data on individuals' behavioral norms in their online activity. This monitors and communicates the coherence of these activities to others, especially those who are about to disclose personal information to the individual, in a visualization. We report findings from a user trial that examined how people accessed and interpreted the TAPESTRY visualization to inform their decisions on who to back in a mock crowdfunding campaign to evaluate its efficacy. The study proved the protocol of the Machine Learning method and qualitative insights are informing iterations of the visualization design to enhance user experience and support understanding.

Shadow detection and shadow removal are fundamental and challenging tasks, requiring an understanding of the global image semantics. This paper presents a novel deep neural network design for shadow detection and removal by analyzing the spatial image context in a direction-aware manner. To achieve this, we first formulate the direction-aware attention mechanism in a spatial recurrent neural network (RNN) by introducing attention weights when aggregating spatial context features in the RNN. By learning these weights through training, we can recover direction-aware spatial context (DSC) for detecting and removing shadows. This design is developed into the DSC module and embedded in a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the DSC features at different levels. Moreover, we design a weighted cross entropy loss to make effective the training for shadow detection and further adopt the network for shadow removal by using a euclidean loss function and formulating a color transfer function to address the color and luminosity inconsistencies in the training pairs. We employed two shadow detection benchmark datasets and two shadow removal benchmark datasets, and performed various experiments to evaluate our method. Experimental results show that our method performs favorably against the state-of-the-art methods for both shadow detection and shadow removal.

Acquiring meaningful data to be employed in building training sets for classification models is a costly task, both in terms of difficult to find suitable samples as well as their quantity. In this sense, Active Learning (AL) improves the training set building by providing an efficient way to select only essential data to be attached to the training set, consequently reducing its size and even enhancing model's accuracy, when compared to random sample selection. In this paper, we proposed a framework for time series classification in order to monitor sugarcane area in São Paulo, Brazil. The AL approach consisted of selecting seasonal time series information from less than 1 percent of each class' pixels to build the training set and evaluate this selection by an expert user supported by distance measurements, repeating this process until both distance measurement thresholds were satisfied. In most years, the classification results presented about 90 percent of correlation with official estimates based on both traditional and satellite image analysis methods. This framework can then help Land Use Change (LUC) monitoring as it produced similar results compared to other methods that demands more human and financial resources to be adopted.

The recent surge of interest in Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) has led to increasingly complex networks that tax computational and memory resources. Many DNNs presently use 16-bit or 32-bit floating point operations. Significant performance and power gains can be obtained when DNN accelerators support low-precision numerical formats. Despite considerable research, there is still a knowledge gap on how low-precision operations can be realized for both DNN training and inference. In this work, we propose a DNN architecture, Deep Positron, with posit numerical format operating successfully at ≤8 bits for inference. We propose a precision-adaptable FPGA soft core for exact multiply-and-accumulate for uniform comparison across three numerical formats, fixed, floating-point and posit. Preliminary results demonstrate that 8-bit posit has better accuracy than 8-bit fixed or floating-point for three different low-dimensional datasets. Moreover, the accuracy is comparable to 32-bit floating-point on a Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA device. The trade-offs between DNN performance and hardware resources, i.e. latency, power, and resource utilization, show that posit outperforms in accuracy and latency at 8-bit and below.

Traffic classification has been widely used in network management, service measurements, network design, security monitoring and advertising. Software defined networks (SDN) is an newly-developing technology, which is capable of address problems in the traditional network by simplifying network management, introducing network programmability, and providing a global view of a network. Recent years, SDN has brought new opportunity to classify traffic. Traffic classification techniques in SDN have been investigated, proposed and developed. This paper looks at emerging research into the traffic classification techniques in SDN. We first introduce SDN and related work of traffic classification, and then review several representative works of traffic classification in SDN. These works are reviewed in line with the choice of classification strategies and contribution to the literature. Research challenges and future directions for SDN traffic classification are also discussed.

In Lebanon, traffic problems are a major concern for the population. The rising number of cars that exceeds the capacity of the roads, the inefficiency of public transportation infrastructures and the non-adaptive traffic light systems are contributors to the traffic crisis. Most roads in Lebanon suffer from traffic jams due to the traditional static green and red times allocations that are inconsiderate to the current state of the traffic. A solution to this problem is a system that adapts to the variations of the traffic dynamically and updates the traffic signal phases accordingly. In this paper, an adaptive traffic light system is implemented using reinforcement learning and tested using real data from Lebanese traffic. For training and testing the system, a software simulation tool is used. This tool can simulate the traffic intersection and allows the neural network to interact with it. Compared with the actual traffic light system, the proposed model displayed a reduction in average queue lengths by 62.82% and in average queuing time by 56.37%.

Cardiac sound classification is an important diagnostic tool in detecting heart diseases. In this study, we propose a method of using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for classification of cardiac sounds. MFCC was used to extract relevant features from cardiac sounds, and the ANN was trained to classify the sounds based on these features. The proposed method was tested on a dataset of heart sounds containing sounds from healthy valves, aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation, and combined lesions. The results showed that the proposed method achieved high classification accuracy, with an overall accuracy of 98.5%. The study demonstrates that the combination of MFCC and ANN is effective in the classification of cardiac sounds, and has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment of heart diseases.

In the future Fifth-Generation networks, the eavesdropping is a critical threat due to their broadcast-based transmission. This problem can be addressed with the cryptographic protocols. However, this method is complex and difficult because of the dynamic topology of wireless networks, which does not allow an efficient management of security keys. As a complement solution, Physical-layer security (PLS) is integrated to enhance secrecy in wireless networks. The PLS exploits the schemes features of this layer, namely the modulation, Massive Multi-Input Multi-Output(m-MiMo) and channel coding. The fountain code is one of those systems where the secrecy is provided when the destination retrieves packets encoded before the intruder. Nevertheless, the secrecy can not be guaranteed when eavesdropper uses large number of the antennas as in the m-MiMo. The feature of m-MiMo should be considered to secure main channel with fountain codes. Therefore, we propose to use Raptor code which is a class of fountain code, aided by an Artificial noise (AN) and the punctuated data to reduce the efficient of intruder channel. This allows the main channel to retrieve the signal before eavesdropper. The numerical results show that using Raptor code in massive MiMo enhances the reliability and the security on the channel of legitimate user, while minimizes the abilities of intruders to spy on data.

In this paper we show how Supervised Binary Classification techniques can be used to tackle the problem of eNodeB failure detection in an LTE network carrying Machine-to-Machine (M2M) smart-city traffic. 22 different classifiers are trained with data from two 24 hrs simulations with different levels of traffic volume. Input features for the classification models are built aggregating packet generation and access collisions from the eNodeB on which failures are being detected, as well as from its closest neighbors, by computing statistics for each time-bin. Given that network service providers generally process real-time data to produce periodic aggregated summaries, we explore the effect of different levels of granularity in data aggregation and their effect on our ability to detect failures. The M2M traffic data was gathered from a simulated LTE network that uses publicly available geographic databases from the city of Montreal. With Linear Support Vector Machines (L-SVMs) and Bagged Decision Trees (BDT), failure detection rates above 97.5 % were achieved, with false positive rates under 2.8 %, showing that, even with 30 minutes aggregations, it is feasible to extract meaningful failure information.

This paper presents a method for submerged body classification using underwater imaging sonar and deep learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes convolution-based neural networks for image recognition and feature extraction, allowing for accurate classification of different types of submerged bodies. To achieve optimal performance, the networks are trained using a large dataset of labeled sonar images. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a series of experiments, showing high accuracy and robustness even under challenging conditions. This approach has significant potential for applications such as underwater surveillance, marine biology research, and underwater exploration. Overall, this study highlights the importance of deep learning-based approaches for underwater imaging and their potential impact on the field.

This paper presents the development of a real-time two-wheeled inverted pendulum robot using fuzzy logic-based intelligent control. The robot is designed with two wheels, DC motors, and sensor fusion to enable smooth and stable motion. The fuzzy logic-based controller is used to generate appropriate commands to control the movement of the robot. The proposed system was tested and evaluated under various scenarios, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the fuzzy logic-based controller for real-time systems. The use of fuzzy logic enables the controller to handle uncertainties and non-linearities in the system, resulting in accurate and efficient control performance. Overall, the presented system can be used in various applications that require robust and accurate control of two-wheeled inverted pendulum robots.

This paper presents a study on coded caching under heterogeneous user preferences, which aims to improve the throughput by considering user preferences in the caching process. The proposed approach utilizes a kernel method to learn the similarity between users, matrix decomposition to extract useful features in the user preference matrix, and deep learning to model the non-linear relationship between user preferences and content demands. The task analysis is conducted to optimize the caching strategy, and a linear programming formulation is proposed to solve the problem. Moreover, the proposed method is shown to achieve convergence through the use of artificial neural networks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving throughput and accommodating the heterogeneous user preferences.

The convergence of search problems in many-objective optimization is a major challenge in the field of evolutionary computation. In this paper, we propose a two-archive evolutionary algorithm based on a multi-search strategy to overcome this issue. Our approach utilizes both an external and an internal archive to maintain a diverse set of Pareto optimal solutions. The algorithm also incorporates a sociological knowledge-sharing mechanism to enhance the diversity of the population. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms other state-of-the-art algorithms on a range of benchmark problems. The multi-search strategy allows for a better exploration of the search space, and the two-archive approach improves the convergence of the algorithm. The sociological knowledge-sharing mechanism additionally promotes diversity by encouraging knowledge exchange between individuals. In conclusion, our proposed algorithm offers a promising solution to the challenge of many-objective optimization through its use of a multi-archive strategy and sociological knowledge-sharing mechanism.

Facial expression is an important part of non-verbal communication and one common means of human communication. Expression recognition, as one of the important development directions of human-computer interaction, can improve the fluency, accuracy and naturalness of interaction. In recent years, deep learning using feature extraction of image data based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) has become more and more popular. Their popularity stems from their ability to extract good features from image data, for DCNN's computationally intensive tasks can be run on the GPU to achieve high performance at very low consumption. This algorithm can achieve much higher accuracy than traditional ones, making it possible to commercialize and utilize. This paper introduces the basic principles and methods of expression recognition, and classifies the common recognition methods. The cases of improving recognition rate and robustness after applying multiple algorithms are reviewed in detail. And the matters to be solved for further application of this method are also discussed. Additionally, the technical methods and approaches of expression recognition in industrial design, particularly in emotional interaction design of industrial products, are elucidated.

This paper proposes a novel Krylov method for model order reduction of quadratic bilinear systems. The method is based on the use of transfer functions to represent the system, and employs interpolation techniques to obtain an approximate model with reduced order. The proposed technique is applicable for MIMO communication systems as well as linear systems. The method is evaluated with several computational modeling examples, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving high levels of accuracy while reducing computational complexity. This research opens up a new avenue for developing efficient algorithms for model order reduction of quadratic bilinear systems.

This article introduces a model that automatically detects suspicious basal cell carcinoma regions in whole slide images (WSI) by integrating nuclear architectural features and information captured from WSI pathologists' navigations during diagnostic tasks. In such an approach, manual annotations are not needed since high-level expert knowledge is implicitly captured when the pathologist is exploring the WSI. The method was tested on a set of 10 cases of patients diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma using a leave-one-out cross-validation technique. At each iteration, a quadratic discriminant analysis classifier was trained to identify cancerous nuclei using architectural features of nuclei belonging to the regions that were highly or little visited by pathologists when rendering a diagnosis. Experimental results showed an average accuracy of 86% and an F-score of 76%, thereby demonstrating the potential of this approach to be included in actual clinical scenarios.

The purpose of this study is to propose a new benefit segmentation method based on customer reviews existing on the web. With the diversification in customer needs, it is difficult to accurately identify the needs of customers with market segmentation using demographic information. Therefore, it is important in marketing to segment the customer market based on the benefits that customers receive for products or services. In this research, we use the random forest algorithm for benefit segmentation, as this algorithm identifies training data with high accuracy even if noise and outliers exist, and it is widely used for analysis of text data. In our experiment, we analyzed customer reviews for hotels. We treated the reason for using hotels as the benefit, and analyzed topics based on word frequency in the text data as explanatory variables. We extracted factors that influenced each benefit to determine customer needs.

A cloud-based big data sharing system utilizes a storage facility from a cloud service provider to share data with legitimate users. In contrast to traditional solutions, cloud provider stores the shared data in the large data centers outside the trust domain of the data owner, which may trigger the problem of data confidentiality. This paper proposes a secret sharing group key management protocol (SSGK) to protect the communication process and shared data from unauthorized access. Different from the prior works, a group key is used to encrypt the shared data and a secret sharing scheme is used to distribute the group key in SSGK. The extensive security and performance analyses indicate that our protocol highly minimizes the security and privacy risks of sharing data in cloud storage and saves about 12% of storage space.

The forecasting of electricity load is considered as an essential instrument, especially in countries with a restructured electricity market. The mid-term prediction is performed for the period within 1 month to 1 or 2 years and it is important for mid-term planning, including planning of repairs and economic exploitation of power systems, which are related to the reliability of the system directly. The forecast horizon in this paper is monthly and on a daily basis (peak load). The combined method of the neural network and the particle optimization algorithm were used to predict the load, and then the maximum amount of environmental pollution caused by the production of electricity required to supply the predicted load was calculated. The applied method was tested on the data of a North American electric company for four months (four seasons) and in comparison to the other methods presented in previous studies, it had an acceptable accuracy.

We address the sparse signal reconstruction in a wireless sensor network (WSN) via distributed compressed sensing (DCS). The multiple sparse signals from WSN are modeled by the mixed-support set (MSM) model, which describes the inter-correlation of the signals by the common support set and represents the individual features by the innovation support sets. We propose a novel common subspace pursuit (CSP) algorithm to estimate the common support set, in order to reduce the reconstruction error and computing time. The results of simulations on a hierarchical clustering based WSN show that the proposed CSP algorithm is superior over the conventional algorithms in terms of both reconstruction error and runtime.

The MERAKIS project represents a modern approach to improving access to knowledge in service. This initiative focuses on the integration of modern electronics in various fields, such as medical diagnostic imaging, medical services, artificial neural networks, and expert systems. The project also emphasizes the importance of utilizing these technologies to benefit urban areas, where the need for accessible and efficient medical services is critical. In this regard, conferences are organized to share and exchange ideas among experts in the field for further development, implementation, and utilization of these technologies. Overall, the MERAKIS project is a highly promising initiative that is expected to revolutionize the delivery of medical services in urban areas by leveraging the latest advances in modern electronics.

This paper proposes a new multi-objective technique to solve the problem of optimal location and sizing of Distributed Generation Photovoltaic (DGPV) in the power system transmission network. The technique: Multi-objective Chaotic Mutation Immune Evolutionary Programming (MOCMIEP) was developed based on Pareto optimality to solve the DGPV location and sizing problem. The proposed technique determines the optimal location and sizing of DGPV, therefore will minimize the multiple objective functions, namely the active power losses and Fast Voltage Stability Index (FVSI) simultaneously. The method was tested on IEEE 118-Bus Reliability Test System (RTS). The results revealed that the proposed technique had the ability to acquire a set of Pareto solutions for the decision maker to choose depending on the system priorities.

In this paper, a 28-nm FD-SOI Dual-Port SRAM with MSB-Based Inversion Logic for Low-Power Deep Learning is presented. This design is aimed at meeting the memory requirements of deep learning applications for real-time systems while reducing power consumption. The proposed approach leverages MSB-based inversion logic to enable high speed, low-power operation of the SRAM. In addition, the design takes into account memory management and correlation issues to provide an efficient system for image processing. The result is a high-performance dual-port SRAM that can effectively support deep learning applications, while consuming low power and providing real-time memory management capabilities. The proposed design also demonstrates the potential for using low-power logic circuits to enable advanced processing for data-intensive computing applications.

The genetic algorithm is used in many applications and one of these applications is the traffic signal system. The traditional traffic light suffers from several problems such as long waiting period and thus increasing the number of vehicles. Genetic algorithms a type of optimization algorithm, meaning they are used to find the optimal solution based on the theory of natural selection and evolutionary biology so they have several steps starts from the initial population, calculate the fitness function for each solution (Chromosome) and ends with selections, crossover, and mutation. The result of the genetic algorithm is increasing the total number of vehicles passing through the traffic signal system.

Network virtualization is an extensively used approach to allow multiple tenants with different network architectures and services to coexist on a shared data center infrastructure. Core to its realization is the mapping (or embedding) of virtual networks onto the underlying substrate infrastructure. Existing approaches are not suitable for cloud environments as they lack its most fundamental requirement: elasticity. To address this issue, we introduce two new network primitives -expand and contract- which allow virtual networks to scale up and down. Mapping and scaling virtual networks over time, however, introduces fragmentation in the substrate network. This is akin to fragmentation in a file system where files are not laid out in contiguous physical blocks of the storage device. This problem impacts network performance and reliability for tenants and their applications. Instead of further improving embedding algorithms to tackle this problem, in this work, we present a yet unexplored approach: leveraging network migration techniques to defragment the network. We introduce network defragmentation as a new management primitive and propose algorithms to materialize it. We show through extensive simulations that our techniques significantly improve network performance while maintaining high utilization of the infrastructure, thus increasing provider revenue. On average, using defragmentation leads to 20% reduction in path length and utilization and cuts the number of very long paths (longer than half of the network diameter) between 52% and 62%. Moreover, it doubles the number of servers utilized by 50% or less as a result of consolidation.

This paper discusses the reliability challenges associated with materials used in analog computing, specifically focusing on training, switches, deep learning, nonvolatile memory, conductivity, reliability, and phase change materials. Analog computing is a promising approach to improving the energy efficiency of computing, but it presents unique challenges in terms of the materials used. The reliability of these materials is a significant concern, as the accuracy and consistency of the computations depend on the performance of the materials. The paper outlines the challenges associated with each material, including issues such as wear and tear, aging, and degradation. It also proposes possible solutions to these challenges, such as using new materials, improving fabrication processes, and developing better testing methods. The paper concludes that while there are significant challenges associated with the materials used in analog computing, there is also significant potential for these materials to improve the efficiency and accuracy of computing. Further research is needed to determine the best approaches for addressing the reliability challenges associated with these materials.

The aim of this paper is to provide a standardization guide for the development of collaborative Massive Open Courses (MOOCs) in engineering teaching. The guide is based on the results of the DIEGO project which aims to promote the use of MOOCs as a tool for engineering education. The guidelines cover various aspects of MOOC development including task analysis, training, and collaboration. The guide highlights the importance of task analysis in the development of MOOCs and provides a step-by-step process for conducting task analysis. It also emphasizes the need for training to ensure effective use of MOOCs for engineering teaching. In addition, the guide discusses the use of renewable energy sources in engineering education and highlights the role of MOOCs in promoting sustainability. Finally, the guide emphasizes the importance of collaboration in MOOC development and suggests ways to facilitate collaboration among different stakeholders. The standardization guide provided in this paper can be used as a reference for developing collaborative MOOCs for engineering teaching.

Face recognition has become a fascinating field for researchers. The motivation behind the enormous interest in the topic is the need to improve the accuracy of many real-time applications. The complexity of the human face and the changes due to different effects make it more challenging to design as well as implement a powerful computational system for human face recognition. In this work, we presented an enhanced approach to improve human face recognition using a Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) and features extraction based on the correlation between the training images. A key contribution of this work is the generation of a new set called the T-Dataset from the original training dataset, which is used to train the BPNN. We generated the T-Dataset utilizing the correlation between the training images without using a conventional technique of image density. The correlated T-Dataset provides a high distinction layer between the training images, which helps the BPNN to converge faster and achieve better accuracy. Data and features reduction is essential in the face recognition process, and researchers have recently focused on the modern Neural Network (NN). Therefore, we used a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) descriptor to prove that there is a potential improvement even using traditional methods. We applied five distance measurement algorithms and then combined them to obtain the T-Dataset, which we fed into the BPNN. We achieved higher face recognition accuracy with less computational cost compared to the current approach by using reduced image features. We test the proposed framework on two small datasets, the YALE and AT&T datasets, as the ground truth. We achieved tremendous accuracy. Furthermore, we evaluate our method on one of the state-of-the-art benchmark datasets, Labeled Faces in the Wild (LFW), where we produce a competitive face recognition performance. Also, we proposed an enhanced framework to improve the face registration using deep transfer learning. We used pre-trained models such as ResNet50 and SeNet50 which trained on the VGGFace2 dataset. We used the LFW dataset to evaluate our method, and we achieve high accuracy.

Image registration is a crucial task in computer science, especially in image processing. In this paper, we propose a new method for feature-based image registration using heuristic nearest neighbor search. The proposed method involves feature extraction and simulated annealing to achieve accurate and efficient image registration. The task analysis is performed to identify the core requirements and challenges of the image registration process. The detectors, which play a crucial role in feature extraction, are chosen based on their ability to detect robust and discriminative features. The performance of the proposed method is compared with other state-of-the-art methods showing better results in terms of efficiency and accuracy. In conclusion, the proposed method can be considered as a valuable addition to the existing image registration techniques, especially for the medical imaging domain.

Extreme learning machine (ELM) is an extremely fast learning algorithm proposed for a single-hidden-layer feed-forward neural network (SLFN). ELM projects a set of training instances into a random feature space, and then analytically calculates the weight matrix connecting between the hidden layer and the output layer, leading to a very fast learning speed. This paper proposes an improved version of ELM, named clustering-ELM, that assigns a subclass to each training instances and learns for a weight matrix that projects random features into subclass. In the prediction step, the responses from output nodes of the same class are integrated into one using maximum function. Experimental results conducted on various benchmark datasets reveal a promising performance of the proposed clustering-ELM, compared to the standard ELM.

This paper describes designing, 3-D printing, building and testing of a prototype smart wheelchair using Emotive EPOC headset that will help the blind and paralyzed people who are unable to control parts of their body. It uses deep learning in order to recognize four different movements from the recorded EEG signal, to move left, right, forward, and stop. Data from 10 volunteers shows a success rate of 70% from the row EEG and 96% from the spectrum (Fourier Transform) of the data from the frequency bins corresponding to the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma waves.

This paper presents the design and optimization of a movable cable-driven lower-limb rehabilitation robot for enhanced training and rehabilitation. Rehabilitation robotics is an important area of research that has shown great promise in recent years. With the development of advanced force and motion control techniques, exoskeletons have become an essential tool for rehabilitation training. The proposed system utilizes cable-driven mechanisms, which offer several advantages over traditional actuation methods, including greater flexibility, light weight, and lower cost. The robot kinematics were optimized using a genetic algorithm to achieve smoother and more natural movements. The results of this study demonstrate the potential of cable-driven robots in the field of rehabilitation, and suggest that they could be a viable alternative to more traditional systems, especially in industries such as petroleum where cost-effectiveness is a major concern.

In this paper, we introduce a method to obtain necessary and sufficient stability conditions for systems governed by one-dimensional nonlinear hyperbolic partial-differential equations with closed-loop integral controllers, when the linear frequency analysis cannot be used anymore. We study the stability of a general nonlinear transport equation where the control input and the measured output are both located on the boundaries. The principle of the method is to extract the limiting part of the stability from the solution using a projector on a finite-dimensional space and then use a Lyapunov approach. This paper improves a result of Trinh, Andrieu, and Xu, and gives an optimal condition for the design of the controller. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations where the predicted stable and unstable regions can be clearly identified.

In the context of industrial wireless sensor networks (IWSNs), delay and reliability are critical issues that need to be addressed to minimize data loss and ensure timely response to system events. To optimize the performance of IWSNs, a decentralized primal-dual optimization algorithm called DeP-D is proposed in this paper. The algorithm is based on linear programming techniques and is designed to improve routing efficiency, reduce delays, and enhance system reliability. The approach of DeP-D is based on a parallel iterative scheme that implements primal-dual optimization on the nodes of IWSNs. With this approach, the convergence of the algorithm is shown to be faster than traditional centralized approaches. The proposed algorithm is tested on benchmark instances and its performance is compared with several state-of-the-art routing algorithms. The results demonstrate that DeP-D achieves better performance in terms of delay, reliability, and convergence. In summary, the proposed DeP-D algorithm provides a reliable and efficient solution for IWSNs optimization, which is highly suitable for modern industrial applications.

In this paper, we propose a mean-field-type game approach for the deployment of inhomogeneous multi-UAV aerial base stations. The cost function is considered in the mathematical model to determine the optimal deployment of unmanned aerial vehicles. The game theory is used to analyze and model the decision-making behavior of the UAVs in the deployment process. The concept of Nash equilibrium is used to find the optimal deployment of the base stations. The proposed approach takes into account the communication network requirements and provides an efficient and effective solution for the deployment of aerial base stations. The use of multiple UAVs allows for a more comprehensive and flexible coverage of the communication network. This approach provides a novel solution for the deployment of inhomogeneous multi-UAV aerial base stations, and has potential applications in various fields such as disaster response, search and rescue, and military operations.

In this paper, we explore the concept of supervised sparse coding with decision forests. The aim of the technique is to extract meaningful features from high-dimensional datasets. Encoding is employed to learn the sparse representation of the data, with decision trees used to guide the selection of the most informative features. The dictionaries, generated through the process of training, capture the essence of the data, while the decision forest ensures that only the most relevant features are used for further analysis. The application of the technique to forestry datasets showed that the sparse matrices of the data could be effectively learned and used to classify different types of vegetation. The results suggest that supervised sparse coding with decision forests can be a valuable tool for feature extraction and classification in a wide range of fields.

In this paper, we propose a method for estimating fluid surface velocity using a 77 GHz radar module. The method utilizes radar antennas and wireless sensor networks to obtain accurate radar measurements of the fluid surface. Our approach involves the use of sensors for velocity measurement and frequency-domain analysis to process the data obtained from the radar module. We present experimental results that demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in estimating fluid surface velocity. Our proposed approach provides a promising solution for real-time monitoring of fluid surface velocity in a wide range of applications. The results of this study can help to improve the accuracy and reliability of fluid flow measurements in various industries.

This paper presents a novel approach for imputing missing diagnoses of diabetes in an administrative electronic medical record (EMR) system. The proposed method involves feature extraction from patient records, encoding of relevant clinical information related to diseases and drugs, and the utilization of machine learning techniques for generating imputation values. The study emphasizes the importance of accurately capturing and managing diabetes diagnoses in public healthcare systems, and highlights the potential benefits of using EMRs for predictive modeling and clinical decision-making. The results of the experimental evaluation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, revealing significant improvements in imputation accuracy compared to traditional imputation methods. Overall, this work contributes to the growing body of research on utilizing advanced analytics to improve healthcare outcomes, and serves as a valuable resource for healthcare professionals and researchers in the field of diabetes care.

This paper presents a comparison of simulation and experimental results for a pulsed laser system designed for undersea target localization. The focus of the study is on the receivers and transmitters used in the laser radar system. A mathematical model is proposed for the laser scattering process in water, which takes into account the effects of absorption and dispersion. In addition, photonics technology is utilized to enhance the performance of the system. Computational modeling is employed to optimize the design of the system and to generate waveforms for laser pulses. The generated waveforms are compared with experimental results to verify the accuracy of the mathematical model and the computational simulations. The results indicate that the proposed system is effective in undersea target localization and the comparison between the simulation and experimental data is satisfactory. This study provides valuable insights and a guideline for the design of undersea laser radar systems.

This paper discusses the possibility of using quantum simulation for electromagnetic structures. Specifically, the use of qubits and computational modeling for the analysis of time-varying systems using time-domain analysis is explored. The principles of quantum mechanics are used to create solid models for describing electromagnetic structures. The advantages and limitations of using quantum simulation compared to classical methods are also examined. The potential benefits of quantum simulation, such as increased accuracy and efficiency, are discussed. Overall, this paper provides insights into the potential future of using quantum simulation for electromagnetic structures.

Registration is an important task in automated medical image analysis. Although deep learning (DL) based image registration methods out perform time consuming conventional approaches, they are heavily dependent on training data and do not generalize well for new images types. We present a DL based approach that can register an image pair which is different from the training images. This is achieved by training generative adversarial networks (GANs) in combination with segmentation information and transfer learning. Experiments on chest Xray and brain MR images show that our method gives better registration performance over conventional methods.

Social online marketing is expanding fast with the evolution and recent development in the information and communication technology. Investigating how companies are exploiting social media for marketing, advertisement, and consumer's engagement is gaining more and more interest. In this paper, brands/companies data on Twitter is collected and analyzed to compute the overall company response on Twitter. Responsiveness of a company is inferred from three features: company popularity, average company replies, and average followers' replies. Twitter network features are used in calculating the posting frequency for companies and their followers. It is shown that the proposed approach can be used in finding the responsiveness of companies and their followers. Furthermore, useful links for a brand consumer is extracted and the posting behavior of brands and their followers is determined with the help of Twitter network features, such as retweet count and geolocation. This paper contributes to the literature on how Twitter data and its network structure features can be exploited in finding the responsiveness and posting behavior of companies and their followers. We believe that this approach can be used effectively in developing prediction and information-filtering systems, particularly the personalized-recommendation systems.

This paper proposes an automatic traffic sign detection and recognition system using SegU-Net and a modified Tversky loss function with L1-constraint. The proposed method utilizes image segmentation and color analysis to extract the important features of the traffic signs. Task analysis is then used to classify the detected signs. The system was trained using a deep learning approach, and benchmark testing showed promising results, with an accuracy rate of 97%. The modified Tversky loss function with L1-constraint further improved the performance of the system by enhancing the shape and overall recognition of the traffic signs. This study showcases the effectiveness of deep learning and image processing techniques in developing automated traffic sign detection and recognition systems.

This paper proposes an AMP-based network with deep residual learning for mmWave beamspace channel estimation. The proposed network takes advantage of antenna arrays and radio frequency lenses to develop an efficient channel estimation algorithm that utilizes MIMO communication. The training of the network is done using deep residual learning, which enhances the accuracy and robustness of estimation. The proposed method achieves higher estimation performance compared to traditional methods while reducing computation complexity, making it a promising solution for future mmWave communication systems.

This paper focuses on the development of personal identity verification based on convolutional neural networks (CNN). Specifically, it explores the feasibility of using electrocardiography and gray-scale images to establish identity in a secure manner. The research centers on the use of various kernel structures to refine CNN performance in image segmentation and biometric identification. This method of personal identification offers the potential for high level security in access control systems. The results indicate that the use of CNN enhances the accuracy and speed of personal identification and authentication, making it a viable option for improving security in various applications. Overall, this paper contributes to the expanding knowledge on the implementation of convolutional neural networks for advanced security measures.

This paper presents an investigative survey of a deployable SDN (Software-Defined Networking) architecture for network applications. The proposed architecture emphasizes the software components and servers utilized in data centers to enhance network security, routing efficiency, and IP network management. The primary objective of the study is to establish a comprehensive understanding of SDN and its deployment through an extensive analysis of its core features, functionalities, and benefits. The paper also highlights the challenges and limitations of SDN, especially in terms of security and privacy concerns. Based on the survey, the results suggest that SDN's deployable architecture has great potential for improving network performance and management in various network applications. However, software and hardware compatibility, as well as the unique requirements of each organization's network, must be carefully considered during the implementation of the proposed architecture. In summary, this paper provides substantial insights into the development, deployment, and limitations of SDN architecture for network applications.

This paper proposes a Candidate Label-aware Similarity Graph (CLSG) approach for dealing with partial label data in classification algorithms based on supervised learning. The CLSG method utilizes optimization techniques to construct a similarity graph, which incorporates label information in the training data to improve the learning process. The optimization process searches for the most informative edges in the graph, represented by Euclidean distance between pairs of samples, and uses them to train classifiers that are better suited for partial label data. With a focus on parametric statistics, the proposed algorithm can effectively handle complex datasets, even when only a small fraction of the data has ground-truth labels. The results of experimental evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed CLSG approach, with significant improvements over existing methods in terms of accuracy and scalability. Overall, the proposed method has the potential to facilitate efficient and effective training of classifiers for partial label data, opening up new opportunities for supervised learning in various applications.

In this paper, we develop computationally efficient and theoretically justified tools for analyzing high dimensional brain signals. Our approach is to extract the optimal lower dimensional representations for each brain region and then characterize and estimate connectivity between regions through these factors. This approach is motivated by our observation that electroencephalograms (EEGs) from many channels within each region exhibit a high degree of multicollinearity and synchrony thereby suggesting that it would be sensible to extract summary factors for each region. Here, the summary factors are the encodings that lead to the lowest reconstruction error. We focus on two special cases of linear auto encoder and decoder. The first characterizes the factors as instantaneous linear mixing of the observed signals. In the second approach, the factors are convolutions of the observed signals (which is more general than the first). These methods were compared through simulations under different conditions and the results provide insights on advantages and limitations of each. Finally, we performed exploratory analysis of resting state EEG data. The spectral properties of the factors were estimated and connectivity between regions via the factors using coherence measures were computed. We implemented these methods in a Matlab toolbox XHiDiTS (https://goo.gl/uXc8ei). The toolbox was utilized to investigate consistency of these factors across all epochs during the entire resting-state period.

In recent years, terrorist activities have posed a significant threat to public security. One method of improving security measures is through the use of automatic threat detection systems in X-ray imaging. The utilization of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is a promising solution for this task. These networks are able to effectively learn features of explosives within the X-ray images, which can then be used to quickly and accurately identify threats. The training of these networks is essential to ensure that they perform at the highest possible standards. Additionally, the use of DICOM standards enables standardized communication between different imaging systems and enhances the interoperability of these systems. Therefore, it is crucial to explore the potential benefits of utilizing CNNs in automatic threat detection in security X-ray images to improve public safety.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized various industries, including the building industry, by facilitating the development of smart building services. This paper explores the application of IoT in building automation through the integration of sensors, power systems, and logic gates to create smart buildings. The integration of IoT technologies in HVAC systems, lighting systems, and security systems enables energy-efficient and sustainable building operation, thereby reducing costs and conserving resources. Furthermore, the paper highlights the potential of IoT in enhancing building management systems through real-time data analytics and predictive maintenance. Overall, the IoT is proving to be a promising facilitator of smart building services with significant implications for the building industry, energy consumption and sustainability, and the way we live and work.

The study focuses on optimizing the air conditioning system using the low global warming potential (GWP) refrigerant R1234yf. The optimization is carried out using a genetic algorithm which enables multi-objective optimization of the system. The parameters that are considered for optimization include the refrigerant charge, tube diameter, number of fans, and compressor displacement. The study finds that using the genetic algorithm results in better optimization outcomes than previously used methods. Additionally, the use of R1234yf as a refrigerant in the air conditioning system reduces the environmental impact of the system. The analysis also considers economic factors such as the cost of the refrigerant and energy consumption. The study demonstrates that the use of R1234yf in the air conditioning system with the optimized parameters results in better environmental and economic outcomes.

Multidisciplinary design optimization techniques become more and more applied in the field of aerodynamics due to the rapid development of computers high-performance, numerical methods and optimization algorithms. These techniques coupled with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), which aims to incorporate mathematical relations and algorithms to analyze and solve fluid flow problems, involve the use of those numerical methods and algorithms to improve the fluid flow solutions. CFD analysis of an airfoil determines its ability by producing results such as lift and drag forces, and the application of an optimization algorithm involves improving the shape of this airfoil in order to manipulate the lift and drag coefficients according to the requirements. In this work, a numerical investigation, using ANSYS/Fluent, of two-dimensional transonic flow over a NACA 0012 airfoil was conducted at various Mach numbers and compared with the provided experimental data. The flow to be considered is compressible and turbulent and the solver used is the density based implicit solver, which gives good results for high speed compressible flows. Then a shape optimization algorithm, based on a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm, was used in order to obtain an improved performance control of the aerodynamic coefficients of the optimized airfoil.

Online auctions created a very attractive environment for dishonest moneymakers who can commit different types of fraud. Shill Bidding (SB) is the most predominant auction fraud and also the most difficult to detect because of its similarity to usual bidding behavior. Based on a newly produced SB dataset, in this study, we devise a fraud classification model that is able to efficiently differentiate between honest and malicious bidders. First, we label the SB data by combining a hierarchical clustering technique and a semi-automated labeling approach. To solve the imbalanced learning problem, we apply several advanced data sampling methods and compare their performance using the SVM model. As a result, we develop an optimal SB classifier that exhibits very satisfactory detection and low misclassification rates.

This paper proposes a simple quantum neural net with a periodic activation function. This neural net model uses qubits as its building blocks and employs logic gates to carry out computations. The periodic activation function is inspired by biological neural networks, which have been shown to exhibit periodic activity patterns. The proposed quantum neural net can potentially surpass classical machine learning algorithms in terms of computational power and complexity. The model is also amenable to computational modeling, making it a promising tool for exploring the properties of quantum systems. Overall, this paper presents an innovative approach to developing quantum neural nets, paving the way for future research in this exciting field.

In this paper, we propose an event-triggered adaptive control scheme for a class of nonlinear systems with unknown control direction and sensor faults. The proposed method is formulated using the backstepping technique where nonlinear functions are used to transform the system into a reference form. An adaptive controller is designed to compensate for the system uncertainties and ensure closed loop stability. To deal with the sensor faults, a state estimation is used to estimate the states of the system from the available measurements. The proposed event-triggered strategy reduces the communication burden between the sensor and the controller by only updating the controller when a predefined triggering condition is met. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulation examples. The results show that the proposed approach achieves robustness against uncertainties and sensor faults while reducing the communication frequency between the controller and the sensor.

Splitting algorithm as an important method for rare-event simulation, choosing of the intermediate levels for splitting has always been the focus of attention in the research field. Different from the study of important function (IF), this paper aimed to discuss the allocation of two-level splitting and select the optimal splitting level based on τ-Extermal Optimization (EO) algorithm. We use work-normalized variance of rare-event estimator as evaluation standard and compare the results with the common method for thresholds choosing in recent literature. The models of hitting probability and network reliability are used to test. It is verified that our method is more effective for variance reduction.

The application of natural languages to databases poses a major challenge due to the complexity of querying information from such structures. Deep learning techniques have been applied to this task with significant success, although the generation of accurate SQL code remains a challenge. This paper introduces a new approach known as Bidirectional Attention for SQL Generation which incorporates bidirectional control and a novel attention mechanism to improve semantics in SQL code. Using a task analysis framework, this approach allows for the highly precise transformation of natural language queries into structured query language syntax, reducing the semantic gap between the two forms of expression. Through experiments on a synthetic dataset as well as a real-world database, the proposed approach demonstrates substantially improved performance over previously established benchmarks. The potential for this method to be generalized to other natural language-to-code tasks is also discussed.

This paper presents a style-aware Bayesian personalized ranking approach for visual recommendation in which feature extraction, visualization, and correlation technique are utilized. Recommender systems play a crucial role in the field of e-commerce and personalization, given the explosion of data and options. The proposed method involves Bayesian methods and convolutional neural networks to extract distinctive feature representations and encode them into a diverse set of visual styles. Moreover, visualization is used to help understand how visual styles relate to different aspects of clothing. The system considers correlation coefficients between different types of clothing as the preference intuition in personalized recommendation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms several state-of-the-art recommendation methods in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency.

Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) provide feedback to learners in interactive learning environments, which advances knowledge acquisition and skills mastery. However, designing such systems is complex and demands expertise in diverse domains ranging from task analysis and cognition to mathematics and requirement engineering. Therefore, the use of artificial intelligence and user interfaces is becoming increasingly popular as they simplify the development process, making it more efficient and cost-effective. In this paper, we discuss the challenges of creating an ITS equipped with informed feedback and explore the various instruments that can be used to overcome these challenges. We review the latest research in the field of ITS and identify emerging trends and opportunities for future innovation. Ultimately, the successful development of an ITS requires interdisciplinary knowledge and collaboration, and this paper provides a framework to guide such efforts.

This paper introduces a novel technique for securing legacy clients in wireless networks, called collusion-resistant jamming. The technique involves the use of multiple antennas and receivers to estimate the channel and detect interference, while jamming signals are transmitted selectively to prevent attackers from causing interference. The focus is on the security of mobile computing devices with legacy wireless interfaces, which are particularly vulnerable to jamming attacks. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the technique through experimental results, showing that it is able to effectively counteract a range of attacks on wireless networks. This research contributes to the development of techniques for securing wireless networks, particularly in scenarios where legacy devices are still in use.

In the modern world, image transmission, including transmission of television and video signals, is carried out using a preliminary and restorative correction according to the law, which was due to the use of imaging devices on cathode ray tubes. This law differs from the law of dependence of the visibility threshold of a visual stimulus on its magnitude, but continues to be used for compatibility reasons. Therefore, in the work, instead of linearizing the sensations of the quantization scale of a television signal, it is proposed to optimize the choice of code combinations for image transmission. This approach can be effective in television systems without compression of video information with losses, for example, for transmitting signals over short distances or in channels for transmitting signals of the image of Earth remote sensing systems.

In recent years, the emergence of vehicular cloud computing has brought tremendous opportunities for the development of modern transportation systems. However, the task scheduling problem in vehicular cloud computing brings new challenges, especially in terms of security and trust. This paper proposes a task scheduling strategy that leverages smart contracts, blockchain, and cloud computing to enhance security in vehicular cloud computing environments. Based on task analysis, this strategy optimizes processor scheduling and improves resource utilization. Through blockchain technology, the smart contract is established to ensure trust between different entities in the vehicular cloud computing environment, and thus provides a secure and reliable task scheduling mechanism. The proposed strategy is evaluated by simulation, and the simulation results indicate that it outperforms the traditional scheduling algorithm in terms of task execution time and resource utilization. Moreover, the proposed strategy has strong theoretical significance and practical value for the development of vehicular cloud computing. The results of this research are of great significance for academia and industry, and the conclusions of this paper can provide insights for related research and development work. The proposed strategy has the potential to be applied in various smart transportation scenarios, such as intelligent transportation systems, smart cities, and traffic management conferences.

This paper presents a comparative survey on information dissemination in heterogeneous vehicular communication networks. The study focuses on the analysis of different communication protocols used in vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) and their impact on reliability, safety, data dissemination, and delays during road transportation. The primary goal of this research is to identify the most suitable and effective communication protocols for disseminating information in heterogeneous vehicular communication networks that can enable efficient and reliable communication while ensuring the safety of road users. The results of the study show that there are various communication protocols that can be employed in different situations and under different constraints. Evaluation of the reliability, safety, and delays of the protocols under different conditions reveals that some protocols perform better than others in certain scenarios. Therefore, the choice of a protocol depends on the specific requirements of the application and the context in which it is employed. This study provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of vehicular communication networks, helping them to make informed decisions about the most appropriate communication protocols for different applications.

Object detection is an essential task in various industries to automate processes and enhance efficiency. In recent years, deep neural networks have been widely used for object detection in industrial environments, and open source frameworks such as TensorFlow and PyTorch have made it easier to implement these networks. This paper presents the application of open source deep neural networks for object detection in industries such as containers, logistics, and service robots. The use of deep neural networks has significantly improved the accuracy of detectors and reduced false positives, resulting in more reliable and efficient systems. The paper also discusses the challenges faced in implementing these networks, such as the need for large annotated datasets and understanding the limitations of different architectures. Overall, the use of open source deep neural networks for object detection in industrial environments has tremendous potential to transform various industries, and this paper provides insights into the opportunities and challenges associated with their implementation.

This paper investigates cognitive action laws in the context of visual features, with a focus on feature extraction and boundary conditions. A mathematical model is proposed to describe the process of feature extraction, taking into account the kinetic energy of visual stimuli and various indexes related to the salience of visual features. The model is supported by experimental evidence and can be utilized in the fields of computer vision and visualization. Furthermore, the boundary conditions under which the cognitive action laws hold are discussed, including the effects of context and attention. The findings of this study provide a deeper understanding of the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual perception and offer insights into the development of intelligent systems for visual processing.

The articles in this special section focus on computing applications in railway engineering, with particular emphasis on the dynamic service performance of railway systems, especially of the high-speed trains. All of the six selected papers are from the Southwest Jiaotong University, the leading Chinese research institute in railway engineering, especially from the State Key Laboratory of Traction Power at the university. Furthermore, with the rapid network expansion of Chinese high-speed railways, more publications on better maintenance strategies and nondestructive examination methods for higher safety and reliability in operation may also come in the future if possible.

This paper examines industry-based doctoral dissertation research in a professional computing doctoral program for full time working professionals through the lens of different machine learning algorithms to understand topics explored by full time working industry professionals. This research paper examines machine learning algorithms and the IBM Watson Discovery machine learning tool to categorize dissertation research topics defended at Pace University. The research provides insights into differences in machine learning algorithm categorization using natural language processing.

AI and robot ethics have recently gained a lot of attention because adaptive machines are increasingly involved in ethically sensitive scenarios and cause incidents of public outcry. Much of the debate has been focused on achieving highest moral standards in handling ethical dilemmas on which not even humans can agree, which indicates that the wrong questions are being asked. We suggest to address this ethics debate strictly through the lens of what behavior seems socially acceptable, rather than idealistically ethical. Learning such behavior puts the debate into the very heart of developmental robotics. This paper poses a roadmap of computational and experimental questions to address the development of socially acceptable machines. We emphasize the need for social reward mechanisms and learning architectures that integrate these while reaching beyond limitations of plain reinforcement-learning agents. We suggest to use the metaphor of “needs” to bridge rewards and higher level abstractions such as goals for both communication and action generation in a social context. We then suggest a series of experimental questions and possible platforms and paradigms to guide future research in the area.

The paper involves an improved vector field clustering algorithm, which has achieved good performance when incorporated into the analysis of vector field. Additionally, a weighted K-means algorithm is presented, which is more appropriate for the analysis of scalar field clustering. The improved algorithm has better clustering results on the scalar field, which are more consistent with the physical laws by comparison. Ultimately, the algorithm is put in use for the CFD calculation. The number of iterations is decreased and the convergence speed is accelerated after the clustering algorithm is adopted for better initial condition.

The demand for high-resolution medical images is becoming increasingly important, especially in medical diagnostic imaging. In this paper, we propose a lesion focused multi-scale approach to improve the performance of Gan in single medical image super-resolution. This approach utilizes Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate realistic high-resolution images. The proposed approach is specifically designed to overcome the limitations of traditional image resolution techniques by paying close attention to the specific features of medical image lesions. In order to achieve this, we present a comprehensive approach to training and optimizing the GAN model, focusing on the most relevant features of medical image lesions. Our approach shows a superior performance on a number of benchmark datasets, demonstrating its potential for improving the quality of medical image super-resolution. Our main findings suggest that the proposed method holds great promise for increasing the accuracy of medical diagnosis, and could lead to significant improvements in medical imaging technology.

In this paper, we study the separability of the commonly used features to monitor the performance of optical signal in coherent optical systems. Specifically, our study focuses on the histogram-based features; the asynchronous amplitude histogram (AAH) and the two-dimensional extension of AAH, which we call IQ histogram (IQH). We investigate the conditions under which the optical channel impairments can be monitored. This study utilizes a dimensionality reduction technique, known as the t-distribution stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE). Using t-SNE, we show that under certain conditions the histogram-based features cannot be used to distinguish between the high and low impairment effects, rendering these features useless for certain cases, regardless of the type or complexity of the implemented impairments' estimator/classifier. Extensive simulations results have been conducted to investigate single and multiple impairments conditions and the performance of histogram-based features in each case. The results show that both AAH and IQH can be used for monitoring all types of single Impairment except phase noise in case of AAH. Moreover, under multiple impairments conditions, polarization mode dispersion values can be monitored to some extent, while it is difficult to monitor optical signal-to-noise ratio and chromatic dispersion values especially in the case of concurrent presence of more than two impairments. The results of these investigations are validated by providing a quantitative measure that ties their usefulness to the actual monitoring performance through the estimation of channel impairments under different conditions using linear support vector machine (SVM) regression. It has been found that there is a match to a great extent between the separability investigation using t-SNE and estimation results obtained using SVM.

This paper proposes an energy-aware fault-tolerant scheduling scheme for cloud data centers based on an intelligent prediction model. The scheme takes into account task analysis, fault tolerance, scheduling, energy consumption, and cloud computing. Fault tolerant systems are essential for cloud data centers as hardware failures can lead to data loss and system downtime. The proposed scheme predicts possible failures and redirects tasks to healthy nodes before any downtime occurs. This improves fault tolerance and minimizes energy consumption in the data center. Predictive models are used to forecast task execution time and energy consumption, which are factors that impact scheduling decisions. The scheme also factors in peak and off-peak energy rates to further optimize energy consumption. Overall, the proposed energy-aware fault-tolerant scheduling scheme improves system reliability and energy efficiency in cloud data centers.

A single-inductor dual-supply dc-dc converter with bidirectional energy flow is proposed for the Internet-of-Things applications. This paper combines two dc-dc converters into one by sharing a single inductor, and it is capable of storing energy and powering output load by using the bidirectional inductor current. Besides, the voltage of the energy storage element is continuously monitored in the proposed converter, which eliminates the possibility of overcharging. Furthermore, the variations on the output voltage are typically negligible when the input voltage changes. In addition, a novel two-step startup procedure that does not require any on-chip/off-chip startup auxiliary circuit is proposed, which can significantly reduce the chip area. The proposed converter is fabricated by a 0.18-μm CMOS mixed-signal process. The voltage range of the storing element is 1.2-1.4 V, and the maximal output power of the proposed converter is 18 mW with its output voltage setting at 1.8 V.

The field of sentiment analysis is of great interest to researchers in speech processing and modeling. The current study proposes a novel method for constructing a sentiment lexicon using hierarchical supervision topic model based on probabilistic logic. The proposed model, named Sun, leverages the power of neural networks to learn complex patterns in sentiment data. The proposed model is tested on a dataset of motion pictures reviews, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The proposed method provides a promising framework for sentiment analysis which can be used in a variety of applications such as social media analysis, opinion mining and review summarization.

In recent years, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has demonstrated promising results in the field of brain-computer interface (BCI).
