However, the accuracy of fNIRS-BCI still needs to be improved. This paper proposes a data augmentation method based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enhance the performance of fNIRS-BCI. The data models utilized in this approach are GAN generators, which are able to generate synthetic fNIRS data that can improve the training of fNIRS-BCI models. A task analysis is performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Brain modeling and the use of gallium nitride (GaN) are also discussed as potential avenues for improving fNIRS-BCI accuracy. The results show that GAN-based data augmentation improves the performance of fNIRS-BCI compared to traditional training data. Further research and experimentation are necessary to fully understand the potential of this approach and to optimize the training process.

In this paper, we present a method for D2D neighborhood discovery by a mobile device. The proposed method leverages discrete Fourier transforms and artificial intelligence techniques to identify nearby devices in a reliable manner. As mobile devices increasingly rely on direct communication with other devices in close proximity, the ability to accurately and efficiently discover nearby devices becomes crucial. The software implementation of the proposed method is designed to be efficient and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of devices and IP networks. Additionally, the use of iris recognition technology and computer architecture optimizations can further enhance the reliability and accuracy of the proposed method. Overall, our study shows that D2D neighborhood discovery is an important area of research for achieving efficient and reliable communication between mobile devices.

Connected vehicles that communicate with the traffic network around them have several uses in providing road safety and infotainment. Such applications leverage on Vehicle-to-Anything (V2X) communication, which is challenging because of rapidly changing topology and traffic patterns. We propose a differentiated edge caching scheme called FlexiCache for such networks. In FlexiCache, the cache is split into sections to hold data of different classes with suitable replacement policies. Further, FlexiCache uses kernel ridge regression (KRR) to predict the proportion of cache to be allocated to each traffic type, for a desired quality of service(QoS) parameter. It then uses a self-learning mechanism that adapts cache allocation to the network conditions. Simulation results show that FlexiCache performs better than undifferentiated caching and also that the predictions by KRR result in QoS which is very close to the target value.

Emotion recognition is a challenging problem in computer vision and has numerous applications in different domains. Databases play a crucial role in emotion recognition, as they provide a benchmark for evaluating the performance of different algorithms. The EMOTIC dataset is a recently proposed large-scale dataset containing over 24,000 images with rich annotations related to emotion, objects, actions, and attributes. In this context-based approach, face recognition is used for the identification of the observer in the image. The proposed methodology takes into account the contextual information by incorporating the observer's knowledge to improve the recognition of emotions. The experimental evaluation of the approach has achieved state-of-the-art results, proving the effectiveness of this approach for emotion recognition. Therefore, the proposed methodology can be applied to various domains, such as human-computer interaction, medical diagnosis, and intelligent transportation systems.

This paper proposes a fine-grained hardware for integrated look-up architecture to process IPv4 and IPv6 packets. A TCAM-based LPM search architecture is designed to accommodate IPv6 addressing scheme along with the existing IPv4 addressing scheme in an efficient and integrated manner. The architecture is able to deal with immense IP traffic growth and network speed to support multi-gigabit/sec bit rate using lower memory requirement. Moreover, This engine does not require any sort of prefix ordering according to their prefix length unlike conventional TCAM based schemes. Furthermore, it provides an efficient and fast LPM structure by involving only some digital logic gates those operate in a systematic fashion with/without parallel working mechanism. The numerical results show that this lookup engine remarkably decreases memory requirement. The time needed to search a prefix and to perform next-hop lookup is ≈ 1 clock cycle each. The proposed engine performs an LPM lookup in 3.17 ns (IPv4) and 3.12 ns (IPv6). The average search throughput exhibited by the proposed engine is beyond OC-768 wire-speed and is roughly 70 Gbps.

In recent years, the development of computer vision technology has enabled the tracking of vehicle and faces, which has great potential in the assessment of human behavior. The use of advanced algorithms allows for efficient feature extraction and accurate face recognition, enabling computational modeling and analysis. This technology has the potential to revolutionize the way we evaluate social interactions and relationships, and could be used in a variety of applications, such as monitoring public safety or assessing mental health. The ability to track vehicles and faces in real-time provides valuable data that can aid in identifying potential security threats and improving public safety measures. Furthermore, the exchange of information on social networks and other online communities could be monitored using facial recognition technology, providing insight into patterns of behavior and social interactions. As such, the integration of tracking vehicle and faces into the development of socialistic models for assessing human behavior has enormous potential for enhancing our understanding of human behavior and improving societal outcomes.

Voice biometrics has been applied to enhance the security of spoken language proficiency tests and ensure valid test scores by detecting fraudulent activity. These methods can, however, be triggered by certain distortions, including background noise and adjacent test-takers, resulting in false positive alarms. In this paper, a two-layer bi-directional LSTM RNN model is employed to detect these distorted (unusable) responses and a sub-sampling method is applied to reduce the difficulties of model training caused by very long input sequence and imbalanced training data. The system is evaluated on a corpus that was collected from an assessment of English language proficiency around the world. Results show that our approach significantly outperforms two baselines: a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) classifying frame-level features and an AdaBoost classifier operating on i-vectors. Our system's F-score in unusable response detection is 0.60 compared to 0.43 and 0.49 for the two baseline systems.

This paper focuses on input prioritization for testing neural networks, with a particular emphasis on managing uncertainty during the testing process. Neural network testing is critical to ensuring adequate performance for real-world applications, but can be complicated by large, complex networks with numerous inputs. Through the use of Bayes methods and other computational modeling techniques, this paper proposes a strategy for prioritizing inputs during the testing phase to improve efficiency and reduce testing time. Additionally, the paper discusses the importance of incorporating knowledge from biological neural networks in the training process to further enhance network performance. Overall, this paper offers a comprehensive overview of input prioritization in neural network testing and provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become increasingly popular due to their ability to deploy nodes in various fields such as agriculture, environment, medical care and logistics. However, the design of efficient and scalable WSNs still remains a significant challenge. This paper proposes a location updating scheme of the sink node based on topology balance and reinforcement learning in WSN. The proposed scheme addresses the issue of unbalanced energy consumption in the network topology by taking into account the geographic distance and the energy level of the nodes. A reinforcement learning algorithm is integrated to improve the network's energy efficiency by adjusting the location of the sink node. The proposed location updating scheme enables dataproductivity by prolonging network lifetime and enhancing accurate data aggregation. The scheme's efficiency is evaluated through simulations, and the results show that it outperforms the traditional location updating schemes and protocols in terms of network lifetime, data forwarding and monitoring. The proposed scheme can be extended to other WSN protocols and applications, and can be a useful tool to achieve better network efficiency and balance.

This paper presents an artificial neural network (ANN) based simulation and control approach for a 2 MW small hydro power plant, which is integrated with a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG). The focus of the study is on the rotors and stators of the DFIG, as these are key components for generating electrical power. The proposed control approach uses ANN for signal processing, which helps to improve the overall efficiency and performance of the power plant. The study also highlights the utilization of hydroelectric power generation for renewable energy sources, which can help to reduce the dependency on non-renewable sources of energy. Overall, this research provides a valuable contribution to the field of power plant simulation and control, and underscores the importance of utilizing artificial neural networks for signal processing in power generation systems.

Finite mixture models are widely applied in various domains of applications. They assist to analyze datasets, achieve better insight into the nature of data, discover latent patterns and provide critical knowledge that we are looking for. The main focus in past works was on Gaussian statistical models, however there are several applications involving asymmetric and non-Gaussian data. Parameter estimation is one of the essential and fundamental challenges of statistical researches. Some deterministic approaches such as expectation maximization (EM) have been mainly considered as effective techniques to deal with this issue. In this article, we introduce a bivariate Beta distribution with three parameters as our main parent distribution which could be applied in skin detection and image segmentation. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated by experimental results that concern both artificial and real datasets.

For perceptual and acoustical assessment of voice disorder, a commonly asked question is about what type of speech samples should be examined and analyzed. While sustained vowels are simple, easy to produce, and suitable for direct comparison among patients, continuous speech is ecologically more valid and better represents the daily use of voice. This study makes an attempt to compare the effectiveness and contribution of sustained vowels and continuous speech in predicting voice disorder severity. To measure voice disorder severity for sustained vowels and continuous speech utterances, two three-class (mild, moderate and severe) classifiers are trained separately with different acoustic features sets. The acoustic features include measures on perturbation, prosody, noise, spectrum and cepstrum. Experimental results on a Cantonese speech database of disordered voice show that sustained vowels and continuous speech are complementary to each other. Relating to their different production complexities, these two types of utterances may exhibit significantly different degrees of voice abnormality, and hence be assigned different severity levels. This suggests that when predicting the subject-level severity based on the utterance-level measures, the speech types of individual utterances must be taken into account. Specifically a posterior fusion approach is proposed for generating subject-level prediction result. In the three-class (mild, moderate and severe) subject-level disorder severity prediction task, the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 75% and AUC (Area Under Curve of ROC) of 0.862.

The classification falls into the essential tasks of supervised learning. The prediction of highly disperse nature of data, such as clinical medical data, is an open challenge. This study performs experimental analysis of machine learning algorithm to develop an effective prediction model for the clinical dataset. A real time clinical dataset has been considered for the model development. The machine learning algorithms: Decision Tree (J48), Naïve Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) have been applied. The validation of prediction model has been evaluated using both cross validation and split percentage methods. It has been evident that classification algorithms in combination of ensemble methods perform better. Thus, an effective prediction model performs better in presence of ensemble methods. The bagging, voting and stacking - ensemble methods have been used in this study. The experimental outcomes revealed that Naïve Bayes produced better predictive results using 10-fold cross validation method. Whilst, MLP outperformed using split percentage method for evaluation.

In wireless communication, information-centric ad hoc networks (ICNs) are becoming increasingly popular, as they allow devices to connect, communicate, and share data with one another directly. However, due to the decentralized nature of these networks, there are concerns about the privacy and security of the information being shared. One approach to address these concerns is through the use of encryption techniques, such as homomorphic encryption. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving forwarding mechanism for ICNs that utilizes homomorphic encryption to ensure the security and privacy of the data being transmitted. The proposed mechanism is evaluated using manganese measurement, and the results show that it effectively balance the privacy and performance requirements of ICNs. In conclusion, the use of homomorphic encryption in information-centric wireless ad hoc networks can provide data privacy without sacrificing performance or efficiency.

A new nonparametric Bayesian-based motion planning algorithm for autonomous plume source term estimation (STE) and source seeking (SS) is presented in this paper. The algorithm is designed for mobile robots equipped with gas concentration sensors. Specifically, robots coordinate and utilize a Gaussian-plume likelihood model in a Bayesian-based STE process, then they simultaneously search for and navigate toward the source through model based, bioinspired SS methods such as biased-random-walk and surge-casting. Compared with the state-of-the-art Bayesian- and sensor-based STE/SS motion planners, the strategy described takes advantage of coordination between multiple robots and the estimated plume model for faster and more robust SS, rather than rely on direct or filtered sensor measurements. A set of Monte Carlo simulation studies are conducted to compare the performance between the uncoordinated and coordinated algorithms for different robot team sizes and starting conditions. Additionally, the algorithms are validated experimentally through a laboratory-safe, realistic humid-air plume that behaves similar to a gas plume, to test STE and SS using mobile ground robots equipped with humidity sensors. Simulation and experimental results show consistently that the algorithm involving coordination outperforms traditional bioinspired SS algorithms and it is approximately twice as fast as the uncoordinated case. Finally, the plume source is distorted to study the algorithm's limitations and impact on STE and SS, where results show that even for distorted plumes, useful source localization information can be obtained.

It is difficult to balance the convergence and diversity at the same time and select the globally optimal particle (gbest) in the multiobjective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) process. In this paper, a novel method based on adaptive angle division is proposed targeting at archive maintenance and gbest selection. According to the number of particles in the current archive, the angle region of the target space is adaptively adjusted and uniformly divided. The globally optimal particle is selected from the low-density angle region of the particle distribution; in the meanwhile, the superfluous particles are deleted from the high-density angle region. Consequently, the selection of gbest and update of external archive set which including the generation of the optimal solution set and maintenance of external archive set are synchronized. The convergence and diversity are ensured while improving the uniformity of the optimal solution set. In addition, the current highest non-dominated particles in each angle region are preserved, and the particles in adjacent regions are selected to conduct global guidance for such regions and regions of the particle-free distribution area. Through these two ways, the diversity of the population is maintained while the coverage spreadability of the optimal solution set in the target space is enhanced. Four state-of-the-art evolution multiobjective optimization (EMO) algorithms and the two classic EMO algorithms are selected as the peer algorithms to validate multiobjective particle swarm optimization based on adaptive angle division (AADMOPSO) algorithm. A series of extensive experiments are conducted on five groups of standard test functions. The experimental results show the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed AADMOPSO in balancing convergence and diversity.

This paper presents an adaptive task scheduler for a cloud of drones. In recent years, drones have become an important technology for various applications, and drones working collaboratively as a swarm can achieve complex tasks. Task analysis is an important step for efficient management of drone swarms. In addition, the energy consumption of drones is related to battery capacity, and the control of the load of the battery can effectively prolong the flight time of drones. Cloud computing has the potential to solve many challenges associated with drone swarms, such as redundancy, fault tolerance, and scalability. The use of streaming media for drone operations adds new requirements to the networking protocols. The proposed task scheduler adapts to the resources of the drone swarm, and defines operation modes that are friendly to the batteries. This approach can solve the problem of resource waste and prolong battery life. The scheduler also incorporates cloud computing resources, including storage and computing power, which can help drone swarms complete complex or computationally intensive tasks. In this architecture, the protocols for collaboration and communication are critical factors for a successful system. The experimental results show that the adaptive task scheduler can efficiently manage the task execution of drone swarms, and improve the performance and reliability of the system.

This paper introduces a novel approach for the initialization of a visual-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system. The proposed method presents a general linear formulation that enables the fusion of camera and inertial measurements for feature extraction and 3D reconstruction. Additionally, a non-linear optimization technique that considers the effect of gravity is employed to refine the estimated trajectory of the SLAM system. The mathematical model used in this approach is designed to ensure optimization convergence while taking into account the system's robustness against measurement outliers. The proposed method achieves superior results compared to state-of-the-art SLAM initialization techniques, particularly for challenging environments where the gravity vector cannot be assumed to be constant. The use of gravity-observing non-linear optimization enables accurate estimation of the SLAM system's trajectory in six degrees of freedom.

This paper discusses the use of open source resources to advance Electroencephalography (EEG) research, particularly in the context of deep learning. The availability of open source tools has made it easier for hospitals and researchers to access EEG data and analyze it with signal processing algorithms. This paper also emphasizes the importance of training in EEG research, as the field continues to grow and evolve. Overall, open source resources have revolutionized the study of EEG by making it more accessible and providing researchers with valuable tools and insights.

In this paper, we propose a supervoxel-based approach for unsupervised abnormal asymmetry detection in MR images of the brain. The approach involves the use of image segmentation to partition the MR images into supervoxels, which are small, three-dimensional units that provide a local representation of the image. The supervoxels are then trained and tested using a combination of features extracted from the images. Visualization techniques are also used to aid in the detection of abnormal asymmetries in the brain. The proposed approach has potential applications in the fields of neuroimaging and medical diagnosis. It is an effective tool for detecting lesions in the brain, which can be indicative of various pathologies. Furthermore, the use of unsupervised learning allows for more efficient and accurate detection of lesions compared to traditional approaches. The approach may also be extended to other domains, such as forestry, where it can be used to detect abnormal asymmetries in tree growth patterns. Overall, our findings suggest that this supervoxel-based approach is a promising method for unsupervised abnormal asymmetry detection in MR images of the brain.

According to the recent report, 12 000 new Android malware samples will be generated every day. Efficient identification of evolving malware is an urgent challenge. Traditional methods based on structured features such as permissions and sensitive application programming interface (API) calls lack high-level behavioral semantics to detect evolving malware. The methods based on call graphs (CG) are good at behavioral semantic analysis but face the problem of huge time and space consumption, which leads to low detection efficiency. In this paper, we propose a novel Android malware detection method based on the method-level correlation relationship of application's abstracted API calls. First, we split each Android application's source code into separate function methods and just keep the abstracted API calls of them to form a set of abstracted API calls transactions. And then, we calculate the confidence of association rules between the abstracted API calls, which forms behavioral semantics to describe an application. Finally, we combine machine learning to identify the different behavioral patterns of malicious and benign apps to build the detection system. The results of our empirical evaluation show our system is competitive in terms of classification accuracy and detection efficiency. At dataset Drebin (benign 5.9K and malware 5.6K) and AMD (benign 20.5K and malware 20.8K), our system has achieved 96% and 98% detection results both in accuracy and F-measure. Compared with the state-of-the-art system in detecting evolving malware called MaMaDroid on the dataset of 6.0K benign and 20.5K malicious samples spanning from 2010 to 2017, our system achieves higher accuracy while improving detection efficiency by 15 times (2.9 s versus 45.7 s per sample).

This paper introduces a novel approach to harmonic Bayesian prediction under $\alpha$-divergence. The proposed method leverages the principles of Bayes methods and harmonic analysis to improve estimation and robustness of predictive models. One of the main advantages of this method is its ability to handle covariance matrices of arbitrary rank, making it particularly useful for high-dimensional datasets. The performance of the approach is evaluated using a range of indexes, and the results show that it outperforms existing methods, particularly in cases where the target distribution is multivariate or non-normal. This work contributes to the growing body of research on Bayesian methods for prediction and provides a promising approach for the development of more robust and accurate predictive models for complex datasets.

Honeypot technology can be applied to efficiently attract attackers and exhaust their resources. However, the traditional static honeypot is easy to be recognized by anti-honeypot technology. By contrast, most of the dynamic honeypots can simulate the real system in time, thus interacting with an intruder in disguise. In this paper, we employ the dynamic property of honeypot in four kinds of services of our system. However, this dynamic property shows up in a location and identification, indicating that genuine or fake services (honeypots) are changeable in different hosts. Thus, the dynamic property of our system differs from the dynamic honeypot aforementioned. Besides, we adopt the blockchain platform (Ethereum) to decentralize our system and store the port access data by delivering a private chain. To illustrate the effectiveness of our scheme in theory and practice, security analysis, eavesdropping attack, scanning attack, and DoS attack experiments are conducted. The results show that our scheme is valid in safeguarding against network attack.

This paper presents a study on permittivity and conductivity estimation for hyperthermia treatment planning. The goal of the study is to use magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to estimate the permittivity and conductivity of tissues in order to formulate an effective treatment plan for hyperthermia. The approach used by the authors involves solving an inverse problem, where the unknown permittivity and conductivity values are estimated by fitting a model to the MRI data. The paper describes the methodology in detail, including the numerical methods used for the estimation and the experimental setup used to validate the approach. The results show that the proposed method is effective in estimating the permittivity and conductivity of tissues, and can be used to plan hyperthermia treatments with high precision. This work has important implications for the development of more accurate and effective hyperthermia treatment planning tools, which can improve the outcomes of hyperthermia treatment for cancer patients.

Conversion of existing image and video content to High Dynamic Range (HDR) using inverse Tone Mapping Operators (iTMOs) is expected to enable the HDR market and open new market opportunities for studios and content owners. In this paper, we propose a high contrast video iTMO that addresses shortcomings of existing approaches, yielding HDR video quality worth the expectations of the emerging HDR technology. Our approach is content adaptive and is able to convert SDR videos to HDR videos of any target dynamic range. Our approach follows the Human Visual System (HVS) characteristic of being more sensitive to luminance changes in dark areas than bright and normal ones, mapping each of these areas accordingly. Our subjective evaluations demonstrate that our proposed method on average outperforms existing iTMOs in terms of overall HDR visual quality.

This paper discusses the benefits of utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to assist individuals with disabilities. The use of IoT technologies can greatly improve the quality of life for disabled individuals by providing them with increased accessibility and independence. Additionally, this paper examines the use of "surges," "lightning," and "arresters" in the context of IoT technology to prevent damage to equipment and improve overall reliability. The implementation of IoT technologies requires expertise in computer science and thorough testing to ensure proper functioning and security. In summary, the application of IoT technologies to disabilities persons represents a promising avenue for improving their quality of life and should be further explored in future research.

This paper proposes a novel approach for Mandarin Chinese speech keyword spotting using a combination of Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). Unlike the conventional method that relies on Hidden Markov models (HMMs), this new approach operates at character level, utilizing both acoustics and lattices for more accurate recognition. The proposed system undertakes task analysis by using linguistic and phonetic information to create a lattice structure, which is then exploited for keyword search. In contrast to traditional HMM-based techniques, the proposed architecture has the capability to handle large-vocabulary and out-of-vocabulary keywords. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed technique is able to identify target keywords with high accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising solution for Mandarin Chinese speech keyword spotting tasks.

Static code analysis in Continuous Integration (CI) environment can significantly improve the quality of a software system because it enables early detection of defects without any test executions or user interactions. However, being a conservative over-approximation of system behaviours, static analysis also produces a large number of false positive alarms, identification of which takes up valuable developer time. We present an automated classifier based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We hypothesise that many false positive alarms can be classified by identifying specific lexical patterns in the parts of the code that raised the alarm: human engineers adopt a similar tactic. We train a CNN based classifier to learn and detect these lexical patterns, using a total of about 10K historical static analysis alarms generated by six static analysis checkers for over 27 million LOC, and their labels assigned by actual developers. The results of our empirical evaluation suggest that our classifier can be highly effective for identifying false positive alarms, with the average precision across all six checkers of 79.72%.

Fast collective activity recognition under weak supervision is a challenging problem in computer vision. In this paper, we present a novel approach for activity recognition by performing task analysis, detector selection, feature extraction, and training in a coordinated and efficient manner. By doing so, we are able to achieve real-time systems for activity recognition under weak supervision. Our approach is based on the use of detectors to identify relevant activity categories, which are then used to extract features that capture important aspects of the activity. These features are then used to train a classifier that can recognize activities in real time. Our results demonstrate that our approach is both fast and accurate, and can be used in a variety of applications, such as surveillance, smart homes, and healthcare monitoring. Overall, our work represents an important step towards developing robust activity recognition algorithms that can operate in realistic scenarios with minimal supervision.

The problem of improving the processes of professional training of operators (by the example of operators of the portal crane) during training using computer simulators is considered. Computer technologies, in particular, simulators of technological installations and automated training systems, are widely used in the training of professional personnel. This contributes to the reduction of the human factor in the control of complex processes, as a result, the reduction of industrial injuries and emergency situations. However, the problem of automating the learning process in order to shape the future operator with the required level of sensorimotor skills is not well understood. The paper presents models and algorithms of the control system for the formation of operator sensomotor skills. Models and algorithms allow you to control the dynamics of the formation of skills as a multi-step process based on iterative learning. The practical implementation of the proposed scientific results on the training complex provides the necessary level of information support for the student and increases the efficiency of acquiring the ability to self-monitor the quality of technological operations.

This paper proposes a predictive model for estimating the defect density of new software projects. The model is based on the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm utilizing the Upsilon-SVR polynomial kernel. The kernel provides the ability to handle non-linearly separable data and produces better prediction results compared to other kernel functions. The model's accuracy is evaluated using various measurement techniques such as mean absolute error, mean squared error, and root mean squared error. Additionally, the paper compares the proposed model's performance to that of other popular predictive model algorithms, including neural networks and decision trees. Overall, the results show that the Upsilon-SVR polynomial kernel model outperforms other models in accurately predicting defect densities in new software projects.

This paper proposes a novel approach to binary matrix completion, leveraging nonconvex regularizers to improve the convergence speed and accuracy of matrix decomposition. The key idea of this method is to accelerate the optimization process by exploiting the sparsity of the underlying matrix, which is often encountered in real-world applications such as manganese exploration. In particular, the proposed framework incorporates various nonconvex regularizers, such as L1-norm and nuclear norm, to encode the sparsity of the target matrix and enforce low-rank structure. Moreover, the paper presents a detailed analysis of the convergence properties of the proposed method and derives rigorous theoretical guarantees for the recovery performance. Experimental evaluations on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach, which outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both convergence speed and recovery quality. Overall, this work contributes to advancing the field of binary matrix completion and provides valuable insights for exploring the potential of nonconvex regularizers in other optimization problems.

Poultry farms are an important contributor to the human food chain. Worldwide, humankind keeps an enormous number of domesticated birds (e.g. chickens) for their eggs and their meat, providing rich sources of low-fat protein. However, around the world, there have been growing concerns about the quality of life for the livestock in poultry farms; and increasingly vocal demands for improved standards of animal welfare. Recent advances in sensing technologies and machine learning allow the possibility of automatically assessing the health of some individual birds, and employing the lessons learned to improve the welfare for all birds. This task superficially appears to be easy, given the dramatic progress in recent years in classifying human behaviors, and given that human behaviors are presumably more complex. However, as we shall demonstrate, classifying chicken behaviors poses several unique challenges, chief among which is creating a generalizable "dictionary" of behaviors from sparse and noisy data. In this work we introduce a novel time series dictionary learning algorithm that can robustly learn from weakly labeled data sources.

Opinion mining or sentiment analysis used to understand the community's opinions on a particular product. Sentiment analysis involves building the opinion collection and classification system. One of the most crucial tasks of sentiment analysis is the ability to extract aspects or features that opinions expressed on. There are many approaches and techniques used to explore these features from unstructured comments. We proposed a different approach to the above mentioned aspect extraction task in sentiment analysis using a deep learning model combining Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) and Conditional Random Field (CRF). This model is trained on labeled data to extract and classify feature sets in comments. Our model uses a BiGRU neural network with word embeddings achieved by training GloVe on the SemEval 2014 dataset. The SemEval 2014 dataset include 7,686 reviews on two domains, Laptop and Restaurant. Experimental results showed that our aspect extraction model in sentiment analysis using BiGRU-CRF achieved significantly better accuracy than the state-of-the-art methods.

Since the debut of iOS and Android smartphones 10 years ago, the world has seen a mobile era wherein our phones have become a mobile computing platform deeply integrated into our lives [1]-[4]. Due to the advancement of computing, it is believed that the world is shifting to a new era where artificial intelligence (AI) is unlocking capabilities that were previously unthinkable [5]-[13]. Because computing is becoming more universally available, interaction with computing devices needs to be much more natural, intuitive, and, above all, intelligent [14].

Precise segmentation of prostate in magnetic resonance images is an essential step in treatment planning and a challenging task due to high variability in shape and size of the tissue. In this paper, we propose an automatic algorithm for accurate and robust segmentation of prostate in MR images. First, we employ a deep neural network to locate the prostate region of interest which removes background pixels and reduces the size of the image. Then, we obtain an initial segmentation of the tissue using a probabilistic atlas. Finally, we utilize statistical shape models to restrict the final contour inside the allowable shape domain. We performed a quantitative evaluation on 30 MR images and obtained a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.85±0.06. Compared to recent researches, our method is both robust and accurate.

In the field of multi-robots, various research works have addressed the problem of coordination and task division between robots. Coordination in a multi-robot system is necessary when they collaborate to perform a given task or simultaneously share the same resources. The coordination aims to ensure that each robot in the multi-robot system (MRS) performs its tasks safely. As well as a good method of distribution and assignment of tasks must be effective, reliable and well-defined. In this work, we will present a conceptual architecture, that ensures coordination between the entire team of heterogeneous robots and then a new strategy based on artificial intelligence algorithms to assign tasks for a heterogeneous MRS in the optimal way.

Visual sign language recognition is an interesting and challenging problem. To create a discriminative representation, a hierarchical Grassmann covariance matrix (HGCM) model is proposed for sign description. Furthermore, a multi-temporal belief propagation (MTBP) based segmentation approach is presented for continuous sequence spotting. Concretely speaking, a sign is represented by multiple covariance matrices, followed by evaluating and selecting their most significant singular vectors. These covariance matrices are transformed into a more compact and discriminative HGCM, which is formulated on the Grassmann manifold. Continuous sign sequences can be recognized frame by frame using the HGCM model, before being optimized by MTBP, which is a carefully designed graphic model. The proposed method is thoroughly evaluated on isolated and synthetic and real continuous sign datasets as well as on HDM05. Extensive experimental results convincingly show the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

With the exponential growth of data traffic in recent years, optical fiber networks are becoming increasingly important in providing high-speed communication. The building blocks of these networks include network elements such as optical amplifiers, transmitters, switches, and receivers. Optical fibers, as the transmission medium, play a crucial role in ensuring high data transmission rates and low losses. Optical amplifiers are used to amplify the signal and extend its reach, while optical transmitters convert electrical signals into optical signals for transmission. Optical switches allow for the efficient routing of data and optical receivers detect and convert optical signals back into electrical signals for processing. These network elements are essential in ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of optical fiber networks.

This study focuses on the identification of ghost moving detections in automotive scenarios using deep learning techniques. The research aims to enhance the accuracy of radar-based motion detection systems in automotive engineering. In particular, the study uses semantic segmentation and feature extraction methods for deep learning, specifically convolutional neural networks, to identify ghost moving detections in automotive scenarios. The proposed methodology includes image segmentation and convolutional feature extraction, which are used to separate valid targets from ghost detections. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in detecting and eliminating ghost moving detections in real-world driving scenarios. The findings of this study provide a promising direction for future research in the development of more accurate and reliable motion detection systems in the automotive industry.

Constructing reasonable structures of sequences is one of the most important problems. Especially, artificial sequences such as music and languages have some potential structures as human beings tend to build their constructions in creating. Although a recurrent neural network (RNN) has shown remarkable performance in processing sequences, it apparently cannot handle particularly long structures. This paper proposes a novel approach for building structures of sequences based on a genetic algorithm (GA) and a hierarchical RNN. The evaluation of the GA focuses on the negative log-likelihoods when the hierarchical RNN predicts the next elements. Thus, our proposal can be used for different types of sequences. In the experiments, musical notes are applied to this method, so the GA exhibits great structures minimizing the negative log-likelihoods and the hierarchical RNN shows better performance than stacked long short-term memory as a baseline.

This paper proposes a device-free non-privacy invasive indoor human posture recognition system using low-resolution infrared sensor-based wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). This system can monitor the posture of senior citizens without using cameras, which may violate their privacy. Instead, temperature sensors on heating systems in each room are used to detect human presence, and low-resolution infrared sensors are used to capture human body thermal images. DCNN is used to recognize the posture of the person. This system provides a new method for biomedical monitoring, especially for senior citizens who may need constant care but would prefer to maintain their privacy.

This paper proposes a self-guiding multimodal LSTM approach to tackle the issue of having an imperfect training dataset for image captioning. By utilizing task analysis and visualization techniques, the proposed approach not only captures the semantics of the images but also guides the training process towards better performance. This is especially important when dealing with real-world datasets like Flickr and urban areas where training data can be noisy and incomplete. The results show that the self-guiding approach outperforms the traditional LSTM model and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of embedding quality and captioning accuracy. The proposed approach provides a promising direction for improving the performance of image captioning models in scenarios where perfect training datasets are not available.

The emergence of 5G mobile communication technologies leads to an increasing demand for efficient network slicing and resource control frameworks. In this paper, we propose a Multi-Domain Network Slicing Orchestration Architecture, which integrates cloud computing and virtualization techniques for flexible service provisioning. The framework is composed of several Conductor nodes that manage multiple domains and cooperate to orchestrate network slices. Federated resource control mechanisms are also proposed to enable dynamic sharing and allocation of resources among different domains. Our proposed architecture is compliant with 3GPP standards and supports various types of network services, such as ultra-reliable low-latency communication and massive machine-type communication. The performance of the proposed architecture is evaluated through simulations, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving efficient network slicing and resource control.

Deep learning is applied to many research topics; Natural Language Processing, Image Processing, and Acoustic Recognition. In deep learning, neural networks have a very complex and deep structure and it is difficult to discuss why they work well or not. So you have to take a trial-and-error to improve their performances. We develop a mechanism to show how neural networks predict final results and help you to design a new neural network architecture based on its prediction criteria. Speaking concrete, we visualize important features to predict the final results with an attentional mechanism. In this paper, we take up sentient analysis, which is one of natural language processing tasks. In image processing visualizing weights of a neural network is a major approach and you can obtain intuitive results; object outlines and object components. However, in natural language processing, the approach is not interpretable because a discriminate function constructed by a neural network is a complex and nonlinear one and it is very difficult to correlate weights and words in a text. We employ Gated Convolutional Neural Network (GCNN) and introduce a self-attention mechanism to understand how GCNN determines sentiment polarities from raw reviews. GCNN can simulate an n-gram model and the self-attention mechanism can make correspondence between weights of a neural network and words clear. In experiments, we used Amazon reviews and evaluated the performance of the proposed method. Especially, the proposed method was able to emphasize some words in the review to determine sentiment polarity. Moreover, when the prediction was wrong, we were able to understand why the proposed method made mistakes because we found what words the proposed method emphasized.

Cloud computing is defined as a model to access shared computing resources through network in a manner which is ubiquitous, on demand, requires less time for provision and release of resources and requires minimum intervention of management authorities. With such flexibility there arise two problems of data privacy and data security which are open research problem. The first problem of privacy says that how a user's data can be stored such that only authorized persons gets access to it. The problem of security demands the security of data in such a manner that not only on storage but also in between transition of data on network the data will be useless for intruders. In this paper we address both of the problems simultaneously. Specifically, we present a model for privacy and security such that the security is provided by encrypting the data at the owner end and then putting it on the cloud while the privacy is provided by a secured key exchange between the owner and the user. Our model is such that the data remains in the encrypted form throughout the cloud, including network access and hence there is no chance of its misuse.

In this paper, we propose a new, robust near-optimal mutual information combined zero-forcing per-group precoding (ZF-PGP) method for finite alphabets with imperfect channel state information (CSI) at the receiver. ZF-PGP achieves very high gains over ZF precoding techniques, while it simultaneously offers individually separate streams to reach individual user equipment (UE), i.e., it obliterates the need for coordinated, joint decoding by the group's UEs. The proposed robust ZF-PGP scheme comprises an inner linear beamformer (BF), which relies on second-order CSI and is based on the massive MIMO-based joint division and multiplexing for finite alphabets (JSDM-FA) to form orthogonal user groups, and an outer linear precoder that relies on instantaneous group CSI to form a per-group precoding within groups (PGP-WG) with separate data streams to each user. As we show by multiple examples, for a uniform linear array (ULA), the proposed ZF-PGP technique is very efficient, near-optimal design with reduced complexity at the UEs. Due to JSDM-FA second-order CSI inner beamforming, the groups are easily identified. We also demonstrate the robustness of the proposed precoding techniques to channel estimation errors, showing minimal performance loss.

If the eye movement of a driver who makes a long drive during the day and at night can be measured with less stress to the driver in order to estimate the following items for a long time with high accuracy, it is expected that the information will make a great contribution to safe driving: 1) What the driver is looking at or paying attention to (i.e. gaze), 2) A feeling or sign of unwellness such as dizziness, car sickness, and discomfort (i.e. rotational eye movement). In this study, the authors propose an approach in which an area of high intensity gradients in the white part of the eye, i.e. an area that includes a blood vessel with a distinctive shape, is automatically selected to estimate the gaze and calculate the angle of eye rotation, so that the target ocular blood vessel can be tracked with high accuracy even if blood vessels in the white part of the eye differ considerably between individuals in terms of shape, length, and thickness. An evaluation experiment yielded excellent results under various lighting conditions. Especially, extremely positive results were obtained for the estimation accuracy of rotational eye movement, with an estimation error of -0.69° ± 1.02° (mean and standard deviation).

This paper presents a comment on the article titled "Radial Dependence of Induced Current Density and Small Pixel Effect in Parallel-Plate Detectors". The study used Monte Carlo methods and conformal mapping to investigate the radial dependence of induced current density and small pixel effect in parallel-plate detectors. The authors suggest that the convergence of the Monte Carlo simulations does not appear to have been adequately addressed. Furthermore, the use of Green's function methods to solve electric potential problems in electrostatics is highlighted. Overall, this paper provides valuable commentary on important aspects of the original research on parallel-plate detectors.

Surgical gesture recognition is a crucial aspect of robotic surgery. In this paper, we propose a time delay neural network (TDNN) based approach for surgical gesture recognition using kinematic data. The kinematics of surgical instruments such as needles and other instruments were analyzed to extract relevant features. These features were then used to train the TDNN model for gesture recognition. Training data was collected using a robotic surgical system and was used to validate the accuracy of the proposed approach. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in recognizing surgical gestures. The proposed approach has the potential to improve surgical outcomes, reduce errors, and enhance patient safety. The proposed method can also be used in other areas requiring gesture recognition such as the gaming and automotive industries.

Cloud computing has been a significant breakthrough technology in large scale data storage and computation over a decade. However, due to advancement in mobile devices along with other technologies such as Internet of Things (IOT), Augmented Reality (AR), there is a need for real-time responses and reduce delays generated over WAN. Thus concepts of Edge computing such as Fog computing and Mobile Edge computing has evolved in order to bridge a gap between cloud and the consumer devices. This paper gives an overview of MEC in 5G, a brief comparison with Fog Computing and about various aspects and deployment scenarios.

This paper presents an optimized input approach for the CNN-based hyperspectral image classification problem, which leverages the Spatial Transformer Network (STN) to adaptively transform the input features. The proposed method, termed STN-Optimized Input (STNOI), is evaluated on several benchmark hyperspectral datasets, and compared against other state-of-the-art approaches. The feature extraction process is enhanced by introducing the STN module, which learns to identify the most informative spectral and spatial features, and adjust them for the classification task. The STNOI approach also improves the training process by minimizing the computational overhead and avoiding overfitting problems. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through extensive experimental results, showing significant improvements in classification accuracy and faster convergence rate. The success of the STNOI method confirms the importance of exploiting both spectral and spatial information for hyperspectral imaging applications. The work contributes to the growing body of research in convolutional neural networks (CNN) and deep learning techniques for task analysis in remote sensing.

Self-suspending behavior in real-time embedded systems can have a major and non-trivial negative impact on timing predictability. In this work, we investigate how to analyze the schedulability of segmented self-suspending task systems under a fixed-priority assignment. For this purpose, we introduce the multi-segment workload function as well as the maximum workload function in order to quantify the maximum interference from the higher-priority tasks when constructing our (sufficient) schedulability test. Moreover, we derive an optimal priority assignment with respect to our schedulability test since it is compatible with Audsley's Optimal Priority Assignment (OPA). We show by means of comprehensive evaluations that our approach is highly effective concerning the number of schedulable task sets. Furthermore, one set of results reveals a rather non-intuitive observation, namely, that the worst-case suspension time of a computation segment should also be respected to improve the schedulability even if the suspension may finish earlier.

The total delivered power of an MRI radio frequency (RF) coil is an important parameter for MRI safety control. For a 2-channel MRI coil, this parameter is not only dependent on the excitation strength on each channel, but also dependent on the object loading inside the coil. The purpose of this investigation is to propose a fast method to assess the total delivered power of a 2-channel MRI RF coil. Four hundred and ninety simulations for a high-resolution anatomical model were performed to validate this method. Among these simulations, ten random excitation-pairs of the 2-channel coil and forty-nine patient landmarks ranging between -200 to 1000 mm were considered. It is proved that this fast estimation method can calculate the total delivered power of a 2-channel RF coil with any excitation pairs by only two simulations and its relative error is less than 1.5%.

Considerable effort has been expended on the design of control systems for wave energy converters (WECs) over the past two decades. Working from the fundamental requirement of impedance matching, a variety of conceptual and practical algorithms have emerged, which bring various levels of realism to the original complex conjugate ideal, facilitating maximum power transfer. Simplifications can be introduced, such as passive control and causal control, while some enhanced algorithms allow physical constraints to be observed, nonlinear model dynamics to be articulated, or nonideal power takeoff systems to be recognized. However, in general, model-based WEC control systems are evaluated in tandem with identical simulation models, while the sensitivity of controller performance to modeling errors is ignored. In addition, the WEC model utilized by the controller rarely, if ever, fully represents the nonlinear nature of the true WEC dynamics. This paper articulates this model sensitivity issue for different WEC control system architectures and shows that it is of potentially greater impact than for traditional regulation/servomechanism control problems. Recommendations are given on the best WEC control architecture to adopt from a sensitivity/robustness perspective.

The exoskeleton robot in the rapid development requires physical relation interpretation about scene understanding to fulfill effective interaction. Although traditional scene understanding provides good performance of object recognition and semantic segmentation, it tells us little about physical relation interpretation. Meanwhile, there are few methods to demonstrate the contextual relations among objects in the scene. While some of them artificially define prior constrains and solve the equation by minimizing the objective function, others aim at perceiving the stability of 3D blocks to classify the support relation to several classes. In this paper, a novel approach is proposed which can automatically get the prior knowledge based on deep learning and Conditional Random Fields(CRF) to infer support relationship. In addition, unlike all of previous methods applying the post-processing step after segmenting or recognizing objects, our method is based on end-to-end deep network which could be trained by back-propagation algorithm. The support relationship can be directly obtained as the output from a RGB picture input through our approach, where no other intermediate steps are needed. We show the effectiveness of the proposed method on the NYU-Depth V2 dataset in which we manually re-annotate 1449 images.

Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have been employed in rehabilitation training for post-stroke patients. In this study, we present the results of the intervention based on BCI triggered functional electrical stimulation (FES) and avatar mirroring. Seven chronic stroke patients participated in 25 sessions of training over 13 weeks. Seven assessments were conducted to observe any behavioral changes before and after the intervention. The primary outcome measure, i.e. the Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), increased significantly by 6.4 points (p=0.048), which is above the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). The Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), one of the secondary outcome measures, reduced significantly in both the wrist and the finger (p=0.046 and p=0.047 respectively). This study demonstrated motor function improvement and spasticity reduction in chronic stroke patients (n=7) after BCI triggered FES and avatar mirroring. One limitation of this study is that the small sample size may not adequately represent the diverse stroke population. Further work should include a randomized controlled trial to investigate the effectiveness of BCI triggered FES compared to conventional therapies.

This paper explores the sphere of applications related to computer architecture, natural language processing, software, software architecture, linguistics, syntactics, and semantics. With the advancement of technology, computer architecture has seen significant improvements in recent years, leading to more efficient processing and better performance. The field of natural language processing has gained much attention in recent years, with software programs being developed to understand human language, aiding in the creation of better interfaces and user experiences. Software architecture, on the other hand, has become essential to the development of modern software, ensuring that it is reliable, scalable, and maintainable. Linguistics, in its application to computational linguistics, has helped in analyzing and understanding human language through the use of computers, resulting in successful natural language processing. Syntactics and semantics have also played a crucial role in the improvement of natural language processing, with syntactics handling the structure of language and semantics handling its meaning. This paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of these applications, indicating that a better understanding of them will lead to further advancement in technology.

Lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP) waveforms associated with lightning strikes to the 634-m high Tokyo Skytree are calculated by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method in the two-dimensional (2-D) cylindrical coordinate. The three-dimensional (3-D) tortuous lightning channel and the tall strike object are represented by an “equivalent vertical” phased-current-source array. The current propagation speed along the equivalent vertical lighting channel is determined in two steps: first, the channel is projected on a plane including the strike object and a field observation point, and then it is converted into the straight vertical channel right above the strike object. Thus, the height-dependent lightning-current propagation speed along the equivalent channel depends on the direction of the observation point. The proposed method greatly reduces computational resources required for calculating LEMPs without deteriorating accuracy since it allows the use of the 2-D FDTD method. LEMP waveforms measured at a horizontal distance of 27, 57, and 101 km (in different directions) from the strike object are accurately reproduced by the proposed method. The results clarified that the lower region of the tortuous lightning has a large influence on the wavefront of the LEMPs at a horizontal distance ranging from 20 to 100 km from the strike point.

The field of biomedical imaging involves the acquisition and analysis of a vast amount of images, which can be computationally intensive and difficult to process. Complexity theory is an important concept when it comes to addressing this issue, as it allows us to quantify and analyze the inherent complexity of these images. In order to efficiently handle these images, methods such as image coding and compression are commonly used. This paper proposes a network compression method for biomedical image segmentation called CC-NET, which utilizes image complexity as a guiding factor to determine which portions of the network should be compressed. By using this approach, the authors found that they were able to reduce the size of the network while retaining accuracy in segmenting biomedical images. In addition to reducing the computational demands of biomedical image segmentation, this method also has the potential to improve the training and generalization of these algorithms. Overall, the authors demonstrate the viability of using complexity-guided network compression for biomedical image segmentation, which can help to reduce degradation and improve efficiency in this important field.

Software reliability is a critical aspect of software engineering, with numerous predictive models and algorithms developed to estimate and predict software reliability. This paper proposes a hybrid algorithm that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm to estimate model parameters and predict software reliability. The proposed algorithm is a combination of the strengths of both PSO and ABC, providing more accurate and efficient solutions. The study evaluates the proposed algorithm using real-world datasets for software reliability prediction, and the results show that it outperforms traditional algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm and Ant Colony Optimization. The proposed algorithm can help software engineers to quickly and accurately estimate and predict software reliability, thus improving software quality and reducing costs associated with software testing and maintenance. Overall, the study highlights the importance of using hybrid algorithms for software reliability prediction and provides a useful approach for software engineers to improve software reliability.

Internet of Things (IoT) deployments expand as IoT security lags. This article surveys IoT security protocols standardized by the Internet Engineering Task Force and discusses remaining gaps. Although these standardized IoT security protocols do not completely secure IoT devices, they go a long way.

Localization of nodes is a pivotal requirement in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). This paper proposes a localization method based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) measurements by using multiple mobile anchor nodes in MPR. The proposed method incorporates noise measurements and position measurements along with Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. The approach involves the use of a mathematical model comprising of Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), to estimate the positions of unknown nodes. The method has been tested on a real-world dataset, and the results showcase its promising accuracy in localization. The proposed method is beneficial for applications where the availability of GPS signals is scarce, and high accuracy of localization is critical. The method's superiority in terms of the performance demonstrates the potential of the proposed method for future research in WSNs applications.

Neural network decoding algorithms are recently introduced by Nachmani et al. to decode high-density parity-check (HDPC) codes. In contrast with iterative decoding algorithms such as sum-product or min-sum algorithms in which the weight of each edge is set to 1, in the neural network decoding algorithms, the weight of every edge depends on its impact in the transmitted codeword. In this paper, we provide a novel feed-forward neural network lattice decoding algorithm suitable to decode lattices constructed based on Construction A, whose underlying codes have HDPC matrices. We first establish the concept of feed-forward neural network for HDPC codes and improve their decoding algorithms compared to Nachmani et al. We then apply our proposed decoder for a Construction A lattice with HDPC underlying code, for which the well-known iterative decoding algorithms show poor performances. The main advantage of our proposed algorithm is that instead of assigning and training weights for all edges, which turns out to be time-consuming especially for high-density parity-check matrices, we concentrate on edges which are present in most of 4-cycles and removing them gives a girth -6 Tanner graph. This approach, by slight modifications using updated LLRs instead of initial ones, simultaneously accelerates the training process and improves the error performance of our proposed decoding algorithm.

The overall localization error performance for a sensor network employing quantized received signal strength (RSS) measurements largely depends on the number of bits used and their distribution. In this paper, we consider a rate-constrained bit allocation problem in which multiple points of interest (PoIs) are assigned possibly non-uniform error requirements. The main objective is to allocate a number of bits in order to satisfy error requirements as best as possible in a squared error sense. Due to the computational complexity of optimally solving the allocation problem, two novel low complexity allocation algorithms are proposed. The main idea behind these algorithms is to relate localization errors to corresponding bit density requirements. In the first algorithm, bit allocation is formulated as a sequential constrained convex optimization problem which can be solved with efficiency using available convex solvers. The second algorithm is a greedy version of the first algorithm in which sensors are selected for allocation based on the bit density differences at their neighboring PoIs. Numerical experiments show the efficacy of the proposed algorithms in comparison to other available algorithms in terms of overall error, coverage, and computational complexity.

This paper proposes a method for estimating the Remaining Useful Lifetime (RUL) of equipment based on degradation, using a combination of random failure threshold and measurement error. The authors discuss the impact of measurement errors on RUL estimation and suggest that the use of Bayesian methods can account for these errors. They point out that the degradation of equipment can follow a Gaussian distribution, and examine the use of current measurement data to estimate the RUL of manganese-based equipment. The paper presents a case study to demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, and conclude that the proposed method can accurately estimate RUL even in the presence of measurement errors. Overall, this paper contributes to the development of reliable methods for RUL estimation, which can help with maintenance and the efficient use of resources.

The lack of data interoperability is hindering the emergence of Open Science and making data analytics considerably more expensive than it should be. A new technology, FAIR Digital Objects, is seeking to solve this problem along with several others. FAIR is an acronym for findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable. Digital Object Architecture is a very general virtual layer to ride on top of any data system, which can solve the interoperability problem for heterogeneous data, much as the Internet solved the interoperability problem for heterogeneous networks. A specific project employing these technology will be described.

In this study, a circuit technique and training algorithm that minimizes the effect of stuck-at-faults (SAFs) within a memristor crossbar array of neural networks (NNs) are presented. To improve the network performance in the presence of SAFs, a conventional transimpedance amplifier, which is used for summing the currents that flow through the memristors, is modified to ensure that the amplifier output is within the appropriate operating range. Further improvement in the network performance is achieved by using the proposed training algorithm, which utilizes the locations and values of faulty memristors for network training. A feedforward NN employing 32×32 memristor crossbar arrays is implemented to verify the performance improvement in the NNs using the proposed circuit technique and training algorithm.

Quadrotor real-time trajectory planning is a challenging problem due to the complex dynamics of the quadrotor system and the requirement of real-time responses. This paper proposes a novel Matrix Structure Driven Interior Point Method for Quadrotor Real-Time Trajectory Planning. The proposed approach formulates the trajectory planning problem as a convex optimization problem with linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) constraints. In particular, the proposed method exploits the specific structure of the LMIs constraints and employs a matrix structure driven interior point algorithm to solve the problem efficiently. The convergence of the proposed algorithm is analyzed theoretically, and it is shown to converge to the optimal solution within a finite number of iterations. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated through simulations and experiments, and compared with existing trajectory planning methods. The results show that the proposed method can generate optimal trajectories for quadrotor real-time systems with a high level of accuracy and computational efficiency. This work contributes to the advancement of real-time trajectory planning for quadrotors, and also provides a general framework for trajectory planning and programming based on convex functions.

This paper presents a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) based high-level control architecture that uses deep learning technique to realize autonomous picking control of a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) manipulator using the visual information only. The proposed manipulator control system uses a stereo camera as a measurement device to capture a stereo image of the scene in front of the robot. Then, the proposed CNN-based picking controller uses the captured stereo image as an input to predict the optimal picking control command of the manipulator directly. In the collection of the training dataset, we controlled the manipulator to pick up the object-of-interest (OOI) manually and recorded the stereo images and the corresponding control commands. In the CNN training phase, the supervised end-to-end learning technique is used to learn the mapping between the stereo image observation and the picking control commands of the 6-DoF manipulator. Experimental results show that the proposed end-to-end visual picking control system achieves an average of 70% and 60% success rate in the random single-object and multi-object picking task, respectively.

Performing the correct pen-holding gesture plays an important role in handwriting efficiency and quality, especially for early education. In this paper, we present the design, implementation and evaluation of SmartWriting, which utilizes the smartwatch for pen-holding gesture recognition for both Chinese and English writing. SmartWriting can automatically identify whether the user is writing Chinese or English, based on which two classifiers are built to detect pen-holding gestures by strokes in Chinese characters or English letters. In particular, we propose to leverage the combined signal of one vertical stroke and one horizontal stroke for efficient pen-holding gesture identification in Chinese writing, and we are able to infer pen-holding gesture according to any letter in English writing. We build a fully functional prototype of SmartWriting, and extensive experiments confirm its effectiveness and robustness. The detection accuracy is 9. % and 9 % for Chinese and English respectively. SmartWriting provides a natural, convenient and inexpensive way to improve users' writing habits.

Electromyography (EMG) can be used as an input signal for Human-Computer Interfaces, which are used in the disabled community. Typically, both the user-condition and the end-goal application dictate the number and locations of EMG sensors. We developed two cursor control methods intended for high-level spinal cord injury patients, where available muscle sites are limited to the head and neck areas. For patient comfort, it is desirable to minimize the number of sensors and their intrusiveness while maximizing the functionality of the control method. Both our control methods use a single, noninvasive, surface, differential EMG sensor at the temporalis muscle that controls a cursor in two degrees of freedom (DOF). Fourteen inexperienced able-bodied subjects completed a Fitts’s law task-based cursor-to-target paradigm using both control methods ("auto-rotate" and "manual rotate"). Subjects evaluated and compared performance between the two control methods, which both enabled the cursor to move in 2-DOF. They differed in the level of user control, where one allowed direction manipulation in 1-DOF and 2-DOF in the other. Subjects also completed pre- and post-session surveys and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Task Load Index for workload assessment. In general, subjects’ performance improved with subsequent sessions within each control method. Subjects achieved a higher throughput (better performance) in the auto-rotate method, had lower workload scores, and tended to prefer this control method. However, about half the subjects felt the manual rotate method allowed them more control over cursor behavior. Our results suggest that a viable cursor control method can be achieved with only a single muscle site.

Ship detection is a critical task in the field of marine surveillance and can be accomplished through airborne radar systems. In this study, an automatic CFAR ship detection approach is proposed for single-channel range-compressed airborne radar data. The clutter in marine environments make it challenging to accurately detect ships, especially in complex scenarios like littoral regions. To overcome this challenge, the proposed approach utilizes a computational modeling approach to exploit the Doppler effect, which is sensitive to the movement of marine vehicles. A training data set is created with samples of marine vehicles and clutter so that the approach can learn to distinguish between the two. The azimuth of the radar is used to determine the location of the detected ship. The proposed approach shows promising results in the detection of ships in ocean environments, achieving high accuracy while reducing false alarms.

In this paper, we revisit the problem of classifying ships (maritime vessels) detected from overhead imagery. Despite the last decade of research on this very important and pertinent problem, it remains largely unsolved. One of the major issues with the detection and classification of ships and other objects in the maritime domain is the lack of substantial ground truth data needed to train state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms. We address this issue by building a large (200k) synthetic image dataset using the Unity gaming engine and 3D ship models. We demonstrate that with the use of synthetic data, classification performance increases dramatically, particularly when there are very few annotated images used in training.

COSFIRE filters are an effective means for detecting and localizing visual patterns. In contrast to a convolutional neural network (CNN), such a filter can be configured by presenting a single training example and it can be applied on images of any size. The main limitation of COSFIRE filters so far was the use of only Gabor and DoGs contributing filters for the configuration of a COSFIRE filter. In this paper, we propose to use a much broader class of contributing filters, namely filters defined by intermediate CNN representations. We apply our proposed method on the MNIST data set, on the butterfly data set, and on a garden data set for place recognition, obtaining accuracies of 99.49%, 96.57%, and 89.84%, respectively. Our method outperforms a CNN-baseline method in which the full CNN representation at a certain layer is used as input to an SVM classifier. It also outperforms traditional non-CNN methods for the studied applications. In the case of place recognition, our method outperforms NetVLAD when only one reference image is used per scene and the two methods perform similarly when many reference images are used.

This paper discusses the design of a cognitive engine for spectrum situational awareness and signals intelligence. This engine utilizes machine learning algorithms to process real-time data from multiple sources, including radar and radio frequency signals. By analyzing and interpreting this information, the engine is able to make informed decisions about optimal frequency usage and allocation. The use of cognitive radio technology in the design enables efficient and dynamic spectrum utilization.
