This paper proposes a novel method for estimating heart rate from photoplethysmographic signals with motion artifacts using Fourier-sparse dual optimization. The proposed method takes into account the effects of motion artifacts on the signal processing algorithms and utilizes acceleration data from sensors to compensate for these effects. The algorithm relies on the Fourier series representation of the PPG signal and utilizes the sparsity of the signal spectrum to achieve reliable heart rate estimation even under high motion conditions. The proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and can be used for real-time monitoring of heart rate in various biomedical monitoring applications.

This paper proposes a sparse direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method for directive coprime arrays. The complex radiation patterns are extracted using an electromagnetic simulator and then incorporated in the DOA estimation. Three DOA algorithms are compared including Capon, MUSIC, and Lasso based on compressive sensing (CS). It is shown that when the DOA increases in the elevation plane, the performance degrades faster when using real antenna patterns.

Personal Process Management (PPM) systems provide solutions for individuals to effectively manage their own personal processes for improved productivity and performance. This reference model outlines the key components of a successful PPM system, including planning, monitoring, and decision support. The model recommends the use of task analysis and context modeling to create a comprehensive understanding of the individual's processes and the environment in which they operate. Additionally, the model highlights the importance of information systems for organizing and tracking process data, and the use of decision support systems for optimizing process outcomes. The reference model is applicable to a variety of domains and can be tailored to the specific needs of the individual or organization. Using natural gas as an example, this paper demonstrates how the reference model can be applied in practice to improve personal process management and ultimately achieve better overall performance.

In this paper, an improved minor component analysis (IMCA) algorithm based on convergence analysis of 5G multi-dimensional signals is proposed for 5G mobile communication. The proposed IMCA algorithm relies on heuristic algorithms and biological neural networks to enhance the convergence rate of the algorithm. By exploiting the correlation information of multi-dimensional signals, the proposed algorithm can effectively separate the minor component signals. The convergence analysis of the algorithm is conducted to demonstrate the fast convergence rate and robustness of the proposed algorithm. The research in this paper provides an innovative solution to the problem of multi-dimensional signal separation in 5G mobile communication, which has important implications for the development of STEM fields.

Recent studies in decision neuroscience revealed that two different strategies guide trial-by-trial choice behavior during reinforcement learning (RL): a goal-directed strategy and a habitual learning strategy. An increasing number of studies have provided evidence for neural substrates underlying respective strategies, suggesting that a single RL algorithm cannot make accurate predictions about individual choices. Despite rapid progress in predicting humans intentions such as movements or choices, there has been no attempt to read out human learning strategies. We proposed a novel brain-computer interface (BCI) framework for decoding human learning strategies from electroencephalography (EEG) data. To circumvent the issue that there is no gold standard for labeling learning strategies, we trained the proposed framework classifier to best match predictions of the computational model of the neural process underlying human learning strategies. The simulation used a 1D, 2D, and 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) on 18 subjects; the EEG data demonstrated that the proposed framework successfully read out human learning strategies with very high accuracy (98.4%). Subsequently, we examined whether those learning strategies labeled from the computational model exhibited distinctive EEG patterns. We used class activation mapping (CAM) for visualization, and we identified distinctive strategy-dependent patterns in the EEG feature space. We argue that the proposed framework has great potential for decoding high-level cognitive states.

The method to estimate joint motion quickly and accurately from surface electromyogram (sEMG) has been explored by many researchers. However, the effect of different grabbing loads is ignored by most of them, which limits its clinical and daily applicability. In order to eliminate this effect in the course of motion estimation, an Adaboost-AF method based on Adaboost regression was proposed to identify the load information and estimate motion intention. This method is composed of three parts: the sEMG preprocessing part, the load identification part, and the motion intention estimation part. The average value of sEMG feature signal, which is obtained during sEMG preprocessing part, was used to identify the load information. Five features, root mean square (rms), waveform length, difference absolute standard deviation value, the integral signal of sEMG (IEMG), and low-pass filtered signal of sEMG (LPFEMG) similar to sEMG envelope were explored whether the average value of features signal can be used to identify the load under different speeds. After the load was identified, the Adaboost regression framework with the decision tree as the weak learner was applied to be the motion intention estimation part. Experimental results showed that the average rms difference between an actual angle and estimated angle by using the Adaboost-AF method was 0.1193 ± 0.0148, and the average execution time for a section of data with 17.58 s was 0.3932 ± 0.0610s. (Scikit-learn packet was adopted, and the version number was V0.21. The running software was Spyder, Python3.6.) This paper shows that the method based on the average value of sEMG feature signals can eliminate the influence of different loads without adding new sensors; IEMG and LPFEMG from the biceps brachii muscle show the optimal loads identification performance; the proposed Adaboost-AF method takes the influence of different loads into account and ensures the rapid and accurate estimation performance of motion intention.

The simulation modeling of transport flows of copper deposit plays a significant role in optimizing transportation efficiency and improving the overall profit of copper production. This paper develops a mathematical model for load modeling of various ores, specifically copper, and proposes a computational modeling framework for simulating the transportation process. The model takes into account the loading, unloading, and transportation of copper deposits and aims to minimize the overall transportation cost while ensuring timely delivery of the ore to processing plants. The proposed model is verified using real-world data and the simulation results demonstrate its potential in improving copper transportation efficiency. The loading process is found to be a crucial factor in the transportation performance, and thus, the model recommends rigorous maintenance of loading equipment as a measure to improve overall efficiency. The proposed model can be extended to other types of bulk materials transportation and can potentially serve as a tool for decision making in copper production management.

This paper aims to investigate the device variability of Wafer-Scale TaOx and its implications for neuromorphic computing applications. The study focuses on analyzing the table lookup, standards, and task analysis for neuromorphics, which are key components in developing nonvolatile memory and training neural networks. The issue of device variability is particularly important in the context of performance evaluation, as it affects the accuracy and efficiency of neuromorphic systems. The authors present their findings on the variability of TaOx devices, and highlight the challenges and opportunities that arise in designing reliable neuromorphic systems. The results suggest that further research is needed to address the variability issue, and to develop robust methods for performance evaluation of TaOx-based neuromorphic systems.

This paper focuses on security features for proximity verification, especially in the context of wireless fidelity networks and meters. With the increasing popularity of wireless communication and the omnipresence of advanced technological devices, security concerns have become more urgent than ever. Proximity verification is a critical piece in ensuring secure communication and data exchange. In this paper, we explore the use of various technologies such as relays, global positioning system, feature extraction, and Bluetooth to enhance the security of proximity verification. We analyze the benefits and drawbacks of these technologies and provide recommendations on the most effective combination of security features for proximity verification in various scenarios. Our findings highlight the importance of a comprehensive and multilayered approach to security that takes into account the unique challenges posed by different environments and use cases.

This work proposes a new method to accurately complete sparse LiDAR maps guided by RGB images. For autonomous vehicles and robotics the use of LiDAR is indispensable in order to achieve precise depth predictions. A multitude of applications depend on the awareness of their surroundings, and use depth cues to reason and react accordingly. On the one hand, monocular depth prediction methods fail to generate absolute and precise depth maps. On the other hand, stereoscopic approaches are still significantly outperformed by LiDAR based approaches. The goal of the depth completion task is to generate dense depth predictions from sparse and irregular point clouds which are mapped to a 2D plane. We propose a new framework which extracts both global and local information in order to produce proper depth maps. We argue that simple depth completion does not require a deep network. However, we additionally propose a fusion method with RGB guidance from a monocular camera in order to leverage object information and to correct mistakes in the sparse input. This improves the accuracy significantly. Moreover, confidence masks are exploited in order to take into account the uncertainty in the depth predictions from each modality. This fusion method outperforms the state-of-the-art and ranks first on the KITTI depth completion benchmark [21]. Our code with visualizations is available at https://github.com/wvangansbeke/Sparse-Depth-Completion.

In recent years, the opportunistic routing (OR) paradigm has been shown as one of the most viable solutions at the network layer for efficient data delivery under the nosily underwater acoustic channel. Since then, several OR protocols for underwater sensor networks, with major and minor variations, were proposed in the literature. While the performance of these protocols, in terms of data delivery rate, delay, and energy consumption, has been extensively studied in the literature, there is a lack of studies devoted for the evaluation of the topological properties OR will incur. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of the candidate set selection procedures of opportunistic routing protocols designed for underwater sensor networks. We discuss the principles that have been extensively considered for the design of OR protocols for underwater sensor networks. Moreover, we conduct a simulation-based performance evaluation to study topological properties (e.g., number of hops, number of paths and number of candidates), which will impact the performance of underwater wireless sensor network applications.

Machine learning methods have achieved good performance and been widely applied in various real-world applications. They can learn the model adaptively and be better fit for special requirements of different tasks. Generally, a good machine learning system is composed of plentiful training data, a good model training process, and an accurate inference. Many factors can affect the performance of the machine learning process, among which the diversity of the machine learning process is an important one. The diversity can help each procedure to guarantee a totally good machine learning: diversity of the training data ensures that the training data can provide more discriminative information for the model, diversity of the learned model (diversity in parameters of each model or diversity among different base models) makes each parameter/model capture unique or complement information and the diversity in inference can provide multiple choices each of which corresponds to a specific plausible local optimal result. Even though diversity plays an important role in the machine learning process, there is no systematical analysis of the diversification in the machine learning system. In this paper, we systematically summarize the methods to make data diversification, model diversification, and inference diversification in the machine learning process. In addition, the typical applications where the diversity technology improved the machine learning performance have been surveyed including the remote sensing imaging tasks, machine translation, camera relocalization, image segmentation, object detection, topic modeling, and others. Finally, we discuss some challenges of the diversity technology in machine learning and point out some directions in future work. Our analysis provides a deeper understanding of the diversity technology in machine learning tasks and hence can help design and learn more effective models for real-world applications.

The consumer Internet of Things (IoT) platforms are gaining high popularity. However, due to the open nature of wireless communications, smart home platforms are facing many new challenges, especially in the aspect of security and privacy. In this article, we first introduce the architecture of current popular smart home platforms and elaborate the functions of each component. Then we discuss the security and privacy challenges arising from these platforms and review the state of the art of the proposed countermeasures. We give a comprehensive survey on several new attacks on the voice interface of smart home platforms, which aim to gain unauthorized access and execute over-privileged behaviors to compromise the user's privacy. To thwart these attacks, we propose a novel voice liveness detection system, which analyzes the wireless signals generated by IoT devices and the received voice samples to perform user authentication. We implement a real-world testbed on Samsung's SmartThings platform to evaluate the performance of the proposed system, and demonstrate its effectiveness.

Many slip-ring induction motor (SRIM) models are found in the literature. In this paper, new extended state-space slip-ring induction motor models are developed using reference frame theory. All these SRIM models are investigated regarding their diagnostic relevance to rotor turn-to-turn short-circuit fault. Ability to generate distinct residuals is important for any model-based fault diagnostics. The performance of these models in term of their capability to detect a fault is compared and best-suited models are recommended based on discriminatory ability index presented in this paper. Analytical computations are carried out for a 4- hp four-pole slip-ring induction motor using MATLAB software. Simulation results are presented to illustrate and validate the proposed index.

This paper proposes a novel approach to modeling walking behavior of powered exoskeletons using complex-valued neural networks. Wearable robots have seen increasing interest as they can aid in human mobility and provide therapeutic benefits for those with mobility impairments. However, creating a walking gait that is both natural and efficient remains a challenge. Inspired by biological neural networks in the legged locomotion of animals, the proposed method applies complex-valued neurons to model the motor outputs needed for walking. Moreover, the model integrates temperature sensors to adapt to environmental changes and enhance the performance of the exoskeleton. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model in simulating human-like walking behavior in powered exoskeletons. This research opens up a promising avenue for further developments in wearable robotics using complex-valued neural networks.

In biomedical imaging, accurate image segmentation is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, traditional methods often suffer from a high Hausdorff Distance, which measures the maximum distance between two sets of points, and a lack of sensitivity in capturing fine details. In this paper, we propose a solution using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to reduce the Hausdorff Distance in medical image segmentation. By training the CNNs on large datasets of annotated images, we show that our method outperforms traditional approaches and achieves higher accuracy in segmenting two dimensional displays. We also examine the effectiveness of various transforms, such as rotations and translations, in improving sensitivity and reducing the Hausdorff Distance. Our results demonstrate the potential of CNNs as a powerful tool for improving image segmentation in biomedical imaging, and suggest future research directions in exploring their full capabilities.

The explosive growth in the number of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has led to an increased demand for cellular networks to support this technology. In Africa, where the proliferation of smart cities is becoming increasingly common, there is a need for reliable and efficient cellular networks. This paper proposes a mathematical model to estimate cellular IoT capacity in African smart cities using Long Term Evolution (LTE) and 3G mobile communication technologies. The model takes into consideration factors such as the number of poles and towers needed for network coverage, signal strength, and interference. The results of the model are then used to determine the optimal configuration for cellular IoT networks in African smart cities. The findings show that efficient IoT network capacity can be achieved through a combination of 3G and LTE technologies and appropriate placement of poles and towers. This study contributes to the development of cellular IoT networks in Africa, paving the way for the growth of smart cities and promoting the use of IoT for social and economic development in the region.

Increasing longevity remains one of the open challenges for Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery technology. We envision a health-conscious advanced battery management system, which implements monitoring and control algorithms that increase battery lifetime while maintaining performance. For such algorithms, real-time battery capacity estimates are crucial. In this paper, we present an online capacity estimation scheme for Li-ion batteries. The key novelty lies in: 1) leveraging thermal dynamics to estimate battery capacity and 2) developing a hierarchical estimation algorithm with provable convergence properties. The algorithm consists of two stages working in cascade. The first stage estimates battery core temperature and heat generation based on a two-state thermal model, and the second stage receives the core temperature and heat generation estimation to estimate state-of-charge and capacity. Results from numerical simulations and experimental data illustrate the performance of the proposed capacity estimation scheme.

This paper proposes a new process algebra with qualitative calculus that is well-suited for modeling spatio-temporal behavior in various fields including aerospace electronics, real-time systems, and autonomous systems. The algebra includes a new calculus that allows for the representation of qualitative information, such as the relationship between two temperature sensors. The algebra can be used to create computational models for these systems, increasing their efficiency and accuracy. In addition, the algebra is designed to work in real-time, making it a valuable tool for modeling time-dependent systems. The proposed process algebra with qualitative calculus is a promising approach for modeling spatio-temporal behavior and has a wide range of potential applications.

Recently, the deployment and usage of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to monitor and track a geographical region have been increased exponentially. The network infrastructure designed to deploy UAVs consists of sensors, actuators, and other communication smart devices for data collection and processing. As security and privacy is one of the challenging tasks in such an environment, so to design an efficient and secure data dissemination scheme is a challenging task due to limited storage and computation power of UAVs. To mitigate various attacks in such an environment, several efficient signature schemes were proposed in the literature. However, none of these schemes work well due to high computation and communication costs. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a short proxy signature (CB-PS) scheme in certificate-based setting. Due to implicit usage of certificates, CB-PS solves inherent key escrow of ID-based designated verifier proxy signature. It also eliminates the necessity of secret key distribution in ID-based schemes. The proposed CB-PS scheme is adaptively unforgeable in a random oracle model. It is also efficient with respect to both signature length and computational complexity. The comparison of computational costs reveals that the proposed scheme consumes the least cost 15.45 ms in comparison to the costs of existing competitive schemes.

Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) are widely used for various applications in oceanography and other underwater domains. Routing protocol is one of the key aspects to ensure the reliable communication in UASNs. In this paper, a novel distance-vector-based opportunistic routing protocol (DVOR) is proposed for UASNs, which leverages peer-to-peer computing and the characteristics of underwater acoustics to improve the routing efficiency. The DVOR protocol dynamically selects the relay nodes based on their distance and connectivity, in order to minimize the end-to-end delay and maximize the network lifetime. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DVOR protocol outperforms existing routing protocols in terms of packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay and energy consumption. This research provides a feasible solution for improving the routing efficiency and constructing a reliable Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure in UASNs.

In the field of microfluidics, the droplet generation process is essential for various applications such as inkjet printing, drug delivery, and biosensing. In this paper, a BP neural network-based model is proposed to predict the ejection state of a pneumatic valve-controlled micro-droplet generator. The system is composed of reservoirs, valves, solenoids, generators, and monitoring equipment to measure the droplet size and ejection frequency. The BP neural network model is trained on the experimental data obtained from the droplet generator system. The results show that the proposed BP neural network model can accurately predict the ejection state of the micro-droplet generator with a high degree of accuracy. This approach can be useful for optimizing the design and control of micro-droplet generators for various applications such as printing, drug delivery, and biological sensing.

This paper proposes the fusion of body sensors' data and video images as an innovative approach in assistive technology for senior citizens. The feature extraction process enables the acquisition and analysis of critical physiological and environmental data from wearable sensors and image sensors, respectively. The utilization of artificial intelligence in this process allows for accurate and efficient analysis of the collected data, enabling effective monitoring of the senior citizens' activities and health. Additionally, sensor fusion technology transforms the data into useful information and actionable insights, providing valuable feedback and assistance to the senior citizens for a better quality of life. The combination of body sensors and video images creates a holistic approach to assistive technology, allowing for comprehensive and personalized support based on individual needs and requirements. Ultimately, the proposed fusion of body sensors' data and video images presents an innovative and effective solution to the growing needs of senior citizens, promoting greater independence and well-being.

This paper is concerned with the model predictive control (MPC) for Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems under the event-triggered mechanism. First, in order to make a rational and effective utilization of the communication resources, the event-triggered mechanism is employed in the network from the controller to the actuator. Second, a “min-max” optimization is put forward to dealing with the MPC problem for systems in the context of T-S fuzzy nonlinearities, and an online auxiliary optimization problem is constructed to obtain sub-optimal feedback gains. Third, by fully taking the influence of the event-triggered mechanism and the T-S fuzzy nonlinearities into consideration, some sufficient conditions are provided to guarantee the input-to-state stability (ISS) for the underlying system. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the robust MPC-based controller for the closed-loop system under the event-triggered mechanism.

One main challenge in tunnel constructions is to predict the tunnel geological conditions without excavation to ensure safety during the construction process. This paper proposes a data-driven framework for real-time interpreting the operating data of tunnel boring machines (TBMs) without interrupting tunneling operations, and eventually automate the tunneling operation. In this framework, we first convert the indexes of the original data from discontinuous operating time to continuous operating displacement. After screening outliers, to more exhaustively explore the inherent characteristics of the TBM operating data, we then augment features by using the first-order and the second-order difference information. There are two main concerns for developing a desired geological-type predictor: 1) since multiple geological types could coexist in one tunnel section, the predictor should have multiple outputs and 2) since the geological types are specified by the values of 7 kinds of physical-mechanical indexes of geological types, this geological characteristic should also be encoded into the predictor's structure. Therefore, we design a feed-forward multiple-output artificial neural network (ANN) with two hidden layers as the predictor, where the second hidden layer has 7 nodes that correspond to 7 kinds of physical-mechanical indexes. The experimental results show that: 1) the feature augmentation (FA) method indeed improves the prediction performance; 2) the ANN predictor has the best performance on the test set when the second hidden layer has 7 nodes; 3) the proposed ANN predictor outperforms many widely-used learning models, e.g., XGboost, random forest (RF), and support vector regression (SVR); and 4) the predictor is capable of accurately predicting the geological types of stratum.

An adaptive sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) damping controller using Kalman filters are proposed for AC/DC hybrid system with high penetration wind in this paper. First, the supplementary damping coordinated controller of DFIG and HVDC are designed using multiple input multiple output LMIs. Then the adaptive method using Kalman online estimations for tracking the operating points caused by the variable wind power output. The AC/DC hybrid system integration with wind power generation is used as test system. The characteristic of variable SSR modes with wind power outputs is investigated, and the simulation results demonstrated that the adaptive SSR damping control method could not only track the operating condition, but also could give robust and effective control in the case of large fluctuation of wind power output.

Acetabulum fractures are common orthopedic injuries that can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed and treated promptly. X-ray imaging is the most widely used diagnostic tool for detecting these fractures, but the process can be complicated by the presence of noise in the images. To overcome this challenge, processing methods that are focused on noisy images are needed. In this study, support vector machines were used to enhance the accuracy of classification for detecting acetabulum fractures. X-ray imaging data was analyzed using histograms and adaptive equalizers to improve feature extraction. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was evaluated using real-world patient data and the results showed promising outcomes for accurate detection of acetabulum fractures. The proposed approach can be used as an effective diagnostic tool in clinical practice, providing physicians with a reliable means of identifying this type of injury in patients.

In this brief, heterogeneity and noise in big data are shown to increase the generalization error for a traditional learning regime utilized for deep neural networks (deep NNs). To reduce this error, while overcoming the issue of vanishing gradients, a direct error-driven learning (EDL) scheme is proposed. First, to reduce the impact of heterogeneity and data noise, the concept of a neighborhood is introduced. Using this neighborhood, an approximation of generalization error is obtained and an overall error, comprised of learning and the approximate generalization errors, is defined. A novel NN weight-tuning law is obtained through a layer-wise performance measure enabling the direct use of overall error for learning. Additional constraints are introduced into the layer-wise performance measure to guide and improve the learning process in the presence of noisy dimensions. The proposed direct EDL scheme effectively addresses the issue of heterogeneity and noise while mitigating vanishing gradients and noisy dimensions. A comprehensive simulation study is presented where the proposed approach is shown to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem while improving generalization by 6%.

Keywords provide a short way of reflecting a main idea of the document, making it easier for the readers in reading. Extracting keyword is the main task in natural language processing. Since it is not only time consuming but also requires lots of efforts to extract the keywords manually, it arises the need for the automated approaches. This paper has proposed a solution for the automatic keyword extraction in Vietnamese language using hybrid deep learning approaches. Every existing deep learning approach has its own advantages; and the hybrid deep learning model we are introducing is the combination of the superior features of CNN and LSTM models. The proposed model shows enhanced accuracy and f1-score over another approach.

The development of brain-controlled vehicles (BCVs) has spurred interest in accurately predicting driver intentions through electroencephalography (EEG) analysis. This paper proposes a universal prediction model for emergency braking intention based on EEG signals. The proposed model is based on convolutional neural networks and uses feature extraction techniques such as band-pass filters. By capturing the features of EEG signals that indicate emergency braking intention, the model achieved a high level of accuracy in predicting this intention across different individuals. Experimental results showed that the proposed model outperformed the state-of-the-art models in predicting emergency braking intention. The findings of the study shed light on the development of BCVs with enhanced safety features that can interpret driver intentions in real-time. The study also provides new insights into the use of machine learning techniques for analyzing EEG signals and may be useful in other fields requiring EEG-based prediction models.

This paper provides a brief review of data visualization techniques applied to maritime traffic, with a focus on trajectory visualization of marine vehicles. The study examines various visualization approaches, including meteorological information, artificial intelligence, and kernel density estimation. The use of data visualization is crucial for marine traffic management, as it allows for easy identification of patterns and trends. It enhances the interpretation of complex and large data sets, facilitating decision-making processes. The paper concludes that data visualization techniques applied to maritime traffic provide considerable value to improve the safety and efficiency of commercial and public ocean transportation.

Narrative reports in medical records contain abundant clinical information that may be converted into structured data for managing patient information and predicting trends in diseases. Though various rule-based and machine-learning methods are available in electronic medical records (EMRs), a few works have explored the hybrid methods in extracting information from the Chinese EMRs. In this paper, we developed a novel hybrid approach which integrates the rules and bidirectional long short-term memory with a conditional random field layer (BiLSTM-CRF) model to extract clinical entities and attributes. A corpus of 1509 electronic notes (discharge summaries and operation notes) was annotated. Annotation from three clinicians was reconciled to form a gold standard dataset. The performance of our method was assessed by calculating the precision, recall, and F-measure for two boundary matching strategies. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in clinical information extraction from the Chinese EMRs.

This paper presents a torque tracking impedance control strategy for a lower limb rehabilitation robot (LLRR) with three joints, hip, knee and ankle. The strategy allows the human-robot system to track a desired interaction torque. To track the desired torque, the robot reference trajectory and actuator torque are designed properly based on the torque tracking impedance control. A constant torque tracking experiment performed on a healthy male subject has shown that the maximum normalized root mean square deviation (NRMSD) of each joint is less than 32%. It indicates that the control strategy is feasible and the LLRR is capable of providing stroke patients with active rehabilitation training.

The development and verification of a design and simulation system for a digital reactor fluid instruction control system, focusing on inductors, fluids, control systems, instruments, analytical models, tools, and computational modeling is presented. The system aims to address the challenges faced in the design and simulation of complex fluid instruction control systems in the nuclear industry. This paper explores the integration of analytical models and computational modeling to improve the design of the system, presenting methodology and tools used in the verification process. Through systematic testing of the model and verification of the results, the proposed system has demonstrated the capability to provide reliable and robust control of inductors, fluids and other instruments in the digital reactor fluid instruction control system. The integration of analytical models and computational modeling in the design and simulation of digital reactor fluid instruction control system is therefore an effective approach towards improving the overall efficiency, safety, and reliability of nuclear power generation systems.

In this paper, we present a false alarm reduction algorithm for Ventricular Tachycardia (VT) arrhythmias in intensive care unit (ICU) using multivariate statistical process control (MSPC) and frequency analysis of electrocardiogram (ECG) signal. First, we decompose the ECG signal into three different frequency bands. The ECG beats are detected, and VT beats are labeled. In the next step, several features consist of time domain features, bispectrum features, and Poincaré plot features are extracted from ECG Signal The extracted feature vector of each ECG beat is monitored using MSPC for detecting anomalies. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using the Ventricular Tachycardia cases of 2015 Physionet challenge database. This dataset consists of 2 ECG channel, arterial blood pressure (ABP) and/or photoplethysmograph (PPG) signal, and an alarm annotation for each record. The obtained sensitivity and specificity were 86.5%, and 80.7% respectively. We have also investigated the advantage of using ABP signal in improving the results of false alarm reduction. For this purpose, some biological features are extracted from ABP and used as an extra feature vector. Results show that using ABP signal can improve the performance of the algorithm.

This paper presents a study on the edge blurring phenomenon in microdefect inspection using high-frequency ultrasound imaging. The image edge detection through probes was investigated both experimentally and computationally. A computational model was developed to simulate the acoustic propagation and transducer response in the inspection process. The model was validated against experimental results and used to investigate the effect of various factors on the edge blurring phenomenon. It was found that the edge blurring is mainly caused by diffraction of the ultrasound wave at the edges of the sample. The study provides important insights into the mechanisms of the edge blurring phenomenon and offers potential strategies to mitigate it. The findings are significant for the advancement of ultrasonic imaging techniques in microdefect inspection.

This study investigates the problem of adaptive decentralized tracking control for a class of interconnected nonlinear systems with input quantization, unknown function, and time-delay, where the time-delay and interconnection terms are supposed to be bounded by some completely unknown functions. An adaptive decentralized tracking controller is constructed via the backstepping method and neural network technique, where a sliding-mode differentiator is presented to estimate the derivative of the virtual control law and reduce the complexity of the control scheme. On the basis of Lyapunov analysis scheme and graph theory, all the signals of the closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, an application example of an inverted pendulum system is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed methods.

This paper discusses the early experiences of depth estimation on intricate objects using generative adversarial networks (GANs). GANs are a type of deep learning model that is composed of two parts, the generator and the discriminator. The generator creates synthetic data that is similar to the real data, while the discriminator tries to distinguish between the synthetic data and the real data. In this research, the authors explore the use of GANs for estimating depth on intricate objects, specifically gallium nitride (GaN) crystals. The team trained the network using various techniques such as data augmentation, dropout, and batch normalization. They used multiple cameras to capture the images of the objects and displayed them in three dimensions to evaluate the performance. The study shows that GANs have the potential to estimate the depth of intricate objects accurately, but more research is required to optimize the training and generator networks.

Strong correlation of link gains over multiple wavelengths has been demonstrated in non-line-of-sight optical wireless scattering communication. In this paper, we further demonstrate that the channel impulse responses for different wavelengths are also strongly correlated. Thus, a novel channel estimation method based on such correlation over multiple wavelengths is proposed, where only certain reference wavelengths are assigned pilot signal. On each channel with assigned pilot signal, we adopt an improved least-squares channel estimation method to estimate the tap parameters and the tap length (or the number of taps). The channel tap coefficients on other wavelengths can be estimated based on the correlation. Under the proposed channel estimation, the channel estimation accuracy can be improved as shown by the simulations. Moreover, under the same total channel estimation overhead, the accuracy of the proposed channel estimation first increases and then decreases with the number of reference wavelengths.

This paper explores the hydrodynamics of advanced-hull surface vehicles using a mathematical model developed through computational modeling. The focus is on the interaction between fluids and the sea surface, particularly in the presence of surface waves. The dynamics of these vehicles are analyzed and studied, with a particular emphasis on how they interact with the surrounding environment. The color of the vehicle's surface is also considered, as it can impact the hydrodynamics and contribute to the overall performance of the vessel. By examining these factors, this paper provides valuable insights into the design and development of advanced-hull surface vehicles.

Cloud robotics is incessantly gaining ground, especially with the rapid expansion of wireless networks and Internet resources. In particular, computation offloading is emerging as a new trend, enabling robots with more powerful computation resources. It helps them to overcome the hardware and software limitations by leveraging parallel computing capabilities and the availability of large amounts of resources in the cloud. However, the performance gain of computation offloading in cloud robotics is still an ongoing research problem because of the conflicting factors that affect the performance. In this paper, we investigate this issue and we design a distributed cloud robotic architecture for computation offloading based on Kafka middleware as messaging broker. We experimentally validated our solution and tested its performance using image processing algorithms. Experimental results show a significant reduction in robot CPU load, as expected, with an increase in robot communication delays.

Code cloning is a well-known technique in software engineering where small portions of source code are duplicated and used in more than one location within a software system. The prevalence of code clones can result in large-scale integration issues, increased development and maintenance time and can ultimately lead to the decay of software. In order to address these issues, benchmark testing is essential for evaluating the efficacy of code clone detection tools. BigCloneBench is a software clone detection tool which uses an extensive collection of clones to benchmark detection algorithms. This paper investigates the vector-based detection of code clones using BigCloneBench. The study explores the effectiveness of different vector transformations in terms of time measurement and information retrieval quality. The use of neural networks in combination with vector-based detection is also examined. The results of this study contribute to a better understanding of the usefulness of vector-based detection techniques for code clone detection, which can enable software engineers to maintain the quality of software systems with fewer duplication issues.

Data integrity is a critical issue in cloud computing, as sensitive information is frequently stored remotely in a cloud. Cryptography provides a promising solution for ensuring data integrity, and the use of probabilistic logic and hash functions can add an extra layer of protection. However, ensuring computational efficiency is essential, particularly for critical infrastructure that must function in real time. Accumulator-based schemes have emerged as a potential solution to this problem, as they allow for efficient verification of data integrity without compromising computational efficiency. In this paper, we propose a cryptographic accumulator-based scheme for critical data integrity verification in cloud storage. We demonstrate that our scheme significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining the level of security necessary to protect sensitive information in critical infrastructure. Our research has important implications for enhancing the security and integrity of data stored in the cloud, as it provides a practical and efficient solution to the challenges posed by cloud computing and cryptography.

Distribution system state estimation (DSSE) has recently been tested and experimentally deployed in some practical distribution networks. Distinct features of distribution systems, such as diverse and unsymmetrical configurations as well as limited real-time measurements, prohibit the direct application of mature state estimation methods for transmission systems. Targeting at three-phase four-conductor configured unsymmetrical medium-voltage distribution systems (MDS) with neutral conductors and ground resistances, this paper proposes a weighted least square-based DSSE approach, in which voltages are chosen as state variables and load pseudo measurements of low-voltage distribution systems (LDS) are considered to compensate insufficient real-time measurements in MDS. Both rectangular and polar coordinates are studied, and voltage variables of neutrals and zero-injection phases are eliminated to reduce the scale of the DSSE problem. Moreover, in order to enhance the load pseudo measurement accuracy of LDSs, a clustering and partial least square regression-based load estimation model is proposed to leverage the real-time communication ability of smart meters. Case studies on a modified IEEE 123-bus distribution system with actual smart meter data illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

This paper presents comparative experiments conducted on the Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technique in indoor environments. The study focuses on the estimation accuracy and efficiency of the MHE-based SLAM technique for wheelchair users. The paper explores the application of the MHE-based SLAM algorithm on wheelchairs to improve their localization and mapping capabilities. A comprehensive analysis of the estimation accuracy of the MHE-based SLAM algorithm is conducted by comparing it with two other state-of-the-art algorithms. The experiments also investigate the effects of varying time measurements and wheel designs on the measurement uncertainty of the MHE-based SLAM algorithm. The results highlight the MHE-based SLAM algorithm's superiority in terms of estimation accuracy and computational efficiency, making it an excellent candidate for real-world applications.

Virtual reassembly of fractured bones has become a popular method in orthopedic surgery due to the advantages it provides in terms of accuracy and patient outcomes. This technique involves utilizing biomedical imaging, such as computed tomography, to generate 3D models of the fractured bone. These models are then reconstructed using solid modeling and feature extraction to accurately locate and align the individual pieces of bone. Computational modeling is then used to simulate the screw placement and alignment of the reconstructed bone. Overall, virtual reassembly offers a more precise and efficient approach to orthopedic surgeries, resulting in improved patient outcomes and reduced risk of complications. The use of advanced imaging and modeling technologies has greatly improved the accuracy and success rates of this technique, making it a valuable tool in the field of orthopedic surgery.

The prospects of achieving a trillion connected internet of things (IoT) devices by 2020 has created the urgency for effective intrusion detection systems (IDS) for these devices. Although it has been argued that the most effective technique used in such systems is anomaly detection, there exist no mechanisms to determine their performance in real-life deployment. In this paper, we report the results of applying asymptotic analysis to evaluate the performance of an anomaly detection algorithm which is designed using logic reasoning through fuzzy logic methodologies. In order to achieve this, the IDS was included as part of intrusion detection software for ZigBee Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). In particular, the solution is targeted to address the ZigBee protocol's vulnerability to flood attacks during node discovery and association to the network. The intrusion detection software is hosted external to the WSNs in pursue of a light solution mindful of resource preservation in sensor nodes.

The quality of speaker recognition highly depends on the feature extraction step that is used prior to the training stage. In this paper, a novel feature extraction algorithm is proposed which utilizes Discrete Wavelet Transforms (DWT) and Temporal Statistical Techniques for Word Dependent Speaker’s Recognition. The proposed method first employs DWT to break down the speech signal into several sub-bands, which are then analyzed independently for feature extraction. Furthermore, temporal statistical techniques such as mean and standard deviation are utilized to extract additional discriminative features. The extracted features are then utilized in the training phase of the speaker recognition system, where the Euclidean distance metric is used for measuring the similarity between the training and testing samples. The proposed method is evaluated on a speaker recognition dataset and the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art feature extraction methods in terms of recognition accuracy. Overall, the proposed algorithm offers a more efficient and accurate framework for speaker recognition applications, and can be utilized for a wide range of applications including reactive power monitoring and speech recognition.

This paper investigates the problem of task scheduling and bit rate allocation for multimedia big data in cloud computing environments. Given the characteristics of big data, efficient job scheduling frameworks such as data mining and job shop scheduling are explored. In addition, the optimal bit rate allocation for streaming media is studied to increase the quality of service for end users. The proposed approach leverages the power of cloud computing by providing scalability and elasticity in processing and storage capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves performance over traditional scheduling and bit rate allocation methods, and is suitable for handling the challenges of big data in the context of multimedia applications. This work provides valuable insights into the efficient deployment and management of cloud-based multimedia big data systems.

Threat modeling, a structured process for identifying risks and developing mitigation strategies, has never been systematically evaluated in a real environment. Our case study at the New York City Cyber Command—the primary digital defense organization for the most populous city in the United States—found tangible benefits.

This paper proposes a time-varying non-singular terminal sliding mode attitude control strategy for space vehicles. The main focus is on achieving convergence of attitude states towards the desired state in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances. Materials requirements planning is taken into account in the design of the control law. The sliding mode control approach is utilized to ensure robustness against model uncertainties and external disturbances. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control strategy in achieving rapid and accurate attitude control of space vehicles.

This paper focuses on distributed orchestration in cloud data centers, with a particular emphasis on resource management in the context of servers and data centers. The authors explore the use of Markov processes to model the behavior of cloud computing systems, and propose an optimization framework that utilizes these models to improve resource allocation and utilization. They also present a mathematical model that captures the cost and performance trade-offs associated with different orchestration strategies. Overall, the paper highlights the importance of efficient orchestration in cloud data centers, and provides a framework for optimizing resource management through the use of mathematical models and Markov processes.

Half of Indonesian population living in rural area. So that, the development of the rural area is very crucial. Along with technological advances, the Internet of Things(IoT) devices have been increasingly used by numerous parties, including the use of IoT for the growth of rural areas. This study follows PRISMA protocol to explores the various uses of the field area, IoT devices, and technology in rural areas in diverse works of literature systematically including consideration during implementation, then reviewed their implication for potential adoption in rural areas of Indonesia. This study recommends that the agriculture field should be prioritized to implement IoT because it is feasible than healthcare. Besides stakeholder support in infrastructure, user education also becomes challenge consideration of implementing IoT in rural areas.

The adaptive moment estimation algorithm Adam (Kingma and Ba) is a popular optimizer in the training of deep neural networks. However, Reddi et al. have recently shown that the convergence proof of Adam is problematic, and they have also proposed a variant of Adam called AMSGrad as a fix. In this paper, we show that the convergence proof of AMSGrad is also problematic. Concretely, the problem in the convergence proof of AMSGrad is in handling the hyper-parameters, treating them as equal while they are not. This is also the neglected issue in the convergence proof of Adam. We provide an explicit counter-example of a simple convex optimization setting to show this neglected issue. Depending on manipulating the hyper-parameters, we present various fixes for this issue. We provide a new convergence proof for AMSGrad as the first fix. We also propose a new version of AMSGrad called AdamX as another fix. Our experiments on the benchmark dataset also support our theoretical results.

This paper presents a configurable data acquisition system designed for various working conditions. The system is capable of acquiring data from different types of sensors and performing task analysis in real-time. The data collected by the system can be stored in a database located on physical servers or in the cloud. The system utilizes wireless fidelity technology to transmit data from the sensors to the servers. The system is designed to be configurable and can be customized to suit the specific needs of different applications. The system can be used in a variety of applications such as environmental monitoring, industrial control, and medical diagnosis. This paper describes the system's architecture and presents the results of an experimental evaluation of the system's performance. In conclusion, the proposed data acquisition system is an effective solution for acquiring data in various working conditions, and it has the potential to be widely adopted in various fields.

This paper proposes a novel approach of using deep weighted feature descriptors for lip reading of Kannada language. The Lips and Shape are utilized as primary features for extraction with a focus on improving accuracy. Training of the deep models is done with large datasets to ensure effectiveness. Additionally, visualization techniques are applied for a better understanding of the deep learning process. The proposed methodology also considers the role of the Face and Mouth in lip reading, ultimately leading to a more accurate and reliable system. Overall, this research presents a promising approach to lip reading of Kannada language, which has potential applications in various fields including speech therapy and security systems.

Plug-and-play priors (PnP) is a powerful framework for regularizing imaging inverse problems by using advanced denoisers within an iterative algorithm. Recent experimental evidence suggests that PnP algorithms achieve the state-of-the-art performance in a range of imaging applications. In this paper, we introduce a new online PnP algorithm based on the proximal gradient method (PGM). The proposed algorithm uses only a subset of measurements at every iteration, which makes it scalable to very large datasets. We present a new theoretical convergence analysis, for both batch and online variants of PnP-PGM, for denoisers that do not necessarily correspond to proximal operators. We also present simulations illustrating the applicability of the algorithm to image reconstruction in diffraction tomography. The results in this paper have the potential to expand the applicability of the PnP framework to very large datasets.

Intelligent friction compensation has been an important area of research in the field of motion control for several decades. Friction is a major challenge in motion control systems as it often leads to non-linear effects and unpredictable behavior. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current state-of-the-art in intelligent friction compensation research. The review covers various topics including friction modeling, force control, computational modeling, adaptation models, and adaptive systems. The paper also discusses the applications of friction compensation in motion control systems, such as robotics, manufacturing, and aerospace. The review highlights several adaptive techniques that have been developed to compensate for friction and improve the performance of motion control systems. Furthermore, the paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of intelligent friction compensation and possible future research directions. Overall, the review provides valuable insights into the latest developments in intelligent friction compensation and its potential impact on motion control systems.

Efficient group proof of storage is an important issue in cloud computing, which aims to ensure the data integrity of cloud storage systems. In this paper, we proposed a novel approach for efficient group proof of storage with malicious-member distinction and revocation. Our approach enables servers to verify data integrity with reduced communication overhead by utilizing metadata for resists. The proposed scheme can also distinguish malicious members and revoke them accordingly, thereby enhancing the security of the cloud storage system. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches and is efficient and secure. The proposed approach is significant for the computer science community as it provides an effective solution for secure and efficient group proof of storage in cloud computing.

This paper presents a novel approach for vision-based hand gesture recognition using 3D shape context. This technique is particularly useful for three-dimensional displays and involves the extraction of shape features for gesture recognition. The proposed method utilizes sensors and data mining techniques to allow for accurate feature extraction. Moreover, heuristic algorithms are employed to facilitate the recognition process. Overall, our approach demonstrates significant promise as a means of improving the accuracy and efficiency of hand gesture recognition in a variety of applications.

Marine navigation has always been a challenging task for robotics due to the complex and constantly changing environments found in the oceans. In order to effectively navigate through these environments, robots must possess a deep understanding of the dynamics of the ocean and its spatiotemporal phenomena. In this paper, we propose a novel learning approach for marine robotic navigation that trains robots on partially structured environmental dynamics. By incorporating knowledge of vehicle dynamics and decision making, our method allows robots to adapt to changing and uncertain environments, resulting in improved navigation performance. Through experiments in real-world ocean environments, we demonstrate the efficacy of our method for learning and navigating through complex marine environments. Overall, our approach provides a promising avenue for improving the accuracy and reliability of marine robotic navigation systems.

This paper proposes an optimal design of validation experiments based on the area metric factor and fuzzy expert system. The measurement and predictive models are used to evaluate the performance of a computational modeling process. The capability maturity model is applied to assess the maturity level of the modeling process. The expert systems are utilized to provide expert knowledge for the modeling process. A mathematical model is developed to analyze the uncertainties in the modeling process. By combining these methods, an optimal design of validation experiments is proposed to improve the accuracy and reliability of the modeling process. The proposed method can provide a systematic approach for designing validation experiments, and enhance the robustness of the computational modeling process. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reduce the uncertainty and ensure the accuracy of the modeling process.

This paper presents a novel flow estimation approach that assimilates distributed pressure measurements of autonomous underwater robots through coalescing recursive Bayesian estimation and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-based flow model reduction. The proposed flow estimation approach does not rely on any analytical flow models and is thus applicable to many and various complicated flow fields for arbitrarily shaped underwater robots while most of the existing flow estimation methods apply only to those with simple and well-defined shapes. Neural network is further used to establish the relationship between the POD flow model and the flow parameters of interest, e.g., the angle of attack and flow-relative velocity. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed distributed flow estimation approach, two simulation studies, one with a circular-shaped robot and one with a Joukowski-foil-shaped robot, are presented.

The Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) is a concept that combines the power of robotics, sensing systems and the Internet of Things (IoT) to revolutionize how we interact with intelligent machines. The integration of these technologies has the potential to drive intelligent robotics of the future, transforming industries such as manufacturing, healthcare and transportation. 

The architecture of IoRT involves the use of robot sensing systems, enabling robots to gather and process data from their surroundings. This data is then transmitted to the cloud using IoT technologies, where it can be analyzed and used to improve robot performance. In addition to sensing systems, the kinematics of robots is also vital to the success of IoRT, as robots must be able to move and manipulate objects with precision and efficiency. 

Cloud computing plays a crucial role in IoRT, as it allows for large amounts of data to be stored, analyzed and processed in real-time. The use of cloud computing also enables robots to collaborate with each other, sharing data and insights to enhance their performance. 

The computer architecture of IoRT is designed to handle the complex and varied demands of intelligent robotics. It requires powerful processors and advanced algorithms to process the vast amounts of data generated by robot sensing systems and IoT devices. 

Overall, the integration of robotic sensing systems, the IoT, cloud computing and advanced computer architecture is driving the intelligent robotics of the future, with limitless potential for applications across a wide range of industries.

The latest evolution of cellular technologies, i.e., 5G including long term evolution-advanced (LTE-A) Pro and 5G new radio promises enhancement to mobile technologies for the Internet of Things (IoT). Despite 5G's vision to cater to IoT, yet some of the aspects are still optimized for human-to-human (H2H) communication. More specifically, the existing group paging mechanism in LTE-A Pro has not yet clearly defined approaches to group, mobile IoT devices (MIDs) having diverse characteristics, such as discontinuous reception (DRX) and data transmission frequency (DTF) with various mobility patterns. Inappropriate grouping of MIDs may lead to increased energy consumption and degraded quality of service, especially in terms of packet arrival delay (PAD) and packet loss rate (PLR). Therefore, in this paper, we devise novel models to estimate PAD, PLR, and energy consumption for MIDs, specifically for the group paging mechanism. Based on the proposed models, we formulate an optimization problem with the objective to minimize energy consumption of MIDs, while providing required PAD and PLR. The nonlinear convex optimization problem addressed herein is solved using the Lagrangian approach, and the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions have been applied to derive optimal characteristics for MIDs to join the group, namely, DRX and DTF. The extensive numerical results presented verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, and the mathematical models demonstrate the superiority of our proposed approach over random grouping approach concerning significant energy consumption of MIDs.

Crowd counting has been a task of great concern for computer vision researchers in recent years due to its wide range of applications in various fields. In this paper, we propose a novel approach named SMCA-CNN for robust crowd counting. Our approach combines the power of semantic mask and cross-scale adaptive feature extraction techniques to minimize the interference caused by scene complexity, occlusion, and other environmental factors that affect the crowd estimation. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority over existing methods. The adaptable kernel feature analysis in computer architecture was also applied in our research, which provided a more accurate analysis of the crowd density. Our research offers exciting avenues for further task analysis and advances in the field of crowd counting.

Wireless-powered mobile edge computing (MEC) networks with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) have attracted increasing attention in recent years. This study focuses on improving the computation efficiency of such networks. Firstly, a task analysis is performed to identify the optimal resource allocation scheme. Then, computational modeling is used to optimize the resource management strategy at the edge servers. Furthermore, frequency modulation is employed to enhance the signal transmission quality and enable more efficient energy harvesting. Nominal computing resources are allocated to each user, with the excess resources dynamically allocated based on the demands of their tasks. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme significantly improves computation efficiency and reduces the overall energy consumption of the system. Overall, this work provides important insights into the design of efficient wireless-powered MEC networks using NOMA.

In the era of Internet of Things (IoT), the increasing number of time-sensitive requests poses challenges for cloud computing systems due to the unpredictable delays caused by the network transmission and heavy computational modelling. This paper proposes a mathematical model for optimizing the processing time of time-sensitive IoT requests by utilizing edge computing architecture. The proposed model takes into account the delays associated with data transmission, computation and communication among different computing nodes. By incorporating the optimization algorithm, the model is able to reduce the processing time and enhance the overall system performance. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, extensive experiments have been conducted, and the results have shown that the proposed optimization model outperforms the traditional cloud computing models in terms of processing time and computational efficiency. This paper demonstrates the importance of considering the edge computing architecture and optimization algorithm in the design of cloud computing systems for handling time-sensitive IoT requests.

The model identification problem for asymptotically stable linear time invariant systems is considered. The system output is affected by an additive noise with unknown bound, and a finite set of data is available for parameter estimation. The goal is to derive a model with guaranteed simulation error bounds for all predicted time steps, up to a finite horizon of choice. This is achieved in three steps. At first, the noise bound, system order, and impulse response decay rate are estimated from data. Then, the estimated quantities are used to refine the sets of all possible multi-step predictors compatible with data and prior assumptions (Feasible Parameter Sets, FPSs). The FPSs allow one to derive, in a Set Membership framework, guaranteed error bounds for any given multi-step predictor, including the one obtained by simulating the system model. Finally, the wanted model parameters are identified by numerical optimization, imposing the constraints provided by the FPSs and using one of two proposed optimality criteria. Numerical simulations illustrate the validity of the approach.

In this paper, we present a Minimum Sample Quasi Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MS-QMLE) for frequency estimation with applications in signal processing. The MS-QMLE approach is based on the principles of maximum likelihood estimation, which involves finding the parameter values that maximize the likelihood of the data given the model. In particular, we focus on the problem of estimating the frequency of a signal in the presence of noise, which is an important problem in many fields. We consider both cases of additive noise and frequency modulation, and show that the MS-QMLE approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Additionally, we investigate the use of interpolation techniques to improve the performance of the estimator. Finally, we present simulation results to validate the effectiveness of the MS-QMLE approach. Overall, our results demonstrate that the MS-QMLE approach is a promising method for frequency estimation in signal processing applications.

In view of person re-identification (re-ID) as a retrieval process, re-ranking is a crucial step to improve its performance. In the re-ID research, limited effort has been devoted to re-ranking, especially when it comes to fully automatic, unsupervised solutions. In this paper, we propose enhanced expanded cross-neighborhood based Re_ranking with Synchronized ReID in which global features are extracted which are mutually learned with local features and then re ranked to improve performance. Enhanced ECN greatly improves the person retrieval method. Global feature learning greatly took advantage from local feature learning, which performs a synchronization/alignment without requiring extra monitoring by calculating the shortest path between two sets of local features. After the joint learning, we only match the global feature to measure the similarities between images and effective re ranking is applied in the test set to greatly improve the performance of the ReID system.

This paper presents a novel approach for the determination of True-Speed-Over-Ground for trains. The approach utilizes the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) technique. Several focus metrics are evaluated and tested. The tests were carried out in an laboratory environment. The results are compared to an alternative correlation-based approach.

As the demand for machine learning (ML) applications continues to rise, it becomes increasingly important to establish optimal cache behavior for graphics processing units (GPUs) that support parallel processing. Benchmark testing has been conducted on various architectures in order to better understand cache behavior and determine the most efficient use of cache. Matrices are a common data structure in ML, and their characteristics have been evaluated in order to develop effective caching strategies. The power demand of the GPU must also be taken into account, as the cache size can have a significant impact on power consumption. By analyzing cache behavior in the context of parallel processing and power consumption, researchers are able to optimize computer architecture for ML applications, resulting in improved performance and efficiency.

Battery power detection has always been the core of the battery management system of electric vehicles, and the fast and accurate estimation of charged state can guarantee the safe operation of electric vehicles. This article is based on the electric car with iron phosphate lithium-ion battery PNGV model to complete the estimate of the lithium ion battery SOC, using Matlab Simulink module and simulation of the model. And it proves that PNGV model had higher precision. This system uses the extended kalman filter algorithm to estimate the charge state (SOC) of lithium battery and give the concrete implementation steps. Experimental simulation show that using the extended kalman filtering algorithm can rapidly estimate the charged state of lithium-ion batteries, the maximum error is about 4%, the average error is around 2%, can satisfy the accuracy of the battery management system needs.

This paper proposes a methodology for improving the accuracy of Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA) based positioning in a LoRaWAN environment using machine learning techniques. The proposed approach involves the use of logic gates and mobile nodes to obtain accurate time measurements, which are then used to train a neural network. This neural network is deployed in base stations and network servers, which are responsible for predicting the location of mobile nodes based on TDoA measurements. The results show that the proposed method improves the accuracy of TDoA based positioning in a LoRaWAN environment compared to traditional methods. The use of machine learning techniques in TDoA based positioning provides a more precise and reliable approach for location tracking. The proposed approach has important applications in industrial settings, smart city deployments, and other emerging IoT applications where accurate location tracking is crucial.

Early childhood is a significant period when transitions take place in children. This period is a hot topic among researchers who pursue this domain across different scientific disciplines. Many studies addressed social, scientific, medical, and technical topics during early childhood. Researchers also utilized different analysis measures to conduct experiments on the different types of data related to the early childhood to produce research articles. This paper aims to review and analyze the literature related to early childhood in addition to the data analyses and the types of data used. The factors that were considered to boost the understanding of contextual aspects in the published studies related to early childhood were considered as open challenges, motivations, and recommendations of researchers who aimed to advance the study in this area of science. We systematically searched articles on topics related to early childhood, the data analysis approaches used, and the types of data applied. The search was conducted on five major databases, namely, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed from 2013 to September 2017. These indices were considered sufficiently extensive and reliable to cover our field of the literature. Articles were selected on the basis of our inclusion and exclusion criteria (n = 233). The first portion of studies (n = 103/233) focused on the different aspects related to the development of children in early age. They discussed different topics, such as the body growth development of children, psychology, skills, and other related topics that overlap between two or more of the previous topics or do not fall into any of the categories but are still under development. The second portion of studies (n = 107/233) focused on different aspects associated with health in early childhood. A number of topics were discussed in this regard, such as those related to family health, medical procedures, interventions, and risk that address the health-related aspects, in addition to other related topics that overlap between two or more of the previous topics or do not fall into any of the categories but are still under health. The remaining studies (n = 23/233) were categorized to the other main category because they overlap between the previous two major categories, namely, development and health, or they do not fall into any of the previous main categories. Early childhood is a sensitive period in every child's life. This period was studied using different means of data analysis and with the aid of different data types to produce different findings from the previous studies. Research areas on early childhood vary, but they are equally significant. This paper emphasizes the current standpoint and opportunities for research in this area and boosts additional efforts toward the understanding of this research field.

With the change of epoch, the standard of male attractiveness is also changing. Analyzing the trend of facial features changes over time in different environments can reveal the influence of social development on facial attractiveness. In this paper, we propose a method to analyze the trend of facial features of Chinese male. First, a face database with Chinese male of different times is established and rated by raters of different ages. Second, the machine learning method is used to rate face images of different times for verifying the change of male aesthetic. Then, the retrained Inception v3 model is used to realize facial shape classification. After that, the change trend of face shape is analyzed by using massive data. Finally, the change characteristics of the eyebrow are analyzed by calculating the geometric parameters of the eyebrow model, including the area, length, and average width of the eyebrow. Compared with other researches on facial attractiveness, the proposed method can deeply understand the guiding trend of popular culture on facial attractiveness in different times.

This paper proposes a Q-Learning algorithm for joint computation offloading and resource allocation in edge cloud. The proposed algorithm aims to optimize the resource management in edge cloud computing by maximizing the performance of mobile handsets while minimizing the energy consumption. Specifically, the algorithm is designed to identify the optimal allocation of tasks to servers in the edge cloud based on the analysis of the tasks' characteristics.
