The paper utilizes computational modeling to simulate various scenarios and evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. The results have demonstrated that the Q-Learning algorithm is effective in improving the overall performance and energy efficiency of edge cloud computing. This research contributes to the advancement of cloud computing and computer architecture by providing a novel approach for resource management in edge cloud computing.

Green product design aims to improve the environmental and social quality of products and has been recognized as one of the main issues in sustainable operations. This research proposes an incentive-based bi-level joint model to optimize the green product line design in order to deal with the trade-off underlying the profit and carbon emission based on the interactive relationship in a two-tier supply chain. A case study involving one manufacturer and one supplier is developed to test the proposed optimization model. A comparison between the non-incentive-based bi-level model and the incentive-based bi-level model is presented. It is found that the developed incentive-based joint optimization model can achieve a relatively better optimal solution to minimize the amount of carbon emission and maximize the product line profit.

Electrical modeling of vehicular antennas is required for design of modern vehicle-to-everything communication networks. However, full-wave modeling and the existing equivalent source methods still ask for long computation time. To address this issue, a fast simulation method is proposed in this paper: a sparse equivalent source model is developed based on Huygens’ principle where a vehicular antenna is made equivalent to magnetic current placed on a finite conducting plate. The image theory and the uniform theory of diffraction are then applied, a modified Green’s function is derived, and the sparse equivalent source model is constructed to replace the original vehicular antenna. Because of its simple geometry and material, in comparisons with the existing methods, the proposed model uses significantly less expenditures for simulation of vehicular antennas while has better accuracy due to the consideration of the finite conducting plate. Simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method, and a real-world experiment is designed and conducted to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method with real measurement data. It is shown that the proposed method can save simulation time by four times, with less than 1-dB error compared to measurement.

Timing errors and channel mismatches are important factors that can degrade the performance of Time-Interleaved Analog-to-Digital Converters (TIADCs). A Fully Digital Background Calibration Technique has been proposed to address channel mismatches in TIADCs which involves estimating the mismatches and compensating for them. The technique utilizes an estimation algorithm that is executed in the background, without interfering with the normal operation of the converter. It combines a computational modeling component that can accurately estimate the mismatches, with a calibration component that can adjust the samples. The estimation algorithm works by utilizing a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to extract the frequency response of the TIADC, and then using this response to estimate the channel gain and phase mismatches. The calibration component adjusts the samples by multiplying them with complex correction factors that are determined by the estimation algorithm. The proposed technique presents a highly accurate and efficient solution that improves the overall performance of TIADCs, making them more suitable for a wide range of computer science and computer architecture applications.

Online security is a major concern today and incidents of forged identity cards and hacked passwords are common throughout the world. Therefore, there is a need for robust personal authentication mechanisms using biometrics for various access control systems. Popular biometric traits such as fingerprint have problems in rural areas, due to wearing down of fingerprint pattern from hard manual labor. This is also a problem for people who work with calcium oxide, because it is known to dissolve the upper layers of the skin due to its basicity. This paper proposes a finger-knuckle-print (FKP) based human authentication system that is immune to the above problems because the finger dorsal region is not exposed to labor surfaces. The paper uses pre-processed knuckle ROI images to train a Siamese convolutional neural network model. The proposed algorithm has been validated using open-source PolyU finger-knuckle-print database from 165 individuals, and has achieved 99.24% CRR, 0.78% EER that is better than the state-of-the-art.

This paper proposes a risk balancing routing assignment mechanism based on service importance in communication networks. Real-time systems require reliable and secure routing mechanisms to ensure the safety and security of data transmission. The proposed mechanism takes into account the importance of each service and evaluates the risk level of each path based on parameters such as reliability, security, safety, and delays. The risk balancing routing assignment mechanism assigns routes that balance the risk among all available paths, thus ensuring efficient and safe communication. The proposed mechanism provides a reliable and secure means of routing in communication networks, especially in real-time systems where delays and interruptions can cause severe consequences.

This letter provides a brand new way of feature extraction, which can be applied in the supervised classification of hyperspectral image. The convolutional neural network (CNN) has been proven to be an effective method of image classification. However, due to its long training time, it requires a large amount of the labeled data to achieve the expected outcome. To decrease the training time and reduce the dependence on large labeled data set, we propose using the method of transfer learning by taking the advantage of Bayesian framework to integrate with spectrum and spatial information, making use of the Markov property of images to distinguish and separate the ones with class tags, and employing the CNN trained by band samples randomly selected from the data sets. The method of classification mentioned in our letter makes use of the real hyperspectral data sets to perform the experimental evaluation. The result demonstrates that our method is superior to the previous methods.

In the rapidly evolving era of advanced smart cities, the ability to accurately detect human emotion is of great importance. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for IoT-enabled virtual emotion detection, using wireless communication and sensor networks. Our framework is designed to recognize emotions in real-time, with a focus on the communication system security and reflection of the emotions detected. We utilize wireless cameras and IoT technology to capture and analyze facial expressions and other physiological indicators, providing a unique approach to emotion recognition in smart cities. Through our proposed framework, we aim to enhance the emotional well-being and safety of city residents, while also facilitating the implementation of smart city infrastructure. Overall, our research highlights the potential of IoT-enabled emotion detection in smart cities, providing a new avenue for research and practical application in this growing field.

This paper proposes a method for Doppler frequency estimation in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems using Overlap Frequency Domain Equalization (OFDE). The Doppler effect resulting from the motion of the transmitter or receiver can lead to significant distortion in OFDM systems. Accurate frequency estimation is crucial for mitigating this distortion and maintaining high throughput. The proposed approach involves frequency-domain analysis of the received signals and the use of OFDE techniques to enhance the accuracy of the estimation. The results show that the proposed method improves the estimation accuracy and reduces the degradation caused by Doppler effect, thereby improving the overall performance of the system.

In this paper, temperature measurements are utilized to develop health indicators based on principal component analysis toward the probabilistic estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of reciprocating compressors in service. Temperature degradation histories obtained from 13 actual valve failure cases constitute the training data in a data-driven prognostic approach. Two data-driven prognostic methodologies are presented and proposed based on probabilistic mathematical models, i.e., gradient boosted trees and nonhomogeneous hidden semi-Markov models. The training and testing process of all models is described in detail. RUL prognostics in unseen data are obtained for all models. Beyond the mean estimates of the RUL, the uncertainty associated with the point prediction is quantified and upper/lower confidence bounds are also estimated. Prediction estimates for 12 real-life failure cases are presented and the pros and cons of each model's performance are highlighted. Several metrics are utilized to assess the performance of the prognostic algorithms and conclusions are drawn regarding the prognostic capabilities of each of them.

Traditionally, network risk assessment uses a statistical computation method. This paper proposes Lie group kinematics to describe the feature space of the attack behavior. A matrix composed of indicators and topologies in a network system is mapped to a Lie group. The attack behavior path and the powers of the attack and defense are defined. The risk value of the attack and defense is calculated from the change in the indicators. Then, we evaluate the network security risk status using calculus. To examine the validity of the network risk assessment based on a Lie group, we conduct one experiment and utilize the CIC2017 dataset to show the applicability and efficiency of the proposed method. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the calculation method based on a Lie group, and the risk value of the attack and defense is valid compared to those of other machine learning algorithms. The calculation method based on a Lie group can quantitatively analyze network security risks..

In machine learning, supervised classifiers are used to obtain predictions for unlabeled data by inferring prediction functions using labeled data. Supervised classifiers are widely applied in domains such as computational biology, computational physics and healthcare to make critical decisions. However, it is often hard to test supervised classifiers since the expected answers are unknown. This is commonly known as the oracle problem and metamorphic testing (MT) has been used to test such programs. In MT, metamorphic relations (MRs) are developed from intrinsic characteristics of the software under test (SUT). These MRs are used to generate test data and to verify the correctness of the test results without the presence of a test oracle. Effectiveness of MT heavily depends on the MRs used for testing. In this paper we have conducted an extensive empirical study to evaluate the fault detection effectiveness of MRs that have been used in multiple previous studies to test supervised classifiers. Our study uses a total of 709 reachable mutants generated by multiple mutation engines and uses data sets with varying characteristics to test the SUT. Our results reveal that only 14.8% of these mutants are detected using the MRs and that the fault detection effectiveness of these MRs do not scale with the increased number of mutants when compared to what was reported in previous studies.

Due to absorption and scattering effects the under-water scenes are characterized by poor contrast, color shifting, additional noise and hazy appearance. In this paper we introduce a novel solution that estimates locally the backscattered light. While in general the existing solutions estimate a global backscattered light value over the entire scene, our local strategy is able to deal effectively to the more challenging non-uniform illumination generated by multiple light-sources. Our solution computes two complementary estimates of the local backscattered light, covering a large and a small patch size. The optimal local backscattered light is computed as the mean of the outputs processed with the small and the large patches while the transmission map, is estimated based on the dark-channel prior (DCP) [1]. Finally, our restored results are computed by simply inverting the optical model using the transmission and the local backscattered light estimates. The qualitative evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach compared with the recent underwater enhancing techniques.

This paper explores the application of transfer learning in P300 detection, a method used to detect brain waves that signify the recognition of visual stimuli. Support vector machines (SVMs) are used as the classification algorithm in this process, which involves analyzing electroencephalography (EEG) signals. P300 detection can be used in various applications, such as improving communication for individuals with motor disabilities or detecting deception. The paper discusses the use of brain modeling and Hidden Markov models (HMMs) to enhance the accuracy of the detection. The kernel is also examined as a way to improve the performance of SVMs when detecting P300 signals. Additionally, the importance of using appropriate training data in the transfer learning process is highlighted. Overall, this paper shows the potential of transfer learning in P300 detection and its benefits in improving accuracy and efficiency.

Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) may be used for providing seamless network coverage in urban areas for improving the performance of conventional cellular networks. Given the predominantly line-of-sight channel of drones, UAV-aided seamless coverage becomes particularly beneficial in case of emergency situations. However, a single UAV having a limited cruising capability is unable to provide seamless long-term coverage, multiple drones relying on sophisticated recharging and reshuffling schemes are necessary. In this context, both the positioning and the flight strategy directly affect the efficiency of the system. Hence, we first introduce a novel UAV energy consumption model, based on which an energy-efficiency-based objective function is derived. Second, we propose an energy-efficient rechargeable UAV deployment strategy optimized under a seamless coverage constraint. Explicitly, a two-stage joint optimization algorithm is conceived for solving both the optimal UAV deployment and the cyclic UAV recharging and reshuffling strategy. Our simulation results quantify the efficiency of our proposed algorithm.

This paper presents a framework designed to improve the teaching and learning of system analysis using the Unified Modeling Language (UML). The framework contains various analytical models and taxonomies which are utilized to organize information about UML, object-oriented modeling and visualization techniques. In addition, the use of computational modeling and other visual tools are integrated into the framework to help students grasp complex concepts. This approach can enhance the effectiveness of UML instruction in educational settings by increasing the level of interactivity, student engagement and ultimately, student achievement. Moreover, this framework can expand knowledge sharing within the field of system analysis and ultimately benefit software development professionals. Overall, the proposed framework has the potential to promote the development of future professionals whose skills can contribute to high-quality software design and development projects.

Usually Small Hydro Power Plants are frequently constituted of fixed speed drives. With the development power electronics converter, an autonomous variable speed drives i.e. Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) came into the fashion. Small Hydro Power Plant (SHPP) allied with doubly fed induction generator as an alternative source of energy plays a foremost part for changing the face of an emerging country in the terms of the energy crisis, environment protection, and economic development. The foremost objective of this paper is to represent a newly improved control strategy using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in grid-connected doubly fed induction generator associated with the small hydropower plant. The SHPP system embraces the back to back voltage source converter. The suggested control scheme controls both sides of converter i.e. converter of rotor side and grid side and sustains the power factor at unity level in the grid side for abbreviating the loss as well as controlling the effective reactive and real power flow in the rotor side. Optimum reactive and real power flow from the rotor side to grid side occurs at variable speeds with the assistance of DFIG. Here ANN controller improves the transient response of DFIG and makes the system more apposite for real-time applications. The stability of the system is constant under diverse load conditions and it is investigated with the help of the model, and simulations result. A 2 MW DFIG linked with 2 MW SHPP model is simulated in SIMULINK for Time domain applications.

In this study, we propose a simplification approach for the 3-Compartment model by utilizing perturbation methods. The 3-Compartment model is a well-known mathematical model used in various fields, such as analytical models, data models, intelligent systems, and logistics. However, the complexity of the model often leads to difficulties in solving them numerically. Therefore, we suggest using the perturbation method to simplify the model and make it more tractable. The method works by introducing a small parameter, which allows us to derive a simpler form of the model that is easy to solve analytically. Through convergence analysis, we demonstrate that the simplified model provides good approximations for the original 3-Compartment model, especially for small perturbations. Our proposed method offers a promising approach for simplifying the 3-Compartment model, which can lead to faster and more accurate solutions in various applications.

Citizen criminality is a social problem that affects to some big cities un the world. Specifically, in Lima, Peru, there is a serious problem on criminality. However, this problem is very different in each district of Lima city. In addition, people, who comet crime, reside generally in other district. In this way, in this work, a geospatial analysis of the place where reside the people who committed crime, is developed, by applying of the grey clustering method. The case study was carried out in thirty-two districts of Lima city, in order to analyze the provenance of prisoners in the jails of Lima city. The results showed that the districts with more prisoners in the jails of Lima city were San Juan de Lurigancho, Cercado de Lima, and Villa el Salvador. In addition, the districts with less prisoners in the jails of Lima city were Ancon, Carabayllo, and Puente Piedra. The results of this study could help to local and central government to make the best decision on the criminality in the districts of Lima city by applying of focused plans or programs.

Recently, imbalanced traffic classification has attracted more attention due to the fact that most internet traffic exhibits imbalance behavior. However, few works only have considered real-time imbalanced traffic classification. In this project, we propose a comparative study comprising several machine learning algorithms for nine different scenarios. We vary dataset and flow sizes following an under-sampling approach, in order to establish an objective evaluation of the best parameters for classification. The results showed that: 1) Combined with packet length, inter-arrival time and maximum segment size, features related to TCP session signalization enhance imbalanced traffic classification performances; 2) Ensemble approaches, especially Bagged Random Forest, achieve the best results for real-time imbalanced traffic classification; 3) Increasing flow sizes while reducing (to a certain level) training set sizes, enhances classification performances as we learn more about each individual instance. The best classification scenario includes 500 samples in each class with 8 packets flows.

The aim of this research is to investigate the optimal splitting level of the splitting algorithm, which is widely used in computational modeling for optimization. A mathematical model is proposed to simulate the performance of the splitting algorithm and explore the effects of different splitting levels on the optimization results. Genetic algorithms are applied to search for the optimal splitting level that can provide the best performance. The results are evaluated based on standards for reliability and physics. This study provides insights into the optimization process and contributes to the development of more efficient algorithms in computational modeling.

In recent years, deep reinforcement learning methods have achieved impressive performance in many different fields, including playing games, robotics, and dialogue systems. However, there are still a lot of restrictions here, one of which is the demand for massive amounts of sampled data. In this paper, a hierarchical meta-learning method based on the actor-critic algorithm is proposed for sample efficient learning. This method provides the transferable knowledge that can efficiently train an actor on a new task with a few trials. Specifically, a global basic critic, meta critic, and task specified network are shared within a distribution of tasks and are capable of criticizing any actor trying to solve any specified task. The hierarchical framework is applied to a critic network in the actor-critic algorithm for distilling meta-knowledge above the task level and addressing distinct tasks. The proposed method is evaluated on multiple classic control tasks with reinforcement learning algorithms, including the start-of-the-art meta-learning methods. The experimental results statistically demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance and attains better results with more depth of meta critic network.

This paper presents a design methodology for novel adaptive multilayer neural dynamics-based controllers of multirotor UAVs. These controllers are designed to address the challenges posed by the dynamics of unmanned aerial vehicles operating in nonhomogeneous media. The mathematical model of the vehicle dynamics is developed and analyzed for convergence and robustness. The proposed controllers adapt to changes in system dynamics and ensure robust control by utilizing multilayer neural networks. The convergence and robustness analyses demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controllers in ensuring stable and safe operation of multirotor UAVs in nonhomogeneous environments. Overall, this study provides a promising direction for improving the control of unmanned aerial vehicles in challenging conditions.

The increasing cases of wireless communication networks being partly (or even fully) destroyed after the occurrence of natural disasters has made researchers focus on the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) to provide quick and efficient backup communication in post-disaster scenarios. However, the performance of UAVs in the provisioning of wireless coverage is known to be constrained by their battery life, which limits their flight times. In this paper, we explore the use of a single UAV to provide backhaul connectivity to truck-mounted Base Stations (BSs) that have been deployed within a disaster zone to provide network coverage to users based on the principle of delay-tolerant communications. We propose a trajectory design that uses genetic algorithm to find the trajectory with the least energy requirement for the UAV to visit all the BSs and return to a central node that acts as a gateway to the core network. Our trajectory design takes into account both the straight-and-level flight and banked-level turns of the UAV in computing the energy requirement. Simulation results show that our proposed design outperforms two approaches in the literature by up to 14% and 40%.

In this paper a novel method is proposed for state estimation of nonlinear systems using high-gain observers (HGOs) and adaptive techniques. In this regard, Multiple HGOs (MHGO) are run simultaneously, and the information obtained from individual observers are combined adaptively. To be able to suitably combine the state estimations, it is first proved that there exist some constant coefficients that provide the perfect estimation. Then, the RLS algorithm is employed to find those coefficients. The convergence of the state estimations to the system states is guaranteed, and it is shown that the MHGO is able to attenuate the inherent peaking phenomenon in HGOs. Finally, the simulation results are presented which show the superiority of the proposed MHGO method in state estimation and improving the transient response.

Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a deep learning algorithm which is widely used in image processing and pattern recognition due to its robustness to feature invariance. However, it is also computation-intensive that results in a bad real-time performance. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) has good performance in energy-efficiency, flexibility of parallel processing and pipelined operations. Thus it is expected to be used for accelerating deep learning algorithm. In this research, a FPGA based system is developed to realize the real-time Hand Gesture Recognition. We train a designed CNN model with caffe framework and obtain the model's parameters on PC. Bilinear interpolation algorithm is used to adjust the size of the image captured by camera. Then we use FPGA to implement the inference process of Hand Gesture Recognition with obtained parameters by designing an accelerator using Xilinx SDx tools.

Power-over-fibre (POF) has been demonstrated for remotely powering microelectronic devices in hazardous environments [1] and in telecommunication and smart grid applications [2]. The technique can also be used for supplying power to surveillance cameras which reduces their vulnerability to tampering [3]. Ultimately, POF will have significant applications in the development and implementation of all-optical sensor networks. However, there is a limit to the amount of power that can be transmitted via the optical fibre due to processes such as stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) [4]. As such, the aim of this study is to optimise the power delivered to different parts of an optical fibre network, in order to minimise the effects of processes such as SBS. This can be achieved by enhancing the performance of the photovoltaic microcell (also called a photovoltaic power converter, PPC) and tailoring it to match the power requirements of sensors or actuators scattering throughout the network.

In recent times, with the ever-increasing use of Big Data, security has become the number one business concern. Due to the growth of cyberattacks, information security has become the overarching problem all over the world. Prevention alone is not the answer. Therefore, intrusion detection systems have been developed. Intrusion refers to hacking the system or a network that harms the security of information. Intrusion detection systems (IDS) are an essential element of the network security infrastructure and play a very important role in the detection of a large number of attacks. This paper introduces an analysis of network security issues and also represents the various works of current research in Big Data intrusion and detection systems. In this article, we discuss the recent approaches used for intrusion detection in Big Data and especially the predictive analysis proposed to minimize security problems.

Planetary gearbox is widely used in various mechanical equipment, and its reliability is directly related to the normal operation of the entire system. Therefore, how to effectively diagnose the faults of planetary gearbox has become an important research topic. In this paper, a fault diagnosis method based on hierarchical extreme learning machine (HELM) is proposed. The method can achieve accurate fault diagnosis by extracting features of vibration signals and processing them through a hierarchical structure. Specifically, the features of gearbox vibration signals are extracted by wavelet packet decomposition and principal component analysis. Then, the feature matrix is input into the HELM model for classification and fault diagnosis. The method has been tested on a planetary gearbox with surface cracks of different sizes, and the results show that the proposed method has high accuracy and can effectively diagnose the faults of planetary gearbox. Therefore, the method has great potential for application in the monitoring and maintenance of mechanical equipment in the industry.

Crowd simulation becomes one of the active research over the last three decade. Crowd simulation research is part of research about human behavior. One of research focus on crowd simulation was simulation at disaster evacuation. People who trapped in disaster usually has different behavior and abilities when evacuating. So the simulation looks more real, there are several simulations scenario used when disaster simulation like invariant speed and relation between virtual agents scenario. In this research will be used agent-based reciprocal velocity obstacle method. The agent-based method used because applying a microscopic approach. With agent-based method then each virtual agents can have different behavior and abilities. Optimal reciprocal collision avoidance(ORCA) which is the best version of Reciprocal velocity obstacle(RVO) used as virtual agents collision avoidance in crowds simulation. Experiment result demonstrates the simulation of hundreds of agents in a three evacuation scenario. Leader-follower relations on heterogeneous agents result in the possibility of collisions between agents getting bigger with the number of collisions is 7781 collisions. The longest simulation time is 151 seconds with the smallest FPS number is 33 FPS.

In this paper, a novel robust adaptive barrier Lyapunov function (BLF)-based backstepping controller has been proposed for a class of interconnected, multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) unknown nonaffine nonlinear systems with asymmetric time-varying (ATV) state constraints. The design involves a neural-network-based online approximator to cope with uncertain dynamics of the system. To tune its weights, a novel adaptive law is proposed based on the Hadamard product. A theorem has also been proposed to have the bounds on virtual control signals beforehand. This theorem eliminates the need for tedious offline computation for the feasibility condition on the virtual controller in BLF-based controller design. To overcome the problem of unknown control gain in the nonaffine system, Nussbaum gain has been used during the design. A simulation study on the robot manipulator in task space has been performed to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

This paper aims to explore the use of the software BIOMECHANICS in Physical Culture and Sports Specialists’ Preparation. The field of biomechanics is relevant to sports and physical culture, as it focuses on the analysis of human movement and its mechanics. The software BIOMECHANICS provides a computational modeling tool to support coaches, trainers, and athletes in understanding physical performance and identifying areas of improvement. This program includes various features for motion capture, data analysis, and reporting, making it a valuable resource in the realm of sports training. Additionally, BIOMECHANICS is compatible with Microsoft Windows, allowing for widespread access and ease of use. The use of this software in physical culture and sports specialist’s preparation has the potential to significantly enhance athletic performance and contribute to the advancement of the field of biomechanics.

This paper presents a unified subspace fitting framework for direct position determination in the presence of multipath propagation. The proposed framework utilizes a cost function based on direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation to minimize the estimation error. The fitting process involves decomposing the received signal into a series of subspaces, followed by a subspace fitting algorithm that iteratively aligns the subspaces. The accuracy of the proposed framework is evaluated through performance analysis, which demonstrates that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods such as multiple signal classification. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides a reliable and accurate solution for direct position determination in the presence of multipath propagation.

This paper presents an efficient recursive algorithm for computing tight enclosures of the set of states consistent with a given nonlinear discrete-time model, an observed output sequence, and given bounds on disturbances and measurement errors. This is commonly called set-based state estimation, and has applications in verification, fault detection, and robust control. The presented algorithm is based on the theory of differential inequalities (DI), which has been extensively developed for nonlinear reachability analysis. Contemporary DI methods make use of redundant model equations to achieve tight reachability bounds at low cost. Here, we extend these methods to set-based state estimation and show very favorable results relative to other recursive algorithms in common use. Notably, however, this approach is only applicable to forward-Euler-discretized systems satisfying a step size bound.

The LoRaWAN network is a popular technology for the implementation of the Internet of Things (IoT) due to its long-range communication capabilities and low power consumption. In the LoRaWAN system, the joint spreading factor and coding rate assignment plays a crucial role in optimizing the system performance. This paper proposes a methodology for optimizing the sensitivity of receivers by assigning the appropriate spreading factor and coding rate based on the modulation, bandwidth, chirp, and encoding utilized in the LoRaWAN network. The proposed approach improves the network performance by reducing the probability of bit error and increasing the range of the system. The proposed methodology is validated via simulation results, which show the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The presented methodology provides a promising solution for improving the performance of LoRaWAN networks, which is vital for the successful implementation of IoT applications in various domains.

We propose a top-down approach for formation control of heterogeneous multiagent systems, based on the method of eigenstructure assignment. Given the problem of achieving scalable formations on the plane, our approach globally computes a state feedback control that assigns desired closed-loop eigenvalues/eigenvectors. We characterize the relation between the eigenvalues/eigenvectors and the resulting interagent communication topology, and design special (sparse) topologies such that the synthesized control may be implemented locally by the individual agents. Moreover, we present a hierarchical synthesis procedure that significantly improves computational efficiency. Finally, we extend the proposed approach to achieve fixed-size formation and circular motion, and illustrate these results by simulation examples.

This paper presents a predictive model for treatment outcome in autism based on the structure of the brain using sure independence screening, feature extraction, and computational modeling. The study focuses on the correlation between the structure of the brain and the severity of autism symptoms. Biomedical imaging techniques were used to extract features from the brain structure, and predictive models were developed using computational modeling techniques. The results showed that the predictive model was able to accurately predict treatment outcomes in autism based on brain structure. This study highlights the potential of using biomedical imaging and computational modeling to develop predictive models for treatment outcomes in autism. The findings could have significant implications for the development of personalized treatment approaches for individuals with autism.

Foreign Exchange (Forex) market is a financial market that is totally liquid and highly volatile. Traders earn money by placing buying or selling orders on currency pairs by analyzing the market behaviour before they place any orders. There are two types of analysis namely fundamental analysis and technical analysis. Technical analysis is based on historical price data. Several attempts have been made to forecast the forex prices. Among them time series forecasting is significant. According to Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) theory and random walk theory, future prices are independent of the historical prices in financial markets. Thus, to overcome the challenge faced by existing method for technical analysis of short-term trend forecasting in Forex prices was proposed by integrating a DRNN and ARMIA model. Our results have proven the potential for forecasting future Forex prices with a reasonable accuracy.

This paper presents an interdisciplinary and university project-based learning (PBL) curriculum that leverages a robotics challenge to teach various subjects. The project focuses on the development of an autonomous cleaning robot that employs embedded systems and various sensors to determine its location, navigate, and perform cleaning tasks. The curriculum integrates multiple disciplines such as mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, and environmental studies to design, build, and program the robot. The use of springs, estimation techniques, and other related concepts are also covered in the coursework to enhance the knowledge of the students. Overall, the curriculum provides effective hands-on learning experiences that align with the needs of the industry, preparing students to become effective problem solvers, innovators, and leaders in the field of robotics and embedded systems.

This paper presents an interpretable and scalable recommendation method based on network embedding. Recommender systems are widely used in many applications to assist users in making decisions. Matrix decomposition is a common approach used in recommender systems but suffers from scalability issues when dealing with large sparse matrices. To address this challenge, we propose a recommendation method based on network embedding, which is efficient and effective in dealing with sparse matrices. Our method leverages natural language processing techniques and transforms the data into low-dimensional representations that can be easily interpreted. This approach not only achieves high accuracy but also provides insight into the decision-making process. The proposed method has been tested on different datasets and compared with existing state-of-the-art methods in computer science. The results show that our method outperforms other methods both in terms of accuracy and scalability. This paper contributes to the field of recommendation systems by providing a new approach that is both interpretable and scalable.

Blockchain technology is ushering in another breakout year, the challenge of blockchain still remains to be solved. This paper analyzes the features of Bitcoin and Bitcoin-NG system based on blockchian, proposes an improved method of implementing blockchain systems by replacing the structure of the original chain with the graph data structure. It was named GraphChain. Each block represents a transaction and contains the balance status of the traders. Additionally, as everyone knows all the transactions in Bitcoin system will be baled by only one miner that will result in a lot of wasted effort, so another way to improve resource utilization is to change the original way to compete for miner to election and parallel mining. Researchers simulated blockchain with graph structure and parallel mining through python, and suggested the conceptual new graph model which can improve both capacity and performance.

This paper introduces new clustering algorithms for Twitter sentiment analysis, aimed at improving the accuracy and efficiency of classification algorithms. Sentiment analysis on Twitter is a challenging task due to the vast volume of data and the complexity of natural language. The proposed algorithms focus on feature extraction and clustering techniques to group similar tweets together based on their sentiment. The paper describes several tools used in the experiments, including Weka and R programming languages. The results of the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the new clustering algorithms in improving the accuracy of sentiment analysis on Twitter. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the application of clustering algorithms for sentiment analysis, particularly in the context of social media platforms like Twitter.

Retail companies always attempt to find a forecasting method to balance their purchasing and sales, whereas the performances of various prediction techniques are still not reliable. Furthermore, it is a question that how to select the proper forecasting model for some specific type of products. In this research, the classical forecasting models and the latest developing forecasting technologies are compared together based on the perishable products and non-perishable items respectively. The process is designed to compare the performance of typical statistic methods with several machine learning methods based on the thousands of historical transaction record of a large grocery retailer. The criterion is also explored in this study include predictive performance, generalization ability, runtime, cost and convenience to evaluate the comprehensive performance of these models, thus companies can easily choose their most accepted model.

This paper presents a search model based on trajectory data for identifying the region with the maximum coverage value. Trajectory data models are used to represent the movement of objects in space and time. The search problem is to find the region where the objects spend the most time. The model is designed to work with distributed databases and takes into account the road network and urban planning. The computational modeling approach used in this study allows for the optimization of the search process while taking into account real-world constraints. The proposed model provides a valuable tool for planners and decision-makers looking to identify areas with high levels of activity and potential hotspots for urban development.

This paper explores the application of machine learning to prioritize automated testing in an Agile environment. The need for measuring software testing effectiveness and efficiency in companies has become increasingly critical in today's software industry. Prioritizing testing activities can be challenging due to the complexity of modern software development processes. This paper analyzes the integration of machine learning algorithms, particularly in Java-based systems, to cope with testing complexity. We discuss how machine learning can help automate intelligent testing, prioritize test cases, and increase testing efficiency. This paper examines how machine learning can complement emerging software testing practices, such as Agile, to improve the overall quality of software products. Complexity theory and machine learning methods are used to manage testing complexity and evaluate software quality. The results show that machine learning-based testing prioritization can effectively yield the best possible testing coverage with minimum time and resource consumption.

This paper proposes a novel image feature set based on a principled information theoretic analysis of the convolutional neural network (CNN). The output of convolutional filters is modeled as a random variable conditioned on the object class and network filter bank. The conditional entropy (CENT) of filter outputs is shown in theory and experiments to be a highly compact and class-informative feature that can be computed from the CNN feature maps and used to obtain higher classification accuracy than the original CNN itself. Experiments involve three binary classification tasks using the 3D brain MRI data: Alzheimer's disease (AD) versus healthy controls (HC), young versus old age, and male versus female, where the area under the curve (AUC) values for the CENT feature classification (93.9%, 96.7%, and 71.9%) are significantly higher than the softmax output of the original CNN classifier trained for the task (81.6%, 79.4%, and 63.1%). A statistical analysis based on the Wilcoxon test identifies CENT features with significant links to brain labels, which could potentially serve as diagnostic biomarkers.

This paper presents a new method called Deep Reinforcement Learning in Cache-Aided MEC Networks, which is aimed at optimizing the resource management in 5G mobile communication networks. A task analysis is first conducted to identify the problems and challenges in resource management, such as energy consumption and server overload. Then, the proposed method utilizes reinforcement learning techniques to optimize the resource allocation and caching strategy in MEC networks, resulting in improved quality of service and reduced energy consumption. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches, further emphasizing the potential of using reinforcement learning for the optimization of resource management in MEC networks.

Software testing is a critical phase in the software development life cycle, and it is essential to identify the root cause of issues for prompt resolution. To enable efficient root cause analysis in agile software testing environments, prediction algorithms based on machine learning techniques have gained attention. These algorithms employ clustering algorithms to analyze and group testing data into meaningful clusters. Neurons are then trained on this data to predict the root cause of issues based on a set of input features. The application of machine learning in software testing automates the process, eliminating the need for manual analysis of testing data. The use of machine learning in software testing enables teams to detect issues early, reducing the cost and time associated with issue resolution. This paper explores the various techniques employed in machine learning-based root cause analysis and highlights their potential benefits in agile software testing environments.

The concept of trust in human-machine cooperation has gained widespread attention in recent years, particularly in the field of man-machine systems. Task analysis and interference have been identified as key factors in determining the level of trust that humans place in machines, particularly in the context of robots and automobiles. Computational modeling is a useful tool for understanding the complex interactions between humans and machines, and can help to identify factors that may influence trust development. Ultimately, developing a better understanding of trust from the human-machine cooperation framework will be essential for promoting successful collaboration between humans and machines in a wide range of contexts.

In this paper, we investigate the problem of optimal estimation for discrete-time linear systems in the presence of multiple packet dropouts under Markovian communication constraints. Specifically, we propose Kalman filter-based methods to develop optimal filtered and smoothed estimators that can effectively deal with the issue of packet dropouts. We provide analytical expressions for the mean squared errors of the proposed estimators and demonstrate their effectiveness in comparison with existing methods. Furthermore, we also explore the impact of different communication protocols and load modeling approaches on the optimal estimators. Our results suggest that the proposed methods outperform existing approaches and are robust to variations in communication protocols and load modeling. Overall, these findings contribute to the development of improved estimation techniques for linear systems subject to packet dropouts and communication constraints.

This paper proposes the use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm for power scheduling problem with smart batteries in home appliances. The PSO algorithm is used to optimize the power demand of the appliances based on schedules and pricing. The genetic algorithm is also used as a comparison tool to evaluate the effectiveness of the PSO algorithm. Dynamic scheduling is incorporated into the algorithm to accommodate varying power demand and to ensure optimal performance. The results show that the PSO algorithm outperforms the genetic algorithm in terms of power demand optimization and the dynamic scheduling enhances the algorithm's effectiveness. This study provides a promising approach to achieving optimal power scheduling for smart homes with the use of PSO algorithm.

Single-phase line-commutated rectifier loads are broadly used in many commercial and industrial systems. Study and analysis of such systems require accurate and efficient models of the rectifier circuits in simulation programs. The socalled parametric average-value modeling (PAVM) methodology has been introduced to remove discrete switching of power-electronic converters and shown in the prior literature to provide computationally efficient models for three-phase line-commutated rectifiers. In this paper, the PAVM methodology is applied to single-phase line-commutated rectifiers where the dominant ac-side harmonics are also considered. Using extensive experimental measurements and computer studies, the new PAVM of single-phase rectifiers is verified to provide excellent accuracy over the entire range of rectifier operating modes/conditions; meanwhile, being computationally more efficient than the traditional detailed models. The proposed methodology can be very useful for system-level studies of large distribution networks which may contain many switching power electronic converters and single-phase electronic loads, that are otherwise computationally expensive to simulate using conventional detailed models.

The estimation of the direction of arrival for sources impinging on an antenna array has received large attention in mobile communications. In this article we explain how to acquire DOA information using Matrix Pencil (MP) with Uniform Circular Arrays (UCA) and Uniform Linear Array (ULA) based on the analysis of receiving signals. The role of Least Mean Square algorithm (LMS) is to focus the power in the required direction and nullify the interferer for the Uniform Linear Array (ULA). Simulation results show clearly that the matrix Pencil is very performant and stable compared to the published one.

This research paper focuses on the comparative study of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) and Pitch Angle control strategies using PI and Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC) in wind turbines. The study investigates the impact of wind speed and its influence on the performance of both PI and FLC controllers. The results show that FLC control provides better performance than PI control in terms of tracking the maximum power point and controlling the pitch angle of wind turbines under varying wind speeds. With FLC, the torque generated by the wind turbine is efficiently controlled, and the blades are adjusted to optimize the energy generation. This study is significant as it contributes to the understanding of how different control strategies can be utilized to enhance the performance of wind turbines, thus improving the efficiency and sustainability of wind energy generation.

Facial expression recognition (FER) is currently a very attractive research field in cognitive psychology and artificial intelligence. In this paper, an innovative FER algorithm called deep action units graph network (DAUGN) is proposed based on psychological mechanism. First, a segmentation method is designed to divide the face into small key areas, which are then converted into corresponding AU-related facial expression regions. Second, the local appearance features of these critical regions are extracted for further action units (AUs) analysis. Then, an AUs facial graph is constructed to represent expressions by taking the AU-related regions as vertices and the distances between each two landmarks as edges. Finally, the adjacency matrices of facial graph are put into a graph-based convolutional neural network to combine the local-appearance and global-geometry information, which greatly improving the performance of FER. Experiments and comparisons on CK+, MMI, and SFEW data sets reveal that the DAUGN achieves more competitive results than several other popular approaches.

The balanced use of battery power in Ad-hoc wireless sensor networks is a critical factor that determines the success of these networks. In wireless sensor networks, batteries play a significant role in powering the sensor nodes. Therefore, it is essential to use batteries efficiently to increase the lifetime of the networks. Routing is a critical part of wireless sensor networks, and efficient routing protocols can significantly reduce the battery consumption of the sensor nodes. Optimization and estimation techniques can also be used to reduce the energy consumption of the sensor nodes. Spread spectrum communication can also be used to balance the energy consumption of sensor nodes to ensure more efficient use of the batteries. Finally, the use of ad-hoc networks can also help improve the efficiency of wireless sensor networks by increasing the connectivity between the sensor nodes and reducing the need for long-range communication, thereby reducing the energy consumption of the nodes. Overall, the balanced use of battery power in wireless sensor networks is crucial for the success of these networks and can be achieved through the use of efficient routing protocols, optimization and estimation techniques, spread spectrum communication, and ad-hoc networks.

The technological development of the energy sector also produced complex data. In this study, the relationship between smart grid and big data approaches have been investigated. After analyzing which areas of the smart grid system use big data technologies and technologies, big data technologies for detecting smart grid attacks have received attention. Big data analytics can produce efficient solutions and it is especially important to choose which algorithms and metrics to use. For this reason, an application prototype has been proposed that uses a big data method to detect attacks on the smart grid. The algorithm with high accuracy was determined to be 92% for random forests and 87% for decision trees.

Inspired by the thought of TOPSIS, a new multi-attribute decision making (MADM) method is proposed under the interval normal type-2 fuzzy set (INT2FS) environment. Firstly, the Expected value of INT2FS is defined to obtain the ideal solutions. Secondly, the Euclidean distance of INT2FS is given to depict the similarity between each alternative and ideal solutions. Finally, a supplier selection problem is used to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the the proposed approach.

In recent years, Action Detection has emerged as an important research problem in computer vision due to its potential applications in areas such as surveillance, video analysis, and human computer interaction. In this context, the Multi-Scale Based Context-Aware Net (MSCAN) proposes an end-to-end trainable framework for the detection of actions in videos. The proposed method leverages the use of Proposals and Feature Extraction to generate regions of interest and extract informative features from the video frames. Furthermore, the system utilizes Object Detection and Logic Gates to combine object-level and context-level information, enabling it to achieve a higher level of accuracy. In addition, Three-dimensional Displays and Message Passing are utilized to incorporate spatio-temporal information, helping the system to better detect actions across frames. Lastly, MSCAN is designed to work with Streaming Media, making it possible to operate it in real-time settings. Overall, the proposed approach shows good performance in comparison to existing methods on standard datasets, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed approach.

The integration of technology in sports has revolutionized the industry in unprecedented ways. This paper examines the technological advancements used in sports games and ice training to improve performance, as well as the benefits associated with virtual and augmented reality. Wearable sensors, for instance, have substantially changed how sports professionals approach player monitoring and have helped attain new insights into their condition, thereby reducing injury risks. Furthermore, virtual and augmented reality have been found to enhance performance through immersive training, ultimately leading to better player development. This paper explores the use of technology in sports, the impact of implementation, and discusses potential future developments.

This paper proposes a cooperative control strategy for an ankle rehabilitation robot based on human intention. The robot is specifically designed for training and strengthening the muscles in the ankle joint. The strategy uses feature extraction from electroencephalography signals to determine the user's intended movement and then generates corresponding control signals for the robot. The robot employs synchronous motors and pneumatic systems to provide effective support for ankle movement. The proposed strategy not only improves the user's active involvement in the rehabilitation process, but also allows for personalized and efficient training. Results from experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in achieving cooperative control of the ankle rehabilitation robot.

This paper proposes a novel approach for detecting tampered images using blockchain technology. The method involves using feature extraction and semantics to identify suspicious regions within digital images. Transform coding is then applied to these regions to determine if tampering has occurred. The proposed technique leverages the security benefits of blockchain technology, which is a distributed and tamper-proof digital ledger. By storing image metadata and hash values on the blockchain, the integrity and authenticity of digital images can be verifiable. The proposed method has legal implications as it could be used to provide evidence in court cases and protect intellectual property rights. The paper also explores the use of a rare element, Hafnium, as a cryptographic key to enhance the security of the proposed technique. Overall, this research establishes a promising avenue for detecting tampered images and enhancing the security of digital assets.

This paper proposes a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for control of a quarter car semi-active suspension system based on reachable sets approach. The proposed approach provides the flexibility of systematically including the information on the bounds of future road disturbances over the prediction horizon onto the MPC problem formulation by means of reachable sets. This inclusion of future bounds into control design leverages the efficiency of the operation of suspension system. Firstly, a unique Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) model is formulated for control design, which implicitly accounts for the dissipativity constraint of semi-active suspension system. Secondly, an efficient online computation of the reachable sets with the available disturbance information at the current instant for the MPC problem is developed. The proposed methodology is an integration of the preceding steps into a single MPC problem. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is validated through simulations and the results exhibit better performance of the proposed controller compared to skyhook controller in terms of satisfaction of objective and constraint requirements.

Recently, the Internet of Things (IoT) has penetrated many aspects of the physical world to realize different applications. Through IoT, these applications generate, exchange, aggregate, and analyze a vast amount of security-critical and privacy- sensitive data, which makes them attractive targets of attacks. Therefore, it is rather necessary for IoT systems to be equipped with the ability to resist security and privacy risks when fulfilling the desired functional requirements and services. To achieve these goals, there are many new challenges for IoT to implement privacy preserving data manipulation. First, data analysts need to process privacy-sensitive data to extract the expected information without privacy disclosure. In addition, many privacy related factors, including privacy valuation and risk assessment, affect sensitive and private data trading between data owners and requesters. Moreover, the data owners' security behavior also plays an important role in privacy protection in IoT applications. Concerning these issues, this article introduces and surveys privacy preserving techniques in the processes of data aggregation, trading, and analysis: the balance between data analysis and privacy preservation from the data analysts' perspective, secure data trading from the perspective of data owners and requesters, and secure private data aggregation from the data owners' perspective.

This paper focuses on the modeling and steady-state compliance testing of an improved time-synchronized phasor measurement unit, based on the IEEE standard C37.118.1 for phasor measurement units. The device utilizes discrete Fourier transforms and a mathematical model to estimate frequency, which is crucial for monitoring and controlling power systems. The improved device is compared with other models and a biological system modeling approach is applied to assess its performance. The steady-state compliance testing confirms the accuracy and reliability of the device, making it a viable option for power system monitoring. The software implementation of the device on Microsoft Windows is also discussed, further supporting its practicality and ease of use. Overall, the improved time-synchronized phasor measurement unit has been shown to be a valuable tool for power system monitoring and control.

With the fast development of smartphone and wireless network, the real-time news spreads faster because people can use mobile client to broese images, video and audio contents. Many people share and comment to express their mends. redicting the popularity of the online content is a hot research point and many people concentrate on finding out the law of information dissemination. In this paper, taking the Tencent News as a case, we observed that there exists a popularity migration, people sometimes leave comments on irrelevant topics, especially when a hot topic happens. The main contribution of this article is to solve the problem that few or no work for popularity prediction based on topic migration effect. We propose a model based on the reinforced Poisson process model with the weak tie theory and competitive matrix. Our goal is to accurately estimate the popularity of a given viral topic at final based on the observation of its historical characteristics. Also, this method provides a better performance in the popularity prediction according to an empirical study.

As the progress of digitization in industrial society, large amount of production data are outsourced to the cloud server in order to reduce data management costs. Nevertheless, how to ensure the outsourced data integrality, validity, and availability is a challenging research topic. Recently, Zhang et al. (IEEE Trans. Industrial Informatic, doi:10.1109/TII.2019.2894108) presented an efficient and robust certificateless signature scheme to achieve the data authenticity for industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. However, we found that their scheme is insecure. In this paper, we show that an attacker with replacing public key ability can easily impersonate other legitimate users to upload some false messages by forging the target users' valid signatures on these messages. Therefore, their certificateless signature scheme has not solved the IIoT data authenticity issue pointed out by them. Meanwhile, we also demonstrate that their security proof is not sound because the ability of an adversary cannot be applied to solve the difficult problem that they expect.

This paper focuses on event detection from Arabic tweets, specifically the case of Jordan flash floods near Dead Sea. The study aim is to extract useful information and lessons from tweets posted by the public during the event. The paper discusses the use of Twitter as a platform for event detection, as well as the techniques employed, such as tagging, clustering algorithms, and machine learning algorithms. The results of the study indicate that the use of social media platforms like Twitter can be an effective means of monitoring and detecting events in real-time. Furthermore, the paper highlights the important role that media plays in disseminating information about events, but also the potential for inaccuracy in reporting. The lessons learned from this study can be utilized in future event detection efforts, particularly in the Arabic language.

A taxi stand can effectively regulate the behavior of taxi picking up passengers, reduce empty-run rate, and provide a convenient and orderly waiting environment for the public. However, the unreasonable setting of the existing taxi stands in most cities leads to an extremely low utilization rate and a waste of public space resources. This paper presents a novel three-stage strategy to address the taxi stands location problem (TSLP) incrementally. First, taxi demands hotspots are mined from a massive taxi Global Positioning System (GPS) data with GIS platform, and the optimal area for taxi stands siting in the following stages is determined. Then, the spatial interaction between taxi demands and taxi stands is explored to generate demand subsections and stand candidates along both the sides of the road. At last, a taxi stand location model (TSLM) is developed to minimize the total cost, which contains the access cost of passengers and the construction cost of taxi stands. The genetic algorithm-based procedure is adopted for TSLM optimization. A case study conducted in China verifies the effectiveness of the location strategy and investigate the impact of the maximum acceptable distance for passengers on TSLP. The experimental results describe the number and layout of taxi stand under a different demand coverage, which indicates that the proposed approach is beneficial to provide scientific reference for the municipal department in taxi stand site decisions and make a tradeoff between the interests of planners and users.

This paper presents a novel high-speed clustering approach for regional photos based on representative photos of different regions. The proposed method employs linear programming to select a set of representative photos, followed by feature extraction and clustering algorithms to cluster the regional photos efficiently. The clustering methods adopt both greedy algorithms and approximation algorithms to ensure computational efficiency while maintaining high clustering accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in terms of clustering quality and processing speed. The proposed method can be applied to various image clustering tasks and has potential applications in fields such as image retrieval and social media analysis.

Venue2Vec is an efficient embedding model for fine-grained user location prediction in geo-social networks. This model is designed to make accurate predictions of user locations by incorporating data about both the user and the context in which they are located. To do this, the model employs several key techniques including semantics, context modeling, and task analysis. These techniques are used to build data models that capture the relationships between users, locations, and contexts. Additionally, Venue2Vec uses computer networks to efficiently process large amounts of data, enabling it to quickly learn and adapt to new information. The model is then trained on this data, resulting in a highly accurate and effective method for predicting user locations in geo-social networks. Overall, Venue2Vec presents an innovative approach to user location prediction that can be applied to a wide range of contexts and applications.

Cloud computing environments have become increasingly popular due to their scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness. However, with the rise of cloud computing, security concerns have become a major issue, especially in terms of detecting and preventing intrusion attacks. This paper proposes a hybrid intrusion detection system (IDS) for cloud computing environments, which combines signature-based and anomaly-based detectors to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of the intrusion detection process. The proposed system uses monitoring and solid modeling techniques to capture and analyze network traffic and application behavior, and employs switches to filter and redirect traffic for analysis. The experimental results show that the proposed IDS outperforms existing IDSs in terms of detection accuracy, false positive rates, and response time. The proposed system can effectively detect and prevent various types of attacks, including Port Scanning, Denial of Service (DoS), and SQL Injection attacks. Overall, the proposed hybrid IDS is a promising approach to enhance the security of cloud computing environments.

In recent years, object detection in VHR optical remote sensing imagery has attracted much attention due to its wide applications in various fields. However, detecting small targets in such imagery remains a challenging task, which has aroused researchers' interest. In this paper, we propose a novel approach, based on the Sig-NMS method and Faster R-CNN, for small target detection. To improve the performance, we combined transfer learning with our approach, which showed promising results. Our method relies on optical imaging and optical sensors to collect the remote sensing data necessary for the analysis. Object detection, especially small-scale targets, is essential for remote sensing applications, and our approach aims to contribute to this challenging but crucial task. We believe that our research can be useful for various applications, such as optical fiber networks and task analysis. In conclusion, our proposed approach, based on Sig-NMS and transfer learning, outperforms existing methods and provides a promising solution for small target detection in VHR optical remote sensing imagery.

The merger of actors and sensors in a wireless network has evolved those opportunities that we can't think before some years. This merger has captured the interest of researchers from around the globe. In the last decade, wireless networks have become much stronger, reliable and secure but as the technology evolves, it carries their own problems. Researchers are targeting different problem according to their own interest like power consumption, network security, link failure etc., so we are also working on link failure detection that can be caused by power breakage, network delay or traffic overload. This model detects the link failure in the network through Link Failure Detection Algorithm (LFDA) and provide recovery mechanism against failure using cluster-based approach. Our purposed model detects network link failure accuratly and precisely solve the problem by creating alternative virtual route for data packets. Our technique can detect current failures also it can detect weaker links, those might be the cause for future failures. Most of the literature have their proof of correctness as simulation but no technique is there which is formally verified, therefore we have presented our idea including its formal verification and validation with the help of formal methods tool box and its formal specification language like (VDM-SL).

This paper proposes a method called QuickCent for estimating centrality on networks. The QuickCent method is a fast and frugal heuristic that can be used to estimate the importance of nodes in a network. The method is based on harmonic analysis and leverages the power of silicon technology to quickly estimate centrality indexes. The authors explore the potential of this method in computer science and computational modeling, and suggest that machine learning algorithms could be used to further optimize the method. Overall, QuickCent represents a promising approach for quickly and efficiently estimating centrality in large networks.

IoT devices have been gaining popularity and become integral to our daily life. These devices are prone to be compromised as well as any computing system, but lack computing capabilities for cybersecurity software. An important measure for protecting attacks on IoT devices is through isolation of such devices by restriction of communications to the device from firewall/gateway. To this end identification of the IoT device is valuable for network administration and security. In this paper, we introduce a system for automated classification of device characteristics, called System IDentifier (SysID), based on their network traffic. SysID uses any single packet that is originated from the device to detect its kind. We use genetic algorithm (GA) to determine relevant features in different protocol headers and then deploy various machine learning (ML) algorithms (i.e., DecisionTable, J48 Decision Trees, OneR, and PART) to classify host device types by analyzing features selected by GA. GA helps reduce classification complexity and increases its accuracy by eliminating noisy features from the data. SysID allows the ability to have a completely automated way of classifying IoT devices using their TCP/IP packets without expert input for classification. In an experimental study with 23 IoT devices, SysID identified the device type from a single packet with over 95% accuracy.

A majority of the seven million stroke survivors in the U.S. have hand impairments, adversely affecting performance of a variety of activities of daily living, because of the fundamental role of the hand in performing functional tasks. Disability in stroke survivors is largely attributable to damaged neuronal pathways, which result in inappropriate activation of muscles, a condition prevalent in distal upper extremity muscles following stroke. While conventional rehabilitation methods focus on the amplification of existing muscle activation, the effectiveness of therapy targeting the reorganization of pathological activation patterns is often unexplored. To encourage modulation of activation level and exploration of the activation workspace, we developed a novel platform for playing a serious game through electromyographic control. This system was evaluated by a group of neurologically intact subjects over multiple sessions held on different days. Subjects were assigned to one of two groups, training either with their non-dominant hand only (unilateral) or with both hands (bilateral). Both groups of subjects displayed improved performance in controlling the cursor with their non-dominant hand, with retention from one session to the next. The system holds promise for rehabilitation of control of muscle activation patterns.

This paper proposes a Multi-objective Path Planning algorithm that is specifically designed for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) flying in Urban environments. The CDNSGA-II algorithm is used for Pareto optimization, which provides multiple feasible solutions that balance various objectives, including path length, safety, and travel time. The proposed algorithm is based on Octrees, which is a well-known data structure for spatial decomposition in computer graphics. The application of Octrees allows for efficient computation of the collision-free path. Also, Genetic algorithms are used to optimize the search space and reduce the computational requirements. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can generate efficient and safe flight paths in urban areas. This paper contributes to the field of UAV path planning in urban environments and could be used in a variety of applications, including search and rescue, surveillance, and package delivery.

This paper discusses the challenges in achieving distributed consensus when the worlds of Internet of Things (IoT) and Blockchain converge. With the increasing integration of Blockchain and IoT, there is a need to ensure secure and efficient communication between devices in supply chains. Peer-to-peer computing, supported by Blockchain technology, offers a promising solution but still faces challenges such as scalability, transaction throughput, and network latency. The study also highlights the role of Bitcoin as a pioneering cryptocurrency that inspired the development of Blockchain technology, and the potential impact of telecommunications in supporting IoT-Blockchain integration. Ultimately, this paper emphasizes the need for further research to identify effective approaches for achieving consensus within a distributed and decentralized ecosystem of IoT devices and Blockchain networks.

In 3D video coding, distortion estimation is a crucial task and is dependent on the accurate assessment of the rendered views. Pixel-level view synthesis can help improve the accuracy of distortion estimation by synthesizing views that are similar to the original views captured by the cameras. This can be achieved by rendering geometric and photometric information of the original views. The accurate estimation of distortion can then be used to optimize the rate-distortion trade-off in the video coding process. In this paper, we propose a method for pixel-level view synthesis distortion estimation that leverages information science and rendering techniques to improve the accuracy of the estimation. Our results show that the proposed method outperforms existing distortion estimation methods and can improve the overall video coding efficiency.

In this paper, the passivity problem is investigated for neural networks of neutral type with Markovian jumping parameters and time-varying delay. By applying novel Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, using reciprocal convex combination method and improved free-matrix-based integral inequality, the delay-dependent criterion for the passivity of the addressed neural networks is established in terms of linear matrix inequalities(LMIs), which can be checked numerically using the effective LMI toolbox in MATLAB. An example with simulations is given to show the effectiveness and less conservatism of the proposed criterion.
