Simultaneously, by introducing text to speech, speech synthesis and speech recognition (speech to text) APIs, we bring out a novel design of two-way communication system between normal people and hearing-impaired communities. The experiment result shows that such a CSL recognition system, which currently achieved static sign language interpretation with high accuracy, is able to play a much more significant role in this field.

The objective assessment of students' generic skills is an important consideration for educators across the world. Standards have been developed to provide a guideline for the training and planning of these skills in students. In Australia, conferences are held regularly to discuss and share best practices for teaching and evaluating generic skills. The use of tools, such as rubrics and peer evaluations have also been shown to be effective in gauging the development of students' generic skills. In conclusion, the assessment of generic skills is a crucial part of the education process, and requires ongoing attention and evaluation to ensure that students are fully equipped for success beyond the classroom.

Owing to the exponential proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), it is anticipated that the number of small IoT devices will grow expeditiously over the next few years. These billions of small IoT sensor and devices will consume a huge power for data transmission. In this fashion, radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting has been contemplated as an appealing solution to the architecture of long-term and self-sustainable next-generation wireless systems such as IoT network. However, in the practical environment, such as IoT networks or systems are subjected to external interference factors which often results in the loss of the system rate. In this paper, different from generic RF EH system, where only a source node data is relayed through intermediate EH relaying node, we have considered to transmit the data of IoT relay node along with source node data using non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) protocol in the presence of an interfering signal to their respective destinations. Specifically, in the presence on interfering signal, we study the combination of two popular energy harvesting relaying architectures-time switching (TS) relaying and power splitting (PS) relaying with NOMA protocol for IoT relay systems. Considering the interference from the external entity, we have mathematically derived the outage probability, throughput, and sum-throughput for our proposed system. The extensive simulations are carried out to find out the optimal TS and PS factor that maximizes the sum-throughput of the considered system in the presence of an interfering signal. The analytical results of our system model under consideration are validated by the simulation results, and representative performance comparisons are presented.

In this study, external magnetic fields measured by the magnetometer sensors are considered. For low-Earth orbiting (LEO) satellites, there are variety of magnetometers available off-the-shelf commercially. Their noise levels differ based on the mission goals of the satellites and technological advances. Earth's geomagnetic field predicted by the geomagnetic field models is used for satellite attitude control. Any deviations from the model fields, caused by the external sources such as magnetic storms, are treated as magnetometer noise or bias. This may prevent the determination of the magnitude of the effects from the external sources correctly. This study aims to reveal the magnitude of the geomagnetic field variations due to the magnetospheric storms obscured by the magnetometer noise level used in the attitude control systems by implementing a range of magnetometer sensor noise levels on the simulation of the satellite's rotational motion for the selected geomagnetic storm events.

This paper explores the use of smart cameras for parking monitoring in urban areas. With the increasing number of automobiles and limited parking spaces, smart cameras and wireless sensor networks have become an effective solution to provide real-time parking availability to drivers. These smart cameras are equipped with sensors that collect and process data, making it possible to monitor parking occupancy and availability. Wireless communication enables the smart cameras to transmit this information to a central server, which can then be accessed by drivers through mobile applications or other devices. The implementation of smart parking systems can not only improve the convenience of finding parking spaces but also help reduce traffic congestion and air pollution in cities. Therefore, it is crucial to explore the potential of smart cameras and wireless sensor networks to facilitate the development of smart cities.

Digital Signal Modulation (DSM) recognition is an important task in wireless communication systems. However, this task requires high computational resources, making it difficult to implement on edge devices. This paper proposes a Deep Neural Network (DNN) compression technique towards efficient DSM recognition on edge devices. The proposed technique involves convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and a reduced number of neurons for classification. The compression is achieved by reducing the number of neurons, which in turn reduces the number of weights in the network. The performance of the compressed network is evaluated using the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) metric. The proposed technique achieves high classification accuracy while reducing the computational complexity and memory requirements. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique, experiments are conducted on frequency shift keying (FSK) modulation recognition, one of the widely used DSM techniques. Results show that the proposed technique outperforms the traditional DNN model in terms of computational efficiency, making it a promising solution for DSM recognition on resource-constrained edge devices.

This paper proposes a canonical form-based method for designing fuzzy descriptor sliding mode observers in the presence of switches. The design methodology is based on fuzzy systems and linear matrix inequalities, which are used to ensure that the observer errors converge in finite time. The proposed method is applicable to a wide range of nonlinear systems, and is shown to be effective in tracking the state variables of the system. The use of sliding mode control provides robustness to uncertainties in the system while the fuzzy descriptor enables the observer to handle varying modes of operation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulation studies.

Speech spoofing detection is an important task in the field of speech signal processing. In this paper, we focus on the contribution of the voice texture for speech spoofing detection. We use spectrogram and histograms to visualize the voice texture and extract features for training. By applying different transforms to the speech signals, we evaluate the effectiveness of the voice texture in detecting spoofed speech. Our results demonstrate that the voice texture is an important factor to consider in speech spoofing detection and can significantly improve detection performance. Moreover, we provide visualization of the voice texture features and compare different transforms for feature extraction. Our study provides useful insights for developing more accurate speech spoofing detection systems.

In this paper, a distributed randomized gradient-free optimization protocol of multiagent systems over weight-unbalanced digraphs described by row-stochastic matrices is proposed to solve a distributed constrained convex optimization problem. Each agent possesses its local nonsmooth, but Lipschitz continuous, objective function and assigns the weight to information gathered from in-neighbor agents to update its decision state estimation, which is applicable and straightforward to implement. In addition, our algorithm relaxes the requirements of diminishing step sizes to only a nonsummable condition under convex bounded constraint sets. The boundedness and ultimate limit, instead of the supermartingale convergence theorem, are utilized to analyze the consistency and convergence and demonstrate convergence rates with different step sizes. Finally, the validity of the proposed algorithm is verified through numerical examples.

The policy of an optimal control problem for nonlinear stochastic systems can be characterized by a second-order partial differential equation for which solutions are not readily available. In this paper we provide a systematic method for obtaining approximate solutions for the infinite-horizon optimal control problem in the stochastic framework. The method is demonstrated on an illustrative numerical example in which the control effort is not weighted, showing that the technique is able to deal with one of the most striking features of stochastic optimal control.

Nowadays, the success of the different institutions depends on the security of their information against possible attacks. Because much of this information is related to persons' activities, so safeguarding their identities is essential for these successes. For this purpose, persons' identity recognition can be categorized as an effective method to enhance the security of information systems. To do this, most of these systems use biometric methods, which are very efficient compared to traditional methods. In this context, the present paper attempts to design an effective multimodal biometric system using hand biometrics. In this work, Finger- Knuckle-Print (FKP) and PaLMprint (PLM) biometrics are used. In addition, for high accuracy, two simple and effective deep learning based feature extraction techniques, PCANet and DCTNet, are integrated. The security analysis presented in this paper can help simplify the understanding of biometric systems and thus finding a robust solution to protect information systems. Our experimental results, using a synthetic multibiometric dataset of 165 persons, show that our proposed system has a high identification rate and a very low classification error compared to several existing methods.

This paper proposes a multi-attribute aggregation query mechanism in the context of edge computing, where an energy-aware IR-tree is constructed to process query processing in single edge networks, while an edge node routing graph is es-tablished to facilitate query processing for marginal smart things contained in contiguous edge networks. This in-network and localized strategy has shown its e □ ciency and applicability of query processing in IoT sensing networks, and experimental evaluation demonstrates that this technique performs better than the rivals in reducing the network tra □ c and energy consumption.

The detection of informative tweets during disasters is critical for timely and effective response efforts. In this paper, we propose a deep neural network approach for detecting informative tweets. We compare our approach to traditional support vector machines, and demonstrate the superiority of our method. We also explore the importance of feature extraction, specifically with regards to uniform resource locators. Our neural network architecture consists of multiple layers of interconnected neurons, allowing for more sophisticated processing of social networking data. Overall, the use of deep neural networks for detecting informative tweets during disasters shows promise in improving disaster response efforts.

Cloud computing is transforming some biological systems by providing asset combinations that incorporate ownership, simple layout, configuration, quantification, and computerization. This shift in perspective raises many security and protection issues that need to be addressed. These are some of the main challenges of the cloud computing environment: measuring trust, multi-tenure, loss of administration. This document reviews current advances and offers a broad range of cloud security and assurance solutions. In addition, this article discusses information security issues in distributed computing and addresses these security issues.

This paper presents a pen-grip shaped device which can estimate writing pressure and altitude. Writing pressure has long been recognized as an important factor affecting handwriting quality, and hence its accurate estimation is essential for effective handwriting training. In order to achieve this, force sensors are embedded in the device which enables accurate force measurement during writing. The device also employs an altitude measurement system which enables estimation of the relative height of the pen from the paper. A large amount of training data was collected using the device, which demonstrated its effectiveness in accurately estimating writing pressure and altitude. The results of this study suggest that the pen-grip shaped device has the potential to significantly enhance handwriting training and analysis.

This paper studies the fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for unknown affine nonlinear systems with actuators faults. The considered types of faults are stuck (lock-in-place), loss-in-effectiveness (LIE), and bias, under which a part of the actuators is disabled. The objective is to find the remaining (not fully LIE) actuators, and manipulate them to obtain the best achievable performance in real time. First, considering that the best achievable performance is determined by the remaining actuators, a set of basic policies is predesigned with multiple levels of performances for different groups of activated actuators. Second, an identifier is designed based on history data to find the remaining actuators and, thus, the suitable predesigned basic policy. Third, to further accommodate the partial LIEs and biases, a compensator works together with the selected basic policy, to build the predesigned performance. In addressing the FTC problem, several techniques are developed: adjustable mechanisms are novelly integrated to deal with the state-dependent nonlinearities in neural network (NN) approximation, disturbances, and mismatch errors; history data are newly applied to estimate the faulty parameters; and a compensator is specially designed to deal with LIEs and biases in different input channels. Also in theory, the convergences of algorithms and the stability of closed-loop systems are proved, by formally giving the invariant sets of the initial state and the NN weights. Unlike the existing FTC methods dealing with LIE and bias based on model information to optimize the tracking error, this result can handle stuck faults without knowing system dynamics and satisfy different levels of performances described by Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations. Finally, a simulation example of quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed FTC scheme.

As an alternative of the Lyapunov function-based design of adaptive controllers the Fixed Point Transformation based Adaptive controller was introduced that in the first step transforms the control task into a Fixed Point Problem then so solves it via iteration that during one digital control step one step of iteration happens. In the actual step this scheme takes into consideration the controlled system's response obtained for the control action in the previous step, therefore it applies delayed feedback that makes it very flexible in the adaptive control of time-delayed systems. In transforming the control problem into a fixed point problem countless mathematical possibilities exist. Till now only a few versions were in use. On the basis of certain old antecedents in this paper a novel version is suggested that creates abstract rotations in the n dimensional space on the basis of the generalization of the Rodrigues formula. Its main advantage is its simplicity, easy geometric interpretation, lucidity, and better fitting to the features of the particular control task. Its applicability is exemplified by simulations for the adaptive control of two mass-points coupled by nonlinear springs.

Intensity of voxels is a very effective feature, different neurons in human auditory cortex (HAC) are frequency-selective, but whether voxels intensity of HAC whose neurons are frequency-selective could be used as a feature to distinguish different pure sound frequency remains unclear. In order to explore this problem, we analyzed the difference between low frequency (200Hz) and high frequency (6400Hz) of pure tone by the voxels intensity of HAC. The support vector machine (SVM) were used for binary classification, and the correct recognition rate of low frequency and high frequency were 81.82% and 68.18%, respectively. Therefore, we can conclude that the voxels intensity of HAC could be used as a feature to distinguish different pure sound frequency and the frequency preferences of neurons are robust enough to distinguish different pure sound. Our study may be beneficial to the study of brain-computer interface (BCI) and pure tone audiometry (PTA).

This paper presents an MRAM-based deep in-memory architecture (MRAM-DIMA) to efficiently implement multi-bit matrix vector multiplication for deep neural networks using a standard MRAM bitcell array. The MRAM-DIMA achieves an 4.5 × and 70× lower energy and delay, respectively, compared to a conventional digital MRAM architecture. Behavioral models are developed to estimate the impact of circuit non-idealities, including process variations, on the DNN accuracy. An accuracy drop of ≤ 0.5% (≤ 1%) is observed for LeNet-300-100 on the MNIST dataset (a 9-layer CNN on the CIFAR-10 dataset), while tolerating 24% (12%) variation in cell conductance in a commercial 22 nm CMOS-MRAM process.

Endoscopy is a routine imaging technique used for both diagnosis and minimally invasive surgical treatment. While the endoscopy video contains a wealth of information, tools to capture this information for the purpose of clinical reporting are rather poor. In date, endoscopists do not have any access to tools that enable them to browse the video data in an efficient and user friendly manner. Fast and reliable video retrieval methods could for example, allow them to review data from previous exams and therefore improve their ability to monitor disease progression. Deep learning provides new avenues of compressing and indexing video in an extremely efficient manner. In this study, we propose to use an autoencoder for efficient video compression and fast retrieval of video images. To boost the accuracy of video image retrieval and to address data variability like multi-modality and view-point changes, we propose the integration of a Siamese network. We demonstrate that our approach is competitive in retrieving images from 3 large scale videos of 3 different patients obtained against the query samples of their previous diagnosis. Quantitative validation shows that the combined approach yield an overall improvement of 5% and 8% over classical and variational autoencoders, respectively.

Studies on recognising unspoken speech with the use of electroencephalographic (EEG) signals vary in their designs. The participants are either asked to imagine unspoken speech within a specific time frame, or alternatively indicate the start and end of the imagined speech. Optimizing the length and training size of imagined speech is important to improve the rate and speed of recognizing unspoken speech in on-line applications. In this study, we recorded EEG data when the participants performed unspoken speech of five words using two technologies: (1) marking the start and end of the trial by using mouse clicks and (2) performing the imagination in a four-second fixed time window. Four classifiers were trained in all experiment parts: support vector machine, naive bayes, random forest, and linear discriminate analysis. The results show that the best time frame is 3.5-4 seconds length. Moreover, the increase in training size improve the average classification accuracy. However, this improvement becomes slight between 125-175 total training trials. The training data can be recorded in parts, however, the required training size should be increased to have better classification accuracy. In all analysis parts, random forest classifier shows better results among the other classifiers.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing an integrated diagnostic system for neurodevelopmental disorders, particularly for autism. One potential solution is to use expert systems, which are artificially intelligent computer programs that mimic the decision-making ability of a human expert. These systems can incorporate various input variables, such as signal processing and linguistics, to help achieve greater accuracy in diagnosing autism. In addition, fuzzy logic can be applied to incorporate emotional responses, which can be difficult to quantify, but can also provide important insights into an individual's condition. The use of such tools can help clinicians make more accurate and timely diagnoses, ultimately leading to earlier and more effective interventions for children with autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders.

In the past few years, the Subjectivity and Sentiment Analysis (SSA) has garnered a lot of attention, and many unsuccessful attempts were made for developing an SSA model for the morphologically-rich languages like Arabic. In this study, we aimed to fill the gap by designing a new manual and auto-annotated corpus of the Sudanese-Dialect Arabic (SDA) along with a novel polarity lexicon. The corpus is a collection of political tweets, which were annotated by Twitter on a sentence-level. We have also described some automated, online SSA-tagging tools, which could explore all annotated data. Furthermore, we have investigated the effect of various pre-processing techniques on the Sudanese SSA process. Here, we presented a novel SSA technique for the Sudanese dialect, which displayed a good subjectivity classification result and showed an 83.5% accuracy for the Decision Tree performance.

A carrier acquisition algorithm based on delay autocorrelation is proposed due to the failure of applying traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based carrier acquisition method to high-dynamic spread spectrum signal acquisition with large Doppler frequency shift and large change rate. Firstly, two parameters are considered, i.e. highdynamic Doppler initial frequency shift and frequency change rate. Then, the modulation of the high-dynamic spread spectrum receiving signal by square method as well as the influence of spread spectrum code was removed. After that, the Intermediate Frequency (IF) sampling signal is correlated with its delay, and the estimations of Doppler frequency shift and its initial shift are obtained by applying the delay autocorrelation FFT on the signal to complete the compensation. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can not only shorten the capture time, reduce the computational cost, but also quickly complete the estimation of initial carrier Doppler frequency and its change rate. The proposed algorithm satisfies the conditions of large Doppler frequency shift and fast acquisition.

This paper presents the current status and future direction of constructing a National Geospatial Big Data Platform. With the increasing demand for geospatial analysis, the emergence of Big Data provides new opportunities and challenges for the spatial database technology. The governments have taken advantage of this trend by constructing large-scale geospatial databases to meet their decision-making needs. The platform serves as an engine that integrates various data sources from the Internet of Things, making it easier to access and process the data. Furthermore, data mining techniques can be applied to extract useful insights and patterns, which are used for decision-making purposes. This paper introduces the current status of constructing a National Geospatial Big Data Platform and explores the future direction of the technology. Overall, the platform has great potential to revolutionize how governments, businesses, and individuals interact with geospatial data.

Automated test case generation is a crucial problem in the field of software testing. In this paper, we propose a search-based algorithm with scatter search strategy for automated test case generation of natural language processing (NLP) toolkit. Search problems are very common in the optimization of input variables for testing purposes. Our approach involves the use of a mathematical model for generating test cases. The proposed algorithm is based on genetic algorithms and optimization techniques for addressing this problem. The scatter search strategy is used to enhance the optimization capabilities of the algorithm. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is able to generate good quality test cases for NLP toolkits. The algorithm can be efficiently used for testing complex NLP toolkits, and can help testers to efficiently identify and resolve issues. This research provides a novel approach for automated test case generation and highlights the importance of optimization and scatter search strategies in solving search problems.

In optical networks, the signal strength deteriorates as it gets further away from its source. This happens due to deficiencies in the fiber (attenuation, dispersion, conversion). Therefore, we can say that the distance a signal can travel without losing or corrupting information is limited. It is necessary to regenerate the signals periodically using regenerators. Given an optical network, the regenerator location problem tries to install a subset of regenerators with the minimum possible cost, in a way that each pair of nodes can communicate with each other. In this paper bio-inspired algorithms are used to solve this problem. Results obtained using 480 different instances prove their efficiency in solving the regenerator location problem.

In image recognition, the task of object recognition has always been a challenge due to the complex and heterogeneous nature of images. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Deep Feature Fusion Multiple Instance Learning for WaDang Recognition. This approach is based on combining deep feature extraction with multiple instance learning and fusing the extracted features for accurately recognizing WaDang objects. Furthermore, this approach incorporates classification algorithms such as support vector machines to enhance the performance of the recognition task. Our proposed approach has been tested on a benchmark dataset and has shown significant improvements over existing methods. This paper presents an in-depth task analysis of the WaDang recognition problem and outlines the steps and techniques used for solving it using machine learning. Overall, our results demonstrate that our proposed approach is effective and efficient for WaDang recognition and can be applied in various computer vision applications.

This paper proposes a novel predictive model for Electrocardiography (ECG) signals collected from specialized Internet of Things (IoT) devices using Deep Learning. The study focuses on the feature extraction of ECG signals and builds a data model that utilizes Neurons to predict abnormal heart conditions. The proposed model is especially relevant for individuals living in urban areas where exposure to environmental toxins can impact heart health. The training of the predictive model is based on a large dataset of ECG signals, and the results demonstrate its accuracy in detecting and predicting heart abnormalities. The findings of this study have significant implications for the development of specialized IoT devices and the implementation of predictive models for improving heart health.

Web application firewalls (WAF) are crucial in ensuring the security of web-based applications. However, traditional WAFs rely on static rule-based mechanisms and often fail to detect newly emerging and sophisticated attacks. To address this issue, this paper proposes the use of anomaly detection techniques based on machine learning to improve the effectiveness of WAFs. The proposed approach involves the use of training data for the development of an efficient machine learning model, coupled with feature extraction techniques to detect anomalies in network traffic. Results show that the proposed approach significantly outperforms traditional rule-based methods in terms of detection accuracy and false positive rate. In conclusion, the use of anomaly detection techniques based on machine learning has the potential to revolutionize the field of WAFs and improve the security of web-based applications.

This paper proposes a TCP-inspired congestion avoidance scheme for cloud-IoT applications. With the growing popularity of cloud computing and smart devices, there is an increasing demand for efficient management of network resources. The runtime of cloud-IoT applications can be affected by network delays and fluctuations in throughput. This paper focuses on addressing these issues by introducing a congestion control algorithm inspired by TCP. The proposed approach is evaluated through a series of simulations and experiments conducted at various conferences. The results suggest that this TCP-inspired scheme is effective in maintaining a steady-state throughput, while minimizing the impact of network delays on runtime. Overall, the proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the performance of cloud-IoT applications in terms of both efficiency and reliability.

Calibration is an important aspect in the field of computer vision, which involves the estimation of intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameters. In this paper, a novel calibration method is proposed which is based on the image of the absolute quadratic curve. The method utilizes a set of mirrors to obtain images of the quadratic curve from different viewpoints. The geometric constraints imposed by the mirrors are used to estimate the intrinsic camera parameters. The nonlinear distortion introduced by the camera lens is also taken into consideration. The proposed method is capable of calibrating both monocular and stereo camera systems. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method has significant practical applications in various fields such as robotics, 3D reconstruction, and augmented reality.

Traffic Signal control optimization is a key element is future smart cities. We present, in this paper, an optimized agent, based on Reinforcement Learning, with Double Deep Q-Learning. Since intersections influence each other, cooperation between agents will be key in our study. For state representation, we use real-time data, that can be collected by a smart camera, as vehicle position and speed. The rewards function will consider the waiting time of drivers, which has the advantage of better representing the case of congestions in large agglomerations. In our network, we will use Convolutional Layers to extract features that will help our model to learn the best actions to take, in every state. This model will be used to solve convergence and oscillation problems that commonly appears in multi-agent context with Neuronal Networks. A future article will present the details of the implementation and the results obtained and will make a comparison between our model and other state-of-art solutions used in the Traffic Signal Control.

Underwater terrain classification is a crucial task for robot sensing systems in the field of underwater exploration. In this paper, a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) based on a double-tower structure is proposed for underwater terrain classification using sonar data. The proposed CNN can effectively extract discriminative features from the data, which are essential for accurate classification. Moreover, the double-tower structure, which consists of two parallel CNNs, can enable the network to learn both local and global features, making it more robust to variations in the data. The classification performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a public dataset, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, a visualization technique is used to explore the learned features and provide insight into the classification process. The proposed method showcases the potential of deep learning and classification algorithms for underwater terrain classification, and can be applicable for various underwater sensing systems.

This paper presents a study on compact on-body antennas for wearable communication systems. The focus is on antenna measurements and feeds, as well as the use of phantoms for testing. The application of these antennas is mainly for wireless communication in body area networks. The paper discusses the challenges associated with designing antennas for on-body use, including the potential effects of the human body on antenna radiation patterns. The results of various measurements and simulations demonstrate the feasibility of using compact on-body antennas for wearable communication systems. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the design and optimization of antennas for wearable technology.

Compressive sensing can effectively reduce the dimension of a signal vector and has been widely used in many areas. Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using compressive measurements has gained considerable attention due to the reduction in system complexity. In this paper, we extend this structure into two-dimensional (2D) case, where the azimuth and elevation angles are considered. A uniform rectangular array is used as the receive array. Similar to the one-dimensional case, the received signals are compressed before fed into the front-end circuit chains. Then, a DOA estimation algorithm, referred to as 2D compressive measurement-based multiple signal classification is proposed for the proposed scheme, where the azimuth and elevation angles are estimated jointly. The proposed scheme can obtain a higher estimation accuracy than the classical 2D DOA estimation structure when the number of front-end circuit chains keeps the same. On the other hand, when the number of sensors in the receive array is the same, the proposed scheme can dramatically reduce the system complexity and cost by compressing the dimension of the received signal vector. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated by numerical simulations.

The Hybrid Energy-Efficient Protocol in Delay Tolerant Networks for IoT Systems is a protocol designed to allow peer-to-peer computing and communication over the Internet of Things (IoT). One of the main challenges in IoT systems is dealing with delays, which can be caused by factors such as network congestion or low-power devices. To overcome this issue, the protocol incorporates energy-efficient routing protocols that prioritize low-energy consumption and reduce delays. A key feature of this protocol is the use of base stations, which act as a central node for routing and communication. Overall, the Hybrid Energy-Efficient Protocol is a promising solution for improving the efficiency and reliability of IoT systems in delay-tolerant networks.

As the amount of data generated in the power industry continues to increase, effective management of this big data becomes critical for ensuring smooth operation and efficient decision-making. In this paper, we propose a stochastic configuration network (SCN) based adaptive storage replica management system for power big data processing. By utilizing cloud computing and real-time systems, our approach addresses the challenges of handling large volumes of data and limited bandwidth. We also incorporate prediction algorithms to improve the accuracy of data replication and reduce storage overhead. Our system is particularly suited for power industry applications in urban areas where the demand for real-time data processing is high. Through our simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in reducing storage costs while maintaining data availability and improving query processing time. Overall, our proposed system provides a scalable and efficient solution for big data management in the power industry.

This paper proposes a contrast optimization approach for biomedical image enhancement using a combination of elitist metaheuristic optimization and gradient approximation. The approach specifically focuses on enhancing images of biological cells, which have been notoriously challenging to edit due to their complex structures. The proposed technique works by first dividing the image into small regions using histograms and then applying a genetic algorithm to optimize the contrast of each region. To ensure convergence, the algorithm is equipped with an elitist metaheuristic optimizer to avoid local optima. Additionally, a kernel is employed to smooth out the contrast changes between neighboring regions. The approach was tested on a set of biomedical images and compared to other popular optimization methods, demonstrating superior performance in terms of image quality and computational efficiency. The proposed technique has potential applications in various medical services, from diagnostics to clinical monitoring. Overall, the proposed approach provides an innovative solution for biomedical imaging optimization, promising positive impacts on the field of medical imaging.

In the machine learning community, data augmentation techniques have been widely used to make deep neural networks invariant to object transition. However, less attention has been paid to data augmentation in traditional classification methods. In this paper, we take a closer look at traditional classification methods and introduce a new data augmentation technique based on the concept of image transformation. Starting with a few existing examples, we add noise and generate new data points to reduce sparseness in a given feature space. Then, we generate images corresponding to the new data points, although this is usually an ill-posed problem. Herein, the novelty is in constructing an image transformation tree and generating new data from a small number of instances. This allows us to reduce sparseness in the feature space and build more robust classifiers. We evaluate our method on the Caltech-101 dataset to verify its potential. In the context of the situation where the amount of training data is limited, we demonstrate that the support vector machine-based classifiers trained with an augmented dataset using our method outperform classifiers trained with the original dataset in most cases.

This paper discusses the implementation, design, control and stability of a Furuta Pendulum, known for being a highly nonlinear mechatronic system. In this research, the dynamic of a conventional PID controller against a non-linear controller such as the Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) combined with the PID, where the reference model was approximated to a second order system by defining the desired overshoot and settling time of the system are compared. Finally, a real implementation is shown in order to validate the designed controller, discussing the hardware implementation and the nonlinear control design.

In this paper, a new method is proposed for the reconstruction of sparse signals in a fusion center with incomplete measurements. Sparse matrices are used to represent the measurements, and noise measurement and signal processing algorithms are developed for effective reconstruction. Matching pursuit algorithms are used to iteratively identify the non-zero elements in the sparse signal, while optimization techniques are used to enhance the accuracy of the reconstruction. Convergence analysis is performed to ensure the effectiveness of the proposed method in handling the measurement uncertainty. The results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of reconstruction accuracy and computation efficiency. This study contributes to the advancement of signal reconstruction techniques in the context of fusion centers where incomplete measurements are common.

Innovation is developing quickly today. This headways in innovation has changed how individuals cooperate in an expansive way giving communication another dimension. But despite the fact that innovation encourages us in numerous parts of life, it accompanies different effects that influence people in a few or the other way. Cyberbullying is one of such effects. Cyberbullying is a wrongdoing in which a culprit focuses on an individual with online provocation and loathe which has antagonistic emotional, social and physical effects on the victim. So as to address such issue we proposed a novel cyberbullying detection method dependent on deep neural network. Convolution Neural Network is utilized for the better outcomes when contrasted with the current systems.

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of avertible blindness worldwide. Early detection of the disease can help to save the vision of diabetic patients. Presence of exudates, hemorrhages, and microaneurysms indicate an unhealthy eye image. Deep learning models have triumphed in image recognition, object detection and biomedical signal classification. Convolution neural network based DR detection techniques are fast evolving and can identify complex features and thus can accurately classify even severe cases. The presented paper investigates the recent work done in diabetic retinopathy detection using deep learning and collating the milestones achieved to guide researchers working in this domain to the future trend.

This paper presents a study on effective worst-case crosstalk estimation for dynamic translucent SDM elastic optical networks. The focus of the study is on improving the accuracy of estimating crosstalk using heuristic algorithms. The research explores the use of different types of transceivers in optical fiber networks to optimize the crosstalk estimation process. The proposed algorithms enable efficient routing while reducing the impact of crosstalk on optical fibers. Results show that by fine-tuning the crosstalk estimation algorithms, the accuracy of predicted worst-case crosstalk levels can be significantly improved, resulting in more robust and reliable optical networks. This research provides valuable insights for network designers and operators, as effective crosstalk estimation is essential for ensuring high network performance and minimizing signal degradation.

Cognitive Packet Networks represent an innovative approach to ensuring the security and efficiency of the Internet of Things. As many IoT devices are low-powered and resource-constrained, traditional routing methods may not be optimal. By leveraging cognitive techniques, networks can adapt to changing conditions, providing optimized routing paths and quality of service. This is crucial in IoT applications, as delays and packet loss can result in significant consequences, including computer crime and compromised security. Cognitive Packet Networks can mitigate these risks by dynamically adjusting routing paths and prioritizing traffic according to quality of service requirements. Additionally, the use of cognitive software allows for enhanced security measures, such as intrusion detection and prevention. Overall, the application of Cognitive Packet Networks in the Internet of Things is poised to enhance network efficiency, security, and reliability.

Frequently executed methods have major impact in increasing the performance of CPU as well as in code optimization to address the best set of optimization. In this study it is proposed to develop a machine learning based predictive model using Support Vector Machine (SVM), classifier for identification and prediction of frequently executed methods in a program. Since kernel functions play an important role in performance of the SVM and choosing suitable kernel function is still an area of research, here the performance of various kernels of SVM classifier is evaluated and compared. It is found that when trained with ten static program features, the derived SVM model using Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel function predicts the best accuracy of 65% using SPEC CPU 2000 INT dataset. When the same data set was compared with Linear kernel, Polynomial and Sigmoid kernel the prediction accuracy is found to be 40%, 45% and 15% respectively.

Image restoration is an essential task in biomedical imaging, particularly in the retinal image domain. Dust artifacts often occur in retinal images, which can severely affect the detection and analysis of blood vessels in the retina. In this paper, we propose a method for removing dust artifacts in retinal images using dictionary learning and sparse-based inpainting. The proposed method makes use of discrete cosine transforms to obtain a sparse representation of the retinal image, which is used to learn a dictionary of image patches. The dictionary is then used to decompose the image into its most important features, which are used to inpaint the missing regions caused by the dust artifacts. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of retinal images, and the results show that it is effective in removing dust artifacts while preserving the underlying structure of the image. This approach can be extended to other types of medical images and may provide a valuable tool for image restoration in the biomedical imaging community, particularly for the analysis of blood vessels in the retina. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of combining machine learning techniques with signal processing to address challenging problems in biomedical imaging.

Wireless sensor networks are vulnerable to various types of attacks, and jamming is one of the most serious security threats. Jamming attacks can disrupt the communication between nodes and affect the reliability and efficiency of the network. To address this issue, countermeasures against jamming attacks have been proposed, including using switches to alternate between different frequency channels, adjusting the transmission power, and utilizing the fading channels for security purposes. However, these countermeasures may have timing and power constraints, which can affect the effectiveness of the defense mechanisms. In this paper, we propose a decision-making strategy that takes into account the timing and power constraints and optimizes the defense mechanisms against jamming attacks. A simulation-based approach is used to evaluate the performance of the proposed strategy, considering various factors such as delays, power consumption, and network lifetime. The results show that our strategy can effectively mitigate the impact of jamming attacks on sensor networks, even under timing and power constraints.

The model of reactive power optimization including interval uncertainty (RPOIU) is used to make a voltage control strategy for ensuring the interval state variables (including load voltages and reactive power generation) of the power grid within their safe operating limits, under interval active power generation and power load demand input data. To solve the RPOIU model, this paper defined security limits, and then switches the RPOIU model to two deterministic reactive power optimization models, whose constraints bound limits are the security limits. By solving the deterministic models through the interior point method, a voltage control strategy is obtained as the solution of the RPOIU model. The results obtained by the proposed method are compared with the linear approximation method, which is a previously proposed effective method for solving the RPOIU model, and simulation results and analysis demonstrate the advantages, effectiveness, and good applicability of the proposed method.

In the age of industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing, a large volume of sensor data is produced from cyber-physical systems (CPS) and prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) of a machine or system becomes crucial for prognostics and health management (PHM). Several linear regression and deep learning models have been studied to extract features from segmented time windows and learn the degradation patterns. However, distributions of features are varying between source learning domain and target test domains, due to different working conditions and environments. Thus, the generalization of traditional methods will be influenced, which leads to performance degradation. This paper develops a domain adaptive CNN-LSTM (DACL) model to predict the RUL of a system based on the multi-dimensional sensor data. The DACL model combines the CNN and LSTM with domain adaptive transfer mechanism and takes the operating conditions into consideration. The features extracted by CNN of both source and target data are transformed to a higher dimensional space by reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and the loss function is compensated by using maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to reduce the distributions discrepancy. The model is evaluated on C-MAPSS dataset and demonstrate its performance improvement by comparing with previous methods.

This study aims to identify the effectiveness of entrepreneurship training programs on forming an entrepreneurial attitude and spirit in university students. Descriptive qualitative research will be used as research method. Data collection is done through semi-structured interviews. Characteristics of entrepreneurship training programs are generally viewed from four dimensions, namely training design, presentation methods, content and curriculum, and services provided after training. Entrepreneurship training programs have a positive impact on forming an entrepreneurial attitude in the form of mindset, ability and entrepreneurial status. Entrepreneurship training programs also play a role in shaping the intentions of entrepreneurship in the form of desire among the participants of the training program to start and grow the business and see other visible business opportunities.

Gesture recognition has become an important aspect of assistive technology designed to improve communication and accessibility for people with disabilities. Traditional gesture recognition techniques are often limited by their reliance on 2D visual input, which may not capture the full range and complexity of gestures. Three-dimensional displays and deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks, have shown promise in improving the efficiency and accuracy of sign language recognition. By utilizing spatial and temporal information from 3D gesture data, convolutional neural networks can more accurately identify and interpret signs. This technology may have potential applications beyond assistive technology, such as in the design of gesture-based interfaces for telephone sets and other devices. Overall, the use of 3D convolutional neural networks holds great potential in improving sign language recognition and ultimately improving communication and accessibility for individuals who rely on sign language.

This paper proposes a feature-selection based approach for PMU placement in power grids to effectively detect faults. Phasor measurement units (PMUs) are utilized to collect data on voltage and current phasors in power grids. Feature extraction techniques are applied to the PMU data to identify the most relevant features that indicate the presence of faults. The proposed method considers both technical and economic factors, such as transmission lines and substations, and the cost associated with PMU installation, to determine the optimal PMU placement. Radio frequency (RF) features are utilized in the feature selection process for robustness against cyber attacks. The selected features are further fed into a neural network and a decision tree classifier for fault detection. The proposed method has been evaluated on a real-world power grid dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness for fault detection and its promising performance over existing methods.

In this paper, we propose a mask-driven approach for mitosis detection in histopathology images, which utilizes the potential of convolutional neural networks for feature extraction and training. Cancer detection plays a crucial role in early diagnosis, where the identification of mitotic activity is one of the key indicators. Our proposed method generates mitosis proposals by defining the regions of interest using mask-driven techniques. The proposed approach has been evaluated on a dataset of histopathology images from the Cancer Council of Australia. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in detecting mitosis in histopathology images for cancer diagnosis.

This paper focuses on interference management in ad hoc networks, which is a crucial issue as communication links in such networks are highly susceptible to interference from neighboring transmitters. The mathematical model proposed in this paper allows receivers to selectively listen to useful interference while suppressing the harmful interference. This approach, combined with artificial intelligence algorithms, enables efficient interference management in ad hoc networks. The proposed model and algorithms have been implemented in Matlab and the results demonstrate significant improvements in network performance. Overall, the findings presented in this paper contribute to the development of robust and efficient interference management techniques in ad hoc networks.

This paper presents a novel approach for light field image coding using a combination of RDO-based coding, linear approximation and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Light fields have become increasingly popular due to their ability to capture both spatial and angular information, making them ideal for applications such as virtual reality and 3D displays. However, the large amount of data required to represent light fields makes traditional image coding techniques inefficient. Therefore, this paper proposes a new method that uses linear approximation to reduce the amount of data and uses CNNs for optimal encoding. The proposed method achieves high rates of compression while maintaining good image quality. Additionally, a decoding scheme is also presented, which allows for efficient two-dimensional display of the coded light field images. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better rate-distortion performance than other state-of-the-art methods for light field image coding.

In this paper, a novel approach for power-delay tradeoff in multi-cell networks is proposed by introducing two time-scale edge caching and base station (BS) association. The aim is to achieve high spatial diversity in cellular networks while minimizing the power demand and delays. A linear programming model is developed to optimize the system performance for quality of service (QoS) constraints. The proposed method exploits the availability of shared content across multiple cells by caching the popular content at the edges of the network, reducing the backhaul traffic and allowing for efficient content delivery. The BS association is determined using a dynamic approach that considers the channel conditions and user location. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of power reduction, delay performance, and improved QoS for users.

This paper explores the use of derivative-based steganographic distortion and its non-additive extensions for audio as a means of providing enhanced security for media. The concept of distortion is a fundamental aspect of this research, as it serves to alter the original audio in a manner that is imperceptible to the human ear, but still detectable through feature extraction techniques. Additionally, the use of additives is examined, as they can play a role in enhancing the overall security of the steganographic process. The importance of security in media is highlighted, as it is becoming an increasingly important concern in today's digital landscape. Finally, the paper introduces the concept of predistortion, which involves the manipulation of the original audio data prior to the steganographic process in order to improve the overall quality and robustness of the encoded signal. As a whole, this research not only contributes to the field of audio steganography, but also adds to the growing body of work on the intersection of technology and art.

This paper provides a real-time simulation of electric vehicle battery charging systems, which has become an increasingly important topic in recent years. The focus is primarily on batteries and voltage control, with additional emphasis on integrated circuit modeling, mathematical model and computational modeling, topology, and bridge circuits. Through the use of these techniques, the researchers were able to develop a comprehensive simulation model that accurately describes the behavior of charging systems for electric vehicle batteries. The simulation results showed that the battery charging system was able to maintain safe and efficient charging conditions under various operating conditions. Moreover, the researchers found that using a bridge circuit architecture results in higher efficiency and reduced system complexity. Overall, the authors conclude that real-time simulation of charging systems for electric vehicle batteries using advanced control techniques is a promising avenue for improving the system's performance and extending its lifespan.

This paper focuses on the implementation of a hydrodynamic model-based navigation system for a low-cost AUV fleet. Navigation in underwater environments is challenging due to the complex hydrodynamic forces that affect the motion of the vehicles. The hydrodynamics of the AUV fleet as well as the surrounding environment must be accurately modeled in order to achieve effective navigation. Computational modeling techniques are used to simulate the movement of the AUVs in the underwater environment. Mathematical models are developed to describe the hydrodynamic behavior of the vehicles, and sensors such as acoustics are used to gather data for calibration and validation of the models. The resulting navigation system is implemented with computers onboard the AUVs, allowing for real-time adaptation to changing environmental conditions. Overall, this paper presents a novel and low-cost solution for autonomous underwater navigation using hydrodynamic modeling and sensing techniques.

Unit commitment (UC) problems are the most fundamental problems that system operators solve every day in both day-ahead and real-time markets to guarantee secure and economic operation. UC problems are usually formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) or a mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) model with binary variables representing ON/OFF statuses of generators, and is solved via Branch and bound (B&B) type algorithms. With the prosperity of applying semidefinite programing (SDP) in the power system field, researchers attempt to solve UC under the SDP framework by relaxing integrality requirements, seeking an optimal solution or a better lower bound than the traditional linear programming (LP) relaxation. This paper uses 2-order moment relaxation technique to reformulate UC problems as an SDP model, which can be solved by an interior point method. Considering significant computational burden by 2-order moment relaxation, a variable reduction strategy and two refined moment relaxation based UC models are further applied. The relationship among the proposed models in terms of their tightness is studied. In addition, a sufficient condition under which a solution is exact is stated. Numerical studies illustrate effect of the proposed models and potential applicability of the proposed models is also discussed.

Nowadays, the application of fully autonomous system like rotary wing unamnned air vehicles (UAVs) are increasing sharply. Due to the complex nonlinear dynamics a huge research interest is witnessed in developing learning machine based intelligent, self-organizing evolving controller for these vehicles notably to address the system's dynamic characteristics. In this work, such an evolving controller namely Generic-controller (Gcontroller) is proposed to control the altitude of a rotary wing UAV namely hexacopter. This controller can work with very minor expert domain knowledge. The evolving architecture of this controller is based on an advanced incremental learning algorithm namely Generic Evolving Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (GENEFIS). The controller does not require any offline training, since it starts operating from scratch with an empty set of fuzzy rules, and then add or delete rules on demand. The adaptation laws for the consequent paramters are derived from the sliding model control (SMC) theory. The Lyapunov theory is used to guarantee the stability of the proposed controller. In addition, an auxiliary robustifying control term is implemented to obtain an uniform asymptotic convergence of tracking error to zero. Finally, the G-controller's performance evaluation is observed through the altitude tracking of an UAV namely hexacopter for various trajectories.

In this paper, we present a near-optimal phasing method, referred to as Constructive Analytical Phasing (CAP) to perform beamforming for arbitrary oriented antenna arrays of linearly polarized elements. Also, we investigate the resulting electric far-field polarization using Monte Carlo simulations. This simple but efficient method enables us to direct the beam to any desired point in space. In addition, it can be utilized to speed up any further optimization goals for a variety of antenna performance parameters such as pattern synthesis and side lobe level (SLL) reduction.

At the time of more and more devices being connected to the internet, personal and sensitive information is going around the network more than ever. Thus, security and privacy regarding IoT communications, devices, and data are a concern due to the diversity of the devices and protocols used. Since traditional security mechanisms cannot always be adequate due to the heterogeneity and resource limitations of IoT devices, we conclude that there are still several improvements to be made to the 2nd line of defense mechanisms like Intrusion Detection Systems. Using a collection of IP flows, we can monitor the network and identify properties of the data that goes in and out. Since network flows collection have a smaller footprint than packet capturing, it makes it a better choice towards the Internet of Things networks. This paper aims to study IP flow properties of certain network attacks, with the goal of identifying an attack signature only by observing those properties.

Researchers have discovered so far, that there is a closed relationship between psychological conditions and the physiological condition. Many researchers found that emotions affect a person's health, especially negative emotions. In this paper, we evaluated the correlation between the human's emotions and the heart signals. Heart signals were recorded using ECG sensors. Then, by using Kubios HRV we collected the HRV value both in time and frequency domain. This paper focused on data which was extracted using the RR Interval feature. The 29 healthy subjects were induced using video stimuli after they agreed through the consent form. The RR Interval feature that has been extracted was then analyzed using KUBIOS to obtain the value of HRVi (Heart Rate Variability Triangular Index) in time domains. The results show that the average HRVi value after being induced by video stimuli is 14.87. There is a significant difference between HRVi value before and after the stimulation process. Immediate increase of HRVi can lead to a fatal heart attack. The result showed us that in seven minute, HRVi value can immediately increase after experiencing Sad Emotion induced by Sad Video Stimuli.

Single image super-resolution (SISR) is a notoriously challenging ill-posed problem that aims to obtain a high-resolution output from one of its low-resolution versions. Recently, powerful deep learning algorithms have been applied to SISR and have achieved state-of-the-art performance. In this survey, we review representative deep learning-based SISR methods and group them into two categories according to their contributions to two essential aspects of SISR: The exploration of efficient neural network architectures for SISR and the development of effective optimization objectives for deep SISR learning. For each category, a baseline is first established, and several critical limitations of the baseline are summarized. Then, representative works on overcoming these limitations are presented based on their original content, as well as our critical exposition and analyses, and relevant comparisons are conducted from a variety of perspectives. Finally, we conclude this review with some current challenges and future trends in SISR that leverage deep learning algorithms.

FPGAs have made their way into the cloud, allowing users to gain remote access to the state-of-the-art reconfigurable fabric and implement their custom accelerators. Since FPGAs are large enough to accommodate multiple independent designs, the multi-tenant user scenario may soon be prevalent in cloud computing environments. However, shared use of an FPGA raises security concerns. Recently discovered hardware Trojans for use in multi-tenant FPGA settings target denial-of-service attacks, power side-channel attacks, and crosstalk side-channel attacks. In this work, we present an attack method for causing timing-constraints violation in the multi-tenant FPGA setting. This type of attack is very dangerous as the consequences of timing faults are temporary errors, which are often impossible to notice. We demonstrate the attack on a set of self-timed true random number generators (STRNGs), frequently used in cryptographic applications. When the attack is launched, the STRNG outputs become biased and fail randomness tests. However, after the attack, STRNGs recover and continue generating random bits.

With the exponential growth of internet traffic, effective monitoring and analysis of internet traffic has become increasingly important. In this paper, we propose an ensemble framework for imbalanced internet traffic classification. Our framework involves feature extraction, training, and monitoring stages. Specifically, we extract informative features from raw traffic data and use clustering algorithms to address the imbalanced problem. In the training stage, we employ a task analysis approach to select appropriate classifiers from a set of candidate classifiers, and then ensemble them to improve the accuracy of classification. Our proposed framework is evaluated through experiments against several state-of-the-art classifiers, showing its effectiveness and robustness in handling imbalanced internet traffic classification. Additionally, we also discuss the potential hardware implementation of our proposed framework, which can further enhance the classification efficiency in practical applications.

Living on the edge has become the order of the day for computing systems as the demand for processing and storage is increasing with each passing day. This has led to the development of a new paradigm in computing known as edge computing. In this paradigm, computing resources are pushed closer to the edge of the network, where data is produced and consumed, instead of relying solely on cloud computing. The Special issues and sections in edge computing are aimed at discussing the various issues, challenges and opportunities presented by the emerging field of edge computing.

The ecosystem of edge computing is very broad and includes various stakeholders such as device manufacturers, network providers, cloud computing vendors, application developers and end-users. The Internet of Things (IoT) is one field that is highly dependent on edge computing as it involves processing and analyzing data at the edge to ensure real-time decision making. Edge computing is enabling IoT to become more efficient and effective by reducing the latency and network congestion that occurs when data is sent back and forth between devices and the cloud.

Cloud computing has been a dominant paradigm for many years, but edge computing is now challenging this dominance. With edge computing, data is processed and stored locally, which reduces the dependence on cloud computing. This is important as cloud computing can be expensive and unreliable, especially for applications that require real-time responses. With edge computing, applications can be developed for specific use cases, making them more efficient and cost-effective.

In conclusion, edge computing represents a paradigm shift in computing, as it aims to address the limitations of cloud computing and provide an efficient and effective way of processing, storing and analyzing data at the edge of the network. The ecosystem of edge computing includes various stakeholders, such as device manufacturers, network providers, cloud computing vendors, application developers and end-users, who are all working together to develop solutions that meet the demands of today's computing systems. The future of computing is now, and edge computing is set to play a major role in shaping this future.

In the area of multimedia indexing and processing, a big challenge is to classify the mood of the listener through music. It is also a prodigious challenge to separate the noisy signals into speech, music or silence. Mood of a person may depend upon music. According to the music psychologists, behavior of a person is defined by his mood. Thus, this research evaluates the features of audio that have substantial impact on mood of a person and focuses that how to distinguish the speech signals and music from audio file at the same time. Many audio extraction algorithms have been hashed out in this paper and proposes one MMCAD (music mood classification & Audio discrimination) which is the integration of mood detector and speech / music discriminator with improved efficiency and accuracy.

In paper different standards for intelligent medical systems and multimodal architecture interfaces are under review. Application of Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resource (FHIR) standard for data model of intelligent multimodal interface are proposed. Intelligent multimodal interface for EEG and accelerometer bio-signals based on FHIR are shown. Use case diagrams, resource diagrams and class diagrams for production and research mode of this interface are described.

This paper presents a mathematical model for investigating the laminar flow and convective heat transfer in a constricted channel based on double MRT-LBM. Lattice Boltzmann methods are used for computational modelling, and distribution functions are applied to address fluid flow. Through the simulations conducted, it was found that the channel's geometry has a significant impact on the fluid flow and temperature distribution. The results obtained also reveal that the double MRT-LBM model is capable of simulating the flow behavior and temperature distribution with good accuracy, thus serving as a useful tool for predicting fluid flow behaviors and heat transfer in various industrial applications. Overall, this study provides valuable insights and guidance on optimizing heat transfer processes in constrained channels.

A problem of achieving consensus in state of multiagent system consisting of N identical agents is considered. The agents are modeled as discrete time linear time invariant (LTI) systems with bounded inputs (|u| ≤ 1) and complete communication among all agents is assumed. The goal of these agents is to achieve consensus in minimum number of time steps. An algorithm to compute the minimum number of time steps in which the consensus can be achieved is devised by computing the attainable set. Key idea of the proposed algorithm is to compute attainable sets by incrementally varying the time steps and checking for intersection of attainable sets corresponding to all N agents. Since, the attainable set is a convex polytope, intersection of attainable sets translates to checking feasibility of multiple linear inequalities. It is shown that for systems with eigenvalues inside the closed unit circle in complex plane, the proposed algorithm terminates in finite number of steps. The number of time steps counted by the proposed algorithm till the intersection of attainable sets becomes feasible is the minimum time steps required to achieve consensus. Lastly, it is shown using Helly's theorem that the computation of intersection of attainable sets in the proposed algorithm can be performed in distributed manner. The proposed algorithm is demonstrated with the help of an example.

Improving the communication abilities of people suffering from speech disorders or hearing impairments and who are struggling to learn sign or spoken language can improve their quality of life. However, methods to assist such people are not varied, and those that consider the degree of physical disability usually fail to attend particular needs. Thus, it is necessary to provide various communication methods according to the characteristics of each physical disability. In this paper, we devise a customized hand sign recognition system according to the degree of physical disability, and propose a method to select a customized set of signs comprising specific hand motions that an individual can effortlessly perform. We consider the optimal set as that providing high reliability and efficiency to realize smooth communication and apply information theory towards their selection. That is, we consider hand sign recognition from myoelectric potentials elicited by finger movement as a communication channel. Then, the optimal hand sign set is determined considering the set with the maximum channel capacity, as it reflects the most reliable and efficient combination. Finally, experimental results obtained from three subjects verify that the proposed method can determine the optimal set of hand signs according to each subject and that increasing the available hand signs or choosing hand signs with high recognition rate do not necessarily contribute to the optimal set.

Objectives: Administrative HIS (Hospital Information System) and EHR (Electronic Health Record) data are characterized by lower privacy sensitivity, thus easier portability and handling, as well as higher information quality. In this paper we test the hypothesis that the application of machine learning techniques on data of this nature can be used to address prediction/forecasting problems in the Health IT domain. The novelty of this approach consists in that medical data (test results, diagnoses, doctors' notes etc.) are not included in the predictors' dataset. Moreover, there is limited need for separation of patient cohorts based on specific health conditions. Methods: We experiment with the prediction of the probability of early readmission at the time of a patient's discharge. We extract real HIS data and perform data processing techniques. We then apply a series of machine learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors and Deep Multilayer Neural Network) and measure the performance of the emergent models. Results: All applied methods performed well above random guessing, even with minimal hyper-parameter tuning. Conclusions: Given that the experiments provide evidence in favor of the underlying hypothesis, future experimentation on more fine-tuned (thus more robust) models could result in applications suited for productive environments.

Object classification is a fundamental task in computer vision, which has various applications in many fields, such as robotics, medical imaging, and virtual reality. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for object classification using deep learning on extremely low-resolution time-of-flight (ToF) data. Our approach makes use of photonics technology to capture ToF data, which can provide depth information of objects. We apply deep learning techniques to learn features from the ToF data and classify objects into predefined categories. The experimental results show that our approach achieves high classification accuracy even on extremely low-resolution ToF data. This approach can have potential applications in various fields, such as three-dimensional displays, two-dimensional displays, solid modeling, and data models. We believe that by using deep learning on ToF data, we can advance the state-of-the-art in object classification and contribute to the field of computer vision.

In recent years, the development of service robots has led to an increasing demand for effective ways of human-robot interaction (HRI). One key aspect of HRI is emotion regulation, which requires the ability to recognize and appropriately respond to external stimuli. This paper proposes a novel approach for emotion regulation based on multi-objective weighted reinforcement learning (MOWRL). The proposed framework utilizes robot kinematics and emotion recognition algorithms to generate a set of optimal responses to external stimuli. The resulting policy is optimized using MOWRL to achieve both high task performance and emotional regulation. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms baseline methods and provides a promising solution for effective emotion regulation in HRI applications.

Hyperspectral imaging technology has attracted widespread attention due to its high resolution in remote sensing and radio frequency detection. However, extracting features from hyperspectral images is a crucial but difficult task for classification. In this paper, we propose a deep learning ensemble approach for hyperspectral image classification. The proposed approach combines multiple neural networks to enhance the classification accuracy. The deep learning approach enables automatic feature extraction, eliminating the need for manual feature selection. Experimental results show that the proposed deep learning ensemble method outperforms traditional classification methods, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy in hyperspectral image classification. This approach will have broad applications in areas such as remote sensing, agriculture, and medical imaging.

The future industrial networks will not be created from scratch. Rather, they will grow from existing installations without displacing legacy components. The secure integration of these legacy machines and networks will become an important building block in order to realize the vision of Industry 4.0. Secure and high performance virtual private networks (VPNs) will be necessary for that purpose.Therefore, we investigated and compared various VPN solutions. Their performance was tested on multiple hardware platforms ranging from very resource constrained to very powerful. Non-functional aspects, relating around security, manageability and ease of use, were discussed in order to assess their suitability for future use cases.We arrive at clear recommendations on which software VPN solutions to choose for future industrial setups.
