This paper proposes a soft computing-based approach for Electroencephalography (EEG) classification using optimal feature selection and neural networks. The study focuses on the feature extraction technique to enhance the performance of brain-computer interfaces. The authors demonstrate that the cutoff frequency can be used to filter out unwanted noise from the raw EEG signal, and the resulting signal can be used for feature extraction. The extracted features are then optimized using support vector machines (SVM) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA). The study also employs radial basis function networks (RBFN) to classify EEG signals using the optimized features. The proposed approach achieves better classification accuracy compared to other conventional approaches, demonstrating the potential of soft computing techniques in EEG signal processing.

The problem of network function computation over a directed acyclic network is investigated in this paper. In such a network, a sink node desires to compute with zero error a target function, of which the inputs are generated at multiple source nodes. The edges in the network are assumed to be error-free and have limited capacity. The nodes in the network are assumed to have unbounded computing capability and be able to perform network coding. The computing rate of a network code that can compute the target function over the network is the average number of times that the target function is computed with zero error for one use of the network. In this paper, we obtain an improved upper bound on the computing capacity, which is applicable to arbitrary target functions and arbitrary network topologies. This improved upper bound not only is an enhancement of the previous upper bounds but also is the first tight upper bound on the computing capacity for computing an arithmetic sum over a certain non-tree network, which has been widely studied in the literature. We also introduce a multi-dimensional array approach that facilitates evaluation of the improved upper bound. Furthermore, we apply this bound to the problem of computing a vector-linear function over a network. With this bound, we are not only able to enhance a previous result on computing a vector-linear function over a network but also simplify the proof significantly. Finally, we prove that for computing the binary maximum function over the reverse butterfly network, our improved upper bound is not achievable. This result establishes that in general our improved upper bound is non-achievable, but whether it is asymptotically achievable or not remains open.

This paper proposes a new algorithm for view-based 3-D object retrieval that uses Cube Loss to learn descriptors. The algorithm focuses on solid modeling, shape, and computational modeling of objects to create more accurate descriptors. The authors argue that traditional methods for object retrieval rely on human intuition and task analysis, which can be limiting. With the Cube Loss algorithm, the descriptors can be trained, allowing for more accurate and efficient retrieval. The authors discuss the potential for this new algorithm to improve computer architecture for 3-D display systems.

In the field of computer vision, feature extraction is an important step in image processing. However, not all extracted features are relevant or useful for the task at hand. This paper proposes an ORB-oriented mismatching feature points elimination method to eliminate irrelevant feature points using Hamming distance and matched filters. The method was evaluated on datasets containing three-dimensional displays and achieved promising results in terms of feature matching accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method is suitable for real-time systems and can be applied to various fields such as telecommunications.

This paper focuses on the fault ride-through technique, which is used to overcome grid faults in wind turbines powered by doubly fed induction generators (DFIG). The use of channel estimation, OFDM, and neural networks can be effective in improving the performance of the fault ride-through technique. The study also explores the use of deep learning for training data and training the receivers to improve the fault ride-through capability of the wind turbine system. The authors propose a new training method that uses both real-time and simulated data to train the receivers. Overall, the use of advanced techniques and algorithms has the potential to significantly enhance the robustness and fault tolerance of DFIG-based wind turbines, contributing to the development of more reliable and sustainable wind power systems.

This paper represents an optimization method as well as energy management strategy of grid connected renewable energy sources for multi house. Optimization method has been accomplished using HOMER software to bring out optimal size of renewable sources and other components for management strategy. The main purpose of this paper is to design an energy management strategy to optimize the cost and minimize the power loss of extracted power from renewable energy sources based on Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). The system consists of PV array, AC wind generator, Battery, Converter and grid. FLC monitors load profile and delivers a signal to sources. Then FLC changes the switch for appropriate energy supply according to fuzzy rules. The management strategy is controlled by FLC in a way that extra power after meeting the energy demand of the house can be sold to the national grid which is more useful and cost feasible than any other conventional systems. The proposed management strategy is more effective than any other traditional systems which must minimize power loss.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in developing soft robotic systems for use in wearable assistive devices. In this study, we present a novel robotic forearm orthosis which utilizes soft fabric-based helical actuators to generate torque for different tasks. We conducted a task analysis to identify the specific requirements for the device, and designed the soft robotic system to meet these needs. We found that pneumatic systems using flexible fabrics as actuators were an effective solution for generating the necessary torque while maintaining flexibility and comfort for the wearer. Our results demonstrate the potential for fabric-based soft robotics in the development of assistive devices for individuals with upper extremity impairments. Further research in this field could lead to more advanced and effective soft robotic devices for use in a variety of applications.

Video based vehicle detection is an active research area in Intelligent Transportation System. The aim is to efficiently extract the required data from large amount of videos captured by surveillance cameras by detecting, tracking identifying objects of interest and analyze their activities. This paper provides a review of literature on vehicle detection, recognition and tracking. Many approaches have been proposed for detection which includes appearance based models and motion based models .Vehicle recognition based on various attributes such as color, license plate, logos are discussed. Region based and feature based tracking along with various tracking algorithms are surveyed. Multi-view methods for vehicle detection are also discussed.

This paper aims to understand the work environment of therapists in incorporating robots into education for children with developmental disorders. The use of robots in medical treatment has been gaining momentum, particularly in pediatrics. Through several interviews with therapists and attendance in relevant conferences, it was found that the use of robots as supplementary educational tools can be effective in engaging children with developmental disorders. However, one major concern is the potential pain that may be caused by the physical contact between the robot and the child. Therefore, proper training and programming of the robot's interaction with the child is crucial in ensuring its safe use. Further research is needed to explore the specific ways in which robots can be integrated into the therapies for children with developmental disorders.

In the context of Artificial Intelligence, Online learning is focused on environments that are not independent and identically distributed, i.e. the environment may changes its behavior as time goes by. Blum proposed a famous algorithm to this problem, which was called randomized weighted majority algorithm. In this paper, we propose an adaptation of such algorithm to autonomous valuation of financial assets. Our approach is based on learning from expert's advices, in order to create a more adaptable solution and reuse some results achieved for other researchers. We also briefly review some papers in the field. The proposed approach is materialized through an online learning algorithm that defines an analysis derived from many different analyses performed by autonomous analysts. Such analysts may be created using techniques from finance or machine learning fields. Our algorithm is able to take into account different costs of analysis errors. We believe that this skill in fundamental to an efficient analyst. We implemented the algorithm and tested it using several different techniques from finance and one (very simple) algorithm from machine learning area. This implementation was tested and the achieved results are analyzed and discussed. Furthermore, we proved that our algorithm's cost of error is limited by an expression of the cost of error of the best autonomous analyst. We believe that this algorithm may contribute to development of better systems that intend to estimate the price of financial assets in an autonomous way.

We present a comprehensive simulation platform for computational microwave imaging systems based on frequency-diverse metasurface antennas (FDMAs). FDMAs consist of a waveguide patterned with complementary metamaterial elements with resonant frequencies selected randomly from a band of operation, enabling the generation of distinct frequency-indexed radiation patterns. By accurately modeling the fields produced by the FDMA using a dipolar model, it is possible to predict the capabilities of the imaging system in a fast and reliable manner. In contrast to previous works, in this paper we include the mutual interaction between metamaterial elements, and it is demonstrated that these interactions are crucial to a better understanding of the FDMAs' capabilities e. g. effective aperture area and correlation of radiation patterns. The simplicity and accuracy of the proposed model permits the simulation of different metasurfaces for computational microwave imaging, where traditional antenna design- and metamaterial modeling-are prohibitively costly.

In this paper, we propose a model to evaluate the reliability, average reliability, availability, maintainability, and supportability of services using a system dynamics approach. The proposed model takes into account factors such as computational modeling, computer network reliability, software reliability, warranties, data models, and vehicle dynamics. System dynamics modeling provides a structured approach to represent and analyze complex systems, enabling us to identify critical factors for improving the reliability, availability and maintainability of services. Our model considers several scenarios that could impact service performance, such as changes in system parameters, network infrastructure, and supportability policies. We also discuss the challenges in implementing our proposed model and identify opportunities for future research to enhance the accuracy and usability of the model. Overall, our proposed model provides a useful tool for service providers to evaluate and improve the reliability, availability, maintainability, and supportability of their services, thereby enhancing customer satisfaction and reducing operational costs.

To address the shortcomings of the evolution of the fragmentation theme and the evolution of the network structure itself in the cooperation network, this paper introduces the ideas and techniques of complex network research. It firstly discovers the whole time-slice network, and then introduces BLPA (Balanced Label Propagation Algorithm) to extract the mobile author nodes and the corresponding community theme and the mobile author node theme based on community discovery. A research method combining vertical theme distribution and horizontal theme evolution is designed to analyze the interaction evolution mechanism or law between theme evolution and community evolution. The experiment found that there are theme differences between different communities in the same time-slice, the mobility of co-workers tends to be dispersed, the mobile author nodes guide the theme change, and the theme evolution driven by community evolution is in line with the overall theme evolution trend. This method makes use of complex network related technologies to explore the intrinsic dynamic mechanism of community evolution, community theme evolution and evolution on DBLP datasets, which is realistically feasible.

Most of image quality assessment methods are designed for grayscale images on a single domain. Therefore, they do not sufficiently make use of image color and multi-domain information that could provide valuable insights on the human visual mechanisms. In this paper, we propose a new No-reference Image Quality metric named WG-LAB, based on extraction of a set of features from distorted images in multiple domains (i.e., wavelet, and gradient domains) and multiple color channels (i.e., L, a, and b). Features are then exploited using Relevance Vector Machine Algorithm (RVM). The predictive performances of our method have been evaluated and compared to subjective judgments in terms of correlation, monotonicity and accuracy using the LIVE image database release 2 (LIVE II). The predictive performances obtained for our metric show that it has interesting features when compared to an array of existing full-reference (FR) and no-reference (NR) metrics on LIVE database.

This paper introduces an optimal tracking control method, which can be used for a general class of nonlinear system. The method is based on an idea of iterative approximating. The original nonlinear system can be obtained by a series of linear time-varying systems after iterations. In this paper, limited time optimal tracking control method is used to linear time-varying system in every iterative process, which can obtain the optimal tracking control law to every linear time-varying system. After a certain number of iterations, the optimal tracking control law to the original nonlinear system can be achieved. The main advantage of this method is that it is not directly handle with the original nonlinear system, so it can avoid the complex mathematics process to nonlinear system. In the paper, this optimal control method is used to the mini unmanned helicopter, and the effectiveness of the method is verified by numerical simulation.

This paper proposes a Lithium Battery State of Charge (SOC) Estimation method based on the Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF) algorithm. The State of Charge of batteries is an important parameter for the efficient operation and management of battery systems. This method employs a mathematical model of Lithium batteries that incorporates discharge characteristics to predict SOC. Moreover, an integrated circuit modeling technique utilizing Kalman filters is employed to estimate SOC. The proposed method's performance is evaluated by comparing the estimated SOC values with the actual values, and the results indicate that the method is effective in accurately estimating the SOC of Lithium batteries. Overall, the proposed method provides an efficient and reliable approach for estimating the SOC of Lithium batteries, which can be utilized in various applications.

In this paper, we propose an adaptive neural network dynamic surface control method for the post-capture tethered spacecraft. The post-capture tethered spacecraft system is a crucial technology for space-based missions, and the control of space vehicles is highly challenging due to the presence of uncertainties and aerodynamics. To overcome these challenges, we introduce adaptation models and neural networks to the control system. The adaptation models are used to estimate the uncertainties of the system, while the neural networks are employed to approximate the unknown dynamics of the post-capture tethered spacecraft. The dynamic surface control method is then used to ensure global stability of the system. The proposed control scheme is tested on a simulated orbital scenario and the results demonstrate that the method can achieve precise tracking control of the spacecraft's orbits. In summary, our work provides an effective method for the control of post-capture tethered spacecraft, which can enhance the performance and reliability of space-based missions.

Edge computing has become increasingly popular due to its ability to offer faster and more efficient data processing. However, with its rapidly increasing popularity comes the need for accurate benchmark testing and performance evaluation of different edge computing platforms. This paper presents EdgeBench, a benchmarking framework aimed at evaluating the performance of various edge computing platforms for image edge detection tasks. The proposed framework uses pipelines for testing multiple architectures and configurations to get accurate and reliable results. The results of the benchmark testing can be used to compare different edge computing platforms, facilitating better decision-making for selecting the right edge computing platform for specific applications. The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of benchmark testing for edge computing platforms and how the EdgeBench framework can contribute to the growth of the field of edge computing.

This paper proposes an implementable accelerated alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for low-rank tensor completion. The proposed method leverages acceleration techniques to enhance the convergence rate and utilizes convex functions to obtain efficient solutions. Specifically, the proposed method employs acceleration to minimize the objective function, which involves the sum of a convex function and a non-smooth term. Furthermore, the proposed method utilizes the ADMM algorithm to convert the original optimization problem into a series of sub-problems, which can be effectively solved through matrix decomposition techniques. The convergence analysis of the proposed method is presented, showing that it can converge to a global optimal solution. The proposed method has been implemented on the Microsoft Windows platform for experimental validation. Results show that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of convergence rate and solution quality.

This paper presents a performance analysis of radar signals encoded with random sequences. The use of random sequences for radar encoding has gained increasing attention due to its ability to improve the shape and peak to average power ratio (PAPR) of radar pulses. The maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method is employed to estimate the parameters of the random sequence encoded radar signals. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by comparing the detection and tracking performance of random sequence encoded radar signals with that of conventional radar signals. The results indicate that random sequence encoding can significantly improve the performance of radar systems, especially in the presence of interference and noise. Furthermore, the proposed method is shown to enhance the robustness of radar receivers to environmental factors, making it a promising method for practical radar applications.

Radar-based environment mapping is considered as one of the key technology for highly automated driving. This paper presents an efficient radar map generation based on newly proposed Doppler coherent focusing Direction-Of-Arrival (DOA) method. This method consists of Doppler coherent Angle-Of-Interest (AOI) prediction and DOA steering vector adaptation. The simulation shows that the proposed DOA methods outperformed the conventional approach in both computational cost and radar grid map resolution. In addition, real data obtained from a 77GHz radar sensor are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach practically.

This paper presents a method for controller validation utilizing data-driven control and mathematical models. The approach begins with reference model selection and utilizes computational modeling to obtain data models for the system. The method then uses interpolation to generate a mathematical model for the system which can be used for stability analysis and frequency-domain analysis. By analyzing the frequency response of the system, the paper demonstrates the potential for data-driven control to optimize controller design. The application of this method is demonstrated through the use of Loewner data-driven control, with results showing a significant improvement in the performance of the system. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to controller validation using data-driven control and mathematical models.

This paper proposes a low-complexity online model adaptation algorithm which dynamically selects an object detection algorithm among given/implemented algorithms in the system depending on workload-backlog. As well-studied in literature, there exists tradeoff between object detection accuracy and computation time (i.e., delay) because highly accurate algorithms generally take more time due to complicated deep neural network architectures. In our proposed algorithm, the accuracy is reformulated as reward; and the delay is modeled with queue. Based on this queue-based model, Lyapunov control inspired stochastic optimization is utilized for designing time-average reward maximization subject to stability in real-time object detection deep learning platforms. Moreover, our proposed algorithm solves closed-form equation in each model selection interval, thus the proposed algorithm takes low computational complexity. The performance of our proposed algorithm is evaluated via data-intensive real-world implementations under heavy workloads; and is verified that our proposed algorithm works as desired.

The understanding of the Broken Rotor Bar (BRB) features frequencies and amplitudes has a great importance for all diagnostic methods. These characteristics frequencies shows a drawbacks under varying load condition. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) has been widely used to achieve these requirements, because of its efficiency. However, this paper present an enhancing of the fault detection based on a Machine Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) method. Indeed, the use of Sparse Autoencoder (AE) with the combination of Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) shown a good accuracy. Furthermore, the extraction of the new features to use in multi-class classification for the healthy and faulty Induction Motor (IM) is presented.

Lip reading, the ability to recognize text information from the movement of a speaker's mouth, is a difficult and challenging task. Recently, the end-to-end model that maps a variable-length sequence of video frames to text performs poorly in real life situation where people unintentionally move the lips instead of speaking. The goal of this work is to improve the performance of lip reading task in real life. The model proposed in this article consists of two networks that are visual to audio feature network and audio feature to text network. Our experiments showed that the model proposed in this article can achieve 92.76% accuracy in lip reading task on the dataset that the unintentional lips movement was added.

In recent years, interdisciplinary research has become increasingly important due to the complex and interconnected nature of many issues facing society today. However, finding experts in multiple fields who can collaborate effectively can be a challenge. To address this issue, data mining approaches such as clustering algorithms and feature extraction can be used to identify experts who work in related fields or share similar research interests. Coupling these methods with collaboration tools can facilitate knowledge discovery and the development of interdisciplinary projects. Mathematical models and partitioning algorithms can also be used to identify experts with complementary skills and facilitate productive collaborations. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the various data mining approaches and techniques that can be utilized to discover experts for multidisciplinary research, highlighting their strengths and limitations. The findings of this study hold significant implications for the development of interdisciplinary research teams and the advancement of knowledge in a range of fields.

The wide application of mobile terminals has given rise to a large number of trajectory data. These data record spatio-temporal mobility of mobile objects and have important value for urban planning, traffic congestion detection, and other applications. In view of the important reference value of the trajectory data for commercial location selection, this paper proposes the search model of the region with the maximum coverage value based on trajectory data, which aims to maximize the sum of weights of sampling points covered by circular regions. The model considers the difference between the sampling points of different users and the interaction between the sampling points of the same user so as to adapt to different application scenarios such as location selection of signal stations and location selection of shopping malls. In order to further improve computing performance, this paper proposes two distributed schemes for this model. Finally, the extensive experiments on three real data sets demonstrated that the distributed schemes outperformed the centralized scheme and the application scenarios of the two schemes are summarized based on the experimental results.

This paper investigates the use of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in physical layer network coded parallel relay channels. The focus is on the relays and their impact on the throughput in wireless sensor networks. NOMA is a promising technique for improving spectral efficiency and reducing interference, but its effectiveness in relay channels has not been extensively studied. Through simulations, the paper demonstrates that network coding combined with NOMA can significantly improve the transmission rate and reduce interference. Furthermore, the use of relay nodes enhances the performance of the NOMA scheme by reducing the impact of noise and improving the signal to noise ratio. Overall, the results suggest that physical layer network coded parallel relay channels using NOMA can provide significant benefits for wireless networks, particularly in scenarios where multiple users are competing for resources.

Exoskeleton robot is a system with human-machine interaction and could help human to carry heavy load. Series elastic actuators (SEAs) in force-controlled robots can achieve compliant interactions with humans. In order to get flexible position and force control, this paper introduced impedance control into exoskeleton robot and use a recurrent neural network to improve the adaptive ability of the system. Finally, simulation results of force tracking and trajectory tracking are presented. By setting virtual impedance parameters, this controller can achieve stable track tracking and force tracking. Recurrent neural network can improve the performance of adaptability and robustness.

We consider a class of nonlinear equations that are related to the numerical solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for dynamic programming. Equations of this class can be solved with a simple fixed-point iteration, however this method may have slow convergence. We present two main contributions for increasing the efficiency of the solution: a simple preconditioning, inspired by the Jacobi method, and a selective node update procedure that reduces the number of required elementary operations.

Image captioning has become an increasingly interesting topic in the field of computer vision. The ability to automatically describe the contents of an image is a challenging task that requires the integration of various techniques such as feature extraction, task analysis, decoding, and proposal generation. In this paper, we propose a cascade semantic fusion approach to address the challenges faced in image captioning. Our method involves the fusion of semantic information from different sources, such as detectors and proposals, at different stages of the image captioning process. These sources help us extract useful features from the images and provide us with additional information to better understand the contents of the image. Furthermore, our approach involves visualization to better understand the inner workings of the system. We conduct a task analysis of our method and evaluate our approach on standard benchmark datasets. Our results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing methods, in terms of both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has become increasingly popular with the rise of smart homes, autonomous vehicles, and other connected devices. However, the security of these devices has become a major concern as they can be easily hacked or compromised. In this paper, we propose a Secure IoT Architecture enabled by Software-Defined Networking (SDN) to enhance the security of IoT infrastructures. Our architecture employs logic gates and authentication protocols to ensure proper access control and prevent malicious activities. Furthermore, we incorporate control systems to manage and monitor the network traffic to prevent data leakage and unauthorized access. The use of SDN in our architecture provides flexibility, agility and scalability, making it suitable for various IoT applications. Our proposed architecture provides a comprehensive solution to address the security challenges posed by IoT devices and enables users to have better control over their data and devices.

Electrical energy has become the most vital resource in our modern world. However, its access to all parts of the world especially rural areas has not been accomplished. At the same time, rapid exhaustion of fossil fuels, GHG emissions have posed a threat to energy generation. Thus, there is great need to not only find alternate means of energy generation, but also to make it available to all parts of the world. Solar energy is a potential energy source capable of completely resolving our energy demands, but still remains the most underutilized energy resource. In this paper, a standalone solar PV system is developed for a village school as a part of project and awareness initiative for solar energy. The system is designed and simulated using PVsyst 6.7 software. To enhance the system efficiency, maximum power must be extracted. To obtain this, Maximum power point (MPP) tracker is designed, and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK. For more enhancement in extraction of solar power, a prototype model for dual axis tracker with self-cleaning feature is designed and simulated on PROTEUS 8 software.

This paper presents a wireless powered implantable and flexible neural recording and stimulating system based on NFC protocol. The proposed system utilizes wireless communication and implantable electrodes to monitor and stimulate neural activities. The system is designed to be flexible and easily adjustable to fit different neural interfaces. The wireless communication capabilities of the system are achieved by employing near field communication protocols. The system is also equipped with wireless sensor networks that enable remote monitoring and data collection. Overall, the proposed system offers an efficient and reliable framework for neural recording and stimulation, making it a promising solution for a wide range of applications in neural engineering.

Hashing has been recognized as an efficient representation learning method to effectively handle big data due to its low computational complexity and memory cost. Most of the existing hashing methods focus on learning the low-dimensional vectorized binary features based on the high-dimensional raw vectorized features. However, the studies on how to obtain preferable binary codes from the original 2D image features for retrieval is very limited. This paper proposes a bilinear supervised discrete hashing (BSDH) method based on 2D image features which utilizes bilinear projections to binarize the image matrix features such that the intrinsic characteristics in the 2D image space are preserved in the learned binary codes. Meanwhile, the bilinear projection approximation and vectorization binary codes regression are seamlessly integrated together to formulate the final robust learning framework. Furthermore, a discrete optimization strategy is developed to alternatively update each variable for obtaining the high-quality binary codes. In addition, two 2D image features, traditional SURF-based FVLAD feature, and CNN-based AlexConv5 feature are designed for further improving the performance of the proposed BSDH method. The results of extensive experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets show that the proposed BSDH method almost outperforms all competing hashing methods with different input features by different evaluation protocols.

Biomedical named entity recognition (biomedical NER) is a core component to build biomedical text processing systems, such as biomedical information retrieval and question answering systems. Recently, many studies based on machine learning have been developed for a biomedical NER. The machine learning-based approaches generally require significant amounts of annotated corpora to achieve high performance. However, it is expensive to manually create a large number of high-quality corpora due to the demand for biomedical experts. In addition, most existing corpora have focused on several specific sub-domains, such as disease, protein, and species. It is difficult for a biomedical NER system trained with these corpora to provide much information for biomedical text processing systems. In this paper, we propose a method for automatically generating the machine-labeled biomedical NER corpus that covers various sub-domains by using proper categories from the semantic groups of a unified medical language system (UMLS). We use a bootstrapping approach with a small amount of manually annotated corpus to automatically generate a significant amount of corpus and then construct a biomedical NER system trained with the machine-labeled corpus. At last, we train two machine learning-based classifiers, conditional random fields (CRFs) and long short-term memory (LSTM), with the machine-labeled data to improve performance. The experimental results show that the proposed method is effective to improve performance. As a result, the proposed one obtains higher performance in 23.69% than the model that trained only a small amount of manually annotated corpus in F1-score.

The MPSC (Multiple-Perspective Semantics-Crossover) model is a novel approach for matching sentences using natural language processing and computational modeling. The model incorporates multiple perspectives for semantics processing, including task analysis, analytical models, feature extraction, and data mining. By using a crossover approach, the model is able to combine the benefits of multiple perspective semantic processing for more accurate sentence matching. The MPSC model holds great promise for natural language processing applications, in particular for tasks related to sentence matching and semantic processing.

"Modeling and Simulation for Multi Energy Flow Coupled Network Computing" focuses on the development and application of computational modeling techniques to multi-energy flow coupled networks. The paper highlights the importance of couplings between different types of energy flows, such as fluids and power systems, and showcases analytical models that have been developed to simulate and analyze these complex systems. The mathematical models and simulations presented in this paper can aid in the prediction and control of power system dynamics, as well as improve the operation and efficiency of pumps and other related equipment. Overall, this paper demonstrates the value of computational modeling in the design and optimization of multi-energy flow coupled networks.

This paper presents a review of Thread-Level Speculation (TLS) and discusses various perspectives on its applications. TLS is a technique that helps to improve the performance of multi-threaded programs by speculatively executing threads with predicted outcomes. The paper covers a range of topics associated with the use of TLS, including instruction sets, predictive and analytical models, training, feature extraction, computational modeling, and data models. The use of TLS enables faster and more efficient execution of multi-threaded programs, thereby enhancing their overall performance. The paper highlights how TLS can be applied to various real-world scenarios and provides insights into the latest developments and future areas of exploration concerning TLS. Overall, the use of TLS for multi-threaded programs seems promising and offers numerous potential avenues for research and development.

This paper presents a deep learning-based approach to detect and classify persons in video data captured from distances of several miles via a high-power lens video camera. For detection, a set of computationally efficient image processing steps are considered to identify moving areas that contain a person. These areas are then passed onto a convolutional neural network classifier whose convolutional layers consist of the GoogleNet transfer learning. Despite the challenges associated with the video dataset examined in terms of the low resolution of persons appearing in the video data and the presence of heat haze and camera shaking, the developed approach generated 90% classification accuracy.

This paper proposes a modified robust model reference adaptive system scheme for a speed sensorless vector control of induction motors. The focus is on adaptation models for the rotors and stators of the motor. The proposed scheme is designed to handle various uncertainties in the system, such as resistance variations and parameter uncertainties. A mathematical model is developed for the motor, and a computational modeling approach is used to simulate the system's performance. The proposed scheme is found to be effective in regulating the speed of the motor and improving the accuracy of the control system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to other conventional control approaches, making it a promising methodology for speed sensorless vector control of induction motors.

Global growth in participation in higher education has helped to increase diversity of students, and traditionally underrepresented minorities on gender, income and math skills have expanded their presence in engineering education. Nevertheless, late dropout has increased and the number of engineering graduates remains low in western world. The analysis of educational trajectories using process mining techniques can help to explain the relationship between a sequence of academic results and late dropout. This case study seeks to answer how gender, income and entry math skills may explain differences on educational trajectories of engineering students in high-failure rate courses that lead to late dropout. Academic records for 794 engineering students at Universidad Austral de Chile that belongs to cohorts 2007 to 2009, were extracted and analyzed using process mining discovery techniques. Models of educational trajectories on high-failure rate courses were created and then analyzed using the Investment Model as a reference framework. Findings reveal the following: late dropout is related to the number of consecutive semesters that a student maintain pending failed courses; low-income students and those with low entry math skills tend to be more persistent, even if they have unsatisfactory trajectories; female students tend to be more risk-averse when they have unsatisfactory results. Understanding the educational trajectories of students who end in late dropout can help managers and policy makers to improve the curriculum, entry conditions and programs that support disadvantaged students.

This paper proposes a domain decomposition method for solving simplified volume-surface integral equations in the context of dielectrics. The method is based on transmission line matrix methods and involves the use of mathematical models to evaluate the surface impedance. The proposed method ensures convergence of the solution while reducing computational cost. The scattering problem is solved by dividing the domain into smaller subdomains and using a transmission line matrix approach to solve each subdomain. The method is applied to a variety of dielectric structures and compared to other numerical methods. Overall, the proposed domain decomposition method shows promise as an efficient and accurate approach for solving simplified volume-surface integral equations in the context of dielectrics.

This article presents the design and prototype implementation of a low-cost and short-range self-powered wireless IoT device based on energy harvesting for both indoor and outdoor applications. Prototyped devices are deployed in a star network configuration with a custom protocol. Based on measurements, devices achieve a line-of-sight range of 228.5m above 40m from the ground level. Nodes are powered based on energy harvesting from a small 0.36W solar panel and 120mAh lithium button cell as storage elements. The test in the well-lit room shows an average harvested power of 941.94μW over a period of 2.5 days, while under the low lighting conditions showed an average of 212μW over a period of 24h. From measurements, a fully charged rechargeable 120mAh cell lasts for 278 days with 55s transmission interval. Temperature, visible lights level and relative humidity sensors are integrated into the nodes.

This paper proposes a multiple-layer representation learning model for network-based attack detection, which utilizes deep learning techniques and feature extraction methods to improve the accuracy and scalability of intrusion detection systems. The model is designed to learn high-level representations of network traffic data, which can be used to identify abnormal behaviors and potential attacks. The approach involves multiple layers of feature extraction and transformation, enabling the system to efficiently process large volumes of data in real-time. The paper also discusses the importance of data models and their role in facilitating the learning process. Several experiments were conducted using a forestry dataset, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed approach over traditional intrusion detection methods. Overall, this study highlights the potential for deep learning techniques to enhance network security and improve the detection of cyber threats.

This paper proposes a novel approach to optimize numerical mesh truncation boundary conditions in finite element analysis using machine learning algorithms. The accuracy of the numerical results in finite element analysis largely depends on the proper selection of boundary conditions. However, the traditional method of selecting boundary conditions based on trial and error is time-consuming and inefficient. To overcome this limitation, we propose a prediction algorithm based on machine learning to identify an optimal set of boundary conditions. Our approach was tested on patch antennas, and the results showed that the proposed method significantly reduced the computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. In conclusion, this paper demonstrates the potential of machine learning algorithms in improving the efficiency and accuracy of numerical simulations in electromagnetic fields.

Recently several deep learning approaches have been attempted to detect malware binaries using convolutional neural networks and stacked deep autoencoders. Although they have shown respectable performance on a large corpus of dataset, practical defense systems require precise detection during the malware outbreaks where only a handful of samples are available. This paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the latent representations obtained through the adversarial autoencoder for malware outbreak detection. Using instruction sequence distribution mapped to a semantic latent vector, the model provides a highly effective neural signature that helps detecting variants of a previously identified malware within a campaign mutated with minor functional upgrade, function shuffling, or slightly modified obfuscations. The method demonstrates how adversarial autoencoder can turn a multiclass classification task into a clustering problem when the sample set size is limited and the distribution is biased. The model performance is evaluated on OS X malware dataset against traditional machine learning models.

We present a novel design of soft gripper, which can be applied on smooth surfaces like glass as well as the fabric materials through the integration of a thermoresponsive microstructured adhesive layer that switches between Velcro-like and gecko-like adhesion mechanisms. A shape memory polymer (SMP) is integrated along with metallic foil heaters, thin film polyester strain limiting layers, and a silicone pneunet via simple but effective methods. Fabrication can be done outside a cleanroom with low cost and integration of silicone bonded directly to rigid thermoplastics is dramatically simplified using an industrial silicone adhesive that bonds many rigid polymers and metals to silicone rubbers. Experiments show that the gripper can be switched to exhibit high adhesion to a bare glass beaker or a fabric coated beaker of the same diameter using the thermoresponsive Velcro-like adhesive layer and an embedded thin film heater.

The development of Vehicular Ad-hoc NETwork (VANET) has brought many conveniences to human beings, but also brings a very prominent security problem. The traditional solution to the security problem is based on centralized approach which requires a trusted central entity which exists a single point of failure problem. Moreover, there is no approach of technical level to ensure security of data. Therefore, this paper proposes a security architecture of VANET based on blockchain and mobile edge computing. The architecture includes three layers, namely perception layer, edge computing layer and service layer. The perception layer ensures the security of VANET data in the transmission process through the blockchain technology. The edge computing layer provides computing resources and edge cloud services to the perception layer. The service layer uses the combination of traditional cloud storage and blockchain to ensure the security of data.

This paper investigates high dimensional inference through the use of random maximum a-posteriori (MAP) perturbations. Perturbation methods are applied to a set of random variables within the optimization objective, allowing for the efficient exploration of high-dimensional spaces without the need for exhaustive computations. Distribution functions are utilized to better understand the behavior of perturbations and their impact on the optimization process. The proposed method is evaluated through experiments on image segmentation tasks, where MAP estimation is used to optimize the problem objective. Results show that the use of perturbations improves the convergence rate of the optimization algorithm and achieves better segmentation accuracy. Finally, the concept of entropy is explored as a way to quantitatively analyze the effect of perturbations on high-dimensional inference. These findings suggest that random MAP perturbations have the potential to significantly improve computational efficiency and accuracy in high-dimensional inference problems.

As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to expand, the need for low latency and high-performance computing solutions becomes increasingly important. Fog computing, which acts as an intermediary layer between the cloud and the edge, has emerged as a promising solution for achieving ultra-low latency. In this paper, we propose a Smart Gateway Based Multi-Tier Service-Oriented Fog Computing Architecture for achieving ultra-low latency in IoT applications. The architecture incorporates logic gates to ensure efficient data processing, while sensors provide real-time data to the fog nodes. We evaluate the performance of the architecture using computational modeling and demonstrate its efficacy compared to cloud and edge computing. Our results show that the proposed architecture achieves significantly lower latency and better performance, making it a viable solution for real-time IoT applications.

In this paper, we consider a two-way relay (TWR) visible light communication (VLC) system consisting of two users which communicate to each other with the help of a relay. To achieve efficient transmission, we introduce network coding (NC) into VLC system and we develop two energy-efficient NC-based strategies, namely straightforward network coding over finite-alphabet sets (SNCF) scheme and physical-layer network coding over finite-alphabet sets (PNCF) scheme, which need three time slots and two time slots respectively to achieve the communication. Simulation results indicate that our proposed SNCF scheme and PNCF scheme both can achieve great performance gains over the traditional four time-slot transmission scheme.

This paper introduces a Wordnet-based approach for mining criminal networks in cybercrime investigations. The proposed method utilizes data mining techniques to analyze social networking activity online, specifically in the context of computer crime. Clustering algorithms are employed to identify groups of individuals who may be connected through criminal activity. This approach has significant implications for law enforcement, as it can aid in the identification and prosecution of cybercriminals. Additionally, natural language processing techniques are utilized to identify criminal law terminology and patterns within online communications. Overall, this Wordnet-based approach provides a valuable tool for investigating cybercrime and can enhance the capabilities of law enforcement agencies in detecting and preventing criminal activity.

In elastic optical networks (EONs), impairment-aware routing, modulation level, and spectrum assignment strategies are essential for efficient network resource utilization and reliable service provisioning. In this paper, we investigate the problem of impairment-aware manycast routing, modulation level, and spectrum assignment (IMR-MLSA) in EONs. Particularly, we consider a scenario where the traffic demands are many-to-many communication, which requires efficient multicast or broadcast routing techniques. We propose a three-stage heuristic algorithm to address the IMR-MLSA problem, which includes traffic grooming, multicast routing, and modulation level and spectrum allocation. To overcome the impact of physical impairments in EONs, we introduce the concept of throughput margin and a lightpath adaptation mechanism. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in terms of network throughput, spectrum efficiency, and outage probability. The proposed algorithm is generic and applicable for a wide range of optical fiber network architectures, including erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs). In summary, this paper provides a valuable insight into impairment-aware manycast routing, modulation level, and spectrum assignment in EONs, which is of great importance for the design and optimization of future optical networks.

Most existing approaches to anomaly detection focus on statistical features of the data. However, in many cases, users are merely interested in a subset of the statistical outliers depending on the specific domain of interest, e.g., network attacks or financial fraud. The instruction from human experts is therefore indispensable in building predictive models in such applications. However, obtaining labels from human experts is time-consuming and expensive. Obtaining labels from nonexpert labelers are relatively easy and cost-effective. However, the labeling accuracy of a nonexpert is usually difficult to assess. Therefore, it remains open to leverage both the machine intelligence and the knowledge from labelers with diverse backgrounds to construct a machine learning model for domain-specific anomaly detection. To this end, this paper proposes a framework of tripartite active learning for interactive anomaly discovery in large datasets based on crowdsourced labels. This tripartite active learning method consists of two stages. In the first stage, an unsupervised learning algorithm is employed to extract statistical outliers from the dataset. This algorithm is of low computational complexity as well as memory requirement and thus well suited for large datasets. We then develop an iterative algorithm consisting of two steps. The algorithm first evaluates and trains labelers based on gold instances provided by the expert labelers. Then, it assigns the most informative samples to its most confident labeler for relabeling and update the detector based on new labels. The capacity constraints are taken into account in the active learning approach to guarantee the fair allocation of labeling instances as well as robustness against erroneous labels. It is seen through experiments that the proposed algorithm provides an effective means for interactive anomaly detection. As far as we are aware of, this is the first work that considers designing a tripartite machine learning system for domain-specific anomaly detection.

In this paper, a fuzzy supervisor for the neural emulation of MIMO nonlinear processes is proposed. The focus of the paper is on MIMO communication systems and how to emulate them using heuristic algorithms. The goal is to achieve convergence of the emulation process by identifying appropriate indexes to be used by the neural networks. The paper presents a method for selecting appropriate indexes based on the complexity of the nonlinear system being emulated. The method involves the use of fuzzy logic to determine the most suitable set of indexes for the task. The proposed approach was tested using simulation studies, and the results showed that it can successfully emulate MIMO nonlinear systems with good accuracy. The paper concludes that this fuzzy supervisor approach is effective in helping to achieve convergence in neural emulation of MIMO nonlinear processes.

We present a general and computationally tractable method for the operation of a Backwards Information Filter on a linear Gaussian Mixture Model system, which can be used to generate the smoothed density. Unlike other methods, the algorithm proposed here does not make unimodal approximations, and is exact with the exception of the mode reduction strategy.

Wireless body area networks (WBANs) have become increasingly important for healthcare applications, where sensors are implanted or placed on the body to monitor patient vital signs. In this context, an efficient and reliable routing protocol is essential for timely and accurate transmission of data. This paper presents an efficient and reliable directed diffusion routing protocol for WBANs, which utilizes the concept of data-centric routing. The proposed protocol uses a directional gradient mechanism for routing and effective data transmission. It outperforms existing protocols in terms of energy consumption, packet delivery ratio, and end-to-end delay. The simulation results show that the proposed protocol achieves a significantly higher packet delivery ratio and lower end-to-end delay under various WBAN scenarios. Therefore, the proposed directed diffusion protocol can be considered a promising solution for reliable and efficient data communication in WBANs, and it has the potential for applications in other wireless communication networks.

This survey paper discusses the various runtime models used for analyzing and evaluating the quality attributes of self-adaptive software. The paper delves into the different analytical models and adaptation models that are widely used in the software industry. It examines how these models are used to provide insights into the behavior of self-adaptive software at runtime. Additionally, the paper highlights the importance of synthetic aperture sonar for analyzing and evaluating software quality attributes. The authors also discuss the role of software and computational modeling for achieving the desired quality attributes of self-adaptive software. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the various runtime models that are crucial for analyzing and evaluating the quality attributes of self-adaptive software.

This paper presents small-gain results for time-delay systems composed of n subsystems. The input-to-output practically stable (IOpS) and unboundedness observable (UO) of the subsystems are assumed, and the time-delay system can be proved to be IOpS and UO as long as the proposed small-gain condition is satisfied.

This paper proposes an efficient channel estimation technique for Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) systems. Channel estimation is a crucial step in the process of receiving and decoding downlink signals. Several techniques have been proposed to enhance the accuracy of channel estimation in NB-IoT systems. However, the estimation error still remains a critical issue due to the limited signal to noise ratio (SNR). The proposed technique utilizes the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) technique to mitigate the inter-carrier interference caused by frequency offsets. The proposed technique achieves an efficient estimation of a frequency-selective fading channel even under a low SNR environment. The simulation results show that the proposed technique outperforms the 3GPP typical channel estimation method and reduces the estimation error significantly. Overall, this paper presents an effective solution to enhance the performance of NB-IoT systems in terms of channel estimation accuracy.

This paper discusses the optimal configuration of interdependence between communication networks and power grid in the context of power system faults and protection. The robustness of the interdependent infrastructure is crucial as it can influence the system's performance during a crisis. The emergence of smart grids and the incorporation of renewable energy sources intensify the need for robust communication network and power grid interdependence. The paper highlights the importance of balancing the communication infrastructure's capacity and the power system's load requirements to achieve optimal interdependence configuration. The research findings shed light on the significance of robust communication infrastructure and its positive impact on ensuring grid resilience during system failures. The discussion of this topic is vital for policymakers, power industry players, and researchers as they continually seek to enhance the reliability of the power grid and associated communication networks.

Heartbeats and a blink are two major physiological signals that provide crucial information on our stress and drowsiness. Hence, it is highly demanded to detect simultaneously heartbeats and blinks in many applications. A Doppler sensor could be a key device to facilitate the non-contact heartbeat and blink detection in daily life. Although many Doppler sensor-based heartbeat and blink detection methods have been independently proposed, when heartbeats and blinks are detected simultaneously with one Doppler sensor, the detection accuracies of such heartbeat and blink detection methods get degraded because of at least two issues: (i) the low SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) of each signal reflected from a subject's chest and face, and (ii) the similarity of the spectrum distribution of heartbeats and a blink. In this paper, we propose a spectrogram-based simultaneous heartbeat and blink detection using one Doppler sensor. In the proposed method, to extract the spectra that might be due to heartbeats and a blink, the spectra on a spectrogram are integrated. Blink detection is then performed by classifying the peaks of the integrated spectrum into a peak due to a blink or a non-blink based on a supervised machine learning classifier trained with a set of the time domain and the time-frequency domain features. Based on the non-blink peaks, heartbeats are detected considering the RRI (R-R Interval) estimated before the investigated peak to prevent the incorrect heartbeat detection. Through the experiments in the case where microwaves are transmitted from one Doppler sensor toward a body including a chest and a face, our proposal has been shown to be able to simultaneously detect heartbeats and blinks with high accuracy.

A novel method that extracts only regions in products from product images used in consumer-to-consumer (C2C) online marketplaces or auctions is proposed. The proposed method automatically extracts product regions by using GrabCut based on fact that product regions tend to be found in the center part of images. Although GrabCut is known as an interactive segmentation technique, the proposed method automates procedure of extraction by generating an initial seed of GrabCut. To evaluate effectiveness of the proposed method, with 138 product images including 114 images obtained from a C2C online marketplace, the extraction accuracy of the proposed method was compared with that of the interactive GrabCut. The result shows that the extraction accuracy of the proposed method is 2.3 % lower than that of the interactive GrabCut. However, statistically significant difference in the extraction accuracy disappeared. In other words, the proposed method is effective in enabling automation for extraction without significantly degrading the extraction accuracy.

Sentiment analysis of Twitter data has recently become an important research topic due to the explosive growth of social media use. Twitter, being one of the most popular social media platforms, provides an ideal source of data for sentiment analysis. In order to analyze these large volumes of data, data models and mining techniques are employed. Machine learning algorithms and classification algorithms are the most commonly used techniques in sentiment analysis. Among these algorithms, Support Vector Machines (SVMs) have been found to be highly effective in accurately classifying the sentiment of Twitter data. This paper explores the different data models and mining techniques that have been developed for analyzing Twitter data along with a comparison of various machine learning and classification algorithms used in sentiment analysis, highlighting the effectiveness of SVMs in this context. The paper also discusses the challenges faced in sentiment analysis of Twitter data and outlines some future directions for research in this field.

Material degradation is a significant issue that requires detection and diagnosis for proper maintenance and repair. This paper proposes a neural network model for material degradation detection and diagnosis using microscopic images. The model uses histograms to extract features from the images which are then fed into a convolutional neural network for classification. The focus of this study is on the detection of degradation caused by creep in power generation systems. The proposed methodology employs deep learning techniques to enable accurate classification and diagnosis of material degradation. Results show that the proposed model outperforms traditional image processing techniques and offers a promising approach for material degradation detection and diagnosis in power generation systems.

Most user interfaces require motion; the motor-impaired therefore do not have many options to choose from. Electroencephalography (EEG) and the analysis of eye movement are two of the commonly proposed methods for enhancing the user experiences of the motor-impaired. In this paper, we propose an electrooculography (EOG)/EEG-based hybrid BCI that combines the strengths of EOG and EEG by using them simultaneously. We have shown the effectiveness of EOG/EEG-based hybrid BCIs by implementing the proposed interface and applying it to a chess game. Through this paper, we hope to provide improved interface systems for patients who have physical disabilities.

To promote efficient and flexible learning, a conceptual learning model can be developed using the differences between the stable features of various concepts, thereby allowing scalable and continuous learning concepts to be obtained from a small number of labeled samples. By using a stable feature expressed as a vector to represent each concept, the conceptual learning model can distinguish the representative feature of each concept, thus increasing the interpretability of the model. In addition to adjusting the mapping relationship between concept instances and concept stability features, constraints on the differences between stable features of different concepts are also introduced into the model. Because this constraint can improve the sensitivity of the instance features to the stable features of each concept, the proposed model has the ability to learn from a small number of samples. In this paper, sub-networks of the same structure were applied to learn each concept, and unified learning methods were used to achieve scalability and the ability to easily manage new concepts. By training the proposed model using the MNIST dataset, the model demonstrates that prediction accuracy of 96% can be achieved as a result of using 100 labeled training samples for each concept. Furthermore, the proposed model not only demonstrated an improved learning ability for small samples, but it was also found to considerably reduce the training time, with each concept requiring only 18 s on average. Thus, the small-sample and continuous learning capabilities of the proposed model enable the construction of a conceptual space that promotes improved knowledge representation and complex scene understanding.

In computer vision applications, accurate cost estimation of memory systems is crucial for achieving optimal performance. This paper proposes a methodology inspired by machine learning techniques that allows for accurate cost estimation of memory systems. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes task analysis and table lookup to identify the appropriate memory system for the given problem. The method also involves the use of registers and maximum likelihood estimation to fine-tune the cost estimation model. The accuracy of the proposed method was evaluated on various computer vision problems, and it was found to outperform traditional cost estimation techniques. Therefore, the proposed method can be highly beneficial in computer vision applications where memory system cost estimation plays a critical role in achieving optimal performance.

Inverse halftoning is a kind of technology which transforms binary images composed of black and white pixels to continuous-tone images. Many scholars have studied this problem so far, but the results are not satisfactory. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end deep convolutional neural network composed of two parts. The first part is the feature extraction part which consists of 4 convolution layers and 4 pooling layers to extract feature from the halftoning images. The second part is the reconstruction part which contains 4 deconvolution layers to reconstruct the continuous-tone images. A U-Net structure which concatenates the outputs from the feature extraction layers with deconvolution layers is used for better restoring the detail information of the original images. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the state-of-arts in terms of both visual quality and numerical evaluation.

Audio data is a highly rich form of information, often containing patterns with unique acoustic signatures. In pervasive sensing environments, because of the empowered smart devices, we have witnessed an increasing research interest in sound sensing to detect ambient environment, recognise users' daily activities, and infer their health conditions. However, the main challenge is that the real-world environment often contains multiple sound sources, which can significantly compromise the robustness of the above environment, event, and activity detection applications. In this paper, we explore different approaches in multi-sound classification, and propose a stacked classifier based on the recent advance in deep learning. We evaluate our proposed approach in a comprehensive set of experiments on both sound effect and real-world datasets. The results have demonstrated that our approach can robustly identify each sound category among mixed acoustic signals, without the need of any a priori knowledge about the number and signature of sounds in the mixed signals.

This paper aims to explore the thematic correlation of human cognition and artificial intelligence (AI) through the lens of psychology. The research methodology involves conducting interviews with experts in the fields of psychology and AI to determine the relationship between cognition and AI. Through analysis of the interviews, the authors found a significant correlation between human cognition and AI, particularly in regards to how cognition is changing to incorporate AI technologies. In addition, the authors examined the role of robots and buildings in the correlation between cognition and AI, and found that both robots and buildings play a significant role in shaping our understanding of AI and cognition. Overall, this study highlights the importance of understanding the relationship between cognition and AI, and how this relationship will continue to evolve in the future.

An intelligent backstepping control (BSC) using recurrent feature selection fuzzy neural network (RFSFNN) is proposed to construct a high-performance synchronous reluctance motor (SRM) position drive system. First, the dynamics of the SRM position drive system and the BSC are briefly introduced. However, the lumped uncertainty of the SRM is unavailable to obtain in advance. Therefore, an intelligent backstepping control using recurrent feature selection fuzzy neural network (IBSCRFSFNN), which combines the advantages of recurrent neural network, fuzzy logic system and feature selection method, is developed to approximate an idea BSC and to maintain the stability of SRM position drive system. The network structure and online learning algorithm of the IBSCRFSFNN are described in detail. At last, the proposed control system is implemented in a floating-point TMS320F28075 digital signal processor. The experimental results are illustrated to show the validity of the proposed intelligent BSC system.

This article presents the prototype design and testing of a long-range, self-powered IoT devices for use in precision agriculture and aquaponics. The devices are designed using the ultra-low power nRF52840 microcontroller with Bluetooth 5 support and ambient energy harvesting. A power of 942μW is harvested in an indoor environment. The devices are therefore suitable for both indoor and outdoor use, as natural sunlight will provide far more energy compared to artificial indoor lights. A line-of-sight range of up to 1.8km is achieved with the use of coded transmissions. However, the coverage area and range can be extended significantly by deploying the devices in multi-hop network topology. The custom multi-hop protocol provides energy efficient communication from any device in a wireless sensor network to a gateway while consuming an average of 267μW with a transmission interval of 5 minutes. The sensor data is transmitted to a gateway, which then forwards it to a local server or cloud service, where the data can be analyzed to optimize the production in agriculture and aquaponics.

Recently, the Massive Internet of Things (IoT) and Web of Things (WoT) are remarkable research fields aiming to facilitate the connectivity, accessibility, and control of the Things by Web standards and technologies for large-scale deployment. In such context, the end-user is capable of simply creating, mashing-up, and presenting the multiple Things to gain high-level information. However, current research approaches much more pay attention to describe a single Thing. The modeling and building the application for the compound objects consisting of groups of Things namely "Asset" are still limited due to the lack of description and seamless integration mechanism. Moreover, the traditional IoT Device Description Language directly installed on device is highly restricted in Massive IoT scenario because of stringent requirements for power consumption and operation cost. In this paper, we introduce the WoT based Asset Description (WoT-AD), a descriptive language for the Asset aiming to mitigate such limitations. WoT-AD explicitly describes a group of Things as homogeneous object to enable mash-up, self-discovery, and simply access their resources, entities, and services. We also provide a lightweight framework that fully integrates with WoT-AD to enable WoT for Massive IoT scenario. Such integration not only effectively models the Asset but also simplifies the development of mash-up application to different-skilled users. Finally, we evaluate the performance of our proposal to demonstrate its effectiveness and scalability in real use-case.

The aim of our research was to elaborate the current concept of the IoT based on the scientific papers up to now and to draw up the potential legal and security risks, which may affect the users or the state. We categorized the challenges of the IoT usage. The main problems in the aspect of data protection, are traceability and confidentiality issues.

This paper considers fixed-time consensus tracking of second-order multiagent systems (MASs) under directed interaction topology. A novel distributed observer is presented to estimate the leader's states within a fixed time, which overcomes the difficulties caused by the asymmetry of the Laplacian matrix. A sliding surface is designed and a nonsingular terminal sliding mode consensus protocol is developed to achieve fixed-time convergence of the tracking error to the origin. It is shown that each follower can track the leader's trajectory within a fixed time. Particularly, the gain of the presented consensus protocol is directly related to the prescribed time, which makes it convenient to determine and tune the gain according to the requirement of convergence time. Moreover, the presented control protocol reduces the conservativeness of the convergence time estimation for sliding motion. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed consensus scheme.

This paper presents a context-aware factorization machine for recommendation in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) using a combination of recommender systems, context modeling, data mining, mathematical models, electronic learning, and adaptation models. Recommender systems are widely used in the realm of electronic learning to suggest relevant materials to students, but often fail to take into account the context in which a student is learning. Context modeling is a solution to this limitation and involves understanding the context of the learner, such as the course enrolled in, their prior knowledge and interests, and the learning environment. The proposed factorization machine uses data mining techniques to extract meaningful patterns from student interaction data, and a mathematical model to predict the scores of new interactions. This model is then adapted to the individual learner's context with the use of adaptation models. The proposed approach aims to improve the effectiveness of recommendation systems in the context of MOOCs by providing personalized and context-aware recommendations.

Quality-aware task assignment is a critical issue for effective crowdsourcing in opportunistic network-based systems. In this paper, we focus on task analysis and propose a mathematical model for optimal task assignment, taking into account the quality of service requirements of tasks and the resource constraints of network nodes. Our approach utilizes time-frequency analysis for accurate task evaluation and selection. We also address the challenges of wireless fidelity and ad hoc networks by developing a decentralized task assignment algorithm that can effectively utilize available resources while minimizing communication overhead. Our experimental results show that our proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of task quality and network resource utilization. Overall, our work contributes to the development of efficient and quality-aware task assignment techniques for opportunistic network-based crowdsourcing.

Risk assessment is a central element for the development and validation of autonomous vehicles. It comprises a combination of occurrence probability and severity of future critical events. Time headway (TH) as well as time-to-contact (TTC) are commonly used risk metrics and have qualitative relations to occurrence probability. However, they lack theoretical derivations and additionally they are designed to only cover special types of traffic scenarios (e.g., longitudinal following between single car pairs). In this paper, we present a probabilistic situation risk model based on survival analysis considerations and extend it to naturally incorporate sensory, temporal, and behavioral uncertainties as they arise in real-world scenarios. The resulting risk spot detector (RSD) is applied and tested on naturalistic driving data of a multilane boulevard with several intersections, enabling the visualization of road criticality maps. Compared to TH and TTC, our approach is more selective and specific in predicting risk. RSD concentrates on driving sections of high vehicle density where large accelerations and decelerations or approaches with high velocity occur.

Even though several architectures have been in existence for over a decade, a new research model has to be created in order to solve the requirements (volume, velocity, and variety) and constraints that affect the intelligence of smart environments. Thus, the merge of computing technologies has made the collection of Big Data (BD) possible from the Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Data do not include only the information about the environments, but also the daily changes of information and so forth. In this context, We propose new business information architecture for BD and IoT (BDIoT). The proposed architecture uses context-aware computing and combines the Data WareHhouse (DWH) and Data Lake (DL) in order to benefit computing mechanisms. The BDIoT architecture is validated through use case related to E-health service (Alzheimer's disease).
