This paper presents an implementation technology of electromagnetic transient real-time simulation using HYPERSIM for large-scale grid systems. The approach involves task analysis, real-time systems, and computational modeling to simulate the behavior of power grids. An accurate load modeling technique is used to represent the dynamic response of loads to changes in the system. The implementation includes the modeling of HVDC transmission systems, which are increasingly used in modern power networks for their efficiency in long-distance power transmission. The HYPERSIM platform enables the simulation of multiple scenarios in real-time, making it a useful tool for studying the behavior of large-scale power grids under different conditions. Overall, the proposed implementation technology provides a powerful tool for researchers and practitioners in the power industry to analyze and optimize the performance of power grid systems.

The Employment Law Expert System is a form of artificial intelligence that is specifically designed to provide expert knowledge and guidance in the field of employment law. This system is part of a larger group known as "Expert systems," which use machine learning algorithms to mimic human cognition and decision-making processes. Employment law is a complex area that covers a wide range of legal issues such as hiring, firing, discrimination, and safety at the workplace, among others. The Employment Law Expert System can help employers and employees navigate this complex landscape by offering clear guidance based on current laws, regulations, and judicial rulings. With the increasing importance of employment law in today's workplace, this system can help stakeholders mitigate potential legal risks and ensure compliance with all relevant laws and guidelines.

Currently, communication networks provide a fairly large number of services to the end user. At the same time, each service has its own set of performance indicators for the network infrastructure, which determine the quality of the provision of this particular service. It should be noted that the quality of the provision of different communication services can be influenced by both different and the same quality indicators of the network infrastructure. At the same time, the common for some services indicators of the quality of the network infrastructure may have for each service different permissible ranges of values and be related or depend on the values of other indicators of the quality of the network infrastructure. Such complex relationships between the quality of network services and the quality indicators of the network infrastructure make individual monitoring of the values of the quality indicators of the network infrastructure not always advisable, because such monitoring algorithms have a high degree of branching due to a large number of conditions. In this case, it is most expedient to form for each service from the quality indicators of the network infrastructure some evaluation function, the output of which values beyond the allowable range will indicate degradation of the quality of a particular service and define a set of quality indicators for the network infrastructure for their further detailed control.

This study evaluates the effectiveness of novel vibrotactile biofeedback coding schemes in gait symmetry training. The focus of this research is on biological control systems, specifically those related to legged locomotion. Vibrotactile feedback is used in this study to improve the symmetry of gait patterns. The training is based on task analysis, and the encoding of the feedback is done through sophisticated instruments. The study results indicate that the novel coding schemes produce improved outcomes in gait symmetry training, making it a potentially valuable tool in physical rehabilitation. Further research in this area may help optimize the use of vibrotactile feedback for more effective training, lowering the risk of injuries and improving the quality of life for individuals with movement-related impairments.

With the prevalence of smartphones, mobile websites have been more and more popular. However, many mobile websites collect the location information which greatly increases users' risks of being tracked unexpectedly. The current location access control setting is not sufficient since it cannot prevent the service providers which have been granted location-access permissions from tracking the users. In this paper, we propose a novel location privacy preservation mobile app, called MoveWithMe, which automatically generates decoy queries to hide the real users' locations and intentions when they are using location-based mobile services. Unlike the existing works on dummy trajectories which may be easily discovered by attackers through data analysis, the uniqueness of the MoveWithMe app is that our generated decoys closely behave like real humans. Each decoy in our system has its own moving patterns, daily schedules, and social behaviors, which ensures its movements to be semantically different from the real user's trace and satisfying geographic constraints. Thus, our decoys can hardly be distinguished even by advanced data mining techniques. Another advantage of the MoveWithMe app is that it guarantees the same level of user experience without affecting the response time or introducing extra control burdens. Decoys move independently in the back end and automatically submit queries to the same service provider whenever the user does so. Our proposed MoveWithMe app has both iOS and Android versions and has been tested on different brands of smartphones against various location-based services, such as Yelp and TripAdvisor. Experimental results demonstrate its practicality, effectiveness, and efficiency.

This paper presents a fast electromagnetic transient model of a modular multilevel converter based on rotation transformation. The mathematical model considers the switches and bridge circuits in the converter, which allows for high accuracy in analyzing power system dynamics. An analytical model is derived for the converter and harmonic analysis is performed to evaluate its performance under steady-state conditions. Additionally, computational modeling is utilized to validate the accuracy of the proposed model. The fast electromagnetic transient model provides a valuable tool for analyzing the behavior of the modular multilevel converter in power systems.

The physical characteristics of wireless channels, in particular the channel impulse response (CIR), have become an attractive source of shared secrecy between two communicating parties for many wireless applications. However, ensuring high-entropy secret bits from the CIR may not be always feasible, including in IoT and/or indoor environments, where the coherence time may not be easy to obtain, or mobility is limited. Many techniques have been developed to resolve the above problems, including privacy amplification for higher entropy output, and pre-processing for data distillation. In this paper, we develop a framework for extracting entropy from sequentially arriving channel impulse response observation samples, and propose algorithms for both online and offline versions of the problem. We fully characterize the optimal solutions to these problems through a series of analytic results, and establish the optimality of our proposed online and offline algorithms, namely A_EMSON and A_EMSOFF to solve the problem. We also verify the performance of the algorithms through comparisons with the existing related techniques, and evaluate their capability to ensure high-entropy under different channel models using MATLAB simulations.

In recent years, the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become increasingly popular for various applications, such as surveillance, monitoring, and search and rescue missions. However, one major challenge in UAV networks is the management of the network itself, particularly in maintaining the quality of service (QoS) for wireless communication among the UAVs. To address this problem, swarm intelligence-inspired autonomous flocking control has been proposed as an approach for controlling the behavior of UAVs in a network. This approach allows the UAVs to form a flock and move in a coordinated manner, while optimizing the network's efficiency and reducing energy consumption. Wireless sensor networks and ad hoc networks have also been utilized in conjunction with UAV networks to provide additional monitoring and data gathering capabilities. Overall, the use of swarm intelligence-inspired flocking control and wireless communication technologies has shown great potential for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of UAV networks.

This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach for channel state information (CSI) feedback in a superimposed coding framework for both downlink and uplink communication in MIMO systems. The traditional approach to CSI feedback utilizes a fixed bandwidth for all users, which can lead to inefficient communication and reduced throughput. To overcome this limitation, superimposed coding is used to allow multiple users to share the same bandwidth. However, this also introduces high correlation between the different user channels, making it challenging to accurately estimate the CSI. To address this issue, artificial neural networks are introduced to learn the relationship between the superimposed channel and the corresponding CSI. The proposed deep learning scheme achieves better accuracy in estimating the CSI compared to the traditional methods, and can be extended to various multi-user applications. Overall, this paper highlights the potential of using deep learning techniques to enhance the performance of MIMO communication systems in the presence of bandwidth and correlation constraints.

In recent years, community detection has been an essential task in complex network analysis. To address this challenge, various heuristic algorithms have been proposed, and the Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA) is a promising approach for solving this problem. However, there is still room for improvement in terms of EDA's performance in community detection tasks. This paper proposes an improved EDA for community detection that incorporates genetic algorithms and encoding strategy to enhance the algorithm's search capability. The proposed approach is evaluated on several benchmark data sets, and the results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing EDA-based algorithms and achieves state-of-the-art results on several metrics. Moreover, this study provides insights into the potential application of biological cells to improve EDA's performance. This research is useful for researchers in fields such as sociology, statistics, and complex networks who are interested in community detection.

This paper proposes a simulation-optimization approach to solve a sortation conveyor layout design problem. The layout of the conveyor system plays a critical role in determining the efficiency of transportation and logistics operations. Therefore, developing an optimal layout design is important for ensuring the maximum throughput and loading capacity of the system. The proposed approach utilizes genetic algorithms for optimization and simulates the transportation and loading process to evaluate the performance of multiple layout scenarios. The key factors that influence the design of a sortation conveyor system, such as throughput, loading, and transportation, are taken into consideration during the optimization process. The results obtained from the simulation-optimization approach demonstrate significant improvements in system performance, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Overall, the study provides a useful methodology for designing sortation conveyor systems that can significantly enhance logistics and transportation operations.

Handwritten digits recognition is considered as a core to a diversity of emerging application. It is used widely by computer vision and machine learning researchers for performing practical applications such as computerized bank check numbers reading. However, executing a computerized system to carry out certain types of duties is not easy and it is a challenging matter. Recognizing the numeral handwriting of a person from another is a hard task because each individual has a unique handwriting way. The selection of the classifiers and the number of features play a vast role in achieving best possible accuracy of classification. This paper presents a comparison of three classification algorithms namely Naive Bayes (NB), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and K_Star algorithm based on correlation features selection (CFS) using NIST handwritten dataset. The objective of this comparison is to find out the best classifier among the three ones that can give an acceptable accuracy rate using a minimum number of selected features. The accuracy measurement parameters are used to assess the performance of each classifier individually, which are precision, recall and F-measure. The results show that K_Star algorithm gives better recognition rate than NB and MLPas it reached the accuracy of 82.36%.

In recent years, the exponential growth of Big Data has led to the need for efficient processing methods. One such method is the use of parallel algorithms on distributed databases. This paper aims to survey the use of parallel join algorithms using MapReduce on Hadoop for query processing in Cloud computing environments. The focus of this survey is on data handling, as the massive size and complexity of Big Data require efficient and scalable methods. Through an analysis of the current literature, this survey examines the various techniques used in parallel join algorithms, including partitioning, sorting, and hashing. Moreover, the survey investigates the challenges and limitations of using MapReduce on Hadoop, such as performance overhead and data skew. Overall, this survey provides an overview of the state-of-the-art techniques for parallel join algorithms and highlights the future directions for research in this area.

Case Law has a significant impact on the proceedings of legal cases. Therefore, the information that can be obtained from previous court cases is valuable to lawyers and other legal officials when performing their duties. This paper describes a methodology of applying discourse relations between sentences when processing text documents related to the legal domain. In this study, we developed a mechanism to classify the relationships that can be observed among sentences in transcripts of United States court cases. First, we defined relationship types that can be observed between sentences in court case transcripts. Then we classified pairs of sentences according to the relationship type by combining a machine learning model and a rule-based approach. The results obtained through our system were evaluated using human judges. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study where discourse relationships between sentences have been used to determine relationships among sentences in legal court case transcripts.

Health and safety management has been an important issue in construction industry. National regulations impose the using of hard hats in construction sites. However, there are often cases in which the construction workers neglect the regulations. It is desired to monitor the correct wearing of hard hat in real time and explore monitoring techniques facilitated by deep-learning algorithms. In this paper, a convolutional neural network based hard-hat detection algorithm is proposed. In this algorithm, the detection of construction workers and the hard hats are assisted by computer vision technique where deep learning model are trained to identify the proper wearing of hard hats. The optimization of the proposed neural networks can reduce the computational complexity while maintaining a relatively high recognition precision. Experiments have been performed using five different algorithms for comparison and results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm excels in the mAP and FPS performance metrics. The experimental results collected on an embedded platform reveal that the proposed algorithm presents a good candidate for similar applications where real-time deep-learning application is desired.

This paper presents a novel approach for indoor subarea localization using auditory scene analysis-based feature extraction on smartphones. The proposed method uses fingerprints recognition to identify different subareas within a room and acoustics-based analysis to extract features from the audio signals captured by the smartphone sensors. Spectrogram analysis is performed on these signals to identify distinct patterns and extract relevant features. The features are then used for sensor data fusion, localization, and visualization. The proposed method has been tested in real-life scenarios, and the results prove its effectiveness in accurately localizing subareas within indoor environments. The use of smartphones as a sensing platform for feature extraction and localization makes this method highly accessible and cost-effective. Overall, this paper provides an innovative solution for indoor localization that can have real-world applications in various domains.

With the advancement of natural language processing techniques, robots are being built to interact in natural languages, in order to facilitate a more human like experience for its users. This study focuses on building a human-robot interaction system for a document delivering robotic assistant that is capable of following instructions and answering questions related to the domain of an office environment. The semantic analysis carried out in this closed domain intelligent system employs a hybrid approach comprised of both rule based and machine learning based techniques, while addressing the problem of limited domain related training data. Speech inputs obtained through speech recognition libraries are sent through several layers of classifiers in order to extract keywords that maps the input to the intended meaning of the user. Response templates backed by a knowledge base is used to generate the appropriate responses, which will then be converted into speech form. Apart from the rules utilized, machine learning based approaches SVM, KNN, Naïve Bayes and Decision Trees are evaluated in this research for the semantic analysis classifications. The results of this hybrid approach show a significant level of accuracy and provides a solution to the shortage of domain related training data that limits the ability to use neural network based techniques.

Welcome to the first "Tech Travel" column, which will appear as a regular contribution in future issues of IEEE Potentials. As a bioengineering Ph.D. student, my main base is Instituto Superior T?cnico in Lisbon, Portugal, but the second half of my four-year journey took me to Boston, Massachusetts. Boston is a city that loves its sports. You can see this in how residents proudly wear their favorite team gear everywhere.

This paper presents a medium-term power load forecasting model for the Java and Bali power system using both artificial neural network (ANN) and SARIMAX algorithms. Load modeling is discussed and analyzed to determine the relevant parameters and variables that affect the load forecasting process. Predictive models using data models are developed to deliver accurate and reliable forecasting results. Artificial neural network technology is employed, allowing for the use of 'neurons' that work similarly to a human brain in processing complex data sets. The developed model is applied to perform load forecasting, providing reliable forecasts for the Java and Bali power system. The results of the study demonstrate that the proposed model performs well in forecasting load, offering a useful tool for power system operators and planners to make informed decisions about power generation and management.

The variations of photoplethysmography (PPG) morphology for the pregnancies with preeclampsia (PE) were studied in this paper. PPG data from 16 hypertensive pregnancies with PE and 26 normotensive pregnancies were acquired by the standard medical monitor. A novel hierarchical area ratio (HAR) parameter was invented to segment and quantitate the descending domain of a pulse based on the data acquired. The algorithm and features of HAR are fully explained and discussed in the paper. A rough PE distinction based on the statistics of HAR calculated from the original PPG signals was conducted with the precision of 72.7%, sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 76.9% and accuracy of 85.7%. The HAR we proposed in the paper showed favorable prospects in the quick distinction of PE.

This paper presents the design and development of an intelligent wearable virtual reality (VR) gaming controller specifically for people with motor disabilities. The system integrates a range of technologies including games, headphones, physiology, robot kinematics, electrodes, and machine learning to enable users to interact with virtual environments and play games using their own body movements. The system is designed to be compact, lightweight, and wearable, and is capable of detecting and interpreting a wide range of user movements and inputs. By leveraging the latest advances in machine learning and robotics, the system can adapt to the unique needs and abilities of individual users, thereby allowing them to experience the full benefits of VR gaming. The paper outlines the various technical challenges involved in the development of the system, as well as its potential applications in clinical settings and home-based rehabilitation. Preliminary results suggest that the system is highly effective in improving motor function and overall quality of life for people with motor disabilities. Overall, this paper represents an important contribution to the field of assistive technology, and provides a valuable resource for researchers, engineers, and clinicians working in this area.

Since 2015, the Sentinel 2 satellite provides a medium to high spatial resolution (10m-30m) images. For studying the land cover of Gabes area, located in the South- East of Tunisia, we exploited the 10 m bands of this satellite. We have tested the supervised classification with the SVM classifier. The classification is preceded by a segmentation step. The spectral data, the vegetation index and the texture metrics (GLCM) are used for training. The best Overall Accuracy OA (92, 12%) is obtained when all the used features are combined.

Pose estimation is an important task in robot vision systems for industrial applications. However, it remains a challenge to detect and estimate the pose of texture-less industrial parts using cameras. In this paper, a new method is proposed for fast detection and pose estimation of such parts. The method involves feature extraction, image segmentation, and acceleration techniques to achieve optimal results. Specifically, a combination of SIFT and SURF feature extraction algorithms is used along with a novel image segmentation approach to identify texture-less regions of the object. In addition, an acceleration technique based on PCA regression is utilized to speed up the computation time of the pose estimation process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and efficiency in detecting and estimating the pose of texture-less industrial parts. This method has significant potential for applications in manufacturing, inspection, and automation systems.

This paper proposes a method to detect fire using deep learning. Deep learning networks used in the proposal were AlexNet, GoogLeNet and VGG-16 in three ways. Image input from a closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera is classified into three different states (normal, smoke and flame) and then the network is trained to recognize each corresponding state. The datasets used consist of images coming from three areas which are housing, high-rise building, and mountain where fire incidents occurred. A quarter of all datasets were used as test images, half of them for validation, and the rest were used for testing purposes. Experimental results showed that all three network models were classifying fire detection at over ninety percent accuracy.

The paper presents a method for image-based visualization of classifier decision boundaries. The proposed approach utilizes 2D displays to represent the decision boundaries of classifiers, using visualization techniques such as color and brightness. The authors also discuss the importance of training and dimensionality reduction in achieving accurate visual representations of the decision boundaries. A significant focus is placed on task analysis, where the authors examine how the visualizations can be tailored to specific tasks and user needs. The paper highlights the potential of this approach to aid in the interpretation and analysis of classifier decision boundaries, and to facilitate better understanding and communication of machine learning models.

Object detection is an important task in computer vision, with numerous practical applications. In this paper, the authors introduce a new method for training detectors using zoomed object regions. By focusing on fine-grained details within specific areas of an image, this approach takes advantage of semantics to improve object detection accuracy. The proposed method was tested on two datasets of dogs and cows, with promising results compared to existing detection techniques. Overall, this learning approach offers a new direction for object detection research, with potential applications in various fields including agriculture, surveillance, and robotics.

IMACS is a performance evaluation framework designed for image approximation in closed-loop systems. Its purpose is to analyze the performance of various components involved in the image approximation process, such as cameras, pipelines, and computational modeling. The framework is especially useful for evaluating image approximations in IP networks, where bandwidth limitations and quality of service issues can pose significant challenges. IMACS provides insight into how different components of the system interact with one another and how they affect overall performance. It also offers a way to evaluate the effectiveness of various image approximation techniques and their impact on performance. Furthermore, the framework leverages the power of graphics processing units to accelerate the processing time, making it an efficient tool for researchers and practitioners alike. The proposed task analysis and evaluation criteria are useful for designers and developers of image approximation systems.

Scientific workflows define computational processes needed for carrying out scientific experiments. Existing workflow repositories contain hundreds of scientific workflows, where scientists can find materials and knowledge to facilitate workflow design for running related experiments. Identifying reusable fragments in growing workflow repositories has become increasingly important. In this paper, we present PSM-Flow, a probabilistic subgraph mining algorithm designed to discover commonly occurring fragments in a workflow corpus using a modified version of the Latent Dirichlet Allocation algorithm. The proposed model encodes the geodesic distance between workflow steps into the model for implicitly modeling fragments. PSM-Flow captures variations of frequent fragments while maintaining its space complexity bounded polynomially, as it requires no candidate generation. We applied PSM-Flow to three real-world scientific workflow datasets containing more than 750 workflows for neuroimaging analysis. Our results show that PSM-Flow outperforms three state of the art frequent subgraph mining techniques. We also discuss other potential future improvements of the proposed method.

This paper proposes a hybrid expert/data-driven health index for railway axleboxes using auto-encoder neural networks. The proposed method aims to detect anomalies and provide early warnings for maintenance purposes. The study focuses on vibrations, which are a key indicator of the health condition of railway axleboxes. By combining the expertise of maintenance engineering with auto-encoded feature extraction, a more accurate and comprehensive health index can be obtained. The auto-encoder neural network is used to extract relevant features from vibration data, and the extracted features are then incorporated into the health index. The proposed method demonstrates high accuracy in anomaly detection and provides a reliable and effective monitoring solution for railway axleboxes. Overall, this study highlights the potential of using neural networks and feature extraction in developing health indexes for industrial equipment.

Applications of wireless sensor networks span from the agricultural field to the battlefield and from smart city to smart city health care. There are certain applications where millions of sensor nodes or motes are deployed to sense the environmental parameters. However, in certain applications like health care and smart city applications, few hundreds of nodes can solve the purpose. Routing in energy-constrained networks like WSN is a challenging task. Parameters like consumed energy, congestion and signal to noise ratio etc. are considered to find a routing path in WSN. The Survival Path Routing (SPR) protocol is an earlier version of the work proposed here. The said protocol fails to provide a better result when the number of nodes in the network is increased. Thus a Scalable Survival Path Routing (SSPR) protocol is proposed where the method of clustering is applied to meet the efficiency of a scalable network. Weights of the nodes are computed to choose the cluster heads among them. It is observed that the proposed protocol SSPR outperforms SPR and Directed Diffusion protocol in terms of packet delivery ratio, end to end delay and throughput.

The IoT is experiencing massive growth in the industrial sector. This growth requires the development of innovative security concepts to keep up with the changing requirements of industrial IoT systems and applications. One important area of such M2M communication, where appropriate security measures need to be developed, is the authentication between devices. This paper proposes context-awareness as a method to enhance the authentication process in the industrial IoT. First, the problems of industrial IoT authentication are analyzed and the consequential requirements are formulated. Then it is shown, how context-awareness can help to overcome those problems. The advantages, which context-aware authentication brings, are afterwards demonstrated with concrete use cases.

WiderPerson is a new dataset designed for the detection of dense pedestrian in urban areas. This dataset provides a diverse collection of images captured by cameras in the wild. The main objective of WiderPerson dataset is to provide a benchmark testing to evaluate the performance of pedestrian detectors. The dataset is made up of challenging images, including a wide range of poses, occlusions, and scale variations. The dataset is suitable for training and testing different detectors using deep learning techniques. Task analysis is carried out to identify the suitable architecture and parameters for pedestrian detection. This dataset serves as an important tool for the development of state-of-the-art pedestrian detection methods that can be applied to wide-ranging scenarios.

This paper proposes a decision tree-based real-time emergency control strategy for power system stability. The approach involves training a decision tree model with analytical and adaptation models, using stability criteria to make decisions in real-time, and employing load shedding techniques as a last resort option. The proposed technique ensures power system stability while minimizing load losses. Different data models are evaluated to determine the optimal approach for different scenarios. Results show that the decision tree-based approach outperforms traditional approaches in terms of system stability and load shedding effectiveness. This paper presents a promising solution to real-time emergency control in power systems, improving reliability and efficiency in power grid operation.

This paper introduces a new approach for dysgraphic handwriting analysis, based on the tunable Q-factor wavelet transform. Dysgraphia is a neurological disorder that affects writing abilities in both children and adults. This research focuses on analyzing handwriting features in order to identify dysgraphia in students, which is crucial for early intervention and support. The proposed approach uses wavelet transforms for feature extraction, and the tunable Q-factor is used to optimize the signal to noise ratio. The method has been extensively tested using data from pupils with and without dysgraphia, and the results showed a significant improvement in classification accuracy compared to previous methods. The proposed approach could have a significant impact on identifying dysgraphia in pupils and improving their writing abilities, as well as enabling researchers to better understand the underlying causes of dysgraphia.

This paper proposes a new two-phase classifier for face recognition, which aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of face recognition systems. The proposed method focuses on the mathematical models and computer science approaches in order to enhance the information security of face recognition systems. The first phase of the classifier involves training the system with a dataset of known faces, while the second phase involves recognizing unknown faces based on the learned patterns. The mathematical model used in this paper is based on the principle of maximum likelihood estimation, which provides a robust and efficient approach for face recognition. The proposed method has been evaluated using several benchmark datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that it outperforms other state-of-the-art face recognition methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, this paper presents a new and improved approach for face recognition that has important implications for information security in a variety of applications.

The emerging trend of automation in embedded systems has paved the way for the adoption of the Object Management Group (OMG) Model Driven Architecture (MDA) vision for the development of computer systems. This approach leverages the use of adaptation models, computational modeling, and semantics to ensure a high degree of automation in the design and implementation of embedded systems. The automation of hardware and computer architecture has facilitated the development of more efficient and reliable embedded systems. This paper explores the application of OMG's MDA vision and its contribution to the automation of embedded systems. The study investigates the benefits of using adaptation models and computational modeling in achieving automation, as well as the importance of semantics in the design and implementation of efficient embedded systems.

Sleep is an essential part of human life, and adequate sleep is crucial for maintaining good health. However, people who suffer from medical conditions such as stroke are at increased risk during sleep. This study proposes a Real-Time Stroke Early Detection System During Sleep using Wristbands, called RISK-Sleep. The system takes advantage of feature extraction, monitoring, and detectors to analyze sleep and identify potential risks. It utilizes real-time systems to provide immediate notifications to caregivers or family members if detected risks exceed certain thresholds. Data collection is a critical aspect of the system, enabling researchers to continuously refine and improve the algorithms used in the RISK-Sleep system. The proposed system has the potential to reduce the incidence of stroke and improve the quality of life for individuals with a higher risk of stroke. Overall, the RISK-Sleep system is a promising development in the field of healthcare technology and holds substantial promise for the future.

This paper proposes a Lyapunov-based control scheme for point-mass robots to achieve motion camouflage. The control scheme is developed based on Lyapunov methods to ensure trajectory stability and convergence of the robots. Inspired by the motion camouflage strategy used by insects, the proposed control scheme utilizes kinematics to replicate the insect behavior in a robotic system. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is demonstrated through simulations highlighting the ability of the robots to mimic the motion of a target object while maintaining their own safety. Overall, this study provides insights on how the motion camouflage strategy used by insects can be applied to robotic systems through a Lyapunov-based control scheme to achieve safe and effective motion.

Fog computing emerges as a promising mode to meet the stringent requirement of low latency in industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). By offloading partial computation-intensive tasks from fog node to cloud server, the computation experience of users can be further improved in fog computing system. In this paper, we develop an energy-efficient computation offloading scheme for IIoT in fog computing scenario. The purpose is to minimize energy consumption when computation tasks are accomplished within a desired energy overhead and delay. It has a comprehensive consideration on the components of energy consumption at fog node, which includes the energy consumption of local computing, transmitting and waiting states. To address this energy minimization problem, an accelerated gradient algorithm is proposed, it can find the optimal offloading ratio with a fast speed that improves the convergence speed of traditional method. Finally, the numerical results reveal that the proposed offloading scheme is superior to the local computing and full offloading schemes in terms of energy consumption and completion time, and further confirm the advantage of convergence rate.

This paper presents a novel technique for reducing packet loss during rerouting in multicast tree using Label Forwarding. The proposed method is based on the convergence of switches and Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) routing, where the labels are used to forward packets from source to destination. The key aspect of this method is that it creates a backup path for rerouting in case of any network failure or congestion. This peer-to-peer computing approach enables efficient utilization of bandwidth and reduces packet loss during network reconfiguration. Results from our experiments show significant improvement in terms of packet loss reduction and network convergence time. Overall, this method is a promising approach for reducing packet loss in multicast networks, and it can be further extended to other network applications.

This paper presents a new approach for real-time full-body motion-capture using inertial measurement units (IMUs) and constraint-based motion estimation. Current motion-capture systems rely heavily on optical variables measurement, but this approach can be limited by the optical reflection of skin, and the complexity of optical fiber communication. The proposed approach allows full-body motion measurement to be accurately achieved without these limitations by utilizing a combination of IMUs located on different body segments. Constraint-based motion estimation algorithms are used to calculate joint angles and motion trajectories that replicate natural legged locomotive movements in real-time. The results of this study suggest that this constraint-based approach can provide accurate full-body motion estimation and may have the potential for use in a variety of applications, including animation and sports biomechanics.

This paper proposes a novel Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) for texture classification, which utilizes a moving convolutional mask for feature extraction. ALO is a population-based optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of ant lions. It combines the strengths of both particle swarm optimization and clustering algorithms to obtain optimal weights for the convolutional codes. The moving convolutional mask allows for adaptive feature extraction that is tailored to the unique features of each texture. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of geology textures and achieves superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art methods. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of ALO in optimizing convolutional neural networks and highlights the potential of using adaptive feature extraction for texture classification tasks.

In this paper, based on the exponential synchronization of double-layered networks composed of multiple subnets, we bring forward a chaotic secure communication scheme, which is robust to different network sizes, time-varying delays, and stochastic noise. Cluster analysis is used to process the nodes with different dynamics, such that the subnets in the transmitter and receiver are one-to-one correspondence and constitute subnet pairs, while the node size of each subnet can be inconsistent. Each subnet pair is only accountable for encrypting/decrypting a part of information. There are many encryption/decryption units and they are operating in parallel, which can not only indicate the complex characteristic of different nodes but also speed up the information encryption/decryption. The proposed scheme applies the chaotic signals yielded by many chaotic systems as key sequences, such that the key space can grow with node sizes in the transmitter. This scheme is not subject to the constraint on the amplitude of the original message and chaotic signal, the influence of time-delay and stochastic noise, and it shows that only the nodes with large degrees need to apply controllers in restoring the original information. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulation manifest the feasibility and validity of the given scheme.

A transfer function based calculation method is proposed to estimate radio frequency interference (RFI) problems. The closed-form equations are analytically derived from Maxwell's equations and the reciprocity theorem. The derived equations can clearly decompose the RFI problem into two parts: the noise source and the coupling transfer function to the antenna. Based on derivations, a transfer function concept is proposed to quantify the coupling coefficient from each unit dipole moment to the victim antenna. The transfer functions can be easily obtained from S-parameter measurements. The proposed method is validated through numeric simulations and real cellphone experiments. Engineering insights drawn from the method are also discussed. Overall, the proposed method is accurate, fast, and can provide physical insights for practical designs.

The extreme sparsity of the rating data seriously affects the recommendation quality of the recommendation system. In order to alleviate the problem of data sparsity, some convolutional neural network (CNN)-based models make full use of text data to improve the recommendation accuracy. However, due to the inherent properties of the traditional convolutional network, it can only extract features in a fixed position, and rely on the primitive bounding box based feature extraction, thus ignoring the flexibility of the traditional convolution. In this paper, we adopt a flexible convolutional network called deformable convolutional network (DCN), which extends the convolution transformation model capability by adding an offset layer to the traditional convolution layer, and then propose a novel deformable convolutional network matrix factorization (DCNMF) recommendation model. Specifically, we combine the DCN with word embedding to deeply capture the contextual information of document and build a latent model, which is incorporated into the probabilistic matrix factorization (PMF) model to enhance the recommendation accuracy. We conduct extensive experiments on the real-world datasets, and the experimental results show that the DCNMF outperforms the compared benchmarks.

A robust control technique is designed for Inverted Pendulum (IP) system to investigate the behavior of rapid change in the scheduled parameters. The designed mechanism has a monitoring and calibrating Virtual Instrument (VI) which is constructed in LabVIEW. VI sends a step response to the IP and obtains the transient response data of the system used for model identification. This model is used in control designing part because model of every system represents its dynamic characteristics. In this paper Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) controller is designed to cater for the parameters variations to enhance the performance and robustness. Moreover, the designed robust controlled is implemented on hardware platform to show its effectiveness. The identified model is validated by comparing the proposed technique in simulations and real-time results with classical controllers like Linear Quadratic Regulation (LQR) and Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller.

This paper proposes a method of extracting topic-related keywords using a backtracking convolutional neural network (CNN) based text classifier. The focus of the study is on text categorization, wherein feature extraction and data models are employed to identify relevant topics. The use of convolutional neural networks is the key to achieving accurate results as they can learn and recognize patterns in data. In addition, visualization techniques are utilized to provide a better understanding of the results. The proposed approach is compared with traditional methods and demonstrates better performance in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. Overall, this study highlights the effectiveness of CNN-based text classifiers for extracting topic-related keywords and provides a promising solution for text categorization applications.

This paper proposes an adaptive profile-based approach for detecting anomalous traffic in backbone IP networks. Anomaly detection is a crucial task in the field of network security due to the pervasive nature of computer crime. This approach utilizes measurement of key indicators such as entropy, correlation and digital signatures to create a baseline profile of normal network behavior. Deviations from this profile are classified as anomalous and flagged for further investigation. The proposed approach is adaptive, meaning that it can adjust the baseline profile over time to account for changes in network behavior. The authors evaluate the effectiveness of their approach using real-world network traffic data and find that it is able to detect anomalous traffic with high accuracy. Overall, this approach provides a promising solution for detecting and mitigating security threats in backbone IP networks.

This paper presents a methodological framework for investigating microstructure asymmetries in the infant brain cortex by combining structural and diffusion MRI. The study focuses on the microstructure of the brain cortex, as well as the surface morphology, and examines the reliability of the results obtained using this approach. Diffusion tensor imaging is used to generate quantitative measurements of microstructure asymmetries, while artificial intelligence techniques are employed to analyze surface morphology. The study is particularly relevant for pediatrics, as it has the potential to provide new insights into the development of the infant brain. The paper concludes that the approach presented can be used to produce reliable and robust results, which could facilitate future research in this field.

This paper presents a novel approach for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using moving dilated nested arrays. Sensor arrays in nested configuration provide more degrees of freedom for the estimation of DOA compared to conventional linear or planar arrays. The proposed approach utilizes the movement of the nested arrays to increase the effective aperture of the system and improve the estimation accuracy. Array signal processing techniques, such as covariance matrices, are employed to extract the DOA estimates. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional array configurations in terms of estimation accuracy and resolution. This approach has potential applications in many fields, such as radar and sonar systems, where precise DOA estimation is crucial for target tracking and localization.

This paper proposes a joined probabilistic load flow and sensitivity analysis of distribution networks based on the polynomial chaos method. Load modeling and power demand are critical elements in power system analysis, and their uncertainty due to various factors can have a significant impact on system performance. Therefore, probabilistic logic is introduced in load flow analysis to quantify the uncertainty of the system. The sensitivity analysis is also incorporated to identify critical components that have a significant impact on the system's performance. The polynomial chaos method is used to develop a computational modeling framework to simulate the distribution networks' behavior under uncertain conditions. The proposed approach is tested on a distribution network case study, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in identifying critical components and assessing the system's performance under uncertainty. This study provides a useful reference for future research in load flow analysis and sensitivity analysis of power systems.

With the increase in the number of connected devices in the Internet of Things (IoT), the demand for secure and efficient fog computing architectures has become increasingly important. In this paper, we propose a fog computing security architecture for the IoT that utilizes blockchain-based social networks. The architecture leverages the benefits of peer-to-peer computing and edge computing to provide a secure and decentralized system for data processing and storage. With authentication procedures and secure communication protocols, our proposed architecture ensures that sensitive data is protected from unauthorized access. Blockchain-based social networks provide an additional layer of security by allowing users to control access to their data and track any changes made to it. This approach not only provides security, but also enables cost-effective and efficient processing of data. Our proposed architecture has the potential to improve the security of fog computing systems and overcome the challenges of computer architecture in a highly connected world.

This paper presents a study on Resilient Distributed Estimation under Sensor Attacks. The exponential convergence of this estimation method is also analyzed. Network topology and parameter estimation are important factors in the resilience and accuracy of the estimation. The study focuses on the impacts of topology and communication networks on and between sensors, which influences the overall resilience of the system. By using the proposed Resilient Distributed Estimation, sensor attacks can be overcome without sacrificing the accuracy of the estimation. With this technique, it is possible to achieve reliable and accurate pollution measurement under various pollution scenarios. The study emphasizes the importance of resilience in estimation and proposes a solution for dealing with sensor attacks in a communication network.

We present a higher order quadrilateral surface remeshing approach for application to the method of moments. We briefly introduce the motivation for high-quality quadrilateral meshes for accurate and efficient application of cutting edge integration and singularity extraction approaches. Results are demonstrated for simple surfaces and compared with a common quadrilateral remeshing algorithm.

Biometric nowadays has becomes popular in term of authentication system. Many institutions and companies start to use biometric in addition using password or smartcard to authenticate a person in order to prevent unauthorized person to access their system. As the development of biometric in authentication system, the attackers try to search the vulnerability of it in order to have the authority into the system. One of the vulnerability of the biometric system that the attacker addressed is in the biometric database. Many system of biometric still save the biometric template characteristic in database in the form of plain image. There is no encryption method used to secure the biometric database, which makes easier for the attacker to sabotage the biometric system. This research focuses on how to secure the biometric database using EVCS (Extended Visual Cryptography Scheme). The study is applied on 198 training set palmprint images and 10-validation set of palmprint images. Experiment results showed that EVCS could be used for securing biometric template database without losing much information and the quality of the decrypted image reach 40.95 dB. The authentication system with EVCS also successfully authenticated decrypted image with the percentage of true positive that is S2.45% compared with the one without EVCS that reach 76.89% respectively.

With the development of modern network, the demand of users has increased dramatically, and more data and services are required. This has caused tremendous pressure on the Macro-cellular network of infrastructure. Air access has become a new solution for the development of communications. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is used as an air node to improve coverage and capacity. Based on deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm and considering the different quality of service requirements of different users, this paper proposes an optimal 3D location planning algorithm. The results show that the use of multiple UAVs can not only provide capacity enhancement, but also meet the different QoS requirements of different users. The average spectral efficiency of the system is increased by 15.5%, and user coverage to meet QoS requirements increased by 25.5%.

The growth of Internet usage changed the way of human communication, therefore also changing how malicious activity are conducted in the virtual world. Network security is still an issue that is treated by firewalls, Web Applications Filters and proxies in corporate networks, but there is a lack of solutions for personal networks monitoring that require no access to infrastructure, i.e. clients of one Internet Service Provider (ISP). In this paper we present a solution that addresses these issues and we focus on testing its performance on an typical WPA2 personal network scenario.

This paper presents a simulation analysis of data dissemination algorithms using existing Tendermint blockchain client-server system as an example. Algorithm analysis is connected with the Mempool component of the aforementioned system, which is responsible for disseminating data through the network. It is currently implemented in a way that it guarantees a certain outcome, yet it produces a large overhead. Simulation will show that one of the proposed solutions reduces the redundancy by 56.53% (or 3.62 times) on average, which is a significant improvement.

The growing popularity of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has led to the search for efficient computational platforms to enable these algorithms. Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based architectures offer a promising alternative to commonly used GPU-based platforms for CNN training. However, backpropagation in CNNs is susceptible to the limited precision of ReRAMs. As a result, training CNNs on ReRAMs affects the final accuracy of learned model. In this work, we propose REGENT, a heterogeneous architecture that combines ReRAM arrays with GPU cores, and exploits the benefits provided by 3D integration along with a high-throughput yet energy efficient Network-on-Chip (NoC) for training CNNs. We also propose a bin-packing based framework that maps CNN layers and then optimize the placement of computing elements to meet the targeted design objectives. Experimental evaluations indicate that REGENT improves full-system EDP by 55.7% on average compared to conventional GPU-only platforms for training CNNs.

Multi-objective optimization has been a crucial topic in the development of elastic dynamic load balancing strategies in the Internet of Things (IoT) networks. This paper proposes a novel approach for optimizing the load balancing operations in IoT networks using logic gates, sensors, cloud computing, computer architecture, monitoring, protocols, and power demand as its key components. The proposed approach aims to minimize the response time, energy consumption, and delay, while maximizing the throughput, resource utilization, and reliability of the IoT network. The logic gates, computer architecture, and protocols are used to optimize the routing and forwarding of data packets, while sensors and monitoring techniques are utilized to collect real-time information about the network's status. Cloud computing is employed to provide a scalable and flexible infrastructure for the IoT network, whereas power demand is controlled to reduce energy consumption. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through simulation results, which show that it outperforms traditional load balancing techniques in terms of the aforementioned objectives.

This paper proposes an architecture for SSL/TLS traffic processing that is enabled by service function chaining (SFC) and managed using the management and orchestration (MANO) framework. The architecture is designed to run on cloud computing platforms and utilizes network function virtualization (NFV) technologies. The proposed architecture focuses on optimizing the processing of SSL/TLS traffic by utilizing cryptographic techniques and reusing existing resources. This architecture is particularly relevant for the emerging 5G mobile communication networks, which require high-performance SSL/TLS processing capabilities. Additionally, this paper presents the findings of a study of various conferences that address the topics of computer architecture, cloud computing, and cryptography, which provided insights into the latest research trends in these areas. Overall, the proposed architecture provides a powerful tool for optimizing SSL/TLS traffic processing in the context of cloud-based 5G networks, while addressing the challenges of network security, efficiency, and resource utilization.

This paper proposes a parametric estimation algorithm for Hammerstein-Wiener mathematical models, which are widely used for modeling nonlinear systems. The algorithm is designed to estimate the parameters of the model from data, in order to provide an efficient method for integrated circuit modeling and computational modeling of hydraulic systems. The proposed algorithm is based on the principles of estimation theory, and is designed to minimize the cost function associated with the model parameters. The algorithm is evaluated on a range of synthetic and real-world datasets, and the results demonstrate that it is able to achieve accurate and efficient parameter estimation for Hammerstein-Wiener mathematical models. Overall, this work provides a valuable contribution to the field of estimation for nonlinear systems, with important applications for integrated circuit modeling and hydraulic system design.

The arrival of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) creates opportunities for great innovations. One possible application is indoor localization. This paper presents a system that can track mobile device and help finding their location within a building perimeter. With the help of BLE beacons that can be deployed in different locations, the position of a mobile device can be estimated using RSSI techniques and trilateration methods. The overall system is controlled using MQTT protocol. Along this paper, we describe our system, the techniques we use, and the experiments we conducted along with the results.

This paper proposes the design of an Adaptive Fuzzy Finite-Time Control strategy for Nonlinear Systems with Actuator Faults. The research focuses on developing an effective fault tolerant control mechanism that allows actuators to work efficiently, despite faults. The study aims to improve the performance of adaptive systems by introducing a Feedback Control and Backstepping approach to mitigate the effects of faults. The proposed strategy is designed to ensure the system's stability, regardless of actuator faults, in a limited time frame. Fuzzy control allows the system to adapt to changes in the environment by adjusting the control parameters. The effectiveness of the method is illustrated through simulations conducted on a nonlinear system with actuator faults. Overall, the proposed fault-tolerant control strategy shows significant improvement in the performance of nonlinear systems with actuator faults.

This paper is focused on investigating the convergence of the distributed generalized ADMM algorithm under non-strongly convex function components. Convergence of optimization algorithms is a crucial aspect in information processing and knowledge engineering, particularly in the realm of linear programming. Our study has been conducted specifically in the context of convergence in Europe, with a focus on convex functions. The results of our investigation indicate that Q-linear convergence can be achieved in this context. This is an important finding that can contribute to the development of more robust and efficient optimization algorithms for a variety of applications in information processing and knowledge engineering.

This paper proposes a solution for enabling secure dynamic operation in MPSoC through protected communication. Security is a crucial aspect in modern computer systems and the increasing use of IP networks has made it vulnerable to various security threats including malware. Thus, the system performance and hardware need to be safeguarded against such attacks. The proposed solution focuses on securing the network interfaces in MPSoC to ensure that they are protected against malware and other potential threats. The integration of hardware-based security protection provides an efficient and effective solution to safeguard the system performance of MPSoC. By implementing this protection, dynamic operation can be enabled in MPSoC without compromising on system security. The proposed solution provides a compelling case for a secure and efficient System-on-Chip architecture, enabling hardware protection and network interfaces to be better safeguarded against malware attacks.

In a general education course, 2100111 Exploring Engineering World, for all first-year engineering students at Chulalongkorn University, each group of students had to submit a short video clip as an assigned work. Usually, more than ten percents of the submitted clips had problems with Y ouTube copyright concerns. In the second semester of the academic year 2017, the copyright issue was addressed under a minimal intervention approach in two steps. First, students were given a quiz at the start of the course on their practical copyright knowledge in daily life and were found to have the same misunderstanding as normal Thai public. Then, before the video clip submission at the end of the semester, a poster on available resources was posted to the course Facebook group. After the intervention, the number of copyright transgression was halved when compared with the two proceeding semesters. From the reflection, points that had to be further addressed was the changes of the intervention time, additional resources and communication of importance in actively avoiding copyright issues. Then, the expansion of instructional model to other disciplines was recommended.

Diel vertical migration (DVM) of zooplankton can cause velocity fluctuations and a respective increase in the dissipation rate of turbulent kinetic energy dependent on zooplankton concentration (Dean et al. 2016). In this work, we used a 3D non-hydrostatic computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model (ANSYS Fluent) with Lagrangian particle injections (proxy for migrating organisms) to simulate the effect of turbulence generation by DVM. We tested a range of organism concentrations. The simulation at the extreme (10,000 organisms/m3) concentration of zooplankton showed an increase in dissipation rate of turbulent kinetic energy by two to three orders of magnitude during DVM over background turbulence (10-8 W kg-1). At the low (1000 organisms/m3) concentration, almost no turbulence above the background level was produced by DVM in the model. Seawater is an electric conductor; as a result, the motion of seawater in the magnetic field of the Earth induces electrical currents and, consequently, secondary magnetic fluctuations. Therefore, the turbulence produced by DVM can have a measureable magnetic signature. We have applied a magnetohydrodnamics (MHD) module to the CFD model to test this hypothesis. The MHD model results indicate that DVM of the extreme concentration of zooplankton create a magnetic signature on the order of 0.1 nT, which is relatively small but are well within the range of modern magnetometers.

In this paper, we present an experimentation framework for mobile multi-tenant 5G networks integrated with CORE network emulator. 5G mobile communication is the next generation wireless communication technology that promises high-speed data transmission and low latency communication. Our framework provides a set of tools for 5G network emulation that enables the testing and evaluation of various scenarios for computer architecture, protocols, and encapsulation. The emulated network environment provides a realistic platform for computational modeling, which can be used to implement and test different 5G network architectures. The framework's core component is the CORE network emulator, which provides a virtual network environment that can simulate different network topologies, node architectures, and traffic characteristics. Our framework's modular design provides flexibility and scalability for the experimentation of multi-tenant 5G networks. The proposed framework is expected to accelerate the development and testing of 5G mobile communication technologies, which will improve the quality of service and user experience of future mobile networks.

Emotion recognition plays an increasingly important role in human-computer interaction systems, which is a key technology in multimedia communication. Because neural networks can automatically learn the intermediate representation of raw speech signal, currently, most methods use Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract information directly from spectrograms, but this may result in the ineffective use of information in hand-crafted features. In this work, a model based on weighted feature fusion method is proposed for emotion recognition of variable-length speech. Since the Chroma-based features are closely related to speech emotions, our model can effectively utilize the useful information in Chromaticity map to improve the performance by combining CNN-based features and Chroma-based features. We evaluated the model on the Interactive Emotional Motion Capture (IEMOCAP) dataset and achieved more than 5% increase in weighted accuracy (WA) and unweighted accuracy (UA), comparing with the existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents a CNN-based approach for training and classification of MRI brain images with a focus on detecting tumors. The proposed method incorporates feature extraction and image segmentation techniques in order to improve the accuracy of the classification model. The comprehensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Additionally, this work holds significant potential for biomedical imaging, as this approach can be applied to various medical imaging scenarios beyond brain MRIs. In particular, the proposed approach can be used for the development of efficient communication systems in the medical industry.

This paper proposes a method for the classification of electrocardiography (ECG) signals using modified Hjorth descriptors. The study involves feature extraction from ECG signals, which are then used for classification. The heart is one of the most vital organs in the body, and abnormalities in its function can result in serious health issues. The classification of ECG signals is important in identifying these abnormalities. The study makes use of databases containing ECG signals, which are then processed using complexity theory. The modified Hjorth descriptors are used to extract features from the ECG signals, which are then inputted into a support vector machine (SVM) for classification. The results of the study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately classifying ECG signals. This research can be beneficial in the development of automated systems for the analysis of ECG signals, aiding in the diagnosis of heart-related health issues.

This paper proposes a time-domain model for the collector of a Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) using the Electron Beam Auto-cyclotron (EBAC) algorithm. The model allows for steady-state and time-domain analysis of the TWT collector's trajectory. Computational modeling of the collector's radio frequency and electron beam interactions is crucial in understanding the TWT's overall performance. The EBAC algorithm is used to simulate the electron beam's motion in the collector and calculate the RF power transfer efficiency. The proposed time-domain model provides a useful tool for designing and optimizing TWT systems.

In order to improve power quality disturbance feature extraction and pattern recognition, this research proposes a novel approach based on image enhancement techniques. The proposed technique enhances the image of the radio-frequency signal waveform which is often distorted by noise and other factors, thus providing a clearer representation of the signal. This approach also utilizes various signal processing techniques to extract features such as power quality indexes and standards. By combining these features, the pattern recognition algorithm is able to accurately classify power quality disturbances. The proposed approach is effective in selecting relevant features and improving the accuracy of classification results. Overall, the results of this study indicate that the proposed approach can contribute to the development of power quality disturbance analysis and monitoring.

This paper presents a defense analysis against store and forward distributed reflective denial of service (DoS) attacks. These attacks leverage the peer-to-peer computing architecture, targeting servers and IP networks, and inflicting significant damage on information technology infrastructure. To combat this threat, the paper proposes various protocols and technological innovations aimed at strengthening network security. The paper highlights the need for increased awareness of computer crimes and suggests the implementation of effective security measures to prevent such attacks from causing lasting harm. The proposed defense mechanisms aim to ensure that servers remain secure, and user data remains protected, even in the midst of the most severe DoS attacks. Overall, this paper makes a valuable contribution to the field of network security by presenting innovative solutions to mitigate the risks posed by DoS attacks, facilitating the reliable and secure operation of critical infrastructure.

Anonymous Voice over IP (VoIP) communication is an important tool to provide freedom of speech. For achieving a good trade-off between quality of service (QoS) and anonymity, connecting mixes by padded links is a promising approach. However, constructing suitable overlay topologies for establishing padded links is not easy: existing approaches are either not scalable with regard to the number of mixes because of using full meshes or impractical due to computational complexity of the algorithms used to create optimal reduced topologies. This prevents them from being deployed as volunteer-based networks like Tor. In this paper, we propose and study different heuristic strategies for reduced topology construction and path selection with low computational complexity. We evaluate our approach using latency and bandwidth estimations from the Tor network and demonstrate that we can achieve appropriate performance and anonymity metrics for VoIP. Especially, the achieved properties are similar to those of a recently proposed approach that calculates optimal topologies for small networks.

This paper proposes an embedded implementation of a deep learning smile detector using computer architecture and instruction sets optimized for real-time systems. The smile detector is based on deep learning techniques and designed for face recognition applications. The implementation is optimized for embedded systems with limited computational resources, such as small-scale cameras or mobile devices. This approach allows for the real-time detection of smiles with high accuracy, making it suitable for a wide range of applications where real-time performance is essential. The paper discusses the design and implementation of the detector, as well as the results of experiments conducted to evaluate its performance. The proposed embedded smile detector presents a promising approach to meet the requirements of real-time applications and demonstrates the potential of using deep learning on embedded systems.

This paper presents a gamification approach for the creation of serious games that can be used for training purposes. The use of games has already proven to be effective in enhancing various skills and competencies. In this paper, we focus on the use of games for training purposes, particularly in the domain of solid modeling. The proposed approach involves the use of standards for game design, electronic learning and task analysis. The proposed approach ensures that the serious games developed are effective for training purposes while also being engaging and entertaining for the learners. The approach is based on the combination of different game elements such as scoring, rewards, instant feedback, and social interaction. The approach is also flexible and can be adapted to different training needs and requirements. The proposed approach is expected to contribute to the development of more effective and engaging serious games for training purposes.

This paper aims to conduct a topic analysis for the fourth industrial revolution in Korea by utilizing the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and centrality analysis methods. The study analyzed various industries such as finance, service robots, government, and artificial intelligence. The results suggest that the topics related to artificial intelligence have the highest centrality score, indicating the significant influence of this topic in the discussion of the fourth industrial revolution in Korea. Additionally, the service robot and finance industries also showed significant centrality scores, emphasizing the importance of these industries in the fourth industrial revolution. This study provides insights into the key topics that are driving the fourth industrial revolution in Korea and highlights the need for policymakers and stakeholders to focus on these areas to enhance Korea's competitiveness in the global market.

This paper presents a context-aware light-tracking and -redirecting system guided by hand-gesture recognition. It is conceived as yet another mechanism within an ongoing development of a more intuitive and technically sophisticated Ambient Intelligence / Active and Assisted Living ecosystem. The detailed system consists of individual nodes that are strategically installed across regions of a building-envelope, which enables this latter to draw or deflect direct natural light into or away from specific locations within the built-environment as requested by the user(s) via recognized hand-gestures. Each node is capable of sending and receiving sensed-data continuously via ZigBee with one another as well as with microcontrollers embedded within the interior built-environment. Said microcontrollers are equipped with cameras via which four hand-gestures may be recognized. The first or initializing hand-gesture engages the system and enables it to recognize any of the remaining hand-gestures. The second redirects light towards the position of the detected hand-gesture, while the third redirects it away from said position. Finally, the fourth gesture turns the light-tracking and -redirecting system off.

In this position paper, we claim that immersive technologies, such as Augmented and Virtual Reality, are well-suited interfaces for the usage of crowd simulation software in different contexts. We introduce three use cases; planning, awareness creation, and education. Based on an overview of different Augmented and Virtual Reality approaches, we identify the ones most suitable for each of the three scenarios and illustrate related implementations. Initial observations with their usage confirm our statements, but also highlight areas to explore with future research.

To estimate the level of 10kV distribution network line losses more integrally and precisely, an evaluation method based on BP neural network (BPNN) improved by particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been proposed. Making full use of existing data resources in the State Grid Corporation of China, the relevant information in the process of10 kV distribution network line and line loss has been collected and integrated, to formulate the power grid equipment data and operation data in the process of power distribution and utilization. Firstly, the electrical characteristic indices have been selected and established to reflect the structure and operation state of 10kV distribution network. Secondly, the inertia weight and the acceleration coefficient of PSO have been dynamically adjusted so that the weights and biases of BPNN are searched more effectively. Then nonlinear relation between electrical characteristic indexes and line losses is fitted through the learning of training sample sets so as to predict the line losses of test sample sets. Finally, the PSO-BPNN is proved to be effective and proper through an actual 10kV distribution network sample data.

The design of analog and digital hybrid MAC circuit is of great importance in the development of artificial neural networks (ANNs). The focus of this paper is on the implementation of synapses within the circuit, which play a vital role in enhancing the computational power of ANNs. Computer architecture and microprocessors are also important components in the design, as they provide the necessary hardware support for the efficient functioning of the hybrid power systems. The proposed hybrid MAC circuit integrates the advantages of both analog and digital processing, allowing for faster and more accurate data processing. It is expected that the implementation of this circuit will result in significant improvements in the performance of ANNs and contribute to the advancement of hardware technology for artificial intelligence.

Gait analysis is widely used in the field of entertainment, sport, public welfare, and medical services.
