Although, there have been significant efforts to offer shared real-world testbeds, the simulations platforms are required to make the validation process cost and time effective. Existing simulation approaches only offer partial coverage to the key IoT environment characteristics, focus on communication or are specific for particular use cases and domains. In this paper, we propose a novel agent-based model that enables the simulation of the IoT systems with the key characteristics of an IoT environment. This model is designed to be flexible and adaptable to different experiments. Our approach introduces events in IoT environments as stochastic processes, enabling the evaluation of IoT systems under different conditions that otherwise would be time consuming and costly. We present the results of our experiments for evaluation of our model. These show that our proposal is a practical solution for the validation of IoT software systems, complementary to the real-world tests.

This paper presents an automated vision-based system for detecting high intraocular pressure using frontal eye images. The proposed system employs image segmentation and feature extraction techniques to detect iris and lens regions. Optical imaging is applied to capture high-quality images that are then processed using the proposed method. A database containing a large number of images is built to train and test the proposed system. Decision trees are used to classify images into high or normal intraocular pressure categories. The proposed system has shown promising results in accurately detecting high intraocular pressure in real-time applications. The use of frontal eye images and automated techniques removes the need for invasive measurements, making it a convenient and cost-effective solution for screening and monitoring individuals at risk of glaucoma. Further development of the proposed system could improve the accuracy of high intraocular pressure detection, ultimately contributing to the prevention and management of vision-threatening eye diseases.

This paper focuses on the optimal controller design for a two-wheel mobile robot. The two wheels are the main components of the mobile robot, which allows it to have the mobility to move around. The mathematical model of the two-wheel mobile robot is established to understand the relationship between the inputs and outputs of the system. Optimal control is used to optimize the performance of the mobile robot by minimizing a certain cost function. Computational modeling is applied to simulate the system's response to various control strategies. Predictive control is proposed as a promising approach for controlling the two-wheel mobile robot. By selecting the optimal control input, the predictive control algorithm can guarantee the stability of the system while achieving the desired performance. The simulation results show that the predictive control algorithm outperforms traditional control techniques in terms of tracking accuracy and disturbance rejection.

This paper proposes a receding horizon strategy for path planning of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the presence of multiple dynamic objects, while incorporating air-ground coordination. The approach combines task analysis, optimization, and vehicle dynamics to generate feasible and collision-free paths for the UAVs. Both genetic and heuristic algorithms are employed to optimize the path planning process, taking into account the dynamic movements of the objects in real-time. The effectiveness and applicability of the proposed strategy are demonstrated through simulation results, indicating that the receding horizon strategy is a promising approach for UAV path planning in dynamic environments.

This paper explores the use of ensemble machine learning in cyber physical security analytics for transactive energy systems. The focus of the paper is on utilizing decision trees to develop predictive models for safeguarding smart grids against cyber attacks. The authors outline the importance of computational modeling and data models in developing effective security strategies for transactive energy systems. The study demonstrates the potential of machine learning in enhancing cyber security measures with the use of ensemble models to overcome the limitations of individual models. Ultimately, the paper concludes that the proposed approach can contribute to the development of more robust cyber security protocols for transactive energy systems.

In recent years, machine learning has become an essential tool in risk management and optimization. Regularized empirical risk minimization is one of the most commonly used techniques which minimizes the expected risk over a set of possible outcomes. However, this approach requires solving complex optimization problems involving a large number of constraints. The Distributed Primal-Dual Proximal Method has been proposed as an efficient method to solve such problems. This technique leverages the geometry of the optimization problem and enables parallel computation, reducing the task analysis and computational logistics. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the convergence properties of the Distributed Primal-Dual Proximal Method for regularized empirical risk minimization in machine learning tasks. Our findings demonstrate that this method is highly effective in solving such problems, and can deliver excellent outcomes in a short amount of time. This study has important implications for practitioners in the fields of risk management and machine learning, who can now rely on efficient, effective and fast optimization methods.

Verbalization of knowledge base (KB) facts about an entity allows users to absorb information from KB more easily. The drawback of most previous work is that they cannot generalize to unseen frames. This work introduces the task of precise KB verbalization that is aimed at generating an exact description for the given factual triples. We propose a novel sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) model with the local pointer network to deal with this task. The approach to training data construction is also explored. Experimental results show our method improves the performances in terms of Meteor and slot error rates. Human evaluation is also performed to confirm the effectiveness of our model.

The delay-and-sum beamforming technique uses multiple microphones to localize sound sources. One disadvantage of this technique is that adjustments of the position or of the number of microphones change the quality nonlinearly. Additionally, due to the number of combinations possible, it is computationally hard to find the best configuration. This paper uses genetic algorithms to solve this problem. The algorithm searches for the microphone array configuration that provides the highest directivity for each steered orientation. The experiments showed that the genetic algorithm could find the best solution of a constrained search space comprising 33 554 431 solutions in a matter of seconds instead of days. Furthermore, this paper presents the used techniques to reduce the time of evolution, provides a web application and the source code of the implementation.

Dimensioning renewable energy systems to power mobile networks has become an increasingly important topic as the production and use of green products have become more prevalent. Renewable energy sources such as batteries and solar energy offer an environmentally friendly and sustainable solution for powering mobile networks. Computational modeling can be used to predict the energy requirements of base stations and optimize the sizing of renewable energy systems. This paper explores recent research on the dimensioning of renewable energy systems to power mobile networks using a combination of batteries and solar power. The results show that it is possible to significantly reduce the use of non-renewable energy sources and create a more sustainable and efficient telecommunications industry.

In order to accurately predict the remaining useful life of slewing bearings, a novel approach has been proposed using symbolic regression. The model takes into account the effects of degradation and vibrations, which are common causes of failure in these bearings. The model has been developed based on market research and predictive models and uses genetic programming for feature extraction. The symbolic regression approach provides an accurate and efficient method for predicting the remaining useful life of slewing bearings, reducing maintenance costs and downtime associated with unexpected failures. Overall, the proposed model provides significant improvements over existing methods and has the potential to provide valuable insights into the health of a range of mechanical systems.

The Internet of Things (IoT) has brought tremendous convenience to our daily lives, but at the same time, it poses a significant threat to our security and privacy. In order to address this issue, a dynamic IoT security domain enabling framework is proposed in this paper. This framework combines the cellular core network and device management with an authentication framework to create a more secure environment for IoT devices. The framework utilizes 5G mobile communication technology and various software and protocols to establish security domains and ensure communication security among different IoT devices. Moreover, the proposed framework provides a flexible and effective solution for dynamic security management and access control in IoT environments. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the architecture, communication protocols, and authentication mechanisms of the dynamic IoT security domain enabling framework. Results show that the proposed framework significantly improves the security and reliability of IoT networks and provides a promising solution to address the security challenges in the IoT era.

This paper presents a robust localization method for the estimation of body parts during sports activities. The proposed method uses interframe failure correction, which enables accurate pose estimation even under challenging conditions. Specifically, the method focuses on the localization of the elbow joint, which is an important body part for various games and sports. The proposed method employs time series analysis and sensor fusion techniques to achieve accurate and robust elbow localization. It is shown that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in sports-related applications, and suggest potential applications in other domains where accurate body part localization is critical.

It is evident that the objective physiology-based diagnostic methods are desired to improve the evaluation efficiency for stroke assessment, however the assessment relies mainly on the diagnosis scale and the experience of the therapists in clinic. This paper aims to evaluate the features based on sEMG from bilateral upper limb, which can be used to show the bilateral upper limb differences and to map the stroke scale. Preliminary experiments were conducted on eleven healthy subjects and some classical and innovative features were evaluated. With all the work of this paper, we anticipate that Root Mean Square (RMS), Crest Factor (CF) and Impulse Factor (I), are able to be used to evaluate stroke scale.

An adaptive neural output consensus control issue is considered for stochastic nonlinear strict-feedback multi-agent systems (MASs). The traditional backstepping framework is employed combing with the graph theory, as well as neural networks (NNs) technology. NNs are utilized for the approximation of unknown functions, and the Itô’s lemma is used to deal with stochastic dynamics of the system. It is proved that all signals remain bounded in probability and that the tracking errors of all followers converge to a small neighborhood of the origin in the sense of mean quartic value by suitable choice of parameters. A simulation example is provided.

We consider the problem of low-rank tensor decomposition of incomplete tensors that has applications in many data analysis problems, such as recommender systems, signal processing, machine learning, and image inpainting. In this paper, we focus on nonnegative tensor completion via low-rank Tucker decomposition for dealing with it. The specialty of our model is that the ranks of nonnegative Tucker decomposition are no longer constants, while they all become a part of the decisions to be optimized. Our solving approach is based on the penalty method and blocks coordinate descent method with prox-linear updates for regularized multiconvex optimization. We demonstrate the convergence of our algorithm. The numerical results on the three image datasets show that the proposed algorithm offers competitive performance compared with other existing algorithms even though the data is highly sparse.

A predictive neural network based mathematical model has been developed for estimating the concentration of biomass and substrate during the fermentation of Bifidobacterium longum ATCC15707. The model is based on biological system modeling and utilizes neural networks to make predictions. The accurate estimation of substrate and biomass concentration is crucial as it directly affects the fermentation process which is utilized in the production of various microbial products. Microorganisms such as Bifidobacterium longum ATCC15707 are a suitable target for fermentation as they are widely used in the production of functional foods and dietary supplements. The developed mathematical model with predictive neural network improves the estimation accuracy of the concentration of biomass and substrate during fermentation in comparison to conventional methods. The potential application of this model can provide better control and optimization of fermentation processes, leading to improved yields and higher quality products.

This paper proposes a novel approach to mobile visual food recognition using few-shot and many-shot fusion learning techniques. The proposed approach involves training an image recognition model using feature extraction and visualization methods, and utilizing both few-shot and many-shot training data to improve accuracy. The approach is designed specifically for deployment on mobile handsets, and knowledge engineering is used to optimize performance and minimize processing requirements. Results show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating the potential for improved mobile visual food recognition using advanced machine learning approaches. Overall, this study presents a valuable contribution to the field of computer vision, with potential applications in various industries including food service, healthcare, and mobile technology.

In recent years, cloud computing has become an important paradigm for delivering and accessing computing resources. Effective management of these resources is crucial to maintain the quality of service offered by data centers. A key challenge in resource management is optimizing the allocation of servers to minimize energy consumption, while ensuring that the quality of service requirements of users are satisfied. This paper proposes a new approach to resource management based on local regression and the Box-Cox transformation. The method involves developing detection algorithms to identify patterns in the data, and using regression to model the relationships between power consumption and various system parameters. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing energy consumption while maintaining the quality of service offered to users. The findings of this study have important implications for the design and operation of cloud networks, and underscore the importance of using data-driven approaches to tackle complex resource management problems in cloud computing.

This paper investigates the influence of time delay on bifurcation in fractional order BAM neural networks with four delays. Biological neural networks are highly complex and exhibit intricate behaviors that depend on various factors. The phenomenon of bifurcation is a characteristic feature of nonlinear systems and plays a crucial role in the understanding of neural dynamics. In this study, four delays are considered, and stability analysis is conducted using the Lyapunov functional method. The results show that the time delay can induce bifurcation in the neural network, leading to a range of possible behaviors. The study also highlights the importance of the delay effects on the stability of the neuron system. Overall, this work contributes to the understanding of the dynamics of neural networks, which has implications for the design and optimization of artificial neural networks.

SLATE is a new and advanced hardware primitive designed for secure and lightweight entity authentication. This technology combines various ciphers and hardware to deliver unparalleled resistance to sophisticated attacks, which can compromise authentication systems. SLATE also comes with a user-friendly interface that makes it easy for building and training protocols, allowing security experts to integrate the technology in their existing systems with relative ease. With its advanced features, SLATE is set to revolutionize the field of entity authentication, making it easier and more secure for individuals and organizations to protect their data and transactions. The technology is particularly useful in high-security environments like government institutions and financial institutions, where confidentiality is paramount. Overall, SLATE is a promising technology that is set to change the status quo in the world of entity authentication.

This paper focuses on the potential threat of memory Trojan attacks on neural network accelerators. Trojan horses, being one of the most common modes of attack, can create a vulnerability in the hardware that can easily infiltrate the system. As artificial neural networks heavily rely on integrated circuit modeling, it is important to understand the severity of this threat. The payload of such an attack could have the ability to manipulate the data processed by neural networks, influencing the results and compromising the system's integrity. Given that biological system modeling is heavily based on neural networks, tackling this threat is of particular importance. This paper discusses the potentially catastrophic impacts of memory Trojan attacks on neural network accelerators, highlighting the need for better security measures to be implemented in hardware design.

This paper presents a new method for location discovery under sparse reference point conditions using RSS fingerprinting. The method is based on a mathematical model and employs heuristic algorithms for estimation. Calibration is carried out using fingerprint recognition techniques, and the method performs well in indoor environments. The proposed method is expected to provide better accuracy and reliability than existing approaches, making it a potential tool for location-based services, spatial analysis, and other applications. The study highlights the importance of developing location discovery methods that can effectively handle sparse reference point conditions, which are commonly encountered in real-world scenarios. The results show the potential of the proposed method and its suitability for a wide range of applications in different industries. In conclusion, this paper provides valuable insights into the development of innovative location discovery techniques that can meet the demands of various real-world applications.

Day after day, more Internet of Things (IoT) devices are joining the Internet. By 2025, it is expected to have more than 75 billion connected devices compared to only 15 billion in 2015 [1]. Despite their potential, IoT systems have many constraints such as limited capabilities and energy to mention a few. Power consumption is among the most constrained aspects of IoT devices which leads to many challenges. This becomes more challenging in extremely high erasure channel conditions where many packets may be lost due to interference and other impairments. The process of re-transmission creates a huge overhead in terms of power consumption, delay and processing. In this paper, we propose the use of LT codes at the application layer to enhance the performance of MQTT-SN protocol. Our simulation results show savings of up to 75% in power consumption, 90% in overhead, and reduction in delay by 89% for high erasure rates.

The flow network balancing problem, i.e., the problem of balancing the incoming and outgoing flows for each vertex of a directed graph, has been widely investigated with several distributed solutions being proposed in recent years. Flow balancing is crucial in several application domains, ranging from water and traffic networks to complex network synchronization and distributed adaptive networked control. In this paper, we focus on finding the solution for the flow network balancing problem that is optimal in a minimal effort sense. More specifically, we aim at modifying a given set of (unbalanced) flows so that we obtain a balanced solution. We assume that there is a (possibly heterogenous) cost associated to the unit variation of each flow, as well as lower and upper bounds on the peredge flows. More in detail, we first establish a necessary and sufficient optimality condition for network balancing and then propose a distributed protocol, demonstrating its convergence toward the global optimal solution. Simulation results are provided to corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed distributed algorithm.

Objective: Deep learning has recently been applied to electrical impedance tomography (EIT) imaging. Nevertheless, there are still many challenges that this approach has to face, e.g., targets with sharp corners or edges cannot be well recovered when using circular inclusion training data. This paper proposes an iterative-based inversion method and a convolutional neural network (CNN) based inversion method to recover some challenging inclusions such as triangular, rectangular, or lung shapes, where the CNN-based method uses only random circle or ellipse training data. Methods: First, the iterative method, i.e., bases-expansion subspace optimization method (BE-SOM), is proposed based on a concept of induced contrast current (ICC) with total variation regularization. Second, the theoretical analysis of BE-SOM and the physical concepts introduced there motivate us to propose a dominant-current deep learning scheme for EIT imaging, in which dominant parts of ICC are utilized to generate multi-channel inputs of CNN. Results: The proposed methods are tested with both numerical and experimental data, where several realistic phantoms including simulated pneumothorax and pleural effusion pathologies are also considered. Conclusions and Significance: Significant performance improvements of the proposed methods are shown in reconstructing targets with sharp corners or edges. It is also demonstrated that the proposed methods are capable of fast, stable, and high-quality EIT imaging, which is promising in providing quantitative images for potential clinical applications.

Prominent closed frequent itemsets (CFIs) are the set of highly frequent closed itemsets whose support is considerably larger than remaining closed itemsets in the given transactional dataset. The support value between the prominent CFIs and remaining closed itemsets make the optimum minimum support threshold as it segregates frequent and infrequent item-sets. However, finding an optimum minimum support threshold for mining prominent CFIs is not known prior especially when the data arriving as a stream. Also, using a static minimum support threshold for mining CFIs from the data stream may lead to missing of some itemsets due to concept drift and lossy counting. In this paper, the authors propose to use dynamic and adaptive minimum support threshold for mining prominent CFIs in the landmark streaming setting. This work is first of its kind and closely relate to Top-K CFI mining techniques. The novelty is in using Jenks natural break technique to dynamically find an optimum minimum support threshold for a landmark window and adaptation to the concept drift through delayed insertion. The proposed method has experimented on some well-known real and synthetic datasets demonstrating its suitability for mining prominent CFIs in transactional data streams.

With the current surge in the number of devices connected to the Internet all over the world, usage of network bandwidth has also seen a huge increase. This has led to network traffic congestion and slowdowns. It is increasingly important to anticipate future network usage, which would help prepare and provide adequate infrastructure or service support. In this paper, we propose a model that uses machine learning techniques to analyze network logs of access points installed throughout the campus of San José State University (SJSU) to predict its network usage at a future point in time. We also propose to build a classification model to classify user's browsing behavior as either study or leisure, based on the content of the pages they view. Hence, the final model will be able to predict network throughput of access points and the type of activity they will be used for. We utilize these models in a novel mobile phone application we designed that helps students choose an appropriate place to study or hang out at a chosen time in the near future. Our application combines the use of mobile phone sensors for localization with the power of machine learning models executed in the cloud to provide a seamless user experience for students and faculty alike.

We investigate the application of single-input single-output (SISO) digital predistortion (DPD) to mitigate the nonlinearity in millimeter-wave multi-user RF beamforming arrays. In principle, SISO DPD may not be sufficient to linearize such arrays as a multiple-input one may be required due to coupling between the sub-array antennas. Nevertheless, in practice, the coupling between antennas of different sub-arrays may be much smaller than the coupling between antennas of the same sub-array. It is first shown mathematically that if the coupling between sub-arrays is small, then SISO DPD is sufficient to linearize such arrays. This is then confirmed in practice by linearizing two co-located 64-element sub-arrays driven by 800 MHz modulated signals at 28 GHz. Using four sets of SISO DPD coefficients, the EVM and ACPR were improved from as much as 8% and 30 dBc to better than 2% and 40 dBc, respectively, across all steering angle combinations of the two sub-arrays.

This paper presents a study on the effective constitutive parameters evaluation for meta-materials with highly interaction fields, which are characterized by periodic structures and metamaterials. These materials have been widely used in various media applications, ranging from telecommunications to biomedical engineering. In order to accurately model the behavior of these complex materials, computational modeling is often necessary. The paper discusses the importance of reflection coefficient analysis and the use of specialized software to enhance the accuracy of the simulation. Additionally, the contribution of specific features such as wires to the effective parameters is explored. Through this investigation, the paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the evaluation of effective constitutive parameters for meta-materials with highly interaction fields.

Lightweight cryptography has become more and more important in recent years because of the rise of the Internet of Things (IoT) and usage of smart mobile devices. In this paper, we propose a novel secure lightweight entity authentication hardware primitive called SLATE, where its area is about 50% to more than 3X smaller than existing lightweight ciphers and strong physical unclonable functions (PUFs), respectively. Even though the authentication of SLATE is done through challenge response pair (CRP) verification similar to strong PUFs, the source of the key for SLATE must be coming from any existing secret key storage used for any ciphers. A main advantage of SLATE over most existing strong PUFs being an entity authentication primitive is that SLATE is resistant to known attacks to strong PUFs or logic obfuscations, such as model building attacks and Boolean satisfiability (SAT) attacks. Furthermore, we show that the implementation cost of SLATE with a 176-bit key and 244 CRPs is only 663 gate equivalents (GEs). Compared with lightweight ciphers and existing secure strong PUFs, we show that SLATE is a practical security primitive for resource constrained systems for its extremely small footprint and security. Finally, we show that SLATE is information theoretically secure when valid CRPs are communicated through insecure channels.

The objective of this paper is to investigate the spatio-temporal characteristics of synchrophasor data against spoofing attacks in smart grids. Synchrophasor data is collected by Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) that are distributed in various parts of the grid. However, the increasing use of these devices also increases the risk of spoofing attacks on the PMUs that can severely compromise the grid's stability and overall security. Therefore, it is essential to develop robust techniques for the authentication of synchrophasor data. One such technique is time-frequency analysis that can detect any abnormalities or unauthorized changes in the signals. The frequency control and estimation of power measurement are also crucial for the authentication of synchrophasor data. In this paper, we propose a framework that utilizes these techniques to verify the authenticity of synchrophasor data and protect the smart grid against spoofing attacks. The proposed framework aims to provide a secure and reliable way to authenticate synchrophasor data by analyzing its spatio-temporal characteristics. The results of the proposed framework show promising results with high accuracy in detecting spoofed synchrophasor data. Therefore, it can be helpful for the development of secure and reliable smart grid systems.

This paper proposes an Interval Type-3 Fuzzy System (IT3FS) and a new online fractional-order learning algorithm for fuzzy neural networks. The approach takes into account uncertainty by using fuzzy sets, which are characterized by their membership functions. The stability analysis of the proposed system is carried out and it is shown that the IT3FS ensures better stability than the traditional Fuzzy System. To approximate the optimal solution, heuristic algorithms are used, which are known to perform well in handling complex problems. The proposed algorithm is able to learn the optimal solution of a problem in real-time, which is a significant advantage in practical applications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in comparison to other approximation algorithms. This work is a valuable contribution to the field of fuzzy systems and provides a new approach for online learning in fuzzy neural networks.

We propose an end-to-end architecture for joint 2D and 3D human pose estimation in natural images. Key to our approach is the generation and scoring of a number of pose proposals per image, which allows us to predict 2D and 3D poses of multiple people simultaneously. Hence, our approach does not require an approximate localization of the humans for initialization. Our Localization-Classification-Regression architecture, named LCR-Net, contains 3 main components: 1) the pose proposal generator that suggests candidate poses at different locations in the image; 2) a classifier that scores the different pose proposals; and 3) a regressor that refines pose proposals both in 2D and 3D. All three stages share the convolutional feature layers and are trained jointly. The final pose estimation is obtained by integrating over neighboring pose hypotheses, which is shown to improve over a standard non maximum suppression algorithm. Our method recovers full-body 2D and 3D poses, hallucinating plausible body parts when the persons are partially occluded or truncated by the image boundary. Our approach significantly outperforms the state of the art in 3D pose estimation on Human3.6M, a controlled environment. Moreover, it shows promising results on real images for both single and multi-person subsets of the MPII 2D pose benchmark and demonstrates satisfying 3D pose results even for multiperson images.

Data analysis is the most important aspect of any business as it is critical to decision-making. Data quality assessment is a necessary function to be performed before data analysis, as the quality of data has high impact on the outcome of the analysis. Data quality is a multi-dimensional factor that affects the analysis in numerous ways. Among all the dimensions, accuracy is the most important and hardest dimension to assess. With the advent of big data, this problem becomes more complicated. There are only few studies that focus on data accuracy with minimal domain expert dependency. In this paper, we propose an extensive data accuracy assessment tool that uses machine learning to determine the accuracy of data. In addition, our model also addresses the intrinsic and contextual categories of data accuracy. Our model was developed on Apache Spark which serves as the big data environment for handling large datasets.

This paper focuses on the development of a virtual flux oriented sensorless direct power control technique for QZS inverter connected to the grid for solar PV applications. In this method, inverters are used to convert DC power generated by solar panels into AC power and then connected to the grid. The estimation of reactive power and voltage control are critical factors in the synchronization of the inverter with the grid. Traditional sensor-based methods have limitations in providing optimal performance in steady-state conditions. The proposed sensorless method using virtual flux estimation overcomes the limitations of sensor-based methods by improving the accuracy and reliability of the estimation process. The results indicate that the proposed technique has an excellent performance in terms of reactive power and voltage control, ensuring stable operation in different load conditions. This study contributes to the development of efficient and reliable sensorless control techniques for inverter-based solar PV systems, which have become a crucial source of renewable energy.

This paper proposes a method for robust image-based visual servoing under field of view constraints. The main focus of this research is on improving the performance of visual servoing systems by developing a prescribed performance controller, which guarantees transient analysis and steady-state error bounds. To achieve this, camera calibration and feature extraction techniques are employed to reduce the effects of camera pose errors and maintain accurate image measurements. Additionally, visualization tools are used to analyze the performance of the system in real-time. The proposed method has shown to be effective in dealing with challenges such as occlusions and changing lighting conditions. Consequently, this work contributes to the development of more robust and accurate visual servoing systems.

Cloud computing has changed the landscape of computing, with users able to access vast resources through an internet connection. The evaluation of performance in cloud computing is of great importance, ensuring that systems meet their requirements and remain efficient. To achieve this, benchmark testing has become a popular method for measuring and comparing computer performance. However, without systematic and standardized methods, the reproducibility of the results obtained through benchmark testing are in question. This highlights the importance of methodological principles and good software engineering practices, which can ensure that performance evaluations are conducted with consistency and repeatability. Ultimately, these principles can help to improve the quality of performance evaluations in cloud computing, providing users with objective and reliable metrics on which to base their decisions.

The concept of dependency in a neighborhood rough set model is an important evaluation function for the feature selection. This function considers only the classification information contained in the lower approximation of the decision while ignoring the upper approximation. In this paper, we construct a class of uncertainty measures: decision self-information for the feature selection. These measures take into account the uncertainty information in the lower and the upper approximations. The relationships between these measures and their properties are discussed in detail. It is proven that the fourth measure, called relative neighborhood self-information, is better for feature selection than the other measures, because not only does it consider both the lower and the upper approximations but also the change of its magnitude is largest with the variation of feature subsets. This helps to facilitate the selection of optimal feature subsets. Finally, a greedy algorithm for feature selection has been designed and a series of numerical experiments was carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm often chooses fewer features and improves the classification accuracy in most cases.

In this paper, we present a new load balancing algorithm based on multi-criterion decision making (MCDM) to select efficient relay UAV. For MCDM operation, buffer occupancy, remaining energy and link quality given by number of retransmission are consider. Through simulation result, we demonstrate that the proposed scheme can improving packet delivery ratio and end-to-end delay by reducing the congestion significantly.

This paper proposes a dynamic multi-server searchable encryption scheme based on concept hierarchy, which enhances the security and efficiency of keyword search in cloud computing environments. The scheme utilizes multiple servers to distribute the indexes and encryption operations, improving the scalability and reliability of the system. A hierarchical concept structure is used to represent the semantics of the keywords, enabling more accurate and efficient search results. The scheme provides strong security guarantees, such as confidentiality and data privacy, by utilizing various encryption techniques. The proposed scheme has practical applications in cloud-based systems, where data is commonly stored and managed by multiple servers. Overall, this scheme offers an effective way to ensure secure and efficient keyword search in cloud environments, which are becoming increasingly popular in modern society.

The efficient management of a water supply system requires precise water demand forecasts as inputs. This paper compares existing prediction methods and improves their performance by integrating human-related factors with water consumption in an urban area. Furthermore, a framework for processing and transforming mobility data into time-series is presented. Results show that using human mobility data improves forecasting accuracy reaching 87.6%.

In this paper, the nonlinear observability problem is revisited and studied in a novel framework that is particularly well-suited for the consideration of different practical aspects of the corresponding state estimation problem. In establishing this framework, we highlight connections between fundamental theoretical aspects of the general observability problem with more quantitative considerations similar to those encountered in numerical analysis. A key result of our novel analysis of the observability problem is the introduction of quantitative observability measures for nonlinear systems as a generalization of the notion of observability gramians for linear systems.

In production lines with Bernoulli stations, it is essential to manage resources effectively to ensure reliability and optimize performance. This paper proposes a simultaneous balancing and buffer allocation approach for such serial lines. The proposed methodology takes into account task analysis, resource management, transient analysis, and buffer storage allocation. Moreover, genetic algorithms are used to optimize the allocation of resources and balance the tasks among the different stations. The results show that the proposed approach effectively balances the workload and reduces the overall buffer storage required while maintaining the reliability of the system. This methodology can be used as a practical tool to optimize the performance of production lines with Bernoulli stations.

The performance of wireless sensor network (WSN) system is significantly affected by the coverage quality. For the problem of low coverage of static sensor network nodes and high deployment cost of mobile sensor network nodes, a hybrid sensor network based on cuckoo search (CS) is studied. Node deployment optimization strategy. Firstly, the candidate target position of the mobile node is initially determined by the CS algorithm, and then the position optimization scheme is used to reduce the number of mobile nodes and the average moving distance. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively optimize the deployment of mobile nodes in hybrid WSN, improve the coverage of target areas, and reduce the energy consumption of nodes.

This paper focuses on the tuning of parameters in a fuzzy inference based decision support system that addresses economic issues related to water resource management and provides guidance on scholarships. Fuzzy logic is used in the decision support system due to the inherent uncertainty in the domain of water resource management. The goal of this research is to optimize the performance of the decision support system by tuning the parameters that affect the system's inference process. The research methodology involves using a combination of empirical analysis and numerical simulations to identify the key parameters that affect the system's performance. The findings of the study suggest that by tuning the parameters, the performance of the decision support system can be significantly improved, which can lead to more efficient and effective decision making in the domain of water resource management. Additionally, the paper also provides guidance on the allocation of scholarships to students based on their academic performance and economic background, which demonstrates the usefulness of the decision support system in addressing various economic issues. Overall, this study highlights the importance of tuning parameters in decision support systems to improve their performance and utility in addressing complex economic and social issues.

By using such methods as data cleansing, transformation and mining implementation process, etc. related to data mining technique, enterprise financial activities and administrative affairs may be effectively allocated, organized, coordinated and controlled, and accordingly financial allocation process may be effectively optimized and economic benefits of enterprises may be steadily and rapidly enhanced. However by now, due to the improper use of the method, most enterprises in China may not reach this point, and therefore their economic benefits are difficult to be improved dramatically. For this reason, based on the overview of related theories on data mining methods, this Paper specifically analyzes the status quo and countermeasures of the application of data mining method in corporate fiscal management.

This paper introduces an energy-harvesting wireless sensor network (WSN) system for factory environment monitoring, called Cloud Factory Environment Monitoring. The system leverages piezoelectric materials to convert vibrations into electrical energy, thereby providing self-sustaining power for the WSN nodes. The WSN nodes are deployed in production facilities to monitor various aspects of the environment such as temperature, humidity, and air quality. The collected data is transmitted wirelessly to a cloud computing platform, where it is processed and analyzed in real-time. The cloud servers provide users with a web-based interface to visualize and manage the data. The proposed system improves the efficiency of factory environment monitoring by eliminating the need for frequent battery replacements and reducing maintenance costs. Additionally, it allows for real-time monitoring of the environment, enabling timely detection of abnormalities and proactive measures to be taken to mitigate potential issues.

Face restoration from low resolution and noise is important for applications of face analysis recognition. However, most existing face restoration models omit the multiple scale issues in the face restoration problem, which is still not well solved in the research area. In this paper, we propose a sequential gating ensemble network (SGEN) for a multiscale noise robust face restoration issue. To endow the network with multiscale representation ability, we first employ the principle of ensemble learning for SGEN network architecture design. The SGEN aggregates multilevel base-encoders and base-decoders into the network, which enables the network to contain multiple scales of receptive field. Instead of combining these base-en/decoders directly with nonsequential operations, the SGEN takes base-en/decoders from different levels as sequential data. Specifically, it is visualized that SGEN learns to sequentially extract high-level information from base-encoders in a bottom-up manner and restore low-level information from base-decoders in a top-down manner. Besides, we propose realizing bottom-up and top-down information combination and selection with a sequential gating unit (SGU). The SGU sequentially takes information from two different levels as inputs and decides the output based on one active input. Experimental results on the benchmark dataset demonstrate that our SGEN is more effective at multiscale human face restoration with more image details and less noise than state-of-the-art image restoration models. Further utilizing an adversarial training scheme, SGEN also produces more visually preferred results than other models under subjective evaluation.

In recent years, the popularity of deep neural networks (DNNs) has grown rapidly, particularly in applications such as autonomous vehicles and graphics processing units. However, the significant energy consumption of DNNs remains a major concern. In this paper, we propose PredJoule, a novel framework for optimizing the energy consumption of DNNs. PredJoule relies on timing prediction techniques to perform the optimization process while ensuring the predictability of the DNNs timing behavior. By utilizing timing predictability, PredJoule is able to achieve energy savings without sacrificing the accuracy of DNNs. Experimental results demonstrate that PredJoule outperforms state-of-the-art optimization techniques in terms of energy efficiency while achieving comparable or even better prediction accuracy. Overall, PredJoule provides a promising approach for efficient and predictable energy optimization of DNNs, which has the potential to significantly benefit various applications, especially those involving autonomous vehicles and biological neural networks.

Inertial navigation is a widely used technique for determining the position, velocity, and attitude of a moving object without the use of external aids. However, estimation of gyro drift in the inertial navigation system is a challenging task, as it is difficult to accurately measure the drift rate. In this paper, a novel gyrod drift estimation method for inertial navigation system based on particle swarm optimization is proposed. Particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to solve the nonlinear optimization problem of gyro drift estimation, which leads to an improved estimation accuracy compared to conventional Kalman filters. The proposed method is validated by a series of experiments, which demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the error in estimation of gyro drift. Moreover, the method is also applicable to other force measurement applications, as it provides more accurate estimation and improved system stability.

Problem-Based Learning (PBL) and Conceive-Design-Implement-Operate (CDIO) are two essential methodologies for engineering education that are gaining popularity owing to their ability to create innovative solutions to real-world engineering problems. This study presents a polynesian canoes case study that demonstrates the effectiveness of PBL and CDIO in engineering education. The study examines the use of solid and computational modeling, and three-dimensional displays to design and simulate the performance of the canoe. Further, the study explores the optimization of the design through tuning, finite element analysis, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Additionally, computer aided manufacturing (CAM) is used to develop a physical prototype that validates the simulation results. The findings suggest that PBL and CDIO are effective teaching methods that motivate students and enhance their engineering skills through hands-on experiences, thus preparing them for professional practice in the engineering field. The results also indicate that the use of computer-based simulations and CAM technologies can significantly reduce the design cycle time and cost, while improving the quality of the final product or solution. Overall, this study highlights the benefits of using PBL and CDIO in engineering education and provides a practical example of their application through the polynesian canoes case study.

Unsupervised image change detection plays an important role in various fields, such as monitoring urban development and examining geological variations. In this paper, we propose a novel Bipartite Differential Neural Network (BiDNN) for unsupervised image change detection. BiDNN first extracts features from two images using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and then constructs the bipartite graph with the features. By sampling the features and selecting candidate matching pairs in the bipartite graph, BiDNN is capable of identifying changes between two images effectively. Additionally, we combine BiDNN with image segmentation to exclude unchanged regions and achieve more accurate change detection. Experimental results on two public datasets show that BiDNN outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality, and can handle images with large geometric and radiometric variations.

This paper proposes a new approach for large-scale corpus analysis called A Phrase Topic Model. This model, unlike traditional models which rely on individual words, utilizes phrases to capture the relationships between words and their respective semantics. The model incorporates both computational modeling and analytical models to create a reliable and accurate representation of the corpus. It also utilizes probability distributions to calculate the likelihood of a word belonging to a certain topic. The model is highly flexible and can be applied to various data models, making it an invaluable tool for researchers and data analysts. The proposed approach provides a new way to analyze and understand large-scale corpora by focusing on the vocabulary and semantics of phrases, rather than individual words. The results of this study support the effectiveness of A Phrase Topic Model and highlight its potential to advance computational linguistics and natural language processing tools.

Calibration of hand-eye systems is essential in many applications, particularly in robot vision systems. This paper proposes a general hand-eye calibration technique based on the minimization of reprojection error. The calibration technique relies on the use of cameras to estimate both the position and orientation of the hand relative to the robot base. The proposed method is suitable for use in service robots, where accurate hand-eye calibration is critical for high-performance robot operation. The results of the hand-eye calibration are used to estimate the hand-eye transformation matrix, which provides an accurate estimate of the hand's position and orientation. Overall, the proposed method provides an efficient and accurate means of hand-eye calibration for a wide range of robot vision applications.

In this paper, we implemented the architecture of DV700 which is deep learning based image recognition accelerator in edge computing applications, and measured performance in FPGA environment. As a result, it operates at 12.9 fps in GoogleNet and 15.6 fps in SSD algorithms with 79MHz operating frequency environment.

LoRaWAN is a wireless communication protocol that has gained popularity in recent years for its ability to provide long range connectivity with low power consumption, making it ideal for urban areas. This paper explores the use of LoRaWAN in city scale IoT deployments, specifically in the context of air quality monitoring. The design and implementation of a LoRaWAN-based system for air quality monitoring are discussed, including the use of logic gates and hardware components such as sensors. The importance of the Internet of Things (IoT) in urban areas is also emphasized, as well as the need for reliable and efficient wide area networks to support such deployments. Overall, this paper highlights the potential of LoRaWAN for city scale IoT applications, particularly in the realm of air quality monitoring, and provides insights into the practical considerations and challenges of implementing such systems.

A signal emitter can be located using diverse types of direction finding (DF) techniques. One of the most widely used techniques is the direction of arrival (DOA) estimation using antenna arrays. An array configuration that can increase the degrees of freedom (DOF) or the number of estimated sources is desired. Multi-level prime array (MLPA) uses multiple uniform linear subarrays where the number of elements in the subarrays is a pairwise coprime integer. Compared with nested and coprime arrays, the MLPA requires a smaller aperture size which is important in mobile applications. The different MLPA configurations can be constructed for a given number of antennas and the one that maximizes the DOF is exploited. These configurations have a difference coarray with a large number of consecutive lags and few holes. The number of consecutive lags can be increased by properly compressing the inter-element spacing of one subarray under a fixed number of antennas and without changing the aperture size. This paper proposes a new compressed MLPA configuration and demonstrates its performance in sparse DOA estimation. The resultant array, MLPA with compressed subarray (MLPAC), can have a hole-free difference coarray as in nested array case. The MLPAC can estimate a larger number of sources using both MUSIC and sparse reconstruction algorithms. Mutual coupling between sensors has also been evaluated. The simulation results confirm the achievable DOF and the advantage of the proposed configuration in the DOA estimation.

This paper defines flexibility reserve trajectory as a single reserve product that not only supplies the energy imbalance in real-time operation but also the resulting ramping requirements by embedding the flexible ramping trajectories as time derivative of the reserve trajectories. Further, a stochastic optimization model is proposed for multi-fidelity co-optimization of energy and flexibility reserve in day-ahead power systems operation. The proposed model integrates operation decisions with different levels of modeling fidelity in a single stochastic optimization problem. More specifically, day-ahead energy trajectories, day-ahead flexibility reserve capacity trajectories, and real-time flexibility reserve deployment trajectories are modeled by Bernstein polynomials with different degrees as required to match the load and renewable generation with different levels of variability in day-ahead and real-time operations. The proposed model is implemented on the IEEE reliability test system using load and solar generation data of California ISO, where the numerical results demonstrate that the proposed model schedules a reserve capacity that more accurately matches the real-time energy imbalance and ramping requirements of net-load, while reducing the total operation cost of the system.

Modeling of spectrum occupancy is important for better channel utilization, accurate spectrum sensing, and enhanced Quality of Service (QoS) to the primary user (PU) in a cognitive radio (CR) system. Existing models are highly dependent on the spatio-temporal variations of the PU activity as the statistical behavior of the PU changes with respect to the location, spectrum band, and the varying load time. In this work, a generalized Gaussian Mixture model (GMM) has been investigated for characterizing the spectrum occupancy of the PU in three spectrally different CR scenarios, viz. VHF/UHF band, GSM band, and ISM band. The goodness of fit performance of GMM is compared with the widely used spectrum occupancy model based on Beta distribution. Further, the robustness of GMM has been validated through learning based prediction via Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), thereby proposing a hybrid approach of statistical and predictive modeling of spectrum occupancy for enhanced dynamic spectrum access.

Fault detection plays an important role in supervising the operation of robotic swarm systems. If faults are not detected, they can considerably affect the performance of the robot swarm. In this paper, we present a robust fault detection mechanism against noise and uncertainties in data, by merging the multiresolution representation of data using wavelets with the sensitivity to small changes of an exponentially weighted moving average scheme. Specifically, to monitor swarm robotics systems performing a virtual viscoelastic control model for circle formation task, the proposed mechanism is applied to the uncorrelated residuals form principal component analysis model. Monitoring results using a simulation data from ARGoS simulator demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved fault detection performances compared with the conventional approach.

Single-carrier frequency-domain equalization (SC-FDE) is a promising technique for coherent high-rate underwater acoustic (UWA) communications. In this paper, a time-frequency domain turbo equalization (TFD-TE) scheme is proposed for single-carrier modulation. The TFD-TE scheme is to couple a multi-channel frequency domain equalizer with phase rotation compensation and a low-order single-channel time-domain turbo equalizer. To mitigate the error propagation and further enhance receiver performance, a bidirectional equalizer that combined the soft outputs of a conventional equalizer and a backward equalizer is introduced into the proposed TFD-TE scheme (Bi-TFD-TF). The sparse channel is estimated by the improved proportionate normalized least mean squares (IPNLMS) algorithm block by block. Both the simulated and experimental results show the proposed TFD-TE can effectively improve system performance with acceptable complexity. The proposed TFD-TE scheme is evaluated using communication data collected from the DJK15 lake experiment. For the 1 × 4 single-input multiple-output (SIMO) communication system using quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) and 8-phase shift keying (8PSK) modulations, the proposed scheme achieves error-free transmission after a few iterations. Our receiver achieves a maximum raw data rate of 12 kbit/s and a reliable net data rate of 4 kbit/s within 4-kHz bandwidth at a range of 10.8 km. Compared with conventional frequency domain turbo equalization (FD-TE), the proposed TFD-TE scheme can enhance 0.8-1.3 dB in terms of output signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR). The related bi-TFD-TE provides an additional 0.8-1.7-dB OSNR improvements.

The media access control (MAC) layer of the vehicular ad-hoc network (VANET) is designed 3 to provide fast and reliable vehicles to vehicles (V2V) or vehicles to infrastructures (V2I) access. With the development of autonomous driving and intelligent transportation, many sensor information in large-scale vehicles require efficient and reliable transmission with V2V and V2I technologies. In recent years, the demand for various services in VANETs is growing rapidly, which poses great challenges to the design of the MAC protocol. An adaptive scheme for channel frame structure can enhance channel access flexibility to cope with the changing network topologies in vehicular environments. In this paper, we adopt an adaptive frame scheme on the control channel and the service channels, which mainly improves two aspects of channel access performance: improved time slot utilization of the broadcasting period as much as possible while ensuring the vehicle can access the control channel quickly; and increasing the throughput of the service channels without generating excessive overhead. Analysis and simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed mechanism.

Traffic flow is not a strange phenomenon anymore. Currently, traffic density is a big problem faced in big cities. Increasing the vehicle amount which is not balanced with the capacity of road impact on the transportation system, especially the density of vehicles on the road. Thus, traffic monitoring is needed to minimize congestion and traffic accidents and also develope ITS (Intelligent Transport System). This paper discusses realistic vehicle mobility simulation based on traffic surveys of a city using a microscopic model simulation by using Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO). This paper discusses realistic vehicle mobility simulation based on traffic surveys of a city using a microscopic model simulation by using Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO). SUMO is an open source road traffic simulator program that allows users to build simulations of vehicle movement on network topology. In particular, the SUMO network has some information like each edge as a collection of paths including the position, shape and speed limit of each path, the logic of traffic lights sourced from the crossroads, the correct junction rules, the relationship between the lanes at the intersection. The input format which is used is demand data of survey results from the vehicles number at a certain time in each way. It can be known the pattern the traffic distribution. This traffic distribution pattern will be modeled on SUMO applications so that this application can simulate the mobility of the original vehicle in the big city. The data traffic will be managed and computed with Kalman Filter to enhance location accuration. Then, it will be displayed on Website. Based on analyst of vehicle traffic volume in Central Surabaya, it has normal distibution traffic which is the rush hour in 4 pm. - 5 pm Based on SUMO result, Surabaya map from OSM could be integrated with SUMO GUI. adjust the speed of the road limit at Central Surabaya is the maximum speed limit on the motor, car and taxi is 33.33 m / s and from the test results obtained parameter value Q = 1E-04 and R = 1E-04 on Kalman filter seen that in estimating vehicle speed has the biggest percentage of error up to 49,17%.

Situation-aware technologies will create new services and applications in emerging fields such as autonomous transportation, home automation, and smart cities. A main challenge in situation-aware applications is data association with "extended" objects that originate an unknown number of measurements. To address this challenge, we introduce a new method based on factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm. Our approach makes it possible to reduce computational complexity in a principled manner due to an overcomplete description of data association uncertainty that enables a "stretching" of the factor graph. The complexity of the resulting sum-product algorithm for data association with extended objects (SPADA-X), only scales quadratically in the number of objects and linearly in the number of measurements. Without relying on heuristic preprocessing steps, it is suitable for localization and tracking of multiple objects that potentially generate a large number of measurements. Simulation results demonstrate the excellent estimation accuracy and scalability of SPADA-X.

This paper proposes a new approach called Stochastic Artificial Potentials for Online Safe Navigation. The main focus of the research is the navigation of robots in complex and unpredictable environments. The proposed algorithm is based on linear programming and convex functions, which are used to model the robot's movement and avoid obstacles. The robot sensing systems are used to gather information about the environment, and the stochastic potential functions are used to control the movement of the robot. The algorithm is designed to converge to a safe and efficient path, while also taking into consideration the uncertainty of the environment. The proposed approach is particularly useful in aerospace electronics, where reliable navigation systems are critical for the safety and success of missions. Overall, the Stochastic Artificial Potentials for Online Safe Navigation algorithm provides a promising approach for safe and efficient navigation of robots in unpredictable environments.

Speech recognition is a crucial element in the development of smart IoT devices, providing users with the ability to interact with technology in a natural and intuitive way. However, the outsourcing of speech recognition tasks introduces significant privacy concerns, as sensitive audio data may be compromised during the transmission or storage process. Cryptography and logic gates have been proposed as potential solutions to this problem, allowing for the secure processing of audio data without compromising privacy. Various protocols have been developed to implement these techniques in practice, with the aim of ensuring that speech recognition can be carried out effectively while still protecting user privacy. Additionally, the use of neural networks in speech recognition has shown great potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of this technology, while still maintaining the necessary levels of privacy and security for IoT devices. Overall, privacy-preserving speech recognition is an important area of research for the development of smart IoT devices, and the use of cryptography, logic gates, and neural networks are key tools in this effort.

The development of hardware-based neural networks has made significant strides in recent years, with more efficient and powerful designs being made possible by advances in CMOS technology. This paper explores the use of field programmable gate arrays in creating high-performance neural network accelerators, as well as the potential for in-memory computing to further boost the efficiency of these systems. Biological neural networks continue to provide an inspiration for hardware design, with deep learning algorithms leveraging the power of computational models to achieve remarkable results. Circuit analysis is crucial in creating optimally efficient systems, and energy efficiency is a major concern in this field. Ultimately, as the power of neural networks continues to grow, the potential for hardware-based designs to revolutionize fields such as image recognition, natural language processing, and robotics will only continue to increase.

Deep learning has been applied in physical-layer communications systems in recent years and has demonstrated fascinating results that were comparable or even better than human expert systems. In this paper, a novel convolutional neural networks (CNNs)-based autoencoder communication system is proposed, which can work intelligently with arbitrary block length, can support different throughput and can operate under AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels as well as deviations from AWGN environments. The proposed generalized communication system is comprised of carefully designed convolutional neural layers and, hence, inherits CNN's breakthrough characteristics, such as generalization, feature learning, classification, and fast training convergence. On the other hand, the end-to-end architecture jointly performs the tasks of encoding/decoding and modulation/demodulation. Finally, we provide the numerous simulation results of the learned system in order to illustrate its generalization capability under various system conditions.

This paper proposes two methods for parameter identification of multicrystalline modules using five improved mathematical models. The first method involves iterative techniques to estimate the parameters. The second method involves integrated circuit modeling to derive the required parameters. The improved mathematical models allow for accurate estimation of the parameters that influence module performance, such as series resistance, shunt resistance, and ideality factor. The parameters can be estimated using temperature measurement and distance measurement techniques. This research provides practical insights for improving the efficiency and performance of multicrystalline modules in photovoltaic applications.

Detecting anomalous behavior in wireless spectrum is a demanding task due to the sheer complexity of the electromagnetic spectrum use. Wireless spectrum anomalies can take a wide range of forms from the presence of an unwanted signal in a licensed band to the absence of an expected signal, which makes manual labeling of anomalies difficult and suboptimal. We present, Spectrum Anomaly Detector with Interpretable FEatures (SAIFE), an Adversarial Autoencoder (AAE) based anomaly detector for wireless spectrum anomaly detection using Power Spectral Density (PSD) data which achieves good anomaly detection and localization in an unsupervised setting. In addition, we investigate the model's capabilities to learn interpretable features such as signal bandwidth, class and center frequency in a semi-supervised fashion. Along with anomaly detection the model exhibits promising results for lossy PSD data compression up to 120X and semi-supervised signal classification accuracy close to 100% on three datasets just using 20% labeled samples. Finally the model is tested on data from one of the distributed Electrosense sensors over a long term of 500 hours showing its anomaly detection capabilities.

With the proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor networks, mobile social networks, crowdsensing applications, and beyond, huge amounts of data are being explosively generated every day. While big data and IoT bring well-understood benefits to increase knowledge and improve the quality of our daily lives, they also face wide attacking surfaces, and thus raise critical concerns on notions of trust, security, and privacy. One of the fundamental questions is how to collect, store, and process the huge amounts of data in a secure and privacy-preserving manner, without compromising the potential of capitalization on big data and IoT.

The use of technology in education has become increasingly prevalent, with e-learning tools being extensively employed to enhance the delivery of education. In this paper, we propose an e-learning tool designed to enhance technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPCK) in the field of electronic learning. The tool incorporates servers, embedded computing, real-time systems, and machine learning techniques to provide a comprehensive learning experience. Furthermore, the tool offers a unique feature that allows learners to interact with 3D models, which are representations of real-life objects, to enhance their understanding of complex concepts. The 3D models come in different shapes, and learners can manipulate them to gain a deeper insight into the subject matter. Overall, the proposed e-learning tool offers an innovative way of improving learners' TPCK through a varied set of interactive and engaging activities.

Emphysema quantification and sub-typing is actively studied on cohorts of full-lung high-resolution CT (HRCT) scans, with promising results. Transfer of quantification and classification tools to cardiac CT scans, which involve 70% of the lungs, is challenging due to lower image resolution and degradation of textural patterns. In this study, we propose an original deep-learning domain-adaptation framework to use a pre-existing dictionary of lung texture patterns (LTP), learned on gold-standard full-lung HRCT scans, to label emphysema regions on cardiac CT scans. The method exploits convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained for: 1) supervised lung texture classification on synthetic cardiac images, and 2) adversarial learning to discriminate between real and synthetic cardiac images. Combination of the classification and adversarial tasks enables to label real cardiac CT scans, and is evaluated on the MESA cohort (N = 15,357 scans). Our results show that image features derived from the adversarial training preserve the labeling accuracy on synthetic scans. LTP histogram signatures generated on 4,315 longitudinal pairs of cardiac CT scans, show high level of consistency over time and scanner generations. The ability to robustly label emphysema texture patterns on cardiac CT scans will enable large-scale longitudinal studies over 10 years of follow-up, for better understanding of the disease progression.

In this paper, a thinned array design approach utilizing an autocorrelation matching strategy is proposed. The strategy is based on the correlation calculation of each antenna element in the array leading to a considerably reduced number of elements, while maintaining the desired radiation pattern. To optimize the design parameters, genetic algorithms are utilized to identify the ideal arrangements of antenna elements. The pattern matching technique is then incorporated to facilitate the selection of the most suitable thinned array configuration for the specified radiation pattern requirement. The proposed approach is shown to achieve better results compared to the conventional methods in terms of power consumption and cost. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through simulations and experimental results on phased arrays with different radiation pattern requirements. Overall, the proposed thinned array design approach provides a promising direction for antenna optimization with reduced cost and complexity.

This paper presents a self-learning and efficient health-status analysis approach for a core router system. Feature extraction and time series analysis are utilized to obtain high-level information from the raw measurement data. Monitoring is then performed to identify any anomalies in the system. Anomaly detection is achieved by using various detectors that are designed based on the critical parameters of the system. Measurement accuracy is further improved by leveraging fault tolerance techniques. The proposed approach not only enhances the system's robustness and reliability but also reduces the operational cost by minimizing the human intervention. The experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Osteoporosis is a skeletal disorder which is mostly observed in the elderly and women. The radiographs are still in a standard practice to diagnose the bone health especially osteoporosis. In this paper, an automatic methodology is developed as an algorithm that could classify a radiographic image of the bone and predict whether the patient is osteoporotic or healthy which generally is difficult to visualize as radiographs are dark and do not exhibit any information unless exposed to some brightness. A novel approach has been developed which is a fully automatic method for feature selection, classification and detection by the application of machine learning classifiers - all Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Nearest Neighbours(NNs). Further a promising result has been obtained using machine learning accuracy of 95% which is clinically significant for osteoporosis detection.

Handling congestion in LTE/5G cellular networks has become a critical issue due to recent, rapid increase in cellular network traffic. Control plane congestion becomes particularly serious when accommodating massive M2M/IoT terminals into cellular networks. Although various methods have been proposed for accommodation of M2M/IoT terminals, most of them are mainly based on mathematical analysis and simulation experiments. In this paper, we show the experimental evaluation results of the performance of a mobile core network to assess the impact of bursty access from M2M/IoT terminals. First, we constructed our experimental environment based on open-source implementation of mobile core networks and emulated user terminals. Then, we conducted experiments on simultaneous attach requests from multiple user terminals and measured the processing delay at each mobile core node. The results of our evaluations proved that concentrating attach requests from forty user terminals increases the processing time at a mobility management entity (MME) by up to around 510% when an MME node is operated on a virtual machine with 1 GHz / 1 core CPU.

In this paper, models of two fuzzy inference systems for supporting the process of managing micro grid PV systems are presented. The first model is for managing a PV/battery micro grid connected system and uses fuzzy mapping of three input variables: power produced by PV panels, power in battery and consumed power. The output of the FIS, obtained after applying the fuzzy rules, is a decision for choosing which power source is to be used. The second model consists of one additional energy source (diesel generator/fuel cell) and thus the input variables are four. The simulation tests are conducted in MatLab. This research is part of a project for optimizing the energy consumption of a building with the use of independent alternative renewable energy sources. The input test data for the optimization are the amount of used energy for lighting, heating, computers power supply and other needs of one particular building (the building of Burgas Free University) and the corresponding price of each of the used energy sources.

For solving the problem of sequence failure diagnosis of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) water management subsystem, this paper proposes a PEMFC failure diagnosis method of time series based on the bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE). This approach adopts the normalization strategy to eliminate the influence caused by dimensional differences of different parameters. The t-SNE is presented to decrease the dimensionality of normalized data to the estimate of intrinsic dimensionality to extract key characteristic variables.
