The width of the diagnostic window is set to transform the original single moment diagnosis problem into the fault diagnosis problem of multi-variable time series, which is more consistent with the time scale and physical evolution law of the PEMFC water management fault generation. The 672 sets of training sets and 448 sets of test sets are learned and tested by the BiLSTM. The experimental results show that the BiLSTM-tSNE method can realize the sequence fault diagnosis of the PEMFC water management subsystem with 96.88% diagnostic accuracy and 24 s of operation time. Compared with the conventional approach of multi-class support vector machine algorithm, the training accuracy and the testing accuracy of the proposed method are improved by 15% and 16.88%, respectively. The operation time of the presented approach is only about 1/28 of the multi-class support vector machine algorithm.

This paper investigates and computes dust particle alignment in relation to cross polarization discrimination. Relevant forces influencing the particle alignment such as inertial torques and turbulence shear are calculated. The result shows how the forces affect the particle alignment, and the torques dominating the alignment of certain dust particle sizes are established.

Mobile storage systems have become increasingly popular with the rise of cloud computing and the rapid adoption of mobile handsets. However, these systems are not immune to failures and require effective maintenance and repair strategies to ensure their reliability. This paper explores various repair strategies for mobile storage systems, with a focus on maintenance engineering and mathematical models for predicting failure rates. The importance of encoding in ensuring data integrity is also discussed, as well as the impact of bandwidth on repair times. Ultimately, the findings of this paper provide valuable insights for improving the overall reliability of mobile storage systems and optimizing repair strategies to minimize downtime and maximize efficiency.

In article describes an intellectual-information system that will be used to make managerial decisions on the operation of technical personnel of power plants and similar process facilities. In particular, the results of its work will help to make a decision on the appropriateness of upgrading the skills of technical personnel. The methods of intellectualization used to determine the level of knowledge based on odd logic allow not only to assess the level of knowledge, but also to automate the process of its consolidation and enhancement. The use of this method allows the training of technical personnel on the job. The method of intellectualization of an estimation of a level of knowledge of the basic theory of calculation of optimum feeding parameters of regulating devices of automatic control systems is described. Solving this problem in the example of automation evaluation on the parametric synthesis of one-loop, cascade and combined control systems. Control of the level of knowledge for parametric synthesis determined by the correct choice of a point on a graph of the amplitude-phase characteristics and D-partition graphs. The adequacy of established fuzzy output system tested in a program FuzzyTECH.

This paper proposes a mathematical model for estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of single cell Li-Ion batteries based on their state of charge and resistance during discharges. The modeling approach involves taking constant current discharges at different times and estimating the RUL based on the changes in resistance and state of charge. Results show that the proposed model is able to accurately estimate the RUL of Li-Ion batteries with high precision when compared with experimental data. This approach is highly significant given the increasing usage of Li-Ion batteries in various devices, and provides a basis for predicting battery performance and enhancing energy management systems for efficient use of battery power.

This paper presents a Generalized Statistical Spectrum Occupancy Modelling (GSM) framework, which focuses on capturing the spatiotemporal statistical characteristics of radio spectrum occupancy behavior. To represent and analyze these behaviors, data models and predictive models are established. The proposed framework is designed for use in real-time systems that require efficient algorithms for spectrum occupancy prediction. The predictive models in the GSM framework are built using Recurrent Neural Networks, which are trained on the historical spectrum occupancy data. The proposed models are validated using learning-based predictive validation techniques. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed models is demonstrated with a case study on the Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of radio communication systems, where time measurement is used to estimate the accuracy of the predictive models. The results show that the proposed GSM framework provides a promising approach for spectrum occupancy prediction in real-time systems.

This paper proposes a protocol for Smart Grids that enables two-way communication between power generation sources and consumers. The protocol accommodates Renewable Energy Sources such as solar, wind, and hydro power within the power system. The Smart Grids utilize Wireless Sensor Networks for monitoring energy consumption and production. The system is equipped with Batteries that can store and deliver the energy produced. The proposed protocol defines the communication Protocols and data formats for supporting Ad Hoc networks, which can form spontaneously to facilitate interaction between power generation sources and consumers. The system proposed in this paper offers an efficient and effective solution for energy production and consumption that accommodates the integration of Renewable Energy Sources into the power grid, while providing two-way communication and monitoring of energy consumption and production.

This paper proposes an adjacent graph based methodology to assess vulnerability of electrical networks considering fault adjacent relationships among branches. The proposed methodology utilizes the adjacent graph model to identify the impact of fault occurrence in one branch to the adjacent branches, and to consequently quantify the vulnerability of electrical networks. The proposed methodology is validated through a case study, and the results indicate that the proposed methodology achieves better accuracy in vulnerability assessment compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, this paper examines the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in relation to various measurements and indices, and the results suggest that the proposed methodology can be used to identify the most vulnerable branches in electrical networks. The proposed methodology also takes into account complex networks, load modeling, loading, and transient analysis, which are important factors in accurately assessing vulnerability in electrical networks. Overall, the results of this study suggest that the proposed methodology can provide a reliable approach for vulnerability assessment of electrical networks, and can be applied in real-life situations to minimize the impact of faults and increase the reliability of electrical networks.

Network Function Virtualization (NFV) has attracted significant attention from both industry and academia as an important paradigm change in network service provisioning. Most existing studies on admissions of NFV-enabled requests focused on deploying dedicated Virtualized Network Function (VNF) instances to serve each individual request without exploring the sharing of VNF instances among multiple user requests. However, with ever-growing demands of user services, exclusive usages of VNF instances in most networks drastically degrade the network performance and largely under-utilize the VNF instance resources. In this paper, we jointly explore two different VNF instance scaling techniques, horizontal scaling and vertical scaling techniques, to improve the network throughput while minimizing the operational cost of the network, where horizontal scaling that migrates some existing VNF instances from their current locations to new locations to allow the VNF instances to be shared by multiple requests to reduce the resource consumption and operational cost of the network, and vertical scaling that instantiates new VNF instances to meet the demands of new request admissions if existing VNF instances sharing becomes more expensive or the end-to-end delay requirements of currently executing requests will be violated. We first propose a unified framework of maximizing the network throughput, by admitting as many as NFV-enabled requests while meeting the end-to-end delay requirements of the admitted requests. We then provide an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) solution for the problem when the problem size is small. Otherwise, we devise an efficient algorithm through a non-trivial reduction that reduces the problem to the minimum-weight feedback arc set problem and the generalized assignment problem (GAP). We finally conduct experiments to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms a baseline algorithm and achieves a performance on a par with its optimal ILP solution.

The article describes a unique method of processing scanned point cloud on a moving object with variable speed. Point clouds represent a set of trucks loaded by a scanning gate made up of four 2D laser scanners. Three scanners record the surface of the truck from three sides, the fourth scanner records the longitudinal change of the profile of one of a truck's side. From this profile, the method evaluates the motion movement function by which all other point clouds are recalculated. The result is a modified point clouds representing the surface of the standing set. The article also provides a way of point segmentation that separates the points representing the timber load from the truck.

The economic progress of the Internet of Things (IoT) is phenomenal. Applications range from checking the alignment of some components during a manufacturing process, monitoring of transportation and pedestrian levels to enhance driving and walking path, remotely observing terminally ill patients by means of medical devices such as implanted devices and infusion pumps, and so on. To provide security, encrypting the data becomes an indispensable requirement, and symmetric encryptions algorithms are becoming a crucial implementation in the resource constrained environments. Typical symmetric encryption algorithms like Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) showcases an assumption that end points of communications are secured and that the encryption key being securely stored. However, devices might be physically unprotected, and attackers may have access to the memory while the data is still encrypted. It is essential to reserve the key in such a way that an attacker finds it hard to extract it. At present, techniques like White-Box cryptography has been utilized in these circumstances. But it has been reported that applying White-Box cryptography in IoT devices have resulted in other security issues like the adversary having access to the intermediate values, and the practical implementations leading to Code lifting attacks and differential attacks. In this paper, a solution is presented to overcome these problems by demonstrating the need of White-Box Cryptography to enhance the security by utilizing the cipher block chaining (CBC) mode.

This paper proposes a robust real-time embedded face detection system using field programmable gate arrays (FPGA). Face detection is a fundamental task in computer vision and is widely used in various applications. The proposed system is capable of accurately detecting faces in real-time, making it ideal for applications with strict time constraints. The system is implemented on FPGA, which provides high-speed processing and low power consumption. Feature extraction is performed using machine learning algorithms, enabling the system to accurately identify faces from a camera feed. The system is designed to be highly reliable and can operate in harsh environments. The FPGA chip used in the system is the Cyclone series, which provides high-performance computing at a low cost. In summary, the proposed system provides a robust and efficient solution for face detection in embedded systems.

Delay tolerant networks (DTNs) are wireless mobile networks, where the nodes are sparse and end-to-end connectivity is rare. The intermittent connectivity in DTNs makes it challenging to efficiently deliver messages. Research results have shown that the routing protocol based on reinforcement learning can achieve a reasonable balance between routing performance and cost. However, how to predict the next hop of messages more accurately is still open. In this paper, Double Q-Learning Routing (DQLR) protocol is proposed, which investigates the routing selection of the next hop in a distributed manner and solves the overestimation problem by Double Q-Learning algorithm. Further, the intermediate value and dynamic reward mechanisms are proposed to adapt node mobility and network topology change, which improve the network performance. The simulation results show that DQLR protocol can increase the delivery ratio with a low overhead.

Image segmentation using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has become an increasingly popular approach for small organ segmentation in various biological systems, such as forestry. However, due to the limited amount of available training data, the performance of these networks can be significantly affected. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge-aided CNN framework for small organ segmentation, which utilizes additional external knowledge to enhance the network's performance. Our framework integrates both classical image segmentation techniques and informatics knowledge into the CNN architecture. By constraining the network with additional information, our method can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of small organ segmentation, even on limited training data. Experimental results show that our proposed network outperforms state-of-the-art CNN-based methods on small organ segmentation tasks in the forestry domain, while maintaining high efficiency during the training process. Our approach could also be extended to other biological systems with limited training data, where external knowledge can provide additional guidance for the training of CNNs.

Radiomic synthesis has become an important research area in medical image analysis. Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in synthesizing new radiomic features. The entropic nature of radiomic features makes them challenging to analyze and predict. The CNNs can capture these entropic features and generate meaningful new features. This technique can be applied to analyze lesions in medical images and predict correlations between different features. The use of CNNs in radiomic synthesis has great potential for improving the accuracy of cancer diagnosis and treatment. Further research in this area can provide new insights into the complex nature of radiomic features and their application in medical image analysis.

The overwhelming commercial success of connected things and personal mobile devices is driving the dense and uncontrolled deployment of wireless networks using unlicensed frequency bands. This results in heavy congestion and interference, leading to considerable loss of network performance. The only sustainable solution is some form of collaboration between users. Not only does this require new technology to facilitate such collaboration, it also demands for new business models that accommodate new, collaboration facilitating roles. In this paper we propose a generic business model for sustainable spectrum sharing in unlicensed frequency band. It includes two new actors, the Spectrum Broker and the Wi-5 System Operator. The business model is tested against popular use cases, in dialogue with various European network operators. The results indicate that the model is applicable and viable.

This paper proposes a new adaptive layering algorithm for sound speed profile, which is crucial for efficient acoustic signal propagation in various scenarios. The proposed algorithm utilizes ray tracing and mathematical model to estimate the sound speed profile in the surrounding medium. When the sound speed profile is not available, mean square error methods are used for correction. Through trajectory analysis, the algorithm adapts layering depths to accurately fit the sound speed profile, leading to improved accuracy in prediction. The proposed algorithm can be used in a wide range of acoustics applications, which can benefit from more accurate sound speed profile estimation. Additionally, the algorithm can be integrated into Internet of Things (IoT) devices, enabling real-time, adaptive control of acoustic signals. Overall, this research offers a promising approach for improving sound speed profile estimation and its application in diverse fields.

FMRI using naturalistic paradigms such as watching movies has gained increasing interest in recent neuroimaging studies. Data-driven blind source separation (BSS) methods such as independent component analysis (ICA) are widely used to extract meaningful features in fMRI data. Recent studies have shown that BSS based on deep neural networks (DNNs) such as restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and deep belief network (DBN) outperform ICA. Those DNN-based methods interpret spatially aggregated fMRI time series of multiple subjects in group analysis to reduce model complexity, and only brain networks with group-wise temporal consistency can be identified. However, fMRI activities to naturalistic paradigm exhibit both group-wise consistency and inter-subject difference. To address this problem, we propose a two-stage DBN-based BSS method. In the first stage, a DBN model is trained using temporally aggregated fMRI time series of multiple subjects. In the second stage, subject-specific DBN models are initialized using model parameters learned in the first stage and are trained to converge using individual fMRI data to refine brain network identification. We use an fMRI dataset acquired using a movie stimulus to validate the proposed method.

The stability analysis of nonautonomous recurrent neural networks with both bounded and unbounded delays on time scales is the focus of this paper. Artificial neural networks continue to gain importance in modeling a variety of systems in many different fields, and the ability to analyze their stability and synchronization is crucial. This paper provides stability criteria for the system under study, which can be verified using Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals. In addition, the study of synchronization is carried out utilizing a Germanium detector. The results obtained in this study can be applied in a variety of engineering applications where stability and synchronization of recurrent neural networks are crucial.

We propose a sequential and adaptive hypothesis test that operates in a completely distributed setting, relying on a sensor network where no single data-fusion center is present. The test is inspired by Chernoff's optimal solution, originally derived in a centralized setting. We compare the performance of our test with the optimal sequential test in sensor networks and provide sufficient conditions for which the proposed test achieves asymptotic optimality, minimizing the expected cost required to reach a decision plus the expected cost of making a wrong decision, when the observation cost per unit time tends to zero. Under these conditions, the proposed test is also shown to be asymptotically optimal with respect to the higher moments of the time required to reach a decision.

The diversification of wireless network traffic attack characteristics has led to the problems what traditional intrusion detection technology with high false positive rate, low detection efficiency, and poor generalization ability. In order to enhance the security and improve the detection ability of malicious intrusion behavior in a wireless network, this paper proposes a wireless network intrusion detection method based on improved convolutional neural network (ICNN). First, the network traffic data is characterized and preprocessed, then modeled the network intrusion traffic data by ICNN. The low-level intrusion traffic data is abstractly represented as advanced features by CNN, which extracted autonomously the sample features, and optimizing network parameters by stochastic gradient descent algorithm to converge the model. Finally, we conducted a sample test to detect the intrusion behavior of the network. The simulation results show that the method proposed in our paper has higher detection accuracy and true positive rate together with a lower false positive rate. The test results on the test set KDDTest + in our paper show that compared with the traditional models, the detection accuracy is 8.82% and 0.51% higher than that of LeNet-5 and DBN, respectively, and the recall rate is 4.24% and 1.16% higher than that of LeNet-5 and RNN, respectively, while the false positive rate is lower than the other three types of models. It also has a big advantage compared to the IDABCNN and NIDMBCNN methods.

Employee engagement is becoming a critical component of an organization's success. For many companies, increases in engagement mean increases in productivity. While organizations have long used traditional questionnaires to measure engagement, these leave room for interpretation; and trying to get clarity makes the questionnaires longer, which decreases participation. On the other hand, user-generated content can often act as a barometer on employee engagement, but does not lend itself easily to engagement prediction. We present a model leveraging machine-learning techniques to analyze and predict employee engagement, using both user-generated social analytics and text content from organization-wide surveys, to calculate a real-time engagement level for employees. Our method helped identify specific words and phrases used by individual employees that play an important role in engagement prediction. This study was able to uncover critical themes driving employee engagement and behavior at the enterprise level. Our model for textual analysis cannot only predict engagement, but also provide highly valuable, and actionable, data for business leaders about the health of their organizations.

We address the problem of optimal feature selection for a Gaussian vector pair in the weak dependence regime, when the inference task is not known in advance. In particular, we show that multiple formulations all yield the same solution, and correspond to the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the canonical correlation matrix. Our results reveal key connections between canonical correlation analysis (CCA), principal component analysis (PCA), the Gaussian information bottleneck, Wyner's common information, and the Ky Fan (nuclear) norms.

The paper proposes a sub-cycle sample method to mitigate the DC offset in the M-Class Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs). The DC offset in fault currents is a significant concern for power system harmonics, and it can cause errors in measuring sinusoidal signals. The proposed sub-cycle sample method estimates the DC offset by performing harmonic analysis using Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFTs). The estimated DC offset is then subtracted from the original signal to provide accurate measurements of the sinusoidal signal. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on IEEE 13-bus test system under various circuit faults, and the results demonstrate that the sub-cycle sample method can effectively mitigate the DC offset with improved Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) performance.

This paper proposes a new approach to secure cluster heads in wireless sensor networks. Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are widely used for monitoring various processes, however, security is an important issue. Clustering algorithms are commonly used to organize the sensors, and the cluster head plays a critical role in this organization. Therefore, securing the cluster head is critical for the overall security of the network. This paper proposes a genetic algorithm-based approach to secure the cluster head. This approach ensures that the head is in a secure location in the topology, thus minimizing the risk of attacks. The proposed approach is evaluated through simulation, and results show that it provides better security compared to existing approaches. This paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of WSNs security and can be used as a basis for further research in this area.

This paper presents the concept of a self-aware autonomous city, which is achieved through the integration of various technologies and methodologies such as urban sensing, data mining, crowdsourcing, ad hoc networks, and knowledge discovery. The primary goal of this approach is to enable urban areas to become more efficient, resilient, and sustainable by leveraging the power of technology and data. Urban planning is a critical component of this approach, and it involves analyzing the data collected by sensors and crowdsourcing tools to identify trends and patterns. The results of this analysis can be used to inform decision-making processes, such as determining the optimal location for a new transportation hub or identifying areas that require additional community services. The development of a self-aware autonomous city has significant implications for the future of urban living and presents numerous opportunities for further research and innovation in the field of smart cities.

The increase of flexibility is a common objective of softwarized networks based on concepts, such as software defined networking, network function virtualization, and network virtualization. Hence, in the state-of-the-art, flexibility is used as an argument for a certain proposed architecture, solution mechanism or design choice in general. The meaning of flexibility behind such rather qualitative arguments is highly diversified in the literature, as a common understanding of flexibility is missing so far. In this paper, we survey the state-of-the-art in softwarized networks with a focus on the flexibility that is provided by each proposed concept, mechanism or system. In particular, we show that the flexibility provided by different network softwarization technologies can be classified into six different aspects within the three high-level flexibility categories, i.e., configuration adaptation, functions location, and scalability. We analyze the state-of-the-art in flexibility from several viewpoints including flexibility aspects, network technologies, domains and planes in order to derive a common understanding of how flexibility can be provided in softwarized wireline and wireless networks. Moreover, we reveal open issues, which are mostly related to the fact that flexibility is not clearly defined in the literature, and derive concrete research challenges accordingly. Our classification of flexibility and the derived research challenges aim at stimulating the discussion toward a more quantitative analysis of the design requirement of flexibility that has demonstrated increasing importance for softwarized networks and beyond.

This paper aims to improve the technical skills learning experience of engineering students by designing training using the first principles of instruction. The principles of training, conferences, and online services are used to create a learning experience that fosters effective technical skill acquisition. In addition, programming skills, particularly in Python, are emphasized. The use of light emitting diodes is also explored as a tool for teaching technical skills in a hands-on, interactive manner. By utilizing these principles and tools, engineering students can develop technical skills in practical and meaningful ways, leading to improved learning outcomes and greater success in the field.

Blocking Expanding Ring Search(BERS) is the modified scheme of TTL-sequence based ERS(TTL-ERS) to increase the energy efficiency by adding a little latency and decreasing the number of route request packet(RREQ)s which are flooded into network to query the path during the route discovery process for the reactive routing protocol of Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET). Until recently, several variants of BERS have been proposed, and all of them use `chase' packet to stop or cancel the flooding of the RREQ for fulfilled route request. In this paper, we modelled these main variants of BERS, classifying them into Source node Initiated Chase Packet (SICP) type and Reply node Initiated Chase Packet (RICP) type, and analyzed the performance of each scheme installed in AODV protocol over WiFi MANET environment by the NS-3 simulator. The results of this paper show undiscovered aspect, different from the results of mathematical and analytical studies or the results of network simulation performed on the low node density network: the performance value of the BERS series deteriorates dramatically after node density of the network comes high. It means that broadcasting of chase packet as well as broadcasting of RREQ is a large burden on the dense node WiFi network. Notably, this phenomenon is more distinct in the SICP type model (BERS, BERS*, BERS+), and it even leads to greater overhead than TTL-ERS in case of very high node density network. On the other hand, the RICP type models (tBERS, tBERS*, tBERS+), which are improved to start flooding cancellation earlier than SICP, exhibit greater performance improvement than expected in case of higher node density. These results show that, in the BERS series models, flooding cancellation by the broadcasting packet can be another factor of the broadcasting storm, and that the earlier the flooding cancellation, the greater the performance improvement effect than theoretical prediction in the high node density WiFi MANET.

Biomedical imaging plays a crucial role in medical diagnoses and treatments. In recent years, deep learning techniques have been increasingly applied in medical image analysis due to their outstanding performance in feature extraction and classification. Computational modeling has also been employed to simulate various diseases and generate synthetic data for training deep learning models. Task analysis helps to identify the key components and requirements of a particular medical image analysis task, which guides the selection of suitable methods and models. Computer vision techniques such as semantic segmentation and object detection have demonstrated promising results in medical image analysis. Additionally, data models conceptually describe the relationships between different data entities in medical image analysis, providing insights into the data characteristics and model design. However, there remain several challenges in using deep learning methods for medical image analysis, such as data scarcity and efficient data utilization. Future directions in this field include further exploration of model explainability and interpretability, and enhancement of cross-modality approaches.

This paper presents a novel augmented reality guidance system for future informatization experimental teaching. The system integrates education, field programmable gate arrays, three-dimensional displays, hardware, feature extraction, smart glasses, and engines to provide an immersive and interactive learning experience. The proposed system can be used in various educational settings, such as engineering and computer science courses, to enhance student engagement and understanding. The system's hardware consists of a camera, a field programmable gate array, and a three-dimensional display. The developed feature extraction algorithm provides technical assistance by detecting objects and tracking movements. The smart glasses act as a visual display, projecting the objects in a three-dimensional format. The engines generate the augmented reality objects and integrate the entire system. The proposed system allows for a more engaging learning experience by enabling students to interact with their environment in a dynamic and interactive way. Overall, the system has the potential to revolutionize education by incorporating cutting-edge technology and enhancing the effectiveness of teaching methodologies.

In order to effectively control cyanobacterial risks, a Latent Variable Structured Bayesian Network (LV-SBN) is proposed in this study. LV-SBN is an effective biological system modeling method, which utilizes Bayes methods and data models to identify and predict the risk factors of cyanobacterial blooms. By incorporating information from multiple sources and considering the interactions among different ecosystem components, LV-SBN provides a comprehensive and accurate computational modeling framework for cyanobacterial risk pre-control. Additionally, LV-SBN can estimate the probability distribution of cyanobacterial risks, which is essential for decision-making and risk management. Furthermore, the systematic construction and interpretation of LV-SBN facilitate a better understanding of the mechanisms and factors influencing cyanobacterial blooms, and therefore can help to prevent and mitigate the ecological and health impacts caused by cyanobacterial outbreaks.

This study involved a bibliometric analysis of published literature on Industry 4.0, focusing on various relevant topics such as industries, the Internet of Things, bibliometrics, databases, manufacturing, cyber-physical systems, and automation. The analysis was conducted to provide insights into the growth and development of research and knowledge in the field of Industry 4.0. The study utilized a database search strategy based on selected keywords and identified a total of 718 publications across a period of 10 years. The results of the analysis revealed an increasing trend in the number of publications on Industry 4.0, with the majority of the literature originating from Europe and Asia. Furthermore, the study found that the most popular research themes revolve around the concept of cyber-physical systems and the application of Industry 4.0 in manufacturing industries. Overall, this study provides useful information on the current state of research and knowledge on Industry 4.0 and could be used to guide future research endeavors in this field.

In this paper, we investigate the outage performance of the proposed relay-user selection (RUS) scheme for amplify-and-forward full-duplex multi-relay multi-user network, where the direct link between the source node and the user node is used to convey information. Meanwhile, each relay node is energy-constrained and the simultaneous wireless information and power transfer technology is employed to harvest energy. A power splitter is equipped in each relay node to split the received signal into energy harvesting part and signal processing part. The closed-form and a simple asymptotic expression for outage probability is provided. Moreover, the optimal power splitting factor of each relay node is calculated to minimize the outage probability of the system. Finally, the numerical simulations are provided to validate the analysis.

This paper presents a case study focusing on real-time urban drainage monitoring in Hong Kong using IoT sensors. The aim of the study is to analyze the use of smart city technology for flood prevention by implementing a real-time monitoring system that provides immediate information on urban drainage conditions. The implementation of such a system requires the integration of IoT sensors, artificial neural networks, and real-time systems. The paper discusses the role of these technologies in enabling the effective monitoring of drainage systems, allowing cities to react quickly to any issues that arise. The study highlights the benefits of real-time monitoring, including a reduction in delays and the potential to prevent floods in highly populated areas. The findings suggest that the implementation of smart city technology for urban drainage monitoring has the potential to play a vital role in mitigating the impact of floods in densely populated urban areas. As such, the study provides valuable insights into the application of IoT sensors and artificial neural networks in smart city technology for flood prevention.

Neural networks, as powerful models for many difficult learning tasks, have created an increasingly heavy computational burden. More and more researchers focus on how to optimize the training time, and one of the difficulties is to establish a general iteration time prediction model. However, the existing models have high complexity or tedious build processes, and there is still space for improvement in prediction accuracy. Moreover, there is little systematic analysis of multi-GPU which is a special and widely used scenario. In this paper, we introduce a framework to analyze the training time for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on multi-GPU platforms. Based on the analysis of GPU calculation principles and its special transmission mode, our framework decomposes the model and obtain accurate prediction results without long-term training or complex data collection. We start by extracting key feature parameters related to GPUs, CNNs, and networks. Then, we map CNN architectures to constraints, including software platforms, GPU platforms, parallel strategies, and communication strategies. At last, we provide the prediction model and give analysis results of training time from multiple perspectives. The proposed model is verified on four types of NVIDIA GPU platforms and six different CNN architectures. The experiment results show that the average error across varies scenarios is less than 15% and outperform the state-of-the-art results by 5%-30%, which corroborate our model an effective tool for artificial intelligence (AI) researchers.

Data mining of wearable devices data has become a popular research topic in recent years due to the growing popularity and widespread use of wearable devices. The increasing use of wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness trackers has led to a massive collection of data, which has created an enormous opportunity for researchers to analyze this data and gain insights. Time series analysis and machine learning algorithms have been used extensively in the field of wearable device data mining, and biomedical monitoring is one of the primary applications of this research. Parkinson’s disease is one of the diseases that are commonly monitored using wearable devices, and machine learning algorithms have been used to analyze the data collected from these devices. The results of these analyses help clinicians to better understand the progression of the disease and provide better treatment options. In conclusion, data mining of wearable devices data is a rapidly growing field with numerous applications in the biomedical domain. Developing new and effective machine learning algorithms will undoubtedly be crucial in advancing this field further.

The ability to learn various kinds of skills, whether it is motor, sensory or cognitive, is pivotal to animal's survival through evolution. Multiple coding schemes may be involved to encode information needed in learning. Among them, temporal coding is able to provide expanded bandwidth which renders more information to be encoded. Thus, we were motivated to inspect whether animal have the capability of encoding information in temporal precision to acquire skills. In this study, we adopted the brain-machine interfaces (BMIs) to investigate whether the precise spiking patterns can be directly reinforced and volitionally modulated. Rats were trained to learn to control the pitch of an auditory cursor to achieve rewards by volitionally modulating the number of concurrent spiking pairs between two selected units. We found that, performance in the task improved over sessions with successful modulation of relative timing of firings between two selected units to a short interval within 15ms, which indicated that temporal coding can play a part in abstract skill learning. Moreover, the fine temporal structure of neural activity and the yielding behavioral outcomes involved in learning was able to be unified under one experimental framework and robustly controlled for further studies. Successful conditioning of temporal spike patterns also revealed the great potential for high-resolution BMIs and clinical applications.

This paper presents a groundbreaking development in radiation therapy technology, namely Two Photon Dose Engines for Accurate and Fast Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy. Specifically, the development includes computational modeling, engines, photonics, kernel, physics, optimization, and oncology. The two photon dose engines offer a highly precise and efficient method of radiation treatment delivery, enabled by advanced photonics-based technology. By incorporating cutting-edge computational models, the dose engines can optimize the delivery process to minimize unwanted side effects on healthy tissues while delivering the maximum dose to the targeted tumor. Additionally, the inclusion of kernel and physics modules ensures the accuracy of the dose delivery. This approach represents a significant advancement in the field of oncology by providing a highly effective and safe means of radiation therapy delivery. The potential impact of this technology on patient care is significant, with thought leaders anticipating that the Two Photon Dose Engines will enable oncologists to deliver highly targeted and effective radiation doses with accuracy and speed.

This paper focuses on the analysis of cryptocurrency prices using artificial intelligence techniques, specifically predictive models based on artificial neural networks and logic gates. The study examines the price history of Bitcoin, one of the most popular cryptocurrencies, and analyzes it using time series analysis. The main objective of this research is to develop a more accurate and reliable method of predicting cryptocurrency price movements. The results reveal that the proposed method is effective in analyzing the trends and patterns in the cryptocurrency market, and can provide valuable insights for investors and cryptocurrency enthusiasts. The study highlights the significance of artificial intelligence techniques in the field of finance and the growing need for advanced analytics tools to understand the behavior of digital assets.

This paper reports on our experience with deploying network traffic classifiers in a live Software Defined Network (SDN). We select five simple machine learning (ML) algorithms and implement them for Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) detection. Using publicly available datasets, we establish a standard reference for the performance of each classifier (algorithm) in terms of accuracy, precision and detection rate. An identical experiment over a live SDN shows that the classifiers perform significantly poorer compared to the reference standard, exhibiting up to 11.2% lower accuracy, 30.2% lower precision and detection rate lower than 15% (98% in the reference standard). We argue that the interactions between network elements such as the switch and the controller significantly significantly affects the performance of ML algorithms in a live network which must be accounted for in a real deployment.

In this paper, an out-of-sample extension to manifold learning via meta-modeling is proposed. Manifolds and their learning systems are explored as a means of computational modeling. Multivariate regression and Laplace equations are used to reduce dimensionality and refine the manifold representations of the input data. A kernel-based approach is applied to model the relationship between the manifolds and the input data, enabling effective out-of-sample extension. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets. The results indicate that the method can accurately capture the underlying manifold structures of the input data, while providing robustness against noise and sampling variability. The proposed out-of-sample extension to manifold learning via meta-modeling has the potential to enhance the performance of many machine learning applications, including image recognition, speech recognition, and natural language processing.

This paper discusses the use of microsaccades as a tool for asynchronous feature extraction in spiking networks. Microsaccades are small, involuntary eye movements that have been shown to enhance visual perception. The authors propose a voltage-controlled model that enables neurons to spike asynchronously in response to microsaccades. The resulting spatiotemporal activity patterns are then processed using support vector machines and histograms for feature extraction. The resulting features are shown to improve classification accuracy in a streaming media scenario. The authors also provide a visualization tool for analyzing the spatiotemporal activity patterns of the neurons. Overall, the use of microsaccades for asynchronous feature extraction provides a promising avenue for improving the performance of spiking networks in processing visual stimuli.

This paper presents an enhanced intelligent diagnosis method based on multi-sensor image fusion, which uses an improved deep learning network for fault diagnosis in vibrating equipment. The proposed method leverages the power of convolution and feature extraction to obtain meaningful information from raw sensor images. Moreover, a kernel-based data model is introduced to improve the accuracy and stability of the deep learning network. The results of experiments show that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach offers an effective solution for fault diagnosis in vibrating equipment, which has a wide range of applications in the field of industry and engineering.

Designing blockchain architecture is still an open question and encounters a lot of challenges such as scalability, security, high utilization and so on. In this paper, we propose Chameleon, a scalable and adaptive permissioned blockchain architecture. We adopt the principles of non-forking, high security, scalable and high utilization to design the Chameleon to be suitable for next generation blockchain architecture. In Chameleon, we introduce credit value which can only be acquired through honest behavior to enhance the security of the consensus algorithm. We also introduce the QoS of transactions to meet the various needs of different users. While previous work using sharding to improve the scalability, they either store all transactions in every area or just work independently, it either causes too much redundant data or low resource utilization. Combined with the cloud storage, Chameleon partition the nodes into different area according to different scenario, every area process their own transactions and can also cooperate with each other dynamically to improve transaction throughput and resource utilization.

Hybrid storage devices have been widely deployed in cloud platforms to provide cost-efficient storage services. So the performance isolation on hybrid storage devices is important and necessary to ensure the quality-of-service (QoS) of cloud tenants. However, existing performance isolation techniques (e.g., the widely used cgroup) cannot provide accurate performance isolation on hybrid devices, usually leading to an unexpected throughput shrink than the user-specified value. In this paper, we propose a new Self-Adaptive Accurate Throttling (SAAT) method to achieve accurate performance isolation on hybrid storage devices. SAAT can give an accurate estimation of the throughput shift of existing solutions periodically according to the latest status of hybrid storage devices, and then adjust the assigned throughput of cgroup to achieve the accurate performance isolation. The experimental results exhibit that SAAT outperform the original cgroup method for 3.42 times on the difference of average throughput (DAT) between the target and the measured one, i.e., reducing DAT from 6.56% to 1.94%; in the meanwhile, SAAT reduces the Average Jitter of practical throughput from 6.62% to 5.25%.

In this paper, we present a simple method to integrate the discriminative information of video for the action recognition tasks. We introduce the concept of motion map to represent the prefix of video sequences by optimizing the recognition accuracy of original video. 3-dimensional convolution (3Dconv) based model is used to generate the new motion map by integrating current motion map and future video frame. This model is capable of increasing the length of training video in iterative manner and allow us to generate the final motion map. Experimental evaluation results on widely used datasets i.e HMDB51 and UCF101 have revealed effectiveness and flexibility of proposed method over other baseline schemes.

This paper presents a study on the use of wireless sensor networks (WSN) in Internet of Things (IoT) applications in the field of agriculture. The use of WSN technology in agriculture has enabled the deployment of robot sensing systems, which can monitor and collect data from various sensors such as temperature sensors. In this study, the focus is on the use of WSN for monitoring agriculture-related parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and humidity. The study evaluates the protocols used in WSN and the challenges faced in deploying these systems in agriculture. The results of the study show that the use of WSN in agriculture is a promising solution to improve yields and optimize resource usage, but it requires careful consideration of the deployment protocols and maintenance of the system. The use of WSN in agriculture can revolutionize the industry and help address the food security issues faced by many countries.

PANDA is a dual linearly converging method designed for distributed optimization over time-varying undirected graphs. The algorithm has been specifically developed to tackle the challenges of optimization in large-scale networks with distributed information processing. PANDA is able to achieve fast convergence to the optimal solution by using acceleration techniques based on the curvature properties of symmetric matrices. The algorithm has been shown to be highly effective in real-world scenarios, such as those found in radio frequency optimization. PANDA has become increasingly popular in Europe and has been the focus of many conferences and research papers. The algorithm's ability to converge quickly has made it a promising tool for a wide range of optimization problems in large-scale networks.

This paper evaluates the effectiveness of machine learning models, specifically support vector machines (SVMs), for upscaling surface ocean CO2 measurements. The models were trained using data from radio frequency sensors and sea surface measurements. The results suggest that SVMs are a promising method for upscaling CO2 measurements, with potential applications in understanding global carbon cycles and climate change. The study also explores the use of neurons in machine learning models, highlighting the potential for further development in this area. Overall, this research contributes to the ongoing effort to better understand and mitigate the impacts of ocean acidification and climate change.

Continuous memory technology scaling causes memory cells to be vulnerable to wearout. To ensure reliable operations of circuits and systems in the presence of wearout, we require accurate estimation of the lifetime of circuits and systems degraded by wearout. Since the conventional method of estimating circuit and system reliability degradation based on device-level accelerated life test (ALT) does not account for the tolerance of a circuit and a system to a wearout failure of a device, accelerated lifetime testing at the circuit and system level is necessary. For accurate estimation of system reliability using system-level ALT, we propose a method that optimizes the design of experiments for ALT. From significant observations from failure data statistics of system-level ALT with various stress conditions applied to the memory system of the Leon3 as a case study, we define acceptability regions for memory testing of each wearout mechanism. In addition, by analyzing errors in estimating Weibull parameters from system-level ALT, we develop a methodology that optimizes experimental designs in acceptability regions of each wearout mechanism to minimize such estimation errors in system-level ALT.

The primary objective of recommender systems, in a general sense, is to recommend items to users rather than to persuade users to get those items. Hence, a recommender system is not a persuasive technology by itself. In recent years, however, there has been increasing attention in the literature towards augmenting persuasiveness features into recommender systems. Several researchers have discussed the feasibility of enriching recommendations with persuasive messages. Nonetheless, there is a lack of works that discuss how to incorporate personalized and dynamic persuasive capabilities to recommender systems. To mitigate this issue, we propose the Personalized Persuasive RS (PerPer) framework. The PerPer adopts learning automata concepts to dynamically choose a suitable persuasive strategy for users in a personalized manner. PerPer is general enough to be plugged into different recommenders and to consider several persuasive strategies. PerPer aims to provide a simple and straightforward way to incorporate persuasive features to recommenders. By this, it would have the potential of increasing users' perceived acceptance of recommendations.

Wireless communication system design is traditionally carried out in a rather sequential manner. As a result, propagation modeling and network protocol design have largely evolved as independent areas. This conventional fragmented approach does not fully capitalize on potential efficiencies during the design of communication systems. This paper proposes an integrated approach for communication system design, which is illustrated using an example of optimizing access point locations in a curved rectangular tunnel. The simple yet insightful example demonstrates the benefits of co-developing the wireless channel models and network protocol design and hence paves the way for further develooment of this intearated aooroach.

Accurate pupil location is paramount to applications such as gaze estimation, assistive technologies and several man-machine interfaces as the ones found in smartphones and VR applications. We introduce a new classifier stemmed from the Inner Product Detector and investigate its features on the challenging task of pupil localization. IPD (Inner Product Detector) is a classifier with high potential in facial landmarks detection. It is robust to variations in the desired pattern while maintaining good generalization and computational efficiency. However, one possible limitation is its linear behavior, which could be overcome by aggregating non-linear techniques, such as kernel methods. Although kernel classifiers have been exhaustively studied in the past two decades, it was not analyzed or applied with IPD, yet. The proposed KIPD achieves in the worst case an accuracy of 97.41% on the BioID dataset and 93.71% in LFPW dataset both at 10% of the interocular distance. In this paper the KIPD is compared to the state of the art methods, including the ones using deep learning, being competitive in terms of accuracy as well as computational complexity.

A new dynamic test method for amplitude frequency response of broadcast transmitter has been proposed in this paper. The method involves measuring transmitter's frequency response in real-time systems by taking into account the delay effects and voltage measurements. The method is based on the estimation of the transmitter's frequency response, which is obtained by measuring its output voltage and its input frequency. The proposed method provides accurate measurements of the amplitude frequency response of transmitters, which is crucial in the field of frequency measurement. The experimental results show that the proposed method is effective and reliable. It has potential applications in the field of broadcasting and telecommunication. Overall, the proposed method is a significant contribution to the field of frequency response measurements, providing a more efficient and accurate way to measure the amplitude frequency response of broadcast transmitters.

In the DV -HOP algorithm of the wireless sensor network, an inaccurate estimation of the minimum hop count and the average hop distance produces a positioning error. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved DV-HOP algorithm. The algorithm reevaluates the average hop distance of the anchor node and corrects the minimum hop count of the node to be located and the anchor node, which reduces the above error. First, the average hop distance of the anchor node closest to the positioned node is reassessed according to the error. Then, the minimum hop count is obtained by the average hop distance of the revaluation, and the correction coefficient of the ratio of the minimum hop count to the actual minimum hop count is obtained, and the minimum hop count of the node to be positioned is corrected by the correction coefficient. Finally, the distance between the node to be located and the anchor node is calculated, and the position of the node to be positioned is calculated by the least squares method. Simulation results show that the improved dv-hop algorithm can reduce the node positioning error and improve the positioning accuracy.

Liquid level control in a tank can be done using various controllers. Conventionally there are many controllers that give a response which is sometimes not desirable. Industries want to improve the control strategy for making the controller work more efficiently. This can be achieved by optimizing the mechanism of controller using some heuristic optimization technique. In this paper optimization techniques like genetic algorithm, ant colony, fuzzy logic control and ANN are discussed. Fuzzy logic controller and ANN are more preferable over other optimization techniques because of their fast response and ability to reduce the error with a considerable amount. ANN can be used to train the fuzzy logic controller to make it more robust.

The scalability issue in the Internet of Things (IoT) systems is one of the major hurdles that can be tackled by decentralizing data flows in algebraic service compositions. Connectors, semantics, and distributed databases are the key components involved in the decentralized data flows to overcome the scalability issue. Moreover, analytical models and sequential analysis play a significant role in monitoring and optimizing the performance of the system. By utilizing the proposed approach, the IoT system can efficiently handle the massive amounts of data generated by the interconnected devices while ensuring scalability and adaptability. Therefore, decentralized data flows in algebraic service compositions provide a promising approach for addressing the scalability issue in the IoT systems in the future.

This paper presents the problem of block simplex constrained signal recovery, which has been demonstrated to be a suitable formulation for estimation problems in networks such as route flow estimation in traffic. There are several natural approaches to this problem: compressed sensing, Bayesian inference, and convex optimization. This paper presents new methods within each framework and assesses their respective abilities to reconstruct signals, with the particular emphasis on sparse recovery, ability to incorporate prior information, and scalability. We then apply these methods to route flow estimation in traffic networks of various sizes and network topologies. We find that both compressed sensing and Bayesian inference approaches are appropriate for structured recovery but have scalability limitations. The convex optimization approach does not directly incorporate prior information, but scales well and has been shown to achieve 90% route flow accuracy on a full-scale network of over 10 000 links and 280 000 routes on a synthetic benchmark based on the I-210 corridor near Los Angeles, CA, USA.

Ambient Assisted Living (AAL) represents the most promising Internet of Things (IoT) application due to its relevance in the elders healthcare and improvement of their quality of life. Recently, the AAL IoT ecosystem has been enriched with promising technologies such as edge computing, which has demonstrated to be the best approach to overcome the demanding requirements of AAL and healthcare services by providing a reduction of the amount of data to transfer to the cloud, an improvement of the response time, and quality of experience. Also, the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies at the edge provides intelligence to improve the decision making timely. However, this approach has been scarcely studied in AAL scenarios and the few proposals based on deploying machine learning models at the edge lack efficiency, security, mechanisms of resource management, service management, and deployment, as well as a real and experimental AAL scenario. For these reasons, this paper proposes an innovative edge gateway architecture to support the deployment of deep learning (DL) models in AAL and healthcare scenarios efficiently. To do so, we have added a predictive analytics module to deploy the models. Since AI technologies demand more resources, a container-based virtualization technology is employed on the edge gateway to manage the limited resources, and provide security and lifecycle services management. The edge gateway performance was evaluated deploying a DL-based fall detection application on it. As a result, our approach improves the inference time compared to that based on the cloud in 34 seconds and to similar approaches in 8 seconds.

This paper proposes a novel approach for self-configuring integral sliding mode control of robot manipulators utilizing deep reinforcement learning. The proposed algorithm involves the use of switches to explore different control couplings, which are then integrated into a centralized control architecture. The deep reinforcement learning component involves training a neural network to predict the optimal control coupling depending on the current state of the system. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is demonstrated through simulation results, which confirm its ability to achieve improved tracking performance and robustness compared to traditional sliding mode control techniques. Overall, this study presents an innovative and effective approach to self-configuring control of robot manipulators, which has the potential for broad applications in the field of robotics.
